ARCH 100.title: Introduction to the Built Environment
ARCH 100.subject: ARCH
ARCH 100.description: Introduction to the breadth of design in today’s global culture. Exploration of human responses to place, climate, culture, communication, and technology, with emphasis on the impact of scientific knowledge on environmental design. Open to nonmajors.

ARCH 101.title: Design Fundamentals Studio I
ARCH 101.subject: ARCH
ARCH 101.description: Introduction to creative design processes focusing on the investigation of composition within defining perceivable space. Hands-on exploration of materials and structures as an introduction to design processes.

ARCH 102.title: Design Fundamentals Studio II
ARCH 102.subject: ARCH
ARCH 102.description: Continued exploration of design processes. Introduction to CAD technologies, material exploration, and creative exploration including the relationship between digital, physical, and materials aspects of design.

ARCH 132.title: Design Communication
ARCH 132.subject: ARCH
ARCH 132.description: Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, present, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including fundamentals of freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and graphic techniques.

ARCH 200.title: Collaboration in Environmental Design
ARCH 200.subject: ARCH
ARCH 200.description: Investigation of the various disciplines in the environmental design field, including architecture, landscape architecture, interiors, historic preservation, urban design, and construction management. Emphasis given to collaborative methods to address critical issues. Open to non-majors.

ARCH 201.title: Beginning Design Studio I
ARCH 201.subject: ARCH
ARCH 201.description: Exploration of critical judgment and means to conceptualize, develop, represent, and both visually and orally communicate form and space, including freehand drawing, mechanical drawing, physical model making, diagramming, and computer graphic techniques.

ARCH 202.title: Beginning Design Studio II
ARCH 202.subject: ARCH
ARCH 202.description: Development of designs and processes to study precedents and explore solutions responding to human needs in built and natural environments. Analysis and representation of architectonic space and form using hand and computer techniques.

ARCH 220.title: Introduction to Environmental Systems A
ARCH 220.subject: ARCH
ARCH 220.description: Introduction to building systems, including structural, environmental, life-safety, building envelope, building materials and building assemblies. Development of design skills with emphasis on elevating skills in assessing and selecting appropriate building systems.

ARCH 235.title: Computer Applications in Design
ARCH 235.subject: ARCH
ARCH 235.description: Exploration of digital design fundamentals and their application to design analysis, conceptualization, design process, and communication of design intent.

ARCH 251.title: Introduction to Landscape Architecture
ARCH 251.subject: ARCH
ARCH 251.description: Principles and practice of landscape planning, design, and technology. Ecological, sociocultural, and natural science determinants of landscape form and pattern. ARCH and ENVD majors only, open to nonmajors if space available.

ARCH 271.title: World Architecture and Urbanism A
ARCH 271.subject: ARCH
ARCH 271.description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture in the world’s major cultural regions, from early agricultural settlements to 1500 C.E. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.

ARCH 272.title: World Architecture and Urbanism B
ARCH 272.subject: ARCH
ARCH 272.description: Investigation of the history and theory of architecture from the 15th century C.E. to the present. Investigation of architecture in relationship to social, political, technological, and material forces.

ARCH 321.title: Introduction to Environmental Systems B
ARCH 321.subject: ARCH
ARCH 321.description: Introduction to environmentalism; focusing on the impact of building systems of the global environment; the role of environmental regulations/certifications, and understanding of sustainable principles (economic, social, and natural systems).

ARCH 341.title: Intermediate Design Studio A
ARCH 341.subject: ARCH
ARCH 341.description: Building and site design with emphasis on site development, analysis, and climatic response. Introduction to sustainable design, land use ordinances, description and delineation of property and land features, and urban and community design influences.

ARCH 342.title: Intermediate Design Studio B
ARCH 342.subject: ARCH
ARCH 342.description: Architectural design with emphasis on space planning, building materials, technology, climatic responses, and codes including complex functional requirements, multi-story design issues, vertical transportation, structure, and finishes. Production of complete schematic design documents. Detailed writing instruction.

ARCH 350.title: Introduction to Planning
ARCH 350.subject: ARCH
ARCH 350.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning/research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.

ARCH 351.title: Introduction to Landscape Design
ARCH 351.subject: ARCH
ARCH 351.description: Principles and practice of urban design within the comprehensive planning process. Sociocultural, economic, political, environmental determinants of urban form and pattern. ARCH and ENVD majors only, open to nonmajors if space available.

ARCH 352.title: Landscape Architecture History
ARCH 352.subject: ARCH
ARCH 352.description: Survey of the history of landscape architecture from Mesopotamia to present. Review of the physical, cultural, social, economic, and political factors, as well as the environmental concerns, horticultural techniques, and technological innovations of historic landscapes.

ARCH 353.title: Landscape Graphics Studio
ARCH 353.subject: ARCH
ARCH 353.description: Basic skills of landscape graphic communication through a creative process model. Learning free hand and technical drafting techniques to creative effective landscape graphics.

ARCH 354.title: Tropical Landscape Planting Design Studio
ARCH 354.subject: ARCH
ARCH 354.description: Students will develop basic skills of residential landscape graphic and design processes in order to clearly articulate the ability to think, analyze, and extend a physical solution in the proper scale. (Alt. years)

ARCH 371.title: Design Theory
ARCH 371.subject: ARCH
ARCH 371.description: Examination of theories, movements, and periods in architectural history focusing on contemporary issues. Requires a minimum of 4,000 words of writing, and three oral communication assignments.

ARCH 372.title: Special Topics in Architectural History and Theory
ARCH 372.subject: ARCH
ARCH 372.description: An examination of specific theories, movements, or periods of architectural history. Changing topics to be taught by both regular and visiting faculty.
ARCH 372.restrictions_raw: ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only.

ARCH 381.title: Landform and Water
ARCH 381.subject: ARCH
ARCH 381.description: Essential topographic site design concepts and skills needed to reshape the land for human use, circulation, water management, and resilience. Topics will be reinforced through problem sets and analytical, computational, graphical, and technical exercises.

ARCH 400.title: Project Management
ARCH 400.subject: ARCH
ARCH 400.description: Exploration of the management of architectural services from project initiation through project completion. Investigation of project delivery options; management of project design teams, project operations and services; design parameter definition; design service documentation; and project execution.

ARCH 415.title: Concentration Design Studio
ARCH 415.subject: ARCH
ARCH 415.description: Professional experience combined with scholarly and research activity occurring in an off-campus location with a focus on architectural concentration areas.

ARCH 422.title: Green Building Evaluation and Rating Systems
ARCH 422.subject: ARCH
ARCH 422.description: Introduction to green building design, construction, and operation standards and rating systems. Emphasis on understanding the intent, criteria, and process of the LEED system in preparation for application in a professional setting.

ARCH 432.title: Construction Project Management
ARCH 432.subject: ARCH
ARCH 432.description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.

ARCH 433.title: Professional Practice Law and Ethics
ARCH 433.subject: ARCH
ARCH 433.description: Exploration of the practice of architecture including: professionalism; office organization and administration; public, client, consultant, and other contractor relations; project administration, procedure and compensation; construction law and contract administration.

ARCH 434.title: Digital Design Synthesis
ARCH 434.subject: ARCH
ARCH 434.description: Investigation of processes for generating architectonic form using current digital technologies. Making advanced geometric models including investigation of morphological transformations. Study of design optimization, digital fabrication, information modeling, and generative algorithms.

ARCH 436.title: Design Exchange
ARCH 436.subject: ARCH
ARCH 436.description: Seminar centered on academic and cultural exchanges, focused on advanced topics related to the design of built environments.

ARCH 442.title: Introduction to Urban Design
ARCH 442.subject: ARCH
ARCH 442.description: Principles and practice of urban design within the comprehensive planning process. Sociocultural, economic, political, environmental determinants of urban form and pattern. ARCH and ENVD majors only; open to non-majors if space available.

ARCH 451.title: Landscape Architecture Design Seminar
ARCH 451.subject: ARCH
ARCH 451.description: Principles and practice of landscape architecture within the comprehensive design processes of the built environment. Focus on context-specific sociocultural, economic, political, environmental determinants of landscape forms and patterns. ARCH and ENVD majors only; open to non-majors if space available.

ARCH 461.title: Introduction to Interior Architecture
ARCH 461.subject: ARCH
ARCH 461.description: Introduction and orientation to the field. Fundamental design principles and elements as applied to interiors. Basic materials and methods of interior construction; basic professional and business practices. Critical analysis of an existing interior space. ARCH and ENVD majors only; open to non-majors if space available.

ARCH 471.title: Historic Architecture Design Seminar
ARCH 471.subject: ARCH
ARCH 471.description: Introduction to historic preservation. Exploration of design principles and elements as applied to conservation of historic resources, including basic conservation materials and methods, professional practices, and critical analysis of existing methodologies. ARCH and ENVD majors only; open to non-majors if space available.

ARCH 472.title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
ARCH 472.subject: ARCH
ARCH 472.description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, and sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/HAER).
ARCH 472.restrictions_raw: ARCH, ENVD, and AMST majors only.

ARCH 473.title: History of American Architecture
ARCH 473.subject: ARCH
ARCH 473.description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

ARCH 474.title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
ARCH 474.subject: ARCH
ARCH 474.description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.

ARCH 477.title: Research Seminar
ARCH 477.subject: ARCH
ARCH 477.description: Research methodology for the qualitative development of an optimum environment.

ARCH 483.title: Urban Ecological Analysis and Design
ARCH 483.subject: ARCH
ARCH 483.description: Applied urban and landscape ecology principles and strategies for analysis, design, and management of urban regions and sites; emphasis on structure, functions, and processes that form urban landscapes at multiple scales and in diverse contexts.

ARCH 484.title: Plants in Design
ARCH 484.subject: ARCH
ARCH 484.description: Introduction to the use of plants as design elements in the built environment across diverse scales. Examination of the spatial, sensory, ecological, and performative qualities of vegetation through analysis of historic and contemporary examples.

ARCH 490.title: Special Topics
ARCH 490.subject: ARCH
ARCH 490.description: Selected topics in any aspect of architecture. Content to be announced.

ARCH 491.title: Special Topics in Architecture History
ARCH 491.subject: ARCH
ARCH 491.description: Specialized work on the history and theory of architecture.

ARCH 492.title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
ARCH 492.subject: ARCH
ARCH 492.description: Specialized investigation of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

ARCH 493.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
ARCH 493.subject: ARCH
ARCH 493.description: Work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

ARCH 496.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Writing
ARCH 496.subject: ARCH
ARCH 496.description: Reading, research, and work on topics in architecture and design. Includes an intensive writing component. May include specialized research and/or studio experience in architecture, design, and the history and theory of architecture and design.

ARCH 628.title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
ARCH 628.subject: ARCH
ARCH 628.description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

ARCH 631.title: Design Communication for Landscape Architects
ARCH 631.subject: ARCH
ARCH 631.description: Theory and application in design communication, including drawing and presentation skills; emphasis on the design process and critical thinking through analog and digital media, diagramming, three-dimensional modeling, and various other presentation techniques.

ARCH 633.title: Computer Applications in Landscape Architecture
ARCH 633.subject: ARCH
ARCH 633.description: Introduction to the use of computers in landscape architecture, emphasizing two- and three dimensional computer-aided drawings and graphics suitable to landscape architectural design and practice.

ARCH 634.title: Landscape Plants: Identification and Use
ARCH 634.subject: ARCH
ARCH 634.description: Introduction to the identification, recognition, and use of plants in landscape design and built environment applications. Students will be introduced to a variety of landscape plants commonly used in Hawai‘i and the tropics.

ARCH 635.title: Landscape Materials and Construction
ARCH 635.subject: ARCH
ARCH 635.description: Examination of materials and methods of landscape construction from source, extraction, and manufacturing, to use and reuse. Assignments include drawing standard construction details and a report on the history of material use, properties, and qualities. Graduate students only.

ARCH 636.title: Landscape Architectural Professional Practice
ARCH 636.subject: ARCH
ARCH 636.description: Introduction of practices and core methods of the landscape architecture profession. Subjects include business and governmental organization, elements of contract law, business management, professional relationships, marketing, professional licensure, and ethics. Graduate students only.

ARCH 641.title: Land Use Planning
ARCH 641.subject: ARCH
ARCH 641.description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

ARCH 650.title: Vernacular Architecture
ARCH 650.subject: ARCH
ARCH 650.description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

ARCH 651.title: Fundamentals of Landscape Design Studio
ARCH 651.subject: ARCH
ARCH 651.description: Theory and application of foundational landscape design principles, programming, and physical analysis to site-based design problems. Visual, formal, spatial, and functional design principles are applied to ecological and cultural influences in landscape design. Graduate students only.

ARCH 652.title: Site Design Studio
ARCH 652.subject: ARCH
ARCH 652.description: Landscape project design at the site scale; from concept development through detailed design. Synthesis of foundational skills into more complex, layered spatial, and functional problems. Emphasis on site research and design methods. Graduate students only.

ARCH 656.title: Environmental and Cultural Landscape Studio
ARCH 656.subject: ARCH
ARCH 656.description: Exploring, understanding, and implementing Hawaiian and Western cultural and environmental landscape design principles. A concentrated look at how to think about creating and respecting a sense of place through landscape design.

ARCH 658.title: Environmental Landscape Technologies and Systems
ARCH 658.subject: ARCH
ARCH 658.description: Understanding the science and art of green landscape technologies, with a comprehensive understanding of LID (low impact design) principles and practices; to increase knowledge to help produce more viable and enduring built landscapes.

ARCH 679.title: Elements of Style
ARCH 679.subject: ARCH
ARCH 679.description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/ cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

ARCH 682.title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
ARCH 682.subject: ARCH
ARCH 682.description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises. Graduate students only.

ARCH 687.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
ARCH 687.subject: ARCH
ARCH 687.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

ARCH 690.title: Special Topics Seminar
ARCH 690.subject: ARCH
ARCH 690.description: Seminar on a wide range of architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty.

ARCH 691.title: Special Topics: Architecture History/ Theory
ARCH 691.subject: ARCH
ARCH 691.description: Specialized work at an advanced level on the history and theory of architecture.

ARCH 692.title: Special Topics in Architectural Technology
ARCH 692.subject: ARCH
ARCH 692.description: Specialized investigation at an advanced level of technological developments in structural systems, environmental control systems, or materials and methods of construction.

ARCH 693.title: Special Topics in Architecture and Design
ARCH 693.subject: ARCH
ARCH 693.description: Intensive work on specialized topics in the fields of architecture and design. May include research and/or studio experiences in architecture, interior architecture, computer-aided design, professional practice, advanced visual design, and architectural graphics.

ARCH 695.title: Applied Theories of Landscape Architecture
ARCH 695.subject: ARCH
ARCH 695.description: Graduate seminar on discussion of central ideas and theories in landscape architecture and environmental design, drawing on primary literature and speculative or built design work over many decades of thought. Graduate students only.

ARCH 696.title: Special Topics in Landscape Architecture
ARCH 696.subject: ARCH
ARCH 696.description: Seminar on a wide range of landscape architectural topics to be directed by both visiting and regular faculty. Graduate students only.

ARCH 700.title: MLA Thesis
ARCH 700.subject: ARCH
ARCH 700.description: Landscape architectural thesis research and design inquiry. Limited to MLA students under Plan A. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

ARCH 715.title: Asia-Pacific Architectural History and Theory
ARCH 715.subject: ARCH
ARCH 715.description: Study of the history and theory of culture and the built environment with particular focus on the Asia-Pacific region. Graduate students only.

ARCH 716.title: Architecture and Urban Design Theory
ARCH 716.subject: ARCH
ARCH 716.description: Detailed investigation of major theories in architecture and urban design and examination of their impact on contemporary architectural practice in varied geo-political contexts. Open to non-majors.

ARCH 722.title: Architecture Systems I: Introduction to Systems
ARCH 722.subject: ARCH
ARCH 722.description: Study of building materials, assemblies, and integrated design including structural, environmental, life-safety, and building envelope systems. Development of ability to design, analyze and assess appropriate systems.

ARCH 723.title: Architecture Systems II: Qualitative Bioclimatic and Structural Performance
ARCH 723.subject: ARCH
ARCH 723.description: Introduction to the theory of bioclimatic principles and structural systems and the ability to analyze, assess, select, design, and integrate them as initial determinants into the building design.

ARCH 724.title: Architecture Systems III: Quantitative Structural Analysis and Design
ARCH 724.subject: ARCH
ARCH 724.description: Introduction to procedures and wood, steel, concrete, and masonry material properties used for structural analysis and design of individual structural elements and building structural systems.

ARCH 725.title: Architecture Systems IV: Environmental Technology, Sustainability, and Analysis
ARCH 725.subject: ARCH
ARCH 725.description: Application and analysis of highperformance building design principles. Emphasis on climate-appropriate passive design, energy-efficient lighting and conditioning strategies, innovative water systems, and renewable energy production.

ARCH 726.title: Architecture Systems V: Building Systems Integration
ARCH 726.subject: ARCH
ARCH 726.description: Properties, evolution, and range of building materials, assemblies, and systems and their applications in integrated high-performance building design with a focus on the role of detail and systems in the design process.

ARCH 731.title: Advanced Design Communication I
ARCH 731.subject: ARCH
ARCH 731.description: Exploration of digital technologies, their relationship to design, and their application to architectural analysis, conceptualization, design processes, communication, representation, and construction.

ARCH 733.title: Advanced Design Communication II
ARCH 733.subject: ARCH
ARCH 733.description: An interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to digital technology and its applications to current developments in practice and research within architecture and design. Graduate students only.

ARCH 734.title: Forms and Frames of Practice
ARCH 734.subject: ARCH
ARCH 734.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice within the global context with emphasis on the Asia Pacific region. Exploration of information technology systems, materials and design process research, construction technology, computer aided manufacturing, and entrepreneurial approaches. Graduate students only.

ARCH 737.title: Advanced Design Communications III
ARCH 737.subject: ARCH
ARCH 737.description: Interdisciplinary investigation of design theory as connected to architectural presentation techniques, particularly oral and written, to current developments in architectural practice.

ARCH 739.title: Research Methods Seminar
ARCH 739.subject: ARCH
ARCH 739.description: Comprehensive assessment of objectives and function of research in architecture and landscape architecture. Lecture, seminar, independent work with emphasis on research project topic and proposal development. Graduate students only.

ARCH 740.title: Architecture Studio I: Intro to Design
ARCH 740.subject: ARCH
ARCH 740.description: Design theories and systematic analytic and synthetic methodologies applied to creation of building and site spaces responsive to environmental and human needs. Several individual projects.

ARCH 741.title: Architecture Studio II
ARCH 741.subject: ARCH
ARCH 741.description: Design of a medium complexity building and site engaging social, cultural, codes, building systems, and sustainable design. Production of program and schematic design documents. Individual projects.

ARCH 742.title: Architecture Studio III
ARCH 742.subject: ARCH
ARCH 742.description: Design of complex, large scale building and site engaging social, cultural, code, sustainable systems, and acoustic issues. Production of schematic and design development documents. Graduate standing only.

ARCH 743.title: Architecture Studio IV: Urban Design
ARCH 743.subject: ARCH
ARCH 743.description: Urban design focused on Asian cities investigating social, cultural, political, and technological factors; study of historical precedents, building/block typology, circulation, infrastructure, and context response.

ARCH 744.title: Architecture Studio V: Comprehensive Design
ARCH 744.subject: ARCH
ARCH 744.description: Design and programming for a moderately complex building and site. Production of design development and partial construction documents describing sustainable building assemblies and construction cost.

ARCH 745.title: Advanced Practice
ARCH 745.subject: ARCH
ARCH 745.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

ARCH 751.title: Architecture Topics
ARCH 751.subject: ARCH
ARCH 751.description: Range of topics allowing acquisition of knowledge and ability needed for professional architectural practice offered online.

ARCH 754.title: Research Seminar
ARCH 754.subject: ARCH
ARCH 754.description: Varied topics furthering knowledge and ability needed for professional design practice emphasizing communication methods for collaborative and integrated design using digital technologies.

ARCH 755.title: Advanced Global Practice
ARCH 755.subject: ARCH
ARCH 755.description: Comprehensive study of architectural practice investigating architect’s response to global forces, including entrepreneurial practice, office organization, project delivery, compensation, and construction law.

ARCH 761.title: Ecology, Community, and Design
ARCH 761.subject: ARCH
ARCH 761.description: Exploration of the interaction of landscape and community necessities in urban ecological design. Studio problems, design research projects, lectures, and discussion applied to the integration of ecological and social factors in urban contexts. Graduate students only.

ARCH 763.title: Advanced Project Design Studio: Comprehensive
ARCH 763.subject: ARCH
ARCH 763.description: Design and programming for a complex, medium-scale, multi-layered urban landscape architecture project. Iterative, advanced design inquiry and materials exploration. Production of in-depth, comprehensive design development and partial construction documents. Graduate students only.

ARCH 764.title: Capstone Design Research Studio
ARCH 764.subject: ARCH
ARCH 764.description: Advanced landscape architectural design inquiry and applied research investigation. Serves as a capstone experience, synthesizing theory, values, and practice. Limited to MLA students under Plan B. Graduate students only.

ARCH 771.title: Architecture History
ARCH 771.subject: ARCH
ARCH 771.description: Investigation of architectural history and theory in the world from antiquity to present. Examining social, political, technological, material, and environmental forces.

ARCH 777.title: History of Hawaiian Architecture
ARCH 777.subject: ARCH
ARCH 777.description: Investigation of social, cultural, political, climactic, and technological factors influencing the historical development of architecture in Hawai‘i.

ARCH 781.title: Advanced Research Methods and Design Inquiry
ARCH 781.subject: ARCH
ARCH 781.description: Individual development of a doctorate proposal that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, and design.

ARCH 782.title: Case Study and Analysis
ARCH 782.subject: ARCH
ARCH 782.description: Individual development of a case study project that advances architectural knowledge through analysis, research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions. Graduate students only.

ARCH 788.title: Doctorate Project II Extension
ARCH 788.subject: ARCH
ARCH 788.description: Extension of the development of a doctorate project with an approved committee that advances architectural knowledge through research, scholarship, design, and engages theoretical and architectonic propositions.

ARCH 794.title: Digital Design and Fabrication
ARCH 794.subject: ARCH
ARCH 794.description: Theoretical and design investigations into fabrication and construction techniques using computer aided design and manufacturing technologies.

ACM 210.title: Introduction to Cinematic Digital Production
ACM 210.subject: ACM
ACM 210.description: Introduction to the basic techniques of cinematic digital production and allows them to explore their personal voice in this process.

ACM 215.title: Introduction to 3D Computer Animation
ACM 215.subject: ACM
ACM 215.description: A basic overview of the 3D animation production process, including modeling, texturing, rigging, animation, lighting, and rendering.

ACM 216.title: Fundamentals of Animation
ACM 216.subject: ACM
ACM 216.description: Introduction to traditional styles and methods of hand drawn 2D, digital, and stop motion animation through theory and practice.

ACM 255.title: Introduction to Cinema and Digital Media
ACM 255.subject: ACM
ACM 255.description: Introduction to the study of cinema: history, aesthetics, and cultural impact.

ACM 310.title: Cinematic Narrative Production
ACM 310.subject: ACM
ACM 310.description: Production-intensive course with collaborative as well as individual projects. Theories and application of basic digital cinema productions, including camera, lighting, sound, and editing.

ACM 312.title: Cinematography
ACM 312.subject: ACM
ACM 312.description: Comprehensive course in visual styles supporting screen narratives through a study of principles of camera elements, operations, lighting, color and composition. Professional role and responsibilities of cinematographer. Project-oriented. Must have access to manually controlled still camera.

ACM 314.title: Experimental Art and Animation
ACM 314.subject: ACM
ACM 314.description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
ACM 314.prereq_raw: 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113 or THEA 353 (or concurrent) or THEA 356 (or concurrent), or consent
ACM 314.restrictions_raw: ACM, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only.

ACM 315.title: Narrative Game Design
ACM 315.subject: ACM
ACM 315.description: Storytelling through computer games. Effect of interactivity on narrative. Interactive plot structures, conceptual design, artwork, audio, cinematography, two- and three dimensional computer graphics. Design and programming of game narrative using scripting languages.
ACM 315.prereq_raw: 215 and 216 and B or better in 255 , or consent

ACM 316.title: 3D Character Animation
ACM 316.subject: ACM
ACM 316.description: Creating the illusion of life through the principles of animation. Application of theory to practical scene work with emphasis on acting and personality in animated characters. Sophomore standing or higher for (C).
ACM 316.prereq_raw: 215 and 216 and B or better in 255 and ART 113 for (B); 216 (with a C or better) for (C), or consent

ACM 317.title: 3D Cinematography and Dynamics
ACM 317.subject: ACM
ACM 317.description: Computer animation directing and cinematography for the design and creation of visual effects. Using particles and dynamics systems to simulate natural phenomena. Compositing of visual layers.

ACM 318.title: Classical 2D Full Animation
ACM 318.subject: ACM
ACM 318.description: Hand drawn full animation techniques; rough animation, inbetweening, clean up animation and digital color processes. Digital line testing, sync dialog and other advanced skills for classical 2D full animation.

ACM 320.title: Animation Production I
ACM 320.subject: ACM
ACM 320.description: Students work independently to produce a short, animated film. Emphasis on visual storytelling and character animation.

ACM 321.title: Storyboarding and Animatics
ACM 321.subject: ACM
ACM 321.description: Exposes students to the history, application, format, styles, and methods of creating storyboards and animatics. Visual storytelling will be analyzed by examining the foundational components of the visual language of a film. Sophomore standing or higher.

ACM 325.title: Visual Effects
ACM 325.subject: ACM
ACM 325.description: Introduction to the history, theory, design and execution of visual effects for the screen. Project-based learning in traditional photographic and digitally-generated special effects.

ACM 330.title: Independent Producing
ACM 330.subject: ACM
ACM 330.description: Fundamentals of producing for independent filmmaking, focusing on business acumen and role of the producer through various stages of production. Topics include proposal writing, script breakdowns, budgeting, scheduling, legal issues, festival strategy, and distribution.

ACM 350.title: Screenwriting
ACM 350.subject: ACM
ACM 350.description: Introduction to the basics of writing a short narrative screenplay for film or television. Students learn the fundamentals and format of screenwriting as well as basic elements of storytelling and character development.

ACM 352.title: Screening Asian Americans
ACM 352.subject: ACM
ACM 352.description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. ACM majors:

ACM 355.title: Oral Tradition to Screenplay
ACM 355.subject: ACM
ACM 355.description: Adapting the stories, styles, and cultural values of oral tradition storytelling to cinematic narratives.
ACM 355.prereq_raw: 255, and 310 (or concurrent) or 215 (or concurrent); or consent

ACM 360.title: Indigenous Aesthetics
ACM 360.subject: ACM
ACM 360.description: Aesthetic theories and practices of indigenous cultures of the Pacific and their adaptation to the screen in cinematic storytelling.

ACM 370.title: Directing the Actor on Screen
ACM 370.subject: ACM
ACM 370.description: Introduction of the screen-director to the craft of acting for the camera. Students will develop collaborative communication skills and learn practical techniques to elicit spontaneous and relaxed performances from actors.

ACM 372.title: Editing for Cinema
ACM 372.subject: ACM
ACM 372.description: Advanced course examining the theory, techniques, and practices of motion picture editing; use of non-linear digital editing systems; and practical experience in digital editing projects.

ACM 374.title: Post Production Sound
ACM 374.subject: ACM
ACM 374.description: Practical course on the theory, art, and techniques of sound recording, editing, and design for cinema. Students work on projects involving dialogue and sound effects in post production.

ACM 375.title: Directing the Camera for the Screen
ACM 375.subject: ACM
ACM 375.description: Detailed analysis of cinematic grammar, placement, movement, focus, and effects of the camera to create the mise en scene. Practical exercises and projects to apply theory to individual creative work.

ACM 380.title: Genre and Narrative Theory in Creative Media
ACM 380.subject: ACM
ACM 380.description: Focus on the concept of genre, genre films, genre film criticism and popular genres such as Western, film noir, documentary, and Chinese martial arts.

ACM 382.title: Authors in Creative Media
ACM 382.subject: ACM
ACM 382.description: In-depth study of the auteur theory and specific application to authors in creative media, such as film directors, animators, screenwriters or game designers.

ACM 384.title: Study Abroad
ACM 384.subject: ACM
ACM 384.description: Intensive study of selected topics, genres, filmmakers, or digital media production in the host country in a UH Mânoa approved study abroad location.

ACM 385.title: Topics in Creative Media
ACM 385.subject: ACM
ACM 385.description: Topics of interest to faculty and students; taught by regular and visiting faculty.

ACM 386.title: Techniques in Creative Media
ACM 386.subject: ACM
ACM 386.description: Specialized techniques in the creation of digital media: taught by regular and visiting faculty.

ACM 390.title: Workshop in Creative Media
ACM 390.subject: ACM
ACM 390.description: Short-term intensive workshop in focused area of media production.

ACM 399.title: Independent Group Project
ACM 399.subject: ACM
ACM 399.description: Participation in a group research or creative project under supervision of ACM faculty member. Only six credits of 399/499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.

ACM 405.title: Documentary Production
ACM 405.subject: ACM
ACM 405.description: Analysis and practical knowledge of the documentary process including, but not limited to, research, organization and story structure, shooting, camera coverage, and editing.

ACM 410.title: Advanced Cinematic Production
ACM 410.subject: ACM
ACM 410.description: Production of a major cinematic/digital narrative project. Working in groups, each student takes on creative and technical role and responsibilities of a principle crew position. Emphasis on artistic form in narrative development; timely execution from pre- to post-production.

ACM 412.title: Advanced Cinematography
ACM 412.subject: ACM
ACM 412.description: Applies the basic foundations, techniques, and theory of cinematography (covered in ACM 312 ) to a more informed and crafted practice with Camera and Lighting Scene study workshops, and research exercises and film projects.

ACM 415.title: Computer Game Production
ACM 415.subject: ACM
ACM 415.description: Students will work as a team to produce to design and produce a computer game: 2D and 3D elements, animation, story, music, audio, and project software.

ACM 419.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
ACM 419.subject: ACM
ACM 419.description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.

ACM 420.title: Animation Production II
ACM 420.subject: ACM
ACM 420.description: Student teams produce a short, animated film. Prior knowledge of 2D and 3D media authoring tools and animation techniques is necessary.

ACM 450.title: Advanced Screenwriting
ACM 450.subject: ACM
ACM 450.description: Application of narrative principles of character development, story structure and thematic spine to students’ short and feature-length screenplays.

ACM 455.title: Indigenous Filmmaking
ACM 455.subject: ACM
ACM 455.description: Theories and studies of indigenous films and creation of a cinematic project based in indigenous cultural and value systems. Students must complete a certification workshop in camera and editing processes to be enrolled in this course.

ACM 460.title: Ethics and Film
ACM 460.subject: ACM
ACM 460.description: Ethical theory and dilemmas as reflected in film and filmmaking. Social responsibility for filmmakers.

ACM 470.title: Directing the Motion Picture
ACM 470.subject: ACM
ACM 470.description: Students direct a narrative live-action short film from prethrough post-production, learning how to develop a directorial vision and how to implement it through storyboarding, scheduling, and collaborative skill sets.
ACM 470.prereq_raw: 310, and 350 or 355, and 370 (or concurrent); or consent

ACM 480.title: Oceanic Media and Culture
ACM 480.subject: ACM
ACM 480.description: Involves close textual analysis of film, TV and multimedia content. The course includes cinematic and television screenings. Junior standing or higher.

ACM 482.title: The American Documentary
ACM 482.subject: ACM
ACM 482.description: In-depth study of the nature and impact of documentary filmmaking in America, focusing on the interplay between filmmaker, subject, and audience. Will critically examine documentaries for their use of rhetoric, ethics, and narrative voice. Junior standing only.

ACM 484.title: Data Visualization
ACM 484.subject: ACM
ACM 484.description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization. Junior standing or higher.

ACM 485.title: Seminar in Creative Media
ACM 485.subject: ACM
ACM 485.description: Intellectual issues in creative media. Conducted by regular and visiting faculty with extensive student participation and scholarly presentation.

ACM 486.title: Capstone Creative Production
ACM 486.subject: ACM
ACM 486.description: Emphasis on advanced production skills in creating a capstone film project to deepen understanding of cinematic storytelling with individuals taking on the role and responsibilities of key crew positions in collaboration.

ACM 487.title: Video Game Design and Development
ACM 487.subject: ACM
ACM 487.description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.

ACM 490.title: Global Media
ACM 490.subject: ACM
ACM 490.description: Involves close textual analysis and strategic analysis of the globalism phenomenon, with an emphasis on transnational media corporations.

ACM 495.title: Creative Media Internship
ACM 495.subject: ACM
ACM 495.description: Internship in professional cinematic, television, animation and/or digital media production company under professional and faculty supervision.
ACM 495.prereq_raw: 310 or 315 or 316B, and 350 or 355; and consent

ACM 499.title: Directed Study
ACM 499.subject: ACM
ACM 499.description: Independent research or creative project under supervision of ACM faculty member. Only six credits of 399 /499 in any combination can be applied to meet requirements for the major.
ACM 499.prereq_raw: 310 or 315 or 316B, and 350 or 355, and consent

THEA 314.title: Experimental Art and Animation
THEA 314.subject: THEA
THEA 314.description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
THEA 314.prereq_raw: 353 (or concurrent) or 356 (or concurrent) or ACM 216 (or concurrent) or ART 113, or consent
THEA 314.restrictions_raw: ACM, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only.

AMST 110.title: Introduction to American Studies
AMST 110.subject: AMST
AMST 110.description: Introduction to different types of college-level writing through analyses of contemporary American culture and to the main themes and approaches used in American studies and the humanities.

AMST 111.title: Introduction to American Studies Writing
AMST 111.subject: AMST
AMST 111.description: Introduction to different types of college level writing and information literacy with a focus on American culture and society.

AMST 150.title: America and the World
AMST 150.subject: AMST
AMST 150.description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

AMST 150A.title: America and the World
AMST 150A.subject: AMST
AMST 150A.description: Examines America’s role in world history and the influence of world affairs on U.S. culture and society. Focuses on U.S. interdependence with African, European, Native American, Asian, and Polynesian civilizations, from 1492 to present.

AMST 201.title: American Experience: Institutions and Movements
AMST 201.subject: AMST
AMST 201.description: Interdisciplinary course that examines diversity and changes in American values and institutions–political, economic, legal, and social.

AMST 202.title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
AMST 202.subject: AMST
AMST 202.description: Interdisciplinary course that examines diversity and changes in American values and culture-literature, film, visual arts, and architecture.

AMST 202A.title: American Experience: Culture and the Arts
AMST 202A.subject: AMST
AMST 202A.description: Interdisciplinary course that examines diversity and changes in American values and culture– literature, film, visual arts, and architecture.

AMST 211.title: Contemporary American Domestic Issues
AMST 211.subject: AMST
AMST 211.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of such current American domestic issues; topics such as politics, economics, civil rights, family life, the justice system, and the environment.

AMST 212.title: Contemporary American Global Issues
AMST 212.subject: AMST
AMST 212.description: Interdisciplinary exploration of such current global issues as international diplomacy, economic development, national security, demographic change, and environmental protection.

AMST 220.title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
AMST 220.subject: AMST
AMST 220.description: Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

AMST 220A.title: Introduction to Indigenous Studies
AMST 220A.subject: AMST
AMST 220A.description: Interdisciplinary survey that examines the histories, politics, popular representations, self-representations, and contemporary issues of the indigenous peoples of the U.S. and its territories, including Native Americans, Alaska Natives, Kanaka Maoli, Chamorro, and Samoans.

AMST 225.title: Art and Social Change
AMST 225.subject: AMST
AMST 225.description: Will analyze examples from the visual and performing arts, including murals, digital art, film, poetry, and music, paying particular attention to the connections and influence upon social and political movements, both historically and today. A-F only

AMST 301.title: Hip-Hop and American Culture
AMST 301.subject: AMST
AMST 301.description: Survey tracing hip-hop from its Afro-Carribean musical beginnings to contemporary adaptations and interpretations. Students will analyze various materials and will pay attention to the relationships between hip-hop and contemporary social forms.

AMST 308.title: Justice and Asian America: Social Movements and the Law in American History
AMST 308.subject: AMST
AMST 308.description: Examination of demands for and the changing nature of justice, historical and contemporary, through court cases, legislation, presidential orders, and social movements that address legal, social, and political definitions of Asian America.

AMST 310.title: Japanese Americans: History, Culture, Lifestyles
AMST 310.subject: AMST
AMST 310.description: Explores the experiences of Japanese Americans in Hawai‘i and the U.S. at large: historical and cultural heritage, biographical portraits, changing family ties, ethnic lifeways, gender relations, local identity, and the future of island living.

AMST 313.title: African Americans: Issues, Culture, History
AMST 313.subject: AMST
AMST 313.description: Traces the history and culture of African Americans and outlines contemporary issues. Topics include: slavery and racism, community formation and resistance, cultural expression, African American diversity, civil rights, gender and class relations.

AMST 316.title: U.S. Women’s History
AMST 316.subject: AMST
AMST 316.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

AMST 317.title: American Music and Culture
AMST 317.subject: AMST
AMST 317.description: Analysis of a variety of American musical genres and histories through focused writing assignments (record and performance reviews, personal narratives, interviews, research proposals, research papers).

AMST 318.title: Asian America
AMST 318.subject: AMST
AMST 318.description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation.

AMST 319.title: America, Hawai‘i and World War II
AMST 319.subject: AMST
AMST 319.description: Examines WWII as a watershed in American and Hawai‘i history and culture. Topics include: Pearl Harbor, Japanese American internment, sex and racial tensions, Anti-Semitism and the Holocaust, and the dawn of the Atomic Age.

AMST 320.title: American Environments: Survey
AMST 320.subject: AMST
AMST 320.description: Survey of social, political, and cultural relations in diverse, contemporary American environments, including: island societies, urban centers, suburbs, Indian reservations, farming communities, and national parks. Special emphasis on contemporary environmental issues in Hawai‘i.

AMST 325.title: Religion and Law in the U.S.
AMST 325.subject: AMST
AMST 325.description: Surveys church-state jurisprudence since the 1940s, with special attention to difficulty of defining religion, and applies the religion clauses to current issues.
AMST 325.prereq_raw: sophomore or higher standing, or consent. (Once a year)

AMST 326.title: American Folklore and Folklife
AMST 326.subject: AMST
AMST 326.description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism.

AMST 334.title: Digital America: Online Communities and Virtual Worlds
AMST 334.subject: AMST
AMST 334.description: Seminar on the impact of the digital revolution and virtual communities on American culture and society, with an emphasis on questions of identity and participatory democracy. Open to non majors.
AMST 334.prereq_raw: one DH, DA, or DL course, sophomore standing, or consent

AMST 339.title: Religions in America
AMST 339.subject: AMST
AMST 339.description: Examination of American religious traditions, both historical and contemporary, with an emphasis on the principles of religious liberty, non-establishment, and pluralism.

AMST 340.title: War and Media
AMST 340.subject: AMST
AMST 340.description: Examination of a range of media, including photography, film, print journalism, television, video games, and the internet, as they have shaped popular representations and experiences of war in America from the Civil War through the present. (Alt. years)

AMST 343.title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
AMST 343.subject: AMST
AMST 343.description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship with the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of Reconstruction.

AMST 344.title: American Thought and Culture: 20th Century
AMST 344.subject: AMST
AMST 344.prereq_raw: 150 or 201 or 202 or 211 or 212 or HIST 151 or HIST 152; or consent

AMST 345.title: Religion and Conflict in American History
AMST 345.subject: AMST
AMST 345.description: Analyzes selected historical examples of religious conflicts in America, discerning characteristic patterns of American religious discourse, and identifying the social structures, interests, and ethical principles at stake in conflicts about religion.

AMST 348.title: American Design: An Historical Survey
AMST 348.subject: AMST
AMST 348.description: Examination of design in American culture over the last century. Readings in industrial, graphic, interior, architectural, landscape, and user interface design used to study issues of gender, race, and class in the U.S. Open to all class standings. (Alt. years)

AMST 349.title: Contemporary American Design
AMST 349.subject: AMST
AMST 349.description: Investigates design in contemporary American culture. Graphic, industrial, urban, and user-interface design practices are situated within broader social and economic forces. Modes of design practice, production, and consumption studied as reflection of American society today. Open to all class standings. (Alt. years)

AMST 350.title: Culture and the Arts in America
AMST 350.subject: AMST
AMST 350.description: Study of the role of the arts in American society and diverse cultural practices in historical and contemporary contexts.

AMST 352.title: Screening Asian Americans
AMST 352.subject: AMST
AMST 352.description: Survey of Asian and Asian American representations in American film and television from the silent era to the present, with an emphasis on Orientalism and multiculturalism, as well as performance and spectatorship. ACM majors:

AMST 353.title: Indigenous Lands and Waters
AMST 353.subject: AMST
AMST 353.description: Examines indigenous practices born of and located in Indigenous places. Analyzes how indigenous knowledge of place informs Indigenous cultural, linguistic, intellectual, and political survivance and sovereignty, and resistance.

AMST 354.title: American Travel Writing
AMST 354.subject: AMST
AMST 354.description: Survey examines the roles that travel writing plays in American identity- and nation-formation, from early colonial history to the present.

AMST 360.title: American Cinema
AMST 360.subject: AMST
AMST 360.description: Introductory history of American cinema from the silent to the digital era, with an emphasis on criticism, genre and style, as well as cultural and sociopolitical context.

AMST 365.title: American Empire
AMST 365.subject: AMST
AMST 365.description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations.

AMST 373.title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
AMST 373.subject: AMST
AMST 373.description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

AMST 383.title: American Studies Approach
AMST 383.subject: AMST
AMST 383.description: Materials and methods for the study of American life and thought.

AMST 401.title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
AMST 401.subject: AMST
AMST 401.description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.

AMST 405.title: Indigenous Literature and Film
AMST 405.subject: AMST
AMST 405.description: Interdisciplinary, comparative course examining native literary texts (novels, short fiction, poetry), films, etc. that address issues of representation and how native peoples actively resist colonial ideology.

AMST 410.title: Asian American Music Cultures
AMST 410.subject: AMST
AMST 410.description: An exploration of how Asian American music making is related to community formation, labor migration, and cultural sensibilities throughout the 20th century.

AMST 411.title: Japanese Americans: Research Topics
AMST 411.subject: AMST
AMST 411.description: Research and thematic seminar on Japanese American culture, issues, and history.

AMST 413.title: Regionalism: The South
AMST 413.subject: AMST
AMST 413.description: Definition of a Southern identity and its relation to the larger U.S. culture, using literary and polemical works of 19th- and 20th-century.

AMST 418.title: Hawai‘i’s Multiculturalism
AMST 418.subject: AMST
AMST 418.description: A multidisciplinary examination of the dynamics of the Hawaiian Islands’ racial and cultural diversity from the perspectives of historical trends, social processes, and contemporary political, social, and economic issues as they impact interracial relations.

AMST 420.title: American Ideas of Nature
AMST 420.subject: AMST
AMST 420.description: The natural world in American thought from Native Americans to modern ecologists.

AMST 423.title: History of American Architecture
AMST 423.subject: AMST
AMST 423.description: History of American architecture in terms of style, techniques, and symbolic meaning.

AMST 425.title: American Environmental History
AMST 425.subject: AMST
AMST 425.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

AMST 431.title: History of American Workers
AMST 431.subject: AMST
AMST 431.description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

AMST 432.title: Slavery and Freedom
AMST 432.subject: AMST
AMST 432.description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

AMST 433.title: Islands, Empires, and the Arts
AMST 433.subject: AMST
AMST 433.description: Histories of colonialism, neocolonialism, and cultures of resistance in literature, film, and arts of the Caribbean and American diaspora. Role of arts in political dissent; historical memory; nation building; construction of race, class, gender.

AMST 434.title: Politics in Hawai‘i
AMST 434.subject: AMST
AMST 434.description: Discussion of modern politics against the background of recent history and major contemporary issues.

AMST 435.title: History of Crime and Punishment
AMST 435.subject: AMST
AMST 435.description: History of American crime and punishment from 18th century to the present. Topics: changing crime patterns, evolving punishment methods, penal reform movements, convict resistance, growth of prison industrial complex, racism, class, and gender.

AMST 436.title: Gender, Justice and Law
AMST 436.subject: AMST
AMST 436.description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.
AMST 436.prereq_raw: one of WS 151, WS 175, WS 176, WS 202, WS 360, WS 381, or consent

AMST 437.title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/ masculine/gender nonconforming/sexual)
AMST 437.subject: AMST
AMST 437.description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration.

AMST 438.title: Women and Globalization in Asia
AMST 438.subject: AMST
AMST 438.description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
AMST 438.prereq_raw: one of 310, 316, 318, 373, 455, POLS 339, WS 360, WS 361, WS 439; or consent

AMST 440.title: Race and Racism in America
AMST 440.subject: AMST
AMST 440.description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

AMST 442.title: Social Movements
AMST 442.subject: AMST
AMST 442.description: Examination of mass mobilization in U.S. history from the Revolution forward, including abolitionism, feminism, civil rights, labor, and more. Concludes with analysis of various community organizing efforts today.

AMST 445.title: Racism, American Culture and Film/ Media
AMST 445.subject: AMST
AMST 445.description: An exploration of the critique of racial ideologies in American film. The course also examines how aggrieved communities develop cultural sensibilities, aesthetic choices and politicized identities through film, video and media work.

AMST 446.title: Gender in Action Cinema
AMST 446.subject: AMST
AMST 446.description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

AMST 450.title: Victims, Virtue, and Violence
AMST 450.subject: AMST
AMST 450.description: Examination of the history and significance of melodrama as a dominant mode of American cultural production from the early republic to the present, with a focus on issues of race, gender, and national identity.

AMST 451.title: Popular Culture
AMST 451.subject: AMST
AMST 451.description: Major themes, modes, and media of popular or mass culture in the U.S.; emphasis on cultural trends and social implications.

AMST 452.title: The ’20s and ’30s
AMST 452.subject: AMST
AMST 452.description: Novelists, painters, poets, jazz musicians as examples of culture of the 1920s and 1930s in America.

AMST 453.title: Culture, Society, and Literature
AMST 453.subject: AMST
AMST 453.description: Literary and non-fictive exploration of the intellectual and moral response of Americans to institutions and culture of 20th-century marketplace economy.

AMST 454.title: Fashioning America
AMST 454.subject: AMST
AMST 454.description: Examines linkages between American identity, representation, labor and capital through fashion theory, clothing discourses and other practices of textile production over history.

AMST 455.title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
AMST 455.subject: AMST
AMST 455.description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

AMST 457.title: Museum Interpretations
AMST 457.subject: AMST
AMST 457.description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge.

AMST 458.title: Film in American Culture
AMST 458.subject: AMST
AMST 458.description: Comprehensive survey of varieties of film experience from historical and contemporary points of view.

AMST 459.title: Sports in America
AMST 459.subject: AMST
AMST 459.description: Sports as reflected in literature, films, and TV.

AMST 460.title: Early 20th Century American Art
AMST 460.subject: AMST
AMST 460.description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

AMST 461.title: America’s World Role
AMST 461.subject: AMST
AMST 461.description: Examination of America’s role in modern world affairs, against the background of history, perceptions, and values.

AMST 464.title: America and Africa
AMST 464.subject: AMST
AMST 464.description: American attitudes toward Africa, as well as how Africa has functioned within the dynamics of American culture and history.

AMST 465.title: American Experience in Asia
AMST 465.subject: AMST
AMST 465.description: Comparison of American experiences in Japan, China, and Southeast Asia within historical and perceptual framework.

AMST 469.title: Religion, Sex, and Gender in the U.S.
AMST 469.subject: AMST
AMST 469.description: Examines religious and ethical conflicts about sexuality and gender nonconformity in contemporary America. Students gain knowledge, practical wisdom, and communication skills to negotiate moral disagreement in a pluralistic society.

AMST 474.title: Preservation: Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific
AMST 474.subject: AMST
AMST 474.description: Lectures and discussions on historic preservation issues in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific. Emphasis on indigenous and national expressions.

AMST 475.title: Documentation of Historic Architecture
AMST 475.subject: AMST
AMST 475.description: Study and documentation of existing buildings, structures, sites of historic and/or cultural significance, including field measurements and drawings, historical research, photo documentation, and preparation of archival drawings to be deposited in the Library of Congress. Documentation conducted according to standards of the Historic American Buildings Survey/ Historic American Engineering Record (HABS/ HAER).
AMST 475.restrictions_raw: AMST, ARCH, and HIS majors only.

AMST 483.title: Elements of Research
AMST 483.subject: AMST
AMST 483.description: Required research seminar in American Studies in preparation for the senior capstone project.

AMST 484.title: Senior Capstone Project
AMST 484.subject: AMST
AMST 484.description: Capstone course for American studies students to undertake a major research-based project.

AMST 489.title: World Maritime History
AMST 489.subject: AMST
AMST 489.description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

AMST 499.title: Readings in American Studies
AMST 499.subject: AMST
AMST 499.description: Directed readings and research for majors.

AMST 600.title: Approaches to American Studies
AMST 600.subject: AMST
AMST 600.description: Introductory survey of methodological issues underlying research in American studies.

AMST 603.title: Advanced Research and Professional Development
AMST 603.subject: AMST
AMST 603.description: Prepares advanced graduate students to present original research findings to colleagues, write for peer review, design undergraduate classes in their areas of expertise, and participate actively in their fields. Graduate students only.
AMST 603.prereq_raw: (600 and 601) with a minimum grade of B-

AMST 610.title: Early America
AMST 610.subject: AMST
AMST 610.description: Interdisciplinary approach to understanding early American culture and history.

AMST 611.title: Asian America
AMST 611.subject: AMST
AMST 611.description: The Asian American experience from an interdisciplinary and humanities perspective. Asian American history, literature, media, and theater arts. Comparative study of Hawai‘i and the Continental U.S.

AMST 612.title: Women in American Culture
AMST 612.subject: AMST
AMST 612.description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

AMST 614.title: Advanced Topics: American West
AMST 614.subject: AMST
AMST 614.description: Examination of the U.S. colonization of the American West. Topics include: European-indigenous relations, migration and labor, regional literature, frontier ideology, ethnic conflict, and new community formation.

AMST 615.title: Performance, Culture, and Theory
AMST 615.subject: AMST
AMST 615.description: Survey of major critical works in fields of performing arts and public culture (e.g., dance, theater, music, commemoration). Topics include: theoretical application for the discipline of American studies, and the impact of social movements and labor migration on the performing arts.

AMST 616.title: Gender and the African Diaspora in the Americas
AMST 616.subject: AMST
AMST 616.description: Explores the impact of the African Diaspora on the cultures and histories of the Americas through interdisciplinary and feminist scholarship and cultural sources including fiction, foodways, film, poetry, religion, music, and dance. Graduate standing only.

AMST 617.title: Social and Cultural Diversity in America
AMST 617.subject: AMST
AMST 617.description: Examination of selected subcultures in America.

AMST 618.title: American Sexualities
AMST 618.subject: AMST
AMST 618.description: Aspects of sexual identity within the context of American culture.

AMST 619.title: Slavery and the Modern Memory
AMST 619.subject: AMST
AMST 619.description: Exploration of contemporary resonances of slavery in the Americas through literature, historical scholarship, memory and trauma studies, and the visual and performing arts. Graduate students only.

AMST 620.title: Indigenous Identity
AMST 620.subject: AMST
AMST 620.description: Interdisciplinary and comparative focus on how Indigenous identity is constructed, negotiated, asserted, ascribed, and deconstructed within and without Indigenous communities with attention to the U.S. Graduate students only.

AMST 623.title: American Architecture
AMST 623.subject: AMST
AMST 623.description: Cultural analysis of the evolution of American architecture from the Colonial period to the present involving sociopolitical and economic, as well as aesthetic, considerations.

AMST 624.title: Wilderness in America
AMST 624.subject: AMST
AMST 624.description: American wilderness as both physical setting and social construction.

AMST 625.title: Material Culture
AMST 625.subject: AMST
AMST 625.description: Physical artifacts considered as documents of American cultural and regional development.

AMST 626.title: Environment and Society
AMST 626.subject: AMST
AMST 626.description: Technological development in cultural perspective; its relation to the American environment, science, capitalism, public policy, and values.

AMST 632.title: Mass Media
AMST 632.subject: AMST
AMST 632.description: Appraisal of major media of communications in American society with attention to political, educational, cultural, and ethical implications.

AMST 634.title: Technologies of War and Media
AMST 634.subject: AMST
AMST 634.description: Critical examination of the relationship between war and media with particular attention to the overlapping histories of technologies of perception and destruction in the modern era and to the military-entertainment complex today. Graduate students only or consent.

AMST 635.title: Public History and Commemoration
AMST 635.subject: AMST
AMST 635.description: Approaches to public presentations of history and examination of various ways in which historic memory is constructed in sites such as museums, memorials, and theme parks.

AMST 638.title: American Punishment
AMST 638.subject: AMST
AMST 638.description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prisonindustrial complex.

AMST 640.title: Writing for Publication
AMST 640.subject: AMST
AMST 640.description: Advanced seminar designed to convert graduate research projects into publishable scholarly articles.

AMST 643.title: Revolutions and Social Movements
AMST 643.subject: AMST
AMST 643.description: Examines the role of social movements in transforming American society and culture.

AMST 645.title: Historic Preservation
AMST 645.subject: AMST
AMST 645.description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only)

AMST 646.title: Advanced Topics: Social/Cultural/ Intellectual
AMST 646.subject: AMST
AMST 646.description: Readings and research on American social and intellectual history.

AMST 647.title: Advanced Topics: Business/Labor/ Technology
AMST 647.subject: AMST
AMST 647.description: Readings and research on American business, labor, and technological history.

AMST 649.title: American Intellectual Traditions
AMST 649.subject: AMST
AMST 649.description: Examination of intellectual figures and movements in American history.

AMST 650.title: Field Mastery
AMST 650.subject: AMST
AMST 650.description: Prepares students to achieve specialization in an American Studies-related academic field. Graduate students only.

AMST 656.title: Film in America
AMST 656.subject: AMST
AMST 656.description: Examination of various roles of motion picture film in America with particular respect to art form, cultural artifact, document, and myth.

AMST 659.title: Arts in America: Modern to PostModern
AMST 659.subject: AMST
AMST 659.description: Survey of the literature of the field.

AMST 664.title: Transpacific Studies
AMST 664.subject: AMST
AMST 664.description: Critical analysis of regional formation in and across the Pacific and the role of the U.S. therein; migrations within and across the Pacific; political, military, economic, cultural, and environmental dynamics of transpacific exchanges.

AMST 668.title: Globalization and Transnationalism
AMST 668.subject: AMST
AMST 668.description: Examines the socioeconomic and cultural meanings of globalization and transnationalism. Emphasis on how the deployment and flows of power beyond the nation-state have an impact on regional, national, and/ or local communities and cultures.

AMST 669.title: Advanced Topics: America and the World
AMST 669.subject: AMST
AMST 669.description: Historical and contemporary issues in America’s global relationships.

AMST 670.title: Comparative Methods in American Studies
AMST 670.subject: AMST
AMST 670.description: Examines approaches to American studies that use comparison as a primary method. Comparison of histories, institutions, of phenomena between the U.S. and another country as well as among communities in the U.S. Graduate standing only.

AMST 671.title: Indigenous Curation and Museums: Practice Meets Theory
AMST 671.subject: AMST
AMST 671.description: Seminar explores the history, evolution, and contemporary movement towards indigenous curation within museums, emphasis on the Americas and Oceania, as shaped by colonialism, globalization, multiculturalism, selfdetermination, and nationalism.

AMST 672.title: 20th Century U.S. Literature
AMST 672.subject: AMST
AMST 672.description: Selected works of 20th-century literature as cultural documents.

AMST 673.title: African American Literature
AMST 673.subject: AMST
AMST 673.description: Cultural and social imagination of blacks and whites as revealed in literature, poetry, and drama.

AMST 674.title: Preservation Field Seminar
AMST 674.subject: AMST
AMST 674.description: Provides participants with basic knowledge of the field of historic preservation as well as the fundamental knowledge of how to document, conserve, and preserve both tangible and intangible cultural properties. (Summer only

AMST 675.title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
AMST 675.subject: AMST
AMST 675.description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

AMST 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
AMST 676.subject: AMST
AMST 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.

AMST 677.title: Historic Preservation Planning
AMST 677.subject: AMST
AMST 677.description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

AMST 679.title: Elements of Style
AMST 679.subject: AMST
AMST 679.description: The manifestations, visual characteristics, and social/cultural meaning of “style” in American architecture and decorative arts from the early settlement period through the present.

AMST 680.title: Historic Building Technology
AMST 680.subject: AMST
AMST 680.description: History of buildings, building technologies, materials, and finishes, including construction techniques and methods of investigating older buildings. Emphasis on North American building practices c.1600–c.1960.

AMST 681.title: Vernacular Architecture
AMST 681.subject: AMST
AMST 681.description: Methods and approaches in the study of vernacular architecture, cultural landscapes, and material culture, with an emphasis on traditions and innovations in the Americas.

AMST 683.title: Museums: Theory, History, Practice
AMST 683.subject: AMST
AMST 683.description: History and theory of museums and related institutions (art galleries, historic houses, zoos, parks). Relationship between museums, collections, and communities. Introduction to governance, planning, legal, and ethical concerns.

AMST 684.title: Museums and Collections
AMST 684.subject: AMST
AMST 684.description: Work of museums and professionals (registrars, collections managers, conservators, curators and others) in the care of collections, interpretive studies of museum displays and collections and field trips.

AMST 685.title: Museums and Education
AMST 685.subject: AMST
AMST 685.description: Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects.

AMST 686.title: Museum Studies Practicum
AMST 686.subject: AMST
AMST 686.description: Applies coursework in museum studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Museum studies certificate students only.

AMST 688.title: Indigenous Studies Practicum
AMST 688.subject: AMST
AMST 688.description: Applies course work in Indigenous studies to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Graduate students only.

AMST 690.title: Research Seminar
AMST 690.subject: AMST
AMST 690.description: Themes, problems, and issues not addressed in other American studies graduate courses; emphasis upon research methods.

AMST 695.title: Historic Preservation Practicum
AMST 695.subject: AMST
AMST 695.description: Applies course work in historic preservation to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and University faculty. Historic preservation certificate students only.

ART 101.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
ART 101.subject: ART
ART 101.description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

ART 101A.title: Introduction to the Visual Arts
ART 101A.subject: ART
ART 101A.description: Nature of the world’s visual arts and their influences on personal expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and studio practice. (Not for art majors or minors)

ART 103.title: Introduction to Fiber Arts
ART 103.subject: ART
ART 103.description: Broad-based studio exploration of materials, techniques, concepts in contemporary fiber art.
