May include surface patterning/manipulation, papermaking, woven, other 2D/3D hand construction techniques. Focus on creative-problem solving, experimentation in a cooperative studio setting.

ART 104.title: Introduction to Printmaking
ART 104.subject: ART
ART 104.description: Foundation explorations in the processes of relief, intaglio, and stencil printmaking. Direct workshop studio experience in the basic techniques and concepts of wood cut, linoleum cut, drypoint, monotype, and basic stencil processes.

ART 107.title: Introduction to Photography
ART 107.subject: ART
ART 107.description: Studio/ lecture examining the major themes and issues in historical and current photographical production. Direct black and white darkroom experience. Students must have 35mm film-based camera with adjustable shutter speed, aperture, and light meter.

ART 113.title: Introduction to Drawing
ART 113.subject: ART
ART 113.description: Descriptive, expressive, and formal aspects of visual language through drawing practice.

ART 116.title: Introduction to Three-Dimensional Composition
ART 116.subject: ART
ART 116.description: Basic concepts, elements, and principles of art.

ART 123.title: Introduction to Painting
ART 123.subject: ART
ART 123.description: Theory and practice of painting; material and technical procedures. A standalone course aimed at non-majors. ART majors should start with ART 223 after taking ART 113.

ART 130.title: Introduction to Glass
ART 130.subject: ART
ART 130.description: Basic techniques of working with cold and molten glass. Theory of glass studio operation and introduction to glass theory.

ART 175.title: Survey of Global Art I
ART 175.subject: ART
ART 175.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 175A.title: Survey of Global Art I
ART 175A.subject: ART
ART 175A.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from prehistory to the 15th century. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 176.title: Survey of Global Art II
ART 176.subject: ART
ART 176.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 176A.title: Survey of Global Art II
ART 176A.subject: ART
ART 176A.description: Art produced in Asia, Africa, Native America, Europe, and the Pacific Islands, from the 15th century to the present. Religious and philosophical ideas expressed in architecture, painting, prints, sculpture, applied art, body art, and textiles.

ART 189.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Art
ART 189.subject: ART
ART 189.description: Integrated beginning studio art course, which offers students the opportunity to understand and express Hawaiian cultural perspectives through contemporary art practice.

ART 201.title: Introduction to Electronic Arts
ART 201.subject: ART
ART 201.description: Theory and practice course investigating language common to all arts activity particularly as related to the contemporary arts.
ART 201.prereq_raw: any studio art course; or consent

ART 202.title: Introduction to Digital Imaging
ART 202.subject: ART
ART 202.description: Combined theory and practice examining major techniques, concepts, and aesthetics in contemporary digital image production. Direct studio experience in essential software, printing techniques and hardware necessary in producing the gallery quality inkjet print.

ART 207.title: Intermediate Photo: Black and White
ART 207.subject: ART
ART 207.description: Black and white photography emphasizing communication and self-expression. Lectures, demonstrations, and projects. Student must supply camera and material.

ART 213.title: Intermediate Drawing
ART 213.subject: ART
ART 213.description: Extension of the observational foundation established in 113 to address contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches to drawing.

ART 214.title: Introduction to Life Drawing
ART 214.subject: ART
ART 214.description: Investigations of the figure concerning anatomical construction, light, space, diagramatic analysis, and thematic content.

ART 215.title: Intaglio Printmaking
ART 215.subject: ART
ART 215.description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from metal plates including etching, engraving, aquatint, and drypoint.

ART 217.title: Screenprinting
ART 217.subject: ART
ART 217.description: Studio practice in screenprinting on paper. Copy camera and basic photo-stencil techniques introduced.

ART 218.title: Relief Printmaking
ART 218.subject: ART
ART 218.description: Studio practice in the techniques and concepts of woodblock, linoleum cut, monotype, and calligraph printmaking. Emphasis on both traditional and contemporary practices.

ART 223.title: Approaches to Painting
ART 223.subject: ART
ART 223.description: Theory and practice of painting; contemporary conceptual and expressive approaches.

ART 225.title: Painting/Water-Based Media
ART 225.subject: ART
ART 225.description: An introduction to water-based media. Traditional transparent color, gouache and acrylics.

ART 230.title: Glass Casting: Sand and Metal Molds
ART 230.subject: ART
ART 230.description: Expressive explorations in glass casting with wet sand, bonded sand, and metal molds.

ART 234.title: Cold Glass Fabrication
ART 234.subject: ART
ART 234.description: Expressive explorations using architectural sheet glass. Development of 2D and 3D forms using engraving, sandblasting, and cold joinery techniques.

ART 237.title: Woven Structures
ART 237.subject: ART
ART 237.description: Structured studio exploration of creative potential of working with threads under tension. In-depth introduction to a variety of traditional and experimental processes/ materials. Tradition of pattern weaving to experimental woven forms.

ART 238.title: Fiber Forms
ART 238.subject: ART
ART 238.description: In-depth studio exploration of non-loom fiber techniques for creating/ manipulating 2D and 3D forms. Emphasis on concept development, skill mastery, innovative application of materials/techniques. May include felting, knotting, netting, piecing, coiling, found object/sewn constructions, papermaking.

ART 242.title: Introduction to Ceramics
ART 242.subject: ART
ART 242.description: Three-dimensional concepts in clay; hand-building and wheel-throwing techniques. Projects, lectures, and demonstrations.

ART 254.title: Sculpture—Metal Casting
ART 254.subject: ART
ART 254.description: Metal casting and development of associated practices and concepts.

ART 255.title: Sculpture—Carving, Mixed Media
ART 255.subject: ART
ART 255.description: Investigations of traditional and contemporary carving concepts and methods.

ART 265.title: Design: Studio I
ART 265.subject: ART
ART 265.description: Introduction to graphic design. Explorations of rhetorical and semiotic structures and their relationship to visual form and content. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

ART 265L.title: Design: Studio I Lab
ART 265L.subject: ART
ART 265L.description: Beginning instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including hardware, software, and lab networking as it relates to graphic design production. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

ART 266.title: Design: Typography I
ART 266.subject: ART
ART 266.description: Introduction to typography. Exploration of letterform and word compositions in the context of single-page structures. ART 176 is recommended as a prerequisite.

ART 302.title: Introduction to Contemporary Critical Theory
ART 302.subject: ART
ART 302.description: Examination of the significant themes and issues in contemporary critical theory as they relate to the production and reception of art.

ART 303.title: Kiln-Formed Glass
ART 303.subject: ART
ART 303.description: Expressive explorations in the use of kiln-formed, fusible-sheet glasses and enameling on glass.

ART 304.title: Digital Imaging: Professional Printing
ART 304.subject: ART
ART 304.description: Combined theory and practice. Investigates industry standard methods for archival pigment printing. Techniques include: device calibration and profiling, black and white, coating techniques, mounting and adhesive techniques, professional portfolio presentation.

ART 305.title: Digital Imaging: Alternative Printing
ART 305.subject: ART
ART 305.description: Combined theory and practice. Merges digital printing, mark-making, photography, and traditional printmaking. Includes image transfers, lifts, precoating techniques, as well as printing on alternative substrates such as watercolor papers, metals, and cloth.

ART 306.title: Lost Wax Glass Casting
ART 306.subject: ART
ART 306.description: Glass kiln casting techniques, lost wax fuse casting, pâte de verre.

ART 307.title: Advanced Lighting
ART 307.subject: ART
ART 307.description: Emphasis on aesthetic and critical analysis. Techniques covered include continuous light, strobe and handheld flash.
ART 307.prereq_raw: 202 and 207 with a minimum grade of B

ART 313.title: Advanced Drawing
ART 313.subject: ART
ART 313.description: Studio practice in drawing emphasizing contemporary developments in art.

ART 314.title: Intermediate Life Drawing
ART 314.subject: ART
ART 314.description: Further investigations of the figure concerning anatomical and diagramatic construction, light, space, and thematic content.

ART 315.title: Experimental Art and Animation
ART 315.subject: ART
ART 315.description: Provides students an opportunity to experiment with new mediums while collaborating with artists from different backgrounds, such as art, theatre, dance, film, and animation.
ART 315.prereq_raw: 113 or ACM 216 (or concurrent) or THEA 353 (or concurrent) or THEA 356 (or concurrent), or consent
ART 315.restrictions_raw: ACM, ART, THEA, DNCE majors only.

ART 316.title: Lithography
ART 316.subject: ART
ART 316.description: Studio practice in concepts and techniques of making prints from lithographic limestone and plates.
ART 316.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B) 215 or 217 or 218

ART 318.title: Intermediate Printmaking
ART 318.subject: ART
ART 318.description: Intermediate level specialization in either intaglio, lithography, screenprinting, or relief printmaking. Concentration on the techniques and formats of color printing and sequential image development.
ART 318.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B) two of 215, 217, 218, or 316

ART 322.title: Advanced Color
ART 322.subject: ART
ART 322.description: Theory and application of color as related to studio practice.

ART 323.title: Advanced Painting I
ART 323.subject: ART
ART 323.description: Studio practice in painting emphasizing contemporary developments in art.

ART 324.title: Painting from Life
ART 324.subject: ART
ART 324.description: Painting from the model; a survey of the figurative tradition.

ART 330.title: Advanced Glass
ART 330.subject: ART
ART 330.description: Glass as an expressive medium. Individual problems; construction of studio equipment. Readings and discussions of contemporary glass issues.

ART 335.title: Papermaking
ART 335.subject: ART
ART 335.description: Studio emphasis on handmade papermaking techniques, conceptual exploration in two and three dimensions.
ART 335.prereq_raw: one fiber course or one of 104, 113, 116; or consent

ART 336.title: Wearable Art—Body and Material
ART 336.subject: ART
ART 336.description: Studio exploration of clothing as art form and the body as living armature and performance. Emphasis on development of concept, skill, collaborative and individual voice through material investigation, research, discussions, lectures, individual and group projects.
ART 336.prereq_raw: one 200-level fiber course, or 116 and one 200-level studio course; or consent

ART 337.title: Fiber Sculpture—Endurance and Impermanence
ART 337.subject: ART
ART 337.description: Studio exploration in contemporary dimensional fiber using both conventional and non-conventional materials and processes. Emphasis on concept development, sensitivity to the evocative potential of materials, context, surface treatment and its relationship to concept and structure.
ART 337.prereq_raw: one 200 level fiber course or 116 and one 200 level studio course; or consent

ART 339.title: Designing Surface
ART 339.subject: ART
ART 339.description: In-depth studio exploration of fiber techniques for patterning and manipulating cloth and other related experimental surfaces. Engages conceptual exploration through experimentation with traditional fiber patterning techniques such as dyeing, resisting, direct printing, embellishment drawing with thread and piercing. Group and individual projects.

ART 343.title: Ceramics—Sculpture
ART 343.subject: ART
ART 343.description: Sculptural concepts and techniques specifically related to the medium of clay; advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques.

ART 344.title: Ceramics—Vessels
ART 344.subject: ART
ART 344.description: Exploration of the ceramic vessel as function, metaphor, and expression. Advanced hand-building, throwing, glazing, and firing techniques.

ART 345.title: Ceramics—Low Temperature
ART 345.subject: ART
ART 345.description: Form and surface problems related to earthenware clay bodies and low-temperature glazes; mold-making for ceramics.

ART 346.title: History of Western Ceramics
ART 346.subject: ART
ART 346.description: Western ceramics history from chronological, developmental, contextual, and theoretical standpoints; influence of Asian ceramics.

ART 347.title: Technical Ceramics
ART 347.subject: ART
ART 347.description: Clay body development, glaze development, empirical and calculation methods. Emphasis on glaze maturity, surface, and color.
ART 347.prereq_raw: 242, and one of 343, 344, or 345; or consent

ART 351.title: Sculpture—Figure Modeling
ART 351.subject: ART
ART 351.description: Figure modeling, mold making, and casting.

ART 352.title: Kinetic Sculpture
ART 352.subject: ART
ART 352.description: The design and construction of objects incorporating movement as an integral element of their content.

ART 356.title: Sculpture—Metal Fabrication
ART 356.subject: ART
ART 356.description: Metal fabrication and development of associated practices, concepts, and historical references.

ART 357.title: Sculpture—Small-Scale
ART 357.subject: ART
ART 357.description: Fabrication and casting of forms on a small scale such as jewelry. The development of related practices, concepts, and historical references.

ART 358.title: Utilitarian Sculpture
ART 358.subject: ART
ART 358.description: The design and construction of objects intended for use/interaction. Emphasis on wood and synthetic materials.

ART 359.title: Sculpture—Contemporary
ART 359.subject: ART
ART 359.description: Contextualization of late 20th/early 21st century sculptural practice, including stylistic and theoretical frameworks, with references to influences of various historical Western and Asian traditions and applying this knowledge in the creation of sculpture.

ART 360.title: Exhibition Design and Gallery Management
ART 360.subject: ART
ART 360.description: Design theory and techniques for presentation of artworks and mounting exhibitions.

ART 361.title: Art Museums and Preservation Practices
ART 361.subject: ART
ART 361.description: Introduction to collections management and preservation techniques, incorporating both theoretical and practical approaches, and including hands-on work with the collections of the John Young Museum.

ART 365.title: Design: Studio II
ART 365.subject: ART
ART 365.description: Intermediate graphic design. Emphasis on communication problems involving process and analysis. Introduction to modernist precedents and information theory.

ART 365L.title: Design: Studio II Lab
ART 365L.subject: ART
ART 365L.description: Intermediate instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, software, and peripheral devices, including intermediate layout. Introduction to graphic design industry standard multi-media and web design programs.

ART 366.title: Design: Typography II
ART 366.subject: ART
ART 366.description: Intermediate typographic design, exploration of word and text composition in the context of multiple-page structures.

ART 371.title: Medieval Art
ART 371.subject: ART
ART 371.description: Arts of Europe from early Christian era to Renaissance.

ART 373.title: Art of Greece and Rome
ART 373.subject: ART
ART 373.description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome.

ART 374.title: Art of the 19th Century
ART 374.subject: ART
ART 374.description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe.

ART 380.title: Early Art of Japan
ART 380.subject: ART
ART 380.description: Major developments, prehistoric through Kamakura; architecture, painting, sculpture.

ART 381.title: Later Art of Japan
ART 381.subject: ART
ART 381.description: Major developments, Muromachi to modern period; painting, sculpture, architecture.

ART 382.title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
ART 382.subject: ART
ART 382.description: Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups.

ART 384.title: Art of Korea
ART 384.subject: ART
ART 384.description: Ceramics, sculpture, painting, and architecture; neolithic through Yi periods.

ART 385.title: Art and Culture of Early China
ART 385.subject: ART
ART 385.description: A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on jade, bronze, secular and religious sculptures, and paintings from prehistory to the 9th century.

ART 386.title: Art and Culture of Late China
ART 386.subject: ART
ART 386.description: A culturally oriented study of Chinese visual arts; emphasis on the rise of literati painting and theory individualism in art and theory, garden, and architecture, and the Chinese pursuit of modernity and post-modernity in art.

ART 387.title: Sculpture of China
ART 387.subject: ART
ART 387.description: Thematic introduction to sculpture in China from the Neolithic period through the present day.

ART 390.title: Art of Africa, Pacific, North America
ART 390.subject: ART
ART 390.description: Contextual study of art from selected areas in Africa, the Pacific, and North America.

ART 393.title: Art of India and South Asia
ART 393.subject: ART
ART 393.description: Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Art of India and South Asia.

ART 395.title: Art Historical Methodology
ART 395.subject: ART
ART 395.description: Introduction to the methods and approaches of art history. Students will develop skills in perception and comprehension of visual art forms, and a critical understanding of the methods used by art historians to analyze them.

ART 399.title: Directed Work
ART 399.subject: ART
ART 399.description: Individual projects; tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 3 for BA, 6 for BFA.
ART 399.prereq_raw: two 200-level or above art courses in area of directed work, as well as consent of instructor and department associate chair

children.text: above art courses in area of directed work, as well as consent of instructor

ART 401.title: Advanced Electronic Arts Studio
ART 401.subject: ART
ART 401.description: Tutorial studio that encourages exploration in combined and new media through independent work within an environment of theoretical and critical discourse.

ART 405.title: Professional Practice in the Arts: Creative, Career, and Leadership
ART 405.subject: ART
ART 405.description: Examination of the role of the artist in society, the artist as self, as community member, as teacher. Professional Practice skills in the arts; planning, grantsmanship, fundraising, budgeting, marketing, outreach, and media relations. Senior standing or graduate students only.

ART 409.title: Graduation Portfolio (BA)
ART 409.subject: ART
ART 409.description: Required graduation portfolio for BA Art History and Art Studio students. BA ART majors only. Undergraduates only. To be taken during the semester prior to expected graduation.

ART 410.title: BFA Capstone Seminar/Studio
ART 410.subject: ART
ART 410.description: In conjunction with the production of art for the BFA annual exhibition, this seminar will examine, critique, and evaluate the student’s art within the context of contemporary art, professional practices, exhibition theory, and integrate theoretical and practical issues in the life of an artist.

ART 436.title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
ART 436.subject: ART
ART 436.description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making.
ART 436.prereq_raw: 113 and 116 and one 200-level or above fiber course, and consent

ART 439.title: Installation/Performance–Material in Context
ART 439.subject: ART
ART 439.description: Studio investigation of the definition/ transformation of space through artist intervention. Emphasis on the evocative potential of materials in context (physical, social, political, psychological) as well as experiments in non-object based interventions.
ART 439.prereq_raw: two 200-level or above studio courses, or consent

ART 460.title: Early 20th Century American Art
ART 460.subject: ART
ART 460.description: American art in the first half of the 20th century and its impact on American culture. Junior standing or higher.

ART 465.title: Design: Studio III
ART 465.subject: ART
ART 465.description: Advanced graphic design. Emphasis on postmodernist theory, context, audience, and alternative media.

ART 465L.title: Design: Studio III Lab
ART 465L.subject: ART
ART 465L.description: Advanced instruction in the Macintosh computer environment, including software and peripheral devices. Instruction in image manipulation and editing still video images for the web, CD, DVD, and portable interface devices.

ART 466.title: Design: Typography III
ART 466.subject: ART
ART 466.description: Advanced typographic design. Exploration of 2D, 3D, electronic, and intermedia. Emphasis on contemporary typographic models.

ART 467.title: Design: Production Techniques
ART 467.subject: ART
ART 467.description: Advanced techniques in design production from printed and digital media.

ART 467L.title: Design: Production Techniques Lab
ART 467L.subject: ART
ART 467L.description: Advanced study of digital media for graphic designers. Focuses on skills and specific technical information to complement material covered in 467.

ART 469.title: Design: Advanced Studio
ART 469.subject: ART
ART 469.description: Individual and team investigations of complex problems in graphic design. Emphasis on projects with actual clients (when available) and/or independent investigations addressing advanced and current questions in the graphic design field.
ART 469.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B- for (465 and 466) and credit for 465L

ART 471.title: Baroque and Rococo Art
ART 471.subject: ART
ART 471.description: Architecture, sculpture, and painting of Europe in the Baroque and Rococo periods.

ART 473.title: Art of the First Half of 20th Century
ART 473.subject: ART
ART 473.description: Development of modern art in Europe 1900–1939.

ART 476.title: Art of Tribal Africa
ART 476.subject: ART
ART 476.description: Visual form and function of arts in cultural context. Mali, Burkina Faso, Ivory Coast, Liberia, Guinea, Nigeria, Ghana, Cameroon, Congo, Zaire.

ART 477.title: Art of Indonesia
ART 477.subject: ART
ART 477.description: Architecture, sculpture, and textile traditions of indigenous Indonesia in cultural context.

ART 478.title: Topics in Contemporary Art
ART 478.subject: ART
ART 478.description: Thematic approaches to contemporary art and visual culture. Course themes may include identity, local/global issues, and appropriation.

ART 479.title: Art of Hawai‘i
ART 479.subject: ART
ART 479.description: Stylistic and aesthetic characteristics of art of ancient Hawai‘i; relationship to art from other parts of Polynesia.

ART 481.title: Museum Interpretations
ART 481.subject: ART
ART 481.description: Studies the interpretive strategies and methods used by museums to communicate with visitors in museums, art galleries, historic sites, parks, and related places. Considers how interpretations contribute to cultural knowledge.

ART 483.title: Applied Art of Japan
ART 483.subject: ART
ART 483.description: Ceramics, metalwork, lacquer, and textiles throughout Japanese history.

ART 484.title: Contemporary Art and Ecology
ART 484.subject: ART
ART 484.description: Explores the recent history of environmental and ecological art; provides a critical framework for the contemporary image politics of environmentalism, ecology, sustainability, and climate change.

ART 485.title: Contemporary Art in Hawai‘i
ART 485.subject: ART
ART 485.description: History of contemporary art in Hawai‘i: the institutions, artists, critics, and historians that have shaped it. Strong focus on oral history of Hawai‘i artists.

ART 486.title: Traditional Chinese Painting
ART 486.subject: ART
ART 486.description: Stylistic and historic development of two-dimensional arts; painting and calligraphy from prehistory through 18th century.

ART 487.title: Modern and Contemporary Art of China
ART 487.subject: ART
ART 487.description: Introduction to the arts of China in the modern and contemporary periods, in all media and genres, from 1840 to the present.

ART 488.title: Genres of Japanese Cinema
ART 488.subject: ART
ART 488.description: History of Japanese cinema, including silent films, samurai films, monster films, and literary adaptations, analyzed through the lens of genre and genre theory.

ART 492.title: Hindu Visual Culture
ART 492.subject: ART
ART 492.description: Art and architecture of South Asia in historical and cultural context. Hindu visual culture.

ART 493.title: Art of Islam
ART 493.subject: ART
ART 493.description: Major developments in art and architecture.

ART 494.title: Photography: Critical Issues
ART 494.subject: ART
ART 494.description: Seminar on theoretical, ethical and aesthetic issues relating to the practice of photography, past and present.

ART 495.title: History of Modern Design
ART 495.subject: ART
ART 495.description: Major design movements in Europe and America from late 19th century to present; arts and crafts movement, art nouveau, modernist trends of the 20th century.

ART 496.title: Topics in the History of Cinema
ART 496.subject: ART
ART 496.description: Specific period or national style of cinema studied in its historical context.

ART 611.title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art
ART 611.subject: ART
ART 611.description: Selected topics in art. A critique-based course with emphasis on the development of critical analysis, artistic research, and practice.

ART 612.title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art II
ART 612.subject: ART
ART 612.description: Selected topics in art. Emphasis on the analysis of the systems by which art is conceived and the ability to define developing direction and related research.

ART 613.title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art III
ART 613.subject: ART
ART 613.description: Selected topics in art. Emphasis on the development of critical analysis and the understanding of one’s position relative to the contemporary art world.

ART 614.title: Graduate Studio Seminar in Art IV
ART 614.subject: ART
ART 614.description: Selected topics in art. Emphasis on the convergence of one’s studio practice and research, and the refinement necessary to the preparation for entrance into thesis.

ART 620.title: Methods in Contemporary Art
ART 620.subject: ART
ART 620.description: Examines processes of inquiry and experimentation within studio practice. Students explore a range of research methods as a way to challenge habitual methodologies and expand notions of art and art making.

ART 621.title: Materials in Contemporary Art
ART 621.subject: ART
ART 621.description: Explores the physical, historical, symbolic, and contextual capacity of materials, as well as the mutually constitutive roles of artist and materials within the creative process.

ART 630.title: Graduate Studio Teaching Practicum
ART 630.subject: ART
ART 630.description: Observation, analysis and participation in teaching a lower division course under the direction of an instructor in the student’s area of concentration.
ART 630.prereq_raw: 690, admitted to candidacy for MFA in art, and consent
