ART 670.title: Art Historical Methodology
ART 670.subject: ART
ART 670.description: An introduction to art historiography, analytical techniques, and research methods and materials.

ART 677.title: Art of Oceania
ART 677.subject: ART
ART 677.description: Arts from Polynesia, Melanesia, Micronesia explored in context of issues involving belief systems and cultural change.

ART 688.title: Topics in the Art of China
ART 688.subject: ART
ART 688.description: Research topics in the history of Chinese sculpture, ceramics, bronzes, jade, and textiles.

ART 690.title: Seminar in Contemporary Critical Theory
ART 690.subject: ART
ART 690.description: Research and discussion seminar supporting advanced critical theory in the context of contemporary art and other creative practice.

ART 691.title: Seminar in Global Contemporary Art
ART 691.subject: ART
ART 691.description: Selected topics in global contemporary art history.

ART 695.title: Seminar in Western Art History
ART 695.subject: ART
ART 695.description: Selected topics in European and American art history.

ART 699.title: Directed Work
ART 699.subject: ART
ART 699.description: Advanced individual projects; advanced tutorial. Maximum: 3 credit hours per semester; total 6 for MA Plan A, 9 for MA Plan B, MFA students must petition OGE for permission to apply toward degree requirement.
ART 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

ART 780.title: Seminar in Japanese Art
ART 780.subject: ART
ART 780.description: Selected topics in Japanese art history.

ART 791.title: Seminar in South/Southeast Asian Art History
ART 791.subject: ART
ART 791.description: Selected topics in South and/or Southeast Asian art and architectural history with an emphasis on Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

ART 792.title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
ART 792.subject: ART
ART 792.description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.

COMG 102.title: Everyday Communication with Numbers: A Survival Guide
COMG 102.subject: COMG
COMG 102.description: Understanding, communicating, and evaluating quantitative information in everyday contexts. Topics include describing and interpreting data, basic statistics, and evaluating the validity of results.

COMG 151.title: Personal and Public Speech
COMG 151.subject: COMG
COMG 151.description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

COMG 151A.title: Personal and Public Speech
COMG 151A.subject: COMG
COMG 151A.description: Develops communication skills necessary to function effectively in today’s society. Students will enhance their communication skills in one-on-one situations, public speaking, and small group situations. Ideal for new majors and non-majors.

COMG 170.title: Introduction to Nonverbal Communication
COMG 170.subject: COMG
COMG 170.description: Beginning course on the fundamental components of nonverbal communication. Aspects of body movements, facial expressions, eye behavior, physical appearance, voice, touch, space, smell, time, and environmental features will be examined in a lecture/discussion format. Extensive practice in skills.

COMG 181.title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
COMG 181.subject: COMG
COMG 181.description: Introduction to basic principles of interaction between two people. Emphasis is on enhancement of skills in a variety of interpersonal contexts.

COMG 185.title: Multicultural Communication Skills
COMG 185.subject: COMG
COMG 185.description: Expose students to practical skills needed for effective intercultural communication. Offer guidelines for improvement in diverse cultural settings such as business, education, counseling, and healthcare.

COMG 251.title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
COMG 251.subject: COMG
COMG 251.description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

COMG 251A.title: Principles of Effective Public Speaking
COMG 251A.subject: COMG
COMG 251A.description: Combined lecture/laboratory providing extensive practice in preparing and presenting effective public speeches with special emphasis on organization, outlining, audience analysis, analytical reasoning, and delivery skills.

COMG 290.title: Interviewing
COMG 290.subject: COMG
COMG 290.description: Principles and practice; training in informational, persuasive, employment, appraisal, and research interviewing.

COMG 301.title: Introduction to Communicological Theories
COMG 301.subject: COMG
COMG 301.description: Introduction to the theoretical perspectives that are the foundations of the communication discipline. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 302.title: Research Methods
COMG 302.subject: COMG
COMG 302.description: Introduction to methods of inquiry in the field of communication. Topics include research design and problem formulation, sampling, analytic and observational techniques, and data interpretation. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 321.title: Instructional Communication
COMG 321.subject: COMG
COMG 321.description: Analysis of and practice in using models of communication in the classroom. Extends application of oral communication skills to various instructional and teaching contexts. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

COMG 351.title: Professional Presentations
COMG 351.subject: COMG
COMG 351.description: Extends application of public speaking skills to professional contexts: group sales, press conferences, and corporate annual reports. Emphasis on organization, preparation, and delivery.

COMG 352.title: Group Decision-Making and Leadership
COMG 352.subject: COMG
COMG 352.description: Study of decision-making within the small group. Effects of organization, leadership, membership, and goals on achieving group purposes. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 353.title: Argumentation and Debate
COMG 353.subject: COMG
COMG 353.description: Adapting communication theory to forensic strategies for social action. Practice in formal argument. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits

COMG 361.title: Leadership and Organizational Communication
COMG 361.subject: COMG
COMG 361.description: Principles and practices of organizational communication and its relationship to networks, leadership, power, conflict, cultures, and other contemporary views of organizational work, change, and development. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 364.title: Persuasion
COMG 364.subject: COMG
COMG 364.description: Theories, concepts, strategies, and processes of persuasion and social influence in contemporary society. Focus on analyzing, developing, and resisting persuasive messages. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 371.title: Creating Understanding
COMG 371.subject: COMG
COMG 371.description: Introduction to theory and research on human communication, comprehension, creation of understanding. Discussion of codes and media, information and message processing theories. Topics include inference-making, implicature, natural language processing, and deception.

COMG 380.title: Family Communication
COMG 380.subject: COMG
COMG 380.description: Focuses on the role of interaction patterns (both constructive and destructive) in the evolution of family communications. The impact of family dynamics upon these interaction patterns is given equal attention. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 381.title: Interpersonal Relations
COMG 381.subject: COMG
COMG 381.description: Theory and research on the development, maintenance, and termination of interpersonal relationships. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 385.title: Culture and Communication
COMG 385.subject: COMG
COMG 385.description: Survey of major factors affecting interpersonal communication between members of different cultures. Emphasis upon interaction between U.S. and Asian-Pacific peoples. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 386.title: Special Topics in Culture and Communication
COMG 386.subject: COMG
COMG 386.description: Contemporary research and theory on intercultural communication. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 390.title: Interrogation and Interviewing
COMG 390.subject: COMG
COMG 390.description: Survey of theory and research on the communicative demands of obtaining reliable information from others. Restricted to students with 30 or more credits.

COMG 392.title: Evolution and Human Communication
COMG 392.subject: COMG
COMG 392.description: Analysis of the role of human communication in mate attraction, intrasexual competition, cooperation, family dynamics, and coalition formation; discussion on the biological function of language, laughter, yawning, and emotion expressions. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 395.title: Research on Communication Behavior
COMG 395.subject: COMG
COMG 395.description: Survey of research on communication behavior. Verbal and nonverbal data collection; analysis of research data. Students design and implement a research project.

COMG 399.title: Internship
COMG 399.subject: COMG
COMG 399.description: Analysis and application of communication knowledge and behaviors in organizational settings.

COMG 452.title: Intergroup Communication
COMG 452.subject: COMG
COMG 452.description: Surveys theory and research on communication between members of different social groups, highlighting how communication influences and is influenced by social identity. Applies concepts to intergenerational, health, family, educational, multilingual, and computer-mediated contexts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 454.title: Political Communication
COMG 454.subject: COMG
COMG 454.description: Survey of interpersonal and mass communication theories in the political context. Topics may include communication in public opinion processes, elections, debates, political campaigning and advertising. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 455.title: Conflict Management
COMG 455.subject: COMG
COMG 455.description: Examination of the theories, assumptions, practices, models, and techniques of managing interpersonal conflicts. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 464.title: Human Communication and Technology
COMG 464.subject: COMG
COMG 464.description: Analysis of evolving communicative exchanges in the Internet age including how people communicate with computer technology: focus on personal, interpersonal, and cultural effects associated with technology use.

COMG 465.title: Theories and Research in Strategic Communication
COMG 465.subject: COMG
COMG 465.description: An in-depth overview of theories related to strategic communication and scientific approaches to attitude formation and changes. Junior standing or higher.

COMG 470.title: Nonverbal Communication
COMG 470.subject: COMG
COMG 470.description: Understanding communication beyond the words themselves. Review of theory and research on gestures, facial expressions, touch, personal space, and physical appearance. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 471.title: Verbal Communication
COMG 471.subject: COMG
COMG 471.description: Roles of language: perception and assumption in human relationships; relation of language symbols to emotion and attitudes. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 472.title: Deceptive Communication
COMG 472.subject: COMG
COMG 472.description: Survey of major social scientific theories, concepts, and research findings on deceptive communication, in a lecture/discussion format. Emphasis is on how people create deceptive messages, induce deception, and strategies used to detect deception. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 481.title: Relational Management
COMG 481.subject: COMG
COMG 481.description: Survey and critical discussion of current theory and research in relational management literature. Focus on conversation management, deception, jealousy, privacy, communication of emotions.

COMG 490.title: Communication in Helping Relationships
COMG 490.subject: COMG
COMG 490.description: Theory and application of personal and interpersonal elements affecting communication of human-service professionals. Supervised practice. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 493.title: Teaching Speech
COMG 493.subject: COMG
COMG 493.description: For communicology majors who lead, under supervision, a freshman seminar section of communicology.

COMG 495.title: Health Communication
COMG 495.subject: COMG
COMG 495.description: Develop understanding of the process through which communication influences health outcomes, and learn how to design effective health communication programs using theory and research. Restricted to students with 60 or more credits.

COMG 499.title: Directed Reading
COMG 499.subject: COMG
COMG 499.prereq_raw: consent of department chair and instructor

COMG 600.title: Master’s Plan B/C Studies
COMG 600.subject: COMG
COMG 600.prereq_raw: master’s Plan B candidate and consent

COMG 601.title: Theories in Communicology
COMG 601.subject: COMG
COMG 601.description: Major theoretical foundations; humanistic and social scientific perspectives. Examination of the research and the development of different models of human communication.

COMG 602.title: Research Methods in Communicology
COMG 602.subject: COMG
COMG 602.description: Design and analysis of quantitative research in communicology. Focus on measurement issues, research design, descriptive and inferential statistics.

COMG 620.title: Practicum for Instructional Communication
COMG 620.subject: COMG
COMG 620.description: Combined seminar and lecture/ discussion format on techniques and procedures for teaching communication skills and their related components in a laboratory setting.

COMG 660.title: Business Communication
COMG 660.subject: COMG
COMG 660.description: Analysis of communication issues in business through discussion of verbal/nonverbal messages, interpersonal relationships, conflict, and persuasion. Focus on interviewing, group communication, and public speaking skills.

COMG 664.title: Persuasion and Social Influence
COMG 664.subject: COMG
COMG 664.description: Theories of persuasion and resistance to persuasion; assessment of attitudes and measurement of change.

COMG 670.title: Message Processing
COMG 670.subject: COMG
COMG 670.description: Theories of human message processing. Effects of verbal and nonverbal codes, channels, and message forms on encoding and decoding.

COMG 681.title: Relational Communication
COMG 681.subject: COMG
COMG 681.description: Major models and theories of interpersonal communication; research on interpersonal relationships; interaction and functions of human communication.

COMG 685.title: Foundations of Intercultural Communication
COMG 685.subject: COMG
COMG 685.description: Major models, theories, and concepts of intercultural communication; basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to intercultural communication; research on intercultural communication. Graduate standing only.

COMG 699.title: Directed Research
COMG 699.subject: COMG
COMG 699.description: Only three credits can count toward degree.

COMG 702.title: Advanced Research Methods in Communicology
COMG 702.subject: COMG
COMG 702.description: Advanced focus on survey, laboratory, and field study design, data collection, and data analysis. Emphasis on control of variance through design and statistical analysis. Appropriate preparation for graduate theses and dissertations.

COMG 721.title: Approaches to Instructional Communication
COMG 721.subject: COMG
COMG 721.description: Seminar on communication theories and models in instructional environment; emphasis on message processing, classroom dynamics, cognitive and metacognitive processes associated with learning, and learning assessment.

COMG 752.title: Research in Intergroup Communication
COMG 752.subject: COMG
COMG 752.description: Theory, concepts, research, and application of communication processes between members of different social groups.

COMG 760.title: Seminar in Special Topics in Communicology
COMG 760.subject: COMG
COMG 760.description: Substantive areas in communication that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addresed in other COMG courses. Topics vary each semester. Content to be announced.
COMG 760.prereq_raw: (601 (or concurrent) and 602 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B), or consent

COMG 764.title: Seminar in Persuasion and Influence
COMG 764.subject: COMG
COMG 764.description: Contemporary research in persuasion and influence.

COMG 770.title: Issues in Message Processing
COMG 770.subject: COMG
COMG 770.description: Contemporary research in verbal and nonverbal message processing.

COMG 785.title: Research on Intercultural Communication
COMG 785.subject: COMG
COMG 785.description: Functional approach to the study of communication in intercultural settings. Examination of culture-based variables and their impact on social influence, relational management, and message processing.

COMG 787.title: Artificial Intelligence and Communication
COMG 787.subject: COMG
COMG 787.description: Comprehensive understanding of the role and function of computer technology (including. A.I.) within the field of communication. Basic methodological and analytical issues of research related to semi-intelligent artifacts as information source or receiver. COMG majors or consent. Graduate students only.

COMG 795.title: Seminar in Health Communication Research
COMG 795.subject: COMG
COMG 795.description: Contemporary interpersonal and/ or public communication issues in health communication research. Topics include communication functions such as information management, interpersonal influence, relational management, emotional management, social influence.

HIST 151.title: World History to 1500
HIST 151.subject: HIST
HIST 151.description: Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from prehistory to 1500; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

HIST 152.title: World History since 1500
HIST 152.subject: HIST
HIST 152.description: Continuation of 151. Historical narratives and global perspectives on human societies and cross-cultural interactions from 1500 to present; includes ways to think about the past and ways to use primary sources.

HIST 155.title: Issues in World History
HIST 155.subject: HIST
HIST 155.description: In examining aspects of the histories of Africa, Asia, the Americas, Europe and Oceania, this course highlights the myriad ways in which global contact has transformed our world and narratives of the past.

HIST 156.title: World History of Human Disease
HIST 156.subject: HIST
HIST 156.description: Examines how disease has affected humans in terms of society, culture, politics, religion, and economics. Explores the impact over a broad range of time periods, from pre-history to the present/future.

HIST 157.title: Global Environmental History
HIST 157.subject: HIST
HIST 157.description: Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

HIST 161A.title: World Cultures in Perspective
HIST 161A.subject: HIST
HIST 161A.description: Development of civilizations from prehistoric origins to 1500. Offered as discussion and/or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

HIST 162A.title: World Cultures in Perspective
HIST 162A.subject: HIST
HIST 162A.description: Continuation of 161A. Development of civilization from 1500 to the present. Offered as discussion and/ or problems course. Alternative for 151 and 152; students in Honors program only.

HIST 230.title: Early European Civilization
HIST 230.subject: HIST
HIST 230.description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states before 1500, including classical and medieval eras. (Alt. years)

HIST 231.title: European Civilization 1500-1800
HIST 231.subject: HIST
HIST 231.description: Political evolution and major economic, social, and cultural development of European states. 1500–1800.

HIST 232.title: Modern European Civilization 1800-
HIST 232.subject: HIST
HIST 232.description: Continuation of 231. Major political, social, economic, and cultural trends from Napoleon to the present.

HIST 241.title: Civilizations of Asia
HIST 241.subject: HIST
HIST 241.description: Survey of major civilizations of Asia from earliest times to 1500; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

HIST 242.title: Civilizations of Asia
HIST 242.subject: HIST
HIST 242.description: Continuation of 241. Survey of major civilizations of Asia from 1500 to the present; East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia.

HIST 245.title: Atlantic History: Colonies to Revolutions
HIST 245.subject: HIST
HIST 245.description: Comparative and historical survey of colonialism and revolutions in the Atlantic World from 1500 to 1830. (Alt. years)

HIST 281.title: Introduction to American History
HIST 281.subject: HIST
HIST 281.description: Interpretive survey from earliest settlement to 1865.

HIST 282.title: Introduction to American History
HIST 282.subject: HIST
HIST 282.description: Interpretive survey from 1865 to the present.

HIST 284.title: History of the Hawaiian Islands
HIST 284.subject: HIST
HIST 284.description: Survey of state and local history from Polynesian chiefdoms to Hawaiian Kingdom to American territory and state.

HIST 288.title: Survey of Pacific Islands History
HIST 288.subject: HIST
HIST 288.description: Survey of Pacific Islands from pre-colonial to modern times; early settlement, cultural contact, colonization, contemporary problems.

HIST 294.title: History of the Philippines
HIST 294.subject: HIST
HIST 294.description: Traces developments in Philippine history and society from precolonial to contemporary times and explores ways in which the peoples of the Philippines embraced, resisted or negotiated new modes of thought, behavior and social organization influenced by the Spanish, American, and Japanese regimes as well as the postcolonial global order.

HIST 296.title: Topics in History
HIST 296.subject: HIST
HIST 296.description: Introduction to methods of historical inquiry; current issues in World, American, European, or Pacific history.

HIST 301.title: History of Early India
HIST 301.subject: HIST
HIST 301.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

HIST 302.title: History of Modern India
HIST 302.subject: HIST
HIST 302.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from the Mughal Empire to the new millennium, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from the 18th century to the present.

HIST 305.title: History of Southeast Asia
HIST 305.subject: HIST
HIST 305.description: Survey of development of civilizations and growth of nations in Southeast Asia, to the 18th century.

HIST 306.title: History of Southeast Asia
HIST 306.subject: HIST
HIST 306.description: Continuation of 305, from 18th century to the present.

HIST 309.title: East Asian Civilizations
HIST 309.subject: HIST
HIST 309.description: Characteristics of East Asian civilizations as they developed in pre-modern China; variant patterns in Japan and Korea; the modernization process to 1500.

HIST 312.title: History of China
HIST 312.subject: HIST
HIST 312.description: Continuation of 311. Period since the 17th century.

HIST 321.title: History of Japan
HIST 321.subject: HIST
HIST 321.description: Survey of culture, government, economics, and institutions, to 1700.

HIST 323.title: Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
HIST 323.subject: HIST
HIST 323.description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of the tea ceremony (urasenke): Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics.

HIST 324.title: The Samurai of Japan
HIST 324.subject: HIST
HIST 324.description: A social, military, and cultural history of Japan’s samurai (warrior) class.

HIST 327.title: History of Premodern Korea
HIST 327.subject: HIST
HIST 327.description: Survey of political, economic, social, and cultural developments from earliest times to 1400.

HIST 328.title: History of Modern Korea
HIST 328.subject: HIST
HIST 328.description: Continuation of 327. From 1400 to the present.

HIST 330.title: History of North Korea
HIST 330.subject: HIST
HIST 330.description: History of North Korea in terms of industrialism, militarism, nationalism, and state power, from 1945 to today. Focus on construction of national sovereign identity and comparison with postcolonial world.

HIST 331.title: Ancient Greece I
HIST 331.subject: HIST
HIST 331.description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Minoan, Mycenean, and Archaic periods.

HIST 332.title: Ancient Greece II
HIST 332.subject: HIST
HIST 332.description: Political, social, and cultural history of the Classical and Hellenistic periods.

HIST 333.title: Ancient Rome: The Republic
HIST 333.subject: HIST
HIST 333.description: Political, social, cultural history from the Etruscans to Augustus. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: fall)

HIST 334.title: Ancient Rome: The Empire
HIST 334.subject: HIST
HIST 334.description: Political, social, and cultural history from Augustus to 476 A.D. Emphasis on literary and archaeological materials. (Alt. years: spring)

HIST 335.title: Early Medieval Europe 300–1050
HIST 335.subject: HIST
HIST 335.description: Formation of European societies after the western Roman Empire and in relation to Byzantine and Islamic cultures.

HIST 336.title: Medieval Europe 1050–1350
HIST 336.subject: HIST
HIST 336.description: Main trends in European economy, society, religion, politics, thought, and the arts; interactions with Byzantine and Islamic worlds.

HIST 337.title: European Intellectual History
HIST 337.subject: HIST
HIST 337.description: Undergraduate seminar on great debates in Western thought. Discussion of primary source materials; the scientific revolution and Enlightenment.

HIST 338.title: European Intellectual History
HIST 338.subject: HIST
HIST 338.description: Continuation of 337. European thought from French Revolution to the present.

HIST 339.title: Renaissance and Reformation
HIST 339.subject: HIST
HIST 339.description: Political, social, cultural, and intellectual developments in Europe from 1300 to 1600. Emphasis on cultural and intellectual history and its impact on social and political developments; humanism and its influence on thought and reforming movements, Protestant and Catholic Reformations. (Alt. years: fall)

HIST 340.title: Comparative Economic History
HIST 340.subject: HIST
HIST 340.description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

HIST 342.title: The History of Economic Thought
HIST 342.subject: HIST
HIST 342.description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.

HIST 343.title: Reacting to the Past
HIST 343.subject: HIST
HIST 343.description: Exploration of moments of crisis and the clash of ideas in their historical context through the use of simulation games.

HIST 344.title: Modern Germany
HIST 344.subject: HIST
HIST 344.description: Political, social, economic, and cultural history since 1547. Rise of Austria and Prussia, unification, Bismarckian era, World War I and Weimar Republic, Hitler’s Third Reich, post-World War II.

HIST 345.title: France in the Old Regime
HIST 345.subject: HIST
HIST 345.description: Major social, political, and intellectual developments: Renaissance, Reformation, religious wars, Richelieu, Louis XIV, Enlightenment, and Revolution.

HIST 346.title: Modern France
HIST 346.subject: HIST
HIST 346.description: Political, social, economic, and intellectual developments from Revolution and Napoleon to the present.

HIST 347.title: Tudor-Stuart Britain
HIST 347.subject: HIST
HIST 347.description: Traces major developments in British politics, society, and culture between the late Medieval and Modern Eras.

HIST 348.title: Modern Britain 1688-1945
HIST 348.subject: HIST
HIST 348.description: Interaction of 17th-, 18th-, and 19th-century intellectual, political, economic, and social changes, which together produced the British Empire and modern Britain.

HIST 349.title: British Empire
HIST 349.subject: HIST
HIST 349.description: Origins and expansion of the British empire between the seventeenth and twentieth centuries. Includes imperial policies affecting Britain, Australia, India, Ireland, and Southern Africa. Open to non-majors.

HIST 350.title: Iberia in Asia and the Pacific
HIST 350.subject: HIST
HIST 350.description: Comparative exploration of the Iberian empires–Spain and Portugal–and their political, economic, and cultural interactions with indigenous societies in Asia and the Pacific.

HIST 351.title: East European Empires
HIST 351.subject: HIST
HIST 351.description: Comparison of Austrian, Polish, Ottoman, and Russian empires by examining political ideologies, religions, lifestyles, and ethno-linguistic identities.

HIST 352.title: France and Empire
HIST 352.subject: HIST
HIST 352.description: Lecture/discussion exploring the history of France’s relationship with imperialism from the Renaissance to the present.
HIST 352.prereq_raw: upper division standing or consent. (Once a year)

HIST 354.title: Introduction to Islamic History
HIST 354.subject: HIST
HIST 354.description: Muhammad, the Arab conquests, the Caliphate; fundamentals of Islam; classical Islamic civilization; development of Islam into modern times with emphasis on the Middle Eastern heartland.

HIST 355.title: The Making of the Modern Middle East
HIST 355.subject: HIST
HIST 355.description: Survey of developments that created the system of nation-states in the Middle East. History of the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Turkey; Egypt; the Arab world; Israel and Iran.

HIST 356.title: Survey of African History
HIST 356.subject: HIST
HIST 356.description: The history of Africa from earliest times to the present: the rise of indigenous civilizations, European and Muslim impact, colonialism and nationalism, and current issues.

HIST 358.title: The World of Mekong
HIST 358.subject: HIST
HIST 358.description: Historical survey, from BC period to present, of the peoples of the Mekong region, an area covering southwestern China, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, and southern Vietnam. Open to non-majors.

HIST 361.title: U.S. Women’s History
HIST 361.subject: HIST
HIST 361.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

HIST 362.title: Gender and Sexuality in the Classical World
HIST 362.subject: HIST
HIST 362.description: Critical examination of the construction of gender identity and sexuality in ancient Greece and Rome. (Once a year)

HIST 368.title: Global History of Sport
HIST 368.subject: HIST
HIST 368.description: Explores the relationship between sport and society in historical perspective. Analyzes global processes of imperialism, nationalism, globalization, and international relations, and studies themes such as the politics of race, class, and gender.

HIST 371.title: U.S. Foreign Relations to 1898
HIST 371.subject: HIST
HIST 371.description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from initial encounters between Europeans and Native Americans through the 1890s.

HIST 372.title: U.S. Foreign Relations From 1898
HIST 372.subject: HIST
HIST 372.description: Survey of U.S. foreign relations from the wars of 1898 to the present.

HIST 373.title: American Thought and Culture: To 20th Century
HIST 373.subject: HIST
HIST 373.description: Politics, family, philosophy, technology, etc.; their interrelationship within the total society. Pre-Colonial to end of the 19th century.

HIST 378.title: History of American Business
HIST 378.subject: HIST
HIST 378.description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

HIST 379.title: American Empire
HIST 379.subject: HIST
HIST 379.description: Examines the interplay between an “American culture of empire” and the rise of the U.S. as a superpower. Topics: imperialism and political culture, social movements and international affairs, race, gender and class relations.

HIST 386.title: Caribbean History
HIST 386.subject: HIST
HIST 386.description: Survey of the history of the Caribbean region from 1500 to the present.
HIST 386.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

HIST 389.title: The Asia-Pacific War
HIST 389.subject: HIST
HIST 389.description: Explores WWII in the Asia-Pacific region, focusing on the intersection of the grand strategy, military operations, and war crimes. Involves source analyses and discussions.

HIST 391.title: History of Warfare to 1850
HIST 391.subject: HIST
HIST 391.description: Classical and guerrilla warfare, revolution, and military systems and institutions.

HIST 393.title: U.S. Military History
HIST 393.subject: HIST
HIST 393.description: Survey of development of American military forces from War of Independence to war in Vietnam.

HIST 394.title: History of Science to 1700
HIST 394.subject: HIST
HIST 394.description: Evolution of scientific thought and its cultural context. Antiquity to 1700.

HIST 395.title: History of Science Since 1700
HIST 395.subject: HIST
HIST 395.description: Continuation of 394; science, technology, and society since 1700.

HIST 400.title: Digital History in the Global Village
HIST 400.subject: HIST
HIST 400.description: History of the digital age in global perspective connecting people, media, and technology. Faculty and students will use digital media to introduce innovative approaches to doing history.

HIST 401.title: History of the Indian Ocean World
HIST 401.subject: HIST
HIST 401.description: Explores the transnational history of the Indian Ocean world, especially the region connected by the western monsoon. Topics include travel, trade, religion, colonialism, nationalism, diaspora, and globalization, including actors like slaves, sailors, women, and merchants.
HIST 401.prereq_raw: junior or senior standing or consent

HIST 402.title: Researching WWII in Southeast Asia
HIST 402.subject: HIST
HIST 402.description: Introduces students to the practice of conducting archival research by using materials about World War II in Southeast Asia that have been digitized by various institutions around the world and available on the internet.

HIST 403.title: Vietnam: History and Memory
HIST 403.subject: HIST
HIST 403.description: Survey of Vietnamese history with particular attention to the multiple ways that the Vietnamese past has been remembered and represented by different peoples. Open to non-majors.

HIST 406.title: Modern Philippines
HIST 406.subject: HIST
HIST 406.description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

HIST 407.title: Modern Malaysia
HIST 407.subject: HIST
HIST 407.description: History of Malay peninsula and northern Borneo, emphasizing developments since 18th century: trade, commerce, foreign migrations, pluralism, nationalism, and Islam.

HIST 408.title: Modern Indonesia
HIST 408.subject: HIST
HIST 408.description: Indonesia from 14th century to present. Emphasis on period from late 18th-century Western colonial impact to struggle for independence and problems of nationhood.

HIST 409.title: History of Islamic Southeast Asia
HIST 409.subject: HIST
HIST 409.description: History of the coming of Islam to Southeast Asia, the spread of its ideas, and its role in the lives of Muslim communities living in the region. GPA of 2.0 or higher.

HIST 410.title: Twentieth-Century China
HIST 410.subject: HIST
HIST 410.description: An examination of the political, intellectual, economic, cultural, and social transformations of China in the twentieth century. This lecture studies critical events in the making of modern China and explores important issues in the modernization of Chinese life in the twentieth century.

HIST 411.title: Society and Culture in Traditional China
HIST 411.subject: HIST
HIST 411.description: Ch’ing government and Chinese society from local and regional perspectives; modes of control and disorder during the 19th century.

HIST 412.title: Local History of 20th-Century China
HIST 412.subject: HIST
HIST 412.description: Sociopolitical change and continuity at local and regional levels since 1900, stressing provincial reform, Hsien and sub-Hsien politics, warlordism, Kuomintang tutelage, and the Chinese Communist movement and rule.

HIST 416.title: Chinese Intellectual History
HIST 416.subject: HIST
HIST 416.description: An interpretive survey of Chinese ideas and values in their cultural, social and political settings from classical age to 1600.

HIST 417.title: Chinese Intellectual History
HIST 417.subject: HIST
HIST 417.description: Interpretive survey of Chinese thought from 1600 to the contemporary period, with special emphasis on the themes of cultural collision and change.

HIST 418.title: China’s Foreign Relations
HIST 418.subject: HIST
HIST 418.description: Systematic review from traditional times, with emphasis on modern and contemporary history, analyses of foreign policy formulation, objectives, and implementation.

HIST 419.title: The Search for Modern China
HIST 419.subject: HIST
HIST 419.description: Origins, development, and meaning of modern revolution in China, 19th century to People’s Republic.

HIST 420.title: People’s Republic of China
HIST 420.subject: HIST
HIST 420.description: Salient developments from 1949 to the present. Social revolution and modernization, critically relevant foreign relations.

HIST 421.title: China in World History
HIST 421.subject: HIST
HIST 421.description: Interpretative survey of China’s changing position, significance, and function in the evolution of world history as a way to provide a better understanding of its past and present.

HIST 423.title: Okinawa
HIST 423.subject: HIST
HIST 423.description: Survey of social, cultural, economic, and political history from earliest times to present.

HIST 424.title: 20th-Century Japan
HIST 424.subject: HIST
HIST 424.description: Problems of Japan’s political, economic, and social development since institutional consolidation of Meiji state (c.1890).

HIST 425.title: Women in East Asian History
HIST 425.subject: HIST
HIST 425.description: Survey of the changing political, social, economic, and cultural positions of women in China, Japan, and Korea from ancient times to the present.
HIST 425.prereq_raw: one course in Japanese history or consent

HIST 426.title: History of Japanese Cuisine and Foodways
HIST 426.subject: HIST
HIST 426.description: Explores the history of Japanese cuisine and investigates the cultural, economic, and geopolitical aspects of food-ways in Japanese domestic and international identity.

HIST 428.title: WWII and the Making of Modern Japan
HIST 428.subject: HIST
HIST 428.description: Explores how the history of the Asia-Pacific War both shaped and was shaped by the rise and fall of Japan in the twentieth century. Involves extensive source analyses and discussions.

HIST 429.title: War Crimes Trials in Asia
HIST 429.subject: HIST
HIST 429.description: Explores post-WWII Allied war crimes trials in the Asia-Pacific region and transitional justice in Asia. Involves extensive source analyses and discussions.

HIST 430.title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
HIST 430.subject: HIST
HIST 430.description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires.

HIST 431.title: Ancient Near East: Pyramids and Writing Tablets
HIST 431.subject: HIST
HIST 431.description: Civilizations of the Sumerians, Babylonians, Assyrians, ancient Egyptians, Hittites, Hebrews, and Achaemenid Persians. Emphasis on discussion of literary and archaeological materials.

HIST 432.title: Crisis and Conflict in the Middle East
HIST 432.subject: HIST
HIST 432.description: In depth study and analysis of major crises and conflicts in the Middle East since World War II: the Arab–Israeli Wars, revolutions in the Arab countries, the Turkish experiment with secularism, the Iranian/ Islamic revolution, Afghanistan, the Gulf War.

HIST 433.title: Medieval Cultures
HIST 433.subject: HIST
HIST 433.description: Topical study of cultural and cross-cultural issues in the medieval period (circa 300-1500). Class discussion and written work emphasize analysis of primary source documents using cultural and world history theories. Regional focus and readings vary by semester.

HIST 434.title: History of Christianity to 1500
HIST 434.subject: HIST
HIST 434.description: Historical analysis of the main traditions of Christianity and elements of diversity within Europe and in relation to other parts of the world. Focus on the interpretation of primary sources and discussion of cultural issues. (Alt. years: spring)

HIST 436.title: World Environmental History, 1500 to Present
HIST 436.subject: HIST
HIST 436.description: Explores interactions between humans and the natural world from early modern era to the present. Topics include invader species and biotic exchange; environmental politics; and the ecological impact of industrialization, urbanization, science, technology, war, etc.
HIST 436.prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

HIST 438.title: European Cult of the Primitive
HIST 438.subject: HIST
HIST 438.description: Historical investigation of European beliefs in the superiority of primitive societies. Topics include how primitivist ideas shaped historiography, religion, art, gender, political economy, and empire.

HIST 439.title: The Darwinian Revolution
HIST 439.subject: HIST
HIST 439.description: Social and intellectual origins of evolutionary thought and its continuing impact; emphasis on Darwin and the Victorian scientific community.

HIST 440.title: 20th-Century Europe
HIST 440.subject: HIST
HIST 440.description: Contemporary problems and their historical background.

HIST 441.title: Expansion of Europe
HIST 441.subject: HIST
HIST 441.description: Historical processes in modern European colonization from 16th to 20th century; impact on non-Europeans in Asia and Africa. (Alt. years: fall)

HIST 442.title: War and Violence in Early Modern Europe
HIST 442.subject: HIST
HIST 442.description: History of the intellectual, social, and cultural causes and consequences of violence, including military conflicts.
HIST 442.prereq_raw: upper division standing or consent. (Once a year)

HIST 443.title: Nazi Germany
HIST 443.subject: HIST
HIST 443.description: Origins, establishment, and impact of Hitler’s Third Reich.

HIST 444.title: The History of the Holocaust
HIST 444.subject: HIST
HIST 444.description: The origins and progression of the Holocaust, the almost complete destruction of European Jews, and other Nazi genocidal policies. Open to non-majors.

HIST 445.title: French Revolution and Napoleon
HIST 445.subject: HIST
HIST 445.description: Causes, course, and conduct of the Revolutionary and Napoleonic periods, their impact upon Europe; emphasis on the conflict of ideologies inherent in the Revolutionary process.

HIST 446.title: Europe, 1914-1945: War, Peace, and Revolution
HIST 446.subject: HIST
HIST 446.description: Explores war and peace in Europe, from the start of the Great War through the formal end of World War II. Topics include key battles, civilians, peace movements, treaties, the Shoah, Fascism, and Soviet Revolution.

HIST 448.title: Imperial Spain and Portugal
HIST 448.subject: HIST
HIST 448.description: The influence of Spain and Portugal on people and cultures in Europe, Africa, America, and Asia; Portugal’s captivity and the defeat of the Spanish Armada.

HIST 450.title: Topics in African History
HIST 450.subject: HIST
HIST 450.description: Selected themes important in African history, including, for example, the politics, economics, societies, and cultures of pre-colonial, colonial, or modern Africa. Topics to be pre-announced. (Once a year)

HIST 453.title: Colonial Medicine
HIST 453.subject: HIST
HIST 453.description: Evolution of Western medical traditions; challenges created by European expansion and colonial interactions; development of modern racial and gender theories.

HIST 454.title: Tsarist Russia
HIST 454.subject: HIST
HIST 454.description: Development of the Russian state to the 19th century. Kievan state and early development of culture and art; Mongol era; rise of Moscow, autocracy, and serfdom; Petrine reforms; Western impact; emergence as a major European power.

HIST 456.title: Modern Russia
HIST 456.subject: HIST
HIST 456.description: Creation of the Soviet Union, Stalinization, the Cold War, the collapse of the empire, the post-Soviet era.

HIST 457.title: Russia in Asia and the Pacific
HIST 457.subject: HIST
HIST 457.description: Russian/Soviet Siberia and Central Asia; Russian American Company and the Pacific; evolving relations with Asian and Pacific powers.

HIST 458.title: The American Revolution
HIST 458.subject: HIST
HIST 458.description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins, development, and consequences of the American Revolution, explored within the context of the broader revolutionary Atlantic world.
HIST 458.prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

HIST 459.title: African American History
HIST 459.subject: HIST
HIST 459.description: Lecture/ discussion on the origins of racial slavery, slave and free black culture, slave resistance and antislavery, post-emancipation black life, the rise of Jim Crow, the Harlem Renaissance, and the Civil Rights Movement.

HIST 460.title: Native American History
HIST 460.subject: HIST
HIST 460.description: Lecture/ discussion on the history of North American Indians from the seventeenth century to the present. Open to non-majors.

HIST 461.title: Early America
HIST 461.subject: HIST
HIST 461.description: Lecture/discussion on Native Americans, Africans, and Europeans in North America from contact to independence. Social, cultural, and economic themes and intersections of race, class, and gender explored.

HIST 462.title: The Early American Republic
HIST 462.subject: HIST
HIST 462.description: Lecture/discussion on the Constitution, the growth of partisan politics, the market revolution, religious revivalism, abolitionism and the expansion of slavery in the U.S. during the age of Jefferson and Jackson.

HIST 463.title: American Civil War Era 1841–1877
HIST 463.subject: HIST
HIST 463.description: The crisis of the Union: antebellum society and culture, slavery, reform, sectionalism, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

HIST 464.title: Transformation of America 1877–1920
HIST 464.subject: HIST
HIST 464.description: Selected themes that explain major changes in American life during the late 19th and early 20th centuries, including the westward movement, consolidation of capitalism, world power diplomacy, popular culture, progressivism, and World War I.

HIST 465.title: The United States 1920–1948
HIST 465.subject: HIST
HIST 465.description: The Roaring Twenties, the Depression, New Deal, coming of World War II, America during the war, origins of the Cold War.

HIST 466.title: The U.S.: 1948 to the Present
HIST 466.subject: HIST
HIST 466.description: The atomic age and the Cold War, the age of anxiety, the 1960s, the Vietnam War, the Reagan-Bush era, and beyond.

HIST 467.title: American Television History
HIST 467.subject: HIST
HIST 467.description: Lecture/discussion examining the impact of television on American society, culture and politics. Analyzed in depth are family sitcoms, presidential politics, Vietnam and the presentation of gender and ethnicity. Open to non-majors.

HIST 468.title: Viva Las Vegas!
HIST 468.subject: HIST
HIST 468.description: Upper-division lecture on the historical and cultural significance of Las Vegas in twentieth-century America. Open to non-majors.

HIST 469.title: The Cold War
HIST 469.subject: HIST
HIST 469.description: Cold War as a global struggle. Topics will include U.S.-Soviet economic and political rivalry, Capitalism vs. Communism as practical policy and ideology, and the force of Third World anti-colonial nationalism.
HIST 469.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

HIST 471.title: Music, Industry, and Society
HIST 471.subject: HIST
HIST 471.description: History of U.S. music and recording industry. How industry relates to economy as a whole, and how it reflects broad patterns and trends in American culture and society.

HIST 472.title: American Social History
HIST 472.subject: HIST
HIST 472.description: Introduction to the new social history; interdisciplinary approaches to the study of the everyday lives of ordinary Americans in past generations.

HIST 473.title: Slavery and Freedom
HIST 473.subject: HIST
HIST 473.description: Examines the history of slavery, race, and abolition in the Americas from a comparative, global perspective, and traces the legacy of slavery in the post-emancipation societies of the New World.

HIST 474.title: The American West
HIST 474.subject: HIST
HIST 474.description: Lecture/ discussion surveying the conquest, colonization, and consolidation of North American frontiers and the post-frontier development of the American West.

HIST 475.title: Constitutional History of the U.S.
HIST 475.subject: HIST
HIST 475.description: Origins, development of Constitution, Colonial to modern times.

HIST 476.title: Race and Racism in America
HIST 476.subject: HIST
HIST 476.description: Racial ideas and ideologies, and their effects throughout American history.

HIST 477.title: History of American Workers
HIST 477.subject: HIST
HIST 477.description: Conditions of labor in major phases of American development; response of labor and community to changing work environment. Capitalism, unionism, race, gender, law, etc. Emphasis on 20th century.

HIST 478.title: Colonial Latin America
HIST 478.subject: HIST
HIST 478.description: PreColumbian civilizations: Spanish and Portuguese colonization; political, economic, social, and religious evolution to 1810; independence.

HIST 479.title: Latin America Since Independence
HIST 479.subject: HIST
HIST 479.description: Political, economic, and social development since 1825; case studies from Brazil, Mexico, and Cuba.

HIST 480.title: American Environmental History
HIST 480.subject: HIST
HIST 480.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

HIST 481.title: Pacific Islands I
HIST 481.subject: HIST
HIST 481.description: The Pacific past from first human settlement to the start of the colonial period; emphasis on historiography and analysis of islanders’ responses to Euro-American intrusion.

HIST 482.title: Pacific Islands II
HIST 482.subject: HIST
HIST 482.description: The colonial experience to the present.

HIST 483.title: United States in the Pacific
HIST 483.subject: HIST
HIST 483.description: Growth of economic and political interests and policies.

HIST 484.title: The Hawaiian Kingdom 1819–1893
HIST 484.subject: HIST
HIST 484.description: Transformation of Hawai‘i into a state influenced by American and European ideas and institutions and Asian peoples.

HIST 485.title: History of 20th-Century Hawai‘i
HIST 485.subject: HIST
HIST 485.description: Formation of an American Hawai‘i with its unique local culture from 1898 to the present.

HIST 489.title: World Maritime History
HIST 489.subject: HIST
HIST 489.description: Survey of world maritime history from earliest times to the present, with emphasis on the evolution of nautical technology, motives from maritime enterprises, and the impact of cross-cultural encounters between oceanic peoples.

HIST 490.title: Maori and American Indians
HIST 490.subject: HIST
HIST 490.description: Compares indigenous sovereignty issues arising among the Maori or Aotearoa-New Zealand and Indian tribes of the U.S. from 1776 to the present. (Once a year)

HIST 492.title: Women and Revolution
HIST 492.subject: HIST
HIST 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

HIST 493.title: Library Treasures: Exploring Special Collections & Archives
HIST 493.subject: HIST
HIST 493.description: Conduct original research using general library materials, special collections, rare books, archives, and manuscripts, maps, and other historical documents that are uniquely available at libraries and archives at UH and beyond.

HIST 499.title: Directed Reading
HIST 499.subject: HIST
HIST 499.description: Individual projects in various fields. History majors with consent. Maximum 5 credit hours. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean.

HIST 602.title: Seminar in Historiography
HIST 602.subject: HIST
HIST 602.description: History of history and historians; philosophies of history.

HIST 605.title: Seminar in Digital History
HIST 605.subject: HIST
HIST 605.description: Examines the various ways that the production, presentation, and learning of history through digital media is changing the way people access and process information about the past. Graduate standing only.

HIST 607.title: Advanced Topics in Environmental History
HIST 607.subject: HIST
HIST 607.description: Introduction to leading themes, methodologies, and topics in world environmental history. Drawing on new and influential scholarship, readings explore the diverse forces that shape humans’ adaptation to and impact on the natural world. (Alt. years)

HIST 608.title: Seminar on Water in History
HIST 608.subject: HIST
HIST 608.description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

HIST 609.title: Seminar in World History
HIST 609.subject: HIST
HIST 609.description: Analysis, research, and discussion of themes and issues in study of history of humankind.

HIST 610.title: Topics in World History
HIST 610.subject: HIST
HIST 610.description: Selected themes— feudalism, economic and industrial development, etc.— important in global history. Topics pre-announced.

HIST 612.title: Ethnographic History
HIST 612.subject: HIST
HIST 612.description: Critical inquiry into historical representations of the “other” and ways in which modern historians have used culture and other anthropological concepts to write and think about the past.

HIST 613.title: Introduction to Cultural Studies
HIST 613.subject: HIST
HIST 613.description: Graduate seminar designed to introduce history students to the multidisciplinary theories that are appropriate to cultural studies.

HIST 616.title: Topics in Historical Methods and Theory
HIST 616.subject: HIST
HIST 616.description: Seminar covering one specific approach to historical methods or theory. The goal is a deep engagement with a particular historical approach via research and reading not bounded by region, time, or specialty. Graduate standing only.

HIST 617.title: Atrocity Crimes: Law and History
HIST 617.subject: HIST
HIST 617.description: Seminar on history of mass atrocity and international justice in the modern world. Topics include postWWII Allied war crimes prosecution, post-cold war ad hoc international criminal tribunals, and contemporary international law and national legal systems.

HIST 650.title: Seminar: Comparative Asia
HIST 650.subject: HIST
HIST 650.description: This reading seminar in the comparative history of modern Asia will introduce graduate students to themes, particularly in social, cultural, and intellectual history, which lend themselves to comparison across the region.

HIST 656.title: Topics in Southeast Asia
HIST 656.subject: HIST
HIST 656.description: Reading and research seminar on themes about the past and present of Southeast Asia in a comparative framework.

HIST 657.title: Historiography of Southeast Asia
HIST 657.subject: HIST
HIST 657.description: Examination of contested boundaries of Southeast Asia, the various historiographic traditions, the colonial legacy, and the current issues emerging from a dialogue of historians from the “region” and the outside world.

HIST 658.title: Seminar in Modern Southeast Asian History
HIST 658.subject: HIST
HIST 658.description: Graduate level reading seminar in modern Southeast Asian history.

HIST 659.title: The Seas in Southeast Asian History
HIST 659.subject: HIST
HIST 659.description: Seminar on the seas in Southeast Asian history. (Alt. years)

HIST 660.title: Seminar: Vietnamese History
HIST 660.subject: HIST
HIST 660.description: Reading and research seminar on Vietnamese history.

HIST 662.title: Seminar: Islam and Islamic Civilization
HIST 662.subject: HIST
HIST 662.description: Readings on the rise, spread, and development of Islamic cultures and civilizations throughout the world down to modern times.

HIST 663.title: Seminar in South Asian History
HIST 663.subject: HIST
HIST 663.description: Graduate-level reading and research seminar on topics in Indian and South Asian history.

HIST 670.title: Topics on the Asia-Pacific War
HIST 670.subject: HIST
HIST 670.description: Research seminar on topics of the Asia-Pacific War (1931-1945). Explores war, war crimes, and issues of war guilt, accountability, and war commemoration. Involves extensive source analyses and discussions.

HIST 677.title: Seminar in History of Hawai‘i
HIST 677.subject: HIST
HIST 677.description: Reading seminar with short papers required. Covers Kingdom of Hawai‘i and 20th-century Hawai‘i in alternate years. (Alt. years: fall)

HIST 678.title: Hawaiian Historical Research: Documents and Methods
HIST 678.subject: HIST
HIST 678.description: Research and writings emphasizing the interpretation of Hawaiian and English language primary sources. Development of source materials, approaches, and methods in Hawaiian history. Graduate standing only.
HIST 678.prereq_raw: HAW 301 with a B or better, or instructor consent

HIST 699.title: Directed Research
HIST 699.subject: HIST
HIST 699.description: Individual research topics. (1) American; (2) Pacific; (3) Japanese; (4) European; (5) English; (6) Chinese; (7) Russian; (8) Hawaiian; (9) South Asian; (10) Southeast Asian; (11) Korean. Restricted to plan A (thesis) students. Maximum 2 credit hours.

HIST 702.title: Institutional History of Korea
HIST 702.subject: HIST
HIST 702.description: Major political, economic, and social institutions.

HIST 713.title: Chinese Historical Literature
HIST 713.subject: HIST
HIST 713.description: Reading and use of numerous genres of Chinese historical literature and documents. Chinese bibliography. Knowledge of Chinese required.

HIST 790.title: Teaching History
HIST 790.subject: HIST
HIST 790.description: HIST 151-152 faculty supervisors mentor their Teaching Assistants who teach the discussion labs. Course addresses issues of teaching strategy, grading and historical content. Enrollment limited to current Teaching Assistants in the World History Program.
HIST 790.prereq_raw: History graduate Teaching Assistants assigned to 151-152

prereq_tree.text: History graduate Teaching Assistants assigned to 151 -152

MUS 106.title: Introduction to Music Literature
MUS 106.subject: MUS
MUS 106.description: Elements, styles, and forms of music, from listener’s standpoint.

MUS 107.title: Music in World Cultures
MUS 107.subject: MUS
MUS 107.description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific; representative styles and regional characteristics.

MUS 107A.title: Music in World Cultures
MUS 107A.subject: MUS
MUS 107A.description: Folk, popular, and art music from major regions of the world, with emphasis upon Asia and the Pacific; representative styles and regional characteristics.

MUS 108.title: Fundamentals of Music
MUS 108.subject: MUS
MUS 108.description: Basic organization concepts in music and introduction to music theory. Learning through hands-on experience with creative activities in various media. Focused listening, composing original meolodies, utilizing technology to explore how music is created, basic notation.

MUS 114.title: University Chorus
MUS 114.subject: MUS
MUS 114.description: Performance of choral literature from Renaissance to present. Previous choral experience not required.

MUS 125.title: First-Level Secondary Piano
MUS 125.subject: MUS
MUS 125.description: Piano as secondary performance field; application of theory to problems in improvising, harmonizing, creating accompaniments, transposing, and sight-reading at keyboard.

MUS 126.description: Piano as secondary performance field; application of theory to problems in improvising, harmonizing, creating accompaniments, transposing, and sight-reading at keyboard. Continuation of 125.

MUS 157.title: String Techniques

MUS 158.title: Woodwind Techniques

MUS 199.title: Recital Attendance

MUS 225.title: Second-Level Secondary Piano

MUS 240.title: Creative Applications of Music Technology
MUS 240.subject: MUS

MUS 265.title: History of Western Music to 1750

MUS 265.description: Development of Western music from its origins to 1750. Styles, schools, composers.

MUS 266.title: History of Western Music After 1750

MUS 280.title: Basic Theory and Aural Skills

MUS 283.title: Aural Training I

MUS 287.title: Aural Training III

MUS 289.title: Introductory Practicum in Music Composition

MUS 312.title: Hula/Chant Ensemble I

MUS 321.title: Diction for Singers

MUS 325.title: Conducting

MUS 325.description: Problems in directing instrumental and choral ensembles. Score reading, rehearsal techniques, and basic interpretive problems.

MUS 340.title: Electronic Music

MUS 340.description: Basic techniques of electronic sound synthesis.

MUS 341.title: Audio Recording/Mixing/Sound Design
MUS 341.subject: MUS
MUS 341.description: Preproduction, mixing, setup and recording suitable for film. Mixing techniques in software for small systems. Sound design using original synthesis techniques to enhance film and support stories.

MUS 342.subject: MUS

MUS 353.title: Integrating World Music in Education

MUS 354.title: General Music Methods
MUS 354.subject: MUS
MUS 354.description: Required for K-12 music specialists. Scope and nature of music in the lives of children and adolescents; planning, teaching, learning, and evaluating music in elementary, middle, and high school curriculum.

MUS 355.title: Instrumental Music Methods
MUS 355.subject: MUS
MUS 355.description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of instrumental music in schools.

MUS 355L.title: Instrumental Music Methods Lab
MUS 355L.subject: MUS

MUS 356.title: Choral Music Methods
MUS 356.subject: MUS
MUS 356.description: Objectives, materials, and procedures of choral music in schools.

MUS 356L.title: Choral Music Methods Lab
MUS 356L.subject: MUS
MUS 356L.description: Observing, analyzing, participating, and teaching in choral settings. Supervised 30 hours of field experiences required.

MUS 358.title: Piano Pedagogy
MUS 358.subject: MUS
MUS 358.description: Concepts, materials, and procedures for class and individual instruction in piano.

MUS 360.title: Music in Film

MUS 362.description: Traces the history of the Broadway musical in a survey of works from the mid-1800s through the recent “Hamilton” phenomenon, and explores their developmental process, structure, and sociocultural, religious, and political contexts.

MUS 383.title: Orchestration

MUS 386.title: Theory and Practice of Jazz Improvisation
MUS 386.subject: MUS
MUS 386.description: Development of an improvising technique through analysis and performance practice. For instrumentalists only.

MUS 399.title: Directed Study

MUS 421.title: Musical Theatre

MUS 423.title: Keyboard Skills I

MUS 787.subject: MUS

MUS 800.subject: MUS

CHN 451.title: Structure of Chinese

CHN 485.title: Academic/Professional Chinese I
CHN 485.subject: CHN

CHN 486.title: Academic/Professional Chinese II
CHN 486.subject: CHN

CHN 488.title: Flagship Rhetoric and Composition Abroad

CHN 489.title: Flagship Media and Society Abroad

CHN 489.description: Designed for students participating in the Flagship Capstone Year in China taught entirely in Chinese. Students will improve their knowledge of Chinese media, how it operates, and its effects on Chinese society.

CHN 491.title: Oral Fluency Through Chinese Films

CHN 491.description: Development of listening and speaking skills through discussion of Chinese films. Students will be required to watch the films before class.

CHN 495.title: Internship Program
CHN 495.subject: CHN
CHN 495.description: Faculty supervised participation in the operations of an organization in a position making use of students’ Chinese language skills in Hawai‘i. Students must achieve a grade of B- in CHN 302 to take this course. Junior/senior standing only.
CHN 495.prereq_raw: 302 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent

CHN 496.title: Overseas Internship in China
CHN 496.subject: CHN

ENG 691.title: MA Final Project

ENG 705.title: Seminar in Composition Studies

ENG 709.title: Seminar in Rhetoric

ENG 727.title: Seminar in Literary Criticism

ARAB 101.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 101.subject: ARAB
ARAB 101.description: Designed to provide students with basic knowledge of Modern Standard Arabic. Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language, as well as formal spoken Arabic.

ARAB 102.title: Elementary Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 102.subject: ARAB
ARAB 102.description: Focuses on developing proficiency in the standard written Arabic language as well as formal spoken Arabic. It introduces a wide range of situation-based texts and topics that build vocabulary, grammar, and general communicative competence.

ARAB 201.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 201.subject: ARAB
ARAB 201.description: Designed for students who have successfully completed a year of Elementary Arabic. Focus is on acquisition of more complex grammatical structures, expanding vocabulary, and developing competence in a wide range of communicative situations.

ARAB 202.title: Intermediate Modern Standard Arabic
ARAB 202.subject: ARAB
ARAB 202.description: Designed for students who have successfully completed three semesters of Arabic. Focus is on intensive practice of interactive functional skills such as listening comprehension and fundamental conversation strategies.

ARAB 301.title: Third-Level Arabic I
ARAB 301.subject: ARAB
ARAB 301.description: Develop proficiency in reading/listening comprehension in Modern Standard Arabic. The instructional materials consist of authentic written, visual and audio materials. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

ARAB 302.title: Third-Level Arabic II
ARAB 302.subject: ARAB
ARAB 302.description: Continuation of third-level Arabic I. Emphasis on developing writing and interaction ability at advanced levels of proficiency. Course includes extensive reading, composition exercises, listening skills, conversation practice and extensive review of Arabic grammar. Developing fluency is the main objective of this course. Classes meet 3 hours weekly.

CAM 101.title: Introduction to Modern Khmer
CAM 101.subject: CAM
CAM 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets five hours weekly

CAM 103.title: Conversing in Khmer I
CAM 103.subject: CAM
CAM 103.description: Online course aims to develop students’ proficiency skills in speaking and listening at the first year level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

CAM 104.title: Conversing in Khmer II
CAM 104.subject: CAM
CAM 104.description: Online course aims to develop students’ proficiency skills in speaking and listening at the first year level for the purpose of communication, travel, and for enjoyment.

CAM 105.title: Reading/Writing Khmer
CAM 105.subject: CAM
CAM 105.description: Online course aims to develop the student’s proficiency skills in reading and writing Khmer at the First Year level.

CAM 107.title: First Year Khmer
CAM 107.subject: CAM
CAM 107.description: Continuation of 105. This online course aims to develop proficiency skills in listening, reading, and writing Khmer at the first year level. Use a multimedia CD-ROM and a textbook to complement the web-based instruction.

CAM 201.title: Intermediate Modern Khmer
CAM 201.subject: CAM
CAM 201.description: Continuation of 102. Conversation, reading, writing. Meets five hours weekly.

CAM 203.title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare I
CAM 203.subject: CAM
CAM 203.description: Introduction to classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare. The Hare, known as ‘Judge Rabbit,’ is one of the most famous figure in Oral folktale stories.

CAM 205.title: Second Year Khmer I
CAM 205.subject: CAM
CAM 205.description: Online course aims to develop student’s proficiency-based units exploring Cambodian language and culture and focusing on reading and writing at the intermediate level.

CAM 206.title: Cambodian Folktales of the Hare II
CAM 206.subject: CAM
CAM 206.description: Introduction to classical Cambodian folktales of the Hare. Familiarize students to Cambodian basic language, cultures, and custom as seen in daily life.

CAM 207.title: Second Year Khmer II
CAM 207.subject: CAM
CAM 207.description: Continuation of 205. Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the intermediate level. Use a multimedia CD-ROM and a textbook to complement the web-based instruction.

CAM 301.title: Third-Level Khmer
CAM 301.subject: CAM
CAM 301.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced reading, writing, conversation and comprehension. Emphasis on modern contemporary texts. Computer assisted learning. Lab work.

CAM 302.title: Third-Level Khmer
CAM 302.subject: CAM
CAM 302.description: Continuation of 301. Computer assisted learning. Lab work.

CAM 303.title: Accelerated Third-Level Cambodian
CAM 303.subject: CAM
CAM 303.description: Continuation of 212. Practice in idiomatic conversation and extensive reading. Integrated development of listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Meets 10 hours weekly.

CAM 305.title: Third Year Khmer I
CAM 305.subject: CAM
CAM 305.description: Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Use a multimedia CD-ROM and a textbook to complement the web based instruction.

CAM 306.title: Third Year Khmer II
CAM 306.subject: CAM
CAM 306.description: Continuation of 305. Online course provides opportunities for learners to enhance their linguistic, discourse and sociolinguistic competencies in Khmer at the advanced level. Use a multimedia CD-ROM and a textbook to complement the web-based instruction.

CAM 401.title: Fourth-Level Khmer
CAM 401.subject: CAM
CAM 401.description: Continuation of 302. Computer assisted learning. Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of social and cultural issues; advanced conversation and composition.

CAM 415.title: Khmer Language in the Media
CAM 415.subject: CAM
CAM 415.description: Focus on advanced reading, writing, aural comprehension and speaking skills through the study of Khmer newspaper, radio, TV, audio/video clips and film.

CHAM 101.title: Elementary Chamorro
CHAM 101.subject: CHAM
CHAM 101.description: Introduction to Chamorro, emphasis on listening and speaking, language structure. Meets three hours weekly.

CHAM 102.title: Elementary Chamorro
CHAM 102.subject: CHAM
CHAM 102.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills; emphasis on oral and reading proficiency. Meets five hours weekly.

CHAM 201.title: Intermediate Chamorro
CHAM 201.subject: CHAM
CHAM 201.description: Continuation of 102. Emphasis on comprehension and language production (speaking). Meets five hours weekly.

CHAM 202.title: Intermediate Chamorro
CHAM 202.subject: CHAM
CHAM 202.description: Continuation of 201. Emphasis on comprehension and language production.

FIL 101.title: Beginning Filipino
FIL 101.subject: FIL
FIL 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

FIL 201.title: Intermediate Filipino
FIL 201.subject: FIL
FIL 201.description: Continuation of 102. Meets four hours weekly, includes one hour out-of-class field experience (Co-curricular cultural activities) weekly.

FIL 224.title: Filipino for Education
FIL 224.subject: FIL
FIL 224.description: Continuation of 102. Lessons focus on various aspects of Philippine culture and specialized topics that cater to the needs of teachers intending to teach Filipino immigrant students or teach Filipino as a second language. Meets five hours a week; daily lab work.

FIL 301.title: Third-Level Filipino I
FIL 301.subject: FIL
FIL 301.description: Conversation, advanced reading and composition on traditional culture and indigenous knowledge. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 302.title: Third-Level Filipino II
FIL 302.subject: FIL

FIL 315.title: Filipino Aural Comprehension

FIL 330.title: Filipino Film: Art and History

FIL 401.title: Fourth-Level Filipino I
FIL 401.subject: FIL
FIL 401.description: Advanced reading in traditional literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 402.title: Fourth-Level Filipino II
FIL 402.subject: FIL
FIL 402.description: Advanced reading in current literature; discussion of cultural implications; advanced conversation and composition. Meets three hours weekly.

FIL 415.title: Advanced Filipino Aural Comprehension
FIL 415.subject: FIL
FIL 415.description: Continuation of 315. Training in comprehension and analysis/criticism of spoken authentic materials through films.

FIL 435.title: Filipino Translation Techniques

FIL 461.title: Filipino Contemporary Literature
FIL 461.subject: FIL

HNDI 101.title: Elementary Hindi I
HNDI 101.subject: HNDI
HNDI 101.description: Learn to express yourself in Hindi-a language that comes with a beautiful script, ancient philosophy, spicy food, and Bollywood! The course is communicative, creative, flexibly personalized for student interests. No textbook to buy.

HNDI 102.title: Elementary Hindi II
HNDI 102.subject: HNDI
HNDI 102.description: Build on your 101 skills. Content includes Bollywood Film Festival at Honolulu Museum of Art. Create your own audiovisual projects–make movie trailers, write children’s books, or perform at South Asian events.

HNDI 201.title: Intermediate Hindi I
HNDI 201.subject: HNDI

HNDI 202.title: Intermediate Hindi II

HNDI 202.description: Prepare your proficiency for traveling to India. Create audio-visual presentations, documentaries, movie parodies, poetry, plays, dance, or projects from your majors/minors. Develop critical, cross-cultural, and creative skills. Bollywood built into course content.

HNDI 301.title: Third-Level Hindi: Culture
HNDI 301.subject: HNDI
HNDI 301.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected cultural themes.

HNDI 302.title: Third-Level Hindi: Film
HNDI 302.subject: HNDI
HNDI 302.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced listening, reading, writing, conversation skills, language structure, and culture integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected Hindi-Urdu films.

ILO 101.title: Beginning Ilokano

ILO 107.subject: ILO

ILO 201.title: Intermediate Ilokano

ILO 301.title: Third-Level Ilokano
ILO 301.subject: ILO
ILO 301.description: Continuation of 202. Conversation, advanced reading, composition. Meets three times weekly.

ILO 315.title: Ilokano Aural Comprehension

ILO 315.description: Training in listening comprehension of different authentic and simulated materials as presented in documentaries, soap operas, radio and television news and other broadcasts, formal lectures, plays, natural conversations, songs, and student-created sitcoms and dramas.

ILO 331.title: Contemporary Ilokano Literature
ILO 331.subject: ILO
ILO 331.description: Conducted in Ilokano, this course explores the literary landscape of Ilokano literature from the perspective of Ilokano writers based in the Philippines as well as those outside of the country.

ILO 401.title: Fourth-Level Ilokano
ILO 401.subject: ILO
ILO 401.description: Continuation of 302. Conducted in Ilokano. Advanced reading, writing, and conversation. Contemporary Ilokano literature; cultural and historical topics.

ILO 424.title: Introduction to Ilokano for Interpreters
ILO 424.subject: ILO
ILO 424.description: Techniques for interpreting Ilokano into English and vice versa.

ILO 425.title: Ilokano Interpretation Field Practicum

ILO 451.title: Structure of Ilokano
ILO 451.subject: ILO
ILO 451.description: Introduction to phonology, morphology, and syntax.

ILO 486.title: Ilokano for the Mass Media
ILO 486.subject: ILO
ILO 486.description: Ilokano as the medium for print journalism, for radio show programming, and for television production.

IND 101.title: Elementary Indonesian
