IND 301.title: Third-Level Indonesian
IND 301.subject: IND
IND 301.description: Continuation of 202. Conducted in Indonesian. Meets three hours a week. Reading, discussion, composition, and projects.

IND 305.title: Third Level Indonesian
IND 305.subject: IND
IND 305.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring the language of the contemporary Indonesian media with an emphasis on reading, writing, and listening comprehension. Not open to students who have taken IND 301.

IND 306.title: Third Level Indonesian
IND 306.subject: IND
IND 306.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring colloquial and formal Indonesian with a strong emphasis on listening and writing comprehension. Not open to students who have taken 302.

IND 307.title: Third Level Indonesian Conversation
IND 307.subject: IND
IND 307.description: Topic-based course aimed to enhance student’s listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language. Not open to students who have taken 301.

IND 308.title: Third Level Indonesian Conversation
IND 308.subject: IND
IND 308.description: Topic-based course aimed at enhancing students’ listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language. Not open to students who have taken 302.

IND 401.title: Fourth-Level Indonesian
IND 401.subject: IND
IND 401.description: Continuation of 302. Conducted in Indonesian. Meets three hours a week. Readings in various materials; speaking in various settings.

IND 405.title: Fourth Level Indonesian
IND 405.subject: IND
IND 405.description: Online course consists of modular, thematic, proficiency-based units exploring the language of the contemporary Indonesian media with an emphasis on reading, writing, and listening comprehension.

IND 407.description: Topic-based course aimed to enhance students’ listening and speaking skills in the Indonesian language.

IND 461.subject: IND

IP 101.title: Directed Elementary Language Study
IP 101.subject: IP

IP 199.title: Introductory Language Study
IP 199.subject: IP
IP 199.description: Introductory study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language. Contact hours and credits determined by student interests and faculty resources.

IP 261.title: Topics in Indo-Pacific Literature/Culture
IP 261.subject: IP
IP 261.description: Study of a literature or culture of the Indo-Pacific area through readings in various fields in English.

IP 299.title: Intermediate Language Study
IP 299.subject: IP
IP 299.description: Intermediate study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language. Contact hours and credits determined by student interests and faculty resources.
IP 299.prereq_raw: at least six credit hours of elementary study in the same language

IP 300.title: History of Early India
IP 300.subject: IP
IP 300.description: Historical survey of India and South Asia from Mohenjo-Daro to the Mughal Empire, tracing political, social, religious, economic, cultural, and intellectual developments from ancient times to the 18th century.

IP 303.title: Bollywood Dance, Music, and Film
IP 303.subject: IP
IP 303.description: Unique course combining mind and body, discussion and dancing. Learn and perform Bollywood dances and the richness of their Indian poetic, classical, and folk traditions. Understand “Bollywood” in the context of cross-cultural fusion and globalization.

IP 360.title: Filipino Food, Music, and Rituals: Art and Culture Studies
IP 360.subject: IP
IP 360.description: Study and analysis of the art and culture of Filipino food, music, and rituals-history, forms, social development, influences, and impact. Sophomore standing or consent.

IP 361.title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
IP 361.subject: IP
IP 361.description: Survey in English of traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia.

IP 362.title: Philippine Drama: History, Art, Culture
IP 362.subject: IP
IP 362.description: Historical survey from precolonial to contemporary periods. Studies forms, conventions, and literature within the social, political, and cultural context of the times as reflected in the history of Philippine drama. Explores plays in the diaspora. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 363.title: Philippine Contemporary Literature in English
IP 363.subject: IP
IP 363.description: Critical survey of 20th-century Philippine literature written in English; cultural values.
IP 363.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

IP 364.title: Philippine Popular Culture
IP 364.subject: IP
IP 364.description: Explores the ethics of Philippine popular culture forms; teaches students how to produce, act, and perform in a select media form; and engages students in writing a critical analysis of these pop cultural expressions.

IP 365.title: South Asian Literature in Translation
IP 365.subject: IP
IP 365.description: Survey of traditional and modern literatures of South Asia; literature written originally in English.

IP 366.title: Literatures of Ancient India
IP 366.subject: IP
IP 366.description: Survey of South Asia literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation.

IP 367.title: Persian Theater and Culture
IP 367.subject: IP
IP 367.description: Study of Persian and Iranian theater and culture with an overview of history from 2500 B.C. to the contemporary era.

IP 368.title: Introduction to South/Southeast Asian Film, History, Theory and Appreciation
IP 368.subject: IP
IP 368.description: Study and analysis of South/Southeast Asian films– history, forms, development, theoretical framework and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical and aesthetic context. (B) Filipino; (C) Iranian. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. A-F only for (B). ((C) Cross-listed as PER 368)

IP 370.title: Philippine Travelogue: People, Places, and Practices
IP 370.subject: IP
IP 370.description: A virtual guided tour of the Philippines that explores its multi-culture diversity through its people, places, and practices.

IP 373.title: Vedic Hindu Mythology
IP 373.subject: IP
IP 373.description: Study of major Hindu myths of the Vedic Sanskrit literature within the perspective of ancient Indian civilization. Literary sources will be tapped for understanding creation, cosmogony and celestial, atmospheric and terrestrial divinities. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

IP 374.title: Classical Hindu Mythology
IP 374.subject: IP
IP 374.description: Study of major myths of Epic Sanskrit literature, primarily with focus of the Ramayana and Mahabharata. Literary sources will be tapped for appreciating myths and epics, especially with reference to dharma, karma, ways of life. Sophomore standing or consent.

IP 375.title: Philippine Traditional Games and Pastimes
IP 375.subject: IP
IP 375.description: Introduces an experiential approach in the study of games and pastimes from various regions in the Philippines. It also focuses on the historical and socio-cultural aspects of Philippine games.

IP 376.title: Philippine Diasporic Literatures
IP 376.subject: IP
IP 376.description: Appreciation, reexamination, and analysis of Philippine literature of exile; a reevaluation of Philippine writing from the diaspora. Sophomore standing or higher or consent.

IP 377.title: Critical Discourses in IPLL Studies: Philippines
IP 377.subject: IP
IP 377.description: Revaluation and analysis of critical discourses in Philippine languages and literatures and an examination of alternative perspectives to the prevailing studies on Philippine culture; an appreciation of emerging knowledge on the Philippines.
IP 377.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

IP 382.title: Philippine Visual Art from Burial Jars to Burning Effigies
IP 382.subject: IP
IP 382.description: Introduction to the arts and material culture of the Philippines from the pre-colonial to the contemporary period through the examination of sculpture, metalwork, ceramics, textiles, and painting from various ethnolinguistic groups.

IP 389.title: Theories in Ilokano Studies
IP 389.subject: IP
IP 389.description: Examines the various theories employed in the study of Ilokano society, language, and culture from a variety of historical periods. Junior standing or higher, or consent. (Alt. years: spring)

IP 391.title: Literary Cultural Relations (Philippines and Southeast Asia)
IP 391.subject: IP
IP 391.description: An appreciation, a reexamination, and an analysis of the literary and cultural relations among the various nation states of Southeast Asia. Various texts are examined to establish the connections of these nation states. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent. (Alt. years)

IP 394.title: Philippine Sociolinguistics: Language Use, Ideologies, and Identities
IP 394.subject: IP
IP 394.description: Examines the intersection between language and society, specifically Philippine languages in the Philippines and in the Filipino diasporic communities. Will examine how language policies, discourses, and ideologies share people’s use of language.

IP 395.title: Polynesian Folklore in Translation
IP 395.subject: IP
IP 395.description: Traditional Polynesian genres (legends, myths, folktales, fables, proverbs, songs, riddles, jokes) examined in translation and culturally and structurally interpreted.

IP 396.title: Philippine Literature and Folklore in Translation
IP 396.subject: IP
IP 396.description: Philippine folk literature translated into English: epics, myths, legends, and other folklore. Classic works of vernacular writers.
IP 396.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

IP 399.title: Third-Level Language Study
IP 399.subject: IP
IP 399.description: Third-level study of a South Asian, Southeast Asian, or Pacific language. Contact hours and credits determined by student interests and faculty resources.
IP 399.prereq_raw: at least 6 credits of intermediate study of the same language

IP 470.title: Folklore

IP 499.title: Directed Studies

MAO 384.title: Te Reo Waiata: Mâori Language in Song

MAO 401.title: Fourth-Level Maori I

PER 367.description: Study of Persian and Iranian theater and culture with an overview of history from 2500 B.C. to the contemporary era.

PER 368C.title: Introduction to South/Southeast Asian Film, History, Theory and Appreciation
PER 368C.subject: PER
PER 368C.description: Study and analysis of South/Southeast Asian films–history, forms, development, theoretical framework and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical and aesthetic context. (C) Iranian. Sophomore standing or higher, or consent.

PER 430.title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
PER 430.subject: PER
PER 430.description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires.

PRAK 481.title: Introduction to Prakrit I
PRAK 481.subject: PRAK
PRAK 481.description: Survey of principal Prakrit languages; selected readings and analysis.
PRAK 481.prereq_raw: PALI 381, PALI 382, SNSK 281, and SNSK 282; or equivalent

SAM 101.title: Elementary Samoan
SAM 101.subject: SAM
SAM 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four hours weekly.

SAM 201.title: Intermediate Samoan
SAM 201.subject: SAM
SAM 201.description: Continuation of 102. Meets four hours weekly, three of four hours devoted to drill and practice.

SAM 227.title: Overview of Samoan Literature in English
SAM 227.subject: SAM
SAM 227.description: Survey of major writers of Samoan literature in English; lectures, discussions, short paper.

SAM 301.title: Third-Level Samoan: Traditional Culture
SAM 301.subject: SAM
SAM 301.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced reading and composition with development of language structure integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected traditional cultural topics. Meets three times weekly; additional lab work.

SAM 302.title: Third-Level Samoan: Contemporary Culture
SAM 302.subject: SAM
SAM 302.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced reading and composition with development of language structure integrated in a variety of communicative and creative activities based on selected contemporary cultural topics.

SAM 321.title: Samoan Conversation: Traditional Contexts
SAM 321.subject: SAM
SAM 321.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Samoan in traditional contexts.

SAM 322.title: Samoan Conversation: Contemporary Contexts
SAM 322.subject: SAM
SAM 322.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Samoan in modern contexts.

SAM 421.title: Samoan Ceremonial Speech
SAM 421.subject: SAM
SAM 421.description: Development of oratory skills in Samoan ceremonial speech. Emphasis on institutionalized applications such as the kava ceremony and formal speechmaking.

SAM 431.title: Samoan Oral Traditions
SAM 431.subject: SAM
SAM 431.description: Historical survey and analysis of the oral traditions and genealogies of Samoa with special emphasis on the relationship of these traditions with Samoan ceremonial speech.

SAM 452.title: Structure of Samoan
SAM 452.subject: SAM
SAM 452.description: Study of modern Samoan grammar including some sociolinguistic background.

SAM 461.title: Traditional Samoan Literature
SAM 461.subject: SAM
SAM 461.description: A survey of the major genres of traditional Samoan literature. Taught in the Samoan language.

SNSK 181.title: Introduction to Sanskrit
SNSK 181.subject: SNSK
SNSK 181.description: Introduction to basic Sanskrit grammar; reading and analysis of progressively difficult classical texts.

SNSK 281.title: Intermediate Sanskrit
SNSK 281.subject: SNSK
SNSK 281.description: Continuation of 182. Reading and analysis of classical texts with review of grammar.

SNSK 381.title: Third-Level Sanskrit
SNSK 381.subject: SNSK
SNSK 381.description: Continuation of 282. Reading and analysis of various classical texts.

SNSK 481.title: Fourth-Level Sanskrit
SNSK 481.subject: SNSK
SNSK 481.description: Continuation of 382. Reading, analysis, and interpretation of various Vedic or Sanskrit texts selected according to students’ interests.

SNSK 685.title: Advanced Readings in Sanskrit
SNSK 685.subject: SNSK
SNSK 685.description: Advanced study of Sanskrit literature (kâvya) and systematic thought (sâstra), alongside reading and discussion of scholarship on these topics. Specific content will change each semester.

TAHT 103.title: First Year Tahitian I
TAHT 103.subject: TAHT
TAHT 103.description: Basic core skills of listening, speaking and grammar of spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 104.title: First Year Tahitian II
TAHT 104.subject: TAHT
TAHT 104.description: Basic core skills of listening, speaking and grammar of spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 203.title: Second Year Tahitian I
TAHT 203.subject: TAHT
TAHT 203.description: Intermediate core skills of listening, speaking and knowledge of grammar for spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 204.title: Second Year Tahitian II
TAHT 204.subject: TAHT
TAHT 204.description: Intermediate core skills of listening, speaking and knowledge of grammar for spoken Tahitian in a condensed format. Meets three 50-minute sessions weekly.

TAHT 301.title: Third-Level Tahitian
TAHT 301.subject: TAHT
TAHT 301.description: Continuation of 202. Conversation, advanced reading, composition.

TAHT 358.title: Third-Level Tahitian Abroad
TAHT 358.subject: TAHT
TAHT 358.description: Full-time formal instruction at the University of French Polynesia in Tahiti. Third-year level in Tahitian language and culture.

TAHT 401.title: Fourth-Level Tahitian
TAHT 401.subject: TAHT
TAHT 401.description: Continuation of 302. Advanced conversation, reading, and writing with focus on modern formal and colloquial Tahitian styles. The language in the realms of storytelling, radio, folklore, traditional and modern writing. Survey of modern and classical language.

TAHT 458.title: Fourth-Level Tahitian Abroad
TAHT 458.subject: TAHT
TAHT 458.description: Full-time formal instruction at the University of French Polynesia in Tahiti. Fourth-year level in Tahitian language and culture.

THAI 101.title: First-Level Thai I
THAI 101.subject: THAI
THAI 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets one hour daily, Monday–Friday; four out of five hours devoted to directed drill and practice; regular on-line lab work and review of audiovisual materials.

THAI 103.title: Beginning Conversational Thai I
THAI 103.subject: THAI
THAI 103.description: Development of basic skills (listening, speaking, and grammar) of spoken Thai. Regular online lab work and review of audiovisual materials. Not open to students who have taken 101.

THAI 104.title: Beginning Conversational Thai II
THAI 104.subject: THAI
THAI 104.description: Continuation of 103. Development of basic skills (listening, speaking, and grammar) of spoken Thai. Regular online lab work and review of audiovisual materials. Not open to students who have taken 102.

THAI 105.title: Beginning Reading and Writing Thai I
THAI 105.subject: THAI
THAI 105.description: Development of literacy skills in Thai for those who cannot read or write in the language. Focus on Thai script reading and writing. Not open to students who have taken 101.

THAI 106.title: Beginning Reading and Writing Thai II
THAI 106.subject: THAI
THAI 106.description: Continuation of 105. Development of literacy skills in Thai for those who cannot read or write in the language. Focus on Thai script reading and writing. Not open to students who have taken 102.

THAI 107.title: Reading and Writing Thai Script
THAI 107.subject: THAI
THAI 107.description: Focus on Thai script reading and writing skills. For students with some aural and spoken skills in Standard Thai equivalent to those completing THAI 102 or higher, but cannot read or write in Thai script. Lab work.

THAI 201.title: Second-Level Thai I
THAI 201.subject: THAI
THAI 201.description: Continuation of 104 and 106, or 102. Integrated development of skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Thai script. Meets 5 hours/week, regular online lab work and review of on-line audio visual materials.

THAI 301.title: Third-Level Thai I
THAI 301.subject: THAI
THAI 301.description: Continuation of 202. Advanced conversation and reading, emphasis on modern written texts. Regular on-line lab work.

THAI 303.title: Accelerated Third-Level Thai
THAI 303.subject: THAI
THAI 303.description: Continuation of 202. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading; emphasis on modern written texts. Lab work.

THAI 401.title: Fourth-Level Thai I
THAI 401.subject: THAI
THAI 401.description: Continuation of 302/303. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

THAI 404.title: Accelerated Fourth-Level Thai
THAI 404.subject: THAI
THAI 404.description: Continuation of 303. Meets six hours a week. Advanced conversation and reading of specialized, scholarly texts.

THAI 415.title: Thai Language in the Media
THAI 415.subject: THAI
THAI 415.description: Development of reading and aural comprehension of authentic Thai language used in print and broadcast media through reading Thai newspapers, viewing and listening to Thai television and radio programs. Oral and written reports.

THAI 451.title: Structure of Thai
THAI 451.subject: THAI
THAI 451.description: Introduction to information structure of Thai as a basis for developing reading skills. Analysis of rhetorical, sentence, and word structure from different types of written texts.

TONG 101.title: Beginning Tongan
TONG 101.subject: TONG
TONG 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. Structural points introduced inductively. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

TONG 201.title: Intermediate Tongan
TONG 201.subject: TONG
TONG 201.description: Listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills. History and culture. Meets four (4) hours weekly.

URDU 205.title: Reading and Writing in Urdu
URDU 205.subject: URDU
URDU 205.description: Introduces students to the Nastaliq (Urdu) script, alphabets, their various forms, and combination rules. Reading and writing is emphasized.

VIET 101.title: Elementary Vietnamese
VIET 101.subject: VIET
VIET 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Structural points introduced inductively. Meets one hour daily, Monday–Friday; four out of five hours devoted to directed drill and practice.

VIET 201.title: Intermediate Vietnamese
VIET 201.subject: VIET
VIET 201.description: Continuation of 102. After completion, most students should be able to use all major sentence patterns to produce sounds, combinations of sounds, tones, and intonation and have some understanding of Vietnamese culture. Meets one hour daily, Monday– Friday.

VIET 301.title: Third-Level Vietnamese
VIET 301.subject: VIET
VIET 301.description: Continuation of 202. Emphasis on increased proficiency and cultural understanding through interaction with Vietnamese media, including newspapers, radio, film, etc.

VIET 401.title: Fourth-Level Vietnamese
VIET 401.subject: VIET
VIET 401.description: Continuation of 302. Emphasis on cultural understanding through modern literary Vietnamese.

VIET 461.title: Introduction to Vietnamese Literature
VIET 461.subject: VIET
VIET 461.description: Selected readings in major genres; emphasis on analysis. Modern literature.

ASL 101.title: Elementary American Sign Language I
ASL 101.subject: ASL
ASL 101.description: Development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 102.title: Elementary American Sign Language II
ASL 102.subject: ASL
ASL 102.description: Continued development of basic receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 201.title: Intermediate American Sign Language I
ASL 201.subject: ASL
ASL 201.description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 202.title: Intermediate American Sign Language II
ASL 202.subject: ASL
ASL 202.description: Continued development of receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language; linguistic structure introduced inductively through mix of lectures and discussion; includes discussion of history and culture of Deaf community in the U.S.

ASL 301.title: Advanced American Sign Language I
ASL 301.subject: ASL
ASL 301.description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

ASL 302.title: Advanced American Sign Language II
ASL 302.subject: ASL
ASL 302.description: Development of advanced receptive and expressive conversational skills in American Sign Language (ASL).

CLAS 121.title: Ancient Egypt: Mummies, Pharaohs, and Gods
CLAS 121.subject: CLAS
CLAS 121.description: An overview of ancient Egyptian civilization through lectures and class discussion on Egyptian literature, archaeology, history, religion and society.

CLAS 122.title: Greek, Roman, and Ancient Mythology
CLAS 122.subject: CLAS
CLAS 122.description: Combines readings and analyses of myths from the ancient world including Europe, Asia, Africa, and Hawai‘i, with an emphasis on comparative analysis of cultures and religions.

CLAS 123.title: Greek and Latin Elements in English
CLAS 123.subject: CLAS
CLAS 123.description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a literary vocabulary.

CLAS 124.title: Greek and Latin Elements in Scientific Terminology
CLAS 124.subject: CLAS
CLAS 124.description: Important roots, prefixes, and suffixes for building a scientific vocabulary.

CLAS 151.title: World Myth to 1500 C.E.
CLAS 151.subject: CLAS
CLAS 151.description: Reading and analysis of myths and legends from around the globe, from before the dawn of writing to 1500 C.E. Students will learn to interpret traditional stories from several theoretical and cross-cultural perspectives.

CLAS 301.title: Biblical Hebrew I
CLAS 301.subject: CLAS
CLAS 301.description: Orthography and structure of Biblical Hebrew, history and development of Hebrew as the sacred language of Judaism, overview of religious and historical development of the Hebrew Bible.

CLAS 302.title: Biblical Hebrew II
CLAS 302.subject: CLAS
CLAS 302.description: Reading of selected prose passages from the Hebrew Bible; analysis of literacy forms, paying special attention to stories which have played an important role in the development of the Abrahamic religions. Minimum C- grade required for prerequisites.

CLAS 305.title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics I
CLAS 305.subject: CLAS
CLAS 305.description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts.

CLAS 306.title: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphics II
CLAS 306.subject: CLAS
CLAS 306.description: Decipherment of hieroglyphs and reading of Middle Egyptian literary texts, including Tale of Sinuhe.

CLAS 321.title: History of the Written Word
CLAS 321.subject: CLAS
CLAS 321.description: A hands-on history of writing beginning in Ancient Greece and Rome. Content includes the development of the alphabet, scripts, books, libraries, and writing in ancient culture. Sophomore standing or consent.

CLAS 323.title: Greek and Roman Drama
CLAS 323.subject: CLAS
CLAS 323.description: Survey of Greek and Roman drama, both tragedies and comedies, tracing the history of a genre that contains some of the wittiest and most agonizing moments in ancient literature.

CLAS 324.title: Nature in the Ancient World
CLAS 324.subject: CLAS
CLAS 324.description: Study of the relationship between the Greeks and Romans and the natural environment. Particular attention will be given to the place of nature in ancient science, philosophy, literature, and “real life.”

CLAS 325.title: Greek and Roman War Literature
CLAS 325.subject: CLAS
CLAS 325.description: Survey of war-related literature from Greece and Rome, its major themes, and how it reflects the wide range of social, political, intellectual, and literary perspectives on war found in the ancient world.
CLAS 325.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

CLAS 326.title: The Greek and Roman Novel
CLAS 326.subject: CLAS
CLAS 326.description: Survey of Greek and Roman novels, a collection of highly entertaining texts that offer windows into various aspects of life in the ancient world.

CLAS 327.title: Ancient Greek Literature in Translation
CLAS 327.subject: CLAS
CLAS 327.description: Major writers: emphasis on Homer, drama, and philosophy.
CLAS 327.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher or consent

CLAS 328.title: Ancient Roman Literature in Translation
CLAS 328.subject: CLAS
CLAS 328.description: Major writers: emphasis on Vergil, satire, and novel.
CLAS 328.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher or consent

CLAS 329.title: Greek and Roman Epic
CLAS 329.subject: CLAS
CLAS 329.description: A survey of Greek and Roman epic literature, beginning with Homer’s Iliad and Odyssey and proceeding through the Hellenistic Greek and Roman periods.

CLAS 355.title: Archaeology of Ancient Greece
CLAS 355.subject: CLAS
CLAS 355.description: Introduction to the field of Greek archaeology and methods of archaeological research in the Mediterranean.

CLAS 356.title: Archaeology of Ancient Rome
CLAS 356.subject: CLAS
CLAS 356.description: Examines the archaeology of the Roman world from the Etruscan period to the reign of the emperor Constantine.

CLAS 366.title: Literatures of Ancient India
CLAS 366.subject: CLAS
CLAS 366.description: Survey of South Asian literature from ancient times to the early medieval period; focusing on Sanskrit, Prakrit, and Tamil poetry traditions. Readings in English translation.

CLAS 373.title: Art of Greece and Rome
CLAS 373.subject: CLAS
CLAS 373.description: Minoan and Mycenaean arts; Greece and Rome.

CLAS 430.title: Persia, Greece, and Rome in the Classical Age
CLAS 430.subject: CLAS
CLAS 430.description: Historical examination of the interaction between the Achaemenid and Parthian empires of Persia and the classical societies of the Mediterranean, such as the Greek city-states, Macedonia, the Hellenistic, and Roman Empires.

CLAS 490.title: Classics Capstone
CLAS 490.subject: CLAS
CLAS 490.description: The Classics capstone involves the preparation of a major research paper or project that represents the culmination of the Classics degree. Topics are chosen based on student interest and experience.

FR 110.title: Immersion French-Elementary
FR 110.subject: FR
FR 110.description: Content of 101-102 covered in one semester. Three two-hour sessions per week.

FR 210.title: Immersion French-Intermediate
FR 210.subject: FR
FR 210.description: Content of 201-202 covered in one semester. Three two-hour sessions per week.

FR 258.title: Intermediate French Abroad
FR 258.subject: FR
FR 258.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the second-year level in French language and culture in a French-speaking country.

FR 301.title: French Phonetics
FR 301.subject: FR
FR 301.description: Analysis of phonological system; methods of teaching pronunciation; understanding various types of spontaneous speech. Drills in pronunciation, intonation, stress, and rhythm.

FR 302.title: Reading in French
FR 302.subject: FR
FR 302.description: Development of language skills through reading of cultural and literary texts.

FR 306.title: Structure of French
FR 306.subject: FR
FR 306.description: Structure of contemporary French as analyzed by descriptive linguists.

FR 311.title: Conversation
FR 311.subject: FR
FR 311.description: Systematic practice for control of spoken French. Further development of vocabulary for accurate, mature expression.

FR 312.title: Composition
FR 312.subject: FR
FR 312.description: Emphasis on strengthening facility with language through further training in syntax, structure, and composition writing.

FR 321.title: Advanced Conversation
FR 321.subject: FR
FR 321.description: Systematic and advanced practice for control of spoken French, advanced development for accurate, mature expression.

FR 331.title: Survey of French Literature
FR 331.subject: FR
FR 331.prereq_raw: 311 (or concurrent) and 312; only 311 may be concurrent

FR 332.title: Survey of French Literature
FR 332.subject: FR
FR 332.prereq_raw: 311 (or concurrent) and 312; only 311 may be concurrent

FR 358.title: Third-Level French Abroad
FR 358.subject: FR
FR 358.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.

FR 360.title: Intensive Third-Level French Abroad
FR 360.subject: FR
FR 360.description: Intensive formal instruction at the third-year level in French language skills: reading, writing, grammar, or conversation in a French-speaking country.

FR 361.title: Contemporary French Civilization
FR 361.subject: FR
FR 361.description: Survey of culture and institutions of modern France.

FR 364.title: Survey of French Civilization
FR 364.subject: FR
FR 364.description: A historical survey of the development of French culture. The course is interdisciplinary, focusing on the relations between politics, literature, science, and the arts.

FR 399.title: Directed Reading
FR 399.subject: FR
FR 399.description: Independent study of approved reading with faculty supervision.

FR 405.title: Advanced Oral and Written Expression
FR 405.subject: FR
FR 405.description: Further development of listening, comprehension, speaking, and writing skills through viewing of French videotapes, reading French newspapers, frequent oral and written reports.
FR 405.prereq_raw: 311 and 312, or 306, or 358, or 360; or consent

FR 406.title: French-English Translation
FR 406.subject: FR
FR 406.description: Practice in techniques based on contrastive linguistics. Translation of texts from various fields from French into English and the reverse.

FR 408.title: Masterpieces of Medieval Literature
FR 408.subject: FR
FR 408.description: Samplings from epic, novel, verse and prose, tale, lyric poetry, chronicle, theater, didactic literature. Elementary readings in original text in editions giving modern French translation.

FR 409.title: Advanced Language Study: French
FR 409.subject: FR
FR 409.description: Advanced course in spoken and written French with intensive review of alternative grammatical structures and shades of meaning in the modern language. Graduates who have not taken prerequisites may request consent.

FR 410.title: Masterpieces of 16th-Century Literature
FR 410.subject: FR
FR 410.description: Samplings from all major writers of the period. Readings in original text in editions giving modern French equivalents for difficult words.

FR 411.title: Masterpieces of 17th-Century Literature
FR 411.subject: FR
FR 411.description: Principal works of major dramatists: Corneille, Moliere, Racine. Principal movements and major authors of non-dramatic prose and poetry.

FR 417.title: 19th Century French Prose and Poetry
FR 417.subject: FR
FR 417.description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 19th century France: romanticism, realism, symbolism, aestheticism.

FR 421.title: 20th-Century French Theater
FR 421.subject: FR
FR 421.description: Major French playwrights and their works: Claudel, Giraudoux, Anouilh, Sartre, Camus, etc.

FR 423.title: 20th Century French Prose and Poetry
FR 423.subject: FR
FR 423.description: Study of representative prose and poetry of the major trends of 20th century France: modernism, surrealism, existentialism, postmodernism and multiculturalism.

FR 458.title: Fourth-Level French Abroad
FR 458.subject: FR
FR 458.description: Intensive course of full-time formal instruction on the fourth-year level in French linguistics, civilization, culture, and literature in a French-speaking country.

FR 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level French Abroad
FR 460.subject: FR
FR 460.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourthyear level in French language, culture and literature in a French-speaking country. For semester programs only.

FR 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
FR 499.subject: FR
FR 499.description: Independent study of approved readings and research with faculty supervision.

FR 506.title: French for Reading Proficiency
FR 506.subject: FR
FR 506.description: Reading of scholarly and technical French for graduate students; open to undergraduates with consent of department chair. Not applicable to undergraduate language requirement.

FR 601.title: Seminar in 20th-Century French Literature
FR 601.subject: FR
FR 601.description: Authors and movements of modern period.

FR 609.title: French Renaissance
FR 609.subject: FR
FR 609.description: Poetry, theater, prose. Emphasis on Montaigne and Rabelais. Lectures, discussions, reports.

FR 620.title: Masterpieces of the 17th Century
FR 620.subject: FR
FR 620.description: Dramatic or prose works of the classical period.

FR 651.title: Philosophic Currents in 18th Century
FR 651.subject: FR
FR 651.description: Philosophic movements and their impact on the social, political, and literary life of the period and the modern era.

FR 661.title: Advanced French-English Translation: Practice and Theory
FR 661.subject: FR
FR 661.description: Advanced practice in translation into French and from French to English in various fields (literature, business, medicine, other), with reflection on choices. Readings in translation theory.

FR 671.title: History of the French Language
FR 671.subject: FR
FR 671.description: Origins and development of French language in its cultural context. Contrastive analysis.

FR 672.title: Seminar in Medieval Literature
FR 672.subject: FR
FR 672.description: Genesis and evolution of literary genres from the 12th to 15th centuries. Epic, romance, lyric poetry, prose, and drama.

FR 681.title: Seminar: The Novel in France
FR 681.subject: FR
FR 681.description: Novels which have influenced movements or established techniques.

FR 690.title: The Theater in France
FR 690.subject: FR
FR 690.description: Historical development; major dramatists who have influenced movements or established techniques.

FR 735.title: Seminar in French Literature
FR 735.subject: FR
FR 735.description: Study of authors or a period.
FR 735.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and French graduate advisor

GER 110.title: Intensive Elementary German
GER 110.subject: GER
GER 110.description: Combined content of 101 and 102 covered in one intensive course.

GER 260.title: Intensive Intermediate German Abroad
GER 260.subject: GER
GER 260.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the second-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

GER 301.title: Phonetics and Pronunciation Practice
GER 301.subject: GER
GER 301.description: Analysis of the German phonological system and practice in pronunciation.

GER 302.title: Structure of Modern German
GER 302.subject: GER
GER 302.description: Study of syntactic and morphological structures and basic pragmatic principles. Focuses on spoken and written Modern German.

GER 303.title: Reading and Writing
GER 303.subject: GER
GER 303.description: Further development of reading and writing skills through the study of modern short stories by major German language authors.

GER 304.title: Business German
GER 304.subject: GER
GER 304.description: Advanced German conversation, reading, and writing with a special emphasis on the vocabulary and cultural context of the German business world.

GER 305.title: Contemporary Topics in Media
GER 305.subject: GER
GER 305.description: Development of listening and speaking, reading and writing skills through analysis and discussion of media: newspaper articles, radio, and television programs and online sources.

GER 306.title: Conversation
GER 306.subject: GER
GER 306.description: Intensive practice in spoken German designed to increase vocabulary and improve oral proficiency.

GER 307.title: German for Reading I
GER 307.subject: GER
GER 307.description: Development of reading skills through the study of short scholarly, technical, and literary texts.

GER 308.title: German for Reading II
GER 308.subject: GER
GER 308.description: Further development of reading skills through the study of short scholarly, technical, and literary texts.

GER 312.title: Introduction to German Literature 1750- 1914:
GER 312.subject: GER
GER 312.description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1750 to 1914.

GER 313.title: Introduction to German Literature 1914-Present
GER 313.subject: GER
GER 313.description: Reading and discussion of representative works of German literature from 1914 to present.

GER 320.title: German Cinema
GER 320.subject: GER
GER 320.description: Study of German film history, film analysis, film theory, and film study. Lecture/discussion. 6 cr. limit on GER/LLEA 320 courses.

GER 360.title: Intensive Third-Level German Abroad
GER 360.subject: GER
GER 360.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the third-year level in German language and culture in Germany.

GER 361.title: Germanic Civilization to World War II
GER 361.subject: GER
GER 361.description: German cultural heritage and history in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland until World War II.

GER 362.title: Modern German Culture
GER 362.subject: GER
GER 362.description: Modern culture in post-World War II Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

GER 371.title: Practical German for use in Hawai‘i
GER 371.subject: GER
GER 371.description: Use of German in practical situations in Hawai‘i, e.g., in travel industry.

GER 409.title: Enlightenment—Sturm und Drang
GER 409.subject: GER
GER 409.description: Lessing and his contemporaries; early dramas of Goethe and Schiller; Goethe’s early lyrics.

GER 410.title: Classicism
GER 410.subject: GER
GER 410.description: Classical writings of Goethe and Schiller; some reference to other writers.

GER 411.title: Romanticism
GER 411.subject: GER
GER 411.description: Novalis, Tieck, E. T. A. Hoffmann, Eichendorff, etc.

GER 412.title: Poetic Realism
GER 412.subject: GER
GER 412.description: Masterworks by Büchner, Raabe, Storm, Keller, Meyer, Hebbel, and others.

GER 415.title: Culture of Two Germanies: 1945-1989
GER 415.subject: GER
GER 415.description: (taught in German) Literature, culture, and film of East and West Germany, 1945-1989. Credit cannot be earned for both LLEA 415 and GER 415.

GER 416.title: German Literature, Culture and Film: 1989 to Present
GER 416.subject: GER
GER 416.description: Study of German literature, culture and film, 1989 to present. Credit cannot be earned for both 416 and LLEA 416.

GER 428.title: Survey of German Lyric Poetry
GER 428.subject: GER
GER 428.description: Individual interpretation complements lectures on theoretical and historical background.

GER 460.title: Intensive Fourth-Level German Abroad
GER 460.subject: GER
GER 460.description: Intensive course of formal instruction on the fourth-level in German language and culture in a German-speaking country.

GRK 101.title: Elementary Greek
GRK 101.subject: GRK
GRK 101.description: Grammar and vocabulary, with reading of simple Greek.

GRK 201.title: Intermediate Greek
GRK 201.subject: GRK
GRK 201.description: Development of reading and translation skills. Emphasis on prose.

GRK 303.title: Greek Historians
GRK 303.subject: GRK
GRK 303.description: Selections from Herodotus, Xenophon, and others.

GRK 304.title: Greek Epic

ASTR 281.title: Astrobiology
ASTR 281.subject: ASTR
ASTR 281.description: Are we alone in the universe? Modern astronomical, biological, and geological perspectives on this fundamental question. Searches for life on Mars, oceans on Europa, planets orbiting other stars. Space exploration and colonies, interstellar spaceflight and communication.

ASTR 300.title: Observational Astronomy
ASTR 300.subject: ASTR
ASTR 300.description: Principles and techniques of optical and near-infrared astronomical observation. Astronomical coordinate systems. Telescopes, cameras, spectrographs, and detectors. Astrometry, photometry, and spectroscopy of astronomical objects.

ASTR 300L.title: Observational Astronomy Laboratory
ASTR 300L.subject: ASTR
ASTR 300L.description: Optical and near-infrared astronomy laboratory. Error analysis, properties of light, data, and image processing. Astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic measurement.
ASTR 300L.prereq_raw: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or 274; PHYS 152L or 274L; MATH 216, 242, or 252A

ASTR 301.title: Observational Astronomy Projects
ASTR 301.subject: ASTR
ASTR 301.description: Practical astronomical observing. Students select objects to study, plan, and conduct remote observations using research-grade telescopes, reduce data, present results in written and verbal form. Introduces LaTeX, literature research, time allocation.

ASTR 320.title: Astronomical Spectroscopy
ASTR 320.subject: ASTR
ASTR 320.description: Introduction to astronomical spectroscopy. Stellar atmospheres, line formation, elements of radiative transfer. Phases of interstellar medium. Emission line diagnostics. Doppler shift and kinematics.
ASTR 320.prereq_raw: 210 or 242; PHYS 152 or 274; MATH 216 or 242 or 252A

ASTR 380.title: The Cosmos in Western Culture
ASTR 380.subject: ASTR
ASTR 380.description: History and intellectual context of astronomical discovery; the evolution of ideas of space, time, and motion from the Babylonians to relativistic cosmologies; emphasis on the interaction of astronomy with the history of ideas.

ASTR 399.title: Directed Study
ASTR 399.subject: ASTR
ASTR 399.description: Individual reading, observation, or experimentation in astronomy and astrophysics.

ASTR 423.title: Stellar Astrophysics
ASTR 423.subject: ASTR
ASTR 423.description: Advanced survey of stellar astrophysics, including application of astrometry, photometry, and spectrometry to determine fundamental stellar properties; stellar structure and evolution of single and binary stars; astrophysical distance determination methods; stellar nucleosynthesis.

ASTR 426.title: Galaxies & Cosmology
ASTR 426.subject: ASTR
ASTR 426.description: Survey of extragalactic astronomy and cosmology, including: galaxy morphology and kinematics; luminosity functions; dark matter; properties of galaxy groups/ clusters; gravitational lensing; redshifts; cosmological models; the Big Bang; thermal history of the Universe; structure formation.
ASTR 426.prereq_raw: 300 (or concurrent); PHYS 152 or PHYS 274; MATH 216 or MATH 242 or MATH 252A

ASTR 430.title: The Solar System
ASTR 430.subject: ASTR
ASTR 430.description: Observations and physical nature of planets and moons, asteroids, comets, and other small bodies; formation of the Solar System; discovery of other planetary systems; solar activity.
ASTR 430.prereq_raw: 300; and PHYS 152 or 274; and MATH 216, 242, or 252A

ASTR 494.title: Senior Research Project
ASTR 494.subject: ASTR
ASTR 494.description: Seminar focusing on development of professional skills for astronomical research, and on scientific writing as a tool for organizing research. A final paper describing a supervised research project is required.

ASTR 622.title: The Interstellar Medium
ASTR 622.subject: ASTR
ASTR 622.description: Astrophysics of diffuse matter, HII regions, molecular clouds, etc.

ASTR 623.title: Stellar Interiors and Evolution
ASTR 623.subject: ASTR
ASTR 623.description: Structure and evolution; energy sources, radiative processes; relations to observables.

ASTR 626.title: Galaxies
ASTR 626.subject: ASTR
ASTR 626.description: Observations and stellar dynamics of elliptical and spiral galaxies including our galaxy, globular clusters, and dark matter. Galaxy formation and evolution.

ASTR 627.title: Cosmology
ASTR 627.subject: ASTR
ASTR 627.description: Geometry and evolution of the universe. Dark matter. Early universe. Formation of large–scale structure, galaxies, and clusters. Cosmological models.

ASTR 630.title: The Solar System
ASTR 630.subject: ASTR
ASTR 630.description: Survey of observational data and physical concepts on planets and smaller bodies; formation of planetary systems; solar activity.

ASTR 631.title: Radiative Transfer Stellar Atmospheres
ASTR 631.subject: ASTR
ASTR 631.description: Excitation, ionization, and radiative transfer in stellar atmospheres; model atmospheres, formation of line and continuum radiation.

ASTR 633.title: Astrophysical Techniques
ASTR 633.subject: ASTR
ASTR 633.description: Telescopes, positional astronomy, photon detection, error analysis, photometry, spectroscopy.

ASTR 634.title: Astronomical Instrumentation
ASTR 634.subject: ASTR
ASTR 634.description: Design and operation of astronomical instrumentation. Physics of optical and infrared detectors. Wavefront sensors and adaptive optics. Radio and infrared interferometry. Optical design: methods and software.

ASTR 635.title: Fundamentals of Astrophysics
ASTR 635.subject: ASTR
ASTR 635.description: Applications of fundamental physics to astrophysical situations. Elements of general relativity. Basics of hydrodynamics and shock waves. Radiative processes, high energy astrophysics. Modern dynamics.

ASTR 640.title: General Relativity
ASTR 640.subject: ASTR
ASTR 640.description: Introduction to gravity and general relativity. Tensor basics, classical scalar, vector and tensor field theories. Exact symmetric Einstein equation, gravito-magnetic weak field, and radiation solutions.

ASTR 641.title: Active Galaxies
ASTR 641.subject: ASTR
ASTR 641.description: Phenomenology of active galactic nuclei, black holes, accretion flows and jets, emission mechanisms, host galaxies, and cosmic evolution.

ASTR 657.title: Astrochemistry-A Molecular Approach
ASTR 657.subject: ASTR
ASTR 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

ASTR 734.title: Astronomy Seminar I
ASTR 734.subject: ASTR
ASTR 734.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 735.title: Astronomy Seminar II
ASTR 735.subject: ASTR
ASTR 735.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 736.title: Astronomy Seminar III
ASTR 736.subject: ASTR
ASTR 736.description: Selected advanced topics in astronomy and astrophysics. Available for 1 to 3 credit hours by arrangement.

ASTR 740.title: Astrobiology Seminar: Origin, Evolution and the Role of Water for Life in the Universe
ASTR 740.subject: ASTR
ASTR 740.description: Interdisciplinary research topics in astrobiology as they relate to the theme of water: formation in space, role in creating pre-biotic molecules, delivery to earth, and terrestrial planet habitability.
ASTR 740.prereq_raw: graduate level sciences and ideas, or consent

ASTR 750.title: Scientific Grant Writing
ASTR 750.subject: ASTR
ASTR 750.description: Principles of scientific grant writing are taught by working on draft proposals through a mix of lectures, discussions, and hands on activities. The final proposal will be reviewed and evaluated via a review panel. Graduate students only.

ASTR 777.title: Star Formation
ASTR 777.subject: ASTR
ASTR 777.description: Molecular clouds, collapse processes, physics of circumstellar disks and accretion, properties of young stars, outflows and jets, formation of binaries, extrasolar planets and planet formation, meteorites and the early solar system.

ASTR 790.title: Astro-ph Seminar
ASTR 790.subject: ASTR
ASTR 790.description: Seminar discussions of the most recent research papers covering all areas of astronomy. Student lead discussion sessions and discuss papers of their choice during the semester. Graduate students only.

BIOL 101.title: Biology and Society
BIOL 101.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101.description: Characteristics of science, historical development of scientific concepts, and interaction of society with science illustrated by topics from biological science. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 101L.title: Biology & Society Laboratory
BIOL 101L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 104.title: Marine Option Program Seminar
BIOL 104.subject: BIOL
BIOL 104.description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 123.title: Hawaiian Environment Science
BIOL 123.subject: BIOL
BIOL 123.description: Characteristics of science and interaction with society illustrated by topics in geology, astronomy, oceanography, and biology of Hawaiian Islands. Not a BIOL major elective.

BIOL 171.title: Introduction to Biology I
BIOL 171.subject: BIOL
BIOL 171.description: Introductory biology for all life science majors. Cell structure and chemistry; growth, reproduction, genetics, evolution, viruses, bacteria, and simple eukaryotes.
BIOL 171.prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171L (or concurrent), or consent

BIOL 171L.title: Introduction to Biology I Lab
BIOL 171L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 171L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 171. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
BIOL 171L.prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 171 (or concurrent) or consent

BIOL 172.title: Introduction to Biology II
BIOL 172.subject: BIOL
BIOL 172.description: Anatomy, physiology, and systematics of plants and animals; behavior; ecosystems, populations, and communities.
BIOL 172.prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172L (or concurrent), or consent

BIOL 172L.title: Introduction to Biology II Lab
BIOL 172L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 172L.prereq_raw: CHEM (131, 151, 161, 171, or 181A) or concurrent, and BIOL 172 (or concurrent) or consent

BIOL 220.title: Biostatistics
BIOL 220.subject: BIOL
BIOL 220.description: Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
BIOL 220.prereq_raw: 171, 172 or BOT 101; and BIOL/BOT 220L (or concurrent) and MATH 134 or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140

BIOL 220L.title: Biostatistics Lab
BIOL 220L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 220L.prereq_raw: 171 or 172 or BOT 101; and 220 (or concurrent); and MATH 134 or MATH assessment exam (with score for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score for MATH 140

BIOL 265.title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology
BIOL 265.subject: BIOL
BIOL 265.description: Principles of ecology and evolution for life science majors stressing integrated approach and recent advance.
BIOL 265.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172, 172L (or concurrent), and 265L (or concurrent)

BIOL 265L.title: Ecology and Evolutionary Biology Lab
BIOL 265L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 265L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory to accompany 265. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction, and requires a minimum of 4,000 words of graded writing.
BIOL 265L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265 (or concurrent)

BIOL 275.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
BIOL 275.subject: BIOL
BIOL 275.description: Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology.
BIOL 275.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L and CHEM 272

BIOL 275L.title: Cell and Molecular Biology Lab
BIOL 275L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 275L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Laboratory for Cell and Molecular Biology.
BIOL 275L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275 (or concurrent) and CHEM 272

BIOL 295.title: Service Learning for Biology Majors
BIOL 295.subject: BIOL
BIOL 295.description: Directed participation on tutorials and related activities in public schools and approved community and UH Mânoa organizations.

BIOL 301.title: Marine Ecology and Evolution
BIOL 301.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301.description: Functional, ecological, and evolutionary problems faced by life in the sea. Draws from major marine habitats and associated communities, from the deep sea to the plankton. Impacts of overfishing, marine pollution, and land development on the ecology and evolution of marine organisms. Emphasis on developing problem solving and quantitative skills.
BIOL 301.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265/265L, 301L (or concurrent), and OCN 201; or consent

BIOL 301L.title: Marine Ecology and Evolution Lab
BIOL 301L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 301L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 301 (or concurrent)

BIOL 304.title: Biotechnology: Science and Ethical Issues
BIOL 304.subject: BIOL
BIOL 304.description: Introduction to the concepts, goals, ethical issues and consequences of biotechnology using real-life case studies of GMOs, cloning, DNA fingerprinting, gene therapy and genetical engineering.

BIOL 305.title: Ecology
BIOL 305.subject: BIOL
BIOL 305.description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

BIOL 306.title: Ethology
BIOL 306.subject: BIOL
BIOL 306.description: Introduction to animal and human ethology and sociobiology; emphasis on social and interspecific behavior, its causes and adaptive significance. Lab optional.
BIOL 306.prereq_raw: 171 and 171L and 172 and 172L or ANSC 201; or consent

BIOL 306L.title: Ethology Lab
BIOL 306L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 306L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of methods in the study of animal behavior by demonstrations, labs and projects.

BIOL 310.title: Environmental Issues
BIOL 310.subject: BIOL
BIOL 310.description: Global environmental problems in historical perspective; physical, biological, sociocultural views.
BIOL 310.prereq_raw: one of 101, 123, or GEO 101; or consent

BIOL 320.title: The Atoll
BIOL 320.subject: BIOL
BIOL 320.description: Atoll as ecosystem and as human environment. Formation, structure, distribution, biota.
BIOL 320.prereq_raw: two semesters of introductory science or consent. Not a BIOL major elective

BIOL 325.title: Biology of the Vertebrates
BIOL 325.subject: BIOL
BIOL 325.description: Introduction to the evolution and systematics of vertebrates, with emphasis on comparative morphology, physiology, and ecology.

BIOL 331.title: Marine Mammal Biology
BIOL 331.subject: BIOL
BIOL 331.description: Overview of marine mammal science, significance and roles of marine mammals in their ecosystems, and marine conservation issues. Current research topics in marine mammal science will also be covered.
BIOL 331.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172/172L, and 265, 265L; or consent

BIOL 331L.title: Marine Mammal Biology Lab
BIOL 331L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 331L.description: Laboratory to accompany 331. Activities will include taxonomy, anatomy, morphology, necropsy, hematology, population estimating methods, tracking, field distribution surveys, stranding response, and energetics, and/or similar depending on field access and availability of specimens.
BIOL 331L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L and 172/172L and 265/265L and 331 (or concurrent), or consent

BIOL 340.title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
BIOL 340.subject: BIOL
BIOL 340.description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society. Not a BIOL major elective.
BIOL 340.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

BIOL 345.title: Parasitology
BIOL 345.subject: BIOL
BIOL 345.description: Animal parasites of man, and domestic and wild animals; systematics, comparative morphology, life history, pathology, treatment, control.

BIOL 350.title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
BIOL 350.subject: BIOL
BIOL 350.description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance; genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, parenting, menopause, and aging.

BIOL 360.title: Island Ecosystems
BIOL 360.subject: BIOL
BIOL 360.description: Characteristics of island biota; examples from Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Impact of island and continental cultures; policy and ecosystem endangerment; contemporary legislation, policy, and management practices.
BIOL 360.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science or consent. Not a BIOL major elective

BIOL 363.title: Biological Field Studies
BIOL 363.subject: BIOL
BIOL 363.description: Biological survey, collection, and analysis techniques will be reviewed and applied through field studies. Students will be introduced to the uniqueness of the Hawaiian environment and its diversity of life. Emphasis on diversity, evolution and ecology.
BIOL 363.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265/265L (or equivalent), or consent

BIOL 375.title: Genetics
BIOL 375.subject: BIOL
BIOL 375.description: Genetic concepts at advanced undergraduate level; genetic transmission, recombination, gene action, mutation, population and evolutionary genetics.

BIOL 375L.title: Genetics Laboratory
BIOL 375L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 375L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments with a variety of organisms to illustrate principles discussed in BIOL 375.

BIOL 390.title: Communicating in Biological Sciences
BIOL 390.subject: BIOL
BIOL 390.description: Combined lecture/lab impart essential knowledge and skills in technical writing, poster design, and oral presentations for effective communication for life science majors. Research papers, lab reports, project proposals, conference presentations are covered.
BIOL 390.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 171/171L, 172/172L, and ENG 100

BIOL 395.title: Internship in Biology Teaching
BIOL 395.subject: BIOL
BIOL 395.description: Supervised laboratory internship in the preparation and demonstration of laboratory experiments in selected laboratory courses.

BIOL 400.title: Ocean Internships and Research
BIOL 400.subject: BIOL
BIOL 400.description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance.
BIOL 400.prereq_raw: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal

children.text: in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent , project proposal

BIOL 401.title: Molecular Biotechnology
BIOL 401.subject: BIOL
BIOL 401.description: General principles, applications, and recent advances of the rapidly growing science of biotechnology. Topics include impact of biotechnology on medicine, animal sciences, environment, agriculture, forensics, and economic and socio-ethical issues.
BIOL 401.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275 or consent

BIOL 402.title: Principles of Biochemistry
BIOL 402.subject: BIOL
BIOL 402.description: Molecular basis of living processes in bacteria, plants, and animals; emphasis on metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids.
BIOL 402.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275/275L, and CHEM 273; or consent

BIOL 403.title: Field Problems in Marine Biology
BIOL 403.subject: BIOL
BIOL 403.description: Integrated program of intensive lectures, laboratory experiments, and field research that focus on the biological processes that shape the lives of marine organisms. Limited space; enrollment by consent; GPA considered.
BIOL 403.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 301/301L and consent

BIOL 404.title: Advanced Topics in Marine Biology
BIOL 404.subject: BIOL
BIOL 404.description: Current themes in marine biology and experience in scientific assessment.
BIOL 404.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 301/301L or consent

BIOL 406.title: Biology of Marine Organisms
BIOL 406.subject: BIOL
BIOL 406.description: Biology, physiology, and ecology of marine organisms and marine ecosystems, and the physical and chemical factors, which influence them. Cannot be used to satisfy BS-MB major requirements. Credit granted for only one of ZOOL 200, BIOL 301, or BIOL 406. Junior standing or consent.

BIOL 407.title: Molecular Cell Biology I
BIOL 407.subject: BIOL
BIOL 407.description: Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level.
BIOL 407.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 275/275L and CHEM 273, or consent

BIOL 408.title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
BIOL 408.subject: BIOL
BIOL 408.description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules.
BIOL 408.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 407; or consent

BIOL 408L.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
BIOL 408L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 408L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany 407 and 408.

BIOL 410.title: Human Role in Environmental Change
BIOL 410.subject: BIOL
BIOL 410.description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
BIOL 410.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of 101, 123 or GEO 101 and either 310 or GEO 322; or consent

BIOL 411.title: Corals and Coral Reefs
BIOL 411.subject: BIOL
BIOL 411.description: The biogeography, evolution, ecology, and physiology of corals and coral reefs, and the application of this information to the management of coral reefs. Emphasis will be placed on processes such as dispersal, the evolution and operation of mutualisms, calcification, reproduction, and the maintenance of diversity.

BIOL 425.title: Wildlife and Plant Conservation
BIOL 425.subject: BIOL
BIOL 425.description: Principles of conservation biology and wildlife management techniques, illustrated with animal, plant, and ecosystem examples. Examination of ethical, cultural, legal, political, and socio-economic issues impinging on conservation policy and practice. Group project and field trips.
BIOL 425.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 265/265L or consent

BIOL 430.title: The Biology of Fungi
BIOL 430.subject: BIOL
BIOL 430.description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.

BIOL 430L.title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
BIOL 430L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

BIOL 440.title: Psychoactive Drug Plants
BIOL 440.subject: BIOL
BIOL 440.description: Taxonomy, ecology, biochemistry, distribution, cultural history, and contemporary use of mind-altering drug plants; examples from primitive, traditional, and modern societies.
BIOL 440.prereq_raw: junior standing, one semester of biological science, and either ANTH 200 or GEO 151; or consent

BIOL 454.title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
BIOL 454.subject: BIOL
BIOL 454.description: Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
BIOL 454.prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

BIOL 465.title: Fish Diversity
BIOL 465.subject: BIOL
BIOL 465.description: Survey of fish biodiversity focusing on major lineages, their phylogenetic relationships, and their geographic distribution in light of evolutionary history. Taught spring semester in alternate years. Junior standing or higher.

BIOL 465L.title: Fish Diversity Laboratory
BIOL 465L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 465L.description: (2 2-hr Lab) Overview of the major orders and families of fishes of the world; introduction to local Hawaiian fishes; coverage of basic fish anatomy; introduction to field and laboratory techniques in fish research. Junior standing or higher.

BIOL 468.title: The Rise of Fishes: An Evolutionary History
BIOL 468.subject: BIOL
BIOL 468.description: The origins and early evolution of fishes, with a focus on morphological innovations that have led to lineage divergence and adaptive radiation, and the nature of underlying processes associated with novel character trait evolution.

BIOL 470.title: Evolutionary Biology
BIOL 470.subject: BIOL
BIOL 470.description: Process of evolution: genetic basis, natural selection, population genetics, speciation, the fossil record.
BIOL 470.prereq_raw: 171 and 172. Recommended: a BIOL or ZOOL course at 300 or 400 level

children.text: Recommended: a BIOL or ZOOL course at 300 or 400 level

BIOL 472.title: The Biology of Cancer
BIOL 472.subject: BIOL
BIOL 472.description: Integrative, in-depth focus on the genetics, cell biology, and molecular basis of cancer. Combination of classroom lectures and problem-based discussions in small groups. Addresses ethical implications of cancer research and treatment. MCB or BIOL majors only. Senior standing or higher.

BIOL 480.title: Life in the Soil Environment
BIOL 480.subject: BIOL
BIOL 480.description: An interdisciplinary study of the diverse life in the soil beneath our feet that includes bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, invertebrate, viruses, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.
BIOL 480.prereq_raw: 375 or TPSS/PEPS/SUST 371, or MICR 351, or consent

BIOL 480L.title: Life in the Soil Environment Lab
BIOL 480L.subject: BIOL
BIOL 480L.description: Laboratory to accompany 480. Technical examination of bacteria, fungi, protists, nematodes, arthropods, and other invertebrate, and the essential functional roles these organisms contribute to sustainability of the planet.

BIOL 483.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Topics for Biologists
BIOL 483.subject: BIOL
BIOL 483.description: Focuses on the use of computational tools and approaches to analyze the enormous amount of biological data (DNA, RNA, protein) available today.

children.text: ( or equivalent), or consent . ( Once a year)

BIOL 485.title: Biology of the Invertebrates
BIOL 485.subject: BIOL
BIOL 485.description: Body plans, development, cellular construction, physiological integration, natural history, and ecology of invertebrate animals. Emphasis on marine species, especially local ones.

BIOL 490.title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
BIOL 490.subject: BIOL
BIOL 490.description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
BIOL 490.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher and consent

BIOL 499.title: Biological Problems
BIOL 499.subject: BIOL
BIOL 499.description: Directed reading and research. For juniors and seniors majoring in life science 1-12 credits.
BIOL 499.prereq_raw: 2.5 GPA minimum, written proposal and consent

BIOL 603.title: Molecular Ecology
BIOL 603.subject: BIOL
BIOL 603.description: ) Practical introduction to molecular methods used to address ecological and evolutionary questions. Advanced undergraduate/graduate level. Focus on methods and application to independent research project.
BIOL 603.prereq_raw: 265/265L (or equivalent) or 275/275L (or equivalent), and 375/375L, and consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) or 275 / 275L ( or equivalent), and 375 / 375L , and consent

BIOL 650.title: Population Genetics
BIOL 650.subject: BIOL
BIOL 650.description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.
BIOL 650.prereq_raw: consent.  Professional Development Courses for Science Teachers

children.text: Professional Development Courses for Science Teachers

BOT 100.title: Freshman Seminar
BOT 100.subject: BOT
BOT 100.description: Discussion of hot topics in botany, including conservation of rare plants, invasive species, marine botany, ethnobotany, poisonous plants, evolution in action, fungal networks, and careers in botany with emphasis on Hawaiian examples. Students should enroll in BOT 100 and 101/101L, or BOT 100 and BIOL 171/171L.

BOT 101.title: General Botany
BOT 101.subject: BOT
BOT 101.description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

BOT 101A.title: General Botany
BOT 101A.subject: BOT
BOT 101A.description: Growth, functions, and evolution of plants; their relations to the environment and particularly to humans and human activities.

BOT 101L.title: General Botany Lab
BOT 101L.subject: BOT
BOT 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab observations and experiments illustrating basic principles of plant biology.

BOT 105.title: Ethnobotany
BOT 105.subject: BOT
BOT 105.description: Plants and their influence on culture and history including: plant domestication and agriculture; plant biogeography and human migration; plant use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; and cultural aspects of plant conservation.

BOT 105A.title: Ethnobotany
BOT 105A.subject: BOT
BOT 105A.description: Plants and their influence on culture and history including: plant domestication and agriculture; plant biogeography and human migration; plant use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; and cultural aspects of plant conservation.

BOT 105L.title: Ethnobotany Laboratory
BOT 105L.subject: BOT
BOT 105L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory exercises, experiments, and analysis in ethnobotany.

BOT 107.title: Plants, People, and Culture
BOT 107.subject: BOT
BOT 107.description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

BOT 107A.title: Plants, People, and Culture
BOT 107A.subject: BOT
BOT 107A.description: Ethnobotany. Interactions between plants and people: use in religious, medical, and shamanic traditions; roles in cultural formation, destruction, and revolution; plant domestication and food systems; roles in human migration; cultural components of plant conservation.

BOT 110.title: Biodiversity: Evolution, Ecology, & Conservation
BOT 110.subject: BOT
BOT 110.description: Lecture exploring the range of Earth’s diversity, the evolutionary processes that generate it, the ecological roles it plays, the consequences of its loss, and the processes by which it can be conserved.

BOT 110L.title: Biodiversity: Evolution, Ecology, & Conservation Laboratory
BOT 110L.subject: BOT
BOT 110L.description: Laboratory and outdoor observations and experiments examining the range of biological diversity among the Earth’s species and ecosystems.

BOT 130.title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance
BOT 130.subject: BOT
BOT 130.description: Introduction to the native flora of Hawai‘i, its origin, evolution and ecology, and the observation, identification, and systematics of the Hawaiian flora.

BOT 130L.title: Hawaiian Plants-Their Ecology and Cultural Significance Lab
BOT 130L.subject: BOT
BOT 130L.description: The exploration of concepts and the process of science through hands-on experience in studying Hawaiian and introduced plants, their ecology, and cultural significance.

BOT 135.title: Magical Mushrooms and Mystical Molds
BOT 135.subject: BOT
BOT 135.description: Impact of fungi in nature and on humankind. Selected historical events in which fungi played a significant role, their activities as decomposers and pathogens, and their uses as sources for mind altering drugs in religious ceremonies and in food and beverage production in various societies.

BOT 160.title: Campus Plants
BOT 160.subject: BOT
BOT 160.description: Nontechnical course emphasizing recognition of the many interesting tropical plants seen on campus; origin, status in Hawai‘i, and cultural and economic uses of campus plants.

BOT 180.title: Plant Life in the Sea
BOT 180.subject: BOT
BOT 180.description: Combined lecture-lab to introduce common marine plants in Hawaiian coastal areas via discussion of morphology, growth, ecological functions and native/alien status. Field trips to observe plants in local habitats.

BOT 200.title: Sophomore Seminar
BOT 200.subject: BOT
BOT 200.description: Presentations by faculty highlighting research in tropical ecosystems. Topics include alien species, biodiversity, ecosystem services, ethnobotany, marine ecology, plant-animal interactions, and systematics of Hawaiian species. Assigned reading and writing exercises from papers in current journals.

BOT 201.title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity
BOT 201.subject: BOT
BOT 201.description: Significance of evolutionary trends in the plant world, including reproductive, morphological, and life history adaptations by algae, fungi, and vascular plants.

BOT 201L.title: Plant Evolutionary Diversity Lab
BOT 201L.subject: BOT
BOT 201L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab exercises in the morphology and systematics of land plants, fungi, and algae.

BOT 220.title: Biostatistics
BOT 220.subject: BOT
BOT 220.description: Introduction to statistical approaches in biology. Students will learn how to formulate hypotheses, test them quantitatively, and present results. Students will analyze biological datasets using the computer language R.
BOT 220.prereq_raw: 101, BIOL 171, or BIOL 172; and BOT/BIOL 220L (or concurrent) and MATH 134 or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140

BOT 220L.title: Biostatistics Lab
BOT 220L.subject: BOT
BOT 220L.prereq_raw: 101, BIOL 171, or BIOL 172; and BIOL 220 (or concurrent); and MATH 134 or MATH assessment exam (with score for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score for MATH 140

BOT 300.title: Conservation Ethics
BOT 300.subject: BOT
BOT 300.description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.
BOT 300.prereq_raw: any DB course or consent. (Once a year)

BOT 301.title: Plant Conservation Biology
BOT 301.subject: BOT
BOT 301.description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-inpractice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere.

BOT 301L.title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
BOT 301L.subject: BOT
BOT 301L.description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

BOT 302.title: Grant Writing Seminar
BOT 302.subject: BOT
BOT 302.description: Provides three rounds of opportunities for grant writing associated with research in biodiversity, conservation biology, ecology, and plant systematics. Students will gain experience in peer review, grant cycles, and budget preparation.
BOT 302.prereq_raw: 301/SUST 313 (or concurrent) and 303, or consent. (Once a year)

BOT 305.title: Ecology
BOT 305.subject: BOT
BOT 305.description: General survey of the principles of ecology. Focus on processes influencing the distribution and abundance of organisms, interactions among organisms, and interactions between organisms and the environment.

BOT 310.title: Field Botany
BOT 310.subject: BOT
BOT 310.description: Combined lecturelaboratory with intensive field experience for observational and experimental field work in native/impacted Hawaiian ecosystems. Field experience typically held during spring break. Terrestrial, freshwater, and marine habitats considered.

BOT 350.title: Resource Management and Conservation in Hawai‘i
BOT 350.subject: BOT
BOT 350.description: Management of native Hawaiian organisms and terrestrial ecosystems with particular attention to strategies, planning, research, and management actions necessary to control alien influences and promote native species.

BOT 357.title: Tropical forest Ecology
BOT 357.subject: BOT
BOT 357.description: Introduction to the ecological processes and principles of tropical ecosystems, and to conservation issues facing tropical forests, with a particular emphasis on the neotropics.
BOT 357.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or BOT 101; and BIOL 265

BOT 399.title: Botanical Problems
BOT 399.subject: BOT
BOT 399.restrictions_raw: Intended for upper division botany majors.
