BOT 400.title: Senior Seminar
BOT 400.subject: BOT
BOT 400.description: Current research themes in botany presented in discussion format; reading current research papers. Oral presentations of primary research. Senior standing and consent. (Once a year)

BOT 401.title: Teaching Internship
BOT 401.subject: BOT
BOT 401.description: Teaching Internship (TI) allows upper division undergraduates to experience assisting in laboratory courses for BOT 101, 105, 201, 202, 203, or other lab courses in Botany or peer-mentoring for BOT 100, as available.
BOT 401.prereq_raw: 301 or SUST 313, and 301L or SUST 313L, and 303; or consent

BOT 410.title: Plant Anatomy
BOT 410.subject: BOT
BOT 410.description: Structure of vascular plants; origin and differentiation of tissues; relation of structure to function.

BOT 410L.title: Plant Anatomy Lab
BOT 410L.subject: BOT
BOT 410L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Lab study of plant structure.

BOT 420.title: Plant Form and Function
BOT 420.subject: BOT
BOT 420.description: Lecture/laboratory to examine the anatomy, physiology, morphology, and functional ecology of plants. Labs will develop skills in microscopy, experimental techniques for studying plant physiology, and basic functional ecology.

BOT 430.title: The Biology of Fungi
BOT 430.subject: BOT
BOT 430.description: Will introduce the diversity, ecology, evolution, and biology of the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on our current understanding of fungal evolution and diversity and how fungi interact with environments and hosts.

BOT 430L.title: The Biology of Fungi Lab
BOT 430L.subject: BOT
BOT 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to the morphology and life cycles of organisms in the Kingdom Fungi. Focus on learning how to identify a diversity of fungi based on macro- and microscopic features. Field trips to collect specimens.

BOT 440.title: Advanced Ethnobotany
BOT 440.subject: BOT
BOT 440.description: (2 2-hr Lab) Advanced studies of plant uses in cultural contexts, focusing upon impacts of plant-culture interactions in development of cultures, cultivars, medicinals, ethnoecologies, ethics, and intellectual property. Lecture/discussion, term paper.

BOT 442.title: Medical Ethnobotany
BOT 442.subject: BOT
BOT 442.description: Survey and theory of plants used as medicines, cultural perspectives of herbal medicine, and the botanical/ chemical basis of allopathic and naturopathic medicine. Lecture/discussion, term paper or project.

BOT 444.title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
BOT 444.subject: BOT
BOT 444.description: Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems.

BOT 446.title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
BOT 446.subject: BOT
BOT 446.description: Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

BOT 450.title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
BOT 450.subject: BOT
BOT 450.description: Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
BOT 450.prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

BOT 453.title: Plant Ecology and Environmental Measurements
BOT 453.subject: BOT
BOT 453.description: Influence of natural environments on plant behavior (autecology). A field-oriented course to complement 454. Field trips. Should precede 454.

BOT 454.title: Plant Community Ecology
BOT 454.subject: BOT
BOT 454.description: Covers selected topics in plant population and community ecology. Strong emphasis on how ecology is practiced as a science. Labs take advantage of working outdoors in local natural areas.

BOT 455.title: Analysis of Biological Data
BOT 455.subject: BOT
BOT 455.description: Application of computers to analysis of biological data; preparation and storage, report production, database analysis procedures, univariate and bivariate statistical analyses.

BOT 456.title: Plant-Animal Interactions
BOT 456.subject: BOT
BOT 456.description: Interdependence of plants and animals, emphasizing the influence of animals on plant fitness and evolution. Topics include pollination, fruit/seed dispersal, herbivory, and ant-plant mutualisms.

BOT 457.title: ‘Aina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
BOT 457.subject: BOT
BOT 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

BOT 458.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
BOT 458.subject: BOT
BOT 458.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.
BOT 458.prereq_raw: HWST 207/SUST 217 or HWST 307/ SUST 317 or HWST/SUST 356

BOT 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
BOT 459.subject: BOT
BOT 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

BOT 461.title: Systematics of Vascular Plants
BOT 461.subject: BOT
BOT 461.description: “Hands-on” experience with Hawai‘i’s unique tropical flora; emphasis on recognition and identification of vascular plant families and the principles and methodologies that define them; evolution of biodiversity.

BOT 462.title: Plant Evolution
BOT 462.subject: BOT
BOT 462.description: Major events and principles; includes the blue-green algae and fungi.

BOT 470.title: Plant Physiology
BOT 470.subject: BOT
BOT 470.description: Integration of form and function from cellular to whole plant levels in processes from seed germination, through photosynthesis, growth, and morphogenesis, to flowering and senescence.

BOT 470L.title: Principles of Plant Physiology Lab
BOT 470L.subject: BOT
BOT 470L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Principles of experimentation in plant physiology, includes individual investigations.

BOT 480.title: Algal Diversity and Evolution
BOT 480.subject: BOT
BOT 480.description: Principles of algal diversity, structure, and evolution. Identification of common Hawaiian algae.
BOT 480.prereq_raw: one of 101, BIOL 172, MICR 351, ZOOL 101; or consent

BOT 492.title: Wildlife Ecology and Management in the Tropics
BOT 492.subject: BOT
BOT 492.description: Practices from around the world that focuses on the tropics. Integrates across disciplines, considers how science based management interacts with world views and considers management plans that are scientifically rigorous but culturally sensitive.
BOT 492.prereq_raw: BIOL 265 and an upper level ecology course, or consent. (Once a year)

BOT 499.title: Advanced Directed Research
BOT 499.subject: BOT
BOT 499.description: Performance of research project under the direction of a faculty advisor. Preparation of written proposal, final oral presentation to be given to the Botany Department audience and written report required. Preference given to BOT majors.
BOT 499.prereq_raw: 301 or SUST 313, and 301L or SUST 313L, and 302 and 303; and consent

BOT 600.title: Grant Writing and Your Career in Science
BOT 600.subject: BOT
BOT 600.description: Scientific grant writing from inception through management to completion; students will write a DDIG and participate in a panel. Professional skills including “rules,” job applications, interviews, transitioning from graduate student to academic or non-academic job.
BOT 600.prereq_raw: current standing as a graduate student, or consent

children.text: current standing as a graduate student,

BOT 601.title: Foundations of Current Botany I
BOT 601.subject: BOT
BOT 601.description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in history of science, plant diversity, plant interactions with the environment, and plant integration.
BOT 601.prereq_raw: graduate standing in BOT or consent

BOT 602.title: Foundations of Current Botany II
BOT 602.subject: BOT
BOT 602.description: Discussion of current research and classical papers important to modern concepts in ecology, plant interactions with other plants or animals, and ecosystem functioning.
BOT 602.prereq_raw: graduate standing in BOT or consent

BOT 603.title: Darwin’s Origin of Species
BOT 603.subject: BOT
BOT 603.description: Study and discussion of Charles Darwin’s Origin of Species, 1st edition 1859, and related current literature. Graduate students only.
BOT 603.prereq_raw: BA or BS in BOT, BIOL, GEOL, or related field; or consent

BOT 606.title: Graduate Research Skills
BOT 606.subject: BOT
BOT 606.description: Survey of major research areas in the botanical sciences with emphasis upon research opportunities in Hawai‘i and an overview of 1) skills needed by botanical researchers including writing scientific papers and proposals, practicing ethical research procedures, and collection of specimens; and 2) equipment used by botanical researchers including computers, cameras, measuring and monitoring equipment, and global positioning systems. Lecture/ discussion, laboratory.
BOT 606.prereq_raw: graduate standing in biological science or approval

BOT 610.title: Botanical Seminar
BOT 610.subject: BOT
BOT 610.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in botany.

BOT 612.title: Advanced Botanical Problems
BOT 612.subject: BOT
BOT 612.description: Investigation of any botanical problem; reading and laboratory work.

BOT 620.title: Perspectives in Modern Botany
BOT 620.subject: BOT
BOT 620.description: Lectures by distinguished visiting professor on contemporary botanical topics in the lecturer’s area of expertise. No more than 6 credit hours may be counted toward the MS degree requirements.

BOT 621.title: Ecohydrology: Theory and Modeling
BOT 621.subject: BOT
BOT 621.description: Vegetative response to hydrologic controls and nutrient cycles; quantitative linkages between hydrological dynamics and ecological patterns/ processes. MatLab is used to develop and simulate ecohydrological models.
BOT 621.prereq_raw: college level calculus or consent. (Once a year)

BOT 640.title: Quantitative Ethnobotany
BOT 640.subject: BOT
BOT 640.description: Modern ethnobotanical field research project design, execution, data analysis, and documentation methods. Intended for students preparing to conduct field research studies. Lecture/discussion, term paper.
BOT 640.prereq_raw: 105 and one of 201, 461, ANTH 200, or BIOL 172

BOT 644.title: Ethnoecological Methods
BOT 644.subject: BOT
BOT 644.description: Field techniques for assessing the ecological effects of cultural uses of plants. Emphasis on documenting traditional and local patterns of plant use and measuring the effects on plant individuals, populations, communities, and landscapes.
BOT 644.prereq_raw: previous course work in anthropology or biology

BOT 648.title: Conservation Ethnobiology
BOT 648.subject: BOT
BOT 648.description: Practical field training experience for a scientific career conducting ethnobiological research.

BOT 651.title: Invasion Biology
BOT 651.subject: BOT
BOT 651.description: Theories, models, patterns, and predictive methods relating to the introduction, establishment, and spread of introduced organisms. Application of principles of invasion biology to conservation and natural resource management.
BOT 651.prereq_raw: one of 453, 456, MICR 485 or ZOOL 439; and 462 or BIOL 375; or consent

BOT 652.title: Population Biology
BOT 652.subject: BOT
BOT 652.description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
BOT 652.prereq_raw: one of 453, 454, 456, NREM 680, PEPS 671, ZOOL 439, ZOOL 467, ZOOL 620, or ZOOL 623; or consent

BOT 653.title: Population Dynamics Models with R
BOT 653.subject: BOT
BOT 653.description: Learn advanced modeling techniques to investigate the dynamics of size-structure populations (using matrix and integral population models in R), and discuss various applications in ecology and conservation biology.

BOT 654.title: Advances in Plant Ecology
BOT 654.subject: BOT
BOT 654.description: A researchoriented course focusing on recent advances in all areas of plant ecology. Involves critical review of recent literature, independent research project, oral and written presentation of project results.

BOT 660.title: Ecological Statistics with R
BOT 660.subject: BOT
BOT 660.description: Learn how to choose appropriate statistical methods to test hypotheses in ecology, evolution, and conservation biology and applications using R as a platform. Lecture/discussion, term paper.

BOT 661.title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
BOT 661.subject: BOT
BOT 661.description: Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

BOT 662.title: High Throughput Sequencing Approaches to Ecology and Evolution
BOT 662.subject: BOT
BOT 662.description: Fundamentals of experimental design, lab techniques and data analysis to conduct research using high throughput sequencing. Students will work in groups to conduct an amplicon sequencing study with ten samples.

BOT 668.title: Nomenclature and Practical Systematics
BOT 668.subject: BOT
BOT 668.description: Modern issues of naming and classifying of organisms, with a botanical emphasis. Includes lectures, discussions, class projects, and field trips.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . ( Once a year)

BOT 669.title: Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution
BOT 669.subject: BOT
BOT 669.description: Molecular approaches to evolution, phylogenetics, and systematics. Basic use of chloroplast DNA, mitochondrial DNA, nuclear DNA, and electrophoresis. Phylogenetic analysis using parsimony, distance, and comparative methods.

BOT 670.title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
BOT 670.subject: BOT
BOT 670.description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)

BOT 676.title: Environmental Physiology Seminar
BOT 676.subject: BOT
BOT 676.description: Environmental stress; pollution; salinity, geobotany, and other interactions between the environment and plant processes. Current literature emphasized at multidisciplinary and interdisciplinary levels.
BOT 676.prereq_raw: graduate status in a biological science, geosciences, etc.; consent for well-prepared undergraduates

prereq_tree.text: graduate status in a biological science, geosciences, etc.; consent for well-prepared undergraduates

BOT 680.title: Marine Macrophytes Seminar
BOT 680.subject: BOT
BOT 680.description: Discussion of current literature in physiological ecology, cellular and molecular adaptations to environmental factors by marine plants.

BOT 682.title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants
BOT 682.subject: BOT
BOT 682.description: Discussion of current studies in morphological, physiological, cellular, and molecular adaptation to marine environments by macroalgae, phytoplankton, and seagrasses.
BOT 682.prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, 470 (or equivalent), 480 (or equivalent), or consent

BOT 682L.title: Physiological Ecology of Marine Plants Lab
BOT 682L.subject: BOT
BOT 682L.description: Field and laboratory research techniques and projects in the physiological ecology of algae and seagrasses.
BOT 682L.prereq_raw: upper division ecology class recommended, 470L (or equivalent), 480 (or equivalent), or consent

BOT 690.title: Conservation Biology
BOT 690.subject: BOT
BOT 690.description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution, and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.
BOT 690.prereq_raw: BIOL 375 and either 462 or ZOOL 480; and either 453, 454, 456, or 492; or ZOOL 410, 439, 620, 623

BOT 699.title: Directed Research
BOT 699.subject: BOT
BOT 699.description: Research preliminary to thesis or dissertation research.

BOT 700.title: Thesis Research
BOT 700.subject: BOT
BOT 700.prereq_raw: candidacy for MS degree and approval of thesis proposal

BOT 750.title: Topics in Conservation Biology
BOT 750.subject: BOT
BOT 750.description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology.

BOT 800.title: Dissertation Research
BOT 800.subject: BOT
BOT 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD and approval of dissertation proposal

CHEM 100.title: Chemistry and Society
CHEM 100.subject: CHEM
CHEM 100.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of basic chemistry concepts and their application to everyday life.
CHEM 100.restrictions_raw: No credit for science and engineering majors.

CHEM 110.title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
CHEM 110.subject: CHEM
CHEM 110.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of the role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world.

CHEM 131.title: Preparation for General Chemistry
CHEM 131.subject: CHEM
CHEM 131.description: For students lacking preparation in chemistry. Provides background in algebra and elementary concepts of chemistry in preparation for entering the General Chemistry sequence.

CHEM 151.title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry
CHEM 151.subject: CHEM
CHEM 151.description: Nonrigorous but adequate background in fundamentals. Preparation for technical training in life sciences.

CHEM 151L.title: Elementary Survey of Chemistry Lab
CHEM 151L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 151L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments introducing laboratory techniques and illustrating chemical principles.

CHEM 152.title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry
CHEM 152.subject: CHEM
CHEM 152.description: Structure, nomenclature, properties, reactions of organic compounds emphasizing those of practical importance in related fields.

CHEM 152L.title: Survey of Organic and Bioorganic Chemistry Lab
CHEM 152L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 152L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Techniques of preparation, purification, identification of organic compounds.

CHEM 161.title: General Chemistry I
CHEM 161.subject: CHEM
CHEM 161.description: Basic principles of chemistry, including stoichiometry. Introduction to solution phase chemistry. Gas phase chemistry. Thermodynamics, including enthalpies of formation and reaction. Atomic structure, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular structure.
CHEM 161.prereq_raw: C (not C-) in 131 or C (not C-) in 151 or successful completion of placement exam, or consent

CHEM 161L.title: General Chemistry Lab I
CHEM 161L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 161L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry.

CHEM 162.title: General Chemistry II
CHEM 162.subject: CHEM
CHEM 162.description: Continuation of 161. Liquids and solids. Solutions and colligative properties. Continuation of thermodynamics, including entropy and free energy. Principles and applications of chemical equilibrium, including acidbase chemistry (titrations, buffers). Kinetics. Redox reactions and electrochemistry.

CHEM 162L.title: General Chemistry Lab II
CHEM 162L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 162L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments introducing techniques and fundamental principles of chemistry.

CHEM 171.title: Principles of Chemistry
CHEM 171.subject: CHEM
CHEM 171.description: Principles, theories, elementary analytical methods of chemistry. Intended for physical science majors and engineers.
CHEM 171.prereq_raw: Satisfactory Placement Exam score, and MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent)

CHEM 171L.title: Principles of Chemistry Lab
CHEM 171L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 171L.description: (1 3.5-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating fundamental principles of chemistry.

CHEM 181A.title: Honors General Chemistry
CHEM 181A.subject: CHEM
CHEM 181A.description: Rigorous, in-depth introduction to chemical principles with emphasis on experimental and applied aspects of modern chemistry.
CHEM 181A.prereq_raw: satisfactory placement exam score and MATH 215 (or concurrent) or MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) with a minimum grade of C

CHEM 181L.title: Honors General Chemistry Laboratory
CHEM 181L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 181L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory experiments illustrating chemical principles involving advanced techniques and modern instrumentation.

CHEM 272.title: Organic Chemistry I
CHEM 272.subject: CHEM
CHEM 272.description: Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.
CHEM 272.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A

CHEM 272L.title: Organic Chemistry I Lab
CHEM 272L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 272L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.
CHEM 272L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162L, 171L, or 181L; and C (not C-) or better in 272 (or concurrent)

CHEM 273.title: Organic Chemistry II
CHEM 273.subject: CHEM
CHEM 273.description: Continuation of 272. Molecular structure, stereochemistry, spectroscopy, mechanisms, reactions, and synthesis of organic compounds.

CHEM 273L.title: Organic Chemistry II Lab
CHEM 273L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 273L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Techniques, synthesis and qualitative analysis, applications of spectroscopy.

CHEM 274.title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry
CHEM 274.subject: CHEM
CHEM 274.description: Selected methods and principles, e.g., phase equilibria, ionic equilibria, electrode equilibria, separations, spectroscopy, automation, and process control.
CHEM 274.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162 or 171 or 181A, MATH 215 or MATH 241 or MATH 251A

CHEM 274L.title: Principles of Analytical Chemistry Lab
CHEM 274L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 274L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Phase separations, chromatography, titrimetry, spectrophotometry, etc.
CHEM 274L.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 162L or 171L or 181L; and 274 (or concurrent)

CHEM 351.title: Physical Chemistry I
CHEM 351.subject: CHEM
CHEM 351.prereq_raw: 274, 274L, PHYS 272, PHYS 272L, and MATH 243 or MATH 253A

CHEM 352L.title: Physico-Chemical Measurements
CHEM 352L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 352L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Modern laboratory techniques. Includes emphasis on instruction in scientific report writing.

CHEM 361.title: Physical Biochemistry
CHEM 361.subject: CHEM
CHEM 361.description: Biochemical thermodynamics, chemical and enzyme kinetics, biomolecular structure, and biomolecular spectroscopy.
CHEM 361.prereq_raw: 162, PHYS 272, and MATH 242 or 252A with a grade of C or better for prerequisites

CHEM 372.title: Bioorganic Chemistry
CHEM 372.subject: CHEM
CHEM 372.description: Mechanism of biochemical reactions, biophysical structure, techniques for studying biochemical reactions.
CHEM 372.prereq_raw: 273 (with a grade of C or better) or graduate standing with consent, or departmental approval

CHEM 380.title: Professional Ethics for Chemists
CHEM 380.subject: CHEM
CHEM 380.description: Student team-led discussions of contemporary ethical issues and ethical decision making in chemistry using case studies and additional examples from the media. CHEM or BIOC majors only.

CHEM 399.title: Directed Reading
CHEM 399.subject: CHEM
CHEM 399.description: Directed reading and discussion of scientific journal articles culminating in a written literature review. CHEM or BIOC majors only.
CHEM 399.prereq_raw: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0

CHEM 399L.title: Directed Research
CHEM 399L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 399L.description: Directed laboratory research culminating in a written research report. CHEM or BIOC majors only.
CHEM 399L.prereq_raw: minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum in-major GPA of 3.0

CHEM 425.title: Synthesis and Analysis of Inorganic Compounds
CHEM 425.subject: CHEM
CHEM 425.description: Lecture on advanced methods of preparation and characterization of inorganic compounds and materials.

CHEM 425L.title: Preparation and Analysis of Inoraganic Compounds Laboratory
CHEM 425L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 425L.description: Laboratory on preparative methods and analytical techniques and instruments in inorganic chemistry.

CHEM 435.title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
CHEM 435.subject: CHEM
CHEM 435.description: Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience.

CHEM 445.title: Synthesis and Analysis of Organic Compounds
CHEM 445.subject: CHEM
CHEM 445.description: Introduction to multi-step synthesis and instruments/analytical techniques used to characterize organic compounds. Retrosynthesis and diastereoselective reactions; spectroscopy (optical methods, NMR), mass spectrometry. Chromatography (GC, HPLC) and coupled techniques (GCMS, LCMS). CHEM or BIOC majors only.
CHEM 445.prereq_raw: 273 with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval

children.text: ( not C-) or better, or departmental approval

CHEM 445L.title: Preparation and Analysis of Organic Compounds Laboratory
CHEM 445L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 445L.description: Laboratory on the preparation of organic compounds and physical methods for their characterization. Includes optical methods (UV-vis, IR), chromatography (HPLC, GC), mass spectrometry (GCMS and LCMS) and NMR.
CHEM 445L.prereq_raw: 273L with a grade of C (not C-) or better, or departmental approval

children.text: ( not C-) or better, or departmental approval

CHEM 462.title: Advanced Biochemistry
CHEM 462.subject: CHEM
CHEM 462.description: Advanced topics in biochemistry including nucleic acid replication, transcription, and translation; genetic and epigenetic regulation; bioenergetics and control of metabolism; alternative metabolic strategies; and enzyme structure and mechanism.

CHEM 462L.title: Advanced Biochemistry Lab
CHEM 462L.subject: CHEM
CHEM 462L.description: Advanced biochemistry lab techniques: protein purification and characterization, identification of unknown proteins, enzyme kinetics, ligand binding, enzyme kinetics, protein structure, and spectroscopy, with instruction in writing scientific reports.

CHEM 600.title: Introduction to Research
CHEM 600.subject: CHEM
CHEM 600.description: Introduction to field-specific methods and skills needed for success in graduate research. Includes training modules for safety, ethics, and library resources. Short faculty research overviews may also be given.CHEM majors only. Graduate students only.

CHEM 601.title: Theory of Chemical Bonding
CHEM 601.subject: CHEM
CHEM 601.description: Application of quantum mechanics and symmetry principles to descriptions of chemical bonding.

CHEM 602.title: Chemical Applications of Spectroscopy
CHEM 602.subject: CHEM
CHEM 602.description: Introduction to magnetic resonance, infrared, UV, and visible spectroscopy, emphasizing applications to organic and inorganic chemistry. Three topics each semester–1 credit hour per topic.

CHEM 622.title: Organometallics I
CHEM 622.subject: CHEM
CHEM 622.description: Reactivity and reaction mechanisms of compounds containing metalcarbon bonds.

CHEM 623.title: Coordination Chemistry
CHEM 623.subject: CHEM
CHEM 623.description: Survey of Lewis acids and bases, coordination numbers, geometries, stereochemistry, ligand field theory, formation constants, and bioinorganic chemistry.

CHEM 624.title: Organometallics II
CHEM 624.subject: CHEM
CHEM 624.description: Introduction to the principles of catalysis and the classes of catalytic reactions effected by organometallic compounds.
CHEM 624.prereq_raw: 622 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

children.text: a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

CHEM 631.title: Methods of Instrumental Analysis
CHEM 631.subject: CHEM
CHEM 631.description: Theory, instrumentation, applications. Three areas each semester-one credit hour per area.
CHEM 631.prereq_raw: 333 and graduate standing in CHEM or consent

CHEM 641.title: Organic Structure Determination
CHEM 641.subject: CHEM
CHEM 641.description: Interpretation of chemical and physical (primarily spectral) data in the identification of organic compounds.

CHEM 642.title: Organic Synthesis I
CHEM 642.subject: CHEM
CHEM 642.description: Modern synthetic methods with emphasis on the design and execution of multi-step sequences.

CHEM 643.title: Physical Organic Chemistry
CHEM 643.subject: CHEM
CHEM 643.description: Theory of molecular structure, stereochemistry, and reaction mechanisms.

CHEM 647.title: Organic Synthesis II
CHEM 647.subject: CHEM
CHEM 647.description: Continuation of 642, and is the second half of a two-semester course in Modern Organic Synthesis.
CHEM 647.prereq_raw: 642 and a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

children.text: a minimum required grade for prerequisites of B

CHEM 651.title: Chemical Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
CHEM 651.subject: CHEM
CHEM 651.description: Includes statistical thermodynamics, with application to chemical systems.

CHEM 652.title: Chemical Kinetics and Reaction Dynamics
CHEM 652.subject: CHEM
CHEM 652.description: Kinetics and chemical reaction dynamics of elementary reactions relevant to combustion processes, astrochemistry, chemical vapor deposition and planetary sciences.

CHEM 653.title: Quantum Chemistry
CHEM 653.subject: CHEM
CHEM 653.description: Rigorous introduction to quantum mechanics, including operator formalism, matrix formation, group theory, and perturbation theory; introduction to the electronic structure of atoms and molecules.

CHEM 657.title: Astrochemistry–A Molecular Approach
CHEM 657.subject: CHEM
CHEM 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

CHEM 658.title: Crystallography
CHEM 658.subject: CHEM
CHEM 658.description: Crystal symmetry. Elementary x-ray physics. Diffraction theory and its application to crystal and molecular structure determination.

CHEM 661.title: Enzyme Reaction Mechanisms
CHEM 661.subject: CHEM
CHEM 661.description: The chemical mechanisms of reactions catalyzed by enzymes in biochemical pathways, with an emphasis on the major types of cofactor and metal catalyzed reactions.

CHEM 700.title: Thesis Research
CHEM 700.subject: CHEM
CHEM 700.prereq_raw: candidacy for MS degree and consent of thesis chair

CHEM 800.title: Dissertation Research
CHEM 800.subject: CHEM
CHEM 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD degree and consent of dissertation chair

ICS 101.title: Digital Tools for the Information World
ICS 101.subject: ICS
ICS 101.description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc.

ICS 101A.title: Digital Tools for the Information World
ICS 101A.subject: ICS
ICS 101A.description: Fundamental information technology concepts and computing terminology, productivity software for problem solving, computer technology trends and impact on individuals and society. Emphasizes the utilization of operating systems and the production of professional documents, spreadsheets, etc.

ICS 102.title: Introduction to Data Science
ICS 102.subject: ICS
ICS 102.description: Overview of the field of data science. Introduction to subjects such as data format, processing, visualization, and storage. Special emphasis on historical and wider context, and simple practical examples.

ICS 103.title: Introduction to Computer Science Principles
ICS 103.subject: ICS
ICS 103.description: General course that provides a broad overview of computer science. Will address abstraction, data and information, algorithms, programming, the Internet and the global impact of computers.

ICS 111.title: Introduction to Computer Science I
ICS 111.subject: ICS
ICS 111.description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.

ICS 111A.title: Introduction to Computer Science I
ICS 111A.subject: ICS
ICS 111A.description: Overview of the fundamentals of computer science emphasizing problem solving, algorithm development, implementation, and debugging/testing using an object-oriented programming language.

ICS 141.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science I
ICS 141.subject: ICS
ICS 141.description: Includes logic, sets, functions, matrices, algorithmic concepts, mathematical reasoning, recursion, counting techniques, and probability theory.

ICS 210.title: Information Systems in Society
ICS 210.subject: ICS
ICS 210.description: Lecture/discussion critically explores sociopolitical dimensions of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), and the information professions.

ICS 211.title: Introduction to Computer Science II
ICS 211.subject: ICS
ICS 211.description: Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.
ICS 211.prereq_raw: grade of “B” or higher in 111 or consent

ICS 211A.title: Introduction to Computer Science II
ICS 211A.subject: ICS
ICS 211A.description: Reinforce and strengthen problem-solving skills using abstract data types and introduce software development practices. Emphasize the use of searching and sorting algorithms and their complexity, recursion, object-oriented programming, and data structures.
ICS 211A.prereq_raw: grade of “B” or higher in 111 or consent

ICS 212.title: Program Structure
ICS 212.subject: ICS
ICS 212.description: Program organization paradigms, programming environments, implementation of a module from specifications, the C and C++ programming languages.

ICS 215.title: Introduction to Scripting
ICS 215.subject: ICS
ICS 215.description: Introduction to scripting languages for the integration of applications and systems. Scripting in operating systems, web pages, server-side application integration, regular expressions, and event handling for languages such as Perl, JavaScript, PHP, Python, shell scripting.

ICS 222.title: Basic Concepts of Computer Science
ICS 222.subject: ICS
ICS 222.description: What is the subject of computer science? What is a computer? Understand the basic models of computation and the concepts of computability, complexity, and network computation, and learn to use them in practice.

ICS 235.title: Machine Learning Methods
ICS 235.subject: ICS
ICS 235.description: Introduction to contemporary mathematical methods for empirical inference, data modeling, and machine learning.

ICS 241.title: Discrete Mathematics for Computer Science II
ICS 241.subject: ICS
ICS 241.description: Includes program correctness, recurrence relations and their solutions, relations and their properties, divide and conquer relations, graph theory, trees and their applications, Boolean algebra, introduction to formal languages and automata theory.
ICS 241.prereq_raw: 141 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

ICS 290.title: Computer Science Careers: An Exploration of the Specialties of Computer Science
ICS 290.subject: ICS
ICS 290.description: Exploration of the specialties of computer science. Meets every two week for 2.5 hours to explore specific areas in computer science. (Once a year)

ICS 311.title: Algorithms
ICS 311.subject: ICS
ICS 311.description: (4 1-hr Lec) Design and correctness of algorithms, including divide-and-conquer, greedy and dynamic programming methods. Complexity analyses using recurrence relations, probabilistic methods, and NP-completeness. Applications to order statistics, disjoint sets, B-trees and balanced trees, graphs, network flows, and string matching.
ICS 311.prereq_raw: 211, and (241 and (MATH 216 or 242 or 252A)) or (MATH 301 and 372), or consent

ICS 312.title: Machine-Level and Systems Programming
ICS 312.subject: ICS
ICS 312.description: Machine organization, machine instructions, addressing modes, assembler language, subroutine linkage, linking to higher-level languages, interface to operating systems, introduction to assemblers, loaders and compilers.
ICS 312.prereq_raw: 212 (or concurrent), (311 or EE 367), and 314, or consent

ICS 313.title: Programming Language Theory
ICS 313.subject: ICS
ICS 313.description: Syntax, semantics, control structures, variable binding and scopes, data and control abstractions. Programming in functional (LISP) and logic (Prolog) programming styles.
ICS 313.prereq_raw: Pre: 212, (311 or EE 367), and 314, or consent

ICS 314.title: Software Engineering I
ICS 314.subject: ICS
ICS 314.description: Problem analysis and design, team-oriented development, quality assurance, configuration management, project planning. These topics are covered in the sequence 314-414.

ICS 321.title: Database Systems I
ICS 321.subject: ICS
ICS 321.description: Introduction to relational database systems, data modeling, query processing, transaction processing, storage, and indexing.

ICS 331.title: Logic Design and Microprocessors
ICS 331.subject: ICS
ICS 331.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Basic machine architecture, microprocessors, bus organization, circuit elements, logic circuit analysis and design, microcomputer system design.

ICS 332.title: Operating Systems
ICS 332.subject: ICS
ICS 332.description: Operating system concepts and structure, processes and threads, CPU scheduling, memory management, scheduling, file systems, inter-process communication, virtualization, popular operating systems.

ICS 351.title: Network Design and Management
ICS 351.subject: ICS
ICS 351.description: Overview of the internet and its capabilities; introduction to HTTP, TCP/IP, ethernet, and wireless 802.11; routers, switches, and NAT; network and wireless security; practical experience in designing and implementing networks.
ICS 351.prereq_raw: (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 355.title: Security and Trust I: Resource Protections
ICS 355.subject: ICS
ICS 355.description: Security and trust in computers, networks, and society. Security models. Access and authorization. Availability and Denial-of-Service. Trust processes and network interactions.

ICS 361.title: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence Programming
ICS 361.subject: ICS
ICS 361.description: Introduction to the theory of Artificial Intelligence and the practical application of AI techniques in Functional (Common LISP and/or Scheme) and Logic (Prolog) programming languages. Students gain practical experience through programming assignments and projects.
ICS 361.prereq_raw: (212 or 215) and (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent

ICS 390.title: Computing Ethics for Lab Assistants
ICS 390.subject: ICS
ICS 390.description: A lecture/discussion/internship on ethical issues and instructional techniques for students assisting a laboratory section of ICS 101. The class uses multiple significant writing and oral presentation activities to help students learn course content.

ICS 414.title: Software Engineering II
ICS 414.subject: ICS
ICS 414.description: Continuation of 314. Project management, quality, and productivity control, testing and validation, team management. Team-oriented software-implementation project.

ICS 415.title: Introduction to Programming for the Web
ICS 415.subject: ICS
ICS 415.description: Introduction to emerging technologies for construction of World Wide Web (WWW)-based software. Covers programming and scripting languages used for the creation of WWW sites and client-server programming. Students will complete a medium-sized software project that uses languages and concepts discussed in class.

ICS 419.title: The Science, Psychology and Philosophy of Systems Design
ICS 419.subject: ICS
ICS 419.description: Scientific, psychological and philosophical bases of systems design, including a survey of human-factors and ergonomic standards; the nature of innovation and creativity as it relates to systems design. Web-enhanced course.
ICS 419.prereq_raw: (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 421.title: Database Systems II
ICS 421.subject: ICS
ICS 421.description: Very large database systems, data integration, data warehousing, designing big data systems, parallel query processing, distributed transactions.

ICS 422.title: Network Science Methodology
ICS 422.subject: ICS
ICS 422.description: Computational and statistical methods for analyzing network models of social, technological, information, and biological networks. Introduction to relevant data analytics and graph analysis software packages.

ICS 423.title: Data Security and Cryptography I
ICS 423.subject: ICS
ICS 423.description: Secret communication and confidentiality data storage. Elements of cryptography and cryptanalysis. Classical ciphers. Symmetric key cryptography. Public key cryptography. Data security in cyber space.

ICS 424.title: Application Frameworks
ICS 424.subject: ICS
ICS 424.description: Experience producing applications with at least two different applications frameworks.

ICS 425.title: Computer Security and Ethics
ICS 425.subject: ICS
ICS 425.description: Theoretical results, security policy, encryption, key management, digital signatures, certificates, passwords. Ethics: privacy, computer crime, professional ethics. Effects of the computer revolution on society.

ICS 426.title: Computer System Security
ICS 426.subject: ICS
ICS 426.description: Information flow, confinement, information assurance, malicious programs, vulnerability analysis, network security, writing secure programs.

ICS 427.title: Programming Approaches to Software Quality Assurance
ICS 427.subject: ICS
ICS 427.description: Examination of best practices associated with developing and supporting software applications with respect to potential security risks. Will augment software engineering practices learned in other courses with the basic principles of cybersecurity.

ICS 428.title: Digital Forensics
ICS 428.subject: ICS
ICS 428.description: Provides students with the knowledge of underlying principles and skills to identify, preserve, and extract electronic evidence for further analysis.

ICS 431.title: Computer Architecture
ICS 431.subject: ICS
ICS 431.description: Memory management, control flow, interrupt mechanisms, multiprocessor systems, special-purpose devices.

ICS 432.title: Concurrent and High-Performance Programming
ICS 432.subject: ICS
ICS 432.description: Principles of concurrent and high performance programming. Multi-threading in C and Java for shared-memory programming. Distributed memory programming with Java. Introduction to cluster computing.
ICS 432.prereq_raw: 212 and 322 and (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 434.title: Data Science Fundamentals
ICS 434.subject: ICS
ICS 434.description: Introduction to critical statistical and probabilistic concepts that underlie data science as well as tools that play a central role in the daily work of a data scientist.

ICS 435.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
ICS 435.subject: ICS
ICS 435.description: Introduction to machine learning concepts with a focus on relevant ideas from computational neuroscience. Information processing and learning in the nervous system. Neural networks. Supervised and unsupervised learning. Basics of statistical learning theory.
ICS 435.prereq_raw: (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. Recommended: MATH 307. (Once a year)

ICS 438.title: Big Data Analytics
ICS 438.subject: ICS
ICS 438.description: Concepts, tools, and techniques for analyzing and mining massive data sets. Data cleaning and pre-processing. Data analysis and mining techniques. Big Data platforms. Big Data visualization.

ICS 441.title: Theory of Computation
ICS 441.subject: ICS
ICS 441.description: Grammars, sequential machines, equivalence, minimalization, analysis and synthesis, regular expressions, computability, unsolvability, Gödel’s theorem, Turing machines.

ICS 442.title: Analytical Models and Methods
ICS 442.subject: ICS
ICS 442.description: Applications of mathematical methods in computer science with emphasis on discrete mathematics, numerical computation, algebraic models, operations research.

ICS 443.title: Parallel Algorithms
ICS 443.subject: ICS
ICS 443.description: Introduction to parallel models of computation and design and analysis of parallel algorithms.

ICS 451.title: Data Networks
ICS 451.subject: ICS
ICS 451.description: Network analysis, architecture, digital signal analysis and design; circuit switching, packet switching, packet broadcasting; protocols and standards; local area networks; satellite networks; ALOHA channels; examples.
ICS 451.prereq_raw: 212 and (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent

ICS 452.title: Software Design for Robotics
ICS 452.subject: ICS
ICS 452.description: Sensors, actuators, signal processing, paradigms of robotic software design, introduction to machine learning, introduction to computer vision, and robot-to-human interaction.
ICS 452.prereq_raw: two ICS 300-level courses or consent. Recommended: 312 and 313. (Once a year: spring)

children.text: Recommended: 312 and 313 . ( Once a year: spring)

ICS 455.title: Security and Trust II: Information Assurance
ICS 455.subject: ICS
ICS 455.description: Channel security. Trojan and noninterference. Basic concepts of cryptology. Cryptographic primitives. Protocols for authentication and key establishment.

ICS 461.title: Artificial Intelligence
ICS 461.subject: ICS
ICS 461.description: Survey of artificial intelligence: natural language processing, vision and robotics, expert systems. Emphasis on fundamental concepts: search, planning, and problem solving, logic, knowledge representation.

ICS 462.title: Artificial Intelligence for Games
ICS 462.subject: ICS
ICS 462.description: Techniques to stimulate intelligence in video games: movement, pathfinding with A* search, decision/behavior trees, state machines, machine learning, tactics. Extend games with your own AI implementations; experience “shootout” contests for the best AI algorithm/implementation.
ICS 462.prereq_raw: 212 and (311 or EE 367) and 314 and (PHYS 151 or PHYS 170)

ICS 464.title: Human Computer Interaction I
ICS 464.subject: ICS
ICS 464.description: Application of concepts and methodologies of human factors, psychology and software engineering to address ergonomic, cognitive, and social factors in the design and evaluation of human-computer systems.

ICS 465.title: Introduction to Hypermedia
ICS 465.subject: ICS
ICS 465.description: Basic issues of interactive access to information in various formats on computers. Available hardware and software: editing, integration, programming. Implementation of a sample information system.

ICS 466.title: Design for Mobile Devices
ICS 466.subject: ICS
ICS 466.description: Lecture introducing design issues, programming languages, operating systems and mark-up languages for internet-enabled mobile devices, such as cell phones and PDAs. A-F or Audit.

ICS 469.title: Cognitive Science
ICS 469.subject: ICS
ICS 469.description: Introduces basic concepts, central problems, and methods from cognitive science. Identifies contributions from disciplines such as cognitive psychology, linguistics, artificial intelligence, philosophy, and neuroscience.

ICS 471.title: Probability, Statistics, and Queuing
ICS 471.subject: ICS
ICS 471.description: A hands-on introduction to probability, statistical inference, regression, Markov chains, queuing theory. Use of an interactive statistical graphics environment such as R.

ICS 475.title: Introduction to Bioinformatics Sequences and Genomes Analysis
ICS 475.subject: ICS
ICS 475.description: Introduction to bioinformatics to computer sciences students by focusing on how computer sciences techniques can be used for the storage, analysis, prediction and simulation of biological sequences (DNA, RNA and proteins).
ICS 475.prereq_raw: (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 476.title: Bioinformatics Algorithms and Tool Development
ICS 476.subject: ICS
ICS 476.description: Study of commonly used bioinformatic algorithms, with an emphasis on string, tree, and graph algorithms. Presentation of probabilistic and clustering methods. Implementation of the studied algorithms and design of applications.

ICS 481.title: Introduction to Computer Graphics
ICS 481.subject: ICS
ICS 481.description: Fundamentals of computer graphics including graphics hardware, representation, manipulation, and display of two- and three-dimensional objects, use of commercial software.
ICS 481.prereq_raw: (MATH 216, MATH 242, or MATH 252A) and (311 or EE 367) and 314; or consent

ICS 483.title: Computer Vision
ICS 483.subject: ICS
ICS 483.description: Introductory course in computer vision. Topics include image formation, image processing and filtering, edge detection, texture analysis and synthesis, binocular stereo, segmentation, tracking, object recognition and applications.
ICS 483.prereq_raw: 212 and (311 or EE 367) and 314, or consent. Once a year

ICS 484.title: Data Visualization
ICS 484.subject: ICS
ICS 484.description: Introduction to data visualization through practical techniques for turning data into images to produce insight. Topics include: information visualization, geospatial visualization, scientific visualization, social network visualization, and medical visualization.Junior standing or higher.

ICS 485.title: Video Game Design and Development
ICS 485.subject: ICS
ICS 485.description: Students will team design, build, and demonstrate video games or related interactive entertainment environments and applications. Topics will include emerging computer science techniques relevant to the development of these types of environments. Junior standing or higher.

ICS 486.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality Programming
ICS 486.subject: ICS
ICS 486.description: Students will learn to develop virtual reality and augmented reality applications with turnkey tools as well as through programming. Prior programming experience is not required for this course.

ICS 491.title: Special Topics
ICS 491.subject: ICS
ICS 491.description: Reflects special interests of faculty. Oriented toward juniors and seniors.
ICS 491.prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS classes or consent

ICS 495.title: Special Topics in Security
ICS 495.subject: ICS
ICS 495.description: Special topics in security oriented toward juniors and seniors.
ICS 495.prereq_raw: at least two 300-level ICS courses or consent

ICS 496.title: Capstone Project
ICS 496.subject: ICS
ICS 496.description: Project-based course where students work in teams on a software project. Knowledge acquired in the computer science curriculum will be applied to design and implement a software product with potential real-world applicability. Senior standing or higher.

ICS 499.title: Computer Project
ICS 499.subject: ICS
ICS 499.description: Individual or small group projects in system design or application under faculty supervision.

ICS 606.title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
ICS 606.subject: ICS
ICS 606.description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
ICS 606.prereq_raw: 313 or EE 467 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent . ( Once a year)

ICS 611.title: Compiler Theory and Construction
ICS 611.subject: ICS
ICS 611.description: Design and implementation of compilers, syntactic and semantic descriptions of programming languages, algorithms for syntactic analysis and object code generation.

ICS 612.title: Theory of Operating Systems
ICS 612.subject: ICS
ICS 612.description: Advanced study in operating systems theory and design with emphasis on case studies and distributed systems.

ICS 613.title: Advanced Software Engineering
ICS 613.subject: ICS
ICS 613.description: Fundamental software engineering procedures, including planning, estimation, design, testing, process definition and improvement, and software quality assurance. Measurement techniques are used to support empirically-driven software process improvement throughout the course.

ICS 614.title: Medical Informatics I
ICS 614.subject: ICS
ICS 614.description: Introduction to the field of medical informatics, which is found at the intersection of clinical science, public health, information science, computer technology and communications technology. Concentration on current issues.

ICS 616.title: Information Architecture and Web Design
ICS 616.subject: ICS
ICS 616.description: User-centered design of websites; survey Information Architecture (IA) systems (organization, navigation, labeling, searching); gain experience in methodologies for creating IA, tools for IA, web standards and usability tests.
ICS 616.prereq_raw: graduate standing in ICS or LIS or related field or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in ICS or LIS or related field or consent . ( Once a year)

ICS 621.title: Analysis of Algorithms
ICS 621.subject: ICS
ICS 621.description: Analysis and design of algorithms: modeling, comparison, measures, applications.

ICS 622.title: Network Science
ICS 622.subject: ICS
ICS 622.description: Modeling human-made and natural systems as networks to understand their structure and dynamics. Computational and statistical methods and research results they enabled. Use of network analysis software. Applications to topics of interest to students.

ICS 623.title: Advanced Cryptography
ICS 623.subject: ICS
ICS 623.description: Taxonomy of security properties: methods for defining and proving security. Randomness, pseudorandomness, and indistinguishability. Functional encryption and obfuscation. Zero knowledge.

ICS 624.title: Advanced Data Management
ICS 624.subject: ICS
ICS 624.description: Exploration of information retrieval and object-relational tools and methods for the management of distributed multimedia database systems.

ICS 632.title: Principles of High Performance Computing
ICS 632.subject: ICS
ICS 632.description: Principles of high performance computing for single-processor and parallel architectures. Detailed coverage of parallel architectures and exposure to shared-memory, distributed-memory, and hybrid parallelism. Hands-on experience with message-passing and multithreaded programming.
ICS 632.prereq_raw: graduate standing in computer science or closely related field, or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in computer science or closely related field, or consent . ( Once a year)

ICS 635.title: Machine Learning
ICS 635.subject: ICS
ICS 635.description: Introduction to key theoretical concepts of machine learning. Practical experience with decision free methods, artificial neural networks. Bayesian belief networks and contemporary statistical methods including regression, clustering and classification.

ICS 636.title: Information Theory in Machine Learning
ICS 636.subject: ICS
ICS 636.description: Basics of information processing and learning in the brain; neural networks; learning algorithms based on information maximization; applications in molecular biology and bioinformatics.
ICS 636.prereq_raw: graduate standing in computer science or mathematics background, or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in computer science or mathematics background, or consent . ( Once a year)

ICS 637.title: Deep Learning with Neural Networks
ICS 637.subject: ICS
ICS 637.description: Graduate course on deep learning with artificial neural networks. Provides practical techniques for modeling image, video, text, and graph data with supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning approaches. Includes instruction in the latest software frameworks. Graduate students only.

ICS 641.title: Advanced Theory of Computation
ICS 641.subject: ICS
ICS 641.description: Advanced topics in formal languages, automata, computability, computational complexity.

ICS 643.title: Advanced Parallel Algorithms
ICS 643.subject: ICS
ICS 643.description: Design and analysis of parallel algorithms, with emphasis on advanced techniques and latest advances in parallel algorithms.
ICS 643.prereq_raw: 311 (with a minimum grade of B) or equivalent

ICS 651.title: Computer Networks
ICS 651.subject: ICS
ICS 651.description: Elementary principles of modern computer networking. Detailed coverage of overall architecture and the physical, data link, and network layers, with emphasis on the network layer.

ICS 655.title: Security and Trust III: Cyber Security and Commerce
ICS 655.subject: ICS
ICS 655.description: Tools and methods for security managers. Tools and methods to secure and monetize services and applications. Network as a computer and as a market. Problems of cyber war, cyber crime, cyber bullying. Graduate students only.

ICS 660.title: Computer Architecture I
ICS 660.subject: ICS
ICS 660.description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.

ICS 661.title: Advanced Artificial Intelligence
ICS 661.subject: ICS
ICS 661.description: Current issues in artificial intelligence, including expert systems, knowledge representation, logic programming, learning, natural language processing.

ICS 663.title: Pattern Recognition
ICS 663.subject: ICS
ICS 663.description: Nature of the problem in pattern recognition and clustering; explanation of various algorithms.

ICS 664.title: Human-Computer Interaction II
ICS 664.subject: ICS
ICS 664.description: Studies of human performance in designing and using information systems. Emphasizes concepts and methodologies from human factors, psychology, and software engineering relating to human performance.

ICS 665.title: User Interfaces and Hypermedia
ICS 665.subject: ICS
ICS 665.description: Advanced concepts in construction of interfaces between computers and their users. Hypermedia information structures, guidelines, problems, and tradeoffs. Discussion of selected readings, implementation of prototypes.

ICS 667.title: HCI Design Methods
ICS 667.subject: ICS
ICS 667.description: Advanced analytical and empirical methods for the design and evaluation of usable, useful, and robust human computer interfaces. Students will apply selected methodologies to a major system design project.

ICS 668.title: Social Informatics
ICS 668.subject: ICS
ICS 668.description: An advanced introduction to the design of human-computer systems and other technological artifacts for supporting human collaboration in learning, work and social contexts, and to theoretical perspectives and empirical studies of collaboration that inform such design.
ICS 668.prereq_raw: 464 or 465 or 664 or 665 or 667 or LIS 677; or consent

ICS 669.title: Social Computing
ICS 669.subject: ICS
ICS 669.description: Participative analysis of online communities and user-generated content collections. Theoretical and practical aspects of online interaction, identity, trust, and virtual social capital. (Once a year)

ICS 674.title: Evolutionary Computation I: Survey of Methods
ICS 674.subject: ICS
ICS 674.description: Evolutionary computation surveys in the field to prepare students for research. Topics include diverse engineering applications, theory, and concepts including search spaces, representation, objective functions, variation operators, selection, and population based search.
ICS 674.prereq_raw: 211 (B or better) and 241 (C or better) and admitted to a graduate program or capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences, or consent. (Once a year: fall)

children.text: capable of graduate-level work in computer sciences,

ICS 675.title: Bioinformatics: Sequences Analysis
ICS 675.subject: ICS
ICS 675.description: To expose students to bioinformatics at the biological sequences analysis level (DNA, RNA, proteins). Several bioinformatics methods and algorithms are introduced. Students are required to present one paper and to participate in a small group project.
ICS 675.prereq_raw: 475 or MBBE 683, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 676.title: Bioinformatics: Microarrays
ICS 676.subject: ICS
ICS 676.description: Introduction to the basic principles of biology relevant for microarray gene expression data and to Bio-conductor. Collaborative open-source project to develop a modular general framework for the analysis of cDNA arrays and gene chips.
ICS 676.prereq_raw: 311 or background in biology, or consent. (Once a year)

ICS 681.title: Computer Graphics
ICS 681.subject: ICS
ICS 681.description: Selected advanced topics in computer graphics. Substantial project required.

ICS 682.title: Numerical Computation
ICS 682.subject: ICS
ICS 682.description: Selected topics in numerical analysis, mathematical software, and scientific computation; examples include sparse matrix methods, finite element methods, mathematical programming.

ICS 683.title: Advanced Computer Vision
ICS 683.subject: ICS
ICS 683.description: Fundamental problems and core concepts and techniques in computer vision, covering both theoretical and practical issues in the field.

ICS 685.title: Virtual and Augmented Reality
ICS 685.subject: ICS
ICS 685.description: Students will learn the science, engineering, art, and applications of virtual reality and augmented reality, with an emphasis on the construction of working virtual environments. Graduate students only.

ICS 686.title: Digital Video Information
ICS 686.subject: ICS
ICS 686.description: Principles and techniques of technical and context analysis of digital video information. Video capture and editing tools, compression and analysis algorithms, visual culture, narrative structure, juxtaposition of multimedia elements and their effects on information transmission.

ICS 690.title: Seminar in ICS
ICS 690.subject: ICS
ICS 690.description: Series of talks on advanced research topics.

ICS 695.title: Advanced Special Topics in Security
ICS 695.subject: ICS
ICS 695.description: Current topics and upcoming issues relevant to the field of information assurance and cyber security. (Alt. years: spring)

ICS 800.title: Dissertation Research
ICS 800.subject: ICS
ICS 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in computer science

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in computer science

LIS 591.title: Library and Information Studies Workshop
LIS 591.subject: LIS
LIS 591.description: Designed for in-service librarians and other information specialists needing to update their professional skills, focus on a particular topic, or learn new approaches and concepts. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

LIS 601.title: Introduction to Reference and Information Services
LIS 601.subject: LIS
LIS 601.description: Philosophy, principles, and practice of reference services in libraries, information centers and information literacy. Bibliographic control, reference research, reference interview, online searching, evaluation of bibliographic and Webliographic material. Field component. MLISc degree required course.

LIS 602.title: Resource Discovery
LIS 602.subject: LIS
LIS 602.description: Techniques and strategies for discovery of information resources from professional online databases and the Web. Query formulation and use of advanced functions to match retrieved resources with user needs for research and reference work. Graduate students only.

LIS 605.title: Metadata Creation for Information Organization
LIS 605.subject: LIS
LIS 605.description: Theory and practice of metadata creation for organization of information resources, cataloging code for resource description and access, Library of Congress and Dewey Decimal Classification schemes, use of OCLC.

LIS 610.title: Foundations of the Information Professions
LIS 610.subject: LIS
LIS 610.description: Lecture/discussion/survey of the information professions, development of professional identity, professional values and ethics, historical development, current issues in the information professions.

LIS 611.title: Intellectual Freedom
LIS 611.subject: LIS
LIS 611.description: Seminar surveying the core philosophical principles and practices of intellectual freedom with special application to librarianship and information sciences.

LIS 612.title: History of Information
LIS 612.subject: LIS
LIS 612.description: History of the recording, preservation, and transmission of knowledge. Development of libraries and other information organizations as instruments of cultural transmission.

LIS 614.title: Navigating Information Organizations
LIS 614.subject: LIS
LIS 614.description: Principles of effective management of information organizations, with emphasis on organizational information flows, team skills, communication, planning, resource allocation, assessment, outreach, and advocacy. Graduate students only.

LIS 615.title: Collection Management
LIS 615.subject: LIS
LIS 615.description: Principles and issues of collection management and care. Criteria and tools for selecting and deselecting materials. Relationships with publishers/producers.

LIS 619.title: Preservation Management
LIS 619.subject: LIS
LIS 619.description: Introduction to preservation management. Focus on management strategies for preservation of materials in libraries and archives. Covers preservation planning, condition surveys, disaster planning, grantsmanship, and basic issues relating to deterioration.

LIS 620.title: Conservation of Library and Archival Materials
LIS 620.subject: LIS
LIS 620.description: In-depth exploration of the nature of library and archival materials and factors that cause deterioration. Hands-on approach provides practical experience testing, analyzing basic conservation treatments, understanding the role of conservation in preservation planning.

LIS 630.title: Community Engagement
LIS 630.subject: LIS
LIS 630.description: Explores how information professionals in libraries and other settings collaborate with community members and organizations. Provides an overview of theory and practice emphasizing critical analysis of policies, services, and trends. Required course for CALIS. (Alt. years)

LIS 631.title: Introduction to Hawai‘i and Pacific Librarianship
LIS 631.subject: LIS
LIS 631.description: Overview of resources and issues concerning librarianship in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Islands. Reference strategies and materials to answer common research questions, collection development, and management issues. Graduate students only.

LIS 633.title: Indigenous Librarianship
LIS 633.subject: LIS
LIS 633.description: Development and delivery of information services with and for indigenous communities. Issues include cultural protocols, traditional knowledge organization and ethics of access. Graduate students only.

LIS 634.title: Multicultural Resources for Diverse User Groups
LIS 634.subject: LIS
LIS 634.description: Examines resources and materials targeted for diverse user populations in libraries and community organizations, locally and globally. Surveys issues and trends related to diversity initiatives affecting the publishing industry, libraries, and cultural institutions worldwide. Graduate students only.

LIS 635.title: Traditional Literature and Oral Narration
LIS 635.subject: LIS
LIS 635.description: Analysis of traditional literature including Asian and Pacific Island resources. Selection and evaluation of traditional literature emphasizing cultural values. Introduction to oral tradition, history and techniques of storytelling.

LIS 636.title: Responding to Reading in Libraries
LIS 636.subject: LIS
LIS 636.description: Research-intensive seminar that explores the reading process in library contexts and similar settings. Critical examination of ways in which library and literacy services impact reading engagement and interests of library users. Graduate students only.

LIS 641.title: Digital Librarianship
LIS 641.subject: LIS
LIS 641.description: Lecture with demonstrations to introduce the essential types of digital resources and the software tools for finding high quality and relevant information efficiently from digital journal archives and reference databases.

LIS 645.title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
LIS 645.subject: LIS
LIS 645.description: Literature of Asia in Western and Asian languages; bibliography, reference tools, research methods, sources, published and archival repositories.

LIS 646.title: Advanced Cataloging and Classification
LIS 646.subject: LIS
LIS 646.description: Continues 605 with study of authority work, and further study of non-book materials cataloging, including electronic and internet resources. Extensive use is made of OCLC Connexion cataloging client.

LIS 648.title: Government Documents
LIS 648.subject: LIS
LIS 648.description: Survey of government documents at the federal, state/local and international levels in all formats. Covers methods of acquisition and organization, including depository arrangements. Current issues of government information dissemination policies and practices discussed.

LIS 650.title: Management of Libraries and Information Centers
LIS 650.subject: LIS
LIS 650.description: Theories and principles of administration for effective management of libraries and information centers, with emphasis on planning, resource allocation, team skills, project management, assessment, leadership, outreach, and advocacy.

LIS 651.title: Archival Arrangement and Description
LIS 651.subject: LIS
LIS 651.description: Principles and techniques for arrangement and description of archival materials. Topics include basic metadata standards, authority sources, record context, series identification, scope and content.

LIS 654.title: Archival Ethics and Profession
LIS 654.subject: LIS
LIS 654.description: The history and nature of records, archives, and the archival profession. Topics include cultural memory, ethics and values, and colonized and indigenous materials.

LIS 655.title: Digital Archives
LIS 655.subject: LIS
LIS 655.description: The role of technology in archival theory and practice. Topics include digital preservation, authenticity assessment, arrangement and description, content management, and access systems. Graduate students only.

LIS 656.title: Moving Image Archives
LIS 656.subject: LIS
LIS 656.description: Principles and technologies of processing, preservation, and accessibility of archival audiovisual materials in moving image archives. Topics include moving image repositories, critical analysis of archival footage, format identification, digitization strategies, equipment, and vendor considerations. Graduate students only.

LIS 657.title: Records Management
LIS 657.subject: LIS
LIS 657.description: Management of records in all media formats. Selection of media format based on government and internal records requirements. Problems associated with electronic media such as legality and shelf life.

LIS 658.title: Archival and Special Collections Management
LIS 658.subject: LIS
LIS 658.description: Management of archives, manuscript collections, and special collections using approaches and best practices from archival studies. Topics include management theory, appraisal theory, facilities issues, privacy, intellectual property, records management, advocacy, fundraising, reference, and educational outreach. Graduate standing only.

LIS 661.title: Informatics
LIS 661.subject: LIS
LIS 661.description: Sociotechnical concepts and processes underlying information systems, services, and use. Graduate students only.

LIS 662.title: Asian Informatics
LIS 662.subject: LIS
LIS 662.description: Lecture/discussion on the transformative effects of information and communication technologies in East Asia. Topics include media, mobile devices, social media, publishing, e-government, and e-commerce. Graduate students only.

LIS 665.title: Digital Instruction
LIS 665.subject: LIS
LIS 665.description: Study and application of principles and practices that influence digital instruction related to information literacy in libraries and other information environments. Focus on application of instructional design and standards-based outcome assessment. Field research component.

LIS 672.title: Technology for Libraries and Information Centers
LIS 672.subject: LIS
LIS 672.description: Survey of theories, concepts, methods and practices relating to the application of information technology to support the administration and use of information resources. Includes digital, printed and audiovisual materials.

LIS 673.title: Media Technology and Resources
LIS 673.subject: LIS
LIS 673.description: Overview of the use of media technology and the development of media collections and services in libraries. Use and integration of new emerging technologies, including problems and issues.

LIS 674.title: Database Design and Creation
LIS 674.subject: LIS
LIS 674.description: Designing and creating textual and/or directory databases from the viewpoint of information specialists and content providers. Needs analysis, file design, record content and structuring, software choice. Students implement prototype database.

LIS 676.title: Creating Digital Libraries
LIS 676.subject: LIS
LIS 676.description: Principles, techniques, and technologies supporting the creation of user-centered digital libraries. Selection, organization, maintenance, access, and retrieval of digital collections. Graduate students only.

LIS 677.title: Human Dimension in Information Systems
LIS 677.subject: LIS
LIS 677.description: Lecture/discussion on human element in information systems, including physical, cognitive and affective behavior in interaction with information systems. Information retrieval, human-computer interaction and cognitive science research, quantitative and qualitative research methods. Research component.

LIS 678.title: Personalized Information Delivery
LIS 678.subject: LIS
LIS 678.description: Study of the components of personalized information systems: information filtering systems with emphasis on modeling and representation of documents, queries, user information preferences, and user-system interaction. Topics include advanced Information Retrieval (IR) models, metadata and markup languages, query operations, thesaurus based IR, acquisition of user profiles, and user/system performance evaluation.

LIS 681.title: Books and Media for Children
LIS 681.subject: LIS
LIS 681.description: History and criticism of children’s literature. Contemporary books and media. Trends in book publishing and media production. Developmental needs and interests of children. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

LIS 682.title: Books and Media for Young Adults
LIS 682.subject: LIS
LIS 682.description: History and criticism of literature for young adults. Contemporary books and media. Trends in media for young adults. Developmental needs and interests of adolescents. Selection and evaluation. Research studies.

LIS 683.title: Services in Public Libraries
LIS 683.subject: LIS
LIS 683.description: Planning and implementing services and programming in public and school libraries. Trends, issues, networking, public relations, outreach, competencies, services for the disabled and other special groups.

LIS 686.title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
LIS 686.subject: LIS
LIS 686.description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

LIS 690.title: Internship
LIS 690.subject: LIS
LIS 690.description: Field experience in library or information agency settings with supervision of professional librarians or information specialists. Available to classified students only. Selection based on academic advisor approval, application form, interview and possession of required competencies. Students must apply and be accepted before registration. Selection is by agency.

LIS 691.title: Masters Seminar
LIS 691.subject: LIS
LIS 691.description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio and preparation for professional practice. Peer mentoring and student presentations. MLISc degree Plan B required course.

LIS 692.title: Masters Seminar II
LIS 692.subject: LIS
LIS 692.description: Seminar for graduating students focused on the refinement and completion of the culminating portfolio or thesis. Peer mentoring, faculty, and student presentations. MLISc degree required course. Graduate students only.

LIS 693.title: Special Topics in Information Studies
LIS 693.subject: LIS
LIS 693.description: Includes issues of topical interest in the information professions. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as services for specific groups and special collections. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.

LIS 694.title: Special Topics in Information Technology
LIS 694.subject: LIS
LIS 694.description: Includes issues of topical interest in information technology. Concentrates on one major topic of current interest, such as digital archives, content management systems and informatics. Some topics may require prior background or knowledge.

LIS 696.title: Practicum School Librarianship
LIS 696.subject: LIS
LIS 696.description: Skill development and application of academic study through observation and practice in a fieldwork program with accompanying seminar. Required for school library certification in Hawai‘i.
LIS 696.prereq_raw: 12 credits in LIS degree program and consent of practicum coordinator required

LIS 699.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
LIS 699.subject: LIS
LIS 699.description: Individualized program of directed reading and/ or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses. Enrollment requires approval before end of previous semester, with specification of goals, work requirements, number of credits, rationale.

LIS 701.title: Seminar in International Librarianship
LIS 701.subject: LIS
LIS 701.description: International and comparative librarianship; professional organizations; comparative methodology; research; periodicals; international agencies; influence of literacy and social, cultural, political factors.

MBIO 601.title: Marine Biology-Environments and Organisms
MBIO 601.subject: MBIO
MBIO 601.description: (3 hr Lec, 3 hr Lab) Introduction to the diversity of marine organisms and the many specialized coastal, reef, and oceanic habitats in which they live. Lab and field research exercises will complement lecture subjects. Graduate standing in Marine Biology graduate degree program only.

MBIO 602.title: Marine Biology-Processes and Impacts
MBIO 602.subject: MBIO
