MBIO 602.description: (3 hr Lec, 3 hr Lab) Investigation of biological phenomena and processes related to productivity and food webs, community structure and ecology, adaptations, and physiology, and impacts of human activities and fisheries. Graduate standing in Marine Biology graduate degree program only.

MBIO 603.title: Career Skills for Marine Biologists
MBIO 603.subject: MBIO
MBIO 603.description: Introduction to key professional skills including, but not limited to: grant writing, CV preparation, research logistics, data management, reproducible science, peer review, research ethics, publishing, career options, teaching, and professional presentations.

MBIO 604.title: Current Research in Marine Biology
MBIO 604.subject: MBIO
MBIO 604.description: Discussions with marine biology graduate faculty on current primary literature in marine biology. Graduate students only.

MBIO 611.title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods in Fisheries Science
MBIO 611.subject: MBIO
MBIO 611.description: Fisheries and population models including growth, stock-recruitment, surplus production, age-structured and size-based, parameter estimation, uncertainty characterization, resampling methods, and scientific computing. Graduate students only.
MBIO 611.prereq_raw: MATH 215 or 216, or MATH 241 or 242, or consent

MBIO 699.title: Directed Research
MBIO 699.subject: MBIO
MBIO 699.description: Directed research and reading in various fields of marine biology. Graduate students only.

MBIO 700.title: Thesis Research
MBIO 700.subject: MBIO
MBIO 700.description: Research for master’s thesis; (F) 1 credit. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/ Unsatisfactory only.

MBIO 710.title: Topics in Marine Fisheries and Natural Resource Management
MBIO 710.subject: MBIO
MBIO 710.description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine fisheries and natural resource management. Graduate students only.

MBIO 715.title: Topics in Marine Conservation Biology
MBIO 715.subject: MBIO
MBIO 715.description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to marine conservation biology. Graduate students only.

MBIO 720.title: Topics in Marine Education, Outreach, and Policy
MBIO 720.subject: MBIO
MBIO 720.description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to education, outreach, and policy of the marine environment. Graduate students only.

MBIO 725.title: Topics in Marine Physiology, Behavior, and Organismal Biology
MBIO 725.subject: MBIO
MBIO 725.description: Lecture, discussion, and/or projects on selected topics related to the physiology, behavior, and biology of marine organisms. Graduate students only.

MBIO 740.title: Advanced Topics in Quantitative Biology
MBIO 740.subject: MBIO
MBIO 740.description: Reflects faculty expertise and needs for graduate training in quantitative methods for biology, including statistical, computational, and analytic approaches. Format (lecture/lab/discussion) will vary by topic. Graduate students only.

MBIO 800.title: Dissertation Research
MBIO 800.subject: MBIO
MBIO 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Graduate students only. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

MATH 100.title: Survey of Mathematics
MATH 100.subject: MATH
MATH 100.description: Selected topics designed to acquaint nonspecialists with examples of mathematical reasoning. May not be taken for credit after 215 or higher.

MATH 111.title: Math for Elementary Teachers I
MATH 111.subject: MATH
MATH 111.description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas, problem solving, and reasoning. Number systems, place value, fractions, and properties of operations. Prospective elementary education majors only.

MATH 112.title: Math for Elementary Teachers II
MATH 112.subject: MATH
MATH 112.description: Understanding, communicating, and representing mathematical ideas; problem solving; reasoning and proof; and using symbolism. Patterns and algebraic thinking, place value and decimals, geometry, and mathematical modeling.

MATH 134.title: Precalculus: Elementary Functions
MATH 134.subject: MATH
MATH 134.description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational exponential and logarithmic functions, composed and inverse functions, techniques of graphing. Credit not allowed for 134 and 140, or 134 and 161.
MATH 134.prereq_raw: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

prereq_tree.text: two years of high school algebra, one year of plane geometry

MATH 140.title: Precalculus: Trigonometry and Analytic Geometry
MATH 140.subject: MATH
MATH 140.description: Studies trigonometric functions, analytic geometry, polar coordinates, vectors, and related topics. This course is the second part of the precalculus sequence. Credit allowed for one of 134, 135, or 140.

MATH 161.title: Precalculus and Elements of Calculus for Economics and the Social Sciences
MATH 161.subject: MATH
MATH 161.description: Algebra review, functions with special attention to polynomial, rational, exponential, and logarithmic functions, algebra of functions, techniques of graphing, differentiation and integration of algebraic functions, applications in economics and social sciences. Credit allowed for only one of 134, 135, or 161.

MATH 190.title: Introduction to Programming
MATH 190.subject: MATH
MATH 190.description: (3 hr) Introduction to numerical algorithms and structured programming using Fortran, MATLAB, or other appropriate language.
MATH 190.prereq_raw: one semester of calculus (203, 215, 241, 242, 243, 244, 251A, 252A, or 253A) (or concurrent), or consent

MATH 203.title: Calculus for Business and Social Sciences
MATH 203.subject: MATH
MATH 203.description: Basic concepts; differentiation and integration applications to management, finance, economics, and the social sciences. Credit allowed for at most one of 203, 215, 241, 251A.

MATH 215.title: Applied Calculus I
MATH 215.subject: MATH
MATH 215.description: Basic concepts; differentiation, differential equations and integration with applications directed primarily to the life sciences. Credit allowed for at most one of 203, 215, 241, 251A.

MATH 216.title: Applied Calculus II
MATH 216.subject: MATH
MATH 216.description: Differential calculus for functions in several variables and curves, systems of ordinary differential equations, series approximation of functions, continuous probability, exposure to use of calculus in the literature.

MATH 241.title: Calculus I
MATH 241.subject: MATH
MATH 241.description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Credit allowed for at most one of 203, 215, 241, 251A.

MATH 242.title: Calculus II
MATH 242.subject: MATH
MATH 242.description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations.
MATH 242.prereq_raw: 241 or 251A or a grade of B or better in 215; or consent

children.text: a grade of B or better in 215

MATH 243.title: Calculus III
MATH 243.subject: MATH
MATH 243.description: Vector algebra, vector-valued functions, differentiation in several variables, and optimization.

MATH 244.title: Calculus IV
MATH 244.subject: MATH
MATH 244.description: Multiple integrals; line integrals and Green’s Theorem; surface integrals, Stokes’s and Gauss’s Theorems.

MATH 251A.title: Accelerated Calculus I
MATH 251A.subject: MATH
MATH 251A.description: Basic concepts; differentiation with applications; integration. Compared to 241, topics are discussed in greater depth. Credit allowed for at most one of 203, 215, 241, 251A.
MATH 251A.prereq_raw: assessment and consent, or a grade of A in 140 and consent

MATH 252A.title: Accelerated Calculus II
MATH 252A.subject: MATH
MATH 252A.description: Integration techniques and applications, series and approximations, differential equations, introduction to vectors.
MATH 252A.prereq_raw: 251A, or a grade of B or better in 241 and consent

children.text: a grade of B or better in 241

MATH 253A.title: Accelerated Calculus III
MATH 253A.subject: MATH
MATH 253A.description: Vector calculus; maxima and minima in several variables; multiple integrals; line integrals, surface integrals and their applications.

MATH 257.title: History of Mathematics
MATH 257.subject: MATH
MATH 257.description: The historical development of mathematical thought.

MATH 301.title: Introduction to Discrete Mathematics
MATH 301.subject: MATH
MATH 301.description: Symbolic logic, sets and relations, algorithms, trees and other graphs. Additional topics chosen from algebraic systems, networks, automata.
MATH 301.prereq_raw: one semester of calculus from mathematics department; or consent. Recommended: one semester programming

children.text: one semester of calculus from mathematics department;

MATH 302.title: Introduction to Differential Equations I
MATH 302.subject: MATH
MATH 302.description: First order ordinary differential equations, constant coefficient linear equations, oscillations, Laplace transform, convolution, Green’s function.
MATH 302.prereq_raw: 216 or 243 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent

MATH 303.title: Introduction to Differential Equations II
MATH 303.subject: MATH
MATH 303.description: Constant coefficient linear systems, variable coefficient ordinary differential equations, series solutions and special functions, Fourier series, partial differential equations.

MATH 304.title: Mathematical Modeling: Deterministic Models
MATH 304.subject: MATH
MATH 304.description: Deterministic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include difference equations, qualitative behavior solutions of ODEs and reaction-diffusion equations. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

MATH 305.title: Mathematical Modeling: Probabilistic Models
MATH 305.subject: MATH
MATH 305.description: Probabilistic mathematical modeling emphasizing models and tools used in the biological sciences. Topics include stochastic and Poisson processes, Markov models, estimation, and Monte Carlo simulation. A computer lab may be taken concurrently.

MATH 307.title: Linear Algebra and Differential Equations
MATH 307.subject: MATH
MATH 307.description: Introduction to linear algebra, application of eigenvalue techniques to the solution of differential equations. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

MATH 311.title: Introduction to Linear Algebra
MATH 311.subject: MATH
MATH 311.description: Algebra of matrices, linear equations, real vector spaces and transformations. Emphasis on concepts and abstraction and instruction of careful writing. Students may receive credit for only one of 307 or 311.

MATH 321.title: Introduction to Advanced Mathematics
MATH 321.subject: MATH
MATH 321.description: Formal introduction to the concepts of logic, finite and infinite sets, functions, methods of proof and axiomatic systems. Learning mathematical expressions in writing is an integral part of the course.

MATH 331.title: Introduction to Real Analysis
MATH 331.subject: MATH
MATH 331.description: A rigorous axiomatic development of one variable calculus. Completeness, topology of the line, limits, continuity, differentiation, integration. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing.

MATH 351.title: Foundation of Euclidean Geometry
MATH 351.subject: MATH
MATH 351.description: Axiomatic Euclidean geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method.

MATH 353.title: Introduction to Euclidean and NonEuclidean Geometries
MATH 353.subject: MATH
MATH 353.description: Axiomatic geometry and introduction to the axiomatic method; Euclidean geometry; hyperbolic geometry, and other nonEuclidean geometries.

MATH 371.title: Elementary Probability Theory
MATH 371.subject: MATH
MATH 371.description: Sets, discrete sample spaces, problems in combinatorial probability, random variables, mathematical expectations, classical distributions, applications.

MATH 372.title: Elementary Probability and Statistics
MATH 372.subject: MATH
MATH 372.description: Problem-oriented introduction to the basic concepts of probability and statistics, providing a foundation for applications and further study.

MATH 373.title: Elementary Statistics
MATH 373.subject: MATH
MATH 373.description: Estimation, tests of significance, the concept of power.

MATH 402.title: Partial Differential Equations I
MATH 402.subject: MATH
MATH 402.description: Integral surfaces and characteristics of first and second order partial differential equations. Applications to the equations of mathematical physics.

MATH 403.title: Partial Differential Equations II
MATH 403.subject: MATH
MATH 403.description: Laplace’s equation, Fourier transform methods for PDEs, higher dimensional PDEs, spherical harmonics, Laplace series, special functions and applications.

MATH 405.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
MATH 405.subject: MATH
MATH 405.description: Systems of linear ordinary differential equations, autonomous systems, and stability theory applications. Optional topics include series solutions, Sturm theory, numerical methods.

MATH 407.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 407.subject: MATH
MATH 407.description: Numerical solution of equations, interpolation, least-squares approximation, quadrature, eigenvalue problems, numerical solution of ordinary and partial differential equations. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 407–408.)
MATH 407.prereq_raw: 243 or 253A, and 307 or 311, and one semester programming; or consent

MATH 408.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 408.subject: MATH
MATH 408.description: Continuation of 407. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 407.

MATH 411.title: Linear Algebra
MATH 411.subject: MATH
MATH 411.description: Vector spaces over arbitrary fields, minimal polynomials, invariant subspaces, canonical forms of matrices; unitary and Hermitian matrices, quadratic forms.

MATH 412.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
MATH 412.subject: MATH
MATH 412.description: Introduction to basic algebraic structures. Groups, finite groups, abelian groups, rings, integral domains, fields, factorization, polynomial rings, field extensions, quotient fields. Emphasis on writing instruction. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 412–413.)

MATH 413.title: Introduction to Abstract Algebra
MATH 413.subject: MATH
MATH 413.description: Continuation of 412. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 412. Emphasis on writing instruction.

MATH 414.title: Linear Programming
MATH 414.subject: MATH
MATH 414.description: Techniques of mathematical programming. Topics may include linear programming, integer programming, network analysis, dynamic programming, and game theory.

MATH 420.title: Introduction to the Theory of Numbers
MATH 420.subject: MATH
MATH 420.description: Congruences, quadratic residues, arithmetic functions, distribution of primes. Emphasis is on teaching theory and writing, not on computation.

MATH 421.title: Topology
MATH 421.subject: MATH
MATH 421.description: General topology, including compactness and connectedness; the Jordan Curve Theorem and the classification of surfaces; first homotopy or homology groups.

MATH 431.title: Principles of Analysis I
MATH 431.subject: MATH
MATH 431.description: Topology of Rn , metric spaces, continuous functions, Riemann integration, sequences and series, uniform convergence, implicit function theorems, differentials and Jacobians. Emphasis on teaching mathematical writing. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 431–432.)

MATH 432.title: Principles of Analysis II
MATH 432.subject: MATH
MATH 432.description: Continuation of 431. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 431. Emphasis on writing instruction continues.

MATH 442.title: Vector Analysis
MATH 442.subject: MATH
MATH 442.description: Vector operations, wedge product, differential forms, and smooth mappings. Theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss, both classically and in terms of forms. Applications to electromagnetism and mechanics.

MATH 443.title: Differential Geometry
MATH 443.subject: MATH
MATH 443.description: Properties and fundamental geometric invariants of curves and surfaces in space; applications to the physical sciences.

MATH 444.title: Complex Analysis
MATH 444.subject: MATH
MATH 444.description: Analytic functions, complex integration, introduction to conformal mapping.

MATH 449.title: Topics in Undergraduate Mathematics
MATH 449.subject: MATH
MATH 449.description: Advanced topics from various areas: algebra, number theory, analysis, and geometry.

MATH 454.title: Axiomatic Set Theory
MATH 454.subject: MATH
MATH 454.description: Sets, relations, ordinal arithmetic, cardinal arithmetic, axiomatic set theory, axiom of choice and the continuum hypothesis.
MATH 454.prereq_raw: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent

children.text: in a related field or consent

MATH 455.title: Mathematical Logic
MATH 455.subject: MATH
MATH 455.description: A system of first order logic. Formal notions of well-formed formula, proof, and derivability. Semantic notions of model, truth, and validity. Completeness theorem.
MATH 455.prereq_raw: 321 or graduate standing in a related field or consent. Recommended: 454

children.text: in a related field or consent . Recommended: 454

MATH 471.title: Probability
MATH 471.subject: MATH
MATH 471.description: Probability spaces, random variables, distributions, expectations, moment-generating and characteristic functions, limit theorems. Continuous probability emphasized.
MATH 471.prereq_raw: 244 (or concurrent) or 253A (or concurrent), or consent. Recommended: 305 or 371 or 372; or consent

MATH 472.title: Statistical Inference
MATH 472.subject: MATH
MATH 472.description: Sampling and parameter estimation, tests of hypotheses, correlation, regression, analysis of variance, sequential analysis, rank order statistics.

MATH 475.title: Combinatorial Mathematics
MATH 475.subject: MATH
MATH 475.description: Finite configurations. Topics may include counting methods, generating functions, graph theory, map coloring, block design, network flows, analysis of discrete algorithms.

MATH 480.title: Senior Seminar
MATH 480.subject: MATH
MATH 480.description: Seminar for senior mathematics majors, including an introduction to methods of research. Significant portion of class time is dedicated to the instruction and critique of oral presentations. All students must give the equivalent of three presentations.

MATH 490.title: Mathematical Biology Seminar
MATH 490.subject: MATH
MATH 490.description: Reports on research in mathematical biology, reviews of literature, and research presentation. Required for Certificate in Mathematical Biology.
MATH 490.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher and consent

MATH 499.title: Directed Reading
MATH 499.subject: MATH
MATH 499.description: Limited to advanced students who must arrange with an instructor before enrolling.

MATH 511.title: Problem Solving for Teachers
MATH 511.subject: MATH
MATH 511.description: Practicing teachers develop and improve their problem-solving skills by working on challenging mathematical tasks. Students improve their mathematics content knowledge by working on problems and learning to design challenge problems for their own classes. Practicing teachers in grades K-12 only. All 600-courses prerequisites graduate standing or consent.

MATH 601.title: Applied Dynamical Systems
MATH 601.subject: MATH
MATH 601.description: Continuous and discrete dynamical systems; bifurcation theory; chaotic maps. Additional topics from PDEs and linear algebra. Graduate students only.

MATH 602.title: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
MATH 602.subject: MATH
MATH 602.description: Classical existence and uniqueness theory for ODEs and PDEs, qualitative properties, classification, boundary value and initial value problems, fundamental solutions, other topics.

MATH 603.title: Ordinary and Partial Differential Equations
MATH 603.subject: MATH
MATH 603.description: Continuation of 602. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 602.

MATH 607.title: Numerical Analysis
MATH 607.subject: MATH
MATH 607.description: Numerical linear algebra including iterative methods, SVD, and other matrix factorizations, locating eigenvalues, discrete approximation to partial differential equations.

MATH 610.title: Key Elements of Linear Algebra
MATH 610.subject: MATH
MATH 610.description: Key concepts of linear algebra for graduate students in mathematics. Specific topics include vector spaces, linear transformations, multilinear forms, and Jordan decomposition. May not receive credit for both MATH 411 and MATH 610. Graduate students only.

MATH 611.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 611.subject: MATH
MATH 611.description: Modules, Sylow theorems, Jordan-Holder theorem, unique factorization domains, Galois theory, algebraic closures, transcendence bases. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 611–612.)

MATH 612.title: Modern Algebra
MATH 612.subject: MATH
MATH 612.description: Continuation of 611. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 611.

MATH 613.title: Group Theory
MATH 613.subject: MATH
MATH 613.description: Sylow theorems, solvable groups, nilpotent groups, extension theory, representation theory, additional topics.

MATH 615.title: Ring Theory
MATH 615.subject: MATH
MATH 615.description: Ideal theory in Noetherian rings, localization, Dedekind domains, the Jacobson radical, the Wedderburn-Artin theorem, additional topics.

MATH 618.title: Lattice Theory
MATH 618.subject: MATH
MATH 618.description: Introduction with applications to general algebra. Partially ordered sets, decomposition theory, representations of lattices, varieties and free lattices, coordinatization of modular lattices.

MATH 619.title: Universal Algebra
MATH 619.subject: MATH
MATH 619.description: Introduction to basic techniques, including subalgebras, congruences, automorphisms and endomorphisms, varieties of algebras, Mal’cev conditions.

MATH 620.title: Key Elements of Topology
MATH 620.subject: MATH
MATH 620.description: Key concepts of Topology for graduate students in mathematics; topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; continuity. Graduate students only.

MATH 621.title: Topology
MATH 621.subject: MATH
MATH 621.description: Properties of topological spaces; separation axioms, compactness, connectedness; metrizability; convergence and continuity. Additional topics from general and algebraic topology. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 621–622.)

MATH 622.title: Topology
MATH 622.subject: MATH
MATH 622.description: Continuation of 621. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 621.

MATH 623.title: Geometric Group Theory
MATH 623.subject: MATH
MATH 623.description: Geometric, topological, and dynamical methods in the study of finitely generated infinite groups. Graduate students only.

MATH 625.title: Differentiable Manifolds I
MATH 625.subject: MATH
MATH 625.description: Differentiable structures on manifolds, tensor fields, Frobenius theorem, exterior algebra, integration of forms, Poincare Lemma, Stoke’s theorem.

MATH 631.title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
MATH 631.subject: MATH
MATH 631.description: Lebesgue measure and integral, convergence of integrals, functions of bounded variation, Lebesgue-Stieltjes integral and more general theory of measure and integration. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 631–632.)

MATH 632.title: Theory of Functions of a Real Variable
MATH 632.subject: MATH
MATH 632.description: Continuation of 631. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 631.

MATH 633.title: Functional Analysis
MATH 633.subject: MATH
MATH 633.description: Linear topological spaces, normed spaces, Hilbert spaces, function algebras, operator theory.

MATH 637.title: Calculus of Variations
MATH 637.subject: MATH
MATH 637.description: Simple variational problems, first and second variation formulas. Euler-Lagrange equation, direct methods, optimal control.

MATH 644.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 644.subject: MATH
MATH 644.description: Conformal mapping, residue theory, series and product developments, analytic continuation, special functions. (These topics are covered in the year sequence 644–645.)

MATH 645.title: Analytic Function Theory
MATH 645.subject: MATH
MATH 645.description: Continuation of 644. This is the second course of a year sequence and should be taken in the same academic year as 644.

MATH 654.title: Introduction to Logic
MATH 654.subject: MATH
MATH 654.description: Model theory, computability theory, set theory. In particular syntax and semantics of first order logic; incompleteness, completeness, and compactness theorems; Loewenheim-Skolem theorems; computable and computably enumerable sets; axioms of set theory; ordinals and cardinals. Graduate students only.

MATH 655.title: Set Theory
MATH 655.subject: MATH
MATH 655.description: Axiomatic development, ordinal and cardinal numbers, recursion theorems, axiom of choice, continuum hypothesis, consistency and independence results.

MATH 657.title: Recursive Functions and Complexity
MATH 657.subject: MATH
MATH 657.description: Recursive, r.e., Ptime, and Logspace classes. Nondeterminism, parallelism, alternation, and Boolean circuits. Reducibility and completeness.

MATH 661.title: Introduction to Algebraic Number Theory
MATH 661.subject: MATH
MATH 661.description: Number fields and rings of integers; primes, factorization, and ramification theory; finiteness of the class group; Dirichlet’s Unit Theorem; valuations, completions, and local fields. Further topics. Graduate students only.

MATH 671.title: Advanced Probability
MATH 671.subject: MATH
MATH 671.description: Independence and conditioning, martingales, ergodic theory, Markov chains, central limit theorem.
MATH 671.prereq_raw: 631 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

MATH 672.title: Stochastic Processes
MATH 672.subject: MATH
MATH 672.prereq_raw: 671 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

MATH 681.title: Graph Theory
MATH 681.subject: MATH
MATH 681.description: Connected graphs and digraphs. Graph embeddings. Connectivity and networks. Factors and factorizations. Coverings. Coloring. Applications.

MATH 695.title: Directed Reading and Research for Plan B Masters Students
MATH 695.subject: MATH
MATH 695.description: Maximum of 3 credit hours. Graduate standing in MATH.

MATH 799.title: Apprenticeship in Teaching
MATH 799.subject: MATH
MATH 799.description: An experience-based introduction to college-level teaching; students serve as student teachers to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching and participation in planning and evaluation. Open to graduate students in mathematics only.
MATH 799.prereq_raw: graduate standing in mathematics and consent

MCB 275.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
MCB 275.subject: MCB
MCB 275.description: Integrated cell and molecular biology for life science majors. Modern advances in recombinant DNA technology.
MCB 275.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 171/171L and CHEM 272

MCB 314.title: Research Ethics
MCB 314.subject: MCB
MCB 314.description: Introduction to the ethical issues faced by individuals and institutions involved in scientific research. Based on case studies, students will discuss and write about ethical issues in research. Issues include humans and animals in research, mentoring, authorship, ownership of data, genetic technologies and record keeping. This course is designed for students with majors in the natural sciences.
MCB 314.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 (or concurrent), or MATH 307 (or concurrent), or MATH 311 (or concurrent), or PHYS 170 (or concurrent), or CHEM 272 (or concurrent); or consent

MCB 407.title: Molecular Cell Biology I
MCB 407.subject: MCB
MCB 407.description: Relationship between structure and function at macromolecular level.
MCB 407.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in BIOL 275/275L and CHEM 273, or consent

MCB 408.title: Molecular Cellular Biology II
MCB 408.subject: MCB
MCB 408.description: Cell structure and function. Structure, chemistry, and functions of organelles and macromolecules.
MCB 408.prereq_raw: C (not C-) or better in 407; or consent

MCB 408L.title: Advanced Molecular and Cellular Biology Laboratory
MCB 408L.subject: MCB
MCB 408L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) A laboratory to accompany 407 and 408.

MCB 461.title: Immunology
MCB 461.subject: MCB
MCB 461.description: Structure and biological actions of antigens and antibodies; fundamentals of antibody synthesis; the relation of immunology to biology and medical sciences.
MCB 461.prereq_raw: MICR 351 or BIOL 171; or consent. Recommended: BIOL 275/275L

MCB 461L.title: Immunology Lab
MCB 461L.subject: MCB
MCB 461L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Basic exercises and experiments in immunology, immunochemistry, immuno-biology to illustrate principles of 461.

MCB 472.title: The Biology of Cancer
MCB 472.subject: MCB
MCB 472.description: Integrative, in-depth focus on the genetics, cell biology, and molecular basis of cancer. Combination of classroom lectures and problem-based discussions in small groups. Addresses ethical implications of cancer research and treatment. MCB or BIOL majors only. Senior standing or higher.
MCB 472.prereq_raw: BIOL 407 (or concurrent) and BIOL 408 (or concurrent) or consent

MCB 475.title: Bacterial Genetics
MCB 475.subject: MCB
MCB 475.description: Genetic analysis and molecular basis of transmission replication, mutation, and expression of heritable characteristics in prokaryotes.

MCB 475L.title: Bacterial Genetics Lab
MCB 475L.subject: MCB
MCB 475L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Techniques for study of transfer and expression of prokaryotic genes: transformation, conjugation, transposon mutagenesis, preparation and analysis of plasmid and chromosomal DNA.

NSCI 101.title: Natural Sciences and Life-Pulling the Puzzles Apart
NSCI 101.subject: NSCI
NSCI 101.description: Journey through the Natural Sciences finding fun, excitement, and success in science, mathematics, engineering, medicine, and all that is the natural sciences. Focus upon challenging worldviews of belief, invention, impact, and ethics.

NSCI 501.title: Seminar for Science Teachers
NSCI 501.subject: NSCI
NSCI 501.description: Seminar and discussions of current and significant topics and problems in science where teachers can exchange new and innovative teaching ideas and strategies.

NSCI 503.title: Computers in Classroom
NSCI 503.subject: NSCI
NSCI 503.description: Combined lecture, laboratory and discussion on the use of computers as a teaching tool in the classroom. To be taught in a hands-on manner appropriate for the science teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

NSCI 504.title: Mathematics Workshop for Teachers
NSCI 504.subject: NSCI
NSCI 504.description: An in-depth study of topics from intermediate and high school mathematics. Restricted to in-service teachers or consent.

NSCI 505.title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
NSCI 505.subject: NSCI
NSCI 505.description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

NSCI 619.title: Seminar on Science Teaching
NSCI 619.subject: NSCI
NSCI 619.description: Effective teaching methods; organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audiovisual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

PHYS 100.title: Survey of Physics
PHYS 100.subject: PHYS
PHYS 100.description: Mechanics, electricity and magnetism, waves, optics, atomic and nuclear physics. Only algebra and geometry used. For non-science majors.

PHYS 100L.title: Survey of Physics Lab
PHYS 100L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 100L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hooke’s law, falling bodies, collisions, Boyle’s law, electric and magnetic fields, induction, waves, optics.

PHYS 109.title: Physics in the Arts
PHYS 109.subject: PHYS
PHYS 109.description: Introduction to physics of sound and light, with applications to music and visual arts: sound perception, harmony, musical scales, instruments; lenses, cameras, color perception and mixing. Uses algebra and geometry. Intended primarily for non-science majors.

PHYS 121.title: How Things Work: Physics for Everyday Life
PHYS 121.subject: PHYS
PHYS 121.description: Introduction to physics and science in everyday life. It considers objects from our daily environment, and focuses on the principles such as motion, forces, heat, electromagnetism, optics, and modern physics.

PHYS 151.title: College Physics I
PHYS 151.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151.description: Non-calculus physics. Mechanics, wave motion, heat.
PHYS 151.prereq_raw: MATH 140, or 215 or higher; or qualifying score on math assessment exam

children.text: qualifying score on math assessment exam

PHYS 151L.title: College Physics Lab I
PHYS 151L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 151L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Introduction to experimental analysis, physical observation and measurement, experiments on conservation laws, fluid friction, oscillations.

PHYS 152L.title: College Physics Lab II
PHYS 152L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 152L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Optics, electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuitry.

PHYS 170.title: General Physics I
PHYS 170.subject: PHYS
PHYS 170.description: Calculus-based mechanics of particles and rigid bodies: kinematics, force, energy, momentum, rotation, gravitation, fluids, oscillations and waves.
PHYS 170.prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 170.restrictions_raw: Intended for physical science and engineering majors.

PHYS 170A.title: Honors General Physics I
PHYS 170A.subject: PHYS
PHYS 170A.description: Special format for topics: mechanics of particles and rigid bodies, wave motion, thermodynamics and kinetic theory.
PHYS 170A.prereq_raw: MATH 242 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent). MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

children.text: MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 170L.title: General Physics I Lab
PHYS 170L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 170L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 151L but at 170 level.

PHYS 272.title: General Physics II
PHYS 272.subject: PHYS
PHYS 272.description: Electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
PHYS 272.prereq_raw: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 272A.title: Honors General Physics II
PHYS 272A.subject: PHYS
PHYS 272A.description: Special format for topics: electricity and magnetism and geometric optics.
PHYS 272A.prereq_raw: 151 or 170 and MATH 242 or MATH 252A, MATH 216 may be substituted with consent

PHYS 272L.title: General Physics II Lab
PHYS 272L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 272L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Similar to 152L but at 272 level.

PHYS 274.title: General Physics III
PHYS 274.subject: PHYS
PHYS 274.description: Relativity, introduction to quantum mechanics, atomic and nuclear physics, and physical optics.
PHYS 274.prereq_raw: 152 or 272 and MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

PHYS 274L.title: General Physics III Lab
PHYS 274L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 274L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating selected concepts of 274, including diffraction and interference of light, wave nature of matter, photoelectric effect, atomic spectra, and semiconductors.

PHYS 305.title: Computational Physics
PHYS 305.subject: PHYS
PHYS 305.description: Analysis of physical systems and problem solving using computers and numerical methods.
PHYS 305.prereq_raw: 152 or 272 or 272A, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

PHYS 310.title: Theoretical Mechanics I
PHYS 310.subject: PHYS
PHYS 310.description: Particle dynamics, rigid-body dynamics, planetary motion.
PHYS 310.prereq_raw: 151 or 170 or 170A, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

PHYS 311.title: Theoretical Mechanics II
PHYS 311.subject: PHYS
PHYS 311.description: Rigid-body mechanics continued, fluid dynamics, wave motion, theory of relativity.

PHYS 350.title: Electricity and Magnetism
PHYS 350.subject: PHYS
PHYS 350.description: Electrostatic and magnetostatic fields in vacuum and in matter; induction; Maxwell’s equations; AC circuits.
PHYS 350.prereq_raw: 152 or 272 or 272A; and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

PHYS 399.title: Individual Work in Advanced Physics
PHYS 399.subject: PHYS
PHYS 399.description: Limited to students with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in physics.

PHYS 400.title: Applications of Mathematics in Physical Sciences
PHYS 400.subject: PHYS
PHYS 400.description: Mathematical methods, techniques; applications to problems in physical sciences.
PHYS 400.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, and MATH 307 or 311; or consent. Recommended: upper division mathematics course

PHYS 430.title: Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
PHYS 430.subject: PHYS
PHYS 430.description: Laws of thermodynamics, heat transfer, kinetic theory, statistical mechanics.

PHYS 440.title: Solid-State Physics I
PHYS 440.subject: PHYS
PHYS 440.description: Crystal structure: lattice vibrations; phonon effects; electronic processes in solids (metals, semiconductors, and superconductors).

PHYS 441.title: Solid-State Physics II
PHYS 441.subject: PHYS
PHYS 441.description: Energy-band calculations, optical processes, Josephson effect, theories of dielectrics and magnetism, physics of color centers, order-disorder transformation.

PHYS 450.title: Electromagnetic Waves
PHYS 450.subject: PHYS
PHYS 450.description: Field equations, plane, spherical and guided waves.

PHYS 460.title: Physical Optics
PHYS 460.subject: PHYS
PHYS 460.description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
PHYS 460.prereq_raw: 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C) or EE 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-), or consent

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) or EE 372 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) , or consent

PHYS 475.title: Electronics for Physicists
PHYS 475.subject: PHYS
PHYS 475.description: Investigation of Kirchoff’s Laws, electromagnetic circuit theory. Fourier analysis and stability theory with circuits. Applications to physical measurements are stressed.

PHYS 476.title: Modern Electronics for Physicists
PHYS 476.subject: PHYS
PHYS 476.description: Introduction to high performance solid state instrumentation by means of practical research electronics: printed circuit board design/fabrication; complex programmable logic design/verification; integrated circuit SPICE simulation. Detector fabrication and test emphasis during final project.

PHYS 480.title: Quantum Mechanics I
PHYS 480.subject: PHYS
PHYS 480.description: Wave mechanics, Schroedinger equation, angular momenta, potential problems.
PHYS 480.prereq_raw: 274, 310, 350, 400 (or concurrent); either MATH 244 or 253A; and either MATH 311 or 307; or consent

PHYS 480L.title: Advanced Physics Lab
PHYS 480L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 480L.description: Advanced experiments including angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization phenomena, chaos, measurements of c and the muon lifetime, crystal diffraction and the Mossbauer effect. Numerical simulations of particular physics experiments are included.

PHYS 481.title: Quantum Mechanics II
PHYS 481.subject: PHYS
PHYS 481.description: Continuation of 480; atomic physics, scattering, perturbation theory.

PHYS 481L.title: Advanced Physics Lab
PHYS 481L.subject: PHYS
PHYS 481L.description: Advanced experiments including angular correlations in positronium annihilation, optical polarization phenomena, chaos, measurements of c and the muon lifetime, crystal diffraction, and the Mossbauer effect. Numerical simulations of particle physics experiments are included.

PHYS 485.title: Professional Ethics for Physicists
PHYS 485.subject: PHYS
PHYS 485.description: Student seminar on ethical principles and their application to research in physics and astronomy and closely-related fields. Historical examples will be presented and discussed by the participants.
PHYS 485.restrictions_raw: PHYS, ASTP, and ASTR majors only.

PHYS 490.title: Modern Physics
PHYS 490.subject: PHYS
PHYS 490.description: Introduction to nuclear and elementary-particle physics.

PHYS 505.title: Physics Workshop for Teachers
PHYS 505.subject: PHYS
PHYS 505.description: Major concepts of physics taught by means of hands-on conceptual activities for elementary and secondary teachers. Restricted to in-service teachers, or consent.

PHYS 600.title: Methods of Theoretical Physics
PHYS 600.subject: PHYS
PHYS 600.description: Mathematical tools of theoretical physics. Continuation of 400 but with an independent selection of topics.

PHYS 610.title: Analytical Mechanics
PHYS 610.subject: PHYS
PHYS 610.description: Dynamics of particles, particle systems; rigid bodies; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian equations; special relativity.

PHYS 650.title: Electrodynamics I
PHYS 650.subject: PHYS
PHYS 650.description: Potential theory, Maxwell’s equations, electromagnetic waves, boundary value problems.

PHYS 651.title: Electrodynamics II
PHYS 651.subject: PHYS
PHYS 651.description: Relativistic electrodynamics, radiation by charged particles.

PHYS 660.title: Advanced Optics
PHYS 660.subject: PHYS
PHYS 660.description: Contemporary advanced applications in optics including nonlinear optics and optical parametric oscillators, atomic lasers and laser systems, and free-electron lasers.

PHYS 670.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 670.subject: PHYS
PHYS 670.description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

PHYS 671.title: Quantum Mechanics
PHYS 671.subject: PHYS
PHYS 671.description: Physical basis and formulation of quantum theory. Exact solutions of Schroedinger equation and their applications. Approximation methods. Applications to atomic, nuclear, and molecular physics.

PHYS 690.title: Seminar
PHYS 690.subject: PHYS
PHYS 690.description: Discussions and reports on physical theory and recent developments.

PHYS 694.title: Condensed Matter Seminar
PHYS 694.subject: PHYS
PHYS 694.description: Results and discussions of current topics in condensed matter physics.

PHYS 695.title: Seminar on Atomic and Solid-State Physics
PHYS 695.subject: PHYS
PHYS 695.description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in atomic, surface, and solid-state physics.

PHYS 696.title: Seminar on Elementary Particle Physics
PHYS 696.subject: PHYS
PHYS 696.description: Reports and discussion on recent developments in elementary particle physics.

PHYS 711.title: Topics in Particles and Fields
PHYS 711.subject: PHYS
PHYS 711.description: Topics in current theoretical research; e.g., unified field theories, general relativity, gravitation, and cosmology.

PHYS 712.title: Special Topics: Experimental Physics
PHYS 712.subject: PHYS
PHYS 712.description: Topics in current experimental research in low-energy physics, high-energy physics, cross-disciplinary physics.

PHYS 713.title: Advanced Topics in Condensed Matter Theory
PHYS 713.subject: PHYS
PHYS 713.description: Topics in condensed matter theory, e.g., group theory, many-body techniques, renormalization group, density functional theory, other topics of current interest.

PHYS 730.title: Statistical Physics I
PHYS 730.subject: PHYS
PHYS 730.description: Equilibrium thermodynamics; Gibbs ensembles; quantum statistics; ideal and non-ideal Fermi; Bose and Boltzmann gases; phase transitions; and critical phenomena.

PHYS 731.title: Statistical Physics II
PHYS 731.subject: PHYS
PHYS 731.description: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics, transport theory, fluctuation dissipation theorem, many-body Green’s function methods, normal Fermi and Bose liquids, superfluidity, superconductivity.

PHYS 772.title: Quantum Field Theory I
PHYS 772.subject: PHYS
PHYS 772.description: Relativistic wave equations and their solutions. Dirac’s theory of the electron, propagator techniques. Applications to quantum electrodynamics.

PHYS 773.title: Quantum Field Theory II
PHYS 773.subject: PHYS
PHYS 773.description: Local gauge invariance, Yang-Mills theory: quantum chromodynamics, spontaneous symmetry breaking and Goldstone bosons; the standard electroweak theory; grand unified theories.

PHYS 777.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
PHYS 777.subject: PHYS
PHYS 777.description: Nuclear physics; electrodynamics; hadron structure and partons. Techniques of particle physics.

PHYS 778.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics II
PHYS 778.subject: PHYS
PHYS 778.description: Quantum chromodynamics; electroweak interactions; the standard model. Techniques of particle physics.

PHYS 785.title: Solid-State Theory
PHYS 785.subject: PHYS
PHYS 785.description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, electron-electron interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

PHYS 786.title: Solid-State Theory
PHYS 786.subject: PHYS
PHYS 786.description: Crystal symmetry, electronic excitations in solids, transport theory, optical properties, cohesive energy, lattice vibrations, electron-phonon interaction, magnetism, superconductivity.

ZOOL 101.title: Principles of Zoology
ZOOL 101.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 101.description: Structure, development, physiology, reproduction, evolution, behavior, and ecology of animals.

ZOOL 200.title: Marine Biology
ZOOL 200.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 200.description: Biology and ecology of marine plants and animals; coral reefs, the deep sea, rocky shores, marine mammals, fisheries, aquaculture, pollution, and conservation of marine resources.

ZOOL 200L.title: Marine Biology Lab
ZOOL 200L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 200L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory, field trips to accompany 200.

ZOOL 416.title: Histology
ZOOL 416.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 416.description: Functional microanatomy of the animal body, emphasizing vertebrates. Oriented toward pre-professional students.

ZOOL 416L.title: Histology Lab
ZOOL 416L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 416L.description: (2 2-hr Lab) Light microscopic study of animal tissues, especially vertebrates. Primarily for pre-professional students.

ZOOL 417.title: Microtechnique
ZOOL 417.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 417.description: Preparation of animal tissues and organs for microscopic examination; introduction to cytochemical and histochemical techniques.

ZOOL 420.title: Developmental Biology
ZOOL 420.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 420.description: Fundamental principles, methods, concepts, and significance of developmental biology, emphasizing experimental methods.

ZOOL 420L.title: Developmental Biology Lab
ZOOL 420L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 420L.description: (2 3-hr Labs) Analysis of animal development by experimental methods, using local organisms.
ZOOL 420L.prereq_raw: 420 (or concurrent) and BIOL 275, or consent. Recommended: BIOL 407

ZOOL 430.title: Animal Physiology
ZOOL 430.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 430.description: Introduction to function of organs, tissues, and cells, especially in vertebrates. Nerve and muscle physiology, endocrinology, circulation, respiration, excretion, and temperature regulation.

ZOOL 430L.title: Animal Physiology Lab
ZOOL 430L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 430L.description: Laboratory investigation of function of organs, tissues, and cells, especially in vertebrates. Nerve and muscle physiology, circulation, membrane transport, respiration, excretion.

ZOOL 432.title: Comparative Physiology
ZOOL 432.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 432.description: Physicalchemical cellular mechanisms underlying function of organ systems; general principles inferable from study of adaption to diverse environments.
ZOOL 432.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and 172, and MBBE 402 (or concurrent) or BIOC 441 (or concurrent); or consent

ZOOL 439L.title: Animal Ecology Lab
ZOOL 439L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 439L.description: (1 4-hr Lab) Introduction to methodology, experience in characterizing populations and communities.

ZOOL 442.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
ZOOL 442.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 442.description: Nerve cells, their signaling capabilities and the developmental organization of nervous systems, both invertebrate and vertebrate, for sensory reception, integration, behavioral command and learning;insights from on-going research using molecular, genetic, biophysical, and imaging methods.

ZOOL 460.title: Avian Biology
ZOOL 460.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 460.description: Broad coverage of the morphology, physiology, ecology, behavior, and evolution of birds, emphasizing the relation of birds to general theory in biology.

ZOOL 466.title: Fisheries Science
ZOOL 466.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 466.description: General characteristics of fisheries; harvesting methods; principles and techniques to derive data and analyze fished populations. Field trips.
ZOOL 466.prereq_raw: one of the following: 410, 465, 470, 608, or 620; or consent

ZOOL 467.title: Ecology of Fishes
ZOOL 467.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 467.description: Reproduction, early life history, age and growth, feeding, niche specificity, competitive interactions, communities, and evolutionary mechanisms.

ZOOL 470.title: Limnology
ZOOL 470.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 470.description: Biology, physics, chemistry of lakes, streams, estuaries.

ZOOL 470L.title: Limnology Lab
ZOOL 470L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 470L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experimental and descriptive field projects on the biology, chemistry, hydrology, and physics of lakes, streams, and estuaries.

ZOOL 485.title: Biogeography
ZOOL 485.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 485.description: Distribution of plants and animals and processes that cause, maintain, and modify them. Approach is synthetic and dynamic.

ZOOL 492.title: Teaching Internship
ZOOL 492.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 492.description: Teaching internship in zoology. Required of ZOOL BS degree students. ZOOL BS majors only. CR/NC only

ZOOL 499.title: Directed Reading or Research
ZOOL 499.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 499.description: Performance of a laboratory, field or library research project under the direction of a faculty advisor. Preparation of a proposal and written final report required. Limited to zoology majors.

ZOOL 606.title: Animal Behavior
ZOOL 606.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 606.description: Lectures and critical discussions on the mechanisms of animal behavior, social and interspecific behaviors, behavioral ecology, and evolutionary theory.

ZOOL 606L.title: Principles of Animal Behavior Lab
ZOOL 606L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 606L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Group or individual research projects depending on interest of students.

ZOOL 607.title: Genetics of Behavior and Evolution
ZOOL 607.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 607.description: Introduction to concepts and techniques in the genetics of behavior. Techniques include next gen sequencing, GWAS, and more. Students may use real data to analyze associations between genotype and phenotype. Graduate students only.

ZOOL 608.title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology
ZOOL 608.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 608.description: Lectures, readings and presentations on sensory systems and behavior of fishes.

ZOOL 608L.title: Fish Behavior and Sensory Biology Laboratory
ZOOL 608L.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 608L.description: Laboratory study of fish sensory systems and behavior.

ZOOL 610.title: Topics in Development and Reproductive Biology
ZOOL 610.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 610.description: Discussion and survey of literature on specific topics; some field and lab work may be required.

ZOOL 619.title: Seminar on Science Teaching
ZOOL 619.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 619.description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses, lectures, laboratory exercises; development and evaluation of examinations; computers and audiovisual aids. Open to graduate students in various science disciplines.

ZOOL 620.title: Marine Ecology
ZOOL 620.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 620.description: Principles of ecology of marine biota and environment.
ZOOL 620.prereq_raw: graduate standing in zoology, oceanography, or botany; or consent

children.text: in zoology, oceanography, or botany; or consent

ZOOL 623.title: Quantitative Field Ecology
ZOOL 623.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 623.description: Formal quantitative approach in identifying, designing, performing, analyzing, and interpreting ecological field problems.

ZOOL 625.title: Evolution in Marine Systems
ZOOL 625.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 625.description: Fundamental elements of modern evolutionary theory and research, with a strong focus on marine organisms and ecosystems.

ZOOL 631.title: Biometry
ZOOL 631.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 631.description: Basic statistical methods: design of studies; data exploration; probability; distributions; parametric and nonparametric one-sample, two-sample, multi-sample, regression, and correlation analyses; frequency tables.
ZOOL 631.prereq_raw: MATH 215 or 216 or 241 or 251A or NREM 203 (or equivalent), or consent

ZOOL 632.title: Advanced Biometry
ZOOL 632.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 632.description: Multivariate statistical methods: multiple regression and correlation; multiway anova; general linear models; repeated measures and multivariate anova; loglinear analysis and logistic regression.

ZOOL 642.title: Cellular Neurophysiology
ZOOL 642.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 642.description: Biophysical and membrane mechanisms of conduction, synaptic transmission, and other electrical responses of nerve cells.

ZOOL 652.title: Population Biology
ZOOL 652.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 652.description: Theory and applications of population biology; behavior of population models, as revealed by analytical methods and computer simulation; application to population problems such as endangered species; discussion of classical and current literature in population biology.
ZOOL 652.prereq_raw: one of the following: 439, 467, 620, 623, BOT 453, BOT 454, BOT 456, NREM 680, PEPS 671; or consent

ZOOL 670.title: Scientific Teaching Tools to Promote Active Learning
ZOOL 670.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 670.description: Graduate level course to train students in the pedagogical tools to enhance active learning in STEM classes. Includes discussions of the primary literature, demonstrations and practice using scientific teaching techniques. BOT or ZOOL or MBIO majors only. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)

ZOOL 690.title: Conservation Biology
ZOOL 690.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 690.description: Theories and concepts of ecology, evolution and genetics for conservation of biological diversity. Topics will include restoration ecology, management planning, laws and policies, biological invasions.
ZOOL 690.prereq_raw: BIOL 375 and either 480 or BOT 462; and either 410, 439, 620, 623, BOT 453, 454, 456, or 492

ZOOL 699.title: Directed Research
ZOOL 699.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 699.description: Directed research and reading in various fields of zoology.

ZOOL 710.title: Topics in Biometry
ZOOL 710.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 710.description: Selected advanced topics in experimental design or data analysis for biologists.

ZOOL 712.title: Topics in Nerve/Muscle Physiology
ZOOL 712.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 712.description: Advanced treatment of selected topics under current active investigation.
ZOOL 712.prereq_raw: a graduate course in physiology, neurology, or related subjects and consent

children.text: a graduate course in physiology, neurology,

ZOOL 716.title: Topics in Fish and Fisheries Biology
ZOOL 716.subject: ZOOL

ZOOL 718.title: Topics in Animal Physiology
ZOOL 718.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 718.description: Selected problems in environmental physiology, electro-physiology, or neurophysiology. Basic concepts and measurements of function at the organismic or cellular level.

ZOOL 719.title: Topics in Systematics and Evolution
ZOOL 719.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 719.description: Selected problems of current or historic interest.

ZOOL 739.title: Topics in Ecology
ZOOL 739.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 739.description: Advanced topics in ecology; discussion of literature and in depth survey of specific areas.

ZOOL 750.title: Topics in Conservation Biology
ZOOL 750.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 750.description: Advanced topics in conservation and environmental biology.

ZOOL 780.title: Foundations of Evolution and Ecology I
ZOOL 780.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 780.description: Graduate level introduction to evolution and ecology emphasizing foundational literature, modern models and inference, and major questions in evolution and ecology. Topics include population ecology, community ecology, the genetics of populations, systematics, and speciation. (Alt. years: fall)

ZOOL 781.title: Foundations of Evolution and Ecology II
ZOOL 781.subject: ZOOL
ZOOL 781.description: Graduate level introduction to evolution and ecology emphasizing foundational literature, modern models and inference, and major questions in evolution and ecology. This is the second semester continuation of 780. (Alt. years: spring)

ANTH 151.title: Emerging Humanity
ANTH 151.subject: ANTH
ANTH 151.description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Open to nonmajors, recommended for majors.

ANTH 151A.title: Emerging Humanity
ANTH 151A.subject: ANTH
ANTH 151A.description: Introduction to human biological evolution and the archaeology of culture in the world prior to AD 1500. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

ANTH 152.title: Culture and Humanity
ANTH 152.subject: ANTH
ANTH 152.description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order. Open to non-majors, required for ANTH majors.

ANTH 152A.title: Culture and Humanity
ANTH 152A.subject: ANTH
ANTH 152A.description: Introduction to cultural anthropology. How humans create, understand, order and modify their natural, social, supernatural and physical environments, and make meaning and order. Restricted to students in the Honors Program.

ANTH 175.title: Polynesian Surf Culture
ANTH 175.subject: ANTH
ANTH 175.description: Examines environmental and cultural factors in the development of Polynesian surf culture, surfing’s decline due to Western influence, and its revitalization as a modern recreational activity. Business practices of the surfing industry are critically analyzed.

ANTH 175L.title: Polynesian Surf Culture Field Lab
ANTH 175L.subject: ANTH
ANTH 175L.description: 175 co-requisite lab. Surfing sites are visited, ancient and modern Polynesian surfing practices and surfboard design and technology are discussed. Shoreline assessments emphasize ocean safety. Social issues surrounding surfing sites in Hawai‘i are analyzed.

ANTH 204.title: Historical Ecology of Hawai‘i
ANTH 204.subject: ANTH
ANTH 204.description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

ANTH 210.title: Archaeology
ANTH 210.subject: ANTH
ANTH 210.description: Introduction to prehistoric archaeology; methods and techniques of excavation and laboratory analysis; brief survey of theory in relation to change and diversity in prehistoric human groups.

ANTH 215.title: Introduction to Biological Anthropology
ANTH 215.subject: ANTH
ANTH 215.description: Human evolution, primatology, human genetics, biological variation, human adaptability, growth and development.

ANTH 220.title: Quantitative Reasoning for Anthropologists
ANTH 220.subject: ANTH
ANTH 220.description: Achieve basic quantitative literacy and to familiarize them with statistical reasoning so that they are prepared to carry out anthropological (and other social science) research.

ANTH 230.title: Anthropology of Sports
ANTH 230.subject: ANTH
ANTH 230.description: Explores sports from anthropological viewpoint: biological, cultural, linguistic, and archaeological. Open to nonmajors. Sophomore standing only.

ANTH 300.title: Study of Contemporary Problems
ANTH 300.subject: ANTH
ANTH 300.description: Significance of anthropology for contemporary affairs, particularly American ethnic and minority group relations. Relevance to various professions, governmental policy, political action, and accomplishment of change.

ANTH 301.title: Culture and Health
ANTH 301.subject: ANTH
ANTH 301.description: Social and cultural aspects of medicine; the relationship of medicine to the beliefs, social systems, ecological adaptations, and cultural changes of human groups.

ANTH 310.title: Human Origins
ANTH 310.subject: ANTH
ANTH 310.description: Theory of evolution, evolutionary systematics, and taxonomy; evolutionary biology of primates; fossil records for primate and human evolution. Laboratory included.

ANTH 313.title: Visual Anthropology
ANTH 313.subject: ANTH
ANTH 313.description: Historical development of documentary films of non-Western peoples; critical examination of ways in which ethnographic films represent different cultures.

ANTH 315.title: Sex and Gender
ANTH 315.subject: ANTH
ANTH 315.description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual differences; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

ANTH 316.title: Anthropology of Tourism
ANTH 316.subject: ANTH
ANTH 316.description: Anthropological perspectives on the subject of the global phenomenon of tourism. Includes issues of cultural performance, identity, and commoditization. Open to nonmajors.

ANTH 323.title: Pacific Islands Archaeology
ANTH 323.subject: ANTH
ANTH 323.description: Origins of Pacific peoples; chronology of settlement; sequences of culture in Australia, Melanesia, Micronesia, and Polynesia.

ANTH 325.title: Origins of Cities
ANTH 325.subject: ANTH
ANTH 325.description: Combined lecture/ discussion on the emergence and development of ancient cities in comparative perspective and the dynamics of (pre)modern urban life. Examples are drawn from the Near East, Mediterranean, Africa, India, China, and the Americas.

ANTH 326.title: American Folklore and Folklife
ANTH 326.subject: ANTH
ANTH 326.description: Examination of the history and ethics of folklore studies and the dynamics and social functions of traditional culture in diverse communities through topics such as ritual, storytelling, games, gossip, belief, music, and cultural tourism.

ANTH 327.title: Ethnohistory
ANTH 327.subject: ANTH
ANTH 327.description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e., the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

ANTH 328.title: Food Origins, Food Culture
ANTH 328.subject: ANTH
ANTH 328.description: Lectures and discussion offer an anthropological introduction to how humans created and transformed food through time.

ANTH 329.title: Indigenous Peoples and Cultures of North America
ANTH 329.subject: ANTH
ANTH 329.description: Survey of Indigenous peoples of North America. Integrates documentary records, ethnography, and archaeology to explore variability among native communities. Contemporary topics include political recognition and self-determination, health and education, and natural resources and economic development.

ANTH 332.title: Anthropology of Surfing
ANTH 332.subject: ANTH
ANTH 332.description: Applies cultural anthropology to assess surfing as an indigenous Hawaiian and modern globalized activity. Discusses the history of surfing, surfing culture, and the impacts of surfing tourism on coastal development, reef ecology, and ocean safety.

ANTH 333.title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
ANTH 333.subject: ANTH
ANTH 333.description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring)

ANTH 341.title: Anthropology of Virtual Worlds
ANTH 341.subject: ANTH
ANTH 341.description: Anthropological study of computer mediated interaction. Focus on the ethnography of massively multiplayer online games, text-based chat rooms, and blogs.

ANTH 345.title: Aggression, War, and Peace
ANTH 345.subject: ANTH
ANTH 345.description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

ANTH 350.title: Pacific Island Cultures
ANTH 350.subject: ANTH
ANTH 350.description: Introduction to cultures of Polynesia, Micronesia, and Melanesia from time of first settlement to emergence of modern nation states.

ANTH 360.title: Primate Behavioral Ecology
ANTH 360.subject: ANTH
ANTH 360.description: As primates are our closest living relatives, studying the range of variation in areas like life history, diet, communication, and social systems within the order primates can inform on how we ourselves evolved.

ANTH 368.title: Households in Cross-cultural Perspective
ANTH 368.subject: ANTH
ANTH 368.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in household and community level organizations in Latin America and elsewhere. Topics may include gender relations, kinship structures, political economy, impacts of colonialism, modernization, and globalization on households.

ANTH 370.title: Ethnographic Field Techniques
ANTH 370.subject: ANTH
ANTH 370.description: Problems and techniques of social-cultural anthropological fieldwork; ethnographic literature; work with informants.

ANTH 375.title: Race and Human Variation
ANTH 375.subject: ANTH
ANTH 375.description: Human genetic and physical variation; latitudinal, longitudinal, and altitudinal variation across human populations; history of racism; contemporary issues in race and racism.
ANTH 375.prereq_raw: sophomore standing, recommend 152 and 215; or consent. (Once a year)

ANTH 379.title: Archaeology Practicum
ANTH 379.subject: ANTH
ANTH 379.description: Students will gain practical archaeological experience (e.g., materials processing, analysis, documentation, conservation) under the direction of practicing archaeological professionals in the local community and in collaboration with supervising archaeological faculty. ANTH majors or minors only. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 380.title: Archaeological Lab Techniques
ANTH 380.subject: ANTH
ANTH 380.description: Laboratory analysis and evaluation of field data; preservation and restoration of artifacts. Preparation for publication.

ANTH 381.title: Archaeological Field Techniques
ANTH 381.subject: ANTH
ANTH 381.description: Archaeological survey and excavations; field trips, mapping, photography. May focus on terrestrial or underwater. May be taught entirely in the field at a national or international archaeological site.

ANTH 382.title: How Archaeology Works
ANTH 382.subject: ANTH
ANTH 382.description: Uses archaeological examples to illustrate social science research techniques. Students learn how to create, analyze, and evaluate data through lab-based exercises, and examine ethical issues inherent in anthropological practice. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 384.title: Skeletal Biology
ANTH 384.subject: ANTH
ANTH 384.description: Introduction to the human skeleton and methods for analyzing archaeological human remains including age, sex, ethnicity, paleodemography, skeletal and dental variation, paleopathology, population studies.

ANTH 410.title: Ethics in Anthropology
ANTH 410.subject: ANTH
ANTH 410.description: Seminar surveying ethical cases, problems, issues and questions from the inception of anthropology to the present. Junior standing or higher or consent.

ANTH 411.title: Museum Anthropology
ANTH 411.subject: ANTH
ANTH 411.description: Anthropological study of museums and related sites of cultural production (historic sites, memorials, theme parks). (Alt. years)

ANTH 412.title: Evolutionary Anthropology
ANTH 412.subject: ANTH
ANTH 412.description: Lecture discussion providing an overview of evolutionary theory in anthropology: focus on the evolution of culture, behavioral ecology, and cultural diversity; emphasis on archaeological and ethnographic research and explanatory models.

ANTH 413.title: Language and Gender
ANTH 413.subject: ANTH
ANTH 413.description: The role of language in the construction of gender and in the maintenance of the gender order. Field projects explore hypotheses about the interaction of language and gender. No previous knowledge of linguistics required.

ANTH 414.title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
ANTH 414.subject: ANTH
ANTH 414.description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

ANTH 415.title: Ecological Anthropology
ANTH 415.subject: ANTH
ANTH 415.description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

ANTH 416.title: Wealth, Culture, and Economic Anthropology
ANTH 416.subject: ANTH
ANTH 416.description: Analysis of economic activities in non-Western, non-industrial societies; production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services in a variety of cultures.

ANTH 417.title: Political Anthropology
ANTH 417.subject: ANTH
ANTH 417.description: Character of political institutions and their development in nonWestern and non industrial societies.

ANTH 419.title: Indigenous Anthropology
ANTH 419.subject: ANTH
ANTH 419.description: Exploration of how anthropology studies indigenous groups throughout the world. An examination of the changing contexts of anthropological practice as calls for reflexivity lead anthropology of all backgrounds to bring insights from their “homes.” Issues include the question of objectivity, the emicetic distinction, and the ethics of different kinds of anthropological research and the role of anthropologists in indigenous self-determination.

ANTH 420.title: Communication and Culture
ANTH 420.subject: ANTH
ANTH 420.description: Anthropological introduction to communication; intercultural and interspecies comparisons; verbal and nonverbal. Ethnography of communication, discourse and structural analyses, ethnomethodology.

ANTH 422.title: Anthropology of Magic, Witchcraft, and Religion
ANTH 422.subject: ANTH
ANTH 422.description: Cults, legends, millennial movements, myths, possession, rituals, sacred healing, shamanism, sorcery, spirits, symbolism, witchcraft, and other forms of religious and symbolic expression and experience, from small scale to highly urban societies.

ANTH 423.title: Social and Cultural Change
ANTH 423.subject: ANTH
ANTH 423.description: Various approaches to examples of social and cultural change in non-literate societies; evolution, diffusion, acculturation, revolution, etc. Historical features and social processes of colonialism.

ANTH 424.title: Islands as Model Systems: Human Biogeography of the Pacific
ANTH 424.subject: ANTH
ANTH 424.description: Applying the concept of islands as “model systems;” explores the impacts of human populations on the natural ecosystems of oceanic islands, and the reciprocal effects of anthropogenic change on human cultures.

ANTH 426.title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
ANTH 426.subject: ANTH
ANTH 426.description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.

ANTH 427.title: Food, Health, and Society
ANTH 427.subject: ANTH
ANTH 427.description: How human groups identify, collect, create, and transform foods; how they shape those into dietary behaviors, and the influence of those behaviors on health.
ANTH 427.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher or consent

ANTH 428.title: Anthropology of the Body
ANTH 428.subject: ANTH
ANTH 428.description: Exploration of the history and development of theories of the body via topics such as phenomenology, perception, bodily rituals, gender, sex, race, colonialism, power, pain, medicalization, immunology, reproductive health and cyborgs.

ANTH 429.title: Anthropology of Consumer Cultures
ANTH 429.subject: ANTH
ANTH 429.description: Examines the practices and meanings of consumption in the contemporary world. Topics include social class, branding, fandom, global-local nexus.

ANTH 431.title: Indigenous Crops/Food Systems
ANTH 431.subject: ANTH
ANTH 431.description: Schemes for managing sequences and combinations of crops and crop production activities. Ecosystem and social determinants. Multiple cropping. Analysis of alternative cropping systems.

ANTH 440.title: The Agriculture of Identity: Food and Farming in Anthropological Perspective
ANTH 440.subject: ANTH
ANTH 440.description: Exploration of agriculture from the perspective of anthropology, with a focus on alternatives to industrial agriculture, especially in the context of Hawai‘i. Readings include academic writing and also literary non-fiction and journalism.

ANTH 442.title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
ANTH 442.subject: ANTH
ANTH 442.description: Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism.

ANTH 443.title: Anthropology of Buddhism
ANTH 443.subject: ANTH
ANTH 443.description: Selected aspects of national, regional and local manifestations of Buddhism are explored through the perspective of anthropology with an emphasis on the daily lives of monks, nuns and lay persons in their socio-cultural contexts.

ANTH 444.title: Spiritual Ecology
ANTH 444.subject: ANTH
ANTH 444.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of the relationships between religions, environment and environmentalism.

ANTH 445.title: Sacred Places
ANTH 445.subject: ANTH
ANTH 445.description: Lectures and seminars provide a cross-cultural survey of sites which societies recognize as sacred and their cultural, ecological and conservation aspects.

ANTH 446.title: Southeast Asian Cultures
ANTH 446.subject: ANTH
ANTH 446.description: Cultures of Southeast Asia from hunting and gathering groups to high civilizations; kinship, economic, political, and religious systems; recent developments.

ANTH 447.title: Polynesian Cultures
ANTH 447.subject: ANTH
ANTH 447.description: Analysis of Polynesian cultures from their origins to contemporary states.

ANTH 449.title: Anthropology of Melanesia
ANTH 449.subject: ANTH
ANTH 449.description: Close study of cultures of Papua New Guinea, Vanuatu, Solomon Islands, New Caledonia, and Fiji through anthropological ethnography.

ANTH 458.title: Forensic Anthropology
ANTH 458.subject: ANTH
ANTH 458.description: Application of physical anthropology to problems in human identification. Determination of age, sex, ancestry, etc., of the skeleton and preparation of reports for legal medicine.

ANTH 459.title: Extinctions
ANTH 459.subject: ANTH
ANTH 459.description: An extraordinary number of plants and animals have gone extinct. Delves deeply into the primary literature that focuses on extinction and conservation from the beginning of the earth to the present day.

ANTH 460.title: Asian Paleoanthropology
ANTH 460.subject: ANTH
ANTH 460.description: Neogene-Quaternary paleoenvironmental reconstructions; human evolution in East Asia during the Pleistocene; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.

ANTH 461.title: Southeast Asian Archaeology
ANTH 461.subject: ANTH
ANTH 461.description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, India, Australia, and Oceania.

ANTH 462.title: East Asian Archaeology
ANTH 462.subject: ANTH
ANTH 462.description: Prehistory and protohistory of China, Japan, and Korea from earliest human occupation to historic times. Geographical emphasis may vary between China and Japan/Korea.

ANTH 463.title: Anthropology of Global Health and Development
ANTH 463.subject: ANTH
ANTH 463.description: Seminar explores the definitions and histories of development and global health initiatives in developing countries from an anthropological perspective. Reading materials include scholarly and popular texts that propose and critique solutions to global poverty. Sophomore standing or higher.

ANTH 464.title: Hawaiian Archaeology
ANTH 464.subject: ANTH
ANTH 464.description: Archaeological perspective in Hawai‘i’s past; origins of Hawaiians; early settlement and culture change; settlement patterns and material culture; historic sites preservation.

ANTH 465.title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
ANTH 465.subject: ANTH
ANTH 465.description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 466.title: Quantitative Archaeology
ANTH 466.subject: ANTH
ANTH 466.description: Combined lecture/lab. Introduction to the basic principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. Exploratory data analysis approach. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 467.title: Biomedicine and Culture
ANTH 467.subject: ANTH
ANTH 467.description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies and practices of modern medicine.
ANTH 467.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, 152, or consent

ANTH 471.title: Field Mapping
ANTH 471.subject: ANTH
ANTH 471.description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
ANTH 471.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

ANTH 472.title: Ceramic Analysis in Archaeology
ANTH 472.subject: ANTH
ANTH 472.description: Concepts, methods, and approaches used in the analysis of ancient pottery. Emphasis placed on ceramic technology, stylistic analysis.

ANTH 473.title: Lithic Artifact Assemblage Analysis
ANTH 473.subject: ANTH
ANTH 473.description: Combined lecture/lab on the manufacture and analysis of stone tools. Students work with experimental collections and engage in stone tool production. The ways in which lithics enlighten us about past human behavior are discussed.

ANTH 475.title: Faunal Analysis in Archaeology
ANTH 475.subject: ANTH
ANTH 475.description: Analysis of archaeologically recovered faunal collections with emphasis on identification and interpretation of nonhuman vertebrate remains.

ANTH 477.title: Spatial Analysis in Archaeology
ANTH 477.subject: ANTH
ANTH 477.description: Lecture/lab. Introduction to the use of Geographical Information Systems (GIS) and spatial statistics in archaeological research. Topics include: map creation; spatial database management; spatial analysis; image processing, data reporting; and data display. Junior standing or higher.

ANTH 478.title: New World Rituals and Ideologies
ANTH 478.subject: ANTH
