ANTH 478.description: Study of cross-cultural patterns in ritual behaviors and creolization of African, indigenous, and Iberian ideological frameworks in the Americas. Topics may include syncretic religions (voodoo, candomble), Andean Christianity, spiritual conquest, conceptions of death, etc. Sophomore standing or higher. Minimum C- required grade for prerequisites.

ANTH 481.title: Applied Anthropology
ANTH 481.subject: ANTH
ANTH 481.description: The application of anthropological methods and concepts to solving practical human problems such as homelessness, domestic violence, maternal morbidity, conflict over resources, and the loss of indigenous languages. Includes a significant service-learning component.

ANTH 482.title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
ANTH 482.subject: ANTH
ANTH 482.description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

ANTH 483.title: Japanese Culture and Behavior
ANTH 483.subject: ANTH
ANTH 483.description: Sociocultural factors in Japanese behavior. Social structure; traditional institutions

ANTH 484.title: Japanese Popular Culture
ANTH 484.subject: ANTH
ANTH 484.description: Explores contemporary Japanese popular culture through themes such as gender, consumerism, globalization and nostalgia. Rather than a survey of popular culture genres, the course is organized thematically around issues and problematics.

ANTH 485.title: Pre-European Hawai‘i
ANTH 485.subject: ANTH
ANTH 485.description: Pre-European society and culture from an anthropological viewpoint.

ANTH 486.title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
ANTH 486.subject: ANTH
ANTH 486.description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i and utilizes anthropological and ethnic studies approaches to study identity, race, ethnicity, culture, language, gender, sex, class, land, and residence.
ANTH 486.prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

ANTH 487.title: Anthropology of Okinawa and Its Diaspora
ANTH 487.subject: ANTH
ANTH 487.description: Explores the ties of identity that exist within and between Okinawa and its diasporic populations.

ANTH 488.title: Chinese Culture: Ethnography
ANTH 488.subject: ANTH
ANTH 488.description: Critical interpretations of ethnographic and biographic texts depicting individual and family lives in different socioeconomic circumstances, geographical regions, and historical periods of modern China.

ANTH 490.title: History of Anthropology
ANTH 490.subject: ANTH
ANTH 490.description: Development of anthropological ideas, focusing on theoretical issues concerning culture, society, and human nature. Required of majors.

ANTH 491.title: Special Topics in Southeast Asian Art History: Monuments and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
ANTH 491.subject: ANTH
ANTH 491.description: Focused study of particular periods, regions and critical themes in Southeast Asian art and architectural history. Monuments and nationalism in Southeast Asia.

ANTH 493.title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
ANTH 493.subject: ANTH
ANTH 493.description: Literature and methodology; project design. Students develop and execute an oral history project. Junior standing or consent.

ANTH 495.title: Senior Thesis I
ANTH 495.subject: ANTH
ANTH 495.description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. First semester of a two-semester sequence with 496. May be taken concurrently with 496. Optional for majors.

ANTH 496.title: Senior Thesis II
ANTH 496.subject: ANTH
ANTH 496.description: Preparation of a major paper in anthropology with a committee of one chairperson and one other. Second semester of a two-semester sequence with 495. May be taken concurrently with 495. Optional for majors.

ANTH 601.title: Ethnology
ANTH 601.subject: ANTH
ANTH 601.description: Survey, in historical perspective, of theory in social and cultural anthropology, from the origin of anthropology to 1976. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 602.title: Linguistic Anthropology
ANTH 602.subject: ANTH
ANTH 602.description: Investigation of mutual influences of linguistic theory and methodology and anthropological theory and methodology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 603.title: Archaeology
ANTH 603.subject: ANTH
ANTH 603.description: Development of critical and analytical skills in assessment of archaeological literature; emphasis on the science, theory, explanation, and paradigms that comprise archaeology. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 604.title: Biological Anthropology Core
ANTH 604.subject: ANTH
ANTH 604.description: Human evolution and human variability in extant and previously existing populations; emphasis on history of physical anthropology, evolutionary systematics, primate biology and behavior, paleontology, anthropological genetics, climatic adaptation, growth, and nutrition. A course in the graduate core of anthropology.

ANTH 605.title: Discursive Practices
ANTH 605.subject: ANTH
ANTH 605.description: Emphasizes linguistic, semantic, and interactional aspects of culture, exploring ways that discourse constructs social action and social realities, examining processes by which culture is produced as meaningful behavior in actual situations.

ANTH 606.title: Anthropology of Infectious Disease
ANTH 606.subject: ANTH
ANTH 606.description: The role of human behavior, including its social and cultural determinants, in understanding the distribution of infectious diseases and in shaping preventive and therapeutic strategies.

ANTH 607.title: The Media and Discursive Practice
ANTH 607.subject: ANTH
ANTH 607.description: Role of the mass media in constructing meaning in social cultural processes such as nationalism, ritual, identity, and collective memory. Attention to interactional and post-structural theories of discourse that link the mass media to discursive practice.

ANTH 608.title: History and Memory
ANTH 608.subject: ANTH
ANTH 608.description: History and collective memory as culturally formed and politically contested realities. The role of narrative, ritual, and media technologies in shaping representations of the past.

ANTH 610.title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
ANTH 610.subject: ANTH
ANTH 610.description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

ANTH 611.title: Contemporary Anthropological Theory
ANTH 611.subject: ANTH
ANTH 611.description: Graduate seminar that examines the history of theory in sociocultural anthropology from 1960 to present. Designed to be taken in sequence after 601.

ANTH 623.title: Advanced Pacific Islands Archaeology
ANTH 623.subject: ANTH
ANTH 623.description: Advanced theoretical and methodological examination of archaeological research in Oceania, a region including the islands of Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

ANTH 645.title: Historic Preservation
ANTH 645.subject: ANTH
ANTH 645.description: Federal, state, and local laws and regulations that regulate and provide protection to significant archaeological and historical resources in Hawai‘i and the region. (Alt. years: spring only) .

ANTH 659.title: Advances in Extinctions
ANTH 659.subject: ANTH
ANTH 659.description: To delve deeply into the primary literature that focuses on the subjects of extinction and conservation broadly speaking, with particular emphasis on the 6 mass extinction events, including the Anthropocene. (Alt. years)

ANTH 660.title: Paleoanthropology of Asia
ANTH 660.subject: ANTH
ANTH 660.description: Survey of the Asian paleoanthropological record, particularly in its paleoenvironmental setting; Out of Africa I; modern human origins.
ANTH 660.prereq_raw: graduate standing and relevant background in anthropology or related field

ANTH 661.title: Archaeological Perspectives on Southeast Asia
ANTH 661.subject: ANTH
ANTH 661.description: Prehistory and protohistory of Southeast Asia, and of Southeast Asian contacts with East Asia, india, Australia, and Oceania.
ANTH 661.prereq_raw: background in archaeology or Southeast Asian history or consent

ANTH 663.title: Anthropology of Global Aid
ANTH 663.subject: ANTH
ANTH 663.description: Examines ideologies of development, humanitarian, and global health interventions from an anthropological perspective. Explores the disjuncture between discourses that portrays global aid as easing suffering and those that accuse it of maintaining relationships of domination. (Alt. years: spring)

ANTH 666.title: Archaeological Data Analysis
ANTH 666.subject: ANTH
ANTH 666.description: Advanced introduction to the fundamental principles of statistics as applied to the analysis of archaeological data. (Alt. years)

ANTH 667.title: Biomedicine and Culture
ANTH 667.subject: ANTH
ANTH 667.description: Examination of the social and cultural foundations of, and responses to, the values, technologies, and practices of modern medicine.

ANTH 668.title: Archaeology Field Methods
ANTH 668.subject: ANTH
ANTH 668.description: (5 7-hr Lab) Laboratory and field training in the principles and practice of methods of archaeology—survey, mapping, excavation, conservation.

ANTH 670.title: Applied Archaeology Practicum
ANTH 670.subject: ANTH
ANTH 670.description: Applies course work in archaeology to handson activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. MA track in Applied Archaeology students only.

ANTH 671.title: Applied Method and Theory in Hawaiian Archaeology
ANTH 671.subject: ANTH
ANTH 671.description: Graduate seminar focused on method and theory in the practice of applied archaeology in Hawai‘i.

ANTH 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
ANTH 676.subject: ANTH
ANTH 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.

ANTH 681.title: Applied Cultural Anthropology
ANTH 681.subject: ANTH
ANTH 681.description: Theory, methods, and results of application of cultural anthropological concepts to practical problems. Graduate students only.

ANTH 682.title: Applied Cultural Anthropology Practicum
ANTH 682.subject: ANTH
ANTH 682.description: Applies course work in cultural anthropology to hands-on activities under the direction of practicing professionals and university faculty. Graduate students only.

ANTH 695.title: Professional Skills Develop in Anthropology
ANTH 695.subject: ANTH
ANTH 695.description: Seminar prepares graduate students for entry into profession, including employment opportunities, research, presentations, ethics and outreach. Required of all Plan B students.

ANTH 710.title: Seminar in Research Methods in Cultural Anthropology
ANTH 710.subject: ANTH
ANTH 710.description: Ethnographic research methods. Introduction to the approaches and techniques of participatory research, including the collection, analysis, and interpretation of social and cultural data. Politics and ethics of research practice.
ANTH 710.prereq_raw: graduate standing in anthropology or consent

ANTH 711.title: Seminar in Research Design and Proposal Writing
ANTH 711.subject: ANTH
ANTH 711.description: Research design and proposal writing. For students preparing for advanced research.

ANTH 720.title: Anthropology of Japan
ANTH 720.subject: ANTH
ANTH 720.description: Japan examined through three dimensions of cultural anthropology: cultural/symbolic, social/organizational, and individual/psychological. Selected topics analyzed and interpreted in terms of conjunctions of these dimensions.

COM 201.title: Introduction to Communication
COM 201.subject: COM
COM 201.description: An overview of communication emphasizing intercultural, organizational and international communication and media arts with introduction to multimedia, ICTs, and public relations perspectives.

COM 310.title: Media Arts
COM 310.subject: COM
COM 310.description: Combined lecture discussion on theories and criticism of visual media, covering aesthetic development and delivery through multimedia and cinematic principles.

COM 320.title: Communication and Communities
COM 320.subject: COM
COM 320.description: Combined lecture-discussion on communication within organizational communities and between organizations and their communities with attention to intercultural issues in local, global, and online interactions.

COM 325.title: Communicating Sustainability
COM 325.subject: COM
COM 325.description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.

COM 330.title: Information and Communication Technology Concepts
COM 330.subject: COM
COM 330.description: Combined lecture discussion on basic technical concepts related to ICTs embedded in sociocultural context.

COM 331.title: Techniques of Video and Digital Cinema
COM 331.subject: COM
COM 331.description: Orientation to techniques of production. Emphasis on history, language, and theory of the creative process and application to video productions and multimedia.

COM 337.title: Techniques of Multimedia
COM 337.subject: COM
COM 337.description: Combined lecture-lab providing an orientation to, and examination of, procedures and techniques of multimedia. Emphasis on new media literacy, human computer interaction, and basic design of electronic multimedia.

COM 339.title: Public Relations Writing
COM 339.subject: COM
COM 339.description: Enhance students’ professional writing skills in the contemporary public relations field and equip students with the foundations of essential techniques for persuasive communication.

COM 340.title: Intercultural Communication
COM 340.subject: COM
COM 340.description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of intercultural contexts. Focus on theory, research, and managing intercultural effectiveness.

COM 350.title: Mediated Interpersonal Communication
COM 350.subject: COM
COM 350.description: Theory and practice of interpersonal communication from a social science perspective.

COM 355.title: Digital Cultures
COM 355.subject: COM
COM 355.description: Introduction to the social, cultural, and ethical implications of information and communication technologies by studying new and emerging media including games, interactive media, and virtual worlds. COM majors or consent.

COM 392.title: Emerging Topics in Communication
COM 392.subject: COM
COM 392.description: Emerging communication topics of interest to faculty and students.

COM 401.title: Survey of Inquiry Methods in Communication
COM 401.subject: COM
COM 401.description: Exploration of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication studies and related professional work.

COM 420.title: Communication in Multicultural Organizations
COM 420.subject: COM
COM 420.description: Cultural diversity in multicultural and multinational organizations is examined regarding communication-related aspects of working life.

COM 421.title: Public Relations Strategies
COM 421.subject: COM
COM 421.description: Practice and effects of public relations. Strategic management, techniques, new communication technologies, diverse publics, ethics, and social responsibility will be emphasized.

COM 422.title: Public Relations Campaigns
COM 422.subject: COM
COM 422.description: Synthesizing and applying the principles and techniques of public relations to create comprehensive campaigns.

COM 425.title: Filming Social Change
COM 425.subject: COM
COM 425.description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
COM 425.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

COM 431.title: Studio Production
COM 431.subject: COM
COM 431.description: Studio production ranging from three-camera studio production to broadcast and magazine show formats to on-line web production. Fundamental knowledge of lighting, sound, blocking, and equipment competency.

COM 432.title: Social Media
COM 432.subject: COM
COM 432.description: Combined lecturediscussion on situated use of ICTs in various personal and institutional settings.

COM 433.title: Video Scriptwriting
COM 433.subject: COM
COM 433.description: Application of communication theory to creating and revising commercial and dramatic script material for video production.

COM 436.title: Media Effects
COM 436.subject: COM
COM 436.description: Social, political, economic, and cultural effects of broadcast media are examined to understand their impact on human behavior.
COM 436.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

COM 438.title: Telecommunication in the Pacific Hemisphere
COM 438.subject: COM
COM 438.description: Development of international telecommunication, with special emphasis on the evolution of wireless communication and the internet.

COM 444.title: Communication and Gender
COM 444.subject: COM
COM 444.description: Theories, myths, and the missing links in gendered communication. Application of established and emerging theories of gender and communication to interpersonal, organizational, intercultural, and mass communication.
COM 444.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

COM 451.title: Communication and Law
COM 451.subject: COM
COM 451.description: Role of communication in the legal process; impact of law on communication processes.
COM 451.prereq_raw: COM/JOUR major and junior standing, or consent

COM 452.title: Building Communication Theory
COM 452.subject: COM
COM 452.description: Major theories of communication in terms of requirements for a theory, theory development, associated research, and application.
COM 452.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

COM 459.title: Special Topics
COM 459.subject: COM
COM 459.description: Topics of interest to faculty and students; taught by regular and visiting faculty.
COM 459.prereq_raw: COM/JOUR major and junior standing, or consent

COM 460.title: Media Ethics
COM 460.subject: COM
COM 460.description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects.

COM 465.title: Political Communication in the Digital Era
COM 465.subject: COM
COM 465.description: An examination of how various aspects of digital media platforms, such as affordances and communication processes impact political outcomes. COM majors or consent. Sophomore standing or higher.

COM 475.title: Global Communication
COM 475.subject: COM
COM 475.description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of international contexts. Focus on commerce, diplomacy, and mass communication.

COM 476.title: Capstone in Digital Cinema Production
COM 476.subject: COM
COM 476.description: Creating, scripting, and producing complex programs. Media aesthetics and professional production, preparation, and execution are emphasized.

COM 477.title: Capstone in Interactive Multimedia Design and Development
COM 477.subject: COM
COM 477.description: Design, development, and evaluation of interactive computer-based multimedia communication. Emphasizes authoring and production of such multimedia elements as fullmotion images, audio, and graphics.

COM 478.title: Capstone in Communication in Communities
COM 478.subject: COM
COM 478.description: Synthesize knowledge, apply research findings in service to community, and develop proposal for intervention or campaign.
COM 478.prereq_raw: 310 and 320 and 330; and 340 or 421; or consent

COM 479.title: Capstone Project in ICTs and Policy
COM 479.subject: COM
COM 479.description: Focus on specific ICT and policy problems related to Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region.
COM 479.prereq_raw: 310 and 320 and 330; and 432 or 438; or consent

COM 480.title: Communication Seminar
COM 480.subject: COM
COM 480.description: Application of theoretic and methodological criteria to researchable questions. Topics will vary.

COM 489.title: Communicating Creativity
COM 489.subject: COM
COM 489.description: The role of communication in fostering or inhibiting creativity. Exploration of theoretical bases for shared scientific or artistic creativity in communication research. COM major or consent.
COM 489.prereq_raw: 201 and senior standing, or consent. (Once a year)

COM 490.title: Senior Thesis Project
COM 490.subject: COM
COM 490.description: Completion of the thesis project appropriate to the selected area of concentration within the context of a seminar. Emphasis on ongoing process of writing, editing, review, and revision.
COM 490.prereq_raw: COM major and senior standing, or consent

COM 499.title: Special Problems
COM 499.subject: COM
COM 499.description: Independent study of selected topics under faculty supervision.
COM 499.prereq_raw: COM major and junior standing, or consent

COM 611.title: Communication Theories
COM 611.subject: COM
COM 611.description: Systematic study of major theories of communication and current status of communication research.

COM 612.title: Communication Inquiry
COM 612.subject: COM
COM 612.description: Introduction to inquiry and the array of quantitative and qualitative research methods commonly used in communication.

COM 623.title: Strategic Organizational Communication
COM 623.subject: COM
COM 623.description: Theories, concepts, and applications of strategic communication and public relations to achieve organizational goals.

COM 633.title: Information and Communication Technologies
COM 633.subject: COM
COM 633.description: Information and communication technologies, structures, processes, and networks as an area of research and study in the social sciences.

COM 634.title: Social Media
COM 634.subject: COM
COM 634.description: Systematic study from a social science perspective of current and emerging social media. Attention to user needs and impact.

COM 643.title: Intercultural Communication
COM 643.subject: COM
COM 643.description: Problems and opportunities of intercultural communication from theory and research, consulting and training, and policy and program perspectives.

COM 644.title: Global Communication and Journalism
COM 644.subject: COM
COM 644.description: Analysis of the emerging global media landscape as digital technologies enable the sharing of news, information, and commentary across geographical and cultural borders. Focuses on causes, characteristics, and consequences.

COM 645.title: Digital Storytelling
COM 645.subject: COM
COM 645.description: Focus on development of narrative-based creative activities in all mediums (text, audio, video, etc.) within communication contexts, i.e., journalism, film, public relations, etc.
COM 645.prereq_raw: enrolled in the School of Communications MA program, or instructor approval

children.text: enrolled in the School of Communications MA program,

COM 646.title: Intervention in Multicultural Organizations
COM 646.subject: COM
COM 646.description: Describes the array of communication-related intervention programs designed to enhance effectiveness in multicultural organizations at home and abroad.

COM 660.title: ICT Policy and Planning
COM 660.subject: COM
COM 660.description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

COM 691.title: Communication Topics
COM 691.subject: COM
COM 691.description: Coverage in depth of some area of theory and research.

COM 692.title: Communication Research Seminar
COM 692.subject: COM
COM 692.description: General research seminar in communication. In-depth coverage of specific research methods to develop, refine, or interpret graduate students’ thesis or dissertation projects. Graduate students only.
COM 692.prereq_raw: 611 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

COM 695.title: Communication Practicum
COM 695.subject: COM
COM 695.description: Supervised work experience, study of an organization, and career planning. Required of Plan B students in the main communication program.

CUL 609.title: Faculty Seminar Series
CUL 609.subject: CUL
CUL 609.description: Seminar consists of a series of presentations by certificate faculty on topics of ongoing research. Presentations will open current debates about theory and method in cultural studies.

CUL 610.title: International Cultural Studies: History and Theory
CUL 610.subject: CUL
CUL 610.description: Seminar on the history and theory of interdisciplinary cultural studies. The politics of culture are examined in comparative perspective, focusing on their significance for identity formation, intercultural relations, and global flows of images, people and capital. Approaches to the study of media and popular culture are taken up in terms of their relevance for contemporary issues, especially in Hawai‘i and the Asia/Pacific/U.S. region.

CUL 750.title: International Cultural Studies: Research Project
CUL 750.subject: CUL
CUL 750.description: Directed reading and research culminating in a project that engages issues in international cultural studies. Types of projects include scholarly essays, community-based projects, performances or exhibitions. Written statement of purpose and selfevaluation required.

ECON 120.title: Introduction to Economics
ECON 120.subject: ECON
ECON 120.description: One semester survey of the principles of microeconomics and macroeconomics to enable students in all disciplines to understand current economic events.

ECON 130.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 130.subject: ECON
ECON 130.description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

ECON 130A.title: Principles of Microeconomics
ECON 130A.subject: ECON
ECON 130A.description: Examination of the decision-making process of both households and firms. Analysis of the functioning of a competitive market system, using supply and demand models and the role of government in cases where the market system fails. Additional topics include the effects of international rate on the welfare of a nation and the effects of different competitive market structures on society.

ECON 131.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 131.subject: ECON
ECON 131.description: An introduction to macroeconomics–the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

ECON 131A.title: Principles of Macroeconomics
ECON 131A.subject: ECON
ECON 131A.description: An introduction to macroeconomics–the study of the overall economy. Topics include the determination of national income, causes and effects of inflation, unemployment, and income inequality; causes and consequences of international differences in economic growth; sources of business cycle expansions and contractions; role of government policy in stabilizing the economy and promoting long-term growth; financial markets and monetary policy; taxes, spending, consequences of budget deficits, determination of trade imbalances, exchange rate fluctuations, and balance of payment crises.

ECON 256.title: Data Analysis and Visualization
ECON 256.subject: ECON
ECON 256.description: Develops basic techniques of data analysis and visualization. Introduces sources of economic data; methods of preparing data from various file/data formats for analysis; methods of visualization: bubble plots, scatterplot matrices, heatmaps, hexbins, rug plots, etc.

ECON 300.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
ECON 300.subject: ECON
ECON 300.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

ECON 300A.title: Intermediate Macroeconomics
ECON 300A.subject: ECON
ECON 300A.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts used to study the overall macroeconomy and policies that affect it. Study the determinants of national income and long-run growth; causes and consequences of unemployment, inflation, and business cycle fluctuations; determination of foreign exchange rates and current account imbalances, and the role of government policy in various settings.

ECON 301.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
ECON 301.subject: ECON
ECON 301.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

ECON 301A.title: Intermediate Microeconomics
ECON 301A.subject: ECON
ECON 301A.description: Develops basic techniques and fundamental concepts of microeconomic theory. Learn to use economic reasoning to understand the social consequences of decisions made by individual consumers, producers, and governments. Analyze the nature of market outcomes under alternative market structures, and further discuss possible welfare-improving government policies when markets fail to be efficient. Special attention is paid to the analysis of strategic behavior and markets with public goods and externalities.

ECON 311.title: The Economy of Hawai‘i
ECON 311.subject: ECON
ECON 311.description: History of development of Hawaiian economy; current economic problems.

ECON 317.title: The Japanese Economy
ECON 317.subject: ECON
ECON 317.description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

ECON 317A.title: The Japanese Economy
ECON 317A.subject: ECON
ECON 317A.description: Analysis of Japan’s growth past and present. Does Japan’s economy look different in terms of its international trade structure, industrial structure, labor market, savings patterns, government policies, etc.? Does it matter?

ECON 320.title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
ECON 320.subject: ECON
ECON 320.description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.

ECON 321.title: Introduction to Statistics
ECON 321.subject: ECON
ECON 321.description: Basic elements; descriptive statistics, probability, inference, distributions, hypothesis testing, regression, and correlation analysis.

ECON 332.title: Economics of Global Climate Change
ECON 332.subject: ECON
ECON 332.description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
ECON 332.prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

ECON 336.title: Energy Economics and Policy
ECON 336.subject: ECON
ECON 336.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

ECON 340.title: Financial Markets and Institutions
ECON 340.subject: ECON
ECON 340.description: The determination of asset prices; the risk and term structure of interest rates; efficient markets hypothesis; risk management and financial derivatives, asymmetric information models of financial market structure, innovation, regulation and deregulation; and financial crises.

ECON 341.title: Comparative Economic History
ECON 341.subject: ECON
ECON 341.description: Comparative historical study of economic ideas and change since around 1700. Considers the histories of capitalism, poverty, industrialization and labor in Europe, Asia, the U.S., and other regions.

ECON 342.title: The History of Economic Thought
ECON 342.subject: ECON
ECON 342.description: Introduces major western economic theorists and ideas since around 1700. Considers the history of views on work, poverty, the market and government, and the relationship of those doctrines to society, philosophy, and public policy.
ECON 342.prereq_raw: 130, 131, or HIST 151, or HIST 152; or consent

ECON 350.title: Sustainable Development
ECON 350.subject: ECON
ECON 350.description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
ECON 350.prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

ECON 355.title: Network Economics
ECON 355.subject: ECON
ECON 355.description: Fundamental questions about the connections in the social, economic, and technological worlds. Topics include: matching markets, traffic, financial and social networks; and the political and economic consequences of the internet and other large networks.

ECON 356.title: Games and Economic Behavior
ECON 356.subject: ECON
ECON 356.description: Introduces students to the study of strategic behavior with applications to economics, business, and public policy. Simple economic models of strategic decision making are used to analyze provision of public goods; competition, cooperation, and coordination among firms; bargaining between employers and labor unions; international trade negotiations; reputation as a competitive advantage, and others.

ECON 358.title: Environmental Economics
ECON 358.subject: ECON
ECON 358.description: Nature and causes of environmental degradation/economic solutions, with emphasis on relevant ethical issues and decision-making. Topics include air and water pollution, toxic waste, deforestation, soil erosion, biodiversity, global warming, and sustainable development.

ECON 361.title: Seminar: Women and International Development
ECON 361.subject: ECON
ECON 361.description: Women’s role, status, work and treatment in the Third World; economic development, changing work/family roles, and improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World; global feminization of poverty; efforts to promote gender equity. Open to non-majors.
ECON 361.prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent

ECON 362.title: Trade Policy and Globalization
ECON 362.subject: ECON
ECON 362.description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.

ECON 362A.title: Trade Policy and Globalization
ECON 362A.subject: ECON
ECON 362A.description: Political economy of the world trading system. Case studies of trade cooperation and conflict under the World Trade Organization and other institutions. Future challenges, including investment policies, environmental and labor standards.

ECON 390.title: Internship for Economics
ECON 390.subject: ECON
ECON 390.description: Economics majors and minors work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. Students combine academic work with practical experience.

ECON 391.title: Cooperative Education
ECON 391.subject: ECON
ECON 391.description: Economics majors and minors, under the supervision of faculty members, work at paid positions with public agencies, private companies, and campus organizations. The Econ Co-op integrates academics with practical work experience.

ECON 396.title: Contemporary Topics in Economics
ECON 396.subject: ECON
ECON 396.description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester.

ECON 399.title: Directed Reading
ECON 399.subject: ECON
ECON 399.description: Economics majors and minors participate in faculty supervised reading of economic literature. Enables students to self-study topics not covered in the department’s scheduled course offerings.

ECON 409.title: The Ocean Economy
ECON 409.subject: ECON
ECON 409.description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

ECON 412.title: Economic History of the United States
ECON 412.subject: ECON
ECON 412.description: U.S. economy from colonial times: government policies, institutions, industries, financial markets, economic growth, economic crises.

ECON 414.title: Global Economic Crisis and Recovery
ECON 414.subject: ECON
ECON 414.description: Causes and consequences of financial and economic crises: crisis origins and global transmission; macroeconomic and regulatory policy responses; recovery challenges.

ECON 415.title: Asian Economic Development
ECON 415.subject: ECON
ECON 415.description: History and economic development. Resources, population, and income, saving, investment, and consumption patterns. Role of government and private enterprise.

ECON 416.title: The Chinese Economy
ECON 416.subject: ECON
ECON 416.description: The Chinese economy during the imperial and republican periods, under Mao, and into the present reform era, with a brief comparison to Taiwan and Hong Kong.

ECON 418.title: Pacific Island Economies
ECON 418.subject: ECON
ECON 418.description: Historical and current economic development of the Pacific islands (excluding Hawai‘i). Analysis of selected economic issues such as tourism, population growth, etc.

ECON 420.title: Mathematical Economics
ECON 420.subject: ECON
ECON 420.description: Mathematical techniques applied to theories of the consumer, the firm, markets. Linear programming, input-output analysis.

ECON 425.title: Introduction to Econometrics
ECON 425.subject: ECON
ECON 425.description: Regression analysis, analysis of variance, hypothesis testing, problems in estimation of single equation models, simultaneous equation models, problems and methods of estimation.
ECON 425.prereq_raw: 321 or MATH 241 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or (MATH 251A and NREM 203) or (MATH 371 and MATH 373) or (MATH 471 and MATH 472); or consent

ECON 427.title: Economic Forecasting
ECON 427.subject: ECON
ECON 427.description: Forecasting methods for business and economics with applications to the U.S., Asian, and Hawai‘i economies. Topics include time series modeling of trend, seasonal, and cyclical components, multivariate regression modeling, and forecast evaluation.
ECON 427.prereq_raw: 321 or BUS 310 or NREM 310 or (MATH 251A and NREM 203) or (MATH 371 and MATH 373) or (MATH 471 and MATH 472); or consent

ECON 429.title: Spreadsheet Modeling for Business and Economic Analysis
ECON 429.subject: ECON
ECON 429.description: Introduction to quantitative decision-making methods for effective agribusiness management in resource allocation, scheduling, logistics, risk analysis, inventory, and forecasting. Emphasis on problem identification, model formulation and solution, and interpretation and presentation of results.
ECON 429.prereq_raw: 130 or NREM/SUST 220, and 321 or NREM 310; or consent. (Once a year)

ECON 430.title: Economics of Human Resources
ECON 430.subject: ECON
ECON 430.description: Economic analysis of labor market. Investment in human capital, education, health, migration, etc.

ECON 432.title: Economics of Population
ECON 432.subject: ECON
ECON 432.description: Determinants and consequences of growth and structure of human populations. Relationships between economic factors and fertility, population growth and economic growth.

ECON 434.title: Health Economics
ECON 434.subject: ECON
ECON 434.description: Private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; efficient production and utilization of services; models of hospital and physician behavior; optimal public policy.

ECON 440.title: Monetary Theory and Policy
ECON 440.subject: ECON
ECON 440.description: Micro-foundations and critical analysis of monetary and macroeconomic theory and policy. Topics include the causes and consequences of inflation, optimal monetary policy and international monetary systems, bank risk and insurance, and national debt and taxation.

ECON 442.title: Development Economics
ECON 442.subject: ECON
ECON 442.description: Theoretical foundation and empirical evidence for analyzing key issues facing today’s developing world. Topics include characteristics of underdeveloped economies, economic growth, structural change, poverty, inequality, education, population growth, foreign aid and financial sector.

ECON 450.title: Public Economics
ECON 450.subject: ECON
ECON 450.description: Welfare economics, public expenditure and policy evaluation, public finance by debt and taxes.

ECON 452.title: State and Local Finance
ECON 452.subject: ECON
ECON 452.description: Fiscal institutions, operations, and policy questions within state and local governments in U.S. grant programs and other links with central government.

ECON 458.title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
ECON 458.subject: ECON
ECON 458.description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

ECON 460.title: International Trade and Welfare
ECON 460.subject: ECON
ECON 460.description: Theory of international specialization and exchange; general equilibrium, tariffs, quotas, common markets.

ECON 461.title: International Macroeconomics
ECON 461.subject: ECON
ECON 461.description: The determination of output, price levels, exchange rates and the balance of payments for economies that are integrated with the global economy; theory and application to historical and/or contemporary policy issues.

ECON 470.title: Industrial Organization
ECON 470.subject: ECON
ECON 470.description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of contemporary topics in industrial organization. Uses economic theory to analyze important issues facing firms, and examines the practical challenges of empirical applications of theory.

ECON 476.title: Law and Economics
ECON 476.subject: ECON
ECON 476.description: Legal issues of property rights, contracts, torts, and crime. Efficiency of U.S. legal process. Economics of law enforcement, juries, prosecutors; evolution of legal rules.

ECON 495.title: Land and Housing Economics
ECON 495.subject: ECON
ECON 495.description: Microeconomics explains urban land and housing phenomena, and analyzes selected land and housing issues relevant to Honolulu.

ECON 496.title: Contemporary Economic Issues
ECON 496.subject: ECON
ECON 496.description: Economic analysis of current events. Topics announced each semester, e.g., environmental pollution, crime control, racial discrimination, traffic congestion.

ECON 499.title: Advanced Directed Research
ECON 499.subject: ECON
ECON 499.description: Economics majors and minors conduct research, under faculty supervision, on a topic of their choice.
ECON 499.prereq_raw: minimum GPA of 3.0 in economics and consent

ECON 604.title: Microeconomics and Policy Analysis
ECON 604.subject: ECON
ECON 604.description: Theory of the consumer, firm, and market. Role of governments and analysis of public policy. Applications to both industrialized and developing countries.

ECON 606.title: Microeconomic Theory I
ECON 606.subject: ECON
ECON 606.description: Theory of the firm: production, costs, duality; theory of the market: competition, monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition; theory of the consumer: preferences, expenditures, duality; expected utility theory.

ECON 607.title: Macroeconomic Theory I
ECON 607.subject: ECON
ECON 607.description: Neoclassical theory of real and monetary equilibrium, economics of J. M. Keynes, standard IS/LM models and aggregate demand/supply analysis in the closed and open economy, theory of rational expectations.

ECON 608.title: Microeconomic Theory II
ECON 608.subject: ECON
ECON 608.description: General equilibrium analysis: production, consumption and Walrasian equilibria; Pareto efficiency, fundamental theorems of welfare economics; externalities; public goods; game theory; information theory.

ECON 609.title: Macroeconomic Theory II
ECON 609.subject: ECON
ECON 609.description: Models of economic growth and fluctuations; stochastic and dynamic macroeconomic models; econometric testing of rational expectations models; theory of public debt; current topics in macroeconomic theory.

ECON 610.title: Economic Development
ECON 610.subject: ECON
ECON 610.description: Nature and causes of economic growth and structural change. Roles of macroeconomic policy and foreign trade.

ECON 611.title: Economic Development Policy
ECON 611.subject: ECON
ECON 611.description: Analysis of policies for the promotion of industrial and agricultural development. Project evaluation, industrial regulation, public administration, investment and capital market policies, land-use policies, trade policies, pricing, and stabilization.

ECON 614.title: Economic Development of Japan
ECON 614.subject: ECON
ECON 614.description: Analysis of growth from Meiji period to present. Problems of population change, capital formation, income distribution, industrial structure.

ECON 620.title: Microeconomic Theory III
ECON 620.subject: ECON
ECON 620.description: Game theory and strategic behavior. Economics of information and incentives principal-agent theory. Economic design. Applications include: theory of contracts; incentive compatible mechanism for provision of public goods; auction theory.

ECON 627.title: Mathematics for Economics
ECON 627.subject: ECON
ECON 627.description: Sets, functions, limits, convexity, continuity; constrained and unconstrained optimization; difference and differential equations; matrix algebra; simultaneous equations; comparative statics; Kuhn-Tucker theory; game theory; mathematical programming.

ECON 628.title: Econometrics I
ECON 628.subject: ECON
ECON 628.description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.

ECON 629.title: Econometrics II
ECON 629.subject: ECON
ECON 629.description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference and forecasting of econometric models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

ECON 635.title: Disasters and Economic Policy
ECON 635.subject: ECON
ECON 635.description: Economic analysis of disasters. The economics of prevention and mitigation, as well as post-disaster economic consequences and policy, will be examined. Graduate students only.

ECON 636.title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
ECON 636.subject: ECON
ECON 636.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
ECON 636.prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent

ECON 637.title: Resource Economics
ECON 637.subject: ECON
ECON 637.description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

ECON 638.title: Environmental Resource Economics
ECON 638.subject: ECON
ECON 638.description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

ECON 639.title: Marine Resource Economics
ECON 639.subject: ECON
ECON 639.description: Seminar on the economics of the marine environment. Topics include fisheries management, ocean recreation, shipping, and coral reef protection.

ECON 650.title: Foundations of Public Policy
ECON 650.subject: ECON
ECON 650.description: Microeconomic principles for expenditure and tax policies. Externalities, public goods, non-convexities, regulation; cost-benefit analysis, general equilibrium, shadow-pricing; rent-seeking, corruption; optimal taxation, incidence, excess burden; dynamic public finance, national debt, social security.

ECON 651.title: Public Economics
ECON 651.subject: ECON
ECON 651.description: Theoretical and empirical analysis of public-sector allocation. Adverse selection, moral hazard, networks, auctions, public choice and political mechanisms; tax and mandate incidence; economics of education and local public goods; social insurance programs.

ECON 660.title: International Trade and Welfare
ECON 660.subject: ECON
ECON 660.description: Classical and new theories of international trade: why nations trade, gains from trade, patterns of trade, and trade policy effects under perfect and imperfect competition. Empirical trade and other special topics.

ECON 661.title: Advanced International Trade and Investment
ECON 661.subject: ECON
ECON 661.description: Surveys theoretical and empirical research on topics such as regionalism and multilateralism, trade and wages, foreign direct investment and multinational firms, trade and the environment, and trade and economic growth.

ECON 662.title: International Macroeconomics
ECON 662.subject: ECON
ECON 662.description: Advanced international monetary and macroeconomic theory: balance of payments, output, price and exchange rate determination, international aspects of growth and economic fluctuations, alternative exchange rate regimes, international capital flows.

ECON 664.title: Applied International Finance
ECON 664.subject: ECON
ECON 664.description: Surveys empirical research in international macroeconomics, finance and econometric methods: including balance of payments adjustment, international equilibrium, international prices, interest rates and exchange rates, models of exchange rate determination, capital flows, balance of payments crises.

ECON 670.title: Labor Economics I
ECON 670.subject: ECON
ECON 670.description: Supply of and demand for labor; implications for labor markets and unemployment level.

ECON 672.title: Economics of Population
ECON 672.subject: ECON
ECON 672.description: Economic determinants and consequences of population change.

ECON 674.title: Health Economics and Policy
ECON 674.subject: ECON
ECON 674.description: Economic analysis of health-care policy; efficient design of health-care financing schemes; private and public demand for health, health insurance, and medical care; provider behavior.

ECON 686.title: Strategic Behavior and Experimental Economics
ECON 686.subject: ECON
ECON 686.description: Experimental economics: methodology. Experimental game theory. Market experiments. Applications include: topics in industrial organization, provision of public goods, asset markets, auctions.

ECON 696.title: Advanced Topics in Economics
ECON 696.subject: ECON
ECON 696.description: Reflects interests of visiting and permanent faculty, focusing on specialized methods or topics in economics.

ECON 730.title: Research Seminar
ECON 730.subject: ECON
ECON 730.description: Selected issues emphasizing research techniques. Required for students who have passed the two theory qualifying exams and have not passed the comprehensive exam.

ECON 732.title: MA Capstone Research
ECON 732.subject: ECON
ECON 732.description: Student applies theoretical and quantitative techniques, critical thinking, and communicative skills to prepare a written and oral presentation of original research on a topic of his or her choice.

ES 101.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
ES 101.subject: ES
ES 101.description: Basic concepts and theories for analyzing dynamics of ethnic group experiences, particularly those represented in Hawai‘i, and their relation to colonization, immigration, problems of identity, racism, and social class.

ES 101A.title: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
ES 101A.subject: ES
ES 101A.description: Basic concepts and theories for analyzing dynamics of ethnic group experiences, particularly those represented in Hawai‘i, and their relation to colonization, immigration, problems of identity, racism, and social class.

ES 213.title: Race, Class, Gender in Popular Culture
ES 213.subject: ES
ES 213.description: Contemporary issues of race, class, and gender in popular culture (film, television, music, social media, sports, etc.). Introduction to critical media analysis and social science theories and methods.

ES 214.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
ES 214.subject: ES
ES 214.description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

ES 221.title: Hawaiians
ES 221.subject: ES
ES 221.description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance.

ES 301.title: Ethnic Identity
ES 301.subject: ES
ES 301.description: Individual and group problems of identity, identity conflict, culture conflict, inter-ethnic relations. Critical review of available material on Hawai‘i.

ES 305.title: African American Experience I
ES 305.subject: ES
ES 305.description: Afrocentric perspective. Analysis of the black political/cultural diaspora, including ancient African kingdoms, the slavery experience, organized resistance, emancipation struggles, the Civil War and Reconstruction.

ES 306.title: African American Experience II
ES 306.subject: ES
ES 306.description: Afrocentric sociopolitical analysis. The struggle for freedom: Reconstruction period, reign of terror, intellectual and cultural awakenings, civil rights movements, contemporary issues.

ES 308.title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
ES 308.subject: ES
ES 308.description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
ES 308.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

ES 310.title: Ethnicity and Community: Hawai‘i
ES 310.subject: ES
ES 310.description: Site visits to museums, social welfare units, etc., as well as guest lecturers from the community including police, health, education.

ES 318.title: Asian America
ES 318.subject: ES
ES 318.description: History of selected Asian immigrant groups from the 19th century to the present. Topics include: immigration and labor history, Asian American movements, literature and cultural productions, community adaptations and identity formation.

ES 320.title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
ES 320.subject: ES
ES 320.description: Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

ES 330.title: Japanese in Hawai‘i
ES 330.subject: ES
ES 330.description: Issei roots in Japan; the role of Japanese in labor, politics, and business; sansei and perspectives on local identity and culture. The Japanese in light of changing economic, social, and political conditions in Hawai‘i today.

ES 331.title: Power and Place: Chinatowns
ES 331.subject: ES
ES 331.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of Chinese in Hawai‘i and the U.S. continent with a focus on Chinatowns; urbanization; economic development, community organizing; comparative racialization.

ES 333.title: Filipinos in Hawai‘i
ES 333.subject: ES
ES 333.description: Historical and contemporary experiences; immigration; traditional culture and values; plantation experience; labor organizing; development of Filipino community; racism; discrimination; and ethnic identity.

ES 338.title: American Indian Experience
ES 338.subject: ES
ES 338.description: Provides a comprehensive look at the indigenous foundation of life and society in the Americas and elaborates on historical and contemporary importance of American Indian rights issues.

ES 339.title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
ES 339.subject: ES
ES 339.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation. Pre one ES or WS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent. (Once a year)

ES 340.title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
ES 340.subject: ES
ES 340.description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

ES 345.title: The Sounds of Race and Inequality
ES 345.subject: ES
ES 345.description: Explore inequality as manifested and contested in silence, music, dialect, nature, voice, and acoustic space by listening through a matrix of race, ethnicity, gender, class, and sexualities. Combination of hands-on work and current scholarship.

ES 350.title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
ES 350.subject: ES
ES 350.description: Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

ES 360.title: Immigration to Hawai‘i and U.S.
ES 360.subject: ES
ES 360.description: Historical overview: “push and pull factors”; effect of changing economy; experiences of various ethnic groups; problems of recent immigrants; immigration policies in the U.S. and Hawai‘i.

ES 365.title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawai‘i
ES 365.subject: ES
ES 365.description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawai‘i; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
ES 365.prereq_raw: one ANTH, SOC, or WS course

ES 370.title: Literatures of Hawai‘i
ES 370.subject: ES
ES 370.description: Writings of various ethnic groups in Hawai‘i, ancient to contemporary. Songs, stories, poetry, fiction, essays that illustrate the social history of Hawai‘i.
ES 370.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

ES 372.title: Asian American Literature
ES 372.subject: ES
ES 372.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of Asian American literature by writers from a variety of backgrounds.
ES 372.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

ES 373.title: Filipino Americans: History, Culture and Politics
ES 373.subject: ES
ES 373.description: An introduction to the study of Filipino Americans in the U.S. and the diaspora. The course pays special attention to labor migration, cultural production and community politics.

ES 375.title: Issues of Diversity in Higher Education
ES 375.subject: ES
ES 375.description: Examines issues of diversity within higher education. Examines different dimensions of diversity including ethnicity, gender, national origin, age, and sexual orientation. Will utilize national and local case studies. Junior class standing or higher.

ES 380.title: Fieldwork in Ethnic Studies
ES 380.subject: ES
ES 380.description: Supervision of individual student research projects pertinent to ethnic studies, including service learning, civic engagement, internship, oral history, or supervised practicum experience in teaching select ethnic studies courses.

ES 381.title: Social Movements in Hawai‘i
ES 381.subject: ES
ES 381.description: Role of various contemporary movements for social change in Hawai‘i: community, ethnic, labor, student, etc. Theories of social movements and social change.

ES 390.title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
ES 390.subject: ES
ES 390.description: Historical and sociological studies of race and gender in U.S. society; grassroots feminist and racial/justice activism on the continent and in Hawai‘i.

ES 391.title: Oceanic Gender, Sexual, and Kinship Identities
ES 391.subject: ES
ES 391.description: Oceania-centric perspective. Analysis of imperialism, colonialism, gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, and queer(ed) relations and identities in Hawai‘i and the Pacific. Junior standing or higher.
ES 391.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

ES 392.title: Change in the Pacific—Polynesia
ES 392.subject: ES
ES 392.description: Impact of cultural and physical change and their interrelationship.

ES 395.title: Multiethnic Popular Culture: Hip Hop
ES 395.subject: ES
ES 395.description: Historical, social, cultural, and political aspects of the formation and development of Hip Hop culture in Hawai‘i and other Pacific islands. Special attention to the significance of Hip Hop in facilitating cultural interactions. Junior standing or higher.
ES 395.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

ES 400.title: Ethnic Studies in the Digital World
ES 400.subject: ES
ES 400.description: The digitally networked world mediates race and ethnicity–and vice-versa. We will challenge racism and discrimination manifested in social media, changing notions of identity and group belonging, ewaste, gaming, big data, and more.

ES 410.title: Race, Class, and the Law
ES 410.subject: ES
ES 410.description: Historical context and implications of landmark court decisions and legal issues affecting social change in ethnic communities in Hawai‘i and the continental U.S.
ES 410.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

ES 418.title: Women and Work
ES 418.subject: ES
ES 418.description: Gender and racial division of labor nationally and internationally; racial and gender differentials in wages, training, working conditions and unemployment; historical trends and future directions.
ES 418.prereq_raw: one 300-level ES or WS course, or SOC 300; or consent

ES 420.title: American Ethnic and Race Relations
ES 420.subject: ES
ES 420.description: Surveys ethnic and race relations in the U.S. Focus on historical conflicts and critical issues such as racism, immigration, affirmative action, changing economic structures, and the role of government.

ES 422.title: Mixed Race Identities, Multiracial Experiences
ES 422.subject: ES
ES 422.description: Critically examines historical and contemporary issues surrounding mixed race identities and experiences through themes that resonate in localized contexts within the continental U.S. and Oceania.
ES 422.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

ES 425.title: Filming Social Change
ES 425.subject: ES
ES 425.description: Introduction to visual documentary theory and methods. Basic instruction in using digital video technology and hands-on production to tell visual stories and examine social issues related to diverse peoples, cultures, and communities through video projects.
ES 425.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

ES 440.title: Contemporary Diasporas in Comparative Perspective
ES 440.subject: ES
ES 440.description: Compares the circumstances under which contemporary Asian, Pacific Islander, or African migrants form diasporas across the globe; focus on a particular ethnic group to examine its site-specific experiences.

ES 443.title: Filipino Americans: Research Topics
ES 443.subject: ES
ES 443.description: A research seminar on the study of Filipino Americans. Special themes in film/video/media, the performing arts, or literature may be offered.

ES 450.title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
ES 450.subject: ES
ES 450.description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher.
ES 450.prereq_raw: at least one course in WS or ES; or consent by instructor

children.text: at least one course in WS

ES 456.title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
ES 456.subject: ES
ES 456.description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i.
ES 456.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent

ES 457.title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
ES 457.subject: ES
ES 457.description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.
ES 457.prereq_raw: one of WS 151, WS 175, WS 176, or WS 202; or consent

ES 460.title: Global Ethnic Conflict
ES 460.subject: ES
ES 460.description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
ES 460.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

ES 470.title: Latinx Experience in Hawai‘i
ES 470.subject: ES
ES 470.description: Examines historical, socio-cultural, and contemporary Latinx presence; relations among Latinx, other immigrant, and Indigenous communities; causes and patterns of immigration; racism and discrimination; ethnicity and identity issues; struggles for justice.
ES 470.prereq_raw: one DH or DS course, or consent

ES 480.title: Oceanic Ethnic Studies: Theories and Methods
ES 480.subject: ES
ES 480.description: Engagement with theoretical elements and qualitative and quantitative research methods of Oceanic Ethnic Studies: theories of class, race, indignity, migrancy, diaspora and political economy; community-based and participatory research methods.
ES 480.prereq_raw: one upper division ES or SOCS course or consent

ES 486.title: Peoples of Hawai‘i
ES 486.subject: ES
ES 486.description: Critically examines the historical and contemporary experiences of various people of Hawai‘i and utilizes anthropological and ethnic studies approaches to study identity, race, ethnicity, culture, language, gender, sex, class, land, and residence.
ES 486.prereq_raw: junior standing or consent. (Once a year)

ES 492.title: Politics of Multiculturalism
ES 492.subject: ES
ES 492.description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
ES 492.prereq_raw: SOC 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent

ES 493.title: Oral History: Theory and Practice
ES 493.subject: ES
ES 493.description: Literature and methodology; project design. Students develop and execute an oral history project. Junior standing or consent.

ES 495.title: Hawai‘i’s Labor History
ES 495.subject: ES
ES 495.description: Conditions of work under varying political, social, and economic transformations in Hawai‘i; anthropological, sociological, and historic data.
ES 495.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

ES 496.title: Special Topics in Ethnic Studies
ES 496.subject: ES
ES 496.description: Selected themes in ethnic studies exploring current issues and new topics; taught by regular and visiting faculty.

GEO 101.title: The Natural Environment
GEO 101.subject: GEO
GEO 101.description: Introduction to physical geography including weather, climate, vegetation, soils, geology, and landforms. Environmental issues and natural hazards.

GEO 101L.title: The Natural Environment Lab
GEO 101L.subject: GEO
GEO 101L.description: A survey of field and laboratory methods commonly used by physical geographers.

GEO 102.title: World Regional Geography
GEO 102.subject: GEO
GEO 102.description: World’s major cultural regions; geographic aspects of contemporary economic, social, political conditions.

GEO 104.title: Digital Earth
GEO 104.subject: GEO
GEO 104.description: Cartographic representation and meaning in a digital age. Earth models, map projections, coordinate systems, scale, distance, and direction. Data types and transformations in graphic and digital representation. Manual, automated, and web-based map making and analysis.

GEO 151.title: Geography and Contemporary Society
GEO 151.subject: GEO
GEO 151.description: Elements of economic geography and resource management, population and urban geography; application to current problems of developed and underdeveloped worlds.

GEO 300.title: Introduction to Climatology
GEO 300.subject: GEO
GEO 300.description: Elements and controls of climate. World patterns of insolation, temperature, evaporation, precipitation, atmospheric circulation. Climatic classifications.
GEO 300.prereq_raw: 101 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200, or consent

GEO 302.title: Global Environmental Issues
GEO 302.subject: GEO
GEO 302.description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. (Once a year)

GEO 303.title: General Geomorphology
GEO 303.subject: GEO
GEO 303.description: Introduction to geomorphological concepts, process mechanics, and relationships between forms and processes. Emphasis on various subdisciplines of geomorphology: coastal hillslopes, fluvial, aeolean, and glacial.

GEO 305.title: Water and Society
GEO 305.subject: GEO
GEO 305.description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
GEO 305.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

GEO 309.title: Introduction to Biogeography
GEO 309.subject: GEO
GEO 309.description: Introduction to ecosystem concept; environmental adaptations for energy and nutrient transfer; characteristics, dynamics, productivity, and distribution of principal vegetation communities. Human dominance.
GEO 309.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

GEO 310.title: Introduction to Planning
GEO 310.subject: GEO
GEO 310.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning–research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.

GEO 314.title: Tropical Agrarian Systems
GEO 314.subject: GEO
GEO 314.description: Analysis of environmental potential and constraints and of spatial organization of economy and society of tropical agrarian systems. Emphasis on change through colonial and post-colonial periods.

GEO 320.title: Economic Geography
GEO 320.subject: GEO
GEO 320.description: Examines how factors of production like land, labor and capital; economic activities like consumption, trade, production, and investments; and institutions like state, markets, and corporations alter economic space.

GEO 322.title: Globalization and Environment
GEO 322.subject: GEO
GEO 322.description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change.

GEO 324.title: Geography of Global Tourism
GEO 324.subject: GEO
GEO 324.description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions.
GEO 324.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

GEO 325.title: Geography, Environment, and Society
GEO 325.subject: GEO
GEO 325.description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems.

GEO 330.title: Culture and Environment
GEO 330.subject: GEO
GEO 330.description: Introduction to cultural geography, the cultural landscape, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures.

GEO 335.title: Politics, Nations, and States
GEO 335.subject: GEO
GEO 335.description: Examines the political organization of space in the sovereign state system. Contemporary and historical analyses of boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, nations, nationalism, and territory.
GEO 335.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

GEO 340.title: Geography of North America
GEO 340.subject: GEO
GEO 340.description: Overview of the physical and cultural geography. Regions and characters. Patterns of population, natural resources, industry, agriculture, and transportation/ communication networks.

GEO 352.title: Geography of Japan
GEO 352.subject: GEO
GEO 352.description: Regional synthesis of physical and cultural features; economic, social, political geography; origins and development of cities.

GEO 353.title: Geography of China
GEO 353.subject: GEO
GEO 353.description: Topics: environmental parameters and resource base, ecological control and resource management, institutional and technological transformation of agriculture, industrial potential and industrial location, settlement patterns and rural urban symbiosis.

GEO 355.title: Geography of South Asia
GEO 355.subject: GEO
GEO 355.description: Introduction to physical and human geography of India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Himalayan kingdoms. Environmental, economic, social, cultural, and political factors in development.

GEO 356.title: Geography of Southeast Asia
GEO 356.subject: GEO
GEO 356.description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

GEO 365.title: Geography of the Pacific
GEO 365.subject: GEO
GEO 365.description: Physical character of the Pacific; cultural, political, economic geography of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia (except Hawai‘i).

GEO 366.title: Geography of Honolulu
GEO 366.subject: GEO
GEO 366.description: Development of Honolulu and O‘ahu from 1778. Evolution of function, land use, and social patterns. Contemporary planning and environmental issues arising from urban growth.

GEO 368.title: Geography of Hawai‘i
GEO 368.subject: GEO
GEO 368.description: Regional, physical, cultural geography. Detailed study of people and resources.

GEO 370.title: UAV and Aerial Photography
GEO 370.subject: GEO
GEO 370.description: Introduction to UAV (unmanned aerial vehicle systems) and the measurement, interpretation, analysis, and use of photography acquired by UAV and other aerial systems.

GEO 375.title: Introduction to Cartography and Air Photo
GEO 375.subject: GEO
GEO 375.description: Principles of cartography: compilation and measurement from aerial photographs, alternate forms of data presentation, symbolism, design, and map projection.

GEO 376.title: Map Design and Production
GEO 376.subject: GEO
GEO 376.description: (3 2-hr Lab) Compilation, design and production of maps for presentations, research, and illustration using artists and mapping software.
GEO 376.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 380.title: Statistical Methods in Geography
GEO 380.subject: GEO
GEO 380.description: Quantitative statistical methods will be explored for describing and interpreting geographic/environmental phenomena. Topics will include data display, measurement, sampling, spatial statistics, dimensional analysis, nonparametric and parametric models.

GEO 388.title: Introduction to GIS
GEO 388.subject: GEO
GEO 388.description: Design, implementation, and use. Database construction and documentation. Techniques for spatial data manipulation and display. Evaluation of existing systems. Student research projects.

GEO 399.title: Directed Reading
GEO 399.subject: GEO
GEO 399.description: Limited to senior majors with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in geography.

GEO 400.title: Vegetation and the Climate System
GEO 400.subject: GEO
GEO 400.description: Role of vegetation in the climate system; links to hydrology and biogeochemical cycling; vegetation and climate history; evolution of terrestrial ecosystems; effects of global warming.
GEO 400.prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

GEO 401.title: Climate Change
GEO 401.subject: GEO
GEO 401.description: Approaches to the study of past and future climate change.
GEO 401.prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

GEO 402.title: Agricultural Climatology
GEO 402.subject: GEO
GEO 402.description: Analyzing climatic data; relation to photosynthesis, phenological development, and crop yields. Crop-weather models as guides to improved land-use planning and agronomic practices.
GEO 402.prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 405 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

GEO 403.title: Fluvial Geomorphology
GEO 403.subject: GEO
GEO 403.description: Introduction to the single most important geomorphic agent shaping the terrestrial environment. Focus on fluvial process, fluvial dynamics, fluvial landforms, and sediment transport.

GEO 404.title: Atmospheric Pollution
GEO 404.subject: GEO
GEO 404.description: Examination of air quality problems from scientific and policy perspectives. Includes case studies that explore economic, political, technical, and legal aspects of pollution control.
GEO 404.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 405.title: Water in the Environment
GEO 405.subject: GEO
GEO 405.description: Water fluxes in the environment. Occurrence and movement of water; methods of quantification. Water balance of soil-plant system: precipitation, interception, infiltration, runoff, soil moisture, evapotranspiration, and groundwater recharge.
GEO 405.prereq_raw: 101 or 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or ATMO 101 or ATMO 200 or ATMO 302 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310, or consent

GEO 408.title: Conservation and Evolutionary Biogeography
GEO 408.subject: GEO
GEO 408.description: Theories and techniques for the analysis of spatial microevolutionary patterns, taught from an interdisciplinary perspective. Examples and readings emphasize Hawai‘i and the Pacific region.
GEO 408.prereq_raw: either 309, BIOL 265 or ZOOL 485, or consent

GEO 409.title: Cultural Biogeography
GEO 409.subject: GEO
