GEO 409.description: Coevolution of human societies and plants over the last 10,000 years. Foraging, farming and urban societies economies; spread and modification of selected plants; issues of preservation of genetic resources and traditional plant knowledge. The form and function of gardens.
GEO 409.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 410.title: Human Role in Environmental Change
GEO 410.subject: GEO
GEO 410.description: Human impacts through time on vegetation, animals, landforms, soils, climate, and atmosphere. Special reference to Asian/Pacific region. Implications of long-term environmental change for human habitability.
GEO 410.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B, one of 101, BIOL 101, BIOL 123 and either 322 or BIOL 310; or consent

GEO 411.title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
GEO 411.subject: GEO
GEO 411.description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
GEO 411.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 412.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
GEO 412.subject: GEO
GEO 412.description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
GEO 412.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 413.title: Resource Management
GEO 413.subject: GEO
GEO 413.description: Management of land, water resources, coastal fisheries, forests and agriculture. Focus on problems facing Hawai‘i and the Pacific.

GEO 414.title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
GEO 414.subject: GEO
GEO 414.description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters.

GEO 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
GEO 415.subject: GEO
GEO 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

GEO 421.title: Urban Geography
GEO 421.subject: GEO
GEO 421.description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.

GEO 422.title: Agriculture, Food and Society
GEO 422.subject: GEO
GEO 422.description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to non-majors.
GEO 422.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 423.title: Marine Policy
GEO 423.subject: GEO
GEO 423.description: Introduction to the law and policies concerning the marine environment, commerce and security. Role of science, law and politics in historical and current policies for maritime trades, navigation safety, marine resources, and marine exploration.
GEO 423.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 424.title: Regional Analysis
GEO 424.subject: GEO
GEO 424.description: Spatial dynamics and environmental implications of urban and rural development. Concepts of regions, process of regional development, patterns of spatial interaction, and theoretical bases for development strategies; emphasis on Hawai‘i.
GEO 424.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 425.title: Geographies of Popular Culture
GEO 425.subject: GEO
GEO 425.description: Examines contemporary geographical debates related to concepts of discourse, identity, space/place, power, representation, and popular culture. Considers various landscapes of popular culture and how popular culture mediate a sense of place, geopolitics, and identity formation.
GEO 425.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 426.title: Environment, Resources and Society
GEO 426.subject: GEO
GEO 426.description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

GEO 432.title: Tea and Culture
GEO 432.subject: GEO
GEO 432.description: Examines cultural practices of tea in different parts of the world, focusing on history and culture of tea in China, Japan, and England. Also includes changing technologies and economies of tea worldwide.

GEO 435.title: Political Geography of Oceans
GEO 435.subject: GEO
GEO 435.description: The geopolitics of the oceans and the law of the sea as applied to regions of conflict and cooperation in marine resource development and preservation. Focus on Indo-West Pacific, South China Sea, Arctic Ocean.
GEO 435.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 436.title: Geography of Peace and War
GEO 436.subject: GEO
GEO 436.description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
GEO 436.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

GEO 453.title: Environment and Society in China
GEO 453.subject: GEO
GEO 453.description: Explores the relationship between environment and society in the Chinese society, including both traditional nature-culture connections and modern human-environmental issues. Examines China’s long-range cultural change, environmental transformations, and modern development challenges.

GEO 468.title: Topics in Geography
GEO 468.subject: GEO
GEO 468.description: Selected topics in geography not offered in the regular geography curriculum.

GEO 470.title: Remote Sensing
GEO 470.subject: GEO
GEO 470.description: Introduction to the principles of remote sensing and image processing skills. Topics include electromagnetic spectrum, sensors, aerial photo and satellite imagery interpretation, geometric and radiometric correction, digital image processing. Research project, lab.

GEO 471.title: 3D Mapping and Analysis
GEO 471.subject: GEO
GEO 471.description: Environmental mapping and analysis using 3-dimensional geographical data acquired from high resolution remote sensing systems.

GEO 472.title: Field Mapping
GEO 472.subject: GEO
GEO 472.description: Techniques for field measurement and recording of cultural and physical data. Field sketching, Brunton surveying, plane table mapping, oblique photo compilation, topographic mapping, and representation of field data.
GEO 472.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

GEO 476.title: Web Mapping
GEO 476.subject: GEO
GEO 476.description: (3 2-hr Lab) Introduction to interactive web mapping techniques for sharing and visualizing various forms of geospatial data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

GEO 487.title: GIS and Spatial Analysis for Social Sciences
GEO 487.subject: GEO
GEO 487.description: Introduction to spacial analysis and GIS for social science studies, using open-source GIS tools to collect, visualize, and analyze social data; public health, socio-economic and social media data. Requires basic knowledge about GIS.

GEO 489.title: GIS for Environmental Sciences
GEO 489.subject: GEO
GEO 489.description: Applications of GIS technologies to solve real-world problems in natural and environmental sciences. Research project, lab.

GEO 490.title: Senior Thesis
GEO 490.subject: GEO
GEO 490.description: Preparation of research paper under individual faculty supervision. Recommended for admission to graduate program.

GEO 492.title: Practicum in Geography
GEO 492.subject: GEO
GEO 492.description: Internship in applied geography under professional and faculty supervision. Field placement integrated with academic study.

GEO 493.title: Capstone Undergraduate Seminar
GEO 493.subject: GEO
GEO 493.description: Current and historical geographic literature provides a background for local and global issues. Through discussion, written reviews, and research reports, the geographic perspective in modern life will be explored.

GEO 499.title: Directed Research
GEO 499.subject: GEO
GEO 499.description: Geography majors conduct research under faculty supervision on a topic of their choice. Minimum GPA of 3.0 and consent. Senior standing only.

GEO 600.title: Seminar in Climatology
GEO 600.subject: GEO
GEO 600.description: Methods of determining energy budget and water balance; applications in agriculture, hydrology, climatic classifications. Theory of climatic change. Bibliography.
GEO 600.prereq_raw: 300 or 400 or 401 or 402 or 405 or ATMO 303 or ATMO 310 or ATMO 320; or consent

GEO 610.title: Cultural Geographies of Tourism
GEO 610.subject: GEO
GEO 610.description: Social and cultural analysis of tourism practices, with emphasis on Hawai‘i, Asia and the Pacific. Tourism in relation to consumer culture, transnational flows of people and images, post-colonial politics, performance and identity formation.

GEO 618.title: Human Environment Systems
GEO 618.subject: GEO
GEO 618.description: Role and potential of systems science in analysis of human environment interaction, especially resource management. Framework and methodology for problem structuring; overview of techniques.
GEO 618.prereq_raw: graduate standing or advanced undergraduate standing with consent

GEO 620.title: Theories and Policies of Development
GEO 620.subject: GEO
GEO 620.description: Will critically examine what constitutes progress, advancement, or betterment in this highly uneven world, where inter-regional, inter-class, inter-group, and inter-gender differences in development are expanding. Graduate standing only.

GEO 621.title: Human Geographies of the Ocean
GEO 621.subject: GEO
GEO 621.description: Core course in the ocean studies specialization in human geography introduces graduate students to themes and methods of human geography and cognate fields as applied to the oceans.

GEO 622.title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
GEO 622.subject: GEO
GEO 622.description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

GEO 630.title: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia
GEO 630.subject: GEO
GEO 630.description: Key issues and policies in urban planning, rural-urban relations, rural regional planning, and frontier settlement in Asia and the Pacific.

GEO 633.title: Seafood in Southeast Asia
GEO 633.subject: GEO
GEO 633.description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood.

GEO 637.title: Environment and Development
GEO 637.subject: GEO
GEO 637.description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

GEO 638.title: Asian Development and Urbanization
GEO 638.subject: GEO
GEO 638.description: Theories of globalization and sustainability in development, impacts of globalization and sustainability on development planning and policy formation, selected case studies of Asia-Pacific development.
GEO 638.prereq_raw: (ASAN 600 or PLAN 630) with a grade of B or above

GEO 639.title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
GEO 639.subject: GEO
GEO 639.description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.

GEO 652.title: Contemporary Japan Seminar
GEO 652.subject: GEO
GEO 652.description: Selected physical and human features that represent economic, social, and political life of modern Japan.

GEO 654.title: Seminar in Geography of Southeast Asia
GEO 654.subject: GEO

GEO 665.title: Seminar in Geography of the Pacific
GEO 665.subject: GEO
GEO 665.description: Investigation of geographic problems of Melanesia, Micronesia, Polynesia.

GEO 680.title: Geospatial Analysis of Natural Resource Data
GEO 680.subject: GEO
GEO 680.description: The application of geostatistics to estimate spatial dependence to improve soil and regional sampling; provide insight into underlying soil, geographic, and geologic process, and to provide quantitative scaling up of point measurements to fields, regions, and watersheds. State-space modeling also will be included.

GEO 692.title: Faculty Seminar Series
GEO 692.subject: GEO
GEO 692.description: Graduate seminar required of all department MA students and PhD students. Single credit course in which faculty present ongoing research in their fields.

GEO 693.title: Technology and Natural Risks Methods of Analysis
GEO 693.subject: GEO
GEO 693.description: Survey of tools for evaluating risks to human health from technological and natural hazards. Historical and international context of methods.

GEO 695.title: Concepts and Theories in Geography
GEO 695.subject: GEO
GEO 695.description: Concepts, theory, models. Geographic approaches to spatial and environmental problems. Required of entering graduate students unless waived by department.

GEO 696.title: Research Design/Methods in Geography
GEO 696.subject: GEO
GEO 696.description: Elements of research design, practical field experience, exposure to research and ideologies, broad exposure to heritage and ethos of the discipline.

GEO 703.title: Geomorphology
GEO 703.subject: GEO
GEO 703.description: Current understanding of geomorphological concepts, processes, and the dynamic relationship between human landscape modification and system response.

GEO 720.title: Critical Resource Geography
GEO 720.subject: GEO
GEO 720.description: Graduate seminar to provide geography students a roadmap through the important literature and research on political economic theories of population, natural, and critical resources. Graduate standing only.

GEO 728.title: Seminar: Resource Management in Asia-Pacific
GEO 728.subject: GEO
GEO 728.description: Examination of resource management problems in Asia and the Pacific. Problems of resource use—agriculture, forestry, energy, minerals, ocean, air quality.

GEO 735.title: Seminar: Political Geography
GEO 735.subject: GEO
GEO 735.description: Topics vary; may include borders, boundaries, geopolitics, homelands, identity politics, nations and nationalism, social categorization, the sovereign state system, territoriality.
GEO 735.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Once a year)

GEO 736.title: Environmentalism and War in the Pacific
GEO 736.subject: GEO
GEO 736.description: Two forces shape the Pacific: Imperial geopolitical efforts and indigenous environmental knowledge and practices. Analyzes how the ongoing history of war and environmental struggles make and remake the region and the world.

GEO 766.title: Society and Space
GEO 766.subject: GEO
GEO 766.description: Advanced seminar on social production of space. Topics include spatial metaphor in social theory; western spatiality from the renaissance through the enlightenment, modernity and post modernity; and geography of the body, home, landscape, and nation.

JOUR 150.title: Journalism and Society
JOUR 150.subject: JOUR
JOUR 150.description: News literacy, and the role of journalism in society–its influence, rights and responsibilities; issues and trends.

JOUR 200.title: Introduction to Multimedia Journalism
JOUR 200.subject: JOUR
JOUR 200.description: Fundamentals of multimedia reporting: finding and developing story ideas, photojournalism, audio storytelling, design, infographics, and cross-platform digital convergence.

JOUR 250.title: Media Writing
JOUR 250.subject: JOUR
JOUR 250.description: Fundamentals of writing for various news media and public relations; ethics.

JOUR 300.title: Reporting
JOUR 300.subject: JOUR
JOUR 300.description: Theory and practice of information gathering using a variety of primary and secondary sources, finding information online, use of databases and interviews for news stories, with emphasis on writing. JOUR majors only, or consent.

JOUR 307.title: Photojournalism
JOUR 307.subject: JOUR
JOUR 307.description: Production, selection, and use of digital photographs for publications. Storytelling action and feature photography with digital cameras, worked up through Adobe Photoshop and InDesign programs. Students must have a digital camera.

JOUR 316.title: Advanced Editing
JOUR 316.subject: JOUR
JOUR 316.description: Intensive training in editing, planning, and organizing stories and visual elements for publication; news judgment; managing projects. JOUR majors only, or consent.

JOUR 320.title: Visual Journalism: Multimedia
JOUR 320.subject: JOUR
JOUR 320.description: Fundamentals of visual journalism; visual theory, principles, and tools to create multimedia journalism projects for online, emerging media, and print platforms. JOUR majors only, or consent.

JOUR 325.title: Magazine Writing
JOUR 325.subject: JOUR
JOUR 325.description: Writing nonfiction articles for magazines, newspapers, and newsletters; preparing material for specific audience; marketing articles.

JOUR 327.title: Interpretive Journalism
JOUR 327.subject: JOUR
JOUR 327.description: Writing articles of news analysis, editorials, and critical reviews.

JOUR 330.title: Video Journalism
JOUR 330.subject: JOUR
JOUR 330.description: Fundamentals of video journalism using digital video cameras for writing, reporting, editing, and producing news stories. JOUR majors only, or consent.

JOUR 360.title: Journalism History and Trends
JOUR 360.subject: JOUR
JOUR 360.description: Development of the news media and trends that may affect the future of journalism.

JOUR 365.title: Communication and Law
JOUR 365.subject: JOUR
JOUR 365.description: Role of communication in the legal process; impact of law on communication processes.
JOUR 365.prereq_raw: COM/JOUR major and junior standing, or consent

JOUR 385.title: Practicum
JOUR 385.subject: JOUR
JOUR 385.description: Working on campus student or quasi-professional publications under professional and faculty supervision.

JOUR 407.title: Advanced Photojournalism
JOUR 407.subject: JOUR
JOUR 407.description: Computer experience in the creation, manipulation, and editing of color news, feature, sports, and documentary images. Study of the ethical and legal dimensions of electronic imaging.

JOUR 425.title: Publication Layout and Design
JOUR 425.subject: JOUR
JOUR 425.description: Visual display concepts and procedures for newsletters, brochures, newspapers, magazines.

JOUR 459.title: Special Topics
JOUR 459.subject: JOUR
JOUR 459.description: Topics of interest to faculty and students; taught by regular and visiting faculty.
JOUR 459.prereq_raw: COM/JOUR major and junior standing, or consent

JOUR 460.title: Media Ethics
JOUR 460.subject: JOUR
JOUR 460.description: Ethics and social responsibility for media professionals. Application of ethical theories and principles to case studies and research projects.

JOUR 470.title: Broadcast Projects/Production
JOUR 470.subject: JOUR
JOUR 470.description: Applied, problem-based application of skills and knowledge of visual story telling to the production of broadcast newscasts. Junior standing or higher.
JOUR 470.prereq_raw: 250, 300, 330; and ICS 101 or ICS 110 or ICS 111 or LTEC 112

JOUR 471.title: Advanced Multimedia Journalism
JOUR 471.subject: JOUR
JOUR 471.description: Advanced fundamentals of multimedia reporting, including finding and developing journalistic story ideas, photojournalism, audio storytelling, design, infographics, and cross-platform digital convergence. Junior standing or higher.
JOUR 471.prereq_raw: 250, 300, 330; and ICS 101 or ICS 110 or ICS 111 or LTEC 112

JOUR 475.title: Global Communication
JOUR 475.subject: JOUR
JOUR 475.description: Problems and opportunities of communication in a variety of international contexts. Focus on commerce, diplomacy, and mass communication.

JOUR 480.title: Advanced Broadcast News
JOUR 480.subject: JOUR
JOUR 480.description: Intensive experience in field and studio production of television news programs; preparation of form and content; theory, practice and ethical dimensions of planning and producing broadcast news materials. Junior standing or higher.

JOUR 481.title: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in Journalism
JOUR 481.subject: JOUR
JOUR 481.description: Exploration of the leading edge of the journalistic ideology today as well as a projection of future forms, styles, and strategies. Junior standing or higher.

JOUR 485.title: Internship
JOUR 485.subject: JOUR
JOUR 485.description: Internship in media or PR operations under professional and faculty supervision.

JOUR 499.title: Directed Research
JOUR 499.subject: JOUR
JOUR 499.prereq_raw: senior standing and consent of department chair

PACE 247.title: Survey of Conflict Management
PACE 247.subject: PACE
PACE 247.description: Survey of contemporary conflict management and resolution: negotiation, mediation, conciliation, ombuds, fact-finding, facilitation techniques, arbitration, and litigation.
PACE 247.prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent

PACE 310.title: Survey Peace and Conflict Studies
PACE 310.subject: PACE
PACE 310.description: Survey of basic concepts, relationships, methods, and debates in modern peace research and conflict resolution studies.
PACE 310.prereq_raw: any social science 100- or 200-level course or consent

PACE 315.title: Personal Peace: Stories of Hope
PACE 315.subject: PACE
PACE 315.description: Interviewing, writing, and publishing stories of those who have overcome great difficulties to find personal peace.
PACE 315.prereq_raw: grade of B or better in ENG 100 or consent

children.text: grade of B or better in ENG 100

PACE 345.title: Aggression, War, and Peace
PACE 345.subject: PACE
PACE 345.description: Biocultural, evolutionary, and cross-cultural perspectives on the conditions, patterns, and processes of violence, war, nonviolence, and peace.

PACE 373.title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
PACE 373.subject: PACE
PACE 373.description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics.
PACE 373.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course; or consent

PACE 387.title: The Meaning of War
PACE 387.subject: PACE
PACE 387.description: Exploration of ethical questions related to the many facets of war–e.g., patriotism, tribalism, holy war, self-sacrifice, cowardice, media coverage, propaganda, torture, genocide, pillage, suicide tactics, battlefield immunity.

PACE 399.title: Directed Reading
PACE 399.subject: PACE
PACE 399.description: Directed reading in peace and conflict resolution.

PACE 407.title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawai‘i
PACE 407.subject: PACE
PACE 407.description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

PACE 410.title: History of Peace Movements
PACE 410.subject: PACE
PACE 410.description: Examination of two centuries of U.S., European, Australian, and Hawaiian peace, thought, and action. Also surveys early Christian and secular attitudes to war. Open to nonmajors.

PACE 412.title: Gandhi, King, and Nonviolence
PACE 412.subject: PACE
PACE 412.description: Life and thought of Mahatma Gandhi and Martin Luther King, Jr.
PACE 412.prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

PACE 413.title: Terrorism
PACE 413.subject: PACE
PACE 413.description: Multidisciplinary approach to the origins, dynamics, and consequences of international terrorism, including the psychological, legal, ethical and operational concerns of counterterrorism.

PACE 420.title: Introduction to Human Rights: International and Comparative Perspectives
PACE 420.subject: PACE
PACE 420.description: Introduction to international, regional, and domestic human rights law; comparative perspectives on the theoretical origins of human rights and policy debates on the protection of human rights, dispute resolution, and enforcement mechanisms.
PACE 420.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level social sciences course, or consent

children.text: level social sciences course, or consent

PACE 429.title: Negotiation
PACE 429.subject: PACE
PACE 429.description: Negotiation theory, negotiation skills and application of negotiation in conflict prevention, conflict management and conflict resolution.
PACE 429.prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

PACE 430.title: Leadership for Social Change
PACE 430.subject: PACE
PACE 430.description: In-depth study of current models and emerging theories of ethical leadership in community service; development of tangible leadership skills, including communication, conflict resolution, team-building, and management skills. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 436.title: Geography of Peace and War
PACE 436.subject: PACE
PACE 436.description: Geographical factors underlying conflict in the world.
PACE 436.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

PACE 447.title: Introduction to Mediation
PACE 447.subject: PACE
PACE 447.description: Learn the core components of the mediation process and the tools for empowering mediation participants to reach customized resolutions. Emphasis on learning and applying the skills through exercises and mock mediation sessions.

PACE 450.title: Protest Under Occupation
PACE 450.subject: PACE
PACE 450.description: Explore nonviolent protests when one Independent State controls the territory of another Independent State (or international organization, such as the United Nations), without the transfer of sovereign title. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 460.title: Indigenous Nonviolent Action in the Asia-Pacific
PACE 460.subject: PACE
PACE 460.description: Study of nonviolent methods (i.e., United Nations structures, international law, boycotts, and peaceful protest) used to gain political goals and examines their successes, failures, and the prospects for those that remain ongoing. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 468.title: Introduction to Facilitating Organizational Change
PACE 468.subject: PACE
PACE 468.description: Explores the characteristics of organizations from different perspectives including structural, political, ethical, and cultural frames from organizational theory and practice. Focuses on how to design organizational change strategies and facilitate their implementation. Sophomore standing or higher.
PACE 468.prereq_raw: any 200-level DS course (with a minimum grade of C+)

children.text: any 200 -level DS course ( with a minimum grade of C+

PACE 470.title: Advocating for Children: Rights and Welfare
PACE 470.subject: PACE
PACE 470.description: Multi-disciplinary advocacy for children’s rights and welfare in various social and political systems; the role of families, justice, economics, media, race, culture, environment on policy-making for children. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 477.title: Culture and Conflict Resolution
PACE 477.subject: PACE
PACE 477.description: Conflict resolution techniques for major world culture. Emphasis on cultures of the Pacific Basin, Pacific Islands, and Asia.

PACE 478.title: International Law and Disputes
PACE 478.subject: PACE
PACE 478.description: Management, prevention, resolution of international disputes and the role of international law.
PACE 478.prereq_raw: any Social Science 100 or 200 level course, or consent

PACE 480.title: Managing Human Conflict
PACE 480.subject: PACE
PACE 480.description: Introduction into the field of conflict analysis and resolution through the examination of theory and role-play. Major theories of conflict studies are considered and the forms of conflict resolution, such as negotiation, mediation, and arbitration. Sophomore standing or higher.

PACE 485.title: Topics in Peace and Conflict Resolution
PACE 485.subject: PACE
PACE 485.description: Recent issues, practices in peace and conflict resolution.

PACE 489.title: Hiroshima & Peace
PACE 489.subject: PACE
PACE 489.description: 10-day intensive course at Hiroshima City University, Japan, in the 2-weeks before the annual August 6 commemoration of the atomic bombing. Home-stay with Japanese family. Sophomore standing.
PACE 489.prereq_raw: any 200 level social science course, or consent

PACE 495.title: Practicum and Internship
PACE 495.subject: PACE
PACE 495.description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
PACE 495.prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent

PACE 621.title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
PACE 621.subject: PACE
PACE 621.description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict. Graduate students only.

PACE 629.title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
PACE 629.subject: PACE
PACE 629.description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills. Graduate standing only.
PACE 629.prereq_raw: one of the following courses: 429, 447, 477, 647, 652, or 668; or PLAN 627; or COMG 455 or SOC 730; or LAW 508; or MGT 660

PACE 637.title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
PACE 637.subject: PACE
PACE 637.description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

PACE 640.title: Seminar: Social Studies
PACE 640.subject: PACE
PACE 640.description: Study in trends, research, and problems of implementation in teaching field.

PACE 647.title: Mediation: Theory and Practice
PACE 647.subject: PACE
PACE 647.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and mediation simulations. Theory of ADR field. Theory of major different models of mediation, both in the U.S. and internationally. Application of mediation process to categories of disputes, family, workplace, and international.
PACE 647.prereq_raw: graduate standing, or departmental approval. (Once a year)

PACE 650.title: Dispute Resolution System Design
PACE 650.subject: PACE
PACE 650.description: Conflict prevention, management and resolution in the workplace. Design and implementation of effective systems integrating ADR and recent advances in dispute resolution methodology to government, health, nonprofit, educational, private sector and other institutions.

PACE 652.title: Conflict Management for Educators
PACE 652.subject: PACE
PACE 652.description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes.

PACE 660.title: Family Mediation
PACE 660.subject: PACE
PACE 660.description: Theory and skills for practicing divorce and custody mediation. Negotiation and conflict intervention skills used by social workers, lawyers, and other intervenors in family conflict. Focus on Hawai‘i’s divorce and custody laws and practices. Graduate students only.

PACE 668.title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
PACE 668.subject: PACE
PACE 668.description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
PACE 668.prereq_raw: graduate standing, or departmental approval. (Once a year)

PACE 690.title: Topics: Conflict Theory
PACE 690.subject: PACE
PACE 690.description: Recent issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory.

PACE 695.title: Conflict Resolution Practicum
PACE 695.subject: PACE
PACE 695.description: Practice in conflict resolution skills. Open to candidates for Certificate in Conflict Resolution.

PACE 790.title: Advanced Topics: Conflict Theory
PACE 790.subject: PACE
PACE 790.description: Advanced seminar covering issues of policy and practice in peace and conflict management theory. Graduate standing only.

PLAN 101.title: Sustainable Cities
PLAN 101.subject: PLAN
PLAN 101.description: How do we plan and design cities to meet our long-term economic and environmental needs? Students will learn how sustainability applies to key urban issues like energy, transportation, land, and food.

PLAN 301.title: Survey of Urban Sociology
PLAN 301.subject: PLAN
PLAN 301.description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawai‘i.
PLAN 301.prereq_raw: SOC 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent

PLAN 310.title: Introduction to Planning
PLAN 310.subject: PLAN
PLAN 310.description: Perspectives on planning; planning tools and methods; specific Hawai‘i planning–research problems from a multidisciplinary approach.

PLAN 399.title: Directed Reading in Planning
PLAN 399.subject: PLAN
PLAN 399.description: Independent research on topics in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 412.title: Environmental Impact Assessment
PLAN 412.subject: PLAN
PLAN 412.description: Introduction to analytical methods for identifying, measuring, and quantifying the impacts of changes or interventions in resource, human-environment, and other geographic systems.
PLAN 412.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

PLAN 414.title: Environmental Hazards and Community Resilience
PLAN 414.subject: PLAN
PLAN 414.description: Investigation of the forces behind natural and technological hazards, and human actions that reduce or increase vulnerability to natural disasters.

PLAN 421.title: Urban Geography
PLAN 421.subject: PLAN
PLAN 421.description: Origins, functions, and internal structure of cities. Problems of urban settlement, growth, decay, adaptation, and planning in different cultural and historical settings. Dynamics of urban land use and role of policies and perceptions in shaping towns and cities.
PLAN 421.prereq_raw: GEO 102 or GEO 151 or GEO 330, or consent

PLAN 438.title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
PLAN 438.subject: PLAN
PLAN 438.description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.
PLAN 438.prereq_raw: 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent

PLAN 442.title: Principles of Environmental Management Systems
PLAN 442.subject: PLAN
PLAN 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

PLAN 449.title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
PLAN 449.subject: PLAN
PLAN 449.description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
PLAN 449.prereq_raw: 310 or ASAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent

PLAN 473.title: GIS for Community Planning
PLAN 473.subject: PLAN
PLAN 473.description: Exploration of geographic information systems (GIS) area analysis techniques for spatial information management in community planning. Students will learn the basic concepts and principles, and practical skills of GIS through lectures, discussions, and labs.

PLAN 495.title: Housing, Land, and Community
PLAN 495.subject: PLAN
PLAN 495.description: Analyzes availability for housing, particularly affordable housing, and its relationship to use of land and building of community. Examines public policies impacting housing, land use, and community development and ways they can be improved.

PLAN 600.title: Public Policy and Planning Theory
PLAN 600.subject: PLAN
PLAN 600.description: Designed to a) impart a historic and comparative perspective on the evolution of urban and regional planning in public policy; b) explore the spatial and built environment dimensions of society, planning and policy; c) assess the justifications for planning and differing processes of planning in the U.S. and AsiaPacific with a focus on the role of the planner in policy formulation and implementation. Graduate students only or with permission.

PLAN 601.title: Planning Methods
PLAN 601.subject: PLAN
PLAN 601.description: Introduction of the basic methods in planning, including problem definition, research design, hypothesis testing, statistical reasoning, forecasting and fundamental data analysis techniques required by the planning program and the planning profession.
PLAN 601.prereq_raw: one of ECON 321, GEO 380, or SOC 476

PLAN 602.title: Advanced Planning Theory
PLAN 602.subject: PLAN
PLAN 602.description: Advanced planning theory for PhD students (others by petition) to prepare for careers in planning education and/or high level professional practice. Covers key contemporary planning policy issues and themes from the perspective of values, explanations of the real world, policy alternatives and implementation. Students must have passed 600 or equivalent (by petition) with a B or better. PhD students only or by consent.

PLAN 603.title: Urban Economics
PLAN 603.subject: PLAN
PLAN 603.description: Reviews and builds skills in applying basic theories and principles of urban and regional economics in contemporary U.S., Hawai‘i and Asia-Pacific.

PLAN 604.title: Qualitative Methods in Planning
PLAN 604.subject: PLAN
PLAN 604.description: Provides a general introduction to qualitative research methods for planning and planning research. Includes data collection methods (focus groups, interviews, ethnography, participant observation, and participatory action research) and various analytic methods and approaches. Graduate standing only.

PLAN 605.title: Planning Models
PLAN 605.subject: PLAN
PLAN 605.description: Allocation, decision, derivation, and forecasting models used in the analysis of demographic, economic, land use, and transportation phenomena in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 606.title: Comparative Planning Histories
PLAN 606.subject: PLAN
PLAN 606.description: Provides students with an overview of the history of urban and regional planning in the U.S., Europe, and Asia, and the role that planning has played in shaping contemporary urban settlements. Graduate standing only.

PLAN 607.title: Introduction to Public Policy
PLAN 607.subject: PLAN
PLAN 607.description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation.

PLAN 608.title: Politics and Development: China
PLAN 608.subject: PLAN
PLAN 608.description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

PLAN 610.title: Community Planning and Social Policy
PLAN 610.subject: PLAN
PLAN 610.description: Social issues and conditions; consequences of social policies experienced by different groups; community social plans and programs organized by various kinds of agencies and organizations.

PLAN 615.title: Housing
PLAN 615.subject: PLAN
PLAN 615.description: Housing delivery systems as an aspect of urban and regional planning.

PLAN 616.title: Community-Based Planning
PLAN 616.subject: PLAN
PLAN 616.description: Planning and programmatic aspects of community-based development projects. East-West and local planning perspectives on participatory development and intentional communities.

PLAN 618.title: Community Economic Development
PLAN 618.subject: PLAN
PLAN 618.description: Community-based economic development approaches and methods explored with an emphasis on low income communities.

PLAN 619.title: Multiculturalism in Planning and Policy
PLAN 619.subject: PLAN
PLAN 619.description: Graduate seminar focuses on issues of governance, policy and planning in diverse multicultural societies. Differences in backgrounds, languages, privilege, preferences and values are often expressed in planning and policy controversies such as affirmative action and land use planning. Will examine these controversies and explore theories of governance in a multicultural setting.

PLAN 620.title: Environmental Planning and Policy
PLAN 620.subject: PLAN
PLAN 620.description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

PLAN 621.title: Environmental Conflict Resolution
PLAN 621.subject: PLAN
PLAN 621.description: Explore how environmental conflicts emerge and the efforts to find common ground for resolution. Examine the issues, debates, and theoretical aspects that help to explain and frame environmental conflict. Graduate students only.

PLAN 622.title: Advanced Environmental Impact Assessment
PLAN 622.subject: PLAN
PLAN 622.description: Theory and practice of environmental impact assessment. Policy and planning frameworks supporting environmental assessment in the U.S. and abroad. Cumulative environmental effects and strategic environmental assessment.

PLAN 624.title: Environmental Valuation and Policy
PLAN 624.subject: PLAN
PLAN 624.description: Build valuation skills to assess best use, conservation, and policies relating to environmental amenities. Provides an overview of policy solutions to environmental degradation used by planners.

PLAN 625.title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
PLAN 625.subject: PLAN
PLAN 625.description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via videoconferencing.

PLAN 626.title: Topics in Resource Management
PLAN 626.subject: PLAN
PLAN 626.description: for different resource systems including land, water, energy, coastal resources, forests and fisheries. Course focus varies from year to year.

PLAN 627.title: Negotiation and Mediation in Planning
PLAN 627.subject: PLAN
PLAN 627.description: Applicability and limitations of selected approaches; role of planners; impact on planning.

PLAN 628.title: Urban Environmental Problems
PLAN 628.subject: PLAN
PLAN 628.description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

PLAN 629.title: Negotiation & Conflict Resolution
PLAN 629.subject: PLAN
PLAN 629.description: Negotiation as a foundational skill of conflict resolution; mastery of negotiation skills for strategic dispute resolution; non-routine problem-solving, creating partnerships and alliances; crafting optimal agreements. Students participate in simulations and acquire vital leadership skills. Graduate standing only.
PLAN 629.prereq_raw: one of the following courses: 627; or PACE 429, PACE 447, PACE 477, PACE 647, PACE 652, or PACE 668; or COMG 455 or SOC 730; or LAW 508; or MGT 660

PLAN 630.title: Urban and Regional Planning in Asia
PLAN 630.subject: PLAN
PLAN 630.description: Key issues and policies in urban planning, rural-urban relations, rural regional planning, and frontier settlement in Asia and the Pacific.

PLAN 632.title: Planning in Hawai‘i and Pacific Islands
PLAN 632.subject: PLAN
PLAN 632.description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawai‘i, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

PLAN 633.title: Globalization and Urban Policy
PLAN 633.subject: PLAN
PLAN 633.description: Urbanization and urban policies in the Asia and Pacific region with focus on the international dimension of national and local spatial restructuring.

PLAN 634.title: Shelter and Services in Asia
PLAN 634.subject: PLAN
PLAN 634.description: Examines government and non-government organizations’ responses to urban and rural shelter issues and services in Asia.

PLAN 636.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
PLAN 636.subject: PLAN
PLAN 636.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

PLAN 637.title: Environment and Development
PLAN 637.subject: PLAN
PLAN 637.description: Theories and practice of development; how changing development paradigms shape different ideas concerning the environment and the management of natural resources; emerging debates in development and environment in post-modern era.

PLAN 638.title: Asian Development and Urbanization
PLAN 638.subject: PLAN
PLAN 638.description: Theories of globalization and sustainability in development, impacts of globalization and sustainability on development planning and policy formation, selected case studies of Asia-Pacific development.
PLAN 638.prereq_raw: (630 or ASAN 600) with a grade of B or above

PLAN 639.title: Community-based Natural Resource Management
PLAN 639.subject: PLAN
PLAN 639.description: Concepts and theories of community, resource access, and governance. Practical challenges to CBNRM in contemporary political economy.

PLAN 640.title: Land Use Policies and Programs
PLAN 640.subject: PLAN
PLAN 640.description: Land use public policy planning in urban and regional settings. Growth management and land use guidance systems.

PLAN 641.title: Neighborhood and Community Land Use Planning
PLAN 641.subject: PLAN
PLAN 641.description: Land use planning for urban neighborhoods and small towns. Theory and practice of neighborhood planning. Neighborhood and community dynamics, reinvestment, and stabilization.

PLAN 642.title: Planning Urban Infrastructure
PLAN 642.subject: PLAN
PLAN 642.description: Introduction to the planning of various urban infrastructures. Explores approaches and tools to plan, evaluate, and regulate urban infrastructure systems in support of sustainable and resilient cities and communities.

PLAN 643.title: Project Planning and Management
PLAN 643.subject: PLAN
PLAN 643.description: Examines project management in theory and practice and the roles and responsibilities of the project manager. Focuses on planning, organizing, and controlling the efforts of projects.

PLAN 645.title: Land Use Planning
PLAN 645.subject: PLAN
PLAN 645.description: Issues and methods of urban land use planning practice and plan making.

PLAN 647.title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
PLAN 647.subject: PLAN
PLAN 647.description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered. Graduate students only.

PLAN 648.title: Urban Transportation Policy and Planning
PLAN 648.subject: PLAN
PLAN 648.description: Theory and practice of urban transportation planning in developed and developing countries with an emphasis on the U.S., Asia, and Pacific region.

PLAN 649.title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
PLAN 649.subject: PLAN
PLAN 649.description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

PLAN 650.title: Research Design Seminar
PLAN 650.subject: PLAN
PLAN 650.description: Research design and preparation of thesis proposal. Normally taken after admission to candidacy in MURP.
PLAN 650.prereq_raw: (600, 601, 603) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

PLAN 652.title: Policy Implementation and Program Evaluation
PLAN 652.subject: PLAN
PLAN 652.description: Implementation and evaluation in public policy analysis; philosophical and methodological issues; impact of policies and plans; use of evaluation research in program implementation.

PLAN 654.title: Applied Geographic Information Systems: Public Policy and Spatial Analysis
PLAN 654.subject: PLAN
PLAN 654.description: Use of advanced and specialized spatial methods and models in urban and regional planning. Uses GIS software and builds upon 601. Skills are useful applied to planning, economic development, and environmental planning and resource management.

PLAN 655.title: Planning Research Methods
PLAN 655.subject: PLAN
PLAN 655.description: Advanced methods and deterministic and stochastic models used in urban and regional planning.

PLAN 661.title: Collaboration Between Sectors
PLAN 661.subject: PLAN
PLAN 661.description: Examine theories and practices of multisector collaboration (public, private, nonprofit). The use of collaboration as an alternative way of solving public problems.

PLAN 668.title: Facilitation: Facilitating Community and Organizational Change
PLAN 668.subject: PLAN
PLAN 668.description: Advanced conflict resolution course. Covers key issues in the prevention, management and resolution of multiparty conflicts. Combined lecture, discussion, and simulations.
PLAN 668.prereq_raw: graduate standing, or departmental approval. (Once a year)

PLAN 670.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
PLAN 670.subject: PLAN
PLAN 670.description: Overview to the field of disaster management and humanitarian assistance with a specific focus on risk reduction. Includes background knowledge and skills for preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and adaptation to hazards and threats.
PLAN 670.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Once a year)

PLAN 671.title: Disaster Management: Understanding the Nature of Hazards
PLAN 671.subject: PLAN
PLAN 671.description: Combined lecture/ discussion in disaster management focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.

PLAN 672.title: Humanitarian Assistance: Principles, Practices and Politics
PLAN 672.subject: PLAN
PLAN 672.description: Combined lecture/ discussion aimed at understanding the theoretical basis and working structure of humanitarian assistance programs and international responses to natural and human-induced disasters.

PLAN 673.title: Information Systems for Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance
PLAN 673.subject: PLAN
PLAN 673.description: Combined lecture/laboratory in disaster management focusing on essential methodological and practical issues that are involved in spatial analyses using GIS and other information technologies to inform decision making related to natural hazards, disasters, and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.
PLAN 673.prereq_raw: 473 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

PLAN 674.title: Disaster Recovery: Theory and Practice
PLAN 674.subject: PLAN
PLAN 674.description: How do communities recover from disaster? Provides students with an overview of recovery theory and an understanding of how planners, policy makers, and ordinary citizens rebuild communities, cities, and nations following catastrophic events. Graduate standing only.

PLAN 675.title: Preservation: Theory and Practice
PLAN 675.subject: PLAN
PLAN 675.description: History and philosophy of historic preservation movement. Analysis of values and assumptions, methodologies and tactics, implications for society and public policy.

PLAN 676.title: Recording Historic and Cultural Resources
PLAN 676.subject: PLAN
PLAN 676.description: Techniques in recording and evaluation of historic buildings and other resources, with an emphasis on field recordings and state and federal registration procedures.

PLAN 677.title: Historic Preservation Planning
PLAN 677.subject: PLAN
PLAN 677.description: Local-level historic preservation, with an emphasis on historic districts, design guidelines, regulatory controls, and community consensus-building.

PLAN 678.title: Site Planning
PLAN 678.subject: PLAN
PLAN 678.description: Fundamental principles that guide site planning, including planning and design determinants of the site taking into account its regional context, site-specific characteristics and applicable codes, ordinances, and standards.

PLAN 680.title: Land Use Management and Control
PLAN 680.subject: PLAN
PLAN 680.description: Survey course of public land use management.

PLAN 683.title: Housing and Community Development Practicum
PLAN 683.subject: PLAN
PLAN 683.description: Laboratory and field testing of selected topics related to housing design and technology; site development and infrastructure; social, health and economic community development; and housing implementation strategies.

PLAN 686.title: Housing and Community Services in Asia and Pacific
PLAN 686.subject: PLAN
PLAN 686.description: Application of analysis and construction technology to problems associated with physical development of suburban and neighborhood communities. Development of design and construction programs. Emphasis on low and intermediate technology solutions. Open to nonmajors.

PLAN 699.title: Directed Reading and Research
PLAN 699.subject: PLAN
PLAN 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

PLAN 700.title: Thesis Research
PLAN 700.subject: PLAN
PLAN 700.description: Limited to MURP students under Plan A.

PLAN 721.title: Homeland Security: Terrorism
PLAN 721.subject: PLAN
PLAN 721.description: Combined lecture/discussion in disaster management and humanitarian assistance track focusing on developing a multidisciplinary understanding of international terrorism and anti-terrorism planning and response.

PLAN 740.title: Seminar in Planning Theory
PLAN 740.subject: PLAN
PLAN 740.description: Special topics in theory, history, analysis.

PLAN 741.title: Seminar in Planning Practice
PLAN 741.subject: PLAN
PLAN 741.description: Project planning, programming, and similar topics.

PLAN 751.title: Planning Practicum
PLAN 751.subject: PLAN
PLAN 751.description: Team experience in defining and addressing a current planning problem; identification, substantive review, research design, preparation and presentation of analysis. Topic varies. Limited to 10 students.

PLAN 752.title: Directed Project
PLAN 752.subject: PLAN
PLAN 752.description: Individual project in analysis, plan preparation and evaluation, and policy/ program evaluation.

PLAN 754.title: Urban Design Studio
PLAN 754.subject: PLAN
PLAN 754.description: Group experience in defining urban and regional design problems and potentials, developing and evaluating alternatives, formulating strategies for implementation.
PLAN 754.prereq_raw: (600 and 601) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

PLAN 800.title: Dissertation Research
PLAN 800.subject: PLAN
PLAN 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation. S/U only. PhD student only.

PSY 100.title: Survey of Psychology
PSY 100.subject: PSY
PSY 100.description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

PSY 100A.title: Survey of Psychology
PSY 100A.subject: PSY
PSY 100A.description: An overview of the field: psychophysiology, perception, learning, cognition, stress, personality, social psychology.

PSY 170.title: Personal Development
PSY 170.subject: PSY
PSY 170.description: The application of psychology to the understanding, management, and enhancement of one’s life.

PSY 202.title: Psychology of Gender
PSY 202.subject: PSY
PSY 202.description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to gender and its impact on the lives of women and men: socialization of gender, mental health, racial identity, majority-minority status, sexual orientation, life-span issues and violence.

PSY 212.title: Survey of Research Methods
PSY 212.subject: PSY
PSY 212.description: Survey of standard methods and related conceptual issues employed in psychological research. Both experimental and non-experimental methods will be reviewed.

PSY 220.title: Introduction to Behavioral Psychology
PSY 220.subject: PSY
PSY 220.description: Outline of basic learning principles. A general, unified approach to study of human personality and behavior. Based upon a learning conception; various areas of psychology and the other social sciences are treated.

PSY 225.title: Statistical Techniques
PSY 225.subject: PSY
PSY 225.description: Frequency distributions; graphic methods; central tendency; variability; correlation; reliability; tests of significance.

PSY 230.title: Introduction to Psychobiology
PSY 230.subject: PSY
PSY 230.description: Survey of study of behavior from a natural sciences viewpoint. Evolution, ethological analysis of behavior genetics, neural mechanisms, drugs and behavior, biological development.

PSY 240.title: Developmental Psychology
PSY 240.subject: PSY
PSY 240.description: Emotional, mental, physical, social development from infancy to adulthood; interests and abilities at different age levels.

PSY 250.title: Social Psychology
PSY 250.subject: PSY
PSY 250.description: Cognitive, behavioral, and emotional effects of people: interpersonal relations, attribution, attitudes, group behavior, stereotypes, social roles, aggression, helping, self-concept; applications.

PSY 260.title: Psychology of Personality
PSY 260.subject: PSY
PSY 260.description: Scientific study of personality, its meaning, assessment, development, relation to cultural-social determinants.

PSY 270.title: Introduction to Clinical Psychology
PSY 270.subject: PSY
PSY 270.description: History, theories, types of psychological problems, methods of assessment, forms of intervention, current developments.

PSY 280.title: Introduction to Community Psychology
PSY 280.subject: PSY
PSY 280.description: Examination of human functioning in social and ecological context. Topics include stress, health, intergroup relations, culture, ethnicity, social competence, and community empowerment.

PSY 301.title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
PSY 301.subject: PSY
PSY 301.description: Psychology as applied to education, including major theories and research and development, cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching and learning. Incorporates introductions to standardized testing, classroom assessment, motivation, instructional planning and classroom management.

PSY 322.title: Learning and Motivation
PSY 322.subject: PSY
PSY 322.description: Theoretical interpretations; survey of major theorists and contemporary controversial issues; major influences in classical and instrumental conditioning.

PSY 324.title: Psychology of Emotion
PSY 324.subject: PSY
