POLS 381.subject: POLS
POLS 381.description: Historical emergence of modern bureaucracy; mutual impact of administrative forms on social life; relation of bureaucracy to capitalism and patriarchy; constitution of the administered individual.
POLS 381.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

POLS 382.title: Political Leadership
POLS 382.subject: POLS
POLS 382.description: Exploration of concepts and theories of political leadership, partly through biography, as preparation for public service or advanced scholarly inquiry.
POLS 382.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

POLS 383.title: Politics and Public Policy II
POLS 383.subject: POLS
POLS 383.description: Overview of the policy-making process in various political arenas (families, cities, nations, etc.); emphasis on conceptual and empirical analysis.
POLS 383.prereq_raw: any 100 level POLS course or consent

POLS 384.title: Women and Politics
POLS 384.subject: POLS
POLS 384.description: Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries. Female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions.
POLS 384.prereq_raw: any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent), WS 151 (or concurrent), or WS 362 (or concurrent); or consent

POLS 385.title: American Politics
POLS 385.subject: POLS
POLS 385.description: Institutions (parties, interest groups, legislatures, executives, local government); policies (national defense, poverty, energy, etc.), politics (symbolism, inequality, race, and gender).

POLS 386.title: Public Policy-Making
POLS 386.subject: POLS
POLS 386.description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/ discussion and field-trips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence.
POLS 386.prereq_raw: HON 101 or HON 291, or departmental approval

POLS 387.title: Politics of the Ocean
POLS 387.subject: POLS
POLS 387.description: Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. Sophomore standing or higher.
POLS 387.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent

POLS 389.title: Health Politics
POLS 389.subject: POLS
POLS 389.description: Examines the politics of health care. Focus on institutional models to health care, the politics of health care reform, and contemporary health care issues and controversies. Sophomore standing or higher.

POLS 390.title: Political Inquiry and Analysis
POLS 390.subject: POLS
POLS 390.description: Introductory survey and analysis of methods used in empirical research, policy analysis, and social criticism.

POLS 393.title: Advanced Topics in Law, Policy, and Society
POLS 393.subject: POLS
POLS 393.description: Studies integrating concerns of public law, public policy, public administration, and social movements.
POLS 393.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent

POLS 394.title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives
POLS 394.subject: POLS
POLS 394.description: Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change.
POLS 394.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course or 390 (or concurrent) or WS 151, or consent

children.text: -level POLS course or 390 (or concurrent) or WS 151 , or consent

POLS 396.title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
POLS 396.subject: POLS
POLS 396.description: Exploration of scientific and cultural resources for nonviolent alternatives in politics.
POLS 396.prereq_raw: any 100- or 200-level POLS course, or consent

POLS 401.title: Teaching Political Science
POLS 401.subject: POLS
POLS 401.description: Practicum for majors who serve as undergraduate teaching assistants.

POLS 402.title: Legislative Internship
POLS 402.subject: POLS
POLS 402.description: Field placement at the Hawai‘i Legislature integrated with academic study of political institutions and practices.

POLS 403.title: Community Internship
POLS 403.subject: POLS
POLS 403.description: Field placement integrated with academic study of political institutions and community organizations.

POLS 404.title: Senior Thesis
POLS 404.subject: POLS
POLS 404.description: Independent research and thesis writing with supervision of senior advisor.

POLS 405.title: Executive Internship
POLS 405.subject: POLS
POLS 405.description: Open to students awarded a Manoa Undergraduate Political Fellowship for placement in the Governor’s or Lt. Governor’s Office, Prosecuting Attorney’s Office, or Public Defender’s Office. Field placement, integrated with academic study.

POLS 406.title: Senior Seminar in Political Science
POLS 406.subject: POLS
POLS 406.description: Exploration of themes in political science with emphasis on discussion, research, and substantial writing.
POLS 406.prereq_raw: 390 (or concurrent) or senior standing or consent

POLS 408.title: Mânoa Undergraduate Congressional Fellowship Internship Seminar
POLS 408.subject: POLS
POLS 408.description: Hawai‘i Undergraduate Political Internship’s Congressional Fellowship. Award includes stipend and internship experience in a Hawai‘i congressional office. Students review policy processes, House and Senate procedures and produce a final paper. Restricted to fellowship awardees only. Junior and senior standing only.

POLS 600.title: Scope and Methods of Political Science
POLS 600.subject: POLS
POLS 600.description: Main concepts delineating boundaries of discipline; approaches to knowledge employed by political scientists; empirical and normative theory; problems in theory-building; validity and reliability in research design; philosophy of science applied to political science.

POLS 601.title: Political Analysis and Theory Building
POLS 601.subject: POLS
POLS 601.description: Survey of theory-building, approaches and validation techniques.

POLS 602.title: Research Techniques and Analytic Methods
POLS 602.subject: POLS
POLS 602.description: Quantitative models and statistical inference techniques.

POLS 605.title: Topics in Methodology
POLS 605.subject: POLS
POLS 605.description: Specific methodological techniques and practices introduced in 601 and 602.

POLS 610.title: Political Theory and Analysis
POLS 610.subject: POLS
POLS 610.description: Major contemporary approaches and styles in political theory, philosophy, and analysis.

POLS 611.title: Tradition of Political Philosophy
POLS 611.subject: POLS
POLS 611.description: Discussion of texts and themes in the Western political tradition from Plato to Nietzsche.

POLS 612.title: Hawaiian Political Thought: Theory and Method/Na Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i
POLS 612.subject: POLS
POLS 612.description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods.

POLS 620.title: Introduction to Indigenous Politics
POLS 620.subject: POLS
POLS 620.description: Historical treatment of the contact between state and indigenous peoples and a survey of contemporary indigenous political initiatives: social movements, media, indigenous studies programs, and events.

POLS 621.title: Politics of Indigenous Representation
POLS 621.subject: POLS
POLS 621.description: Politics of indigenous representations in media, literature, and academic scholarship.

POLS 630.title: International Relations
POLS 630.subject: POLS
POLS 630.description: Analysis of theories: actors, decisions, systems, conflict, integration, alternative approaches to validation.

POLS 633.title: International Conflict Resolution
POLS 633.subject: POLS
POLS 633.description: Analysis of international conflict and conflict resolution. Theory and practice of negotiation, mediation, conciliation, facilitation, and other “third-party” methods of peaceful settlement.

POLS 634.title: Teaching Model United Nations
POLS 634.subject: POLS
POLS 634.description: Substantive and pedagogical approaches to using Model United Nations simulation for teaching and conflict resolution. Graduate students only.

POLS 640.title: Comparative Politics
POLS 640.subject: POLS
POLS 640.description: Emphasis on Asia, theories of development, and comparative methods. At least one section a semester.

POLS 642.title: Indigenous Peoples and Western Imperialism
POLS 642.subject: POLS
POLS 642.description: Historical examination of U.S. and European imperialisms, including national narratives, politics, and impacts upon indigenous peoples in the Americas, Pacific, and Asia.

POLS 647.title: American Political Institutions in Comparative Perspective
POLS 647.subject: POLS
POLS 647.description: Consideration of American political institutions and development relative to American philosophical foundations and non-American political forms. Federalism as an expansive devise will be emphasized, as will American influence and penetration abroad.
POLS 647.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. (Once a year)

POLS 650.title: Public Administrative Theory
POLS 650.subject: POLS
POLS 650.description: Focus varies among theoretical, comparative and developmental approaches to study of administration. One section each semester.

POLS 651.title: Political Leadership
POLS 651.subject: POLS
POLS 651.description: Exploration of political leadership as a focus for research, teaching, and applied political science.

POLS 652.title: Comparative Public Administration
POLS 652.subject: POLS
POLS 652.description: Detailed examination of implementation of governmental policy in different countries.

POLS 660.title: Law and Politics
POLS 660.subject: POLS
POLS 660.description: Law, courts, and rights as a political resource; analyses of public law (including court decisions), other forms of dispute management, and judicial behavior and policy-making.

POLS 670.title: Introduction to Public Policy
POLS 670.subject: POLS
POLS 670.description: Perspectives on policy analysis; basic approaches to the study of public policy, political economy, and policy evaluation.

POLS 672.title: Politics of the Future
POLS 672.subject: POLS
POLS 672.description: Introduction to political futures studies; images of future, theories of social change, methods of social forecasting and designing preferred futures.

POLS 673.title: The Future of Political Systems
POLS 673.subject: POLS
POLS 673.description: Normative and descriptive forecasts of political institutions, systems, subsystems, and behaviors. Design of preferred systems.

POLS 675.title: Topics in Public Policy
POLS 675.subject: POLS
POLS 675.description: Particular political processes, specific political institutions, or particular policy area.

POLS 676.title: Nonviolent Political Alternatives
POLS 676.subject: POLS
POLS 676.description: Exploration of nonviolent, non-killing alternatives in political science research, teaching, and public service.

POLS 680.title: Asian and/or Pacific Politics
POLS 680.subject: POLS
POLS 680.description: Political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in all or part of Asia and/or the Pacific.

POLS 684.title: Contemporary Native Hawaiian Politics
POLS 684.subject: POLS
POLS 684.description: Study of political and social movements, political status, national and cultural identities, and issues of representation of Native Hawaiians.

POLS 686.title: Politics of Hawai‘i
POLS 686.subject: POLS
POLS 686.description: Examinations from several perspectives of the political, economic, and cultural forces that historically formed Hawai‘i and contemporary political themes, issues, and processes.

POLS 692.title: Teaching Initiative in Political Science
POLS 692.subject: POLS
POLS 692.description: Combines the study of the theoretical and practical aspects of teaching political science with supervised classroom teaching of POLS 110.

POLS 696.title: Graduate Intern Seminar
POLS 696.subject: POLS
POLS 696.description: Seminar for those seeking internship experience.
POLS 696.prereq_raw: 672 and 673 or consent for the alternative futures option; 620 or consent for the indigenous politics option; consent of advisor for all other options

children.text: for the alternative futures option; 620 or consent for the indigenous politics option; consent of advisor for all other options

POLS 702.title: Seminar: Research Methods
POLS 702.subject: POLS
POLS 702.description: Conceptual strategies, data collection approaches, and data analysis techniques appropriate to political inquiries.

POLS 703.title: Writing Politics
POLS 703.subject: POLS
POLS 703.description: Seminar on the politics of writing, grammar, translation, argument, genre, and style with significant content on indigenous issues of oral traditions, alternative modes of writing and argument, and language continuance.

POLS 710.title: Seminar: Political Thought
POLS 710.subject: POLS
POLS 710.description: Pre-announced topics. At least one section a year.

POLS 720.title: Seminar: Indigenous Theory
POLS 720.subject: POLS
POLS 720.description: Pre-announced topics may include gender and sexuality studies, postcolonial theory, colonial discourse analysis, globalization, historiography; emphasis on indigenous epistemologies and the work of native scholars.

POLS 730.title: Seminar: International Relations
POLS 730.subject: POLS
POLS 730.description: Pre-announced problems of both international organization and politics. At least one section a semester.

POLS 740.title: Seminar: Comparative Government and Politics
POLS 740.subject: POLS
POLS 740.description: Pre-announced topics. At least one section a semester.

POLS 750.title: Seminar: Public Administration
POLS 750.subject: POLS
POLS 750.description: Pre-announced administrative theory, comparative and development administration, and functional aspects.

POLS 770.title: Seminar: Public Policy
POLS 770.subject: POLS
POLS 770.prereq_raw: consent of instructor. At least one section a year

children.text: At least one section a year

POLS 776.title: Indigenous Nations and the Problems of Sovereignty
POLS 776.subject: POLS
POLS 776.description: Examines intersections of sovereignty and indigenity from comparative and critical perspectives. Engages indigenous studies of sovereignty and of alternative political frameworks. (Alt. years)

POLS 777.title: Decolonial Futures
POLS 777.subject: POLS
POLS 777.description: Topic engages probable and preferable futures of indigenous struggles and resistances. Emphasis placed on the ethics and responsibilities used to move towards those futures.

POLS 780.title: Seminar: Politics of Regions
POLS 780.subject: POLS
POLS 780.description: Analysis of political development, international relations, decision-making processes, and systems of political thought in regions and subregions of the world.

PPC 101.title: Introduction to Public Policy
PPC 101.subject: PPC
PPC 101.description: Covers a broad overview of the issues facing communities today and various individual and community approaches to navigate and address these issues.

PPC 301.title: Governing, Politics, and Public Policy
PPC 301.subject: PPC
PPC 301.description: Analysis of the major processes that translate citizen preferences into public policy.

PPC 330.title: Survey of Public Policy and Analysis
PPC 330.subject: PPC
PPC 330.description: Students will learn about the policy making process, the results of policy decisions and how public policy is assessed, analyzed, and responded to. Also discusses important policy issues that currently fill the political landscape.

PPC 336.title: Energy Economics and Policy
PPC 336.subject: PPC
PPC 336.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

PPC 340.title: Energy Technologies for Addressing Climate Change, Economic, Policy and Security Issues
PPC 340.subject: PPC
PPC 340.description: Interdisciplinary course designed to describe the inter-relationships and dynamic interactions between energy systems, the environment (climate), policy, security, and economics. Sophomore standing or higher.
PPC 340.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

PPC 495.title: Topics in Public Policy
PPC 495.subject: PPC
PPC 495.description: Seminar on current issues in U.S. or international government policy. Topics vary and may include energy, long-term care, sustainability, etc.

PPC 499.title: Directed Readings or Research
PPC 499.subject: PPC
PPC 499.description: Requires the sponsorship of a faculty member. Together they will agree on the study topic and the work to be accomplished. Depending on the scope of the project, credits range from 1-3. Needs instructor consent.

PPC 695.title: Topics in Public Policy
PPC 695.subject: PPC
PPC 695.description: Seminar on current issues in U.S. or international government policy. Topics vary and may include energy, long-term care, sustainability, etc.

PPC 699.title: Directed Readings or Research
PPC 699.subject: PPC
PPC 699.description: Requires the sponsorship of a faculty member. Together they will agree on the study topic and the work to be accomplished. Depending on the scope of the project, credits may range from 1-3. Instructor consent only. Graduate standing only.

PUBA 304.title: Governing, Politics, and Public Policy
PUBA 304.subject: PUBA
PUBA 304.description: Analysis of the major processes that translate citizen preferences into public policy.

PUBA 350.title: Research Methods for Policy Evaluation
PUBA 350.subject: PUBA
PUBA 350.description: Explores methodological approaches to the evaluation of public policies and strengths and weaknesses of various social science research methods. Students will learn how to employ them to determine the effectiveness of various public policies. Sophomore standing or higher.

PUBA 360.title: Foundations of Nonprofit Management
PUBA 360.subject: PUBA
PUBA 360.description: Broad overview of nonprofit organizations, including what it means to be a nonprofit, strategies of nonprofit organizations, and the management of nonprofits. Topics include advocacy, leadership, and evaluating success.

PUBA 424.title: Multicultural Leadership in Public Service
PUBA 424.subject: PUBA
PUBA 424.description: Develop students’ culturally agile leadership to allow them effectively lead in work on international, regional, and local projects and problems of compelling public interest that cross cultures.

PUBA 495.title: Practicum and Internship
PUBA 495.subject: PUBA
PUBA 495.description: The practicum and internship in Peace and Conflict Resolution provides an opportunity for students to apply the skills and concepts learned in earlier courses.
PUBA 495.prereq_raw: any two other PACE courses or consent

PUBA 499.title: Directed Reading and Research in Public Administration
PUBA 499.subject: PUBA
PUBA 499.description: Independent research and reading on topics in public administration, public service, and community development.

PUBA 602.title: Introduction to Public Administration
PUBA 602.subject: PUBA
PUBA 602.description: Develop a comprehension of the history and foundation of public administration. Topics include economic, political, and social dynamics; decision-making and leadership theories, management challenges, human resources, budgeting, program evaluation, policy, and technology. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 603.title: Organizations: Theory and Change
PUBA 603.subject: PUBA
PUBA 603.description: Explores characteristics and structural, human resources, political, and cultural frames of organizational theory. Focus on organizational change strategies and theories. Discusses how to use these frames and theories in everyday management of public service organizations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 604.title: Leadership and Ethics
PUBA 604.subject: PUBA
PUBA 604.description: Applies leadership and ethical theories to public and non-profit sectors, focusing on ethical leadership; emphasizes critical thinking to address value conflicts; and teaches moral reasoning as a practical professional skill. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 605.title: Effective Communication in Public Administration
PUBA 605.subject: PUBA
PUBA 605.description: Knowledge and skills to effectively communicate in the public sector. Focus on communication foundations and skills, levels and contexts of public sector communication, and handling challenges such as diverse and multi-cultural settings. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 606.title: Public Administration Personnel Management
PUBA 606.subject: PUBA
PUBA 606.description: Understand the pivotal role that effective human resource management (also known as personnel management) plays in improving organizational effectiveness. Topics include managing diversity, employment law and discrimination, performance appraisal, and labor-management relations. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 607.title: Public Administration Research Methods
PUBA 607.subject: PUBA
PUBA 607.description: Introduction to research methods for public administrators to understand the principles and methods used to conduct and analyze valid research. Examples are oriented to the field; theory and hands-on practice utilized. PUBA and PUBA Cert. majors only. Graduate students only.

PUBA 608.title: Public Budgeting
PUBA 608.subject: PUBA
PUBA 608.description: Institutions and issues related to public-sector budgeting at federal, state, and local levels. Process of developing public budgets and constraints on public policy reflected in budgets.

PUBA 609.title: Policy Analysis and Implementation
PUBA 609.subject: PUBA
PUBA 609.description: Explore contemporary policy issues relating to public administration practice. Develop analytic techniques and models of public policy-making processes, administrative rules, and policy implementation strategies. Learn how social forces, political, and economic pressures influence policy orientation.

PUBA 614.title: Program Evaluation for Public and Nonprofit Organizations
PUBA 614.subject: PUBA
PUBA 614.description: Methods for evaluating the effectiveness of programs in the public and nonprofit sectors; performance measurement to inform managerial decision making.

PUBA 620.title: Reforming Public Organizations
PUBA 620.subject: PUBA
PUBA 620.description: Looks at the challenges and opportunities for changing public organizations so that they may be more successful in meeting their public responsibilities and better places for people to work. Focus is on the creation of positive images of organization and effective change strategies.

PUBA 621.title: The Political Environment of Public Organizations
PUBA 621.subject: PUBA
PUBA 621.description: Seminar on the role of public managers in shaping public opinion and public policy. Using evidence from theory and practice presents students with tools for understanding management roles within a political context.

PUBA 622.title: Strategies of Change: Leaders and Leadership
PUBA 622.subject: PUBA
PUBA 622.description: Explores the key elements of leadership in public settings by examining what leaders actually do, looking at popular media portrayals of leadership, and talking together with guests about the challenges of leadership, effective followership, and positive change.

PUBA 623.title: Organizational Communication
PUBA 623.subject: PUBA
PUBA 623.description: Communication theory/research applied to formal organizations; assessments of strengths and weaknesses of organizational communications systems.

PUBA 624.title: Intercultural Challenges in the Public Sector
PUBA 624.subject: PUBA
PUBA 624.description: Seminar on the dimensions of cultural variability and how they affect government operations from macro to micro levels, from international policy transfer to major intercultural task interaction processes such as negotiation, planning, and relationship management. Graduate standing only.

PUBA 625.title: Law, Economics, and Public Administration
PUBA 625.subject: PUBA
PUBA 625.description: Explore U.S. law as applied to public institutions using economic lens. Rationale of property, contract, and tort law; evolution of administrative law, economic efficiency of common law system, effects of legal rules on economic behavior.

PUBA 626.title: Collaboration for Public and Nonprofit Leaders
PUBA 626.subject: PUBA
PUBA 626.description: Theories, skills, and tools needed to effectively manage networks in government and nonprofit organizations; explores how to administer, assess performance, and evaluate success in these dynamic new partnerships. Graduate students only or consent.

PUBA 627.title: Managing Workplace Diversity and Inclusion
PUBA 627.subject: PUBA
PUBA 627.description: Examines rationales, impacts, and various dimensions of diversity and inclusion beyond race and gender. Students learn and apply public management tools used to foster workplace diversity and inclusion.
PUBA 627.prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

PUBA 628.title: ICT Policy and Planning
PUBA 628.subject: PUBA
PUBA 628.description: Processes and methods of planning appropriate to the information and communication sectors, including future economic, social, political, technical, and environmental perspectives.

PUBA 630.title: Nonprofit Management
PUBA 630.subject: PUBA
PUBA 630.description: Fundamental aspects of managing a nonprofit organization: overview of the nonprofit sector; mission and scope of nonprofit organizations; organizational structures and functions; resource and volunteer development; major management issues. A-F only

PUBA 631.title: Nonprofit Management Practices and Tools
PUBA 631.subject: PUBA
PUBA 631.description: Skills and tools needed by nonprofit managers. Topics include but are not limited to grantwriting, strategic planning, business practices, program evaluation, and advocacy.

PUBA 640.title: International Perspectives on Public Administration
PUBA 640.subject: PUBA
PUBA 640.description: Key dimensions of public administration systems on a global scale; historic and contemporary forces shaping national systems; the dimensions that distinguish them, the opportunities and constraints for comparison and the transfer of knowledge and experience.

PUBA 641.title: Indigenous Governance
PUBA 641.subject: PUBA
PUBA 641.description: Overview of indigenous governing systems, particularly in the Americas and the Pacific. Students will learn the legal frameworks and principles of these systems, and how services are provided to citizens.

PUBA 667.title: Special Topics
PUBA 667.subject: PUBA
PUBA 667.description: Topics of current interest in the field of public service and public administration, taught by regular and visiting faculty.

PUBA 690.title: MPA Practicum
PUBA 690.subject: PUBA
PUBA 690.description: Placement in public, private, and nonprofit organizations to observe and analyze organizational functions and processes while undertaking projects of use to the host agency.
PUBA 690.prereq_raw: with a minimum grade of B: 602, 603, and 604

PUBA 691.title: Certificate Practicum
PUBA 691.subject: PUBA
PUBA 691.description: Students in the nonprofit management track of the certificate will learn by doing and observing in a nonprofit organization selected in consultation with the student’s advisor. PUBA graduate certificate students only.

PUBA 695.title: Capstone Planning Seminar
PUBA 695.subject: PUBA
PUBA 695.description: Develops topics, methods, objectives, and resources to guide work of capstone seminar.

PUBA 696.title: Capstone Seminar
PUBA 696.subject: PUBA
PUBA 696.description: Culminates public administration core courses by incorporating theoretical, analytical, and practicum observations into examination of public issues of importance to Hawai‘i and the region.

SOC 100.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOC 100.subject: SOC
SOC 100.description: Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

SOC 100A.title: Introduction to Sociology
SOC 100A.subject: SOC
SOC 100A.description: Basic social relationships, social structures, and processes.

SOC 176.title: Introduction to Data Analysis
SOC 176.subject: SOC
SOC 176.description: Basic analytic skills widely used in quantitative analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, rates and probability, comparison of groups, introduction to causal relationships, and application of these techniques to real life examples.

SOC 180.title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
SOC 180.subject: SOC
SOC 180.description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region.

SOC 214.title: Introduction to Race and Ethnic Relations
SOC 214.subject: SOC
SOC 214.description: Race and ethnic relations in world perspective; social, economic, and political problems associated with perception, existence, and accommodation of these groups within the wider society.

SOC 218.title: Introduction to Social Problems
SOC 218.subject: SOC
SOC 218.description: Theoretical and substantive survey of the nature and causes of social problems; selected types: poverty, inequality, deviance, etc

SOC 231.title: Introduction to Juvenile Delinquency
SOC 231.subject: SOC
SOC 231.description: Forms of juvenile deviance; conditions and processes that result in alienation and deviance of youth. Juvenile corrections as institutionalized societal responses.

SOC 251.title: Introduction to Sociology of the Family
SOC 251.subject: SOC
SOC 251.description: Family patterns, mate selection, parent-child interaction, socialization of roles, legal sanctions, trends in organization, functions.

SOC 300.title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
SOC 300.subject: SOC
SOC 300.description: Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics.

SOC 300A.title: Principles of Sociological Inquiry
SOC 300A.subject: SOC
SOC 300A.description: Basic methods of sociology for production and analysis of data. Foundations for understanding research and for advanced courses in methods and statistics. Restricted to students in the honors program and required for students taking the honors track in sociology.

SOC 301.title: Survey of Urban Sociology
SOC 301.subject: SOC
SOC 301.description: Urban processes and social problems, such as poverty, crime, racial segregation, homelessness, housing policy, urbanization, and neighborhood ethnic diversity. How places shape identity and opportunity. Research methods applied to communities, places, and neighborhoods of Hawai‘i.

SOC 305.title: Women and Health
SOC 305.subject: SOC
SOC 305.description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
SOC 305.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WS 151 or WS 202, or POLS 110; or consent

SOC 311.title: Survey of Social Inequality and Stratification
SOC 311.subject: SOC
SOC 311.description: Introduction to social stratification theory and research; definition and measurement of socioeconomic status; racial, ethnic and gender inequality; differences in lifestyles and life chances; social mobility.

SOC 313.title: Survey of Sociology of Work
SOC 313.subject: SOC
SOC 313.description: Work from viewpoint of individuals; meaningfulness versus productivity; how work, economics, and the industrial system affect individual goals.

SOC 316.title: Survey of Social Change
SOC 316.subject: SOC
SOC 316.description: Causes, processes, and effects of social change, using single and multi-cause models in simple and complex industrialized societies.

SOC 318.title: Women and Social Policy
SOC 318.subject: SOC
SOC 318.description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
SOC 318.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent

SOC 321.title: Survey of Sociological Theory
SOC 321.subject: SOC
SOC 321.description: Major theorists and their influences, from Comte to today.

SOC 332.title: Survey of Sociology Law
SOC 332.subject: SOC
SOC 332.description: Law as a political enforcement of the social order; how it is organized and operates; determinants of effectiveness; ways it adapts to and facilitates changing social conditions.

SOC 333.title: Survey of Criminology
SOC 333.subject: SOC
SOC 333.description: Concepts used in crime, law enforcement, criminal justice, and corrections. Types of criminal behavior; costs and effects of control.

SOC 335.title: Survey of Drugs and Society
SOC 335.subject: SOC
SOC 335.description: Use of mood- and mind-altering drugs in America among adults, youth, and cross-culturally. Illicit drug culture, psychedelics, and perception; social norms and deviant behavior.

SOC 336.title: Deviant Behavior and Social Control
SOC 336.subject: SOC
SOC 336.description: Interrelations of deviance, criminology, juvenile delinquency, corrections, social control, sociology of law. Key concepts, theories.

SOC 337.title: Criminal Justice Organizations
SOC 337.subject: SOC
SOC 337.description: Examines major criminal justice organizations–police, courts, and prisons. Using organizational theory, identifies the role of organizational goals, structure, resources, legitimacy, culture, and front-line workers in shaping criminal justice policy and practice.
SOC 337.prereq_raw: 100 or a 200-level SOC course, or consent

SOC 341.title: Survey of Social Psychology
SOC 341.subject: SOC
SOC 341.description: Major principles; social attitudes, theories of conformity and change, person perception and attribution theory, social role, role conflict and role behavior, group structure, and behavior.

SOC 352.title: Survey of Sociology of Education
SOC 352.subject: SOC
SOC 352.description: Formal education as one aspect of socialization. Emphasis on American system; business, military, and religious institutions.

SOC 353.title: Survey of Sociology of Aging
SOC 353.subject: SOC
SOC 353.description: Aging as a social phenomenon, including social impacts of growing elderly population and emerging social patterns among the elderly. Important theoretical perspectives and cross-national research.

SOC 354.title: Survey of Medical Sociology
SOC 354.subject: SOC
SOC 354.description: Social factors in disease and treatment; illness behavior, roles of patients and healers; nature of healing professions; use of medical services; alternative systems of medical organization.

SOC 356.title: Chinese Society and Culture
SOC 356.subject: SOC
SOC 356.description: Social institutions, family, community, education, stratification, government, economy; impact of modernization and revolution on their contemporary transformation.

SOC 357.title: Japanese Society and Culture
SOC 357.subject: SOC
SOC 357.description: Persistence and change in economy, policy, religion, education, family, and other institutions of modern Japan.

SOC 358.title: Sociology of Korea
SOC 358.subject: SOC
SOC 358.description: Social institutions, family, education, religion, cultural values, social classes, economic development, social movements, gender relations, North-South relations, and unification issues.
SOC 358.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent

SOC 362.title: Sociology of Gender
SOC 362.subject: SOC
SOC 362.description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems.
SOC 362.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent

SOC 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
SOC 367.subject: SOC
SOC 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
SOC 367.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or consent

SOC 374.title: Law, Politics and Society
SOC 374.subject: SOC
SOC 374.description: Relationships between law, politics, and society will be explored. Emphasis is placed on several dimensions of legality: legal “indeterminacy” and some of the many things that law does for us and to us; law’s response to violence; the connections between law and social change; access to the law and its sociological dimensions; how/why law fails and what happens when it does.
SOC 374.prereq_raw: 100 or any 200 level SOC course, or a 100 level or 200 level POLS course, or consent

SOC 400.title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics
SOC 400.subject: SOC
SOC 400.description: Explores how food, body, and other “matter of life” are imbedded in biopolitics from the feminist perspectives.
SOC 400.prereq_raw: WS 151 or three credits of upper division WS courses, or consent.

children.text: three credits of upper division WS courses,

SOC 401.title: Analysis in Urban Sociology
SOC 401.subject: SOC
SOC 401.description: Urbanization in developed and developing countries, the rural-urban continuum, structure and process of metropolitan regions, theories of urban location and growth, housing and urban renewal.

SOC 411.title: Analysis in Social Stratification
SOC 411.subject: SOC
SOC 411.description: Approaches to research in social inequality: community studies; historical and cross-cultural analyses of poverty, working class, middle class, power structure, social mobility, etc.

SOC 412.title: Analysis in Population and Society
SOC 412.subject: SOC
SOC 412.description: Global and U.S. patterns of population growth; composition and distribution, elementary demographic techniques; development issues and population policy.

SOC 413.title: Economy and Society
SOC 413.subject: SOC
SOC 413.description: Study of the dominant trend of economic change and its impact on society; globalization of economic activities and transformation of industrial society to postindustrial one; corporate restructuring and downsizing and their impact on employment and income distribution; gender relations in workplaces; the impact of globalization on the newly industrializing countries.

SOC 415.title: Technology and Society
SOC 415.subject: SOC
SOC 415.description: Nature of technology, social forces that affect its adoption; impact on society; innovation.

SOC 418.title: Women and Work
SOC 418.subject: SOC
SOC 418.description: Gender and racial division of labor nationally and internationally; racial and gender differentials in wages, training, working conditions and unemployment; historical trends and future directions.
SOC 418.prereq_raw: 300, or one 300-level WS or ES course; or consent

SOC 419.title: Organizations and Society
SOC 419.subject: SOC
SOC 419.description: Schools, hospitals, industries, prisons, and government agencies analyzed in terms of self-actualization, alienation, human relations, communication, leadership, organizational conflicts.

SOC 431.title: Analysis in Criminology/Juvenile Delinquency
SOC 431.subject: SOC
SOC 431.description: Research in systematic social deviation. Scaling and measurement of delinquents/ criminals, official data, gangs, identification and measurement of delinquent/criminal value orientations, etc.

SOC 432.title: Analysis in Corrections
SOC 432.subject: SOC
SOC 432.description: Behavioral assumptions of various correctional practices and modes of organization; current “in-community” approaches.

SOC 433.title: Analysis in Law and Social Change
SOC 433.subject: SOC
SOC 433.description: Interrelationships between legal orders and other social institutions; use of “law” to change major status relationships, e.g., boss-worker, woman-man, child-adult.

SOC 435.title: Women and Crime
SOC 435.subject: SOC
SOC 435.description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system.
SOC 435.prereq_raw: 300, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent. (

SOC 441.title: Social Structure and the Individual
SOC 441.subject: SOC
SOC 441.description: Effects of social institutions on individuals. Role of socioeconomic status, cultural background, family structure, peer group, schools, and occupational roles in socialization.

SOC 445.title: Analysis in Gender Violence
SOC 445.subject: SOC
SOC 445.description: Historical and structural theories of gender-based violence, including domestic and sexual abuse, prostitution, trafficking, cross-cultural perspectives, social policy and practices. Junior standing or graduate standing only.

SOC 446.title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
SOC 446.subject: SOC
SOC 446.description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
SOC 446.prereq_raw: 300, WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent

SOC 451.title: Analysis in Marriage and the Family
SOC 451.subject: SOC
SOC 451.description: Theory and methods of studying social interaction in marriage and the family; examination of marriage, mating, love, and choice. Empirical research emphasizing Hawai‘i.

SOC 452.title: Marriage and Family: A Feminist Perspective
SOC 452.subject: SOC
SOC 452.description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries.
SOC 452.prereq_raw: 300, or WS 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course; or consent

SOC 453.title: Analysis in Sociology of Aging
SOC 453.subject: SOC
SOC 453.description: Social and research issues significant to delivery of long-term care services to the elderly; cost, quality, availability of services, evaluation of programs, role of family, formal and informal care services.

SOC 454.title: Analysis in Medical Sociology
SOC 454.subject: SOC
SOC 454.description: Application of sociological theories and concepts to medical social situations and behavior; problems of obtaining data for research.

SOC 455.title: Sociology of Religion
SOC 455.subject: SOC
SOC 455.description: Seminar in research on sociological aspects of religious sectarianism; attention to Hawai‘i.

SOC 456.title: Racism and Ethnicity in Hawai‘i
SOC 456.subject: SOC
SOC 456.description: The historical and contemporary social processes involved in inter-ethnic relations in Hawai‘i.
SOC 456.prereq_raw: 300 or one ES 300 level course, or consent

SOC 457.title: Sociology of the Arts
SOC 457.subject: SOC
SOC 457.description: Relation of art to society; role of artist, audience, critic, patron, museum; Western and other societies; attitudes toward new styles.

SOC 458.title: Analysis in Sports and Society
SOC 458.subject: SOC
SOC 458.description: Critical perspectives on sports and society. Topics include power and inequality; mobility, status, and economics; youth development; globalization; gender; and violence in sports and the wider society.

SOC 459.title: Popular Culture
SOC 459.subject: SOC
SOC 459.description: Popular culture as manifested in film, sports, TV, comics, magazines, etc.; relation to sociological theories and studies.

SOC 475.title: Analysis in Survey Research
SOC 475.subject: SOC
SOC 475.description: Survey research design and analysis, including theory selection instrument construction, sampling techniques, data collection, computerized data analysis, and writing up research reports of the findings.

SOC 476.title: Social Statistics
SOC 476.subject: SOC
SOC 476.description: Common statistical procedures emphasizing univariate and bivariate description; some attention to multivariate techniques and statistical inference, within context of research procedures.

SOC 476L.title: Social Statistics Laboratory
SOC 476L.subject: SOC
SOC 476L.description: Required lab for computer applications for analysis of sociological data.

SOC 478.title: Analysis in Field Research Methods
SOC 478.subject: SOC
SOC 478.description: Techniques for collecting and analyzing qualitative data. Participant observation; small groups in natural settings; community studies. Grounded theory; theories of everyday life; reality construction.

SOC 491.title: Discussion Group Leader–Freshman Seminar
SOC 491.subject: SOC
SOC 491.description: Students lead a freshman seminar section of sociology and meet weekly with instructor for substantive background.

SOC 492.title: Politics of Multiculturalism
SOC 492.subject: SOC
SOC 492.description: The development of ethnic relations and political approaches to multiculturalism in two multiethnic nations: Canada and the U.S.
SOC 492.prereq_raw: 300 or one 300 level ES course, or consent

SOC 494.title: Social Sciences Internship
SOC 494.subject: SOC
SOC 494.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.

SOC 495.title: Topics in Sociology
SOC 495.subject: SOC
SOC 495.description: Topics course that explore current issues and try new ideas.

SOC 496.title: Topics in Sociology: Student Projects
SOC 496.subject: SOC
SOC 496.description: Students create their own study group and solicit an advisor from faculty. Consult department for assistance.

SOC 605.title: Statistics for Regression Analysis
SOC 605.subject: SOC
SOC 605.description: Dealing with the multiple linear regression and logistic regression models, focusing on modeling, i.e., specification of the explanatory variables to answer different research questions. Emphasis on applications using statistical package programs. SOC 605L is required.

SOC 605L.title: Regression Analysis Laboratory
SOC 605L.subject: SOC
SOC 605L.description: Lab for computer analysis skills is required for students taking 605.

SOC 606.title: Research Methods and Design
SOC 606.subject: SOC
SOC 606.description: Emphasis on theory selection, theory construction, and choice of research strategies.

SOC 607.title: Seminar in Methods of Content Analysis
SOC 607.subject: SOC
SOC 607.description: Content analysis combines quantitative and qualitative methods to analyze text systematically. Covers sampling and case selection; manual and computer-assisted methods of coding and analyzing textual data; writing reports using content analysis data. (Once a year)

SOC 608.title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
SOC 608.subject: SOC
SOC 608.description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

SOC 609.title: Seminar Qualitative Research
SOC 609.subject: SOC
SOC 609.description: Advanced seminar on conducting fieldwork in natural social settings with emphasis on qualitative techniques, political and ethical considerations, data management and assessment, interpretation and reflexive writing.

SOC 611.title: Classical Sociological Theory
SOC 611.subject: SOC
SOC 611.description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociological theory from 19thcentury to the 1960s, including intellectual contexts and historical development.

SOC 612.title: Contemporary Sociological Theory
SOC 612.subject: SOC
SOC 612.description: Seminar offers a critical overview of major perspectives and representative works in sociology theory from the 1960s to the present, including intellectual contexts and historical development.

SOC 613.title: Organizational Analysis
SOC 613.subject: SOC
SOC 613.description: Theoretical approaches to organizations; organizational structure and process; organizational pathologies and effectiveness; the organization and its environment.

SOC 615.title: Medical Sociology
SOC 615.subject: SOC
SOC 615.description: Covers the major paradigms in medical sociology for analyzing social epidemiology, the political economy of health systems, health service organizations, health and wellness behaviors illness perception and help-seeking, doctor-patient interaction, and adaptations to illness.

SOC 616.title: Seminar in Stress and Health
SOC 616.subject: SOC
SOC 616.description: Analysis of current theory and empirical research on relationship of stress and health; sociological, psychological, and community psychiatry models and current issues.

SOC 617.title: Sociology of Mental Health and Illness
SOC 617.subject: SOC
SOC 617.description: Examines sociological research and theories about mental health and illness. A key question in medical sociology will be addressed: What is the relationship between society and mental health?

SOC 620.title: Seminar in Social Stratification
SOC 620.subject: SOC
SOC 620.description: Classical theories of social class, contemporary developments; crucial research issues, appropriate methodologies.

SOC 625.title: Feminist Criminology
SOC 625.subject: SOC
SOC 625.description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

SOC 631.title: Seminar in Criminology
SOC 631.subject: SOC
SOC 631.description: Major current theories, history of their development, elaborations of typologies, implications for treatment modalities.

SOC 632.title: Criminal Justice System
SOC 632.subject: SOC
SOC 632.description: Examination of the criminal justice system; the exercise of discretion and limits placed upon it.

SOC 638.title: American Punishment
SOC 638.subject: SOC
SOC 638.description: Examines the history of American criminal punishment, from the birth of the penitentiary to the rise of the prison industrial complex.

SOC 651.title: Introduction to Human Population
SOC 651.subject: SOC
SOC 651.description: Comparative analysis of quantitative and qualitative aspects of population; factors affecting size, distribution, and composition; impact of population size and composition on society.

SOC 659.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
SOC 659.subject: SOC
SOC 659.description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

SOC 660.title: Teaching Seminar
SOC 660.subject: SOC
SOC 660.description: Examines research on teaching, learning, and ethics, as well as practical skills for teaching at the university level. Syllabi and teaching philosophies are developed, which are useful for the academic job market. Graduate standing only.

SOC 670.title: Sociology of Sustainability
SOC 670.subject: SOC
SOC 670.description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only.

SOC 701.title: Seminar in Evaluation Research
SOC 701.subject: SOC
SOC 701.description: Research design, data collection, field problems and analysis in the evaluation of social programs. Examples from criminal justice, corrections, drug treatment, mental health, and public health.

SOC 705.title: Advanced Statistics
SOC 705.subject: SOC
SOC 705.description: Dealing with advanced statistical methods beyond multiple linear regression, such as logit, event history analysis, and multi-level analysis. Emphasis is on applications of the techniques to social science research.

SOC 706.title: Cultural Analysis
SOC 706.subject: SOC
SOC 706.description: Contemporary issues in cultural sociology, covering key theoretical perspectives, analytic methods and substantive areas for empirical research.

SOC 711.title: Seminar in Sociology of Knowledge
SOC 711.subject: SOC
SOC 711.description: Sociological theory applied to bases of knowledge in everyday life, professional communities, and the sciences. Research and theory-building activities of sociologists; ethnomethodology; construction of social structure, culture, and consciousness.

SOC 715.title: Seminar in Current Issues in Sociology
SOC 715.subject: SOC
SOC 715.description: Substantive areas that are of current interest and the focus of research, but not addressed in other courses.

SOC 716.title: Advanced Medical Sociology
SOC 716.subject: SOC
SOC 716.description: Application of theoretical paradigms and methodologies to the examination of selected research topics in the field of medical sociology.

SOC 718.title: Seminar in Aging, Culture, and Health
SOC 718.subject: SOC
SOC 718.description: Overview of the major theories, perspectives, and empirical findings relating to aging in various cultural contexts.
SOC 718.prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent
SOC 718.restrictions_raw: SOC, PSY, NURS, SW, PH majors only.

SOC 719.title: Comparative Family and Gender
SOC 719.subject: SOC
SOC 719.description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures. (Alt. years)

SOC 720.title: Comparative Study of East Asia
SOC 720.subject: SOC
SOC 720.description: Comparative analysis of social organization, social processes, and change of both capitalist and communist countries of East Asia, with each other and other areas of the world.

SOC 721.title: Social Change–Pacific Islands
SOC 721.subject: SOC
SOC 721.description: Analysis of social change; transformation from subsistence societies to commodified, wage-labor societies with participation in world economy.

SOC 722.title: Modern Japanese Society
SOC 722.subject: SOC
SOC 722.description: Social and behavioral studies of Japanese values, social organization, and personality development. Problems of value conflict, political protest, world role, tradition, and social change.

SOC 723.title: Seminar in Modern Chinese Society
SOC 723.subject: SOC
SOC 723.description: Developmental policies, social change, and impact on modern Chinese social institutions. Includes China, Hong Kong, and Taiwan. May include social and demographic change, population, social stratification, gender, and family problems.

SOC 730.title: Conflict Analysis/Resolution
SOC 730.subject: SOC
SOC 730.description: Seminar on the analysis of conflict resolution. Faculty from law, planning, political science and guest practitioners will present multidisciplinary analysis and intervention strategies on contemporary conflicts.

SOC 741.title: Seminar in Social Structure and the Individual
SOC 741.subject: SOC
SOC 741.description: Intensive study and individual research projects in a selected topic. Theoretical and methodological issues in relating social and individual levels of analysis.

SOC 750.title: Seminar in Social Movements
SOC 750.subject: SOC
SOC 750.description: Study of sociology of social movements, plus independent student research.

SOC 751.title: Development in Asia
SOC 751.subject: SOC
SOC 751.description: Theories and available research methods examined for applicability to developing areas; specific examples from Asia.

SOC 753.title: Urban Sociology
SOC 753.subject: SOC
SOC 753.description: Demographic trends in urban growth: nature and dimensions of urbanization and urbanism; ancient, American, and Third World cities; ecological theories of urban growth; lifestyles.

SOCS 124.title: Leadership and Social Issues
SOCS 124.subject: SOCS
SOCS 124.description: Fosters understanding of key societal and community issues, social science perspectives on them, the qualities of effective leadership, and invites examination of personal responsibilities, intentions, and abilities to make a difference on those issues.

SOCS 150.title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
SOCS 150.subject: SOCS
SOCS 150.description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

SOCS 150A.title: Street Science: Evaluating and Applying Evidence in Daily Life
SOCS 150A.subject: SOCS
SOCS 150A.description: Develops necessary tools for effective reasoning and problem-solving through use and application of analytic techniques, including question formation, understanding/interpreting data presented in the public sphere, and evaluating the validity of sources.

SOCS 180.title: Introduction to International and Global Studies
SOCS 180.subject: SOCS
SOCS 180.description: Introduces undergraduate students to the major political, social, economic, cultural, technological, and historical dimensions of globalization. Special attention will be paid to globalization process that have impacted Hawai‘i and the Asia-Pacific region.

SOCS 225.title: Statistical Analysis for Social Sciences
SOCS 225.subject: SOCS
SOCS 225.description: Statistical reasoning in the analysis of social science data, including descriptive statistics, exploratory data analysis, inference measures of association, decomposition of variance, and regression analysis. Lab required.
SOCS 225.prereq_raw: any 100 level social science course or consent

SOCS 250.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
SOCS 250.subject: SOCS
SOCS 250.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

SOCS 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
SOCS 251.subject: SOCS
SOCS 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

SOCS 385.title: Service Learning
SOCS 385.subject: SOCS
SOCS 385.description: Intended for students undertaking the service learning option in another course in the College of Social Sciences. Discussions on student’s experiences, types of learning occurring, and issues encountered in service learning activities in the community.

SOCS 489.title: Social Sciences Internship
SOCS 489.subject: SOCS
SOCS 489.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.

SOCS 601.title: Topics in Teaching Innovations
SOCS 601.subject: SOCS
SOCS 601.description: Examination and critical analysis of contemporary curriculum and instruction issues in social sciences. Concepts, theories, principles underlying active learning, critical thinking, values inquiry, assessment, and multidisciplinary approaches to integration of knowledge.

SOCS 735.title: Ocean Policy and Management
SOCS 735.subject: SOCS
SOCS 735.description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

WS 141.title: Introduction to LGBTQ+ Studies
WS 141.subject: WS
WS 141.description: Introductory survey of the key terms, texts, and histories of Lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender communities.

WS 149.title: Introduction to the World’s Goddesses
WS 149.subject: WS
WS 149.description: Cross-cultural analysis of the religious narratives, beliefs, practices, iconography, and sacred sites related to female deities in the Americas, Polynesia, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and Europe from prehistory to 1500 C.E.

WS 151.title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
WS 151.subject: WS
WS 151.description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures, with a focus on gender, race, class, and sexual dynamics; exploration of women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics.

WS 151A.title: Introduction to Women’s Studies
WS 151A.subject: WS
WS 151A.description: Introduction to feminist interdisciplinary analysis from global and critical perspectives; relationships between women and men from Asia-Pacific, Hawaiian, and other cultures. Focus on gender, race, class, sexual dynamics, and women’s negotiations with institutional dynamics. Honors students only.

WS 175.title: History of Gender, Sex, and Sexuality in Global Perspectives to 1500 CE
WS 175.subject: WS
WS 175.description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from prehistory to 1500 CE. Examines ancient world civilizations from multiple perspectives stressing issues and forces still influential today.

WS 176.title: History of Gender, Sex and Sexuality in Global Perspective, 1500 CE to the Present
WS 176.subject: WS
WS 176.description: Explores how gender, sex, and sexuality become key elements in human society from 1500 CE to present. Examines world cultures from multiple perspectives, stressing issues and forces of continuing influence.

WS 200.title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
WS 200.subject: WS
WS 200.description: Social construction of gender within culture and its visual expression through appearance. Analysis of role, identity, conformity, and deviance in human appearance. Open to nonmajors.

WS 202.title: Psychology of Gender
WS 202.subject: WS
WS 202.description: Survey of topics in psychology relevant to women’s lives: socialization of gender, mental health, violence against women, achievement motivation, lifespan issues, domestic violence.

WS 230.title: Gender and Sport
WS 230.subject: WS
WS 230.description: Explores the influence of gender in sport from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives. Examines women’s and men’s role as participants, spectators, and employees of sport and sports organizations.

WS 245.title: Women Writers of World Literature
WS 245.subject: WS
WS 245.description: Major women writers of world literature examined in context of female literary tradition.
WS 245.prereq_raw: one of ENG 100A, 101, or ELI 100; or consent

WS 257.title: Sexual Identity in Literature
WS 257.subject: WS
WS 257.description: Selected themes in major works of various types, cultures, periods. Requires a minimum of 3,000 words of writing.
WS 257.prereq_raw: one of ENG 100A, 101, or ELI 100. DL

WS 304.title: Women, War, and the Military
WS 304.subject: WS
WS 304.description: The military as it includes and excludes women as soldiers, nurses, wives, prostitutes, and victims. Women and war economics; feminism, war, and peace.
WS 304.prereq_raw: one of 151, 362, 375 or SOC 362; or consent

WS 305.title: Women and Health
WS 305.subject: WS
WS 305.description: Explores current issues in the conceptualization and delivery of health care for women.
WS 305.prereq_raw: 151 or 202, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or POLS 110; or consent

WS 306.title: Indigenous Women’s Health
WS 306.subject: WS
WS 306.description: Examines issues of indigenous women’s health pre and post colonial in Hawai‘i, Asia, and the Pacific regions.
WS 306.prereq_raw: one of 151, 202, 305; or HWST 107, HWST 270 or HWST 285; or consent

WS 310.title: U.S. Women’s History to 1890s
WS 310.subject: WS
WS 310.description: A survey of history of U.S. women and gender relations up to 1890s. Emphasis on women’s labor, women’s involvement in social movement, development of suffrage movement, women’s literary and popular culture.
WS 310.prereq_raw: AMST 201 (or concurrent), or AMST 202 (or concurrent), or WS 151 or WS 151A (or concurrent), or consent

WS 311.title: U.S. Women’s History
WS 311.subject: WS
WS 311.description: History of U.S. women and gender relations. Topics include women’s work in and outside the household, women’s involvement in social movements, changing norms about gender and sexuality, and shared and divergent experiences among women.

WS 315.title: Sex and Gender
WS 315.subject: WS
WS 315.description: Cross-cultural theories and perceptions of sexual difference; linkage between biology and cultural constructions of gender; relationship of gender ideology to women’s status.

WS 318.title: Women and Social Policy
WS 318.subject: WS
WS 318.description: Social and economic policies affecting women in families, education, social services, government, health care, the economy; public policy implementation and development; policy impact on women.
WS 318.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent

WS 330.title: Gender and Sport
WS 330.subject: WS
WS 330.description: Explores the influence of gender in sport from cultural, psychosocial, and political perspectives. Examines women’s and men’s role as participants, spectators, and employees of sport and sports organizations.

WS 339.title: South Asian Migrants: Culture and Politics
WS 339.subject: WS
WS 339.description: Historical and contemporary experiences of South Asian migrants in North America, Pacific, Caribbean, and/or African diasporas; causes and patterns of migration, inter-ethnic relations policies; role of race, gender, culture in community, identity formation. Pre one ES or WS course in the 100, 200 or 300 level; or consent. (Once a year

WS 345.title: 20th-Century Literature by Women
WS 345.subject: WS
WS 345.description: Twentieth-century women writers and their works; novels, short stories, poems, autobiographies. Interrelations of gender and literature.

WS 346.title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
WS 346.subject: WS
WS 346.description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
WS 346.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent

WS 350.title: Sex Differences in the Life Cycle
WS 350.subject: WS
WS 350.description: Human sex differences, their biological basis and significance; genetic, hormonal, and behavioral determinants of sexual differentiation; biology of gender, sexuality, menopause, and aging.

WS 351.title: Women, Ideas, and Society
WS 351.subject: WS
WS 351.description: Status of women in American society today in light of the cultural, historical, and philosophical forces that have produced it.

WS 356.title: Women and Religion
WS 356.subject: WS
WS 356.description: Examining roles of, and attitudes toward, women in major religious traditions through autobiographies, films, and primary texts.

WS 360.title: Pacific/Asian Women in Hawai‘i
WS 360.subject: WS
WS 360.description: Adaptive strategies of Hawaiian, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Filipino, Samoan, and Southeast Asian women in Hawai‘i; feminist anthropological and historical analysis.
WS 360.prereq_raw: any ANTH, SOC, or WS course

WS 361.title: Seminar: Women and International Development
WS 361.subject: WS
WS 361.description: Topics: Women’s role, status, work and treatment in the Third World; economic development, changing work/family roles, agriculture and business, improvement/deterioration in gender equity across the Third World global feminization of poverty. Open to nonmajors.
WS 361.prereq_raw: a 100 level economics course or any women’s studies course; or consent

WS 362.title: Sociology of Gender
WS 362.subject: WS
WS 362.description: Effect of sex and gender roles (both traditional and nontraditional) on attitudes and behavior within the family and educational, economic, and governmental systems.
WS 362.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 100 or any 200-level SOC course; or consent

WS 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
WS 367.subject: WS
WS 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
WS 367.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent

WS 375.title: Women and the Media
WS 375.subject: WS
WS 375.description: Media portrayal of women and men; role of the media in reproducing gender inequality. Women as producers and consumers of media. Feminist alternatives to mainstream media.

WS 381.title: Gender, Sexuality and Literature
WS 381.subject: WS
WS 381.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of literary constructions of gender and sexuality.
WS 381.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

WS 382.title: Island Feminisms: Art, Literature, and Culture

WS 384.title: Women and Politics
WS 384.subject: WS
WS 384.description: Women’s role in political institutions and processes in the U.S. and other countries; female and male approaches to power; feminist political goals and actions.
WS 384.prereq_raw: 151 (or concurrent) or 362 (or concurrent) or any 100 level POLS course (or concurrent); or consent

WS 390.title: Gender and Race in U.S. Society
WS 390.subject: WS

WS 394.title: Co-ops, Communes, Collectives

WS 394.description: Theory and practice of democratic organizations: women’s and feminist organizations; co-ops, communes, and collectives; indigenous people’s organizations; workplace democracy and social change.

WS 400.title: Food, Body, and Women: Analysis of Biopolitics

WS 410.title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
WS 410.subject: WS

WS 414.title: Women in Drama and Theater
WS 414.subject: WS
WS 414.description: The role of women and their representation in the theater from ancient Greece to the present; focus on the sociopolitical status of women.

WS 418.title: Women and Work

WS 419.title: Feminist Issues in Philosophy

WS 424.title: Gender, Sexuality, and Cyberspace
WS 424.subject: WS
WS 424.description: Students learn how gender and sexuality are constructed online and produce a website to post their analysis and contribute to knowledge production about gender and sexuality in cyberspace.

WS 426.title: The Anthropology of Sexuality
WS 426.subject: WS
WS 426.description: Explores the intersection of sexuality research and queer theory with other anthropological concerns such as identity, race, gender, religion, economy, politics, and globalization.

WS 430.title: Seminar in the Biology of Women

WS 434.title: Women and Madness
WS 434.subject: WS
WS 434.description: Interdisciplinary critical examination of the relationship between gender and mental health. Psychological research, feminist theory, autobiography, literature, and cinema.

WS 435.title: Women and Crime
WS 435.subject: WS
WS 435.description: Women’s relations with the criminal justice system; types of women’s offenses; responses to women’s crime; women as victims; women as workers in the criminal justice system.
WS 435.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent

WS 436.title: Gender, Justice and Law
WS 436.subject: WS
WS 436.description: Exploration of landmark U.S. Supreme Court cases related to sex and gender. Topics may include sex discrimination, sexual orientation discrimination, privacy, and reproductive freedom.

WS 437.title: Gender and Violence
WS 437.subject: WS
WS 437.description: Interdisciplinary course will examine western constructs of gender violence on its correlates with ethnicity, class, sexuality, nation, and empire.

WS 438.title: Gender and Environmental Philosophy
WS 438.subject: WS
WS 438.description: Interdisciplinary approach to women’s perspectives and roles on ecological and environmental issues; critical analysis of eco-feminism as a social and political movement; cross-cultural comparison of women’s roles in human ecology.
WS 438.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or WS or any course 200 or above with a DB or DP designation, or consent

WS 439.title: Feminist Theory
WS 439.subject: WS
WS 439.description: Contemporary debates in feminist theory concerning gender, race, and class; subjectivity and representation; gender and colonialism; bodies, sexualities and “nature.”
WS 439.prereq_raw: any 300 level WS or POLS course, or consent

WS 440.title: Feminist Methods and Research
WS 440.subject: WS
WS 440.description: Overview of feminist issues with dominant theories of knowledge and major methodologies employed in the social sciences; and exploration of role of gender theory and feminist politics in feminist research.

WS 441.title: Queer Theory
WS 441.subject: WS
WS 441.description: Intensive survey of the key theories, texts, and questions of the interdisciplinary fields that make up queer theory.

WS 444.title: Gender and Consumption in a Global World
WS 444.subject: WS
WS 444.description: Students learn theories of the global economy, histories of consumerism, constructions of gendered public spaces, and how the cultural production of consumers and consumer culture functions in the process of globalization.

WS 445.title: U.S. Women’s Literature and Culture
WS 445.subject: WS
WS 445.description: Reading of selected works of U.S. women’s literature and cultural texts (such as art and film). Emphasis on historical and cultural context and diverse expressions of women’s gendered identities.

WS 446.title: Gender Violence Over the Lifecycle
WS 446.subject: WS
WS 446.description: Examines the problem of violence, particularly sexual violence, over the life cycle. Offers gendered perspective in activities aimed at prevention and treatment of violence, and cross cultural perspectives.
WS 446.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, SOC 300; or consent

WS 450.title: Food, Culture, and Empire in U.S. and Hawai‘i
WS 450.subject: WS
WS 450.description: Examines the cultural, historical, and political processes that have informed our understandings and practices involving food. We will analyze food and foodways in the U.S. and Hawai‘i. Junior standing or higher.

children.text: at least one course in WS

WS 452.title: Marriage and Family: Feminist Perspective
WS 452.subject: WS
WS 452.description: Sex-role socialization, motherhood, work-family conflicts. Alternative family structures in U.S. and other countries.
WS 452.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or SOC 300; or consent

WS 453.title: Gender Issues in Education
WS 453.subject: WS
WS 453.description: Examination of current and historical issues in education and how they are impacted upon by gender, with particular reference to gender as it intersects with ethnicity and class, locally and globally.

WS 454.title: Gender, Sexuality, and Global Popular Culture
WS 454.subject: WS
WS 454.description: A study of gender, race, and sexuality as constructed in contemporary global popular culture, including music, films, novels, television shows, and internet culture.

WS 456.title: Politics of Men and Masculinity in U.S. Culture
WS 456.subject: WS
WS 456.description: Examines American understandings of man, manhood, and masculinity, at the intersection of gender, race, class, and sexuality in the context of American nation and empire building in the 19th and 20th centuries.

WS 460.title: Feminism, Nation and Empire
WS 460.subject: WS
WS 460.description: Examines U.S. feminist movements in the 19th and 20th century by exploring how U.S. racism, nationalism and imperialism have provided the context from which feminism emerged.

WS 462.title: Women and Globalization in Asia
WS 462.subject: WS
WS 462.description: History, culture, and contemporary reality of Asian women in Asia and the U.S. Includes critical analysis of American feminist methodology and theory.
WS 462.prereq_raw: 360, 361, or 439 or AMST 310, AMST 316, AMST 318, AMST 373, AMST 455, or POLS 339; or consent

WS 463.title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
WS 463.subject: WS
WS 463.description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g. with class, religion, ethnicity).

WS 465.title: Science, Sex, and Reproduction
WS 465.subject: WS
WS 465.description: Explores anthropology’s critical analysis of approaches to reproductive health and procreation, primarily in developing countries. Examines sex and reproduction as sites of intervention from public health, development, and biomedical specialists, while also considering local strategies. Junior standing or higher.

WS 466.title: Gender in Action Cinema
WS 466.subject: WS
WS 466.description: Investigates gender representation in the evolving genre of American action cinema through combined stylistic and cultural analysis, with special attention to the relationship of gendered action to categories of morality, race, class, and nation. Junior standing or consent.

WS 481.title: Women and Film
WS 481.subject: WS
WS 481.description: Exploration of film as a philosophical and artistic form in the context of gender, race, and sexuality.
WS 481.prereq_raw: one of 151, 175, 176, and THEA 201; or consent

WS 483.title: Studies in Literature and Sexuality and Gender
WS 483.subject: WS

WS 489.title: Social Sciences Internship
WS 489.subject: WS
WS 489.description: Internship in public, private, or non-profit organizations providing opportunity for practical experience and application of social sciences concepts and theories. Three to six credits per semester; Consent of instructor.

WS 492.title: Women and Revolution
WS 492.subject: WS
WS 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons.

WS 493.title: Trans* Studies: Trans(feminine/masculine/ gender nonconforming/sexual)
WS 493.subject: WS
WS 493.description: Focus on various aspects of Trans* identities, biographies, cultural productions, and communities. It also addresses issues on racism, medical intervention, dating, societal condemnation, mental health, and incarceration.

WS 495.title: Selected Topics
WS 495.subject: WS
WS 495.description: Problems and issues for reading and research: feminist theory, criticism, affirmative action, etc.

WS 496.title: Teaching Women’s Studies
WS 496.subject: WS
WS 496.description: Strategies for teaching women’s studies; addressing complex issues of gender, race, nation, class, sexuality and culture in a contemporary multiethnic campus environment. Emphasis on classroom techniques, teaching pedagogies, and hands-on experience.
