WS 602.title: Transnational Feminist Teaching and Research
WS 602.subject: WS
WS 602.description: Introductory graduate seminar designed to develop common vocabulary and explore the core debates in transnational feminist teaching and research to encourage critical reflection about teaching assumptions, approaches, and techniques in the contemporary college or university environment.

WS 610.title: Faculty Seminar Series
WS 610.subject: WS
WS 610.description: Seminar/ discussion to introduce students pursuing the Graduate Certificate to the Woman’s Studies faculty and their areas of research, and to initiate student’s graduate studies in a woman’s studies field.
WS 610.prereq_raw: classified graduate status (or status pending) and consent

WS 612.title: Women in American Culture
WS 612.subject: WS
WS 612.description: Historical/contemporary status of women in the U.S.; women’s roles as defined by legal, educational, political, economic, and social institutions; implications for social science method.

WS 613.title: Feminist Research and Methods of Inquiry
WS 613.subject: WS
WS 613.description: Examination of an emergent body of literature about how to shape questions concerning gender, sex, race, class, colonialism, and other vectors of power. Includes methods from social sciences and humanities and debates in the philosophy of science.

WS 615.title: Feminist Theory
WS 615.subject: WS
WS 615.description: Selected ideas from contemporary feminist theory concerning power, knowledge, and self; articulating women’s voice; deconstructing gender.

WS 618.title: Writing and Publishing in an Interdisciplinary Field
WS 618.subject: WS
WS 618.description: Writing-intensive and publishing-focused class, students learn how to publish in an interdisciplinary field. Readings and assignments are designed to help students succeed in academic publishing. Graduate students only.

WS 620.title: Feminism and Its “Others”
WS 620.subject: WS
WS 620.description: Relationship between feminist and other sites of critical insight and scholarship that have contributed to creating anticolonial, antiracist, antihomophobic theory, method and action. Questions the legacy of feminist coalition practices and engages the ongoing transformations that have begun to produce new alliances and coalitions that disrupt traditional boundaries of identity and power.

WS 623.title: Topics in Feminist Social Policy Research
WS 623.subject: WS
WS 623.description: Feminist social scientists from a variety of fields have explored issues of gender, social change and social justice. Draws from their work to critically examine strategies for conducting social policy research that is feminist in values and impact.

WS 625.title: Feminist Criminology
WS 625.subject: WS
WS 625.description: Key themes in feminist criminology are explored including focus on masculinities and crime, race and intersectionality, global criminology, and the ways in which the criminal justice system controls women and girls.

WS 647.title: Gender: Law and Conflicts
WS 647.subject: WS
WS 647.description: Examines how international law and domestic legal systems address and resolve conflicts regarding women’s rights, gender roles, and gender identity. Takes a comparative approach with emphasis on the Asia-Pacific region.

WS 650.title: Research in Feminist Studies: Capstone Experience
WS 650.subject: WS
WS 650.description: Provide women’s studies graduate certificate students with an opportunity to design, develop and complete a research project culminating in a publishable quality work and a professional quality seminar presentation.

WS 699.title: Directed Reading and Research
WS 699.subject: WS

ACC 200.title: Introduction to Accounting I
ACC 200.subject: ACC
ACC 200.description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part I.

ACC 210.title: Introduction to Accounting II
ACC 210.subject: ACC
ACC 210.description: Introduction to managerial and financial accounting and methods used to record and report managerial and financial information to decision makers internal and external to the firm. Part II.

ACC 321.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting I
ACC 321.subject: ACC
ACC 321.description: Accounting process and the application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of cash, receivables, inventories, property plant and equipment, depreciation and depletion, intangibles, and current liabilities.

ACC 323.title: Intermediate Financial Accounting II
ACC 323.subject: ACC
ACC 323.description: Application of GAAP to the recognition and measurement of long-term liabilities, investments, contributed capital, retained earnings, accounting changes and errors, income recognition, accounting for income taxes, pensions, leases, and statement of cash flows.

ACC 395.title: Accounting Internship
ACC 395.subject: ACC
ACC 395.description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Term paper and meetings with faculty advisor required.

ACC 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
ACC 399.subject: ACC
ACC 399.description: Reading and research of a special area in major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and faculty advisor.

ACC 401.title: Federal Individual Income Taxation
ACC 401.subject: ACC
ACC 401.description: Examines federal income tax concepts, such as gross income, exclusions, deductions, exemptions, and tax credits, especially for sole proprietors. Introduces taxation of property transactions. Development of professional writing skills is integral to this course.
ACC 401.prereq_raw: (201, 202, 210, or BUS 624) with C- or better

ACC 407.title: Taxation of Business Entities
ACC 407.subject: ACC
ACC 407.description: A survey of the general concepts, rules, and practices involved in the taxation of sole-proprietorships, corporations, partnerships, and subchapter S corporations.

ACC 409.title: Accounting Information Systems
ACC 409.subject: ACC
ACC 409.description: Accounting systems analysis, control and design in manual and computerized environments. Knowledge and skills of information technology for auditing AIS systems. Hands-on experience with microcomputers and a computerized accounting system.
ACC 409.prereq_raw: 323 (with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 (with C or better)

children.text: ( with C- or better or concurrent) and BUS 311 ( with C or better )

ACC 413.title: Law for the Accountant
ACC 413.subject: ACC
ACC 413.description: Intensive study of areas of law of importance to accountants. Particular attention is given to principles of law relating to contracts, sales, commercial paper, secured transactions, property, legal entities, agency, securities, and accountant’s legal liability.

ACC 415.title: Advanced Financial Accounting
ACC 415.subject: ACC
ACC 415.description: Accounting topics relating to consolidation requirements and introduction to the fundamentals of fund accounting, including the general fund, restricted funds, debt service funds, enterprise funds, general long-term account group, general fixed assets accounting group, and accounting entries for encumbrances.

ACC 416.title: Special Topics in Accounting
ACC 416.subject: ACC
ACC 416.description: Addresses current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

ACC 418.title: Auditing
ACC 418.subject: ACC
ACC 418.description: Auditing concepts including standards, objectives and ethics for external auditors. Emphasis on reporting standards, internal control, evidence, statistical sampling, IT audits and assurance. Development of professional writing skills is an integral part of this course.
ACC 418.prereq_raw: 323 and 409, both with C- or better

ACC 425.title: Forensic Accounting
ACC 425.subject: ACC
ACC 425.description: Theoretical and real life aspects of forensic accounting. Includes discussions of the legal environment, types of forensic engagements such as, lost earnings, business valuations, fraud, and real world forensic cases.

ACC 460.title: Accounting Capstone
ACC 460.subject: ACC
ACC 460.description: Lectures, discussions, case analysis. Integration of numerous elements of the accounting program. Current accounting issues discussed. Relevant topics for (B) managerial; (C) financial, (D) auditing and accounting information systems; (E) tax and ethics. Together with 460B, 460E, includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.
ACC 460.prereq_raw: 418 (or concurrent), no waiver for (B), (C), (D); 401 and 418 (or concurrent, no waiver for (E)
ACC 460.coreq_raw: E for (B); D for (C); C for (D); and B for (E)

ACC 602.subject: ACC

ACC 603.title: CPA Review-The Business Environment and Concepts
ACC 603.subject: ACC

ACC 604.title: CPA Review-The Financial Accounting and Reporting
ACC 604.subject: ACC
ACC 604.description: The (FAR) section focuses on U.S. GAAP, including concepts and standards for financial statements, typical items in financial statements, specific types of transactions and events, accounting and reporting for governmental and other entities.

ACC 605.title: CPA Review-The Regulation
ACC 605.subject: ACC
ACC 605.description: The Regulation section focuses on federal taxation, especially taxation of business entities; individuals, and property taxation, but also tests on business law, business ethics, and professional and legal responsibilities.

ACC 610.title: International Corporate Governance
ACC 610.subject: ACC
ACC 610.description: Understanding of complex and critical issues of international corporate governance, financial reporting, and ethical conduct. Includes corporate governance in the U.S., major European markets, and Asia. Emphasis on internal and external stakeholders, regulators, and gatekeepers. Graduate students only.

ACC 616.title: Accounting Theory and Development
ACC 616.subject: ACC
ACC 616.description: History and theoretical background of accounting standards. Including accounting theories, formulating and testing theories; scientific, pragmatic, syntactic and semantic theories; normative and positive theories. Literature supportive and critical of accounting theories and standards.
ACC 616.prereq_raw: 323 or 582 with C- or better, or consent

ACC 619.title: Information and Assurance and Analytics
ACC 619.subject: ACC
ACC 619.description: Focus on auditing processes, standards, and guidance specific to IT risks. Exposure to advanced IT audit software and its practical application and real world IT audit issues.
ACC 619.prereq_raw: 418 or 585 with C- or better, or consent

ACC 620.title: Global Accounting
ACC 620.subject: ACC
ACC 620.description: Theory and fundamental causes of international variations in accounting. Special emphasis on problems such variations create for financial reporting, control, and decision-making within multinational business enterprises.
ACC 620.prereq_raw: 323 or 582 with C- or better, or consent

ACC 625.title: Accounting and Tax Research
ACC 625.subject: ACC
ACC 625.description: In depth examination of tax and accounting research, IRC, and SEC procedures. Extensive practice in issue identification, reading and analyzing primary authority, and communicating results. Credit not given for both 606 and 625.
ACC 625.prereq_raw: 401 or 584 with C- or better, orientation program, or consent

ACC 631.title: Tax of Partners/Partnerships
ACC 631.subject: ACC
ACC 631.description: Examines advanced topics in federal taxation of partners and partnerships regarding the contribution, operation, and distribution from partnerships and transfers of partnership interests.

ACC 635.title: Advanced Public Sector Accounting
ACC 635.subject: ACC
ACC 635.description: Provides the tools necessary for understanding the principles of fiscal accountability and reporting in governmental and not-for-profit organizations.
ACC 635.prereq_raw: 415 or 582 with C- or better, or consent

ACC 638.title: Estate and Gift Taxation and Planning
ACC 638.subject: ACC

ACC 638.prereq_raw: 401 or 584 with C- or better, or consent

ACC 639.title: Multijurisdictional Taxation
ACC 639.subject: ACC
ACC 639.description: Examines international, state, and local tax issues. Topics include U.S. International taxation of in- and out-bound transactions, sourcing of income and deductions and nexus.

ACC 648.title: Financial Statements Analysis
ACC 648.subject: ACC
ACC 648.description: Analyses of a firm’s profitability, liquidity, and solvency using ratios and common size financial statements. Students are expected to find strengths and weaknesses of the firm based on their analysis.

ACC 649.title: Data Analytics for Accountants
ACC 649.subject: ACC
ACC 649.description: Introduction to visual analytics. Tableau and Power BI for Excel. Introduction to data processing and blending, data visualization and other visualization techniques. Introduction to PowerQuery, PowerPivot, PowerView, and PowerMap.

ACC 660.title: Analysis and Decision-Making
ACC 660.subject: ACC
ACC 660.description: Integrates learning through analysis and communication of comprehensive business problems. Stresses research, critical thinking, and analytical and communication skills applied to contemporary accounting and tax issues.
ACC 660.prereq_raw: 415 or 625 with C- or better (or concurrent), no waiver

ACC 690.title: Current Topics in Accounting
ACC 690.subject: ACC
ACC 690.description: Concentration on current issues impacting the accounting profession. Topics vary each semester.

ACC 695.description: On-the-job experience in the accounting community. Necessary evaluation reports and meetings with faculty advisor required.

BUS 099.title: International Exchange Study/Research
BUS 099.subject: BUS
BUS 099.description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.

BUS 102.title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
BUS 102.subject: BUS
BUS 102.description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors. Freshmen only.

BUS 200.title: Introduction to Business
BUS 200.subject: BUS
BUS 200.description: Introduction to each of the functional areas of business. Intends to help students understand the interrelationships of business functional areas and the role of business in society. Stresses written communication in business. Freshman or sophomore standing only.

BUS 209.title: Written Communication in Business
BUS 209.subject: BUS
BUS 209.description: An interactive writing class stressing persuasive writing in the context of memos, letters, and business reports.

children.text: Students may not earn credit for both BUS 209 and ENG 209

BUS 250.description: Provides problem-solving and quantitative skills essential in business. Reviews algebra, mathematics of finance, calculus in business applications, probability, introductory statistics, and hypothesis testing.

BUS 313.title: Economic and Financial Environment of Global Business
BUS 313.subject: BUS
BUS 313.description: International trade, financial flows, and direct investment. Public and private institutions including government policies and capital markets. Emphasis on Asia Pacific issues, with attention to the cultural differences among countries.

BUS 314.title: Business Finance
BUS 314.subject: BUS
BUS 314.description: Introduction to the theory and practice of financial management: analysis and decision making for asset management, capital budgeting, capital structure, and dividend policy. Prerequisite for all other finance courses.
BUS 314.prereq_raw: ACC 200 and ACC 210, ECON 130 and ECON 131; or consent

BUS 315.title: Global Management and Organizational Behavior

MGT 341.title: Behavior in Organizations

MGT 341.description: Contributions made by sociology, psychology, and related behavioral sciences to the understanding and prediction of human behavior in organizations.

MGT 342.title: Multinational Business Management
MGT 342.subject: MGT
MGT 342.description: Introduction to the unique problems and challenges in managing multinational business enterprises. Systems approach to the management process in such multinational firms stressed.

MGT 343.title: Comparative Management Systems: United States and Japan
MGT 343.subject: MGT
MGT 343.description: Similarities and differences in managers, in process of management, and in relevant environmental constraints in Japan and the U.S.

MGT 344.title: Seminar in Management
MGT 344.subject: MGT
MGT 344.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration. May be repeated with change in topic.

MGT 345.title: Entrepreneurial Ventures
MGT 345.subject: MGT
MGT 345.description: Integrative course in entrepreneurship designed around the development of an original business concept and the completion of a comprehensive business plan for a new venture. Intended as final course for students completing entrepreneurship minor.

MGT 348.title: History of American Business
MGT 348.subject: MGT
MGT 348.description: The evolution of business enterprise from colonial times to the present. Emphasis on entrepreneurship, technological change, labor-management relations, government-business relations, and economic thought. Case studies of industrial development.

MGT 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MGT 399.subject: MGT

MGT 450.title: Family Business
MGT 450.subject: MGT
MGT 450.description: The exploration of business, personal, and interpersonal issues associated with a family owned and managed company. Topics include: family psychology and organizational structure, life cycles in family business, strategic family and business planning, succession planning, family business conflict resolution, estate planning, the role of professional managers, and others. This is not a course about how to become an entrepreneur or how to start or manage a business. It is most appropriate for those students who are part of a family that owns and manages a business.

MGT 460.title: Asia Pacific Business Systems

MGT 461.title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
MGT 461.subject: MGT
MGT 461.description: Exploration of the nature and role of entrepreneurship behavior inside larger, established organizations. An examination of obstacles to entrepreneurial activity and approaches to creating work environments that foster entrepreneurship.

MGT 644.title: Comparative Management
MGT 644.subject: MGT
MGT 644.description: Cross-cultural analysis of the values and environmental constraints that shape management patterns and policies. Emphasis on Pacific area nations. MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 645.title: New Venture Management
MGT 645.subject: MGT
MGT 645.description: Technical aspects of entrepreneurship, components and requirements for developing a business plan.

MGT 648.title: International Business: Environment and Enterprise
MGT 648.subject: MGT
MGT 648.description: Survey of the environment of international business with theory and policy focusing on strategic planning, international management and operational issues confronting the multinational corporations in the global environment. MBA or MAcc students only.

MGT 650.title: Management Topics
MGT 650.subject: MGT
MGT 650.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in administration. May be repeated four times with change in topic.

MGT 651.title: Corporate Entrepreneurship
MGT 651.subject: MGT
MGT 651.description: Entrepreneurship behavior involving the founding of new business units within established companies; understanding and dealing with barriers to entrepreneurship in corporations; recognizing corporate entrepreneurship opportunities; and learning various approaches organizations can take to increase entrepreneurship.

MGT 660.title: Negotiation
MGT 660.subject: MGT
MGT 660.description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

MGT 671.title: International Strategic Management
MGT 671.subject: MGT
MGT 671.description: Analysis of the strategic management of firms engaged in multinational business including specific content on Asia. Permits students to focus on specific countries such as China and Japan.

MGT 680.title: Entrepreneurship for Science and Technology
MGT 680.subject: MGT
MGT 680.description: Recognizing and screening technology opportunities, the commercialization process, intellectual property acquisition, business model related to high technology strategies needed for growth in high tech firms.

MGT 681.title: Asian/Pacific Entrepreneurship
MGT 681.subject: MGT
MGT 681.description: Innovative ventures, issues related to noticing opportunities, conceptualizing and developing a business model, starting and growing a new venture with specific emphasis on the Asian/Pacific region.

MGT 688.title: Health Policy, Systems, and the Legal Environment
MGT 688.subject: MGT
MGT 688.description: Covers health care policy topics including: analyzing health service needs, access, use, disparities; health professional supply; policy issues for health organizations; health care financing policy; health law/ethical issues.

MGT 701.title: Cross-Cultural Management
MGT 701.subject: MGT
MGT 701.description: Provides tools to compare and contrast management practices across nations and to examine the role of culture in shaping those practices.

HRM 351.title: Human Resource Management

HRM 354.title: Organizational Change and Effectiveness

HRM 354.description: Identify and evaluate methods to promote an effective change transition through efficient integration of corporate goals with the organizational culture.

HRM 361.title: Labor Problems

HRM 399.title: Directed Reading and Research

HRM 453.title: Personnel Compensation
HRM 453.subject: HRM
HRM 453.description: Selected topics. Emphasis on trends, recent issues, job evaluation, incentive systems, salary administration, executive compensation, profit sharing, benefit programs, retirement plans.

HRM 455.title: The Staffing Process
HRM 455.subject: HRM
HRM 455.description: Contemporary practices and trends in personnel planning for a competent work force; legal constraints, recruitment and selection, differential placement, training, career programming.

HRM 463.subject: HRM

HRM 467.title: Labor Management Relations
HRM 467.subject: HRM
HRM 467.description: Review and analysis of basic factors that distinguish employment relations; examination of the development of recent legislation and programs at federal, state, and municipal levels. Specific consideration given to current problems on the mainland and Hawai‘i.

HRM 468.title: Training and Development
HRM 468.subject: HRM
HRM 468.description: Analysis of the current concepts and practices in the design, delivery, and assessment of training.

HRM 469.title: Seminar in HRM
HRM 469.subject: HRM
HRM 469.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in HRM.

HRM 671.title: Human Resource Management
HRM 671.subject: HRM
HRM 671.description: Analysis and critical evaluation of basic issues, policies, and trends in personnel administration. Graduate students only.

HRM 672.title: Training and Development
HRM 672.subject: HRM
HRM 672.description: Covers issues in design, delivery, and assessment of training, theoretical background of training and development process, types of training process, cross cultural and other types of diversity training and development of training modules. Graduate students only.

HRM 673.title: Advanced Organizational Behavior
HRM 673.subject: HRM
HRM 673.description: Organizational development (OD) and major concepts in organizational behavior.

HRM 674.title: Finance for Human Resource Management
HRM 674.subject: HRM
HRM 674.description: Intends to give HR professionals a basic overview of the vocabulary and concepts of financial decision-making. Topics include: understanding financial information, budgeting, the finance of retirement and employee benefit and business valuation.

HRM 675.title: Compensation
HRM 675.subject: HRM
HRM 675.description: Survey of compensation methods and procedures including job evaluations, incentive systems, salary administration, fringe benefits, appropriate legislation, policies and strategy issues of compensation systems. Graduate students only.

HRM 676.title: The Staffing Process
HRM 676.subject: HRM
HRM 676.description: Recruiting and selection to optimize organizations including job design, job analysis, recruitment and selection methods, such as types of interviews and assessment centers, within legislative environment. Graduate students only.

HRM 677.title: Negotiations and Labor Relations
HRM 677.subject: HRM
HRM 677.description: Theory and practice of negotiation. Exploration of appropriate strategies, tactics, and communication techniques. Study of dyadic multi-party, cross-cultural, and assisted negotiations.

HRM 678.title: International Human Resources
HRM 678.subject: HRM
HRM 678.description: Exploring global trends in human resources with focus on the Asia Pacific region. Graduate students only.

HRM 679.title: Human Resource Management-Topics
HRM 679.subject: HRM
HRM 679.description: In-depth analysis of selected current practices and trends in human resources.

HRM 680.title: Human Resource Management Capstone
HRM 680.subject: HRM
HRM 680.description: The final course in the MHRM curriculum. It provides students opportunity to integrate and apply previous course content to their professional organization offering a value-added opportunity to enhance organizational performance.

HRM 688.title: Human Resources Leadership in Healthcare Organizations
HRM 688.subject: HRM
HRM 688.description: Builds on previous leadership and management courses, focus on development of individual leadership skills emphasizing ethical and critical decision making, effective working relationships, and a systems-perspective relevant to healthcare organizations.

MKT 311.title: Consumer Behavior
MKT 311.subject: MKT
MKT 311.description: Analysis of consumer behavior and motivation; principles of learning, personality, perception, and group influence, with emphasis upon mass communication effects.

MKT 321.title: Marketing Research and Data Analytics
MKT 321.subject: MKT
MKT 321.description: Use of marketing research and marketing management and data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: the research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; and digital media analytics.

MKT 331.title: Marketing Communications
MKT 331.subject: MKT
MKT 331.description: In-depth coverage of the major communication tools used in marketing such as advertising, sales promotion, public relations and the internet. Emphasis on integrated marketing communications.

MKT 332.title: Integrated Communication Campaigns
MKT 332.subject: MKT
MKT 332.description: Management of integrated marketing communications campaigns. Includes: conducting target market and competitor research, developing creative content and media strategies, production of communication materials and completion of major real world project.

MKT 341.title: Retailing Management
MKT 341.subject: MKT
MKT 341.description: Principles, functions, and analysis of opportunities and problems in retailing: location and layout; merchandise planning; buying and selling; organizational forms and design; expense analysis and control; coordination of store activities.

MKT 351.title: Professional Selling
MKT 351.subject: MKT
MKT 351.description: Emphasis on selling technique, social-psychological principles of persuasion, and interpersonal communication. Lecture, discussion, and application of relevant principles and techniques.

MKT 352.title: Sales and Sales Management
MKT 352.subject: MKT
MKT 352.description: Delves into selling and the sales management process. Through a variety of activities, students experience applying selling techniques, sales planning, recruiting and training salespeople, methods of motivating and compensating, territory management and sales team communications.

MKT 361.title: Seminar in Marketing
MKT 361.subject: MKT
MKT 361.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in the field of marketing. May be repeated four times with change in topic.

MKT 362.title: Digital Marketing
MKT 362.subject: MKT
MKT 362.description: Provides comprehensive understanding of digital marketing’s growing role in new product development; marketing research; direct sales; and marketing communications. Students learn multiple digital tools for analysis of customer behavior. Real-world projects provide opportunities for application.

MKT 363.title: Customer Relationship Management
MKT 363.subject: MKT
MKT 363.description: Focuses on the evolving field of customer relationship management. Students learn how to manage marketing information and decision-making systems that maximize customer retention and build long-term relationships.

MKT 368.title: Sustainable Marketing
MKT 368.subject: MKT
MKT 368.description: Provides environmental knowledge and managerial tools that help for profit and not-for-profit organizations address pressing issues like global warming, plastic pollution, and fair trade while earning surplus revenue and remaining socially accountable.

MKT 372.title: Marketing for New Ventures
MKT 372.subject: MKT
MKT 372.description: Examines role of marketing in the formation and launch of entrepreneurial ventures within and outside of ongoing businesses. Emphasis on new product development and low cost, high impact marketing activities.

MKT 381.title: International Marketing
MKT 381.subject: MKT
MKT 381.description: Principles and topics related to international marketing, with emphasis on strategic planning and applications.

MKT 391.title: Marketing Strategies
MKT 391.subject: MKT
MKT 391.description: Decision-making by the marketing executive; integration of all elements of the marketing program based on actual business situations.

MKT 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MKT 399.subject: MKT
MKT 399.description: Reading and research in a special area of major under direction of faculty member(s). Project must include statement of objectives, outline of activities planned, results expected, and how they are to be reported and evaluated. Must be approved in advance by the department chair and the faculty advisor.

MKT 410.title: Software Tools in Marketing
MKT 410.subject: MKT
MKT 410.description: Focuses on computer software tools designed to help managers make more informed marketing decisions. Through hands-on experience, students learn software skills useful in marketing management, marketing research, sales and advertising.

MKT 411B.title: Imagination, Entrepreneurship and Business Problem-Solving
MKT 411B.subject: MKT
MKT 411B.description: Application of creative process to problems encountered in venture creation/growth. Student problem-solving styles are characterized and implications drawn for generation of breakthrough ideas. Tools for facilitating creative solutions to marketing problems are investigated.

MKT 648.title: Consumer Behavior and Satisfaction Management
MKT 648.subject: MKT
MKT 648.description: Designed to help students better understand how consumers process information, form attitudes, and make decisions. Draws on theories from social sciences to help students manage consumer needs and satisfaction. Graduate students only.

MKT 650.title: Sales Leadership
MKT 650.subject: MKT
MKT 650.description: Sales managers participate in diverse activities including hiring, designing and implementing training programs, in-field coaching and development, motivating and compensating employees, and team building. Helps students develop knowledge and skills in these areas. Graduate students only.

MKT 651.title: Advanced Marketing Management
MKT 651.subject: MKT
MKT 651.description: A case course in the application of advanced marketing methods.

MKT 652.title: Japanese Marketing Systems
MKT 652.subject: MKT
MKT 652.description: Specialized study of Japanese marketing systems, considers both global and domestic marketing activities in the context of the Japanese economy.

MKT 653.title: International Marketing Management
MKT 653.subject: MKT
MKT 653.description: Integrated and comparative approach to international marketing management. Emphasis on the development of a competitive strategy in a global environment. Applications to both developing and industrialized markets.

MKT 654.title: Strategic Brand Management and Marketing Communications
MKT 654.subject: MKT
MKT 654.description: The study of brands and strategic brand management with emphasis on developing integrated advertising, sales promotion, public relations, and internet communication strategies that build brand equity. Includes relevant theory and real world applications.

MKT 655.title: Marketing Research Management
MKT 655.subject: MKT
MKT 655.description: Examines use of marketing research/data analytics to support marketing management. Topics include: research process; survey design; sampling; measurement; primary data analysis; customer data analytics; digital media analytics. Real world project reinforce learning.

MKT 656.title: Creativity in Marketing
MKT 656.subject: MKT
MKT 656.description: Thought processes that relate to creativity. Through a series of exercises, students experience enriched creativity and enhanced communication skills.

MKT 657.title: Services Marketing
MKT 657.subject: MKT
MKT 657.description: Conceptual understanding of distinctive aspects of services, services management, and services research.

MKT 658.title: Digital Marketing Management
MKT 658.subject: MKT
MKT 658.description: Examines digital marketing’s role in new product development; direct sales; marketing communications via the internet, social media, and mobile devices; and digital tools such as online tracking and analysis. Real activities provide opportunities for application.

MKT 688.title: Patient Centered Communication Management in Health Care Organizations
MKT 688.subject: MKT
MKT 688.description: Provides training on managing patient communications in general and shared decision making in particular. Increases ability to use tools available to improve patient-provider decision making quality and satisfaction.

MKT 701.title: Seminar in Marketing Theory
MKT 701.subject: MKT
MKT 701.description: Focuses on the building blocks of theory, their use, and evolution within a marketing context. Explores marketing theories, theory construction, and the creation of marketing knowledge.

FDM 101.title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry

FDM 200.title: Culture, Gender, and Appearance
FDM 200.subject: FDM

FDM 205.title: Basic Apparel Construction
FDM 205.subject: FDM
FDM 205.description: Principles, concepts, and procedures for quality construction and custom fitting of clothing.

FDM 210.title: Western World Fashion History

FDM 215.title: Block Pattern Designing

FDM 216.title: Fashion Illustration

FDM 221.title: Textiles I

FDM 269.title: Costumes/Cultures of East Asia
FDM 269.subject: FDM
FDM 269.description: Development of traditional dress as visual manifestation of culture. Ethnic and national dress of China, Japan, Korea, Mongolia, Okinawa, Tibet, and Vietnam.

FDM 301.subject: FDM
FDM 301.description: Principles and practices in fashion trend forecasting and their role in apparel company marketing strategies. Analysis of aesthetics as it related to apparel and marketing. Adapting fashion trend forecasts to apparel lines.

FDM 315.title: Draping
FDM 315.subject: FDM
FDM 315.description: Principles of pattern making through draping muslin models on standard garment forms.

FDM 316.title: Advanced Specialty Design
FDM 316.subject: FDM
FDM 316.description: Advanced study in the specialty market design, pattern making, and construction for fashion design majors. Different specialty designs, such as swimwear, menswear, or others, will be offered each semester.

FDM 321.title: Textiles Quality Assurance
FDM 321.subject: FDM
FDM 321.description: Chemical nature and structure of fibers and fabrics, their properties and finishes.

FDM 321L.title: Textiles Quality Assurance Laboratory
FDM 321L.subject: FDM
FDM 321L.description: Examination of textile properties through standardized textiles testing laboratory equipment.

FDM 330.title: Advanced Apparel Construction
FDM 330.subject: FDM
FDM 330.description: Principles of advanced techniques for garment construction with emphasis on new, difficult-to-handle fabrics.

FDM 338.title: 2D/3D Computer Aided Design
FDM 338.subject: FDM
FDM 338.description: Exploration of CAD applications from the design to the pattern-making process. Use of Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop for fashion illustration. Use of OptiTex PDS pattern design software featuring 2D and 3D CAD.

FDM 339.title: 3D Retail Store Design
FDM 339.subject: FDM
FDM 339.description: Visual merchandising concepts and planning; use of a virtual 3D store modeling software package. Visual Retailing/ Mockshop, to design store interiors, fixtures, lighting, signage, window displays, and planograms.

FDM 340.title: Computerized Pattern Grading
FDM 340.subject: FDM
FDM 340.description: Gerber Technology (GT) AccuMark System Management. The system is designed to use CAD for specific apparel industry applications in grading patterns into different sizes and making production markers.

FDM 350.title: Embellishments
FDM 350.subject: FDM
FDM 350.description: Emphasis on design principles as applied to stitchery using a variety of techniques and raw materials. Processes and problems experienced and critiqued in a group environment.

FDM 360.title: Writing for the Fashion Industry
FDM 360.subject: FDM
FDM 360.description: Analysis and creation of different types of writing in the fashion industry, with emphasis on creating a professional writing style.

FDM 371.title: Retail Buying and Merchandising
FDM 371.subject: FDM
FDM 371.description: Theories and procedures in selecting, buying and selling apparel and textiles. Types of merchandising organizations, analysis of consumer demand, brick-and-click opportunities and challenges, development of an image, operation location, store and floor layout.

FDM 375.title: Merchandise Planning and Control
FDM 375.subject: FDM
FDM 375.description: Theories, problems, and procedures of financial and assortment planning and control of merchandise inventories. FDM majors and merchandising minors only.

FDM 411.title: Product Lifecycle Management
FDM 411.subject: FDM
FDM 411.description: Application of principles of apparel production management, including methods engineering (detail construction for ordering), story boards and color tables, production measurements, costing, and PLM computer applications.

FDM 418.title: Costumes of South and Southeast Asia
FDM 418.subject: FDM
FDM 418.description: Development of traditional dress as visual manifestation of culture. Ethnic and national dress of Afghanistan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Pakistan, Philippines, Thailand and Saudi Arabia.

FDM 419.title: Apparel Design Studio I
FDM 419.subject: FDM
FDM 419.description: Development of independent expression through creative designing for a ready-to-wear collection. Problem solving in the design process; includes sketching, draping, blocking, muslin proofs, complete garments, and portfolio. Studio courses must be taken in sequence.

FDM 430.title: Fashion Show Production

FDM 471.description: Theories, concepts, problems of international trade of textile and apparel products. Issues of importing and exporting apparel products globally. Social, political and economic factors affecting textile and apparel trade.

FDM 491.title: Topics in Fashion
FDM 491.subject: FDM
FDM 491.description: Study and discussion of special topics, problems. Offered by staff and visiting faculty.

FDM 492.title: Internship
FDM 492.subject: FDM
FDM 492.description: Examination of issues and opportunities associated with careers in fashion and related businesses and industries. Topics include interpersonal skills development, job search and interview strategies, and ethical issues in the workplace. Junior standing or higher.

FDM 495.title: Capstone Portfolio
FDM 495.subject: FDM
FDM 495.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

FDM 496.title: Field Study in the Fashion Industry
FDM 496.subject: FDM
FDM 496.description: Study tours to various centers of the world to examine historical and modern apparel and textiles. Merchandising and design methods and operations examined.

HDFS 230.title: Human Development

HDFS 331.title: Infancy and Early Childhood

HDFS 332.title: Childhood
HDFS 332.subject: HDFS

HDFS 333.title: Adolescence and Early Adulthood
HDFS 333.subject: HDFS
HDFS 333.description: Problems, concepts, and research related to development from puberty through early adulthood. Examination of biological, cognitive, social, and cultural factors affecting the individual.

HDFS 334.title: Middle Age and Aging
HDFS 334.subject: HDFS
HDFS 334.description: Change and continuity in midlife and late life from theoretical and applied perspectives. Coverage of physical and psychological events as well as social attitudes, values, and programs regarding aging.

HDFS 340.title: Intimacy, Marriages and Families
HDFS 340.subject: HDFS
HDFS 340.description: Study of intimate relationships, marriages and families, their dynamics, strengths, growth and development, challenges, choices and opportunities, in the context of social change and cultural diversity.
HDFS 340.prereq_raw: 230 or PSY 100 or SOC 100; or consent

HDFS 341.title: Parenting
HDFS 341.subject: HDFS
HDFS 341.description: Parenting theories, methods, skills, issues, and resources; parent-child relations in various cultural contexts.

HDFS 350.title: Leadership and Group Process
HDFS 350.subject: HDFS
HDFS 350.description: Exploration of leadership research and theories and their application to leadership development; designed to enhance personal and interactive leadership.

HDFS 352.title: Community Needs and Resources
HDFS 352.subject: HDFS
HDFS 352.description: Theory and practice in determining community needs and resources; community resources development based on needs identification.

HDFS 360.title: Family Resource Management
HDFS 360.subject: HDFS
HDFS 360.description: Concepts, principles, and practices in managing family and household resources.

HDFS 361.title: Family Financial Planning
HDFS 361.subject: HDFS
HDFS 361.description: Analytical approach to family financial planning from the perspective of changing family demands over the life cycle.
HDFS 361.prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

HDFS 363.title: Consumer Economics
HDFS 363.subject: HDFS
HDFS 363.description: Consumer rights, responsibilities, and resources; consumer decision-making; factors affecting consumer functioning within economy.
HDFS 363.prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

HDFS 365.title: Soft Skills for Success in the Workplace
HDFS 365.subject: HDFS
HDFS 365.description: Employers regard soft skills as a key criteria when hiring and retaining employees. Students learn critical skills essential to work place success. This class prepares students to be work ready.

HDFS 380.title: Research Methodology
HDFS 380.subject: HDFS
HDFS 380.description: Fundamentals of scientific methodology and techniques in design and data collection; introduction to statistics for decision-making and program evaluations in agriculture and human resources. FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.
HDFS 380.prereq_raw: 230 or FDM 200 or TPSS 200/SUST 211, or consent

HDFS 380L.title: Research Methodology Lab
HDFS 380L.subject: HDFS
HDFS 380L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Test design, computer use, data analysis. FDM, HDFS, or TPSS majors only.

HDFS 425.title: Partnerships with Families and Professionals
HDFS 425.subject: HDFS
HDFS 425.description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, prepares students for direct, educational work with parents and children and for continued graduate work in child and family studies, counseling, psychology, social work and/or family life education.

HDFS 435.title: Mindfulness and Skillful Living
HDFS 435.subject: HDFS
HDFS 435.description: Lecture, discussion, experiential activities of principles and practice of an evidence-based contemplative science discipline, including applications to daily life and with youth and families.

HDFS 442.title: Marriage Development
HDFS 442.subject: HDFS
HDFS 442.description: Marital interaction and development; divorce and remarriage; resources and techniques for marital adjustment, enrichment, and growth.

HDFS 444.title: Contemporary Family Issues
HDFS 444.subject: HDFS
HDFS 444.description: Investigation of current issues with impact upon family quality of life, with emphasis on the interdependent nature of families and their environments.

HDFS 445.title: Family Life Education Methodology
HDFS 445.subject: HDFS
HDFS 445.description: Lecture, discussion and hands-on course, with service learning on Family Life Education Methodology.

HDFS 452.title: Community Program Development
HDFS 452.subject: HDFS
HDFS 452.description: Concepts and theories of community program development; principles, practices, and procedures in administration and supervision of volunteer services surveyed and analyzed.

HDFS 454.title: Family Public Policy
HDFS 454.subject: HDFS
HDFS 454.description: Cross-national survey of family public policy; analysis, revision, and development of family public policy; impacts of policy on consumers and families.

HDFS 455.title: Consumer Communications
HDFS 455.subject: HDFS
HDFS 455.description: Development, production, analysis, and evaluation of consumer materials for print media. Use of desktop publishing computer programs.
HDFS 455.prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

HDFS 468.title: Family Economics
HDFS 468.subject: HDFS
HDFS 468.description: Study of personal family resources and its interaction with the economy. Focuses on contemporary economic problems that affect the welfare of families.
HDFS 468.prereq_raw: 360 or an ECON course, or consent

HDFS 491.title: Topics in Family Resources
HDFS 491.subject: HDFS
HDFS 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

HDFS 492.title: Internship
HDFS 492.subject: HDFS
HDFS 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills in supervised work at an approved internship site and through analytical writing assignments and class discussions.

HDFS 495.title: Capstone Portfolio
HDFS 495.subject: HDFS
HDFS 495.description: Preparation of a senior portfolio to be used as assessment of competence relative to national FCS standards. Includes extensive instruction on writing.

HDFS 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
HDFS 499.subject: HDFS
HDFS 499.description: Independent reading and research on a topic, done under supervision of a faculty member; outcomes contracted in writing with faculty member at beginning of semester.

ANSC 200.title: Humans, Animals, and Agriculture
ANSC 200.subject: ANSC
ANSC 200.description: Introduction to animal agriculture, animal science, and the use of animals by humans. Ethics and importance of human use of animals in agriculture are emphasized.

ANSC 201.title: Principles and Practices of Animal Science
ANSC 201.subject: ANSC
ANSC 201.description: Biology, behavior, and management of animals of economic and social importance. Topics include physiology, genetics, nutrition, reproduction, behavior, care, and management to achieve productivity, performance, and welfare. (lecture, discussion, and field trips)

ANSC 244.title: Comparative Nutrition
ANSC 244.subject: ANSC
ANSC 244.description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.

ANSC 301.title: Anatomy of Domestic Animals
ANSC 301.subject: ANSC
ANSC 301.description: Micro and gross anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.

ANSC 301L.title: Domestic Animal Anatomy Laboratory
ANSC 301L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 301L.description: Laboratory to accompany 301. Dissection and identification of anatomical arrangements of tissues and organ systems of domestic animals.

ANSC 321.title: Applied Animal Nutrition
ANSC 321.subject: ANSC
ANSC 321.description: Application of the principles of nutrition to feeding of farm animals; composition and nutritional value of feed stuffs; nutritional requirements of beef cattle, dairy cattle, horses, poultry, and swine.

ANSC 350.title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
ANSC 350.subject: ANSC
ANSC 350.description: Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.

ANSC 353.title: Horses and Horsemanship
ANSC 353.subject: ANSC
ANSC 353.description: Origin of species, breeds, nutrition, care, management. Lab on management practices with work on light horses.

ANSC 431.title: Beef Production
ANSC 431.subject: ANSC
ANSC 431.description: Principles of economic beef production, including beef breeds, selection, breeding, management systems, feeding, and marketing under tropical conditions.

ANSC 432.title: Swine Production
ANSC 432.subject: ANSC
ANSC 432.description: Principles of efficient pork production, including comparative breed evaluation, breeding, feeding, management, marketing, and business aspects. Problems and practices associated with tropical environment emphasized.

ANSC 433.title: Tropical Dairying
ANSC 433.subject: ANSC
ANSC 433.description: Principles involved in economical milk production in the tropics, including management, recordkeeping, breeds, breeding, selection, culling, feeding, housing, milking, quality control, and raising young animals.

ANSC 445.title: Genetics and Animal Breeding
ANSC 445.subject: ANSC
ANSC 445.description: Review and application of genetic principles to livestock, poultry, companion, aquatic, and laboratory research animals. Current practices and future developments.
ANSC 445.prereq_raw: BIOL 171/L or ZOOL 101/L, and MATH 140 or higher. Recommended:biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

children.text: / L or ZOOL 101 / L, and MATH 140 or higher . Recommended:biochemistry and genetics or equivalent

ANSC 446.title: Genes and Animal Biology
ANSC 446.subject: ANSC
ANSC 446.description: An understanding of animal biology at the level of genes and their regulations; emphasis on gene structure, recombinant DNA, transgenic animals and functional genomics being used for agricultural, nutritional and biomedical sciences. Open to nonmajors.

ANSC 450.title: Aquaculture Production
ANSC 450.subject: ANSC
ANSC 450.description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
ANSC 450.prereq_raw: 321 and 445: or BIOL 172/L and CHEM 162/L or higher

children.text: : or BIOL 172 / L and CHEM 162 / L or higher

ANSC 451.title: Physiology of Domestic Animals
ANSC 451.subject: ANSC
ANSC 451.description: Functions and relationships of organs and organ systems of domestic animals excluding reproduction and lactation. Problem-based learning and case studies are emphasized.

ANSC 453.title: Animal Diseases and Their Control
ANSC 453.subject: ANSC
ANSC 453.description: Disease problems of livestock, poultry, and companion animals; their economic significance, causes, public health implications, and control.

ANSC 454.title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology
ANSC 454.subject: ANSC
ANSC 454.description: Development, growth, function, carcass evaluation of muscle tissue.

ANSC 454L.title: Meat Science and Muscle Biology Lab
ANSC 454L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 454L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Livestock and poultry slaughter, carcass evaluation, meat chemistry, muscle physiology and biochemistry, meat microbiology, and meat processing.

ANSC 455.title: Companion Animals and Society
ANSC 455.subject: ANSC
ANSC 455.description: Explore human and companion animal relationships in biological, social, cultural, economic, legal, health, and welfare contexts to prepare students for careers in the various animal-related fields in Hawai‘i, the Pacific rim, and worldwide.

ANSC 460.title: Biology and Culture of Shrimp and Prawns
ANSC 460.subject: ANSC
ANSC 460.description: Aspects of the biology and culture of the freshwater prawn Macrobrachium rosenbergii and marine shrimp Penaeus (sp) species. Scientific research results and case studies presented and analyzed.

ANSC 462.title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination
ANSC 462.subject: ANSC
ANSC 462.description: Introductory exploration of anatomy, development, and physiology of reproduction of domestic animals and artificial insemination.

ANSC 462L.title: Reproduction and Artificial Insemination Lab
ANSC 462L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 462L.description: Reproductive anatomy and physiology of domestic animals, estorus synchronization, breeding soundness, and artificial insemination laboratory, field trips. One week offisland field trip. ANSC majors or consent.

ANSC 465L.title: Aquaculture Production Laboratory
ANSC 465L.subject: ANSC
ANSC 465L.description: Intensive, hands-on course involving the culture of larvae and juveniles of marine shrimp, freshwater prawns, molluscs, fish, and their food. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing and flexible time for continuous live animal care. Lab fee required.

ANSC 472.title: Comparative Endocrinology
ANSC 472.subject: ANSC
ANSC 472.description: Structure and function of endocrine systems across vertebrate groups, surveying how hormones mediate adaptive responses to dynamic environments and coordinate key aspects of growth, development, metabolism, osmoregulation, and stress.

ANSC 490.title: Aquaculture Business Planning and Entrepreneurship
ANSC 490.subject: ANSC
ANSC 490.description: Practical aspects of planning and developing an aquaculture business from conceptualization to a final business plan. Topics include species/technology, project planning, business structuring, permitting, contracts, production plans, financial planning and analysis, market/competition analysis, capital acquisition, intellectual property and legal issues.
ANSC 490.prereq_raw: 450 or OCN 450. Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

children.text: Must have strong interest in hands-on rearing aquaculture animals and flexible time for live animal care

ANSC 491.title: Topics in Animal Sciences
ANSC 491.subject: ANSC
ANSC 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

ANSC 492.title: Field Experience
ANSC 492.subject: ANSC
ANSC 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.

ANSC 499.title: Directed Study or Research
ANSC 499.subject: ANSC
ANSC 499.description: Limited to exceptional undergraduate students, generally with a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or a minimum GPA of 3.0 in major. Exceptions may be granted for students with high achievement in last three semesters.

ANSC 601.title: The Science of Food Systems
ANSC 601.subject: ANSC
ANSC 601.description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr Discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.

ANSC 603.title: Experimental Design
ANSC 603.subject: ANSC
ANSC 603.description: Design of experiments and variance analyses in biological and agricultural research.
ANSC 603.prereq_raw: graduate standing or consent. Recommended: ZOOL 632

ANSC 641.title: Seminar in Animal Sciences
ANSC 641.subject: ANSC
ANSC 641.description: Topics of current interest and current research related to nutrition, genetics, and physiology.

ANSC 642.title: Advanced Animal Nutrition
ANSC 642.subject: ANSC
ANSC 642.description: An advanced course in the nutrition of mono-gastric, ruminant, avian, and aquatic species. Topics include digestive system structures, utilization of nutrients, energy metabolism, and experimental techniques used in the study of animal nutrition.

ANSC 643.title: Physiology of Reproduction
ANSC 643.subject: ANSC
ANSC 643.description: Comparative differentiation, development, growth, and function of the reproductive systems of mammals and birds; external factors that influence response; artificial insemination.

ANSC 644.title: Growth Biology of Meat Animals
ANSC 644.subject: ANSC
ANSC 644.description: Growth and development of meat-producing animals; skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, and bone; protein turnover, lipid metabolism, and bioenergetics; regulation of animal growth.

ANSC 650.title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
ANSC 650.subject: ANSC
ANSC 650.description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.

ANSC 652.title: Information Research Skills
ANSC 652.subject: ANSC
ANSC 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

ANSC 657.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
ANSC 657.subject: ANSC
ANSC 657.description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

ANSC 687.title: Advanced Laboratory Techniques
ANSC 687.subject: ANSC
ANSC 687.description: Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.

FSHN 112.title: Food Service Safety and Sanitation
FSHN 112.subject: FSHN
FSHN 112.description: Principles and procedures of sanitation and safety in the food service industry, including the study of foodborne illnesses, biological, chemical, physical hazards and cross-contamination as they may occur during the flow of food.

FSHN 141.title: Culture and Cuisine: The Global Diversity of Food
FSHN 141.subject: FSHN
FSHN 141.description: A timeline of the world history of food and how it relates to culture, diversity, ethnicity, and religion. International food demonstrations and tastings included.

FSHN 181.title: Introduction to Food Preparation
FSHN 181.subject: FSHN
FSHN 181.description: Lectures, discussions, and demonstrations on how food components contribute to the functional, sensory, and safety characteristics of foods, and what changes occur in foods due to preparation, processing, and storage.

FSHN 181L.title: Food Preparation Lab
FSHN 181L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 181L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments in foods emphasizing ingredient function and standard preparation methods for food groups.

FSHN 185.title: The Science of Human Nutrition
FSHN 185.subject: FSHN
FSHN 185.description: Integration of natural science concepts basic to the study of human nutrition. Emphasis on nutrient requirements of healthy individuals, food sources, functions of nutrients.

FSHN 244.title: Comparative Nutrition
FSHN 244.subject: FSHN
FSHN 244.description: Digestive systems and nutrient functions, interrelationships and metabolism are compared among animal species, including humans. An intermediate, general nutrition course for Food Science and Human Nutrition and Animal Science majors.

FSHN 311.title: Food Service Systems Management
FSHN 311.subject: FSHN
FSHN 311.description: Critical and essential aspects of management and effective leadership practices to direct and delivery quality foodservices. Focus on the role and competencies of the Registered Dietitian (RD) working in these environments.

FSHN 312.title: Food Service Production and Operations
FSHN 312.subject: FSHN
FSHN 312.description: Principles and procedures of menu planning, quantity food production, production scheduling, recipe adaptation, equipment operation, and formula costing. Principles of procurement including purchasing, selection, storage of equipment and quantity foods.
FSHN 312.prereq_raw: 181 and 181L (with a minimum grade of C), or consent

FSHN 322.title: Marketing Nutrition and Food
FSHN 322.subject: FSHN
FSHN 322.description: Fundamental marketing principles applied to nutrition and food. Will include concepts such as the psychology of food purchasing decisions and consumer behavior. Field trips and group projects included. Open to non-majors.

FSHN 350.title: Humans, Food, and Animals: Ethics, Issues, and Controversies
FSHN 350.subject: FSHN
FSHN 350.description: Ethical issues and other controversies related to human and animal needs; their impact on resource sustainability and quality of life are explored from scientific perspectives.

FSHN 360.title: Applied Professional Skills in Nutrition
FSHN 360.subject: FSHN
FSHN 360.description: Will apply skills in technology, research, and career development to nutrition. Students will identify evidence-based nutrition information and demonstrate their academic skill sets for future professional success through technology.

FSHN 370.title: Lifespan Nutrition
FSHN 370.subject: FSHN
FSHN 370.description: Physiological changes and nutritional requirements during human life stages: prepregnancy, pregnancy, infancy, childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and older adulthood. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.
FSHN 370.prereq_raw: B or better in 185; C or better in CHEM 161/161L; C or better in PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent)

FSHN 381.title: Experimental Foods
FSHN 381.subject: FSHN
FSHN 381.description: Experimental approach to study food preparation problems. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports. Subject matter used to practice critical thinking and problem solving skills.

FSHN 381L.title: Experimental Foods Laboratory
FSHN 381L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 381L.description: Experimental approach to study food preparation, food formulation, and sensory evaluation with laboratory exercises in a certified kitchen environment. Applying basic food science research design to conduct experiments, interpret data and write reports.

FSHN 389.title: Nutritional Assessment
FSHN 389.subject: FSHN
FSHN 389.description: Addresses concepts and uses of nutrition assessment tools at individual and community levels. Students will be introduced to national surveys and new, more sophisticated body composition measurements. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

FSHN 403.title: Microbiology of Foods
FSHN 403.subject: FSHN
FSHN 403.description: Microorganisms encountered in foods; types of food spoilage; microbial hazards in food; methods of food preservation.

FSHN 411.title: Food Engineering
FSHN 411.subject: FSHN
FSHN 411.description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
FSHN 411.prereq_raw: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Once a year)

FSHN 420.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
FSHN 420.subject: FSHN
FSHN 420.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
FSHN 420.prereq_raw: EE 160, EE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or EE 326; or consent

FSHN 430.title: Food Chemistry
FSHN 430.subject: FSHN
FSHN 430.description: Chemical properties of food constituents studied in relationship to their effects on processing, nutrition, and spoilage.

FSHN 430L.title: Food Chemistry Lab
FSHN 430L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 430L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical methods in the study of food constituents—proteins, lipids, carbohydrates, pigments, enzymes, etc.

FSHN 440.title: Food Safety
FSHN 440.subject: FSHN
FSHN 440.description: Discussion of potential microbiological, parasitic, chemical, and natural food hazards; food laws and standards; and related aspects of consumer protection.

FSHN 445.title: Food Quality Control
FSHN 445.subject: FSHN
FSHN 445.description: Fundamental principles of quality control in the food industry: measurement of quality parameters, utilization and integration of the individual test procedures into grades and standards of quality, sampling, and reporting results.

FSHN 451.title: Community Nutrition and Nutrition Education
FSHN 451.subject: FSHN
FSHN 451.description: Concepts and methods of nutrition program planning and nutrition education; analysis of nutritional problems of local, national, and international communities; strategies used to educate groups or individuals.
FSHN 451.prereq_raw: 370 and either HDFS 380 or NREM 310; or consent

FSHN 454.title: Foundation of Childhood Obesity Prevention in the Pacific
FSHN 454.subject: FSHN
FSHN 454.description: Provide students with a basic overview of the causes and effects of childhood obesity, evidence-based approaches, community-based research, and policies to prevent childhood obesity as it relates to the Pacific region.

FSHN 455.title: Childhood Anthropometric and Dietary Assessment Field Techniques
FSHN 455.subject: FSHN
FSHN 455.description: Teaches techniques for measuring anthropometry and collecting dietary intake in children. Online course imitates hands-on training through partnering with local organizations and the use of technology.

FSHN 456.title: Child Health and Nutrition Monotiring
FSHN 456.subject: FSHN
FSHN 456.description: Covers topics related to health and nutritional status monitoring and surveillance, including epidemiology, biostatistics, health and nutrition surveillance systems, and the uses of technology for conducting these activities.

FSHN 457.title: Culture and Child Health in the Pacific
FSHN 457.subject: FSHN
FSHN 457.description: In-depth study of Pacific culture, land, people, and history and its relationship to child health. Explores cultural competency, cultural safety, and multidisciplinary approaches to promote a healthy Pacific. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

FSHN 460.title: Food Processing Operations
FSHN 460.subject: FSHN
FSHN 460.description: Principles and applications of food dehydration, thermal processing, low temperature preservation, chemical and biochemical preservation, irradiation, packaging, manufacturing, plant sanitation, water and waste management.

FSHN 467.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy I
FSHN 467.subject: FSHN
FSHN 467.description: Development of dietary, anthropometric and clinical lab assessment skills measuring nutritional status. Understanding pathophysiology of disease processes, medical terminology and nutritional intervention, utilizing case studies.

FSHN 468.title: Medical Nutrition Therapy II
FSHN 468.subject: FSHN
FSHN 468.description: Understanding of the pathophysiology of disease processes and nutritional intervention, using medical terminology and case studies.

FSHN 469.title: Nutrition Counseling Skills
FSHN 469.subject: FSHN
FSHN 469.description: Theory and practice in nutritional counseling. Combined lecture and discussion on nutrition/dietary counseling. Knowledge and theories. Application through lab experiences including role playing, case presentations, and performing actual counseling sessions.

FSHN 475.title: Applied Human Nutrition
FSHN 475.subject: FSHN
FSHN 475.description: Application of basic nutrition principles; includes sources and functions of essential nutrients and food patterns compatible with nutrient needs, health, disease prevention, and sustainability. Intended for undergraduate and graduate students.
FSHN 475.prereq_raw: CHEM 161 (or higher) or BIOC 241 (or higher); PHYL 141, BIOL 171; or consent

FSHN 476.title: Cultural Aspects of Food Habits
FSHN 476.subject: FSHN
FSHN 476.description: Study of eating from behavioral perspectives. Implications for health practitioners and health education.
FSHN 476.prereq_raw: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher or SOC 100 or higher or PSY 100 or higher

children.text: two classes from ANTH 151 or higher

FSHN 477.title: Food Analysis
FSHN 477.subject: FSHN
FSHN 477.description: Principles of sample preparation and chemical and physical analysis of food components using current methodology.
FSHN 477.prereq_raw: 430; and CHEM 162 or higher; and BIOL 402 or MBBE 402 or PEPS 402

FSHN 477L.title: Food Analysis Lab
FSHN 477L.subject: FSHN
FSHN 477L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of different chemical and physical methods for the identification and quantitation of food components.

FSHN 480.title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
FSHN 480.subject: FSHN
FSHN 480.description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.

FSHN 485.title: Nutritional Biochemistry I
FSHN 485.subject: FSHN
FSHN 485.description: Metabolism and biochemistry of carbohydrates, lipids, and proteins, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, cellular/molecular functions in human nutrition; integration of metabolic pathways; energy metabolism and balance, including relevance to chronic disease.
FSHN 485.prereq_raw: 185; PHYL 142/142L or PHYL 302/302L; BIOC 341 or higher (or concurrent) or MBBE 402 (or concurrent); or consent

FSHN 486.title: Nutritional Biochemistry II
FSHN 486.subject: FSHN
FSHN 486.description: Metabolism and biochemistry of vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber, including chemical structure, digestion, absorption, transport, and cellular/ molecular functions in human nutrition; relevance to establishing nutrient requirements and to mechanisms of chronic disease.

FSHN 488.title: Obesity, Science, and Issues
FSHN 488.subject: FSHN
FSHN 488.description: In-depth study of obesity, including research, etiology, treatment, and prevention.

FSHN 491.title: Topics in Food Science and Human Nutrition
FSHN 491.subject: FSHN
FSHN 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics, problems, or laboratory experiments.

FSHN 492.title: Field Experience
FSHN 492.subject: FSHN
FSHN 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer. Writing a learning plan and field report.

FSHN 494.title: Food Science Capstone
FSHN 494.subject: FSHN
FSHN 494.description: Field practicum designed to integrate knowledge from previous FSHN courses to develop novel and innovative food products. Students deal with shelflife, marketing, packaging, labeling, sensory evaluation, and quality assurance.

FSHN 601.title: The Science of Food Systems
FSHN 601.subject: FSHN
FSHN 601.description: (1 50-min Lec, 1 2-hr discussion) Discussion of food systems as they apply to animal science, food science, and human nutrition.

FSHN 607.title: Advanced Food Science I
FSHN 607.subject: FSHN
FSHN 607.description: Advanced topics in chemical and physical characteristics of foods as well as their role in human nutrition.
FSHN 607.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological science, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

FSHN 608.title: Advanced Food Science II
FSHN 608.subject: FSHN
FSHN 608.description: Advances in sensory quality and evaluation, deterioration of foods and food safety, as well as food processing technology.
FSHN 608.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics, and biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected; or consent

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in organic chemistry, microbiology, additional biological sciences, physics,
biochemistry. Basic knowledge of food science is expected;

FSHN 609.title: Advanced Food Safety
FSHN 609.subject: FSHN
FSHN 609.description: Real and perceived food hazards, their ethical issues and implications, advanced emerging topics in food safety, and controls, including laws and regulations of food safety issues and public perception of food safety will be discussed.
FSHN 609.prereq_raw: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in biochemistry, microbiology, food processing, physics and organic chemistry. Basic food science knowledge is required; or consent

children.text: graduate student status with undergraduate courses in biochemistry, microbiology, food processing, physics
organic chemistry. Basic food science knowledge is required;

FSHN 633.title: International Nutrition
FSHN 633.subject: FSHN
FSHN 633.description: Analysis of major nutrition problems in developing countries. Comparative review of the design, implementation, and evaluation of programs to intervene in the development of malnutrition.

FSHN 650.title: DNA and Genetic Analysis
FSHN 650.subject: FSHN
FSHN 650.description: Combined lecture-lab for students interested in genetic analysis of humans, animals, and other species. Molecular techniques, such as PCR, DNA marker identifications, transgenics, expression analysis and functional genomics, are included. Open to nonmajors.

FSHN 652.title: Information Research Skills
FSHN 652.subject: FSHN
FSHN 652.description: Examines the use of libraries and information technology for scholarly investigation in support of scientific research; provides experience utilizing and critically evaluating a variety of print and electronic sources in basic and applied sciences.

FSHN 657.title: Grant Writing for Graduate Students
FSHN 657.subject: FSHN
FSHN 657.description: Combined lecture/discussion on grants and grant writing. Designed to introduce graduate students to grants and grant proposal writing through lectures, class discussion, writing assignments, and peer review. Open to CTAHR graduate students only; others with consent.

FSHN 668.title: Advanced Topics in Clinical Nutrition
FSHN 668.subject: FSHN
FSHN 668.description: Advanced topics in nutrition assessment, diagnosis, and interventions of patients with specialized clinical conditions. Students will further their knowledge in clinical research methods through case study presentations and evidence-based review.

FSHN 681.title: Seminar in Food and Nutritional Sciences
FSHN 681.subject: FSHN
FSHN 681.description: Student presentation of literature reviews and research.

FSHN 682.title: Topics in Nutritional Sciences
FSHN 682.subject: FSHN
FSHN 682.description: Advanced topics in nutritional sciences, from basic to applied research, including current issues in nutrition and critical analysis of current research literature.

FSHN 683.title: Global Nutrition
FSHN 683.subject: FSHN
FSHN 683.description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

FSHN 684.title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
FSHN 684.subject: FSHN
FSHN 684.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

FSHN 685.title: Nutrition and Disease: Cellular and Molecular Aspects
FSHN 685.subject: FSHN
FSHN 685.description: In-depth lecture, discussion, and student presentations on selected topics relating nutrition to the etiology and prevention of chronic diseases at the cellular and molecular level.

FSHN 686.title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
FSHN 686.subject: FSHN
FSHN 686.description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

FSHN 687.title: Advanced Lab Techniques
FSHN 687.subject: FSHN
FSHN 687.description: Advanced laboratory techniques used in food science and human nutrition research.

FSHN 688.title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
FSHN 688.subject: FSHN
FSHN 688.description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored. Graduate students only.

FSHN 689.title: Nutritional Epidemiology
FSHN 689.subject: FSHN
FSHN 689.description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

FSHN 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
FSHN 695.subject: FSHN
FSHN 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B Master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

FSHN 701.title: Topics in Food Science
FSHN 701.subject: FSHN
FSHN 701.description: Advanced topics in food science and technology, from basic to applied research, including current issues in food science and technology and critical analysis of current research literature.

FSHN 749.title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
FSHN 749.subject: FSHN
FSHN 749.description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.
FSHN 749.prereq_raw: 663 (with a minimum grade of B-) or consent

FSHN 784.title: Dietary Fiber, Bioactive Food Components and Health
FSHN 784.subject: FSHN
FSHN 784.description: Lecture/discussion of current research on gut physiology, gut microbes, dietary fiber, bioactive food components, and their impact on health, including colorectal cancer, inflammatory bowel disease, heart disease, diabetes, and immune function.
FSHN 784.prereq_raw: 485 and 486 (or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent), statistics, physiology; or consent

FSHN 785.title: Diet and Cancer Seminar
FSHN 785.subject: FSHN
