FSHN 785.description: Presentation-discussion of selected research topics in the field of diet-cancer relationships including: nutritional epidemiology of cancer, diet and supplement intervention trials, and cellular/molecular effects of diet on cancer pathophysiology.

FSHN 800.title: Dissertation Research
FSHN 800.subject: FSHN
FSHN 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation in nutrition. Graduate standing only. Satisfactory/ Unsatisfactory only.

BE 110.title: Introduction to Sustainable Engineering
BE 110.subject: BE
BE 110.description: Sustainability and its social and technical significance; global population growth; resource management and quantification; designs for sustainable society; challenges interfacing technology and culture/religion; green and ecological engineering; life cycle analyses; engineering ethics; selected case studies.

BE 120.title: Introduction to Quantitative Biology
BE 120.subject: BE
BE 120.description: Quantitative approach to applied topics in biology including synthesis and metabolism, kinetics, physiological systems, cellular processes and signaling, informatics, and emerging technologies for health, biological production/processing, and discovery.
BE 120.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) and CHEM 162 (or concurrent), or consent. (Once a year)

BE 150.title: Introduction to Biological Engineering
BE 150.subject: BE
BE 150.description: Discussion and experimental investigation of physical and chemical principles underlying representative biological processes and systems. Bioproduction, energy conversion processes, physiological systems, biological treatment, biosensors, biomechanics, and related natural and engineered systems.

BE 191.title: Introduction to Applications in Biological Engineering
BE 191.subject: BE
BE 191.description: Discussion and investigation of special topics, problems and applications of biological engineering.

BE 260.title: Mass and Energy Balances
BE 260.subject: BE
BE 260.description: Introduction of the principles of mass and energy conservation; development of systematic approaches to apply these principles in calculations for design and analysis of biochemical, chemical, and physical processes.
BE 260.prereq_raw: BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or 171 or 181A, PHYS 170, and MATH 242 or 252A; or consent

BE 350.title: Dynamic Systems Modeling
BE 350.subject: BE
BE 350.description: Introduction to analytical and numerical solutions for systems of differential equations. Modeling and computer simulation of representative dynamic systems encountered in biological engineering.
BE 350.prereq_raw: 260, EE 110 or 160, MATH 243 or 253A, CEE 270; or consent

BE 350L.title: Dynamic Systems Modeling Laboratory
BE 350L.subject: BE
BE 350L.description: Industry field trips and lab experiences to illustrate behavior of representative dynamic systems in biological engineering. Data acquisition and model validation.

BE 373.title: Transport Phenomena
BE 373.subject: BE
BE 373.description: Fundamental principles and applications relating to mass, momentum, and energy transfers in biosystems and other systems for engineers and scientists.
BE 373.prereq_raw: 260, CEE 270, MATH 243 or 253A, CEE 320 (or concurrent) or ME 322 (or concurrent, ME 311 (or concurrent)

BE 405.title: Engineering Economics
BE 405.subject: BE
BE 405.description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decision-making, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.

BE 410.title: Biomass Conversion to Biofuels and Bioenergy
BE 410.subject: BE
BE 410.description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production; fundamental concepts in biofuel/ bioenergy production; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel/bioenergy; biodiesel production; environmental impacts, economics and life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies.

BE 411.title: Food Engineering
BE 411.subject: BE
BE 411.description: Principles and applications of thermodynamics, electricity, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, psychrometry, and material and energy balances of food processing and preservation.
BE 411.prereq_raw: (BIOL 171, CHEM 162 or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A, MATH 243 or MATH 253A, PHYS 151 or PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C; or consent. (Once a year)

BE 420.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
BE 420.subject: BE
BE 420.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
BE 420.prereq_raw: (EE 160, EE 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or EE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

BE 421.title: Bioprocess Control
BE 421.subject: BE
BE 421.description: Process control in both time and Laplace domains with an introduction to the frequency domain; selection and design of appropriate control systems for bioprocesses with consideration of the impact on the total system; identification of safety concerns in designing control systems and process equipment.

BE 431.title: Environmental Biotechnology
BE 431.subject: BE
BE 431.description: Environmental impact and control; the microorganism and its nutrition and growth conditions; microbial growth and substrate removal kinetics; bioreactors; biological treatment systems; biodegredation of xenobiotic organic chemicals; case studies.

BE 437.title: Biosystems Unit Operations
BE 437.subject: BE
BE 437.description: Introduction to unit operations in biological, environmental, food, and manufacturing processes. Integration of biology and chemistry into engineering using basic concepts in mass and energy conservation and transport in reacting and non-reacting systems.
BE 437.prereq_raw: 373; and either CEE 320 or ME 322; or consent

BE 440.title: Bioremediation: Principles and Practices
BE 440.subject: BE
BE 440.description: Soil environment, fate and transport of contaminants; microbial ecology, metabolism, and energy production; biodegradation of selected compounds. In situ treatment, solid-phase bioremediation, slurry-phase bioremediation, and vapor-phase biological treatment. Open to nonmajors.

BE 460.title: Bioreactor Design and Analysis
BE 460.subject: BE
BE 460.description: Application of mass/energy balances and reaction kinetics for the design and analysis of bioreactors for microbial, plant, and animal cell cultures.
BE 460.prereq_raw: 373 or CEE 320 or ME 322; or consent

BE 470.title: Bioprocess Design and Analysis
BE 470.subject: BE
BE 470.description: Combined lecture/computer lab on theory and practice of bioprocess design and analysis, involving biological basics and engineering principles of bioprocessing, computer-aided unit operations, process integration, and economic evaluation.
BE 470.prereq_raw: 373, or 437 (or concurrent) or 460 (or concurrent); or consent

BE 481.title: Senior Engineering Design I
BE 481.subject: BE
BE 481.description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) First of a two-semester sequence that provides a major design experience for senior students in biosystems engineering. Design process; project management; design methods; modeling and simulation; design optimization; engineering economics; engineering statistics, initiation of an open-ended design project.
BE 481.prereq_raw: 350/350L, 373, CEE 320 or ME 322, ME 311, EE 211; or consent

BE 482.title: Senior Engineering Design II
BE 482.subject: BE
BE 482.description: (1 1-hr Lec, 2 3-hr Lab) Continuation of 481. Properties of biological materials; risk and reliability; design ethics; guest lectures on engineering design by practicing engineers; extension and completion of the design project with submission of a final design report.

BE 491.title: Biological Engineering Topics
BE 491.subject: BE
BE 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. Offered by visiting faculty and/or for extension programs.

BE 492.title: Internship
BE 492.subject: BE
BE 492.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development. Placement with an approved cooperating supervisor/employer.

BE 499.title: Directed Research
BE 499.subject: BE
BE 499.description: Research in the area of biosystems engineering.

BE 606.title: Instrumentation and Measurement
BE 606.subject: BE
BE 606.description: Measurement concepts and operating principles applied to the selection and use of instruments important to scientists and engineers dealing with biological systems, including automatic data acquisition and processing.
BE 606.prereq_raw: CHEM 151, MATH 241, and ME 311; or consent

BE 610.title: Biofuel and Bioenergy
BE 610.subject: BE
BE 610.description: Overview of biofuel/bioenergy production, biorefinery concept; renewable feedstocks; thermochemical and biochemical conversions of biomass to biofuel; biodiesel production; algal-biofuel; environmental impacts, life-cycle analysis; value-added processing of biofuel residues; selected case studies; term paper and presentation.

BE 622.title: Experimental Methods in Cause-Effect Modeling
BE 622.subject: BE
BE 622.description: Factorial designs and fractional factorial designs for screening variable and response optimization. Response surface methodology. Experimental designs appropriate to building and testing multi-variable behavior relationships. Sequential experimental designs.

BE 625.title: Biological Instrumentation
BE 625.subject: BE
BE 625.description: System integration for computer-based control, automation, and study of biological systems. Topics include physical, chemical, and biological sensors, actuators, digital interfacing/communication, image analysis, and structured code for microcontrollers and other portable computers.

BE 634.title: Biological Treatment
BE 634.subject: BE
BE 634.description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

BE 638.title: Biosystems Modeling
BE 638.subject: BE
BE 638.description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system models, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
BE 638.prereq_raw: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent

BE 664.title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
BE 664.subject: BE
BE 664.description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

BE 750.title: Seminar
BE 750.subject: BE
BE 750.description: Use of computer and video technology in technical presentation, review of current biosystems engineering research.

AREC 610.title: Biosystems Modeling
AREC 610.subject: AREC
AREC 610.description: Introduction to system thinking, procedures for developing system models, characteristics of important agricultural system modes, computer approach to evaluation and optimization of system models.
AREC 610.prereq_raw: one of MATH 215, MATH 241, MATH 251A; or consent

AREC 626.title: Econometrics I
AREC 626.subject: AREC
AREC 626.description: Review of probability, estimation, small sample and asymptotic properties. Bivariate and multiple regression and matrix algebra formulation. Regression diagnostics. Introduction to heteroskedastidity, autocorrelation, simultaneity, dichotomous variables, advanced topics.
AREC 626.prereq_raw: NREM 310 or ECON 321, and MATH 241; or consent

AREC 634.title: Econometrics II
AREC 634.subject: AREC
AREC 634.description: Specification, statistical estimation, inference, and forecasting of economic models. Includes advanced topics for single-equation models, pooled models, qualitative dependent variables, simultaneous systems, distributed lags, and time series.

PEPS 210.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
PEPS 210.subject: PEPS
PEPS 210.description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

PEPS 250.title: The World of Insects
PEPS 250.subject: PEPS
PEPS 250.description: Biology/ecology of insects with emphasis on relationships to plants, animals, and especially people in Hawai‘i and the tropics. Open to nonmajors.

PEPS 310.title: Environment and Agriculture
PEPS 310.subject: PEPS
PEPS 310.description: Overview of environmental issues and impacts associated with agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts.

PEPS 340.title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
PEPS 340.subject: PEPS
PEPS 340.description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i.

PEPS 350.title: Invasive Pest Species
PEPS 350.subject: PEPS
PEPS 350.description: Ecological, economic and sociological impacts of invasive pest species on tropical ecosystems; characteristics of invasive species and nature of vulnerable habitats; management of invasive species or eradication options; impacts on evolution, biological diversity and ecological stability. Open to nonmajors. (Alt. years: spring)

PEPS 363.title: General Entomology
PEPS 363.subject: PEPS
PEPS 363.description: Biology, diversity, and ecology of insects with emphasis on Hawaiian fauna. Classification to order level.
PEPS 363.prereq_raw: BOT 101 or ZOOL 101 or BIOL 171; or consent

PEPS 363L.title: General Entomology Laboratory
PEPS 363L.subject: PEPS
PEPS 363L.description: Laboratory in the biology and classification to family level of Hawai‘i’s insects and arthropods.

PEPS 371.title: Genetics: Theory to Application
PEPS 371.subject: PEPS
PEPS 371.description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

PEPS 405.title: Plant Pathogens and Diseases
PEPS 405.subject: PEPS
PEPS 405.description: Classification, morphology, ecology, and biology of bacteria, fungi, nematodes, and viruses that attack economic crops. Etiology and control of plant diseases.
PEPS 405.prereq_raw: 210/SUST 210 or BOT 101 or MICR 130, or consent

PEPS 410.title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
PEPS 410.subject: PEPS
PEPS 410.description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems. (Alt. years: spring)

PEPS 418.title: Turfgrass Pest Management
PEPS 418.subject: PEPS
PEPS 418.description: Provides students with knowledge and real world experience on common turfgrass pests and management strategies in Hawai‘i, with emphasis on integrated pest management. Common cool-season turfgrass and pest management are also discussed.

PEPS 421.title: Foundations of Pest Management
PEPS 421.subject: PEPS
PEPS 421.description: Principles and concepts of insect pest management using biological, ecological, cultural, behavioral, legislative, microbial and chemical methods.
PEPS 421.prereq_raw: one of the following: 250 or 363, BIOL 171, BIOL 172, or BOT 101; or consent

PEPS 422.title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
PEPS 422.subject: PEPS
PEPS 422.description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

PEPS 430.title: Plant Disease Management
PEPS 430.subject: PEPS
PEPS 430.description: Diagnosis, epidemiology, and integrated management of important plant diseases and pathogens for key plants and cultivated crops in various agroecosystems in Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and the global tropics.

PEPS 451.title: Environmental Law
PEPS 451.subject: PEPS
PEPS 451.description: Exploration of federal laws, regulations, and precedents that govern our interaction with the environment. Analysis of laws regulating air, water, toxins, pests, endangered species, and environmental justice.

PEPS 463.title: Urban Pest Management
PEPS 463.subject: PEPS
PEPS 463.description: Biology, ecology, and management of pest organisms associated with people, structures and the urban environment.

PEPS 481.title: Weed Science
PEPS 481.subject: PEPS
PEPS 481.description: Weed classification, identification, adaptations for weediness; principles of weed control; properties, uses, and action of herbicides. Lab: pesticide application equipment and techniques, no-till farming, greenhouse and field experiments.

PEPS 486.title: Symbioses
PEPS 486.subject: PEPS
PEPS 486.description: Study of symbioses in insects and a wide range of organisms. Students will learn the types of symbioses, evolution, and ecology of symbiotic lifestyles, and their impact on agriculture and human health.

PEPS 491.title: Topics in Plant & Environmental Protection
PEPS 491.subject: PEPS
PEPS 491.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems. May be offered by visiting faculty, extension faculty or research faculty.

PEPS 495.title: PEPS Capstone
PEPS 495.subject: PEPS
PEPS 495.description: Integration and application of academic knowledge and critical skills emphasizing professional development, Directed Research, field studies, employment with cooperating businesses, government or schools are all options.

PEPS 499.title: Directed Research
PEPS 499.subject: PEPS
PEPS 499.description: Conduct original research in environmental protection sciences. Limited to qualified undergraduate students.

PEPS 601.title: Agrosecurity and Food Safety
PEPS 601.subject: PEPS
PEPS 601.description: Concepts of agrosecurity and food safety (including plant and animal biosecurity), global impacts of introduced pests and diseases, and current mechanisms for interception of pests and mitigation of disease.

PEPS 605.title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Fungi and Nematodes
PEPS 605.subject: PEPS
PEPS 605.description: Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology and management of plant diseases caused by fungi, oomycetes, and nematodes. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

PEPS 606.title: Biology of Plant Pathogens: Bacteria and Viruses
PEPS 606.subject: PEPS
PEPS 606.description: Principles and concepts in pathogen biology, epidemiology, and management of plant diseases caused by bacteria and viruses. Laboratory techniques for isolation and identification of pathogens and disease diagnosis.

PEPS 615.title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases
PEPS 615.subject: PEPS
PEPS 615.description: Iterative and interactive course integrating plant pathogen and pest biology with diagnostic and management approaches. Will use biological information about pathogens, anthropods, and abiotic stresses to diagnose diseases, disorders, or other injuries of plants.
PEPS 615.prereq_raw: (605 and 606) with a minimum grade of B, or consent

PEPS 615L.title: Diagnosis and Management of Tropical Plant Diseases Laboratory
PEPS 615L.subject: PEPS
PEPS 615L.description: Diagnosis and management of plant pathogen and pest problems in laboratory and field. Taught concurrently with 615.
PEPS 615L.prereq_raw: (605 and 606) with a minimum grade of B, or equivalent

PEPS 627.title: Molecular Diagnostics: Principles and Practices
PEPS 627.subject: PEPS
PEPS 627.description: Molecular diagnostics principles, comparative genomics, genome annotation and bio-informatics, phylogenetics, gene target selection, advanced primer, and probe design. Graduate students only or consent.

PEPS 641.title: Insect Physiology
PEPS 641.subject: PEPS
PEPS 641.description: Study of the principal physiological and biochemical functions in insects, with emphasis on hormonal interactions.

PEPS 652.title: Molecular Plant–Fungal Interactions
PEPS 652.subject: PEPS
PEPS 652.description: Focuses on the actions of plant pathogenic fungi/ oomycetes and their host responses at the molecular and cellular level. Current genetic and genomic approaches to study plant-fungal interactions will be discussed. Graduate standing only.

PEPS 660.title: Seminar in Plant Pathology
PEPS 660.subject: PEPS
PEPS 660.description: Seminar on research and topics in plant pathology.

PEPS 662.title: Systematics and Phylogenetics
PEPS 662.subject: PEPS
PEPS 662.description: Classification and study of diversity among insects and other life forms. Use of morphological and molecular characters to reconstruct evolutionary histories.

PEPS 665.title: Quantitative Genomics and Evolution
PEPS 665.subject: PEPS
PEPS 665.description: Overview and lab-based course exploring theory and methods to understand genome evolution and adaptation; focus will be on a range of organisms.

PEPS 671.title: Insect Ecology
PEPS 671.subject: PEPS
PEPS 671.description: Insects as living units in an environment of physical and biotic factors.

PEPS 675.title: Biological Control of Pests
PEPS 675.subject: PEPS
PEPS 675.description: Fundamental concepts. Critical study of major biological control projects.
PEPS 675.prereq_raw: 421 or consent. Recommended: 662; and ZOOL 631 or 632

PEPS 676.title: Biological Control of Weeds
PEPS 676.subject: PEPS
PEPS 676.description: Examine approaches to weed biological control of invasive plants in various environments with different agents (insects, pathogens, and vertebrates), integration with other management tactics, sociopolitical aspects, and history of the practice. Graduate students only.

PEPS 686.title: Invertebrate Microbiology
PEPS 686.subject: PEPS
PEPS 686.description: In-depth study of the molecular and cellular interactions between microbes and animals. Topics will cover types of symbioses, gut microbiome, parasites, and agricultural pathogens, and disease and human health disease.

PEPS 690.title: Seminar in Entomology
PEPS 690.subject: PEPS
PEPS 690.description: Seminars on research and topics in entomology.

PEPS 691.title: Special Topics
PEPS 691.subject: PEPS
PEPS 691.description: Study and discussion of significant topics and problems in plant and environmental protection sciences at an advanced level. Offered by visiting or existing faculty as a special course.

PEPS 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
PEPS 695.subject: PEPS
PEPS 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
PEPS 695.prereq_raw: graduate standing in entomology or tropical plant pathology

children.text: in entomology or tropical plant pathology

PEPS 699.title: Directed Research
PEPS 699.subject: PEPS
PEPS 699.description: Directed research, critical reviews in environmental protection sciences, entomology, or plant pathology.

PEPS 716.title: Advanced Plant Nematology
PEPS 716.subject: PEPS
PEPS 716.description: Advanced study of nematode taxonomy, genetics, behavior, host interactions, and sustainable management in an integrated lecture-laboratory.
PEPS 716.prereq_raw: 605 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

PEPS 730.title: Advanced Plant Virology
PEPS 730.subject: PEPS
PEPS 730.description: Characterization, genome organization, gene expression, and molecular mechanisms of plant viruses.
PEPS 730.prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

PEPS 746.title: Advanced Plant-Bacteria Interactions
PEPS 746.subject: PEPS
PEPS 746.description: Molecular biology, genomics, molecular genetics, and infection mechanisms of bacterial plant pathogens and symbionts.
PEPS 746.prereq_raw: 606 (with a minimum grade of B or better) or consent

PEPS 799.title: Proposal/Defense Seminar
PEPS 799.subject: PEPS
PEPS 799.description: Thesis/ dissertation proposal and defense seminars.

PEPS 800.title: Dissertation Research
PEPS 800.subject: PEPS
PEPS 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation. CR/ NC only.

TAHR 099.title: International Exchange Study/Research
TAHR 099.subject: TAHR
TAHR 099.description: Study overseas in an approved international or similar exchange program.

TAHR 250.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
TAHR 250.subject: TAHR
TAHR 250.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

TAHR 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
TAHR 251.subject: TAHR
TAHR 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

TAHR 415.title: Extension Education & Outreach
TAHR 415.subject: TAHR
TAHR 415.description: Introduces an essential component of the Land Grant Mission. Students will explore the foundational components of extension education including agent expectations, program development and evaluation, audience engagement, building partnerships, funding structures.

DIS 380.title: Foundations in Disability and Diversity
DIS 380.subject: DIS
DIS 380.description: Focuses on disability as a category of diversity and identity, as well as diversity within disability. Different strategies used to increase the freedom or liberty of people with disabilities are critically examined.

DIS 382.title: Accessible Learning Technology
DIS 382.subject: DIS
DIS 382.description: Focuses on creating accessible technology and instructional media, developing long-term resources, advancing accessible social interaction between students and students with instructors, and using case studies as examples of good practices.

DIS 383.title: Disability History and Culture: From Homer to Hip Hop
DIS 383.subject: DIS
DIS 383.description: How have people over many centuries, and from broad geographical perspectives perceived and treated individuals with disabilities? An overview of the history of the conditions in which people with disabilities lived.

DIS 606.title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
DIS 606.subject: DIS
DIS 606.description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, Action Research, mixed methods, and Curriculum Based Assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal.

DIS 675.title: Supporting Multilingual Learners
DIS 675.subject: DIS
DIS 675.description: Strategies for identifying and adopting best practices that support all students in inclusive learning environments with an emphasis on STEM curriculum for English Language Learners; (B) science; (C) technology; (D) math.

DIS 678.title: Practicum in Applied Behavior Analysis
DIS 678.subject: DIS
DIS 678.description: Supervised field experience in applied behavior analysis. The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

DIS 680.title: Disability History Through the Ages
DIS 680.subject: DIS
DIS 680.description: A historical overview of disability that visits diverse perspectives, attitudes, and treatment toward individuals with disabilities through many centuries, societies, and cultures throughout the world; and how people with disabilities perceived themselves.

DIS 681.title: Multicultural Issues in Disabilities
DIS 681.subject: DIS
DIS 681.description: Provide background and understanding of various Pacific Rim cultural issues in the conceptualization and treatment of individuals with disabilities and their families.

DIS 682.title: Special Topics in Disability and Diversity Studies
DIS 682.subject: DIS
DIS 682.description: Explores disability and diversity across time to gain an understanding and context of issues such as difference, culture, identity, community, privilege, and oppression and how the past affects the present and future.

DIS 683.title: Interdisciplinary Disability and Diversity Issues
DIS 683.subject: DIS
DIS 683.description: Develop understanding of current issues faced by individuals with disabilities and their families within the disability paradigm and across cultures.

DIS 684.title: Interdisciplinary Team Development
DIS 684.subject: DIS
DIS 684.description: Develop knowledge and skills to participate effectively on interdisciplinary teams for the common goal of promoting service integration and coordination of education, social, health, mental health, and other services with individuals with disabilities and their families.

DIS 685.title: Interdisciplinary Assessment
DIS 685.subject: DIS
DIS 685.description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

DIS 686.title: Advanced Interdisciplinary Assessment
DIS 686.subject: DIS
DIS 686.description: Assessment methods and techniques to instructional research-based practices and supports across disciplines, cultures and PK-12 that address barriers to learning for all students with the context of the Comprehensive Student Support System (CSSS).

DIS 687.title: Seminar on Disability Issues
DIS 687.subject: DIS
DIS 687.description: In-depth explorations of current and compelling interdisciplinary topics related to advancing the social, political, educational, and economic integration of individuals with disabilities of all ages.

DIS 688.title: Portfolio/Field Work
DIS 688.subject: DIS
DIS 688.description: Interdisciplinary community experience and portfolio in disability and diversity studies.

DIS 780.title: Mixed Methods Research Design
DIS 780.subject: DIS
DIS 780.description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. (Once a year)

EDCS 415.title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years)
EDCS 415.subject: EDCS
EDCS 415.description: Emphasizes interrelated historical and philosophical roots and socio-cultural context and their influence on policy and practice in early childhood education settings.

EDCS 415L.title: Foundations in the Field of Early Childhood Education (Birth to 8 Years) Lab
EDCS 415L.subject: EDCS
EDCS 415L.description: Direct experience with children in early childhood settings in order to apply concepts from 415 and gain perspective on the role of the practitioner in ECE settings.

EDCS 416.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
EDCS 416.subject: EDCS
EDCS 416.description: Continuation of 415: focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children (pK-3).

EDCS 416L.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
EDCS 416L.subject: EDCS

EDCS 417.title: STEM Pedagogy
EDCS 417.subject: EDCS
EDCS 417.description: Provides introductory information to individuals new to the field of STEM education. Designed to integrate educational theory, pedagogy, content, and practical concerns into teaching practices in the STEM fields.

EDCS 431.title: Collaborative Language and Learning
EDCS 431.subject: EDCS
EDCS 431.description: Examination of language (talking, reading, and writing) processes within a collaborative teaching framework in the secondary curriculum. Field experience may be required.

EDCS 432.title: Adolescent Literature and Literacy
EDCS 432.subject: EDCS
EDCS 432.description: Selection and interpretation of young adult literature, including multicultural literature for middle level and high school students. Theory and teaching strategies for integrating literacy instruction in the literature program for diverse student populations.

EDCS 433.title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
EDCS 433.subject: EDCS
EDCS 433.description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

EDCS 440.title: Curriculum Implications of Multicultural Education
EDCS 440.subject: EDCS
EDCS 440.description: Examination of trends, issues, school practices, and program in multicultural education and its related area of study–bilingual-bicultural education.

EDCS 450.title: Methods and Materials in Science
EDCS 450.subject: EDCS
EDCS 450.description: Selecting and using methods and materials, demonstrations and simulations, open-ended experimentation, inquiry and discovery, task analysis measurement tools and techniques, activities from various curricula, opportunity for individualized goals and projects.
EDCS 450.prereq_raw: ITE 323, ITE 404(H), teaching experience; or consent

EDCS 451.title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
EDCS 451.subject: EDCS
EDCS 451.description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers, including criteria for evaluation and planning.
EDCS 451.prereq_raw: (HDFS 230 (or concurrent), HDFS 331 (or concurrent)) with a minimum grade of B-; or consent

EDCS 453.title: Gender Issues in Education
EDCS 453.subject: EDCS
EDCS 453.description: Examination of current and historical issues in education and how they are impacted upon by gender, with particular reference to gender as it intersects with ethnicity and class, locally and globally.

EDCS 480.title: Issues in Computer Education
EDCS 480.subject: EDCS
EDCS 480.description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

EDCS 494.title: Problem Solving in Mathematics Education
EDCS 494.subject: EDCS
EDCS 494.description: Experiencing and learning to teach heuristics of solving mathematical problems; designing curricula, classroom organization, evaluative measures for problem solving.

EDCS 495.title: Difficulties in Learning Mathematics
EDCS 495.subject: EDCS
EDCS 495.description: Identification, analysis, and remediation of difficulties in learning mathematics.

EDCS 600.title: Language, Learning and Teaching
EDCS 600.subject: EDCS
EDCS 600.description: Examines the role that language plays in the social construction of knowledge within various disciplines, K–adult. Collaborative group learning strategies will be modeled.
EDCS 600.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent

EDCS 601.title: Advanced Topics in Reading
EDCS 601.subject: EDCS
EDCS 601.description: Current theories and teaching strategies of reading throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Topics include psychological, sociological, and cultural foundations of reading; 21st century literacies; emergent literacy; diversity; multilingual learners, formative assessment; state/national initiatives.
EDCS 601.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent

EDCS 602.title: Advanced Topics in Writing and Oral Language
EDCS 602.subject: EDCS
EDCS 602.description: Current theories and teaching strategies of writing and oral language throughout the lifespan within various social contexts. Focus on teaching writing and oral language as tools for learning and to demonstrate learning.
EDCS 602.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent

EDCS 603.title: Children’s Literature in the Elementary Curriculum
EDCS 603.subject: EDCS
EDCS 603.description: In-depth examination of traditional and current books/media, birth through young adult, with emphasis on applications in schools or other educational contexts. Focus on use of narrative, exposition, and other genres across the curriculum.
EDCS 603.prereq_raw: student teaching or teaching experience or consent

EDCS 604.title: Effective Writing Practices
EDCS 604.subject: EDCS
EDCS 604.description: Analysis and practical application of principles and strategies of effective writing and informed writing instruction in K-12 classrooms.

EDCS 605.title: Literacy Coaching and Leadership
EDCS 605.subject: EDCS
EDCS 605.description: Exploration and application of literacy specialist roles. Includes teaching, coaching, providing resources, advocating for all students, and collaborating with other professionals.

EDCS 606.title: Introduction to Research in Curriculum and Teaching
EDCS 606.subject: EDCS
EDCS 606.description: Classroom-based research covers the fundamentals of qualitative, quantitative, action research, mixed methods, and curriculum based assessment. Exploratory, explanatory, and confirmatory research will be highlighted culminating in an outline for Plan B/Thesis proposal.

EDCS 607.title: New Literacies Leadership +
EDCS 607.subject: EDCS
EDCS 607.description: New approaches to analyzing 21st century literacies K-12, including visual, media, digital, and critical literacies as well as developing leadership practices in multi-literacies pedagogy.

EDCS 608.title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
EDCS 608.subject: EDCS
EDCS 608.description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts. Graduate students only.

EDCS 610.title: Early Career Teaching, K-12
EDCS 610.subject: EDCS
EDCS 610.description: Focuses on research and practice related to the first five years of teaching. Especially recommended for beginning teachers and graduate students interested in this stage of teaching development.

EDCS 617.title: Early Literacy and Language Development
EDCS 617.subject: EDCS
EDCS 617.description: Theory and practice for PK-3 early literacy and language development. Focus is on content knowledge and pedagogical strategies that support the optimal development of oral language, reading, and writing skills in PK-3 classrooms.

EDCS 618.title: Early Childhood Education: Advanced Topics
EDCS 618.subject: EDCS
EDCS 618.description: Analysis and practical application of selected early childhood education program and/ or instructional materials. Restricted to majors.

EDCS 619.title: Social and Cultural Constructions of Childhood
EDCS 619.subject: EDCS
EDCS 619.description: Seminar examines the interrelated socially constructed concepts of children and childhood and places them in the larger contexts informed by sociological, anthropological, historical, critical, and technological perspectives. Graduate students only.

EDCS 623.title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
EDCS 623.subject: EDCS
EDCS 623.description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

EDCS 624.title: School Mathematics Curriculum
EDCS 624.subject: EDCS
EDCS 624.description: Analysis of research related to teaching and learning school mathematics, application of research to classroom practices. Appraisal of recent curriculum trends; critical examination of assumptions underlying proposed curriculum changes.

EDCS 625.title: Social Studies Curriculum
EDCS 625.subject: EDCS
EDCS 625.description: Examination and evaluation of social science content, societal values and research findings as basis for development and revision of social studies materials, texts, curriculum guides, methodology.
EDCS 625.prereq_raw: ITE 322 or equivalent, social studies teaching experience, or consent

EDCS 626.title: Art Education K-12
EDCS 626.subject: EDCS
EDCS 626.description: Principles, goals, and objectives in teaching and learning art K-12; curriculum, instruction, and assessment in art education; laboratory experiences in art media.

EDCS 627.title: Teaching and Learning with Art Objects, Museums, Collections, and Site Visits
EDCS 627.subject: EDCS
EDCS 627.description: Interdisciplinary inquiry and examination of the role of physical objects and site visits in schools and other educational contexts, through visits to local art museums and related sites.

EDCS 628.title: Function of Play in Early Childhood Education
EDCS 628.subject: EDCS
EDCS 628.description: Review of research and theory illuminating the nature, purposes, and meaning of play as a critical aspect of early childhood education.

EDCS 630.title: Cultural Diversity and Education
EDCS 630.subject: EDCS
EDCS 630.description: Examines issues, theories, perspectives and practices in multicultural education and promotes awareness, encourages knowledgeable reflection and develops skills necessary for multicultural practitioners.

EDCS 632.title: Qualitative Research Methods
EDCS 632.subject: EDCS
EDCS 632.description: Methods of qualitative research in education or related social science from an interdisciplinary framework.

EDCS 639.title: Business and Marketing Education Curriculum
EDCS 639.subject: EDCS
EDCS 639.description: Theory, philosophy, objectives, and development of business and marketing education curriculum.

EDCS 645.title: Seminar In Multicultural Literacy
EDCS 645.subject: EDCS
EDCS 645.description: Interdisciplinary examination of research and issues in the teaching and learning of literacy in diverse multicultural settings.

EDCS 646.title: Literacy Assessment, Instruction, and Intervention
EDCS 646.subject: EDCS
EDCS 646.description: Application of formative assessments to better monitor/guide struggling readers and writers. Topics include diversity and state/national initiatives.

EDCS 647.title: Classroom and School Literacy Assessment
EDCS 647.subject: EDCS
EDCS 647.description: Advanced use of formative and summative assessments to monitor/lead classroom and school literacy programs. Focus on diversity, leadership, state/national initiatives, and practical applications in schools or other educational contexts.

EDCS 648.title: Reading for English Language Learners
EDCS 648.subject: EDCS
EDCS 648.description: Presents key concepts and theories in teaching reading to K-12 English language learners. Topics include instructional decisions in teaching reading to ELLs, the interrelationship of language skills, strategies, and teaching academic content.

EDCS 649.title: Theory/Practice in Cooperative Occupational Education
EDCS 649.subject: EDCS
EDCS 649.description: Theory and practices of coordinating cooperative education in high school and community college.

EDCS 654.title: Ethnomathematics
EDCS 654.subject: EDCS
EDCS 654.description: Research and practice in ethnomathematics from an interdisciplinary framework. Analysis of ethnomathematics content knowledge and pedagogy; connections among curriculum, standards, and classroom practice; examination of theory and research; and building sustainable campus-community networks. Topics vary.

EDCS 656.title: Seminar in Issues in ECE
EDCS 656.subject: EDCS
EDCS 656.description: Concepts and inquiry regarding the application of early childhood educational principles and approaches to programs serving children between birth and age five. Study and discussion of topics and problems presented in required summer courses and by invited experts in early childhood education. Restricted to masters in Early Childhood Education. (Two times a year)

EDCS 677.title: Curriculum Design in Early Childhood Education
EDCS 677.subject: EDCS
EDCS 677.description: Designed to help classroom teachers understand sources and principles of curriculum in early childhood education and to provide experience in evaluating, selecting, and developing appropriate curriculum for young children.

EDCS 685.title: Museums and Education
EDCS 685.subject: EDCS
EDCS 685.description: ) Overview of museum education including museum learning theories, informal learning programs, audience research, national and international policies and reports, and community projects.

EDCS 686.title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
EDCS 686.subject: EDCS
EDCS 686.description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

EDCS 690.title: School and District Literacy Leadership
EDCS 690.subject: EDCS
EDCS 690.description: Exploration and application of school and district-wide roles of the literacy specialist, such as collaborating with other educators to: (1) design and implement literacy programs, and (2) provide research-supported professional development.

EDCS 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
EDCS 695.subject: EDCS
EDCS 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project.

EDCS 696.title: Graduate Certificate Capstone
EDCS 696.subject: EDCS
EDCS 696.description: Independent study and/or seminar for students working on a capstone for a graduate certificate.

EDCS 732.title: Qualitative Data Analysis
EDCS 732.subject: EDCS
EDCS 732.description: Advanced seminar in qualitative research methods with an emphasis upon qualitative data analysis, theory construction, data presentation and reporting.

EDCS 760.title: Research on Teaching and Teacher Education
EDCS 760.subject: EDCS
EDCS 760.description: Examination of alternative approaches and multidisciplinary perspectives on research on teaching and learning in and out of school, on educational change, and on teacher education and professional development.

EDCS 761.title: Dissertation Research and Writing
EDCS 761.subject: EDCS
EDCS 761.description: Intended for doctoral students who are at the dissertation stage in their program. Supports students in developing their dissertation proposals and/or initial dissertation drafts.

EDCS 767.title: Issues and Trends in Curriculum
EDCS 767.subject: EDCS
EDCS 767.description: Uses problem-centered approach and field experiences. Topics include historical review of curriculum development since 1900, examination of current curriculum practices at all levels of education, and prediction of future directions in curriculum theory and design.

EDCS 768.title: Seminar in Curriculum and Instructional Theories
EDCS 768.subject: EDCS
EDCS 768.description: Analysis and critical examination of models and curriculum theory and theories of instruction leading to generation of theories by seminar members.

EDCS 769.title: Curriculum and Program Evaluation
EDCS 769.subject: EDCS
EDCS 769.description: Critical examination of theoretical and methodological positions on curriculum and educational program evaluation.

EDCS 780.title: Mixed Methods Research Design
EDCS 780.subject: EDCS
EDCS 780.description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. (Once a year)

EDEA 360.title: Dynamics of Student Leadership

EDEA 370.title: Peer Leadership Education and Mentoring

EDEA 499.title: Directed Reading

EDEA 601.title: Introduction to Education Administration
EDEA 601.subject: EDEA
EDEA 601.description: Develops view of administrative process and organization elements in context of system of personal, social, and physical variables. Emphasis on role and functions of school administrator.

EDEA 602.title: Research in Education Administration
EDEA 602.subject: EDEA
EDEA 602.description: Develops basic concepts of research on educational administration: methodology, status of particular topics, communication, and application of findings to problems of school administration. (Meets PhD common core inquiry methods requirement.)

EDEA 604.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
EDEA 604.subject: EDEA
EDEA 604.description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.)

EDEA 608.subject: EDEA

EDEA 610.title: School-Community Relations
EDEA 610.subject: EDEA

EDEA 623.title: Administration in Kinesiology
EDEA 623.subject: EDEA
EDEA 623.description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings.

EDEA 629.title: Educational Statistics
EDEA 629.subject: EDEA

EDEA 645.title: Principles of School Leadership
EDEA 645.subject: EDEA
EDEA 645.description: Examine the emergent theories, issues, practices, and problems relevant for educational leaders in school organizations. Integrates the aspects of management and administration within the context of leadership.

EDEA 646.title: College Student Development Theory
EDEA 646.subject: EDEA
EDEA 646.description: Study of psycho-social characteristics of the American college student and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work.

EDEA 650.title: Organizational Leadership in Education
EDEA 650.subject: EDEA
EDEA 650.description: Analysis of the nature of organizations, human nature and needs, and their relationship to leadership, staffing, and staff development. Implications of group structure and human conflict, communications, and supervision and evaluation considered.

EDEA 652.title: Conflict Management for Educators
EDEA 652.subject: EDEA
EDEA 652.description: Conflict resolution theory and practice for administrators, faculty and staff in educational organizations. K-12, community colleges and universities. Application and theory of negotiation, mediation, facilitation and hybrid ADR processes.

EDEA 655.title: Intercultural Interactions

EDEA 655.description: Theory-based frameworks and training methods of intercultural interaction and their applications to educational administration situations.

EDEA 657.title: Introduction to Higher Education
EDEA 657.subject: EDEA
EDEA 657.description: Salient historic, social, and organizational aspects of higher education; history, philosophy, purposes, governance, administration, structures, financing, faculty and student selection, curricula, legal and social issues.

EDEA 660.title: Leadership in Higher Education

EDEA 661.description: Philosophy, history, organization, and administration of student personnel services at college and university levels, including admissions, housing, student activities, financial aids, placement, counseling, health services.

EDEA 662.subject: EDEA
EDEA 662.description: Traditional and contemporary curriculum issues. Development of performance competencies in curriculum design and evaluation using systems and design theory as central paradigms.

EDEA 663.title: Community College Leadership
EDEA 663.subject: EDEA
EDEA 663.description: Development and changing missions of community colleges; in-depth study of emerging leadership issues: planning, financial management, decision-making, governance, and student personnel.

EDEA 670.title: Teacher Development and Evaluation

EDEA 670.description: The role of teacher evaluation in the development of teachers and learning communities and to support effective teaching.

EDEA 675.description: Examines theories and models of educational policy and policy-making and the contribution of policy analysis to the policy-making and change processes.

EDEA 676.description: Examination of the ways in which education can be viewed as political, arising from its connection to the larger political system including local, state, and federal governments.

EDEA 767.subject: EDEA
EDEA 767.description: Examination of structure and dynamics of the educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior.

EDEA 775.title: Seminar on the Principalship
EDEA 775.subject: EDEA
EDEA 775.description: Series of planned seminar experiences on problems and issues confronting school principals, such as contract administration, program planning and budgeting systems (PPBS), teacher evaluation. Topic to be announced.

EDEF 352.subject: EDEF
EDEF 352.description: History of educational though and practices from pre-contact Hawaii through statehood. (Spring only

EDEF 360.description: Concepts and methods to develop sensitivity and awareness of cultural influences on behavior as these relate to the schooling process.

EDEF 686.description: Focuses on the development of an ecological consciousness through a cultural and environmental approach to teaching and learning in schooling and everyday life.

EDEF 725.description: Study of classical and contemporary theories of social change as these relate to school, the profession of teaching, planning of change, and social stability.

EDEF 762.title: Seminar on the Social and Cultural Contexts of Education
EDEF 762.subject: EDEF
EDEF 762.description: Examination of social, political, and cultural issues affecting educational policy with special emphasis on methods of inquiry and theoretical constructs.

EDEF 764.title: Advanced Seminar in Philosophy of Education
EDEF 764.subject: EDEF
EDEF 764.description: Advanced studies in philosophical inquiry. Examination of philosophically based methods of analysis and interpretation and their influence in educational research and practice.

EDEF 766.title: Seminar in History of Education
EDEF 766.subject: EDEF
EDEF 766.description: Aspects of the history of education. Application of historiography to educational problems and policy.

EDEF 767.title: Seminar on the Educational System
EDEF 767.subject: EDEF
EDEF 767.description: Examination of the structure and dynamics of educational system. Particular focus on how educational policy interacts with principles that explain educational system behavior.

EDEF 771.title: Seminar in Comparative/International Education
EDEF 771.subject: EDEF
EDEF 771.description: Advanced reading, research and writing in selected topics dealing with comparative and international education, including such themes as policy studies, minority education and educational reform.

EDEP 201.title: Introduction to Teaching as a Career
EDEP 201.subject: EDEP
EDEP 201.description: An experience-based introduction to teaching as a career.

EDEP 311.title: Introduction to Educational Psychology
EDEP 311.subject: EDEP
EDEP 311.description: Psychology as applied to education, including major theories and research and development, cognitive, sociocultural, and multicultural approaches to teaching and learning. Incorporates introductions to standardized testing, classroom assessment, motivation, instructional planning and classroom management.

EDEP 327.title: Self-Regulated Learning
EDEP 327.subject: EDEP
EDEP 327.description: Theory and use of self-regulated learning strategies in academic contexts.

EDEP 408.title: Fundamentals of Research in Education
EDEP 408.subject: EDEP
EDEP 408.description: Introduction to the methodology of systematic study of problems in education: principles of research design, data processing, technical writing, and evaluation of research proposals and reports.

EDEP 411.title: Seminar in Contemporary Perspectives in Educational Psychology
EDEP 411.subject: EDEP
EDEP 411.description: In-depth analysis of contemporary issues in education from the theoretical and methodological perspectives of the faculty in educational psychology.

EDEP 416.title: Student Assessment
EDEP 416.subject: EDEP
EDEP 416.description: Introduction to basic concepts and issues in assessment and measurement, development of formative and summative assessment procedures, descriptive statistics, scales of measurement, and standardizing testing.

EDEP 429.title: Introductory Statistics
EDEP 429.subject: EDEP
EDEP 429.description: Introduction to concepts and logics of statistical reasoning and statistical literacy. Topics include descriptive statistics, sampling distribution, and inferential statistics such as z-test, t-tests, correlation, and one-way ANOVA.

EDEP 432.title: Human Motivation and Education
EDEP 432.subject: EDEP
EDEP 432.description: Application of motivation theory and research to understanding and increasing human motivation for education.

EDEP 489.title: Applied Psychology: Advanced Topics
EDEP 489.subject: EDEP
EDEP 489.description: Coverage in-depth of some areas of theory and research.

EDEP 601.title: Introduction to Quantitative Methods
EDEP 601.subject: EDEP
EDEP 601.description: Introductory graduate-level statistics in education and social sciences. Topics on descriptive and inferential statistics including central tendency, variability, sampling distribution, z-test, t-test, correlation, simple linear regression, and one-way ANOVA. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

EDEP 602.title: Survey Research Design and Analysis
EDEP 602.subject: EDEP
EDEP 602.description: Survey study designs, survey sampling, questionnaire construction, interviewing, pre-tests, pilot studies, logic of measurement and association, table construction, and elaboration models.

EDEP 603.title: Design and Analysis of Psychological Experiments
EDEP 603.subject: EDEP
EDEP 603.description: Analysis of variance and other models of assessing results of experiments. Relation of analysis to design.

EDEP 604.title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
EDEP 604.subject: EDEP
EDEP 604.description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.
EDEP 604.prereq_raw: 601 or EDEA 629 (with a grade of B+), or consent

EDEP 606.title: Multivariate Methods
EDEP 606.subject: EDEP
EDEP 606.description: Multivariate forms of multiple linear regression, analysis of variance and co-variance, and exploratory factor analysis are developed.

EDEP 607.title: Nonparametric Methods for Behavioral Science
EDEP 607.subject: EDEP
EDEP 607.description: Conditions for valid applications of nonparametric statistical techniques in education and behavioral sciences; theoretical and methodological perspectives.

EDEP 608.title: Introduction to Educational Research
EDEP 608.subject: EDEP
EDEP 608.description: Fundamental design and evaluation procedures in educational research. Topics include an introduction to qualitative and quantitative research, the review of literature, developing research questions, research design, instrumentation, data collection, and writing a research proposal.
EDEP 608.prereq_raw: 601 (or concurrent) (with a minimum grade of B or higher) or consent

EDEP 611.title: Graduate Introduction to Educational Psychology
EDEP 611.subject: EDEP
EDEP 611.description: Graduate level introduction to educational psychology theories, research, and topics.

EDEP 612.title: Multilevel Modeling for Cross-Sectional and Longitudinal Data
EDEP 612.subject: EDEP
EDEP 612.description: Theories and applications of multilevel model to analyze cross-sectional and longitudinal data. Topics include two-level and three-level models, growth models, and multilevel logistic regression.
EDEP 612.prereq_raw: 604, PSY 610, 612 (with a minimum grade of B or higher), or consent

EDEP 613.title: Qualitative Research Methods in Education
EDEP 613.subject: EDEP
EDEP 613.description: Introduction to methods of qualitative research in education. (Meets PhD common core requirement.)

EDEP 616.title: Measurement in Education and Social Sciences
EDEP 616.subject: EDEP
EDEP 616.description: Concepts, theories and practices in testing and measurement. Specific topics include classical and modern test theories, reliability estimation, validity, psychometric validation methods including factor analysis and item response theory.

EDEP 618.title: Categorical Data Analysis
EDEP 618.subject: EDEP
EDEP 618.description: Theories and methods for data analysis with categorical and discrete variables; analysis of contingency tables, loglinear models, introduction to generalized linear models for binary, nominal, ordinal, and count outcomes in cross-sectional and longitudinal data sets.

EDEP 625.title: Structural Equation Modeling
EDEP 625.subject: EDEP
EDEP 625.description: Theories and applications to test models with manifest and latent variables. Topics include path analysis, factor analysis, latent variable model, multi-group analysis, latent means model, and other advanced topics in SEM.

EDEP 626.title: Psychometric Methods
EDEP 626.subject: EDEP
EDEP 626.description: Theories and applications of modern psychometrics. Topics include item response theory, detecting biased items, measurement invariance, and current issues in psychometrics.
EDEP 626.prereq_raw: 604 (with a minimum grade of B+) or consent

EDEP 631.title: Adolescence and Education
EDEP 631.subject: EDEP
EDEP 631.description: Discussion-based course presenting an overview of educational psychology applied to teaching adolescents, including theory and research on human learning, adolescent development and its social context, and student assessment.

EDEP 657.title: Introduction to Program Evaluation
EDEP 657.subject: EDEP
EDEP 657.description: Introduction to concepts and issues related to program evaluation. Topics include formative and summative uses, planning and design approaches, and metaevaluation processes.

EDEP 661.title: Development and Learning
EDEP 661.subject: EDEP
EDEP 661.description: Analysis and critique of (Piagetian) developmental stage theory and traditional behavioristic and cognitive learning theories; introduction to current models of learning and development.

EDEP 662.title: Social Context of Learning
EDEP 662.subject: EDEP
EDEP 662.description: Research methods and theories relating social mediation and learning group structures to intellectual growth.

EDEP 663.title: Models of Cognitive Learning
EDEP 663.subject: EDEP
EDEP 663.description: Cognitive models of knowledge acquisition, organization, and utilization; theory and research relating learning and cognition to interactive instructional models.

EDEP 664.title: Instructional Psychology
EDEP 664.subject: EDEP
EDEP 664.description: Application of learning theory and cognitive skills training in instructional settings.

EDEP 665.title: Social Cognition and Competence
EDEP 665.subject: EDEP
EDEP 665.description: Systematic analysis of social reasoning abilities conjunctive with or prerequisite to effective social interaction in educational settings.

EDEP 685.title: Capstone Project in Educational Psychology
EDEP 685.subject: EDEP
EDEP 685.description: To be taken in the final semester or the second to last semester to complete the certificate. Students are expected to integrate, extend, critique and apply knowledge learned in the certificate program.

EDEP 711.title: Practicum in Educational Psychology
EDEP 711.subject: EDEP
EDEP 711.description: Supervised practicum in teaching or program evaluation as each is reflected by professional activities of the members of the faculty.

EDEP 745.title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
EDEP 745.subject: EDEP
EDEP 745.description: Analysis of psychology of adult learner; forces that affect learning in dynamics of individual, group, and organizational behavior; concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.

EDUC 615.title: Action Research in Education
EDUC 615.subject: EDUC
EDUC 615.description: Theory and practice in collaborative action research; critical inquiry into current educational work in schools with goals of improvement of teaching and participation in school and curriculum reform.

EDUC 616.title: Prevention of School Violence
EDUC 616.subject: EDUC
EDUC 616.description: Examines cultural and societal factors contributing to and extent of violence in schools, and outlines schoolwide education for social and emotional literacy, conflict resolution, peer mediation, and appreciation of diversity for peaceable and inclusive schools and communities.

EDUC 617.title: HIV, STD, and Pregnancy Prevention
EDUC 617.subject: EDUC
EDUC 617.description: Development of effective school-based HIV, STD, and unintended pregnancy prevention strategies, based on curriculum evaluation research and participant and student inquiries. Emphasis on serving as classroom models and mentors for other educators.

EDUC 710.title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Consultancy Project
EDUC 710.subject: EDUC
EDUC 710.description: Practicum in the EdD program in professional practice; involves a group consultancy project requiring independent research and reflective activity embedded in a group project dealing with a problem of practice. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 720.title: Professional Doctorate Practicum: Individual Applied Research Project
EDUC 720.subject: EDUC
EDUC 720.description: Practicum in conducting individual practitioner research within the EdD. Includes the formulation of individual applied research project, developing a plan of action, selection of appropriate methods, implementation of plan and composition of practitioner research report. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 730.title: EdD Conference
EDUC 730.subject: EDUC
EDUC 730.description: Capstone for the Doctoral Degree in Professional Education Practice. Involves a conference presentation of research project results to an audience of faculty, fellow graduate students, and interested members of the public. Restricted to students in the Doctoral Degree in Professional Educational Practice.

EDUC 740.title: Field Project
EDUC 740.subject: EDUC
EDUC 740.description: Practicum experience in area of specialization. Variable credit: minimum of 3 credit hours, maximum of 6 credit hours.

EDUC 799.title: Internship in College Teaching
EDUC 799.subject: EDUC
EDUC 799.description: Introduction to college-level teaching; doctoral students serve as apprentices to professors; responsibilities include supervised teaching, planning and evaluation.
EDUC 799.prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy and consent

ESEE 310.title: Learner in the Environment I: Social and Cultural Contexts for Learning
ESEE 310.subject: ESEE
ESEE 310.description: Knowledge and skills related to the context of teaching. Teacher candidates will examine the impact of culture, family, school, classroom, and individual characteristics on learning, and orally present, in varied formats, acquired knowledge and competencies.

ESEE 311.title: Learner in the Environment II: Classroom and Behavior Management
ESEE 311.subject: ESEE
ESEE 311.description: Teacher candidates explore the ethical implications for establishing, maintaining, and restoring the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning.

ESEE 312.title: Learner in the Environment III: Behavior Project Implementation
ESEE 312.subject: ESEE
ESEE 312.description: Teacher candidates demonstrate the ability to establish, maintain, and (when necessary) restore the classroom as an effective environment for teaching and learning. Candidates demonstrate ability to identify maladaptive student behaviors and implement effective, research-based interventions.

ESEE 320.title: Assessment I: Foundations of Assessment
ESEE 320.subject: ESEE
ESEE 320.description: Introduction to foundational aspects of assessment and emphasizes the importance of linking assessment with planning and instruction. Candidates develop knowledge, skills, and dispositions important for designing, implementing, and analyzing effective assessments for diverse learners.

ESEE 321.title: Assessment II: Formal Assessment
ESEE 321.subject: ESEE
ESEE 321.description: Understand techniques in the assessment, planning, and instructional process appropriate for students with mild/moderate disabilities. Inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment is stressed. Significant instruction on writing individualized education programs.

ESEE 330.title: Planning and Instruction: Introduction to Inclusive Teaching
ESEE 330.subject: ESEE
ESEE 330.description: Teacher candidates engage in reflective, procedural, and research writing to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

ESEE 331.title: Planning and Instruction: Science
ESEE 331.subject: ESEE
ESEE 331.description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to the teaching and learning of science in elementary settings, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, using evidence-based practices.

ESEE 332.title: Planning and Instruction: Mathematics in Inclusive Settings
ESEE 332.subject: ESEE
ESEE 332.description: Prepares beginning elementary school teachers of mathematics, K-6. Candidates learn to differentiate instruction based on learner needs, planning to facilitate inclusion of students with disabilities in the general education environment through evidence-based practices.

ESEE 333.title: Planning and Instruction: STEM
ESEE 333.subject: ESEE
ESEE 333.description: Examination of content, processes, strategies, and issues related to teaching and learning of Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) content for inclusive elementary classrooms, K-6. Teacher candidates focus on planning, teaching, and assessing STEM.

ESEE 334.title: Planning and Instruction: Integrating Social Studies and the Performing Arts
ESEE 334.subject: ESEE
ESEE 334.description: Social Studies and Performing Arts integrated content in diverse K-6 classrooms. Teacher candidates engage with social issues through collaborative, expressive, aesthetic, creative, and critical pedagogy. Candidates perform, present, and teach to develop oral communication skills.

ESEE 340.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy I: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, K-3
ESEE 340.subject: ESEE
ESEE 340.description: Overview of principles and practices for teaching reading (phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary, comprehension) to diverse students, grades K-3; including planning, instruction, and assessment. Writing assignments include lesson reflections, case studies, modules, and reading responses.

ESEE 341.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy II: Teaching Children to Read in Inclusive Settings, Grades 4-6
ESEE 341.subject: ESEE
ESEE 341.description: Teacher candidates demonstrate essential reading comprehension strategies, engaging students in complex text by planning, instructing, and assessing elementary students in grades 4-6, in inclusive settings. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ESEE 342.title: Planning and Instruction, Literacy III: Writing and Visual Arts in Inclusive Settings, K-6
ESEE 342.subject: ESEE
ESEE 342.description: Methods, programs, and strategies for planning, teaching, and assessing writing for elementary students in inclusive settings, grades K-6. Visual arts methods are integrated to develop visual literacy.

ESEE 350.title: Field Experience I: Response to Intervention in Reading
ESEE 350.subject: ESEE
ESEE 350.description: Teacher candidates in this field based course will use an evidencebased practice in reading within a response to intervention (Rtl) framework. Supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

ESEE 351.title: Field Rounds
ESEE 351.subject: ESEE
ESEE 351.description: Field-based course engages teacher candidates in a variety of purposeful observation and reflection activities aligned with course work. Field settings are appropriate to concurrent classes; supervision provided by participating site personnel and college supervisor.

ESEE 352.title: Field Experience II: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
ESEE 352.subject: ESEE
ESEE 352.description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

ESEE 353.title: Field Experience III: Elementary and Special Education Classroom Settings
ESEE 353.subject: ESEE
ESEE 353.description: Teacher candidates are immersed in a general education, inclusion, or a self-contained special education field setting. A mentor teacher and a field supervisor from the university provide support and oversight.

ESEE 354.title: Student Teaching in Elementary and Special Education Classrooms
ESEE 354.subject: ESEE
ESEE 354.description: Full-time student teaching in grades K-6 in an elementary school inclusion classroom, or a combination of general education and special education settings. The experience is directed by a qualified mentor teacher and has university-provided supervision.

ESEE 355.title: Seminar for Student Teaching
ESEE 355.subject: ESEE
ESEE 355.description: Seminar to support student teaching experiences and prepare teacher candidates to transition into a full time teacher, examine ethical issues in the field, prepare for employment, and demonstrate ability to meet professional standards.

ITE 315.title: Field Training – Blended ECE
ITE 315.subject: ITE
ITE 315.description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.
ITE 315.prereq_raw: 415 and SPED 304 (with a minimum grade of B-), or consent

ITE 316.title: Field Experience
ITE 316.subject: ITE
ITE 316.description: Supervised field experience in schools. Minimum of 8 hours per week in conjunction with professional education courses.

ITE 318.title: Child Development from Prenatal Through Age Eight
ITE 318.subject: ITE
ITE 318.description: Growth and development of children from prenatal through age eight. Historical and current issues through a research-based ecological, cross-cultural perspective. Focus on children’s optimal development and how this informs teaching practices in early education.

ITE 319.title: Children’s Literature
ITE 319.subject: ITE
ITE 319.description: Acquaintance with wide range of children’s books; criteria for evaluation of literature; using literature in the classroom.

ITE 320.title: Instructional and Assessment Methods for Multilingual Learners
ITE 320.subject: ITE
ITE 320.description: Introduction to language use and development as it relates to multilingual learners (MLL). Candidates analyze and apply strategies to create inclusive and collaborative classrooms for learners at various levels of English language development.

ITE 321.title: Social Studies and Science in Early Childhood Education
ITE 321.subject: ITE
ITE 321.description: Assessment, instructional methods, and materials for teaching social studies and science to children in preschool through grade 3. Emphasis on developmentally appropriate practices and lesson planning for teaching social studies and science.

ITE 327.title: Curriculum, Materials, and Assessment Development for Multilingual Learners
ITE 327.subject: ITE
ITE 327.description: Introduction to the development of curriculum materials, and assessments for diverse and multilingual learners. Teacher candidates will develop their ability to organize, develop, and assess learning around standards-based subject matter and language learning objectives.

ITE 328.title: Responsive Pedagogy for Multilingual Learners
ITE 328.subject: ITE
ITE 328.description: Introduction to the teaching of multilingual learners (MLL) in an elementary school context. Teacher candidates will learn specific strategies and methods for teaching non-native speakers of English.

ITE 346.title: Methods of Instruction, Industrial/ Agricultural Education
ITE 346.subject: ITE
ITE 346.description: Techniques of individual and group instruction in laboratory and related classes, evaluation of various methods.

ITE 347.title: Management of Industrial/Agricultural Facilities
ITE 347.subject: ITE
ITE 347.description: Organization of instruction; handling supplies; maintaining equipment and tools; purchasing materials; keeping records; making inventories.

ITE 348.title: Teaching Business and Office Education
ITE 348.subject: ITE
ITE 348.description: Theory and methods of teaching business and office education courses.
ITE 348.prereq_raw: ACC 201 and either ACC 200 or ACC 202

ITE 349.title: Teaching Marketing and Distribution
ITE 349.subject: ITE
ITE 349.description: Theory and methods of teaching marketing and distribution courses.

ITE 353.title: Music in the Elementary School
ITE 353.subject: ITE
ITE 353.description: Goals, concepts, literature, materials, procedures, and evaluation for teaching music in grades K–6. For students in elementary education. Not intended for elementary music majors.

ITE 360.title: Introduction to Multicultural Education
ITE 360.subject: ITE
ITE 360.description: Concepts and methods to develop sensitivity and awareness of cultural influences on behavior as these relate to the schooling process.

ITE 371.title: Home Economics Education
ITE 371.subject: ITE
ITE 371.description: Curriculum design. Current educational philosophies and practices in home economics education. Teaching materials and techniques.

ITE 380.title: Managing Classrooms
ITE 380.subject: ITE
ITE 380.description: Analysis of the factors that contribute to learning in the classroom and the development of teacher behaviors that promote such learning.

ITE 399.title: Directed Study
ITE 399.subject: ITE
ITE 399.description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, observation/participation, teaching, and/or projects.

ITE 401.title: Principles & Methods of Literacies Within and Across the Disciplines (6-12)
ITE 401.subject: ITE
ITE 401.description: Examines how reading, writing, speaking, listening, technology, etc. are tools for learning content and engaging diverse adolescents across and within all disciplines. Includes a disciplinary literacies framework influencing curriculum planning, classroom culture, and assessment practices.

ITE 406.title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
ITE 406.subject: ITE
ITE 406.description: Analysis and resolution of current ethical issues and practices in classrooms; teaching skills and strategies; curriculum planning, professional growth and development; and integration of teaching experiences with professional standards. Instruction in preparing an extensive written portfolio.
ITE 406.prereq_raw: successful completion of all required courses or consent

children.text: successful completion of all required courses

ITE 410.title: Supervision of the ObservationParticipation Student
ITE 410.subject: ITE
ITE 410.description: Basic guidelines for developing effective team relationships between the professional teacher and the observation-participation student.
ITE 410.prereq_raw: two years’ teaching experience and consent
