ITE 415.title: Observation and Assessment in Early Childhood Education
ITE 415.subject: ITE
ITE 415.description: Introduction to the purposes, theories, and methods of early childhood assessment. Emphasizes observation, documentation, and assessment to provide evidence of children’s development and learning and how to use assessment to guide teaching and learning.

ITE 415L.title: Observation and Assessment in Early Childhood Education Lab
ITE 415L.subject: ITE
ITE 415L.description: Field experience in early childhood settings to facilitate young children’s growth and learning.

ITE 416.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children
ITE 416.subject: ITE
ITE 416.description: Continuation of 415: focuses on the design, implementation, evaluation of meaningful, challenging integrated curriculum that promotes comprehensive developmental and learning outcomes for diverse young children (pK-3).

ITE 416L.title: Teaching and Learning for Diverse Young Children Lab
ITE 416L.subject: ITE

ITE 417.title: Foundations of Early Childhood Education, Ages 3–8
ITE 417.subject: ITE
ITE 417.description: Planning child-centered, responsive programs for children. Focuses on play, learning environments, integrated thematic instructional design, guidance, assessment, and family engagement in early childhood and early elementary to promote enjoyment, growth, and development.

ITE 420.title: Supervision of Student Teaching
ITE 420.subject: ITE
ITE 420.description: Principles and methods; role of supervisor; human resources supervision in student teaching. Open to teachers interested in pre-service teacher education.
ITE 420.prereq_raw: three years teaching experience and consent

ITE 425.title: Family and Community Centered Programs
ITE 425.subject: ITE
ITE 425.description: Knowledge and appreciation for the complex characteristics of children, families, and communities. Analysis and development of skills for creating respectful, reciprocal relationships with diverse children and families from diverse backgrounds. Lecture/lab.
ITE 425.prereq_raw: 318 (or concurrent), or HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent

ITE 430.title: Advanced Supervision of Student Teaching
ITE 430.subject: ITE
ITE 430.description: Advanced principles and methods: clinical supervision, observation recording, analysis, interpretation of classroom teaching; human resources supervision in student teaching.
ITE 430.prereq_raw: 420, successful supervision of two or more student teachers, and consent

ITE 436.title: Cooperative Vocational Education
ITE 436.subject: ITE
ITE 436.description: Planned work-experience program for special areas of vocational technical education. Acceptable type of wage-earning employment. Minimum of six 40- hour weeks or 240 work hours required.

ITE 438.title: Foundations of Vocational Education
ITE 438.subject: ITE
ITE 438.description: Historical and philosophical foundations of vocational technical education, overview of federal and state legislation and contemporary practices. Special emphasis on vocational education program in Hawai‘i.

ITE 439.title: Office and Marketing Technology
ITE 439.subject: ITE
ITE 439.description: Understanding and use of word processing, spreadsheet, and database software for business applications. Explore software across the office and marketing content areas.

ITE 440.title: Curriculum Implications of Multicultural Education
ITE 440.subject: ITE
ITE 440.description: Examination of trends, issues, school practices, and program in multicultural education and its related area of study–bilingual-bicultural education.

ITE 441.title: Hawaiian Studies, Methods
ITE 441.subject: ITE
ITE 441.description: Examination of issues in Hawaiian and U.S. views of education and their application to the teaching of Hawaiian studies. Field experience required.
ITE 441.prereq_raw: 312C, 312D; or consent. Co-requisite for BEd students: 317

ITE 444.title: Education of Exceptional Children in Regular Classroom
ITE 444.subject: ITE
ITE 444.description: Practices that facilitate teaching special needs students in regular classrooms. Techniques for meeting academic needs, managing behavior, motivating students, increasing peer interactions, communication between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

ITE 445.title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms, Secondary
ITE 445.subject: ITE
ITE 445.description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

ITE 480.title: Issues in Computer Education
ITE 480.subject: ITE
ITE 480.description: Integration of microcomputers into school curriculum and key issues related to microcomputer use in education.

ITE 499.title: Directed Activity
ITE 499.subject: ITE
ITE 499.description: Individual work supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, teaching, and/or projects.

ITE 572.title: Common Core State Standards in ELA: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
ITE 572.subject: ITE
ITE 572.description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of ELA content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the ELA practices of the Common Core State Standards.

ITE 578.title: Common Core State Standards in Mathematics: Content and Curriculum for Teachers
ITE 578.subject: ITE
ITE 578.description: Professional development for K-12 teachers to upgrade their knowledge of mathematics content and develop their instructional strategies to be consistent with the mathematical practices of the Common Core State Standards.

ITE 600.title: Master of Education in Teaching Program Seminar
ITE 600.subject: ITE
ITE 600.description: Mandatory program seminar for Master of Education in Teaching (MEdT) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success, introduction to the teaching profession.
ITE 600.prereq_raw: admission into the MEdT program, or consent

KRS 101.title: Physical Fitness
KRS 101.subject: KRS
KRS 101.description: Conditioning exercises and activities to develop and maintain physical efficiency. Motor fitness tests administered to measure status and progress.

KRS 102.title: Aerobic Fitness
KRS 102.subject: KRS
KRS 102.description: Aerobic fitness improvement upon completion of course by regularly attending and practicing safe workout routines. Learn fitness components, names of muscles and exercises associated with each one.

KRS 103.title: Swimming: Beginning
KRS 103.subject: KRS
KRS 103.description: Adjusting to and immersing in water, floating, sculling; correct arm stroke, leg kick, breathing techniques and their coordination. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 104.title: Swimming: Intermediate
KRS 104.subject: KRS
KRS 104.description: Perfecting and integrating basic strokes with added emphasis for speed and distance. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 105.title: Swimming: Advanced
KRS 105.subject: KRS
KRS 105.description: Correct techniques used in competitive swimming, racing starts, correct turning techniques, long-distance swimming. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 106.title: SCUBA Diving: Beginning
KRS 106.subject: KRS
KRS 106.description: Learning watermanship, equipment handling skills, and the knowledge to become safe divers. Additional costs for equipment, diver manual, dive tables, and certification fee.

KRS 107.title: Aqua-Aerobic Fitness
KRS 107.subject: KRS
KRS 107.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on aerobic fitness improvement through total body aquatic workouts with music, and development of individualized aquatics fitness program. Open to all students.

KRS 110.title: Golf: Beginning
KRS 110.subject: KRS
KRS 110.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, stance, drive, normal iron shots, approach shots, putting.

KRS 111.title: Golf: Intermediate
KRS 111.subject: KRS
KRS 111.description: Corrective work on basic swing mechanics and rhythm; adjustments for bunker play, uphill lies, downhill lies, short game around and on the green; handicapping and match play competition.

KRS 112.title: Golf: Advanced
KRS 112.subject: KRS
KRS 112.description: Improving drive, fairway wood shots, long iron shots, control shots, trouble shots, putting, course management, competitive strategy, problems in rules. Greens fees paid by students for play on courses.

KRS 113.title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
KRS 113.subject: KRS
KRS 113.description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of those interested in pursuing health-related careers. Structure and function of major systems examined (gross anatomy, microanatomy, physiology, and pathology).

KRS 115.title: Bowling
KRS 115.subject: KRS
KRS 115.description: Rules, etiquette, arm swing, approach, execution, scoring, spare pickups. Students pay charge for use of alley.

KRS 120.title: Badminton
KRS 120.subject: KRS
KRS 120.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, smash, drive, net play, offensive and defensive strategy; singles and doubles play.

KRS 123.title: Folk and National Dances
KRS 123.subject: KRS
KRS 123.description: Popular dances of various national groups, including square dances.

KRS 124.title: Dances of Hawai‘i
KRS 124.subject: KRS
KRS 124.description: Background and fundamentals of hula. Selected dances with and without instruments.

KRS 125.title: Dances of Hawai‘i: Advanced
KRS 125.subject: KRS
KRS 125.description: Advanced techniques in hula movements. Selected dances taught will be more complex, including work with instruments. Individual choreography will be emphasized.

KRS 126.title: Social Dance: Ballroom
KRS 126.subject: KRS
KRS 126.description: Social dances including fox trot, waltz, swing, and other popular dances. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.

KRS 127.title: Social Dance: Latin
KRS 127.subject: KRS
KRS 127.description: Social dances of a Latin flavor including rhumba, cha-cha, tango, samba, and others. Basic steps, rhythm pattern, styling, and variations are taught. Social etiquette is stressed.

KRS 130.title: Tennis: Beginning
KRS 130.subject: KRS
KRS 130.description: Rules, etiquette, grip, forehand and backhand strokes, serving, volleying; singles and doubles play.

KRS 131.title: Tennis: Intermediate
KRS 131.subject: KRS
KRS 131.description: Corrective work in three basic strokes and in net play; the lob, drop shot, overhead smash, and half-volley; applying spin in basic strokes; basic strategy in singles and doubles play.

KRS 132.title: Tennis: Advanced
KRS 132.subject: KRS
KRS 132.description: Improving upon the strokes introduced in 130 and 131; advanced competitive strategy; problems in rules; officiating; elements of tournament play.

KRS 135.title: Volleyball: Beginning
KRS 135.subject: KRS
KRS 135.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on beginner skills and knowledge relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students.

KRS 136.title: Volleyball: Intermediate
KRS 136.subject: KRS
KRS 136.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on improving skills and knowledge through practice and cognitive activities relative to serving, passing, spiking, digging, blocking, and offensive and defensive strategy. Open to all students.

KRS 137.title: Basketball
KRS 137.subject: KRS
KRS 137.description: Rules, passing, shooting, dribbling, rebounding, individual defensive and offensive maneuvers; team offense and defense.

KRS 151.title: Adapted and Prescribed Exercises
KRS 151.subject: KRS
KRS 151.description: Small group and individual guidance and instruction for students recommended by student health service.

KRS 152.title: Weight Training
KRS 152.subject: KRS
KRS 152.description: Kinesiology of lifting and weight training, various types of exercises and methods of training with resistance.

KRS 153.title: Olympic and Power Lifting
KRS 153.subject: KRS
KRS 153.description: Exercise technique and prescription with an emphasis on anaerobic exercise. Explores advanced periodization models and their utilization, mastery of Olympic lifts, and plyometric programs.

KRS 154.title: Tumbling and Rebound Tumbling
KRS 154.subject: KRS
KRS 154.description: Single and combination stunts on tumbling mats and trampoline, balancing stunts; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.

KRS 156.title: Heavy Apparatus
KRS 156.subject: KRS
KRS 156.description: Single and combination stunts on side horse, horizontal bar, parallel bars, still rings; techniques of spotting; safety procedures.

KRS 160.title: Judo
KRS 160.subject: KRS
KRS 160.description: Rules, etiquette, method of falling and breaking the fall, simple throws and their counters, simple holds and breaking of such holds, randori. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 161.title: Aikido
KRS 161.subject: KRS
KRS 161.description: Rules, etiquette, basic rolls, simple holds and the breaking of such holds, specific physical conditioning exercises. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 163.title: T’ai Chi Ch’uan
KRS 163.subject: KRS
KRS 163.description: Classic forms of t’ai chi ch’uan.

KRS 164.title: Karate: Beginning
KRS 164.subject: KRS
KRS 164.description: Rules, etiquette, basic stances, blocks, thrusts, kicks, ippon kumite, and selected kata. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 165.title: Karate: Intermediate
KRS 165.subject: KRS
KRS 165.description: Emphasis on improving the basic techniques (stances, punches, kicks, forms, and sparring); introduction to combination techniques. (Student to provide own gi.)

KRS 167.title: Wrestling: Beginning
KRS 167.subject: KRS
KRS 167.description: Rules: fundamental defensive and offensive maneuvers and competitive strategy, i.e., takedowns, reversals, escapes, and pinning combinations; conditioning exercises.

KRS 170.title: Yoga: Beginning
KRS 170.subject: KRS
KRS 170.description: Experiencing yoga and its effects on body, mind and consciousness of individual. Encompasses exercise, breathing techniques, deep relaxation, meditation, practice in concentration, and yogic postures.

KRS 171.title: Yoga: Intermediate
KRS 171.subject: KRS
KRS 171.description: Corrective work and improvement of basic techniques. Exercise sets and combinations designed to develop endurance, flexibility, muscle and nerve strength, meditation, and deep relaxation technique.

KRS 173.title: Water Polo
KRS 173.subject: KRS
KRS 173.description: Fundamentals of basic water polo skills, namely, ball handling, passing, shooting, dribbling plus a brief introduction into beginning techniques of individual offense and defense.
KRS 173.prereq_raw: 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swimming attire approved by instructor.)

KRS 181.title: Sport Proficiency I: Invasion
KRS 181.subject: KRS
KRS 181.description: Knowledge, skill development, and strategy of various invasion type games and sports. Sports like basketball, soccer, ultimate frisbee and/or others are introduced within a tactical framework.

KRS 182.title: Sport Proficiency II: Net, Field, and Target
KRS 182.subject: KRS
KRS 182.description: Knowledge, skill development, position, and strategy of net, field and target sports. Sports like volleyball, tennis, softball, and golf are introduced within a tactical framework.

KRS 185.title: Floor Exercise Gymnastics
KRS 185.subject: KRS
KRS 185.description: An entry-level course designed to develop students’ knowledge of men’s and women’s gymnastics floor exercise routines, including injury prevention, skill progression, spotting techniques, and routine choreography. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.

KRS 186.title: Track and Field for Physical Education
KRS 186.subject: KRS
KRS 186.description: Knowledge, skills, and rules of various track and field events. Organization of track meets and strategy in competition. Primarily for KRS majors; others admitted on space-available basis.

KRS 187.title: Softball
KRS 187.subject: KRS
KRS 187.description: Combined lecture-lab-physical activity with emphasis on basic skills, rules, etiquette, offensive and defensive strategies, position play, and game situations. Open to all students.

KRS 201.title: School Health Problems: Elementary
KRS 201.subject: KRS
KRS 201.description: Responsibilities of elementary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing teacher’s role in health instruction, health services, school health policies.

KRS 202.title: School Health Problems: Secondary
KRS 202.subject: KRS
KRS 202.description: Responsibilities of secondary school teacher in recognizing and meeting pupils’ needs, emphasizing health instruction, health services, healthful school living, school health policies.

KRS 203.title: Introduction to Kinesiology
KRS 203.subject: KRS
KRS 203.description: Kinesiology as a professional field. Overview of history, philosophy, and current trends in kinesiology. Survey of psychological and sociological foundations of kinesiology, exercise, fitness and sport. KRS majors or approval.

KRS 208.title: Recreation Services in Contemporary Society
KRS 208.subject: KRS
KRS 208.description: Theories and philosophies in recreation: history; contemporary issues; roles in modern society; relationship to health, physical education, and exercise science.

KRS 210.title: Human Development
KRS 210.subject: KRS
KRS 210.description: Developmental processes across the life span. Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Human growth and development from conception to death with major theories and related research on maintaining healthy lifestyles.

KRS 232.title: Safety and Risk Management
KRS 232.subject: KRS
KRS 232.description: Understanding the fundamental principles and techniques of safety and accident-prevention programming emphasizing school, home, public places, on the job, and motor vehicle situations.

KRS 238.title: Outdoor Recreation Management
KRS 238.subject: KRS
KRS 238.description: Objectives and values of outdoor recreation; characteristics and determinants of programs; planning, organization, leadership, and facilities for recreational uses of natural environments.

KRS 241.title: Health Education Curriculum
KRS 241.subject: KRS
KRS 241.description: Objectives of school health program, emphasizing scope and sequence of health instruction; critical examination of health curriculum guides from various states.

KRS 249.title: Programming and Leadership
KRS 249.subject: KRS
KRS 249.description: Factors in planning and leading recreation programs; characteristics and responsibilities of leadership in relation to nature, scope, and resources of a variety of programs.

KRS 270.title: Introduction to Health and Physical Education
KRS 270.subject: KRS
KRS 270.description: Introduction to foundational knowledge for effective teaching, history, philosophy, and current practices in physical education. Provides the basis for later coursework in K-12 physical education. Required field experience.

KRS 271.title: Performance Based Assessment in Health and Physical Education
KRS 271.subject: KRS
KRS 271.description: Assessment and evaluative techniques applied to health and physical education, including test construction, performance-based assessment, measurement criteria and instruments, interpretation of data and content, as well as program evaluation.

KRS 302.title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
KRS 302.subject: KRS
KRS 302.description: Understanding standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment in health with a focus on advocacy, as well as the incidence, prevalence, and prevention of disease within sub-topics of health (mental, social, emotional, environmental, financial, etc.).

KRS 305.title: Principles of Sports Medicine
KRS 305.subject: KRS
KRS 305.description: Examines with some depth, principles of risk management and pathology of athletic injuries, major musculoskeletal structures, and concepts of evaluative skills, treatment, and rehabilitation for common athletic injuries.

KRS 310.title: Coaching of Football
KRS 310.subject: KRS
KRS 310.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive football coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 311.title: Coaching of Basketball
KRS 311.subject: KRS
KRS 311.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive basketball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 312.title: Coaching of Baseball
KRS 312.subject: KRS
KRS 312.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive baseball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 313.title: Coaching of Volleyball
KRS 313.subject: KRS
KRS 313.description: Theory and strategy of offensive and defensive volleyball coaching. Emphasis on coaching philosophy, selecting and developing an offense and defense, organizing practices, special situations, scouting, and training and conditioning.

KRS 323.title: Music and Rhythm in Physical Education
KRS 323.subject: KRS
KRS 323.description: Use of music in physical education programming (K-12), emphasizing selection of appropriate music for specific activities as expressive or creative movement, movement exploration, rhythmic gymnastics, and dancing. A variety of strategies for teaching dance will be shared.

KRS 329.title: Managing Recreation Services
KRS 329.subject: KRS
KRS 329.description: Administrative framework and procedures pertinent to the operation of agencies providing recreational services to the various publics.

KRS 331.title: Water Safety Training
KRS 331.subject: KRS
KRS 331.description: Theory and methods of advanced lifesaving and water safety leading to American Red Cross Water Safety Instructor (WSI) certification.
KRS 331.prereq_raw: 104 or consent. (Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

children.text: ( Student to provide own swim attire approved by the instructor.)

KRS 332.title: Emergency Care and First Aid Training
KRS 332.subject: KRS
KRS 332.description: Practicum in training of persons to become qualified in emergency care knowledge, basic life support, and first aid skills. First Aid and CPR certificates may be earned.

KRS 333.title: Movement Education I
KRS 333.subject: KRS
KRS 333.description: A movement-based approach to teaching basic motor skills in preschool/elementary physical education. Students actively participate and learn about developmentally appropriate content and pedagogy for children in grades P–5/6. Peer bit teaching is included.

KRS 334.title: Movement Education II
KRS 334.subject: KRS
KRS 334.description: Content and pedadogy for teaching Pre/K-5 physical education. Students will learn to plan and teach physical education for children. Peer bit and field teaching included.

KRS 335.title: Coaching of Track and Field
KRS 335.subject: KRS
KRS 335.description: Techniques and rules of sprints, distance runs, relays, hurdles, long jump, high jump, pole vault, shot put, discus, and javelin throws; conduct of track and field meets; specific conditioning and training problems.

KRS 336.title: Coaching of Swimming
KRS 336.subject: KRS
KRS 336.description: Theory and methods of coaching competitive swimming. Technical, organizational, and administrative aspects. Emphasis on stroke mechanics and training methods.

KRS 337.title: Fieldwork in Recreation I
KRS 337.subject: KRS
KRS 337.description: Initial supervised leadership experience in recreational agencies. One hour per week in class discussion sessions. For recreation majors only.

KRS 339.title: Special Recreation
KRS 339.subject: KRS
KRS 339.description: Special recreation as a professional field. Overview of special recreation services. Emphasis on recreation services for special populations.

KRS 353.title: Structural Kinesiology
KRS 353.subject: KRS
KRS 353.description: Gross human anatomy, emphasizing identification and description of parts of the musculoskeletal system; selected applications to motor activity. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent.
KRS 353.prereq_raw: 113 or BIOL 171/171L or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141/141L or PHYL 301/301L

KRS 354.title: Exercise and Sport Physiology
KRS 354.subject: KRS
KRS 354.description: Emphasis on physiological responses to exercises and physical training as related to strength, muscular endurance, cardio-respiratory endurance. Primarily for KRS majors, but open to others with consent. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/ Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.
KRS 354.prereq_raw: 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent), or BIOL 171/171L (or concurrent); or consent

KRS 354L.title: Exercise and Sport Physiology Lab
KRS 354L.subject: KRS
KRS 354L.description: Laboratory section to accompany KRS 354. Emphasis will be hands-on data collection and analysis of the physiological responses to exercise and physical training. Lab report development and scientific writing will also be emphasized. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.
KRS 354L.prereq_raw: 113 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 142/142L (or concurrent), or BIOL 171/171L (or concurrent); or consent

KRS 371.title: Teaching Techniques I: Elementary
KRS 371.subject: KRS
KRS 371.description: Teaching techniques and methods of elementary physical education. Content to include basic skills and games in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

KRS 372.title: Teaching Techniques II: Secondary
KRS 372.subject: KRS
KRS 372.description: Teaching techniques and methods of secondary physical education. Content to include invasion, net, field, and target activities. Emphasizes the tactical approach in a school-based experience. Primarily for KRS majors.

KRS 384.title: Drugs and Society
KRS 384.subject: KRS
KRS 384.description: Introduction to psychoactive drugs and their effects; drug regulations; education and rehabilitation programs; psycho-social variables related to the decisions to use/abuse drugs.

KRS 385.title: Physical Fitness for Physical Education Teachers
KRS 385.subject: KRS
KRS 385.description: Diagnosis and prescription for basic health and fitness problems, scientific principles of training, guidelines for exercise; essentials of scientifically based individualized physical fitness program.

KRS 388.title: Field Work in Strength and Conditioning I
KRS 388.subject: KRS
KRS 388.description: Supervised practicum in strength training and conditioning. Students will be exposed to the theory and practice of designing and implementing both strength/power, and general conditioning programs.

KRS 395.title: Personal Health and Wellness
KRS 395.subject: KRS
KRS 395.description: Scientifically based information will be presented to help the student make decisions and take responsibility for his/her own health and health-related behaviors. The student will develop a personal, daily physical activity/exercise program, in which he/ she will participate and be monitored.

KRS 399.title: Directed Reading
KRS 399.subject: KRS
KRS 399.description: Individual problems. Limited to senior majors in health education, physical education, athletic training, or recreation with a minimum GPA of 2.75 in major field.

KRS 401.title: Advanced Health Concepts
KRS 401.subject: KRS
KRS 401.description: Understanding health issues for individuals, families, schools, and communities, in regards to Hawaii K-12 schools. Focusing on the acquisition of functional health content and proficiency in health-related skills to enhance healthy behaviors in learners.

KRS 403.title: Guidance and Classroom Management
KRS 403.subject: KRS
KRS 403.description: Guidance principles applied to classroom management for teachers.

KRS 404.title: K-12 Teaching Methods in Physical Education
KRS 404.subject: KRS
KRS 404.description: Methods and materials in teaching physical education activities program; techniques; leadership; selection of appropriate activities and program evaluation for teaching licensure.

KRS 406.title: Seminar in Teaching Residency
KRS 406.subject: KRS
KRS 406.description: Analysis and resolutions of issues in teaching residency; teaching strategies and techniques; curriculum planning; professional growth and development.
KRS 406.prereq_raw: 402E, 402S, and 404 or consent; admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

children.text: admittance to licensure track, pass Praxis II Core Academic Skills tests

KRS 407.title: Psychosocial Aspects of Sport
KRS 407.subject: KRS
KRS 407.description: Examination and application of sociological and psychological theories to sport including the influence of race, ethnicity, gender, identity and human development, social class, disabilities, and sexual orientation on the sport experience.

KRS 415.title: Prevent/Care of Athletic Injuries
KRS 415.subject: KRS
KRS 415.description: An examination of the most recent practices and procedures in the prevention and care of athletic and sports injuries. Observational field experiences in athletic training will be required.
KRS 415.prereq_raw: 113, or PHYL 103, or PHYL 141/141L and PHYL 142/142L, or BIOL 171/171L

KRS 416.title: Fundamentals of Ergonomics
KRS 416.subject: KRS
KRS 416.description: Introduction to ergonomics principles and their application in understanding and prevention of Muscular Skeletal Disorders encountered in the working environment including introduction to legal aspects of ergonomics. Post-Master’s Certificate in Nursing majors only.

KRS 419.title: Administration in Athletic Training, Exercise Science, Allied Health
KRS 419.subject: KRS
KRS 419.description: An examination of organization and administration in Athletic Training, Allied Health and Exercise Science. Content includes leadership and motivation models, legal liability, ethical considerations and management strategies for all aspects of Health Care Administration.

KRS 420.title: Lower Extremity Assessment
KRS 420.subject: KRS
KRS 420.description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the lower extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals.

KRS 421.title: Upper Extremity Assessment
KRS 421.subject: KRS
KRS 421.description: An examination of the pathology of injuries to the upper extremities and their care and treatment designed for Athletic Training, Exercise Science and Allied Health professionals. Kinesiology and Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 423.title: Curriculum and Supervision
KRS 423.subject: KRS
KRS 423.description: Effective program development, planning, and supervision, including issues in legal liability and administration of all aspects of physical education programming in grades K-12.

KRS 428.title: Current Issues in Leisure Services
KRS 428.subject: KRS
KRS 428.description: Philosophical foundations and current and emerging issues in leisure services management and programming. Coverage of leisure research and its implications to practice.

KRS 429.title: Evaluating and Marketing Leisure Services
KRS 429.subject: KRS
KRS 429.description: Basic methods in marketing, planning, evaluating programs and problem-solving methods, survey research, research design, data analysis, and report generation for park, recreation, and tourism systems.

KRS 432.title: Emergency Care for the Professional Rescuer
KRS 432.subject: KRS
KRS 432.description: Combined lecture-lab on advanced emergency care for injuries and illnesses and includes certifications for CPR/First Aid/AED. Class size of approximately 20 students. Open to all majors.

KRS 434.title: Coaching Athletics
KRS 434.subject: KRS
KRS 434.description: Combined lecture-lab with emphasis on scientific principles, theory and practice, and professional qualities of the coach.

KRS 437.title: Camp Resources and Planning
KRS 437.subject: KRS
KRS 437.description: Combined lecture-lab for camp counselors and camp leadership. Plan and evaluate camp experiences for children and youth, including those with disabilities. Includes field trips.

KRS 438.title: Practicum in Camping
KRS 438.subject: KRS
KRS 438.description: Supervised leadership at a camp setting with children and youth, including those with disabilities. Day or residential camps. One full week camping for each credit hour. Maximum of four credit hours.

KRS 443.title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
KRS 443.subject: KRS
KRS 443.description: Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

KRS 463.title: Sport Biomechanics
KRS 463.subject: KRS
KRS 463.description: Concepts and scientific principles essential to efficient human movement; proper application of bio-mechanical principles to fundamental movements and selected complex motor skills.
KRS 463.prereq_raw: 353, and either PHYS 100, PHYS 151, or PHYS 170; or consent

KRS 470.title: Fitness for Life
KRS 470.subject: KRS
KRS 470.description: Physical education teachers will gain knowledge, skills, and experience necessary to plan, implement, and evaluate Fitness for Life curriculum (grades 6-12). Information is guided by national and state standards. Includes lecture, lab, and teaching experiences. (Once a year)

KRS 471.title: Teaching Methods in Health Education
KRS 471.subject: KRS
KRS 471.description: Experiences in developing standards-based, interactive learning opportunities to teach quality health education in schools. Focus on creating curriculum and assessments aligned with the National and State Standards for Health Education.

KRS 472.title: Learning Communities
KRS 472.subject: KRS
KRS 472.description: Theory, basic research, interactive process, and methodology of the cooperative learning process known as Tribes. Will develop participants’ abilities to foster and facilitate learning communities in a variety of settings.

KRS 473.title: Sociocultural Issues in Physical Activity
KRS 473.subject: KRS
KRS 473.description: Contemporary and historical perspective on sociocultural issues that influence American youth and instruction in a physical activity setting. Understanding culturally responsive practice in regards to culture, race, ethnicity, gender, sexual identity, class, obesity, and urbanization.

KRS 474.title: Introduction to Statistics in Kinesiology
KRS 474.subject: KRS
KRS 474.description: Basic elements for: descriptive statistics, probability, inference, regression, and correlation analysis.

KRS 476.title: Motor Learning and Performance
KRS 476.subject: KRS
KRS 476.description: Basic consideration is kinesthesis, motor ability, fatigue, developmental factors, practice, motivation in relation to motor learning and human performance.

KRS 477.title: Motor Development and Learning
KRS 477.subject: KRS
KRS 477.description: Motor development through the lifespan with emphasis on fundamental principles and patterns. Factors affecting motor learning performance as a function of memory, practice, knowledge of performance, and motivation are incorporated. Required field experience.

KRS 478.title: Adapted Physical Activity in Early Childhood
KRS 478.subject: KRS
KRS 478.description: Concepts of developmentally appropriate practice, importance of movement in overall development, and design of physical activity sessions and environments for young children with and without disabilities are covered.

KRS 480.title: Nutrition in Exercise and Sport
KRS 480.subject: KRS
KRS 480.description: Effects of physiologic demands of exercise on nutrition. Emphasis on physiologic and biochemical basis for nutrition recommendations to enhance exercise participation and optimize athletic performance.
KRS 480.prereq_raw: FSHN 185, and KRS 113 or PHYL 103 or (PHYL 141/141L and 142/142L) or PHYL 301

KRS 481.title: Introduction to Research in KRS
KRS 481.subject: KRS
KRS 481.description: Research methods in the study of physical activity, types of research, statistical concepts and techniques, and reporting research results.

KRS 482.title: Commercial Recreation
KRS 482.subject: KRS
KRS 482.description: Overview of leisure services and trends in commercial, private and employee recreation, and resort and recreational tourism. The social, economic, and environmental significance is examined.

KRS 483.title: Recreation Planning and Maintenance
KRS 483.subject: KRS
KRS 483.description: Examination of social, economic, and environmental factors of recreation and tourism development. Emphasis on methods, processes, citizen participation, design issues/regulations, and land use.

KRS 484.title: Drug Abuse, Violence, and Injury Prevention
KRS 484.subject: KRS
KRS 484.description: Standards-based planning, teaching, and assessment on the scientific, socio-cultural, and attitudinal aspects of drug abuse, violence, and injury prevention. Focus on incidence and prevalence, roles, prevention, and high-risk populations.

KRS 485.title: Sexual Health Education
KRS 485.subject: KRS
KRS 485.description: Program planning, curriculum development and classroom teaching strategies in the areas of human sexuality, reproductive health, family planning, and family health. Focus on research-based curriculum and strategies to promote personal and social responsibility for health.

KRS 487.title: Exercise Assessment and Conditioning Lab
KRS 487.subject: KRS
KRS 487.description: Designed to provide knowledge of laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of aerobic and anaerobic testing results, and individual exercise program/prescription.

KRS 488.title: Practicum in Health and Exercise Science
KRS 488.subject: KRS
KRS 488.description: Culminating 160 hours of supervised practicum experience in health, wellness, fitness assessment, lifestyle management, and/or exercise leadership. Qualifying hours are contingent upon instructor’s approval in the registered semester. Health and Exercise Science majors only.
KRS 488.prereq_raw: current CPR and First Aid Certification, 152, 332, 353, 354, and 463; or consent

KRS 489.title: Program Design in Strength Training and Conditioning
KRS 489.subject: KRS
KRS 489.description: Designed to provide theoretical and practical experience in supervision of a strength training center. Content includes program design, exercise techniques, organization, testing, evaluation, methods of strength development, facility design and special populations. Kinesiology & Rehabilitation Science, Health/Exercise Science and Lifestyle Management, and Physical Education majors only.

KRS 490.title: Introduction to Athletic Training Clinic
KRS 490.subject: KRS
KRS 490.description: Introduction to the Professional Athletic Training Education Program and the Clinical Education Plan. Students are required to document all requirements and demonstrate proficiency in basic clinical skills. ATEP Program students only. (Once a year)

KRS 491.title: AT Practicum I
KRS 491.subject: KRS
KRS 491.description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

KRS 492.title: AT Practicum II
KRS 492.subject: KRS
KRS 492.description: Introductory-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is required for the KRS entry-level Graduate Athletic Training Education Program.

KRS 493.title: Athletic Training Practicum III
KRS 493.subject: KRS
KRS 493.description: Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

KRS 494.title: Athletic Training Practicum IV
KRS 494.subject: KRS
KRS 494.description: (5 2-hr Practicum) Advanced-level supervised experiences within the profession of athletic training. This practicum is a requirement for entry to the KRS Master’s Athletic Training Program.

KRS 600.title: Counseling in the Schools
KRS 600.subject: KRS
KRS 600.description: History, philosophy, and organization of school counseling programs. Counselor role and functions, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, current methodology and resources. (Meets EdD common core elective.)

KRS 603.title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
KRS 603.subject: KRS
KRS 603.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen with emphasis on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

KRS 604.title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
KRS 604.subject: KRS
KRS 604.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

KRS 605.title: Human Growth and Development—Life Span
KRS 605.subject: KRS
KRS 605.description: Life span perspective on psychological, social, and physical development. Major theories and related research on human development; applications in policy planning and service delivery in counseling.

KRS 606.title: Counseling: Theory and Practice
KRS 606.subject: KRS
KRS 606.description: Theory and techniques of counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

KRS 607.title: Scientific Principles of Physical Conditioning
KRS 607.subject: KRS
KRS 607.description: Application of physiological principles to physical conditioning and athletic performance.

KRS 608.title: Muscular Strength and Power Development
KRS 608.subject: KRS
KRS 608.description: Interpretation of scientific principles of muscular strength and power development. Examination of muscular adaptations to increased and decreased use.

KRS 609.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience I
KRS 609.subject: KRS
KRS 609.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Must be completed during first semester post admission into program. Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 610.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience II
KRS 610.subject: KRS
KRS 610.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Practicum includes duties and responsibilities of athletic training students. Practicum must be completed during second semester post admission to the program. Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 611.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience III
KRS 611.subject: KRS
KRS 611.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required. Athletic Training majors only. (Fall only

KRS 612.title: Athletic Training, Clinical Experience IV
KRS 612.subject: KRS
KRS 612.description: (1 Sem, 5 3-hr Practicum) Culminating practicum requiring performance of duties and responsibilities of second year graduate athletic training students. A practical field experience in athletic training is required. Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 613.title: Athletic Training Clinical Practicum
KRS 613.subject: KRS
KRS 613.description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced clinical practicum in which the BOC certified or certification eligible graduate student experiences an enhancement of athletic training knowledge and refinement of athletic training skills.

KRS 614.title: Athletic Training Research Practicum
KRS 614.subject: KRS
KRS 614.description: (1 Sem, 5 4-hr Practicum) Advanced research practicum in which the BOC certified or certification eligible graduate student deepens their understanding and enhances their critical thinking abilities in order to contribute to the advancement of the discipline and the athletic training profession.

KRS 616.title: Advanced Orthopedic Assessment
KRS 616.subject: KRS
KRS 616.description: Advanced knowledge and skills of athletic training as they are specifically applied to the understanding, treatment, and rehabilitation of sport-related injuries. (e.g. epidemiology, legal, ethical concerns, sports psychology, pharm, drug abuse, health issues)

KRS 617.title: Therapeutic Interventions: Modalities
KRS 617.subject: KRS
KRS 617.description: Physiology principles and operational procedures of contemporary therapeutic modalities as they relate to the care and treatment of athletic injuries. Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 618.title: Therapeutic Interventions: Rehabilitative Exercise
KRS 618.subject: KRS
KRS 618.description: Concepts and principles of comprehensive rehabilitation programs (therapeutic goals and objectives, exercise selection, methods of evaluation and recording progress, progression and return to competition criteria, and physiological effects of tissue trauma and inactivity). Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 619.title: General Medical Conditions in Sports Medicine
KRS 619.subject: KRS
KRS 619.description: An examination/evaluation of general medical conditions associated with sports medicine including pathology, care and treatment. Athletic Training majors only.

KRS 620.title: Seminar in Athletic Training
KRS 620.subject: KRS
KRS 620.description: Designed to provide the student with analytical skills and practical experience relative to research as it applies to sports related injuries.

KRS 621.title: Advanced Therapeutic Exercise
KRS 621.subject: KRS
KRS 621.description: Advanced concepts and evidence-based principles of rehabilitation programs. Enhancement of previously learned therapeutic exercise techniques and integration of therapeutic modalities and therapeutic exercise, including objective and functional goal setting and evaluation for appropriate progression and expedited return to activity.
KRS 621.prereq_raw: 617 and 618 or basic therapeutic exercise and therapeutic modalities courses, or consent

KRS 622.title: Athletic Training Capstone Experience
KRS 622.subject: KRS
KRS 622.description: Capstone culminating experience preparing the student for the computer-based BOC Exam and for a career in athletic training. Follows the students’ didactic and clinical preparation in the 12 competency areas of athletic training.

KRS 623.title: Administration in Kinesiology
KRS 623.subject: KRS
KRS 623.description: Current problems, trends, and strategies in the administration of athletic training, physical education, recreation, sport and fitness programs in school and non-school settings.

KRS 625.title: Introduction to Community Counseling
KRS 625.subject: KRS
KRS 625.description: Philosophy, organization, and function of community service agencies, programs, and institutions as related to professional work in counseling.

KRS 626.title: Introduction to Practicum
KRS 626.subject: KRS
KRS 626.description: Pre-practicum training for supervised experiences in school, community, and human service organizations. Focus on the counseling relationship. Includes a specialty observation-participation field experience.

KRS 627.title: Career Development and Vocational Counseling
KRS 627.subject: KRS
KRS 627.description: Theory and practice in career development and vocational counseling with individuals and groups; utilization of educational, vocational, and social resources in career counseling.

KRS 628.title: Research and Evaluation in Rehabilitation
KRS 628.subject: KRS
KRS 628.description: Framework for understanding basic statistics, methodology, and evaluation of research in rehabilitation and related fields. Students will analyze research, conceptualize research, and apply research to practice.

KRS 629.title: Counseling: Group Theory and Practice
KRS 629.subject: KRS
KRS 629.description: Theories and techniques of group counseling and guidance as preparation for practicum and internship. Application in school, college, rehabilitation, and community settings.

KRS 630.title: Tests and Inventories in Guidance
KRS 630.subject: KRS
KRS 630.description: Tests and inventories for the assessment of aptitudes, achievement, and interests. Applications to educational, instructional, and career guidance.

KRS 631.title: Problems of School Adjustment
KRS 631.subject: KRS
KRS 631.description: Principles of behavior affecting interpersonal relationships in school with emphasis on application to actual situations.

KRS 632.title: Theory and Assessment of Intelligence
KRS 632.subject: KRS
KRS 632.description: Theory and supervised experience in individual intelligence testing, psychological report writing; psychometric and social issues in intelligence testing.

KRS 633.title: Crisis Intervention
KRS 633.subject: KRS
KRS 633.description: Professional concerns about crisis intervention strategies, and counseling skills development. Crisis theory as applied to suicide, sexual assault/rape, natural and man-made disasters, personal loss, terminal illness, life cycle crisis, and the like.

KRS 634.title: Inclusive Physical Activity
KRS 634.subject: KRS
KRS 634.description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

KRS 635.title: Elementary Physical Education
KRS 635.subject: KRS
KRS 635.description: Content and pedagogy for teaching preschool/ elementary physical education. Students will learn appropriate content and pedagogy for learners in elementary school. Bit teaching and field experiences are included.

KRS 636.title: Theory and Assessment of Personality
KRS 636.subject: KRS
KRS 636.description: Personality testing; practice in administration and use of personality assessment; examination of psychometric and social issues.

KRS 637.title: Cross-Cultural Counseling
KRS 637.subject: KRS
KRS 637.description: Significance of cultural factors in counseling relationships, delivery of counseling services in multicultural settings with attention to Hawai‘i. Emphasis on process of cultural learning and implications for counselor roles and functions.

KRS 640.title: Seminar in Physical Activity
KRS 640.subject: KRS
KRS 640.description: Trends, research, and problems related to physical activity across the lifespan. A variety of topics and contexts will be addressed. Enrolled in KRS graduate program only.

KRS 641.title: Seminar: Health/Exercise Science
KRS 641.subject: KRS
KRS 641.description: Review of selected current literature in exercise/sport science and leisure studies. Practice of presentation in group setting.

KRS 643.title: Secondary Physical Education
KRS 643.subject: KRS
KRS 643.description: Detailed examination of effective physical education curriculum and instruction in middle and high schools.

KRS 646.title: American College Student
KRS 646.subject: KRS
KRS 646.description: Study of psychosocial characteristics of American college students and college environment, from viewpoint of student personnel work.

KRS 660.title: Marriage, Family, and Child Counseling
KRS 660.subject: KRS
KRS 660.description: Theory/practice of marriage, family, and child counseling, including major model in clinical practice; supervised counseling project by each student. Liability insurance required.

KRS 663.title: Biomechanics of Human Motion
KRS 663.subject: KRS
KRS 663.description: Principles of motion as applied to sport and physical rehabilitation. Introduction to the technology used in the analysis of motion.

KRS 664.title: Physiology of Exercise
KRS 664.subject: KRS
KRS 664.description: Physiological bases of modern physical training methods and sports science.

KRS 665.title: Metabolic Analysis
KRS 665.subject: KRS
KRS 665.description: Theory and practice of metabolic analysis of human performance examining each of the power systems used in energy production during exercise and how to use this information to prescribe exercise programs.

KRS 666.title: Advanced Fitness Assessment and Exercise Prescription
KRS 666.subject: KRS
KRS 666.description: Provides knowledge of field and laboratory techniques and procedures for aerobic and anaerobic fitness assessment, interpretation of testing results and individual exercise program/ prescription techniques.

KRS 667.title: Body Composition and Weight Management
KRS 667.subject: KRS
KRS 667.description: Analysis of the theory and practice used in the assessment of body composition and human physique. Includes strategies for implementing changes in body composition.

KRS 670.title: Consultation: Theory and Practice
KRS 670.subject: KRS
KRS 670.description: Consultation in educational, business, health, community, and human services agencies.

KRS 673.title: Research Methods in KRS
KRS 673.subject: KRS
KRS 673.description: The use of experimental designs/models in physical education research with emphasis on understanding the concepts, applications, and interpretations of statistical analysis.

KRS 674.title: Assessment in Physical Activity
KRS 674.subject: KRS
KRS 674.description: Overview of assessment purposes, types, practices and procedures used in physical education for those with disabilities. Frequently used motor assessments and practices in collection of data will be specifically addressed.

KRS 675.title: Transdisciplinary Approach to Teaching the Motor Domain
KRS 675.subject: KRS
KRS 675.description: Highlights a trans-disciplinary approach for effectively teaching students with disabilities in the motor domain. Important characteristics and components of this approach will be shared. Strategies for its implementation will also be addressed.

KRS 680.title: Principles and Practice of Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 680.subject: KRS
KRS 680.description: Principles, practices of rehabilitation counseling; review of history and influence of legislation on vocational rehabilitation; current issues, developments, with emphasis on local situation.

KRS 681.title: Medical and Psychosocial Aspects of Disability
KRS 681.subject: KRS
KRS 681.description: Functional implications of chronic illnesses and disabilities on psychological, social and vocational areas of an individuals life. Case studies and presentations will stimulate discussion and help students to apply theoretical information into practical everyday context.

KRS 683.title: Case Management in Rehabilitation
KRS 683.subject: KRS
KRS 683.description: Knowledge and skills required in case and case-load management in public as well as private sector rehabilitation sites. Emphasis on professional/ client relationship, interviewing process, decision-making, goal-setting, recording/documentation, time management, and other tasks.

KRS 684.title: Psychopathology in Counseling
KRS 684.subject: KRS
KRS 684.description: Discussion-oriented course (potentially Web-based). Examination of theory and practice of diagnosis in the assessment and treatment of mental disorders and the use of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-IV) multi-axial system. Case studies will illustrate diagnostic issues.

KRS 685.title: Ethical Issues for the Helping Profession
KRS 685.subject: KRS
KRS 685.description: Developing ethical reasoning capabilities for resolution of ethical dilemmas likely to be encountered in counseling, psychology, and specialty practices (e.g., community, rehabilitation, school, mental health, alcohol and substance abuse, marriage and family counseling, and the like).

KRS 686.title: Vocational Evaluation and Assessment in Rehabilitation
KRS 686.subject: KRS
KRS 686.description: Theory, process, and techniques of vocational evaluation and assessment. Assessment methods and processes as they relate to vocational choice and adjustment of special groups.

KRS 687.title: Assistive Technology in Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 687.subject: KRS
KRS 687.description: Study of application of assistive technologies to enhance the lives of people with disabilities. Case studies provide the vehicle in guiding students toward integration of available information into reality of actual situations. Special emphasis on the importance of using a consumer-centered approach in providing assistive technology services.

KRS 688.title: Theory and Techniques of Job Placement
KRS 688.subject: KRS
KRS 688.description: Theory, process, and techniques of job readiness, job development, and job placement.

KRS 695.title: Promoting Physical Activity
KRS 695.subject: KRS
KRS 695.description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

KRS 699.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
KRS 699.subject: KRS
KRS 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

KRS 704.title: Contemporary Issues in Counseling
KRS 704.subject: KRS
KRS 704.description: Current issues and problems. (Meets EdD common required elective.)

KRS 741.title: Seminar in School Counseling
KRS 741.subject: KRS
KRS 741.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in school counseling.

KRS 751.title: Seminar in Community Counseling
KRS 751.subject: KRS
KRS 751.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in community counseling.

KRS 761.title: Seminar in College Counseling
KRS 761.subject: KRS
KRS 761.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in college counseling.

KRS 775.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research I in Kinesiology
KRS 775.subject: KRS
KRS 775.description: Will expose the PhD student to the basic nature of behavioral and somatic science research. Learning experiences will consist of journal review, laboratory/field techniques, and subject or data collector exposures as directed by faculty mentors.

KRS 776.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research II in Kinesiology
KRS 776.subject: KRS
KRS 776.description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to be involved in research, under the direction of the faculty mentor, as the assistant project director and as the project director for pilot studies. Student will gain experience in these roles with close supervision by the faculty mentor.

KRS 777.title: Doctoral Seminar and Research III in Kinesiology
KRS 777.subject: KRS
KRS 777.description: Provide the PhD student the opportunity to assume the role of director of a research project under the supervision of the faculty mentor. The research project will represent a piece of the ongoing line of research of the faculty mentor. Responsibilities will be comparable of a project director of research funded by a research grant.

KRS 778.title: Doctoral Seminar IV in Kinesiology
KRS 778.subject: KRS
KRS 778.description: Designed to enable PhD students to gain a perspective of the discipline, both historically and philosophically, prepare them for the issues they may face in the real world, particularly higher education and help them initiate their dissertation.

KRS 781.title: Seminar in Rehabilitation Counseling
KRS 781.subject: KRS
KRS 781.description: In-depth study of professional concerns in rehabilitation counseling.

LTEC 112.title: Technologies for Academic Success
LTEC 112.subject: LTEC
LTEC 112.description: Virtual and hands-on analysis of technology resources and utilization in learning.

LTEC 113.title: Technologies for Academic Success– Business
LTEC 113.subject: LTEC
LTEC 113.description: Virtual and hands-on analysis of technology resources and utilization in learning with an emphasis on business education.

LTEC 414.title: Educational Media Technology
LTEC 414.subject: LTEC
LTEC 414.description: Introduction to educational technology theory and practice with an emphasis on meaningful integration of technology and media into a variety of face-to-face and online learning environments for diverse populations.

LTEC 415.title: Technology for Teachers
LTEC 415.subject: LTEC
LTEC 415.description: Introduction to the application of educational technology in teaching and learning using strategies in design, selection, development, integration, and evaluation. Interactive delivery via distance education technologies.

LTEC 430.title: Video Technology
LTEC 430.subject: LTEC
LTEC 430.description: Overview of video uses in educational contexts. Includes video planning, production, and simple editing procedures, as well as selection, evaluation, and integration into learning plans.

LTEC 442.title: Technology in Education
LTEC 442.subject: LTEC
LTEC 442.description: Planning and implementation of computer systems and applications for effective integration into classroom settings. Emphasis is on methods and strategies for using digital technologies to enhance standards-based learning by K-12 students.

LTEC 448.title: Social Media: Links to Lifelong Learning
LTEC 448.subject: LTEC
LTEC 448.description: Exploration of social media and effects on individuals, communities, and world. Analyze and evaluate impacts of social media and ethical implications. Service learning component and research project link social media to personal fields of study.

children.text: upper division standing ( junior or higher

LTEC 499.title: Directed Activity
LTEC 499.subject: LTEC
LTEC 499.description: Individual work, supervised by instructor. May consist of reading, research, and/or projects.

LTEC 501.title: Professional Development in Educational Technology: Technology Skills for Educators
LTEC 501.subject: LTEC
LTEC 501.description: Exploring technology resources needed for distance learning and classroom integration.

LTEC 502.title: PDET: Technology Skills for Educators
LTEC 502.subject: LTEC
LTEC 502.description: Exploring technology resources needed for integration into classroom instruction.

LTEC 511.title: Professional Development Education Technology I
LTEC 511.subject: LTEC
LTEC 511.description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course.

LTEC 512.title: Professional Development Education Technology II
LTEC 512.subject: LTEC
LTEC 512.description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course.

LTEC 513.title: Professional Development Education Technology III
LTEC 513.subject: LTEC
LTEC 513.description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course.

LTEC 514.title: Professional Development Education Technology IV
LTEC 514.subject: LTEC
LTEC 514.description: Specialized topics reflecting interests and needs of faculty in current issues of technology integration. Combined lecture, lab and discussion course.

LTEC 600.title: Theory and Practice in Educational Technology
LTEC 600.subject: LTEC
LTEC 600.description: The profession of educational technology and the role of instructional designers. Theoretical and philosophical foundations underlying practice that include instructional systems theory, needs assessment, change theory, and relevant learning models. Practical applications of these theories to solve instructional problems in real-life settings.

LTEC 602.title: Innovations in Educational Technology
LTEC 602.subject: LTEC
LTEC 602.description: Innovative technological advances and new media in the field of educational technology and their application in instruction.

LTEC 611.title: Educational Technology Research and Evaluation
LTEC 611.subject: LTEC
LTEC 611.description: Review of existing research in media/ed technology, with activities leading to the preparation of final study or project proposal. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 612.title: Introduction to E-learning
LTEC 612.subject: LTEC
LTEC 612.description: Introduction to principles of e-learning and their application in formal and informal instructional settings. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 613.title: Instructional Design and Development
LTEC 613.subject: LTEC
LTEC 613.description: Basic concepts and techniques of instructional design and development, for application to solving instructional problems in real-life situations.

LTEC 620.title: Visual Design
LTEC 620.subject: LTEC
LTEC 620.description: Theory and practice involved in planning educational/instructional graphic and photographic material for print and computer-based media. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 622.title: E-learning Theory and Design
LTEC 622.subject: LTEC
LTEC 622.description: Principles of e-learning theory as well as design and development for instruction. Application to new media and web authoring.
LTEC 622.prereq_raw: LTEC majors or consent. A-F only

LTEC 623.title: Digital Video Design
LTEC 623.subject: LTEC
LTEC 623.description: Development and utilization of digital video for the purpose of improving the teaching-learning process.

LTEC 632.title: Developing E-learning Environments
LTEC 632.subject: LTEC
LTEC 632.description: Planning, design, and development of e-learning instruction for educational and training settings. Implementation of online course elements such as student interaction, course management, testing, and content delivery using a learning management environments and open courseware. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 641.title: Emerging Technologies for K-12 Teaching
LTEC 641.subject: LTEC
LTEC 641.description: Exploration and impact of emerging technologies in K-12 classroom teaching and learning and ramifications of these technologies on administrative structure of schools. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 642.title: Facilitating E-learning Communities
LTEC 642.subject: LTEC
LTEC 642.description: Exploration of tools and design considerations for effective online communication and development of learning communities.

LTEC 643.title: Educational Technology in Informal Learning Environments
LTEC 643.subject: LTEC
LTEC 643.description: Exploring the nature, application, and use of educational technology in informal learning environments, such as museums, cultural institutions, tourist attractions, and visitor information centers. Focusing on the analysis, selection, and development of various media choices.

LTEC 651.title: Interactive Multimedia Production
LTEC 651.subject: LTEC
LTEC 651.description: The utilization and application of advanced authoring tools, combining video, animation, graphics, and sound to develop student-centered learning. Primarily for advanced LTEC students. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 654.title: Programming for Games and Simulations
LTEC 654.subject: LTEC
LTEC 654.description: Project-based exploration of the breadth of programming in the context of educational games and simulations.

LTEC 661.title: Design Thinking for Creative Problem Solving
LTEC 661.subject: LTEC
LTEC 661.description: Using real-world problems, students learn an agile design and problem-solving process that is human-centered, iterative, and cultivates individual and group creativity.

LTEC 662.title: Assessment and Evaluation in Educational Technology
LTEC 662.subject: LTEC
LTEC 662.description: Evaluation and assessment processes, sources, and instruments applicable to systematic appraisal of learning with technology.

LTEC 665.title: Research Design: Multiple Methods and Traditions
LTEC 665.subject: LTEC
LTEC 665.description: Explores research methods used in educational technology with a focus on developing a design for dissertation research. Emphasis is on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. LTEC PhD majors only. Graduate students only.

LTEC 667.title: Qualitative Research in Educational Technology
LTEC 667.subject: LTEC
LTEC 667.description: Introduction to qualitative research traditions and designs. Emphasis will be on the use of digital technologies in data collection and analysis. LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent. (Once a year)

LTEC 668.title: Quantitative Research in Educational Technology
LTEC 668.subject: LTEC
LTEC 668.description: Application of methodological and statistical concepts in a projects-based classroom framework. Formative and summative evaluation, measurements, descriptive, and inferential statistics. LTEC PhD majors only. EDUC PhD majors only with consent.

LTEC 672.title: Distance Education Technology
LTEC 672.subject: LTEC
LTEC 672.description: Technical and instructional considerations for developing, delivering, managing, and evaluating distance education including voice, video, print, hypermedia and data transmissions.

LTEC 673.title: Planning for Technology and Resources
LTEC 673.subject: LTEC
LTEC 673.description: Planning, needs assessment, and change theory applied to the development and evaluation of long-range plans and the communication of a vision for technology in education. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 676.title: Social and Ethical Issues in Educational Technology
LTEC 676.subject: LTEC
LTEC 676.description: Examination of social and ethical issues as they relate to technology in instructional settings. Focus on social justice and societal impact.

LTEC 682.title: Cognition and Technology
LTEC 682.subject: LTEC
LTEC 682.description: Interdisciplinary course that introduces a range of empirical research examining aspects of cognition such as attention, memory and learning, and how technologies can enhance and/or hinder these cognitive processes.

LTEC 686.title: Information Literacy and Learning Resources
LTEC 686.subject: LTEC
LTEC 686.description: Process approach to teaching information retrieval, analysis, and use. Emphasizes concepts, practices ineffective instructional design, selection of resources that meets learning needs. Required for Librarian HDOE licensure.

LTEC 687.title: Learning Design Studio
LTEC 687.subject: LTEC
LTEC 687.description: Practicum in instructional design, development, and technology in academic and non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings in seminar format. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 689.title: LTEC Training and Evaluation Practicum
LTEC 689.subject: LTEC
LTEC 689.description: Practicum in educational technology training and evaluation in formal and informal settings, under close supervision, plus class meetings in hybrid format. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 690.title: Seminar in Technology Leadership
LTEC 690.subject: LTEC
LTEC 690.description: Supervised activity in application of research in learning design and technology to teaching/training experiences. LTEC majors only and consent.

LTEC 692.title: Practicum in E-learning
LTEC 692.subject: LTEC
LTEC 692.description: Practicum in e-learning in academic or non-academic settings, under close supervision, plus regular class meetings. LTEC majors only or consent.

LTEC 701.title: Instructional Design Studio
LTEC 701.subject: LTEC
LTEC 701.description: Covers multiple instructional design models within the context of theory and research. Studio approach to focus on facilitating learning and improving performance by creating, using, and managing appropriate technological processes and resources. LTEC PhD majors only. Graduate students only.

LTEC 705.title: Special Topics in Educational Technology
LTEC 705.subject: LTEC
LTEC 705.description: Issues of topical interest in educational technology. Concentrates on a topic of current interest, including the new technologies for learning and teaching, and innovative strategies for design and delivery of instruction.

LTEC 760.title: Seminar in Educational Technology Theory
LTEC 760.subject: LTEC
LTEC 760.description: Doctoral level seminar for advanced students examining the theoretical foundations of research in the learning sciences and technology. LTEC PhD majors only.

LTEC 780.title: Mixed Methods Research Design
LTEC 780.subject: LTEC
LTEC 780.description: Mixed methods research is designed for PhD and masters students in education and social sciences considering combining qualitative and quantitative research. Covers philosophical and practical implications culminating in a mixed methods dissertation/thesis proposal. (Once a year)

LTEC 781.title: Advanced Qualitative Analysis in LTEC
LTEC 781.subject: LTEC
LTEC 781.description: Advanced research methods focused on management and analysis of qualitative data using technology. Reviews of different qualitative designs, data types, analytical methods, and software. Focused study of one qualitative design. Includes independent research project. EDUC, LTEC PhD majors only.
LTEC 781.prereq_raw: 667 or graduate level qualitative research course

LTEC 782.title: Design-Based Research in Education
LTEC 782.subject: LTEC
LTEC 782.description: Provides an introduction to design-based research in education. Reviews different design-based methods and guides students through the process of conducting original design-based research. Focuses on the gap between research and practice.
LTEC 782.prereq_raw: 667 (with a minimum grade of B) and 668 (or concurrent)

LTEC 800.title: Dissertation Research
LTEC 800.subject: LTEC
LTEC 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

SPED 201.title: Disability and Diversity in the Media
SPED 201.subject: SPED
SPED 201.description: Explores the changing disability experience as described in contemporary film, literature, advertising, news, sports and dialogue with persons with disabilities in the Pacific region and around the world.

SPED 202.title: Global and Historical Perspectives of Disability in the Media
SPED 202.subject: SPED
SPED 202.description: Explores the history of disability representation across cultures. Emphasis is placed on examining evolving perceptions of disability as depicted in art, literature, print, film, and digital media.

SPED 304.title: Foundations of Inclusive Schooling
SPED 304.subject: SPED
SPED 304.description: Foundations of “special education” exploring philosophies, diverse and historical viewpoints, laws, and service delivery. Students reflect upon texts, films and interviews with persons with disabilities, their families and professionals to understand the culture of disability.

SPED 315.title: Field Training – Blended ECE
SPED 315.subject: SPED
SPED 315.description: Students spend 15 hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled classes; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.
SPED 315.prereq_raw: 304 and ITE 415 (with a minimum grade of B-), or consent

SPED 332.title: Young Children with Communication Needs
SPED 332.subject: SPED
SPED 332.description: Communication development of infants and young children, ages birth through age 8, with and without disabilities. Assessment and intervention to support the development of communication skills in inclusive community and school environments.

SPED 392.title: Student Teaching in Special Education Modified
SPED 392.subject: SPED
SPED 392.description: Modified student teaching for students from another institution completing student teaching at UH or for students who have prior extensive teaching experience.
SPED 392.prereq_raw: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee and consent

children.text: requirements for registration listed under “Student Teaching,” approval of review committee

SPED 400.title: Field Training in Special Education
SPED 400.subject: SPED
SPED 400.description: Students participate in classroom settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

SPED 402.title: Writing for Educational Professionals
SPED 402.subject: SPED
SPED 402.description: Instruction on learning to write as professional educators. Strategies for developing and enhancing professional writing for the field of education. Peer and instructor feedback on writing throughout course. Technologies used to assist with writing.

SPED 412.title: Individuals with Severe Disabilities/ Autism
SPED 412.subject: SPED
SPED 412.description: Etiology, characteristics, and development of individuals with severe disabilities and autism; historical, theoretical, and legal issues affecting individuals with severe disabilities and autism; multicultural, family, and consumer issues; professional and ethical issues in providing services.

SPED 414.title: Education of Gifted Students
SPED 414.subject: SPED
SPED 414.description: Characteristics and educational provisions for gifted children and youth with particular attention to psychological aspects of creativity

SPED 415.title: Education Program for the Gifted/ Talented
SPED 415.subject: SPED
SPED 415.description: Utilization and evaluation of teaching/ learning models for gifted/talented students, including consideration of roles, expectancies for learning, and organizational procedures.

SPED 443.title: Disability and Diversity in Physical Activity
SPED 443.subject: SPED
SPED 443.description: Participants will explore issues related to individuals with exceptionalities, how these affect learning and behavior in the health and physical activity settings. Oral communication practice and skills are worth >30% grade. Required field experience.

SPED 444.title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Elementary
SPED 444.subject: SPED
SPED 444.description: Teaching elementary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction, collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

SPED 445.title: Educating Exceptional Students in Regular Classrooms–Secondary
SPED 445.subject: SPED
SPED 445.description: Teaching secondary students with disabilities and those who are gifted/talented. Meeting academic/social needs, classroom management, motivation, peer interaction. Collaboration between special and regular educators. Includes an emphasis on instruction in writing.

SPED 446.title: Seminar in Special Education
SPED 446.subject: SPED
SPED 446.description: Study of issues, trends, and research into special education programming and service delivery.

SPED 451.title: Programs for Infants/Toddlers
SPED 451.subject: SPED
SPED 451.description: Examination of current theory, research, issues, and models in programs for infants and toddlers including criteria for evaluation and planning.
SPED 451.prereq_raw: HDFS 230 (or concurrent) and HDFS 331 (or concurrent), or consent

SPED 452.title: Preschool Children–Special Needs
SPED 452.subject: SPED
SPED 452.description: Examination of application of current research and practices for serving preschool children with special needs.
