SPED 478.title: Assistant-Level Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
SPED 478.subject: SPED
SPED 478.description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis at the assistant level supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

SPED 486.title: Theoretical Basis for Teaching Special-Needs Students
SPED 486.subject: SPED
SPED 486.description: Survey of biophysical, behavioral, social/ecological, psychodynamic/ psychoeducational, cognitive/developmental, counter-theoretical approaches to teaching exceptional students. Opportunity for the development and/ or strengthening of one’s own theoretical frame of reference.

SPED 487.title: Characteristics/Strategies for Teaching At-Risk Students
SPED 487.subject: SPED
SPED 487.description: Survey of educational, behavioral, and emotional characteristics of students who are at-risk for school failure and strategies to work with such students.

SPED 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
SPED 499.subject: SPED
SPED 499.description: Individual reading, research, and/or projects under direct supervision of instructors.
SPED 499.prereq_raw: consent of instructor or department chair

SPED 501.title: Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education Program Seminar
SPED 501.subject: SPED
SPED 501.description: Mandatory program seminar for Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education (PBSPED) teacher candidates; access to tools and skills necessary for distance education program success; Introduction to the Special Education teaching profession. Post-Bac in SPED majors only.

SPED 526.title: Field Experience in Special EducationPost Baccalaureate
SPED 526.subject: SPED
SPED 526.description: Students spend a minimum of 100 hours over a minimum of 11 weeks in settings appropriate to SPED-PCert program emphasis (mild/ moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by participating teacher and/or college supervisor. Post-Baccalaureate in Special Education only.

SPED 527.title: Student Teaching in Special EducationPost Baccalaureate Programs
SPED 527.subject: SPED
SPED 527.description: Supervised student teaching with a master teacher in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert emphasis (mildmoderate, severe/autism); minimum 280 hours in minimum 11 weeks. Supervision by master teacher and university supervisor.

SPED 528.title: Internship in Special Education-Post Baccalaureate Programs
SPED 528.subject: SPED
SPED 528.description: Supervised teaching experience in PreK-12 educational settings appropriate to SPED-Pcert program emphasis (mild/moderate or severe/autism); supervision provided by master teacher/university mentor, and university supervisor. Must enroll for two consecutive semesters.

SPED 590.title: Internship, Special Education
SPED 590.subject: SPED
SPED 590.description: Supervised field activities involving the programming and instruction of special-needs students within training programs in Hawai‘i and the Pacific Basin.

SPED 600.title: Foundations of Exceptionality
SPED 600.subject: SPED
SPED 600.description: Theoretical, legal and multicultural foundations for assessing, teaching and developing individual service plans across the lifespan for persons with disabilities.

SPED 601.title: Technology for Diverse Learners: Access, Accommodations, and Universal Design
SPED 601.subject: SPED
SPED 601.description: Strategies for using assistive technologies, multimedia technology, and telecommunications to design engaging learning environments that promote inclusion and give voice to diverse learners. Emerging technologies for access, accommodations, and universal design are explored.

SPED 602.title: Special Education Law and Compliance
SPED 602.subject: SPED
SPED 602.description: Examination of the federal, state, and local government roles in special education with special emphasis on case and regulatory law. Focus on understanding special education law necessary in providing services to students with disabilities in a variety of placements. Appropriate for special/general education teachers, administrators, or related service providers.

SPED 603.title: Principles of Behavior
SPED 603.subject: SPED
SPED 603.description: Principles and laws governing behavior and methods that can be used to accomplish educationally relevant changes in student performance. Emphasis on the conceptual basis for changing behavior and use of technologies for changing behavior in school and community settings.

SPED 605.title: Collaboration in School and Community Settings
SPED 605.subject: SPED
SPED 605.description: Collaboration skills necessary to function as team members and to ensure the success of students with disabilities in inclusive school and community settings.

SPED 606.title: Language Development for Deaf Children
SPED 606.subject: SPED
SPED 606.description: General theories of first and second language development applied to development of ASL and English in deaf children. Relationship of theory to educational practice. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 606.prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent

SPED 607.title: Audiology and Spoken English for Deaf Students
SPED 607.subject: SPED
SPED 607.description: Developmental principles of audiology and speech (i.e., spoken English) will be used to examine assessment procedures and intervention strategies appropriate to deaf students in a variety of educational placements. Classroom applications will be presented. Taught in ASL and English.
SPED 607.prereq_raw: admission into Deaf Education program or consent

SPED 608.title: Literacy Development for Deaf Students
SPED 608.subject: SPED
SPED 608.description: Basic concepts related to language, language development and recognition of language-related learning problems of deaf students; strategies for teaching reading and writing to deaf students.

SPED 609.title: Seminar in Bilingual Deaf Education
SPED 609.subject: SPED
SPED 609.description: Study of issues, trends and methods in ASL/ English bilingual education for deaf students. Taught in ASL and English.

SPED 610.title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development–Deaf
SPED 610.subject: SPED
SPED 610.description: Assessment methods and techniques used with deaf students that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming through planning and providing cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment. Taught in ASL and English.

SPED 611.title: Methods and Strategies for Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
SPED 611.subject: SPED
SPED 611.description: Techniques for providing effective instruction including: best instructional practice, lesson planning, teacher-directed and student-mediated instructional strategies, and curricular approaches for working with students with mild/moderate disabilities.

SPED 613.title: Advanced Assessment and Curriculum Development
SPED 613.subject: SPED
SPED 613.description: Assessment methods and techniques that emphasize the bond between curriculum-based assessment and curriculum-based programming. Planning and cyclical instruction across content areas based on ongoing diagnostic assessment.

SPED 614.title: Assessment and Instruction—Severe Disabilities and Autism
SPED 614.subject: SPED
SPED 614.description: Basic principles of assessment, instruction, and curriculum development; application of formal and informal assessment procedures for goal selection, formulating instructional plans, and adapting instructional materials to accommodate learning needs of students with severe disabilities and autism.

SPED 615.title: Family-Centered Approaches in Deaf Education
SPED 615.subject: SPED
SPED 615.description: Prepare teachers to deliver family-centered home-based services to families of deaf children using the SKI-HI model. Course will be taught in ASL and English.

SPED 616.title: Collaboration–Working with Deaf Students in Inclusive Settings
SPED 616.subject: SPED
SPED 616.description: Collaboration skills for working with general education teachers, specialists, paraprofessionals, families and community members to support the success of deaf students in inclusive settings. Taught in ASL and English.

SPED 617.title: Transition Strategies for Deaf Students
SPED 617.subject: SPED
SPED 617.description: Collaborative model for facilitating the transition of deaf and hard-of-hearing students to develop appropriate transition plans and effective plans of study. Taught in ASL and English.

SPED 618.title: Adaptations and Special ProceduresStudents/Severe Disabilities/Autism
SPED 618.subject: SPED
SPED 618.description: Adaptations and special intervention procedures to support the participation of individuals with severe motor, communication, and/or adaptive behavior disabilities in inclusive school and community settings. Includes lab work.

SPED 620.title: Strategies Across Content Area
SPED 620.subject: SPED
SPED 620.description: Strategies for teaching math, science, and social sciences to students of all ages with mild/moderate disabilities; selection of appropriate materials, teaching techniques, curriculum development.

SPED 621.title: Language Arts Strategies: Students with Mild/Moderate Disabilities
SPED 621.subject: SPED
SPED 621.description: Basic concepts related to language, language development, and recognition of language-related learning problems of students with mild/moderate disabilities; strategies for teaching language arts curricula (listening, speaking, reading, writing) to students of all ages with learning problems.

SPED 622.title: Children’s Literature for Deaf Students
SPED 622.subject: SPED
SPED 622.description: Introduction to English literature translated into American Sign Language (ASL) including discussion of ASL literature genres, the importance of translation, selection of literature; story reading, book reading, and retelling. Taught in ASL.

SPED 625.title: Teaching Skills for Social Competence
SPED 625.subject: SPED
SPED 625.description: Issues in social development, self-determination, and social skills competence training for children and youth with disabilities; experience in group social skills training and development of individualized programs.
SPED 625.prereq_raw: either 485 or 630, and either 611 or 614; or consent

SPED 626.title: Field Experiences in Special Education
SPED 626.subject: SPED
SPED 626.description: Students spend a minimum of nine hours per week in settings appropriate to concurrently enrolled courses; supervision provided by participating teacher and college supervisor.

SPED 627.title: Advanced Practicum
SPED 627.subject: SPED
SPED 627.description: Supervised education/community experiences; minimum of 20 hours weekly with special-needs population (MR, LD, SED, SMH); pre-school through postsecondary settings (public/private). Related seminar or equivalent and completion of SPED core required.

SPED 628.title: Internship
SPED 628.subject: SPED
SPED 628.description: Supervised education/ community experiences with special needs populations (MR, LD, SED, SMH), preschool through postsecondary settings. Completion of SPED core required; must enroll for two consecutive semesters.

SPED 629.title: Clinical Practice Special Projects
SPED 629.subject: SPED
SPED 629.description: Development and implementation of a field-based research professional development project under the direction of the student’s advisor; limited to students enrolled in the interdisciplinary program.

SPED 630.title: Positive Behavioral Support-Severe Disabilities and Autism
SPED 630.subject: SPED
SPED 630.description: Principles and laws governing human behavior and positive methods for eliminating significant behavior problems for students with severe disabilities and autism. Emphasis on the functions of behavior, experimental techniques for documenting behavior change, and the use of technologies for improving behavior in school and community settings.

SPED 631.title: Early Intervention for Special Populations
SPED 631.subject: SPED
SPED 631.description: Issues important to early childhood special education. Early screening and assessment, working with families, curriculum options/models, program evaluation.

SPED 632.title: Language/Communication Intervention-Communication Disorders/Autism
SPED 632.subject: SPED
SPED 632.description: Current research in normal language learning, assessment, planning, implementation, evaluation of language delayed/disordered children, including children with autism. Procedures for attaining language/functional communication objectives using ongoing routines/activities.

SPED 633.title: Motor Development/Intervention for Students with Severe Disabilities
SPED 633.subject: SPED
SPED 633.description: Normal/ abnormal motor development; description/etiology of physically disabling conditions influencing motor development; analysis/application of assessment/intervention strategies to promote motor development; positioning and handling skills.

SPED 634.title: Inclusive Physical Activity
SPED 634.subject: SPED
SPED 634.description: Advanced knowledge on issues of socio-cultural, learning styles, diversity, and exceptionalities, and how these influence instruction, engagement, and behavior in physical activity settings across the lifespan.

SPED 635.title: Procedures for Early Childhood Special Education
SPED 635.subject: SPED
SPED 635.description: Assessment and intervention strategies to promote behavior change with young children with disabilities. Promoting child skill gains and integrated programming options.

SPED 637.title: Topics and Issues in Reading Difficulties
SPED 637.subject: SPED
SPED 637.description: Introduction of foundational knowledge of language and literacy development. Current topics and issues related to literacy development in students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

SPED 638.title: Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
SPED 638.subject: SPED
SPED 638.description: Introduction of basic linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for beginning or struggling readers. Covers evidence-based practices for teaching literacy to students with Dyslexia and related reading difficulties.

SPED 639.title: Advanced Fundamentals of Language and Literacy
SPED 639.subject: SPED
SPED 639.description: Advanced linguistic structures of written English related to reading, spelling, and writing for older students. Covers diagnostic assessment, planning, instruction, and progress monitoring for students with Dyslexia or related reading difficulties.

SPED 640.title: Seminar on Mild/Moderate Disabilities
SPED 640.subject: SPED
SPED 640.description: Study of issues, research, program development in the area of mild/moderate disabilities.

SPED 642.title: Seminar on Applied Research/Special Education
SPED 642.subject: SPED
SPED 642.description: Study and development of applied research topics in special education.

SPED 644.title: Seminar on Severe/Multiple Disabilities
SPED 644.subject: SPED
SPED 644.description: Research, program development trends/issues in the area of severe/multiple disabilities (birth through adulthood). College of Education majors only.

SPED 645.title: Seminar in Early Childhood Special Education
SPED 645.subject: SPED
SPED 645.description: Study of issues/trends. Research and program development in early childhood special education.
SPED 645.prereq_raw: (631 and 635) with a minimum grade of B- or better, or consent

SPED 647.title: Leadership in Special Education
SPED 647.subject: SPED
SPED 647.description: Seminar on topics related to leadership in the field of special education, including issues for teacher leaders, administrators, and teacher preparation personnel.

SPED 650.title: Seminar on Universal Design for Learning
SPED 650.subject: SPED
SPED 650.description: Seminar on issues of research and practice on the application of universal design for learning in K-12 and higher education settings. Focus on culturally and linguistically diverse students diversity, non-traditional students and students with disabilities.

SPED 652.title: Transition/Supported Employment
SPED 652.subject: SPED
SPED 652.description: Transition planning for youth with disabilities in preparation for employment as adults in private and public sector businesses.

SPED 671.title: Advanced Principles of Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA)
SPED 671.subject: SPED
SPED 671.description: Focuses on the definitions and characteristics of applied behavior analysis and the concepts, principles, and processes. Concepts related to ethics and behavior change procedures will also be introduced.

SPED 673.title: Ethics and Professional Conduct
SPED 673.subject: SPED
SPED 673.description: Focuses on content on the Behavior Analysis Certification Board’s code for ethical conduct as well as advanced concepts, principles, and processes of applied behavior analysis.

SPED 678.title: Applied Behavior Analysis Fieldwork
SPED 678.subject: SPED
SPED 678.description: Field experience in applied behavior analysis supervised by a Board Certified Behavior Analyst (BCBA). The format is a combination of fieldwork and seminar meetings.

SPED 688.title: Research Practicum in Special Education
SPED 688.subject: SPED
SPED 688.description: Directed research experience to demonstrate mastery of research skills and techniques through developing and writing research proposals.
SPED 688.prereq_raw: 642 or consent, or departmental approval. (Once a year)

SPED 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
SPED 695.subject: SPED
SPED 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project.

SPED 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
SPED 699.subject: SPED
SPED 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

SPED 705.title: Seminar in Exceptionalities
SPED 705.subject: SPED
SPED 705.description: Current and historical topics, issues, and trends in the field of exceptionalities.

SPED 706.title: Doctoral Internship
SPED 706.subject: SPED
SPED 706.description: Supervised internship (minimum 18 hours per week) in program development and administration or research in the student’s area of emphasis.

SPED 710.title: Professional Seminar in Exceptionalities
SPED 710.subject: SPED
SPED 710.description: Professional norms, duties, and expectations of leaders in exceptionalities; transitioning from practitioner to researcher and leadership roles; familiarity with current research and trends in the field of exceptionalities. PhD in EDUC majors only. Graduate students only.

SPED 740.title: Single-Case Experimental Design
SPED 740.subject: SPED
SPED 740.description: Advanced single-case experimental design; examines the logic of internal and external validity of small “N” design and its functionalist foundations.

SPED 745.title: Special Topics in Exceptionalities
SPED 745.subject: SPED
SPED 745.description: Critical examination and discussion of historical or current topic in early intervention, special education, and/or developmental disabilities. (Once a year)

SPED 760.title: Grant Development/Procurement
SPED 760.subject: SPED
SPED 760.description: Overview of grant development and procurement processes related to special education personnel preparation and research and demonstration programs. Students design a grant proposal related to a particular problem or need within their employment settings.

CEE 270.title: Applied Mechanics I
CEE 270.subject: CEE
CEE 270.description: Forces, resultants, and equilibrium; analysis of trusses, frames, and machines; centroids, moments of inertia; friction.
CEE 270.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in PHYS 170 and MATH 242, MATH 243, or MATH 252A (or concurrent)

children.text: grade of C or better in PHYS 170

CEE 271.title: Applied Mechanics II
CEE 271.subject: CEE
CEE 271.description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
CEE 271.prereq_raw: C or better in 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

CEE 305.title: Applied Probability and Statistics
CEE 305.subject: CEE
CEE 305.description: Description of sample data; correlation and regression; probability and statistical distributions; estimations of population parameters; fitting distributions to histograms; hypothesis testing.

CEE 320.title: Fluid Mechanics Fundamentals
CEE 320.subject: CEE
CEE 320.description: Compressible and incompressible fluid properties; fluid statics; kinematics, energy and momentum considerations in steady flows; application of steady flow concepts to various fluid processes; with an emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

CEE 330.title: Environmental Engineering
CEE 330.subject: CEE
CEE 330.description: Parameters and indices of environmental quality; materials balances; chemical kinetics; ideal reactor models; water and air pollution control; solid and hazardous waste management; emphasis on instruction in writing lab reports.

CEE 355.title: Geotechnical Engineering I
CEE 355.subject: CEE
CEE 355.description: Introduction to geotechnical engineering: soil characterization, index properties, seepage and flow in soil, stresses in soils, compressibility, consolidation, shear strength. Substantial emphasis on writing lab reports.

CEE 361.title: Fundamentals of Transportation
CEE 361.subject: CEE
CEE 361.description: Transportation modes: land, air, water, pipelines. Tourist, urban transportation. Geometric design, human factors, vehicular flow models, capacity analysis. Overview: traffic impact, air quality, parking studies.

CEE 370.title: Mechanics of Materials
CEE 370.subject: CEE
CEE 370.description: Elastic stressstrain relation and behavior of members under flexural, torsional, and axial loading.
CEE 370.prereq_raw: 271 (or concurrent); MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

CEE 370L.title: Mechanics of Materials Lab
CEE 370L.subject: CEE
CEE 370L.description: Tension, compression, and torsion of bars, and bending of beams.

CEE 375.title: Construction Materials
CEE 375.subject: CEE
CEE 375.description: Introduction to the crystalline and molecular structure of materials. Properties of metals, concrete, concrete admixtures, asphalt, wood, and other materials commonly used in construction.

CEE 381.title: Structural Analysis
CEE 381.subject: CEE
CEE 381.description: Analysis of statically determinate plane and space trusses and frames; deflections; introduction to matrix methods; computer applications.

CEE 405.title: Engineering Economics
CEE 405.subject: CEE
CEE 405.description: Economic analysis in engineering and management decisionmaking, interest, depreciation, income tax, cost classification, break-even analysis, economic comparisons of alternatives, benefit-cost analysis.

CEE 417.title: Computer Methods in Engineering Systems
CEE 417.subject: CEE
CEE 417.description: Numerical solutions of engineering problems using digital computers. Regression analysis; numerical differentiation and integration; solutions of algebraic, transcendental, and differential equations; and analysis of large structural systems.

CEE 421.title: Engineering Hydraulics
CEE 421.subject: CEE
CEE 421.description: Hydraulics of closed conduits and open channels with emphasis on engineering applications. Topics also include pump hydraulics, bridge hydraulics, urban drainage engineering, and flood plain management.

CEE 422.title: Environmental Fluid Mechanics
CEE 422.subject: CEE
CEE 422.description: Introduction to basic concepts of pollutant transport phenomenon through theoretical modeling, lab and field experiments and observations. Specific topics include mass balance, jets and plumes, mixing and transport in rivers, reservoirs, groundwater and estuaries; non point course pollution.

CEE 424.title: Applied Hydrology
CEE 424.subject: CEE
CEE 424.description: Surface water hydrology topics include hydrologic cycle, hydrographs, regression methods, urban rain-runoff process, flood frequency analysis, flood routing and hydrology for detention basin design. Groundwater hydrology topics include seawater intrusion, theory of groundwater flow and solutions to steady and unsteady aquifer flows.

CEE 431.title: Water and Wastewater Engineering
CEE 431.subject: CEE
CEE 431.description: Hydrologic fundamentals of water demand and supply; water and wastewater distribution; collection systems; quality characterization; analytical methods for water quality management.

CEE 432.title: Water/Wastewater Treatment Design
CEE 432.subject: CEE
CEE 432.description: Physical operations, chemical and biological processes, design flow and process loading rates, pilot plant testing, and treatment plant design.

CEE 440.title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
CEE 440.subject: CEE
CEE 440.description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation.

CEE 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
CEE 441.subject: CEE
CEE 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

CEE 444.title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
CEE 444.subject: CEE
CEE 444.description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. Senior standing or higher.
CEE 444.prereq_raw: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors

children.text: open to engineering, science, urban planning,

CEE 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
CEE 449.subject: CEE
CEE 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.
CEE 449.restrictions_raw: ATMO, CEE, ERTH, GES, OCN, NREM majors only.

CEE 455.title: Geotechnical Engineering II
CEE 455.subject: CEE
CEE 455.description: Continuation of 355 field exploration, lateral earth pressures, heating capacity theory, slope stability, use of geosynthetics.

CEE 461.title: Pavement Engineering
CEE 461.subject: CEE
CEE 461.description: Design principles of flexible and rigid pavements; HMA mixture design, equipment and construction; and application of life cycle cost analysis (LCCA) in pavement engineering. Includes laboratory sessions for aggregate testing and Superpave mix design.

CEE 462.title: Traffic Engineering
CEE 462.subject: CEE
CEE 462.description: Design/analysis of signalized, unsignalized intersections, urban networks. Traffic impact studies; analysis steps and applications. Design/redesign options. Parking studies: demand, alternative designs (lot layouts).

CEE 464.title: Urban and Regional Transportation Planning
CEE 464.subject: CEE
CEE 464.description: Application of travel demand forecasting models to transportation planning. Evaluation and decision-making. Term projects.

CEE 471.title: Construction Methods
CEE 471.subject: CEE
CEE 471.description: Methods of construction, primarily buildings. Construction types: light and heavy wood; steel; plain, reinforced, and prestressed concrete; masonry. Foundations; associated details of frames, walls, roofs, floors,openings, finishes. Disasters, failures, and their causes. Industrialization of the building process.

CEE 472.title: Construction Project Management
CEE 472.subject: CEE
CEE 472.description: Introductory treatment of the management of construction. Construction supervision, contract documents, estimating and bidding, organization, planning and scheduling, administration, business methods, safety, and labor.

CEE 473.title: Construction Equipment and Methods
CEE 473.subject: CEE
CEE 473.description: Methods and equipment used on horizontal/ heavy engineering projects. Available equipment, their production, and how they are used to excavate, move, process, and place the earth.

CEE 474.title: Construction Estimating and Bidding
CEE 474.subject: CEE
CEE 474.description: Estimating science; techniques of estimating quantities and pricing of work for construction contracting; classification of costs, analysis of plans and specifications for estimating; computerized estimating; cash flow, bidding strategy, preparation and submission.

CEE 476.title: Construction Planning and Scheduling
CEE 476.subject: CEE
CEE 476.description: To teach the theory and the practice of planning, scheduling, and reporting a construction project through the use of bar chart and CPM. Format to include lectures, text, outside speakers, site visits, discussions, case study, and computers.

CEE 481.title: Undergraduate Structural Research
CEE 481.subject: CEE
CEE 481.description: Individual research project for undergraduate students in the structures track. Topic to be determined by consultation with structural faculty advisor.

CEE 484.title: Structural Loads
CEE 484.subject: CEE
CEE 484.description: Introduction to the minimum load requirements for buildings and other structures used in current structural design codes. Derive and apply dead, live, rain, soil, snow, wind, earthquake, flood, inundation, and other loads to structural systems.
CEE 484.prereq_raw: (305 and 381) with a minimum grade of C

CEE 485.title: Reinforced Concrete Design
CEE 485.subject: CEE
CEE 485.description: Behavior and design of reinforced concrete beams, one-way slabs and columns. Laboratory section includes design and hands-on manufacturing and testing of reinforced concrete members.

CEE 486.title: Structural Steel Design
CEE 486.subject: CEE
CEE 486.description: Basic properties of steel; behavior and design of steel beams, columns, and connections; introduction to rigid frames.

CEE 490.title: Senior Design Project
CEE 490.subject: CEE
CEE 490.description: (Lec/Lab) Design problem involving several areas of civil engineering and requiring a team approach for a solution.
CEE 490.prereq_raw: senior standing in CEE or CNST and 489B

CEE 491.title: Special Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 491.subject: CEE
CEE 491.description: Will reflect special interests of visiting and/or permanent faculty.
CEE 491.prereq_raw: junior or senior standing, and consent

CEE 499.title: Special Problems
CEE 499.subject: CEE
CEE 499.description: Individual investigation in civil and environmental engineering topics as approved by instructor.
CEE 499.prereq_raw: senior standing, and minimum cumulative GPA of 2.7 or minimum GPA of 3.0 in engineering

CEE 601.title: Operations Management
CEE 601.subject: CEE
CEE 601.description: Linear programming, simplex method, graphical representation: dual; degeneracy; transportation problem; assignment problems; data envelopment analysis; applications; case studies; managerial deporting; LINDO software. Graduate students only.
CEE 601.prereq_raw: 476 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B-), and consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B- ) , and consent

CEE 602.title: Construction Scheduling and Claims
CEE 602.subject: CEE
CEE 602.description: Precedence networks, CPM, float, updating, resource leveling, least cost scheduling, scheduling case studies, computerized scheduling, exclusion reports, sorting, term project; contract law, types of claims, proving claims, delay claims, impact of changes, Eichleay Formula, acceleration, overtime, stacking, crowding, efficiency losses, contract interpretation, Leonard Study, Kuiper model, labor escalation, claims case studies, term paper.
CEE 602.prereq_raw: graduate standing in civil and environmental engineering and consent

children.text: in civil and environmental engineering and consent

CEE 604.title: Cost Engineering and Quality Control
CEE 604.subject: CEE
CEE 604.description: Study and applications of cost/schedule control systems criteria, earned value analysis, probabilistic cost estimating, construction risk management, construction quality control, and operations research in construction.

CEE 606.title: Process Simulation
CEE 606.subject: CEE
CEE 606.description: Analysis of operations and construction processes; CYCLONE simulation language; MicroCyclone and EZstrobe software; production rates; queue waiting time, resource utilization; throughput; cost measurements; programming variables; projects. Graduate students only.
CEE 606.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of C) 474, 476, and consent
CEE 606.restrictions_raw: CEE, ME, and EE majors only.

CEE 614.title: Negotiation and Alternative Dispute Resolution
CEE 614.subject: CEE
CEE 614.description: Lawyers negotiate settlements in almost all their cases. This class presents a “hands-on,” skill-building approach to the newest ideas, as well as centuries-old techniques, about the skill lawyers will use most often in their private practice-negotiation. The class also examines the rapidly developing field of alternative dispute resolution (ADR), including mediation, facilitation, arbitration, and court-annexed ADR.

CEE 618.title: Parallel Computing for Engineers
CEE 618.subject: CEE
CEE 618.description: Concepts and techniques in high performance parallel computing. Topics include parallel language and algorithms, parallelizing pre-existing serial codes, statistical analysis, and techniques up to increase computational speed and accuracy for problems requiring large memory size.

CEE 620.title: Reforming Public Organizations
CEE 620.subject: CEE
CEE 620.description: Explores the possibilities for reducing the most difficult aspects of the bureaucratic form in public organizations while increasing effectiveness and accountability.

CEE 622.title: Fluid Mechanics
CEE 622.subject: CEE
CEE 622.description: Theory of fluid dynamics in differential form, covering equation of motion, vortex generation, flow in rotating frame, potential theory, laminar flow, and introduction to turbulence.

CEE 623.title: Groundwater Modeling
CEE 623.subject: CEE
CEE 623.description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

CEE 625.title: Hydrologic Processes in Soils
CEE 625.subject: CEE
CEE 625.description: Hydrologic properties in soils and the processes involved in water infiltration drainage and solute transport. Emphasis on key parameters required for modeling.

CEE 626.title: Surface Water Hydrology
CEE 626.subject: CEE
CEE 626.description: Deterministic and probabilistic methods include reliability of empirical distributions, multiple regression analysis, extreme value analysis and domain of attraction. Short-memory models for stochastic simulation of streamflows include autoregressive, Markov chain and moving average models. Time series analysis of hydrologic data is discussed.

CEE 627.title: Groundwater Hydrology
CEE 627.subject: CEE
CEE 627.description: Groundwater occurrence, movement, quality, and resource evaluation, development, and management. Emphasis on saltwater encroachment, well evaluation, aquifer protection, recharge with wastewater, and Hawai‘i type hydrology.

CEE 633.title: Physical and Chemical Treatment
CEE 633.subject: CEE
CEE 633.description: Introduction to physical and chemical processes for water and wastewater treatment: Review of momentum and mass transfer, chemical reactions, colloidal chemistry, coagulation and flocculation, granular filtration, sedimentation, carbon adsorption, gas transfer, disinfection and oxidation.

CEE 634.title: Biological Treatment
CEE 634.subject: CEE
CEE 634.description: Fundamentals of applied microbiology and biochemical reactor engineering, quantitative description of microbial growth, operational theory and design basis of aerobic, anoxic and anaerobic treatment processes. Applications for water, wastewater, air, solid wastes, and soil.

CEE 635.title: Environmental Chemistry
CEE 635.subject: CEE
CEE 635.description: Basic concepts of chemistry as related to the environment, with more emphasis on water. Topics include chemical kinetics, equilibrium, acid-base, precipitation and dissolution redox reactions, sorption, organic chemicals in the environment.

CEE 636.title: Environmental Microbiology
CEE 636.subject: CEE
CEE 636.description: Combined lecture-discussion on major topics in environmental microbiology, microbial ecology, and a broad understanding of microbial processes in natural and engineered environments.
CEE 636.prereq_raw: graduate standing in CEE or consent

CEE 643.title: Hazardous Waste Remediation
CEE 643.subject: CEE
CEE 643.description: Introduces the national problems dealing with the contamination of groundwater and presents remedial measures. Such measures include pump and treat (PAT) technology, in-situ bioremediation, soil vapor extraction, air sparging, electrokinetics, hydraulic fracturing, reactive walls, and phytoremediation.

CEE 644.title: Water Quality Modeling
CEE 644.subject: CEE
CEE 644.description: Mathematical formulation of pollutant transport and mixing in the water environment. Kinetics formulation and parameter identification, model calibration and verification. Design projects.

CEE 648.title: Membrane Separations
CEE 648.subject: CEE
CEE 648.description: Applications of membrane separations to desalination, power generation, and ultrapure water systems. Discussion of reverse osmosis, osmosis-driven processes, ultrafiltration, microfiltration, electrodialysis and ion exchange technologies. Membrane fouling and concentration polarization from practical/theoretical standpoints.

CEE 650.title: Seepage, Drainage, and Dewatering
CEE 650.subject: CEE
CEE 650.description: Theory of seepage, field and laboratory methods of measurement; graphical and numerical methods; design of drainage structures; construction dewatering.

CEE 651.title: Deep Foundations
CEE 651.subject: CEE
CEE 651.description: Analysis and design of deep foundations; driven piles and drilled shafts.

CEE 653.title: Advanced Soil Mechanics
CEE 653.subject: CEE
CEE 653.description: Soil continuum mechanics principles; elastic, plastic, and Cam clay soil behavior; critical state and strength; interpretation of laboratory test results.

CEE 655.title: Slope and Earth Structures
CEE 655.subject: CEE
CEE 655.description: Classification of landslides and triggering mechanisms; field investigation procedures; limit equilibrium slope stability methods; numerical techniques; seepage and dynamic considerations; case studies.

CEE 656.title: Marine Geotechnics
CEE 656.subject: CEE
CEE 656.description: Principles of geotechnical engineering applied to marine environments; marine geology; surveying and sampling methods; seabed sediment types, properties, and behavior; coastal and offshore foundations.

CEE 658.title: Earth Pressures
CEE 658.subject: CEE
CEE 658.description: Estimation of lateral earth pressures; analysis and design of retaining walls and excavation support systems.

CEE 660.title: Systems Analysis for Engineers
CEE 660.subject: CEE
CEE 660.description: Optimization used in design and management of systems for minimizing resources or optimizing outcomes. Evaluation of alternatives, economic efficiency and effectiveness analysis. Logistics. Open to engineering students. Computer applications and labs.

CEE 661.title: Intelligent Transportation Systems
CEE 661.subject: CEE
CEE 661.description: Definition, technologies and their attributes. Analysis and implementation based on FHWA’s User Services. Automated incident detection algorithms. Machine vision applications to traffic engineering.

CEE 664.title: Advanced Transportation Modeling and Statistics
CEE 664.subject: CEE
CEE 664.description: Demand modeling, discrete choice and activity-based modeling. Demand forecasting by simulation. Transportation surveys and sampling methods. Application of cluster, factor, regression, logistic and ARIMA analyses to transportation.

CEE 665.title: Pavement Design and Rehabilitation
CEE 665.subject: CEE
CEE 665.description: Pavement engineering with emphasis given to understanding fundamental issues such as historical development of pavement design, approaches used for design of new pavements and overlays, understanding of construction issues and their effects on pavement performance, and various design factors: environmental, loading and materials characterization. Introduction of pavement management systems.

CEE 671.title: Continuum Mechanics
CEE 671.subject: CEE
CEE 671.description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics; coordinate transformations; analysis of stress and strain; principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations; constitutive relations; field equations. Problems in elasticity.

CEE 672.title: Project Management Systems
CEE 672.subject: CEE
CEE 672.description: Project integration and PMIS; organizational power; conflict, strategic, and life-cycle management in construction management; matrix structure compared to projectized structure; project success; team building; change and culture in construction organizations; competitive bidding.

CEE 675.title: Structural Dynamics I
CEE 675.subject: CEE
CEE 675.description: Response of single and multi degree-of-freedom systems due to dynamic forces. Direct integration of equations of motion. Response spectrum analysis. Application to earthquake loading. Systems with distributed mass and elasticity.

CEE 676.title: Structural Dynamics II
CEE 676.subject: CEE
CEE 676.description: Elastic and inelastic response of structures due to earthquakes. Seismic design criteria. Code design procedures. Advanced topics in time- and frequency-domain dynamic analysis of structures.

CEE 677.title: Smart Structures Technology
CEE 677.subject: CEE
CEE 677.description: Fundamentals of sensor technologies for structural engineering applications. Control devices and strategies for protection of structures against extreme events, i.e. earthquakes, strong winds, etc. Structural health monitoring and smart sensor networks. Smart materials for civil structures.

CEE 681.title: Modern Structural Analysis
CEE 681.subject: CEE
CEE 681.description: Fundamentals of modern structural analysis theory, with emphasis on frame structures. Virtual work. Member stiffness/flexibility. Matrix formulation of stiffness and flexibility methods. Computer modeling issues.

CEE 683.title: Advanced Reinforced Concrete Design
CEE 683.subject: CEE
CEE 683.description: Slender columns; biaxial bending; combined shear and torsion. Building lateral load resisting frame analysis and design—shearwalls, rigid frames. Floor system analysis and design—flat slabs, joist systems. Computer applications.

CEE 685.title: Advanced Structural Steel Design
CEE 685.subject: CEE
CEE 685.description: Load and resistance factored design (LRFD); steel building modeling and analysis; moment-resisting frames; bracing systems; beam-columns; moment connections; composite construction; and plate girders.

CEE 686.title: Finite Elements in Structures
CEE 686.subject: CEE
CEE 686.description: Finite element method in structural engineering. Extension of structural theory. Virtual work. One- two-, and three-dimensional elements; axisymmetric elements; plate bending. Application to linear problems.

CEE 687.title: Prestressed Concrete
CEE 687.subject: CEE
CEE 687.description: Behavior of prestressed concrete members, including prestress losses. Analysis and design of prestressed beams, slabs, and composite sections. Anchorage zone design; continuous systems.

CEE 688.title: Advanced Concrete Technology
CEE 688.subject: CEE
CEE 688.description: Composition and hydration of concrete, chemical, and mineral admixtures, fresh and hardened properties, mix proportions, high performance concretes, durability and retrofitting technology, non-destructive testing, and advanced material characterization techniques. Graduate students only.

CEE 691.title: Seminar in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 691.subject: CEE
CEE 691.description: Discussions and reports on literature, research, developments and activities in civil engineering. One unit of all graduate students for each graduate degree. Student presentations are required.

CEE 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
CEE 695.subject: CEE
CEE 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.
CEE 695.prereq_raw: graduate standing in CEE or consent

CEE 696.title: Selected Topics in Civil and Environmental Engineering
CEE 696.subject: CEE
CEE 696.description: Highly specialized topics in structures, soils, hydraulics, sanitary, water resources, applied mechanics, transportation.

CEE 800.title: Dissertation Research
CEE 800.subject: CEE
CEE 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in civil engineering

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in civil engineering

EE 101.title: Electrical Engineering Skills
EE 101.subject: EE
EE 101.description: Electrical engineering subjects in a skill acquisition context at the freshman level. Learning, creative problem solving, brainstorming, technical information assimilation, and presentation skills development.

EE 110.title: Introduction to Engineering Computation
EE 110.subject: EE
EE 110.description: Engineering problem solving using MATLAB. Basic programming concepts include input/output, branching, looping, functions, file input/output, and data structures such as arrays and structures. Matrix operations for solving linear equations. Engineering computations and visualization.
EE 110.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent

EE 160.title: Programming for Engineers
EE 160.subject: EE
EE 160.description: Introductory course on computer programming and modern computing environments in C with an emphasis on algorithm and program design, implementation, and debugging. Includes a hands-on laboratory to develop and practice programming skills.
EE 160.prereq_raw: MATH 241 (or concurrent) or MATH 251A (or concurrent) or consent

EE 196.title: Freshman Project
EE 196.subject: EE
EE 196.description: Freshman level individual or team project under EE faculty direction and guidance. This project provides early student entry into EE hands-on project activity providing practical skills, EE subject exposure and experience. Second semester freshman standing required.
EE 196.restrictions_raw: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only.

EE 205.title: Object Oriented Programming
EE 205.subject: EE
EE 205.description: Second-level programming for computer engineers. Object oriented programming paradigm, definition and use of classes, fundamentals of object-oriented design in modern object-oriented languages such as C++. Common data structures, simple searching and sorting techniques.
EE 205.restrictions_raw: CEE, EE, ME, PREN majors only.

EE 211.title: Basic Circuit Analysis I
EE 211.subject: EE
EE 211.description: Linear passive circuits, time domain analysis, transient and steady-state responses, phasors, impedance and admittance; power and energy, frequency responses, resonance.
EE 211.prereq_raw: MATH 243 (or concurrent) or MATH 252A (or concurrent), and PHYS 272 (or concurrent); or consent

EE 213.title: Basic Circuit Analysis II
EE 213.subject: EE
EE 213.description: Laplace transforms and their application to circuits, Fourier transforms and their applications to circuits, frequency selective circuits, introduction to and design of active filters, convolution, and state space analysis of circuits.
EE 213.prereq_raw: 211, and MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent); or consent

EE 260.title: Introduction to Digital Design
EE 260.subject: EE
EE 260.description: Introduction to the design of digital systems with an emphasis on design methods and the implementation and use of fundamental digital components.

EE 296.title: Sophomore Project
EE 296.subject: EE
EE 296.description: Sophomore level individual or team project under EE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills.
EE 296.restrictions_raw: CENG, EE, and PREN majors only.

EE 315.title: Signal and Systems Analysis
EE 315.subject: EE
EE 315.description: Discrete time and continuous time signals and systems, linear systems, convolution, Fourier series, Fourier transform, sampling.
EE 315.prereq_raw: 213 and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent

EE 323.title: Microelectronic Circuits I
EE 323.subject: EE
EE 323.description: Semiconductor structures, operating principles and characteristics of diodes and amplifying devices. Their application as circuit elements in building basic digital, analog, and integrated circuit subsystems.

EE 323L.title: Microelectronic Circuits I Lab
EE 323L.subject: EE
EE 323L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments on linear and logic properties of diodes and transistor networks.

EE 324.title: Physical Electronics
EE 324.subject: EE
EE 324.description: Review of quantum mechanics fundamentals, H-atom, and chemical bonding. Introduction to band structure models and materials. Semiconductor doping, charge carrier statistics and charge transport, including ambipolar transport. Metal-semiconductor and PN junctions.
EE 324.prereq_raw: MATH 243 or MATH 253A, and PHYS 274; or consent

EE 326.title: Microelectronic Circuits II
EE 326.subject: EE
EE 326.description: Principles and design of linear electronic circuits including differential, operational, feedback, and tuned amplifiers; integrated circuits, current mirrors, signal generators, filters, and stability.

EE 326L.title: Microelectronic Circuits II Lab
EE 326L.subject: EE
EE 326L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 326, experiments on linear and analog electronics. Includes an emphasis on writing laboratory reports.

EE 327.title: Theory and Design of IC Devices
EE 327.subject: EE
EE 327.description: Band structure models and carrier transport physics review. Theory and design of semiconductor IC devices: Schottky diodes, bipolar devices (PN junction diodes, BJTs), FETs (MOSFETs, JFETs, and MESFETs).
EE 327.prereq_raw: 324 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A; or consent

EE 328.title: Microcircuit Fabrication
EE 328.subject: EE
EE 328.description: Technology principles, materials, and methods for the design and fabrication of semiconductor devices, integrated circuits, and microelectromechanical systems.

EE 328L.title: Microcircuit Fabrication Lab
EE 328L.subject: EE
EE 328L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on laboratory where students make various electronic and electromechanical micro-devices using IC technology. Devices are also tested and analyzed.

EE 342.title: Probability and Statistics
EE 342.subject: EE
EE 342.description: Probability, statistics, random variables, distributions, densities, expectations, limit theorems, and applications to electrical engineering.
EE 342.prereq_raw: 315 (or concurrent) and either MATH 244 or MATH 253A; or consent

EE 343.title: Introduction to Communication Systems
EE 343.subject: EE
EE 343.description: Signal representation, Fourier analysis; amplitude and angle modulated systems; sampling theorems, pulse and digital modulation systems; carrier modulation by digital signals.

EE 343L.title: Communication Systems Lab
EE 343L.subject: EE
EE 343L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of communication systems.

EE 344.title: Networking I
EE 344.subject: EE
EE 344.description: Covers 4 semesters from the Cisco Networking Academy plus supplementary material; hands-on experience with routers and switches; prepares students for the CCNA. Topics include TCP/IP, LANs, WANs, routing protocols, network security; PPP; ISDN, frame relay.

EE 345.title: Linear Algebra and Machine Learning
EE 345.subject: EE
EE 345.description: Mathematical and algorithmic fundamentals of linear algebra and their applications and illustrations to machine learning. Lab introduces programming with data and uses machine learning libraries for an introduction to commonly used technologies.
EE 345.restrictions_raw: MATH, EE, CENG, CEE, ME, ICS majors only.

EE 351.title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems
EE 351.subject: EE
EE 351.description: Analysis/design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/ Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/ observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

EE 351L.title: Linear Feedback-Control Systems Lab
EE 351L.subject: EE
EE 351L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Provides experience in applying theoretical tools to analyze linear systems. Extensive use is made of computer-aided analysis and design packages study system performance.

EE 361.title: Digital Systems and Computer Design
EE 361.subject: EE
EE 361.description: Design methodology, processor design, control design, memory organization, system organization.

EE 361L.title: Digital Systems and Computer Design Lab
EE 361L.subject: EE
EE 361L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Laboratory for 361, experiments on digital systems and interfacing.

EE 362.title: Discrete Math for Engineers
EE 362.subject: EE
EE 362.description: Logic, sets, number theory, properties of functions, properties of relations, methods of proofs, recursion, counting, probability, trees, graphs, analysis of algorithms, finite state autonoma.

EE 366.title: CMOS VLSI Design
EE 366.subject: EE
EE 366.description: Introduction to the design of very large scale integrated (VLSI) systems and use of CAD tools and design languages. Lab includes hands-on use of CAD tools and experiments with field programmable logic devices.

EE 367.title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms
EE 367.subject: EE
EE 367.description: Design and analysis of data structures and algorithms, including correctness and performance. Topics include time complexity, hash tables, sorting, search trees, self-balancing trees, greedy algorithms, dynamic programming, and graph algorithms.
EE 367.prereq_raw: (205 or ICS 212) and (362 or ICS 241) with a minimum grade of C-

EE 367L.title: Computer Data Structures and Algorithms Lab
EE 367L.subject: EE

EE 368.title: Cyber-Physical Systems and the Internet of Things
EE 368.subject: EE
EE 368.description: Topics include General Purpose Input/ Output (GPIO), serial communications, sensors, actuators, low-power wireless communications. TCP/IP networking, dynamic service discovery, distributed network messaging, machine-to-machine communication and cloud-computing interaction.

EE 369.title: Computational Media Systems
EE 369.subject: EE
EE 369.description: Intermediate object-oriented programming within the context of interactive media systems and video game development. Topics: classes, objects, inheritance, polymorphism, abstract classes, interfaces, event-driven programming, vectors, geometric primitives, game mechanics, and relevant design patterns.

EE 371.title: Engineering Electromagnetics I
EE 371.subject: EE
EE 371.description: Transient and steady-state waves on transmission lines. Plane wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations. Application of Maxwell’s equations under static and time-varying conditions.

EE 372.title: Engineering Electromagnetics II
EE 372.subject: EE
EE 372.description: Solution of Maxwell’s equations under various boundary conditions. Introduction to radiation, guided waves, and principles of optics.

EE 372L.title: Engineering Electromagnetics Lab
EE 372L.subject: EE
EE 372L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Experiments illustrating the basic principles of electromagnetics and optics.

EE 396.title: Junior Project
EE 396.subject: EE
EE 396.description: Junior level individual or team project under EE faculty direction and guidance. The project provides design experience and develops practical skills. It may be a continuation of EE 296 or a new project. Junior standing or higher.

EE 406.title: Introduction to Computer and Network Security
EE 406.subject: EE
EE 406.description: Review basic network mechanisms, introduce basic cryptography concepts, and study algorithms and protocols used in computer and network security. Discuss practical security mechanisms.
EE 406.prereq_raw: 361 or ICS 312 or ICS 331 or instructor consent. (Once a year)

EE 415.title: Digital Signal Processing
EE 415.subject: EE
EE 415.description: Discrete-time signals and systems, sampling, Z-transform, transform, transform analysis of linear time-invariant systems, filter design, discrete Fourier transform, and computation of discrete Fourier transform.

EE 416.title: Introduction to Digital Image Processing
EE 416.subject: EE
EE 416.description: Digital image representation, intensity transformations, spatial filtering, filtering in the frequency domain, image restoration, color spaces and transformations, the fast wavelet transform, image compression.

EE 417.title: Introduction to Optimization
EE 417.subject: EE
EE 417.description: Application of linear, nonlinear and integer optimization models and algorithms to communications, control, signal processing, computer networking, financial engineering, manufacturing, production and distribution systems. CE, EE, ME, or CBA majors only.

EE 422.title: Sensors and Instrumentation for Biological Systems
EE 422.subject: EE
EE 422.description: Design course focused on fundamentals of electronic interfacing, control and automation, including biological processes. Topics include sensor physics, basic instrumentation, digital communication, and programming of microcontrollers and other portable computer systems.
EE 422.prereq_raw: (160, 211, and BE 350 or MATH 302 or MATH 307 or EE 326) with a minimum grade of C; or consent

EE 423.title: Computer-Aided Analysis and Design
EE 423.subject: EE
EE 423.description: Algorithms and techniques used in computer-aided analysis and design of electronic circuits. Circuit simulation with interactive computers.

EE 425.title: Electronic Instrumentation II
EE 425.subject: EE
EE 425.description: Instrumentation systems and circuits for measurement, control, signal processing, transmission, and detection. Noise and interference, ADC/DAC, modulation demodulation, high-frequency and high-speed techniques, IC applications.

EE 426.title: Advanced Si IC and Solid State Devices
EE 426.subject: EE
EE 426.description: State of the art Si-based devices including advanced bipolar and MOS devices, heterojunction devices, new device trends. Topics from the most current literature included.
EE 426.prereq_raw: 327 and either MATH 243 or MATH 253A, or consent

EE 427.title: Computer-Aided Circuit Design
EE 427.subject: EE
EE 427.description: Application of the computer to the analysis, design, simulation, and construction of analog and digital circuits.

EE 435.title: Electric Power Systems
EE 435.subject: EE
EE 435.description: Design/ operation of “the grid.” History of electric power systems, three-phrase power, real and reactive power, transformers, transmission, distribution, circuit analysis, protection, load flow, load frequency control, optimal power flow, and renewable energy integration.

EE 438.title: Renewable Energy
EE 438.subject: EE
EE 438.description: Fundamentals of power, electric power grid and conventional electricity generation. Wind and solar power systems. Photovoltaic materials and systems. Distributed generation and energy storage. Junior standing or higher.

EE 442.title: Digital Communications
EE 442.subject: EE
EE 442.description: Baseband transmission, intersymbol interference and pulse shaping, partial response signaling, equalization, bandpass modulation and demodulation, channel coding, synchronization, multiplexing and multiple access, spread spectrum techniques.

EE 445.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
EE 445.subject: EE
EE 445.description: Foundation for algorithms, practice, and theory behind common machine-learning applications. Includes projects, statistical programming, and an introduction to the unique challenges of high-dimensional problems.

children.text: ( or equivalent) and MATH 307 ( or equivalent)

EE 445.restrictions_raw: EE, CENG, CEE, ME, MATH, ICS majors only.

EE 446.title: Information Theory and Coding
EE 446.subject: EE
EE 446.description: Models of communication systems. Channel noise, measurement, and coding of information. Intrinsic limits of performance of communication systems.

EE 449.title: Computer Communication Networks
EE 449.subject: EE
EE 449.description: ISO Reference Model. Physical Layer, Data Link Layer, Network Layer and Transport Layer protocols. Wired and wireless local-area networks. Structure and operation of the Internet including routing, congestion control and flow control.
EE 449.prereq_raw: 315 and one of 342, or MATH 371 or MATH 471; or consent

EE 452.title: Digital Control Systems
EE 452.subject: EE
EE 452.description: Sampling/ reconstruction, Z-transform, DT transfer function. Reachability/observability. State and output feedback, observer design, input-output models, diophantine equations. Implementation procedures.

EE 453.title: Modern Control Theory
EE 453.subject: EE
EE 453.description: Analysis and synthesis of nonlinear control systems by means of Lagrange’s equation, state space techniques, maximum principle. Lyapunov’s theorems, the phase plane, and Z-transform techniques. Optimization and adaptation by means of gradient methods, calculus of variations, dynamic programming.

EE 455.title: Design of Intelligent Robots
EE 455.subject: EE
EE 455.description: Study of the design principles of computer-controlled, intelligent robots such as roving vehicles, hand-eye systems.

EE 461.title: Computer Architecture
EE 461.subject: EE
EE 461.description: Structure of stored program machines, data flow machines, pipelining, fault-tolerant computing, instruction set design, effects of compilation on architecture, RISC vs. CISC architecture, uses of parallelism.

EE 467.title: Object-oriented Software Engineering
EE 467.subject: EE
EE 467.description: Introduction to advanced techniques for designing, implementing, and testing computer software with a particular focus on using object-oriented design, analysis, and programming to produce high-quality computer programs that solve non-trivial problems.

EE 468.title: Introduction to Operating Systems
EE 468.subject: EE
EE 468.description: Computer system organization; multiprocessor systems, memory hierarchies, assemblers, compilers, operating systems, virtual machine, memory management, processor management; information management.

EE 469.title: Wireless Data Networks
EE 469.subject: EE
EE 469.description: Mobile agent’s platforms and systems, mobile agent-based service implementation, middleware, and configuration, wireless local area networks, wireless protocols, network architecture supporting wireless applications, routing protocols in mobile and wireless networks, handoff in mobile and wireless networks.

EE 470.title: Physical Optics
EE 470.subject: EE
EE 470.description: Fundamentals of classical physical optics emphasizing linear systems theory, including optical fields in matter, polarization phenomena, temporal coherence, interference and diffraction (Fourier optics). Specialized applications include Gaussian beams, laser resonators, pulse propagation, and nonlinear optics.
EE 470.prereq_raw: 372 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C-) or PHYS 450 (or concurrent with a minimum grade of C), or consent

children.text: ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C- ) or PHYS 450 ( or concurrent with a minimum grade of C ) , or consent

EE 471.title: Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
EE 471.subject: EE
EE 471.description: Introduction to computational methods used to simulate/solve engineering design problems focusing on electromagnetics. Finite difference, method of moments, and finite elements methods will be described; students will write computer programs in each.

EE 473.title: Microwave Engineering
EE 473.subject: EE
EE 473.description: Passive and active microwave devices and circuits for RF and wireless applications. Scattering parameters, signal-flow graphs, and computer-aided design.

EE 474.title: Antennas
EE 474.subject: EE
EE 474.description: Electromagnetic wave propagation in free space and ionized media. Geomagnetic and solar effects on the ionosphere. Absorption and dispersion. Antenna arrays, apertures, horns, impedance. Design of antenna systems.

EE 475.title: Optical Communications
EE 475.subject: EE
EE 475.description: Principles and applications of optical fibers and waveguides. Fundamentals of optical communication systems (optical links, high-speed systems, wavelengthdivision-multiplexing networks, and network elements) and optical components (guided-wave circuits, lasers, detectors, and optical amplifiers). System and network integration issues.

EE 477.title: Fundamentals of Radar, Sonar, and Navigation Systems
EE 477.subject: EE
EE 477.description: Discussion of basic radar detection and position- and velocity-measurement principles. Applications to various types of radar and sonar systems. Modern navigation aids.
EE 477.prereq_raw: 371 (or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

children.text: ( or equivalent), and familiarity with waveguides or waveguide theory

EE 480.title: Introduction to Biomedical and Clinical Engineering
EE 480.subject: EE
EE 480.description: Application of engineering principles and technology to biological and medical problems. Introduction to human anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, clinical measurements. Systems modeling, physiological control systems, computer applications, health-related problems.

EE 480L.title: Biomedical Engineering Lab
EE 480L.subject: EE
EE 480L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Measurement of bioelectrical signals, computer and electronic simulation of biological systems, design and evaluation of electronic circuits for biomedical measurements, evaluation of instruments for patient safety.

EE 481.title: Bioelectric Phenomena
EE 481.subject: EE
EE 481.description: Study of electrical phenomena in living systems. Mechanisms underlying bioelectric activity. Membrane and transepithelial potentials, skin impedance, electrocardiography, neuroelectric signals, diagnostic considerations, laboratory demonstrations.

EE 482.title: Biomedical Instrumentation
EE 482.subject: EE
EE 482.description: Principles, applications, and design of biomedical instrumentation. Transducers, IC and microcomputer applications, patient safety.

EE 494.title: Provisional Topics
EE 494.subject: EE
EE 494.description: Upper division course with subject matter to be announced.

EE 495.title: Ethics in Electrical Engineering
EE 495.subject: EE
EE 495.description: Equip electrical engineers with the necessary background for ethical reasoning, as it pertains to technology, society, workplace issues, and the environment.
EE 495.prereq_raw: senior standing or consent. (Once a year)

EE 496.title: Capstone Design Project
EE 496.subject: EE
EE 496.description: Significant project integrating the design content of previous courses and incorporating engineering standards and realistic constraints. Written report must document all aspects of the design process: reliability, safety, economics, ethics.

EE 601.title: Graph Theory and Its Applications
EE 601.subject: EE
EE 601.description: Graphs and subgraphs, trees and treelike graphs, planar graphs, connectivity and edge-connectivity, applications.

EE 602.title: Algorithm I
EE 602.subject: EE
EE 602.description: Design and evaluation of machine representations, techniques and algorithms for sorting, pattern processing, computational geometry, mathematical computations, and engineering applications. Introduction to computational issues of time, space, communication, and program correctness.

EE 604.title: Artificial Intelligence
EE 604.subject: EE
EE 604.description: LISP for machine intelligence applications, or related constraint object and logic-oriented languages.

EE 606.title: Intelligent Autonomous Agents
EE 606.subject: EE
EE 606.description: Theory, methods and practical applications of autonomous agent systems, including common applications of both software and hardware (robotic) agents. In-depth practical experience with autonomous agents through programming assignments and projects.
EE 606.prereq_raw: 467 or ICS 313 (or equivalent), graduate standing; or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: ( or equivalent), graduate standing ; or consent . ( Once a year)

EE 607.title: Advanced Network Algorithms
EE 607.subject: EE
EE 607.description: Network algorithms, protocols, and packet switching systems for the internet including TCP/IP, routing algorithms, transmission scheduling, link management, buffer management, and simple network management.

EE 608.title: Optical Networks
EE 608.subject: EE
EE 608.description: Propagation of signals in fibers, components, modulation and demodulation, transmission system engineering, network systems and architectures, network design, control and management and packet switching.

EE 609.title: Computer and Network Security
EE 609.subject: EE
EE 609.description: Basic security theory, current practices, and emerging research issues. First covering the fundamentals of computer and network security, then will work on research projects on computer and network security

EE 615.title: Advanced Digital Signal Processing
EE 615.subject: EE
EE 615.description: An advanced course in digital processing. Topics include fast DFT algorithms, multirate systems and filter banks, power spectrum estimation, linear prediction, optimum linear filters, and adaptive filtering. Open to nonmajors for CR/NC only.

EE 616.title: Digital Image Processing
EE 616.subject: EE
EE 616.description: Human visual perception, image formation, sampling and quantization, enhancement and restoration, color image processing, wavelets and multiresolution representations, image and video compression.

EE 617.title: Linear and Convex Optimization
EE 617.subject: EE
EE 617.description: Algorithms for linear, nonlinear, and convex optimization. Emphasis is on methodology and the underlying mathematical structures. Topics include simplex method, network flow methods, optimality conditions, duality, Newton’s method and interior point methods.
EE 617.restrictions_raw: EE, ME, MIS and MATH majors only.

EE 618.title: Dynamic Programming and Stochastic Control
EE 618.subject: EE
EE 618.description: Sequential decision-making via dynamic programming. Optimal control of stochastic dynamic systems. Applications in linear-quadratic control, inventory control, resource allocation, scheduling, and control of queues. Rollout and other suboptimal methods. Value and policy iteration.
EE 618.prereq_raw: 342 or MATH 371 or MATH 471, or consent

EE 620.title: Advanced Electronic Circuits
EE 620.subject: EE
EE 620.description: Electronic circuits for precision measurement, computation, and signal processing. Low noise and interference reduction techniques. High-frequency and high-speed techniques. Micro-processor and biomedical applications.

EE 621.title: Advanced Solid-State Devices
EE 621.subject: EE
EE 621.description: Advanced physical principles and design of modern solid-state electronic devices. Heterostructures, photodetectors, LED, junction lasers, and other devices of current importance identified from the current literature.

EE 622.title: Optical Electronics I
EE 622.subject: EE
EE 622.description: Fundamentals of optical radiation, including stimulated and spontaneous processes. Optical electronics including optical resonators, lasers, optical detectors, lightguiding, and applications.

EE 623.title: Optical Electronics II
EE 623.subject: EE
EE 623.description: Electro-optics, noise detection, light and sound dielectric waveguide phenomena, lasers, optics, phase conjugation.

EE 624.title: Microsensors and Microactuators I
EE 624.subject: EE
EE 624.description: Technology methods and physical principles of microsensors and microactuators. Vacuum technology, thin film deposition and characterization techniques, solid mechanics, micromachining, acoustics, piezoelectricity and principles of current microtransducers.

EE 626.title: Rapid Prototyping of Electrophysical Devices
EE 626.subject: EE
EE 626.description: Hands on experience in designing, fabricating, testing, and iterating according to rapid-prototyping principles. Students learn state-of-the-art equipment for making their designs, software for simulating designs, and working in design teams. Graduate students only.

EE 627.title: Advanced Topics in Physical Electronics
EE 627.subject: EE
EE 627.description: Recent developments in phenomena and devices of physical electronics.

EE 628.title: Analysis and Design of Integrated Circuits
EE 628.subject: EE
EE 628.description: Fabrication constraints and design guidelines for integrated circuits. Nonlinear model of integrated circuit transistor. Design and analysis of integrated logic circuits and linear circuits.

EE 635.title: Smart Grids and Renewable Energy Integration
EE 635.subject: EE
EE 635.description: Challenges and solutions for integrating intermittent renewable energy sources into the power system, with a focus on “smart grid” approaches and demand-response. Using linear programming and other modeling techniques to answer policy-relevant questions. Graduate students only.

EE 640.title: Applied Random Processes
EE 640.subject: EE
EE 640.description: Random variables, multivariate distributions, random sequences, stochastic convergence, stationary and nonstationary processes, spectral analysis, KarhunenLoeve expansion, Markov processes, mean square estimation, Kalman filters.

EE 641.title: Queueing Theory
EE 641.subject: EE
EE 641.description: Poisson, Markov, and renewal processes, M/G/1 queue, G/M/1 queue, queueing networks, simulation, and performance evaluation of computer systems and communication networks.

EE 642.title: Detection and Estimation Theory
EE 642.subject: EE
EE 642.description: Fundamentals of signal detection and estimation theory. Hypothesis testing, parametric and nonparametric detection, sequential detection, parametric estimation, linear estimation, robust detection and estimation, and applications to communication systems.

EE 643.title: Communication System Performance
EE 643.subject: EE
EE 643.description: Fundamental performance limits, signal detection and estimation, modulation, intersymbol interference, equalization adaptive filtering, sequence detection, synchronization, fading multipath channels, spread spectrum.

EE 644.title: Computer Communication Networks
EE 644.subject: EE
EE 644.description: Fundamentals of computer communication networks including modeling, performance evaluation, routing, flow control, local area networks, distributed algorithms, and optimization algorithms.

EE 645.title: Machine Learning
EE 645.subject: EE
EE 645.description: Learning theory, pattern recognition and regression; gradient based algorithms and least square algorithms; Kernel methods; Bayesian learning algorithms; ensemble learning and boosting; principal component analysis; independent component analysis, and clustering; reinforcement learning and approximate dynamic programming.
EE 645.restrictions_raw: EE, ME, ICS, MATH majors only.

EE 646.title: Advanced Information Theory
EE 646.subject: EE
EE 646.description: Measure of information, coding for discrete sources, discrete memoryless channels and capacity, the noisy channel coding theorem, source coding with fidelity criterion, rate-distortion theory, multiuser channels.

EE 647.title: Source Coding
EE 647.subject: EE
EE 647.description: Theory and applications of source coding, rate-distortion theory, companding, lattice coding, tree coding, trellis coding, entropy-constrained coding, asymptotic theory, predictive and differential encoding, combined source/channel coding, vector quantization.

EE 648.title: Error-Control Coding I
EE 648.subject: EE
EE 648.description: Linear block codes, soft and hard decision decodings, correction of random errors, cyclic codes, BCH codes, ReedSolomon codes, majority logic decodable codes, burst-error correcting codes, concatenated codes.

EE 649.title: Error-Control Coding II
EE 649.subject: EE
EE 649.description: Convolutional codes, Viterbi algorithm, coded modulation, multistage decoding, concatenated coded modulation, probabilistic decoding, turbo codes, low density parity check codes and iterative decoding.

EE 650.title: Linear System Theory
EE 650.subject: EE
EE 650.description: State space theory of linear systems, controllability, observability, stability, irreducible realizations.

EE 651.title: Nonlinear Control Systems
EE 651.subject: EE
EE 651.description: Digital simulations, phase-plane analysis, limit cycles and amplitude bounds, Lyapunov’s theorem, circle criterion of stability, lure systems, Popov’s stability theorem.

EE 652.title: Optimal Control Systems
EE 652.subject: EE
EE 652.description: Optimal controls introduced through parametric optimization, calculus of variations, Euler-Lagrange and Hamilton-Jacobi equations, Pontryagin’s maximum principle, minimum-time and minimum-fuel problems, dynamic programming, applications.

EE 655.title: Robust Control
EE 655.subject: EE
EE 655.description: Multivariable frequency response design, signals and systems, linear fractional transformations, LQG Control, Full Information H-infinity Controller Synthesis, H-infinity filtering, model reduction, the four-block problem.

EE 660.title: Computer Architecture I
EE 660.subject: EE
EE 660.description: Models of computation, high-performance processors, pipelined machines, RISC processors, VLIW, superscalar and fine-grain parallel machines. Data-flow architectures. Hardware/software tradeoffs.
EE 660.restrictions_raw: CEE, EE, and ME majors only.

EE 665.title: Computer Systems
EE 665.subject: EE
EE 665.description: Modern operating system software, process communication, distributed systems, device drivers. Software development and maintenance, integration of software packages. Projects reflecting special interests of faculty.

EE 668.title: Telecommunication Networks
EE 668.subject: EE
EE 668.description: Telecommunication-network architecture; switching, broadcast, and wireless networks; protocols, interfaces, routing, flow- and congestion-control techniques; intelligent network architecture; service creation capabilities; multimedia, voice, data, and video networks and services.

EE 671.title: Electromagnetic Theory and Applications
EE 671.subject: EE
EE 671.description: Solutions of Maxwell’s equations and applications to radiation and propagation of electromagnetic waves.

EE 673.title: Advanced Microwave Engineering
EE 673.subject: EE
EE 673.description: Advanced RF and microwave circuit design for wireless applications.

EE 675.title: Advanced Computational Techniques in Electromagnetics
EE 675.subject: EE
EE 675.description: Develop comprehensive understanding of computations techniques for solving engineering electromagnetic problems formulated in terms of integral or differential equations. Eigenvalue problems, radiation, and electromagnetics scattering problems will be discussed and computer programming is required.
EE 675.prereq_raw: 471 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent
