EE 675.restrictions_raw: EE, BE, and CENG majors only.

EE 680.title: Biomedical Engineering Systems
EE 680.subject: EE
EE 680.description: Systems analysis and electronic instrumentation methods in biomedicine. Network and control-loop modeling, computer simulation, biological transducers, and analysis of electronic and physiological systems.

EE 681.title: Biosensors and Bioelectronics
EE 681.subject: EE
EE 681.description: Advanced topics in the design of biological detection technologies. Topics include fundamentals of electrochemistry, electrochemical biosensors, DNA and protein biochips, and bioelectronics for bio-signal conditioning and processing.

EE 682.title: Biomedical Microdevices
EE 682.subject: EE
EE 682.description: Design and fabrication of micro- and nanodevices for biomedical applications. Topics include micro- and nanoscale physics, microfluidic physics and microfluidic devices, and micro- and nanoscale fabrication techniques.

EE 685.title: Biomedical Signal Processing and Analysis
EE 685.subject: EE
EE 685.description: Biomedical signals, digital filters and filter banks, spike train analysis, time-scale and time-frequency representations, nonlinear techniques, Lomb’s algorithm and the Hilbert transform, modeling, Volterra series, Wiener series, Poisson-Wiener series, multichannel data, causality. CE, EE, ME, ICS majors only and any graduate student in JABSOM who has a suitable technical background.

EE 700.title: Thesis Research
EE 700.subject: EE
EE 700.prereq_raw: candidacy for MS in electrical engineering

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for MS in electrical engineering

EE 790.title: Directed Instruction
EE 790.subject: EE
EE 790.description: Student assists in classroom instruction under direction and close supervision of faculty member.

EE 800.title: Dissertation Research
EE 800.subject: EE
EE 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in electrical engineering

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in electrical engineering

ENGR 100.title: Engineering Freshman Seminar
ENGR 100.subject: ENGR
ENGR 100.description: Overview of the engineering field, the different disciplines, and opportunities. Success strategies for studying engineering.

ENGR 101.title: Introduction to Engineering
ENGR 101.subject: ENGR
ENGR 101.description: Topics include the engineering disciplines, the development of problem solving and technical communication skills, the design process and analysis methods using a team design project, and introduction to programming in Matlab for engineering applications. Freshman standing only.

ENGR 102.title: Introduction to Technology-Based Innovation and Entrepreneurship
ENGR 102.subject: ENGR
ENGR 102.description: Introduces modern tools for launching technology-based new ventures. Teams of students engage in term projects to learn design thinking, business model generation, product development, rapid prototyping, customer validation, and pitching to investors. Freshmen only.

ENGR 196.title: Freshman Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 196.subject: ENGR
ENGR 196.description: Team-based research project for freshman-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a sophomore (ENGR 296).

ENGR 250.title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
ENGR 250.subject: ENGR
ENGR 250.description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders.

ENGR 296.title: Sophomore Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 296.subject: ENGR
ENGR 296.description: Team-based research project for sophomore-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a junior (ENGR 396). Sophomore standing or higher.

ENGR 350.title: Career Development Seminar
ENGR 350.subject: ENGR
ENGR 350.description: Introduction to career development as it pertains to engineering and business industry; client relations, networking, job skills, career assessment and direction.

ENGR 396.title: Junior Vertically Integrated Project
ENGR 396.subject: ENGR
ENGR 396.description: Team-based research project for junior-level students. Project topic varies by instructor. Students are expected to continue working in this project as a senior. Junior standing or higher.

ENGR 401.title: Engineering Management
ENGR 401.subject: ENGR
ENGR 401.description: Introduction to engineering management with emphasis on development of skills for professional advancement.

ENGR 493.title: Field Experience
ENGR 493.subject: ENGR
ENGR 493.description: Supervised internship in engineering practice under professional and faculty direction.
ENGR 493.prereq_raw: junior standing in engineering and consent

ME 113.title: Introduction to Engineering Design I
ME 113.subject: ME
ME 113.description: Introductory experience in analysis, synthesis, and design. Teamwork and project required.

ME 213.title: Introduction to Engineering Design
ME 213.subject: ME
ME 213.description: Introductory experience in communication, presentation, professional ethics, social responsibility, engineering economics, quality control, and computer-aided drafting. Teamwork and project required.

ME 271.title: Applied Mechanics II
ME 271.subject: ME
ME 271.description: Dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; force, acceleration, impulse-momentum, work-energy.
ME 271.prereq_raw: C or better in CEE 270; MATH 244 (or concurrent) or MATH 253A (or concurrent)

ME 311.title: Thermodynamics
ME 311.subject: ME
ME 311.description: Basic laws, closed and open systems. Work, heat, concept of entropy. Properties of pure simple substances. Ideal gases. Introduction to power and refrigeration cycles.
ME 311.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), PHYS 170 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A)

ME 322.title: Mechanics of Fluids and Lab
ME 322.subject: ME
ME 322.description: Incompressible and compressible ideal fluids, effects of viscosity. Similitude, boundary layer flow. Measurement techniques in thermodynamics and fluid mechanics. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems.
ME 322.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of 311 and CEE 271 (or ME 271)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of 311

ME 331.title: Materials Science and Engineering
ME 331.subject: ME
ME 331.description: Electronic, atomic, and crystalline structure of materials and their effect on the mechanical, electrical, optical, and magnetic properties of engineering metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.
ME 331.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CHEM 162 (or CHEM 171 or CHEM 181A), MATH 242 (or MATH 252A), and PHYS 170

ME 341.title: Manufacturing Processes and Lab
ME 341.subject: ME
ME 341.description: Manufacturing components. Energy requirements for manufacturing methods. Manufacturing methods to obtain components with desired size/shape/properties. Conduct tension/ compression tests, cold rolling, welding, casting statistical process control, programming, and milling using a CNC machine.

ME 342.title: Manufacturing Processes Lab
ME 342.subject: ME
ME 342.description: Manufacturing laboratory: tension/ compression tests, cold rolling, welding, casting, statistical process control, programming and milling using a CNC machine.

ME 360.title: Computer Methods in Engineering
ME 360.subject: ME
ME 360.description: Numerical solutions for algebraic and transcendental equations, simultaneous linear algebraic equations, integration and differentiation; integration of ordinary differential equations. Engineering applications.
ME 360.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of EE 160 (or EE 110 or ICS 111), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A), and MATH 302 (or MATH 307)

ME 371.title: Mechanics of Solids
ME 371.subject: ME
ME 371.description: Stress, strain and constitutive relations for elastic solids. Design of shafts, beams, columns and cylinders. Failure theories, statically indeterminate systems.
ME 371.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CEE 270 and MATH 244 (or MATH 253A) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307 or BE 350)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of CEE 270
( or MATH 253A ) and MATH 302 ( or MATH 307 or BE 350 )

ME 372.title: Component Design
ME 372.subject: ME
ME 372.description: Design, analysis, and selection of machine components: shafts, screws, fasteners, welds, rolling contact bearings, journal bearings, gears, clutches, brakes, belts, and roller chains.

ME 374.title: Kinematics/Dynamics Machinery
ME 374.subject: ME
ME 374.description: Velocity and acceleration analysis of planar mechanisms; kinematic synthesis of linkages, cams, and gears; static and dynamic force analysis of mechanisms; balancing of machinery.
ME 374.prereq_raw: CEE 271 or ME 271 (C or better), MATH 244 (or MATH 253A) and either MATH 302 or MATH 307

children.text: ( or MATH 253A ) and either MATH 302 or MATH 307

ME 375.title: Dynamics of Machines and Systems and Lab
ME 375.subject: ME
ME 375.description: Lumped-parameter modeling of dynamic systems. Methods of analysis, including transform techniques. Time and frequency response. Feedback control. Engineering instrumentation. Data acquisition. Dynamic measurements. Design and testing.
ME 375.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (or ME 271) and MATH 302 (or MATH 307)

children.text: grade of C or better in all of CEE 271 (

ME 402.title: Dynamics Systems Laboratory
ME 402.subject: ME
ME 402.description: Analysis, design, fabrication, testing and characterization of engineering instrumentation. Computer-based data acquisition methods. Techniques and procedures associated with carrying out dynamic measurements within the constraints of cost, time and accuracy.
ME 402.prereq_raw: one of 360, MATH 407, or PHYS 305 (or concurrent for any); and 375 (or concurrent)

children.text: ( or concurrent for any); and 375 (or concurrent)

ME 403.title: Advanced Mathematics for Engineers
ME 403.subject: ME
ME 403.description: Applications of ordinary differential equations, Laplace transform, vector field theory, matrices, line integrals.

children.text: ( or MATH 253A ) , and MATH 302 ( or MATH 307 )

ME 404.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics
ME 404.subject: ME
ME 404.description: Basic computational fluid dynamics; four important partial differential equations; introduction to finite element method: Interpolation and Galerkin method; finite element method for transport phenomena; some algorithms for parallel computing.
ME 404.prereq_raw: 422 (or concurrent ), and either 360, MATH 407 or PHYS 305; or consent

ME 411.title: Applied Thermodynamics
ME 411.subject: ME
ME 411.description: Gas mixtures, generalized thermodynamic relationships, combustion and thermochemistry, chemical equilibrium, power and refrigeration cycles.
ME 411.prereq_raw: grade of C or better in 311

prereq_tree.text: grade of C or better in 311

ME 417.title: Applied Thermal Engineering
ME 417.subject: ME
ME 417.description: Principles, design and analysis of practical thermal systems. Engineering applications. Valve, compressor, condenser and evaporator technologies. System integration and control. Thermal loads and thermal comfort.

ME 418.title: Power and Propulsion
ME 418.subject: ME
ME 418.description: Principles, performance, and design of gas turbine power plants and propulsion systems.

ME 419.title: Astronautics
ME 419.subject: ME
ME 419.description: The space environment (vacuum, neutral, radiation, and plasma); motion in gravitational fields; orbit transfers; Earth-satellite operations; rocketry; propulsion analysis and performance; reentry dynamics; interplanetary trajectories; attitude dynamics and stabilization.

ME 422.title: Heat Transfer and Lab
ME 422.subject: ME
ME 422.description: Steady and unsteady conduction; steady convection and radiation; heat exchangers. Emphasis on writing instruction.

ME 423.title: Mass Transfer
ME 423.subject: ME
ME 423.description: Elementary mass diffusion; diffusion in a stationary medium; diffusion in a moving medium; low and high mass transfer theories; simultaneous heat and mass transfer; condensation, evaporation, and boiling; transpiration cooling; species boundary layers; engineering and design of heat and mass exchangers; current refrigerants and environmental regulations.

ME 424.title: Introduction to Gas Dynamics
ME 424.subject: ME
ME 424.description: One-dimensional compressible flow involving change of area, friction, heat transfer. Normal and oblique shocks. Prandtl-Meyer flow. Application to nozzles, diffusers, airfoils.

ME 425.title: Thermal Management of Electronic Systems
ME 425.subject: ME
ME 425.description: To introduce concepts in the thermal management of electronics, and to develop sound technical tools to approach modern electronic packaging and cooling applications.

ME 426.title: Scaling Methods in Engineering
ME 426.subject: ME
ME 426.description: Scaling methods and optimization under global constraints; multi-scale optimal design of mechanical, thermal, and natural systems; effectiveness of heat, fluid, and convective trees; theoretical design optimization of manmade and natural power systems; analysis of time dependent structures.

ME 433.title: Failures in Materials
ME 433.subject: ME
ME 433.description: Analysis of component failures due to imperfections, fatigue, brittle fracture, wear, corrosion, bending, impact, and overload. Fracture mechanics. Case studies.

ME 434.title: Materials Selection for Design
ME 434.subject: ME
ME 434.description: Methodology for the selection of materials for mechanical applications to prevent mechanical failure and environmental degradation. Design considerations associated with the use of metals, ceramics, polymers, and composites.

ME 435.title: Experimental Methods in Materials Research
ME 435.subject: ME
ME 435.description: Common experimental techniques in materials testing and research: x-ray diffraction, optical and electron microscopy, thermal and mechanical properties, electrochemical methods—theory and hands-on experience.

ME 436.title: Corrosion Engineering
ME 436.subject: ME
ME 436.description: Basics of corrosion processes and emphasis on corrosion control. Thermodynamics and kinetics of corrosion, metal alloys and their behavior, corrosion control techniques (cathodic protection, anodic protection, coatings, and inhibitors).

ME 446.title: Advanced Materials Manufacturing
ME 446.subject: ME
ME 446.description: Introduction to anisotropic materials, advanced manufacturing techniques for composite and intelligent materials, joining of composites, thin film processing and stereolithography, computer aided manufacturing and rapid prototyping, manufacturing process optimization, open-ended manufacturing projects.

ME 447.title: Introduction to Nanotechnology
ME 447.subject: ME
ME 447.description: Tools and techniques of micro- and nanotechnology in design, modeling, simulations, analysis, fabrication, testing and characterization; nano-materials, nano-structures, nano-composites, nano-coating, nano-optics, nano-electronics and nano-biotechnology.

ME 448.title: Nanosystem and Microsystem Design
ME 448.subject: ME
ME 448.description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale. Microfabrication/nanofabrication, fabrication process design, electrostatistic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, measurements. Course work will focus on process and system design.

ME 451.title: Feedback-Control Systems
ME 451.subject: ME
ME 451.description: Analysis/ design of feedback systems. Compensator design via root locus and Bode analysis. Routh/Nyquist stability. State space representation and introduction to MIMO formulation. Controllability/observability. Application to physical dynamic systems such as industrial robots.

ME 452.title: Robotics
ME 452.subject: ME
ME 452.description: Principles and design methods for autonomous systems.

ME 453.title: Energy Conversion Systems
ME 453.subject: ME
ME 453.description: Energy conversion and its impact on the environment. Conventional, hydroelectric, nuclear fission and fusion, solar, wind, ocean, geothermal, and biomass power; energy storage, transmission and conservation.

ME 455.title: Nuclear Power Engineering
ME 455.subject: ME
ME 455.description: Nuclear reactor principles. Reactor heat transfer, heat generation and removal. Design and analysis of reactor power systems and plants.

ME 471.title: Experimental Stress Analysis
ME 471.subject: ME
ME 471.description: (1-3 hr Lab) Techniques of experimental stress analysis: strain and deflection measurement of beams and shafts, strain to stress conversion, principal and maximum shearing stresses, failure in biaxial stress states, stress concentrations, residual stresses, buckling, creep, electrical resistance strain gages, brittle coatings, photoelastic methods, transducers.

ME 473.title: Mechanical Vibrations
ME 473.subject: ME
ME 473.description: Response of machines and systems to transient and periodic excitation. Vibration isolation and transmissibility. Modal analysis of multi-degree-of-freedom systems. Applications to design.

ME 474.title: Fundamentals of Acoustics
ME 474.subject: ME
ME 474.description: Plane and spherical acoustic waves. Transmission, reflection, radiation, and absorption. Near and far fields, radiation patterns. Applications to noise control. Instruments.

ME 480.title: Thermofluid Measurements and Design
ME 480.subject: ME
ME 480.description: Measurement techniques in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, and heat transfer. Hands-on experience with instrumentation. Open-ended design of thermofluid systems. Contemporary engineering ethics issues. Final report and presentation are required.

ME 481.title: Design Project I
ME 481.subject: ME
ME 481.description: (2 1-hr Lec, 2 2-hr Lab) Engineering ethics, engineering design methodology, design process, project planning, decision making, materials selection, economic analysis, quality control, finite element analysis, initiation of an open-ended design project.

ME 482.title: Design Project II
ME 482.subject: ME
ME 482.description: Continuation of design project initiated in ME 481. Extension of conceptual design to final design and a prototype. Analysis, materials and part selection, synthesis of working systems. Computer-aided design and finite element modeling. Manufacturing specifications, shop drawings, and a final report are required.

ME 491.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 491.subject: ME
ME 491.description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

ME 492.title: Special Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 492.subject: ME
ME 492.description: Specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, systems, or design.

ME 499.title: Project
ME 499.subject: ME
ME 499.description: Investigation of advanced problems in mechanical engineering design or development. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.

ME 610.title: Renewable Energy Engineering and Sustainability
ME 610.subject: ME
ME 610.description: Analysis of principles of operation of renewable energy systems, and its interactions with sustainability. Fundamentals of renewable energy production, storage, and distribution.

ME 611.title: Advanced Thermodynamics
ME 611.subject: ME
ME 611.description: Introduction to general principles of classical thermodynamics. Main topics include equilibrium conditions, thermodynamic relations, Legendre transformations, Maxwell relations, stability of thermodynamic systems, phase transitions, and critical phenomena. Graduate students only.

ME 612.title: Introduction to Statistical Thermodynamics
ME 612.subject: ME
ME 612.description: Fundamentals of statistical thermodynamics. Main topics include entropy, Boltzmann law, thermodynamic driving forces, statistical mechanics, chemical equilibria, solutions and mixtures, and applications of statistical thermodynamics in biology, chemistry, physics, and nanoscience.

ME 615.title: Advanced Aerodynamics
ME 615.subject: ME
ME 615.description: Advanced topics in aerodynamics, two- and three-dimensional wing theory, slender-body theory, lifting surface methods, vortex and wave drag, analytical and numerical methods, for computing unsteady aerodynamic behavior and introduction to flightdynamics.

ME 618.title: Boiling and Two-Phase Flow
ME 618.subject: ME
ME 618.description: Two-phase flow pattern and flow pattern maps; two-phase flow models (homogeneous, separate, drift flux, annular); laminar and turbulent film condensations; boiling incipience; pool boiling heat transfer; flow boiling heat transfer; critical heat flux (CHF).

ME 620.title: Biological Fluid Mechanics
ME 620.subject: ME
ME 620.description: Review of Newtonian fluid mechanics. Blood rheology and flow in elastic tubes. Murray’s Law and pulsatile flow propagation. Microcirculation dynamics and biological transport. Aquatic movement and comparative biological examples.

ME 622.title: Convection Heat Transfer
ME 622.subject: ME
ME 622.description: Heat transfer in laminar and turbulent boundary layers. Analogy between heat, momentum, mass transfer.

ME 624.title: Microfluidics and Nanofluidics
ME 624.subject: ME
ME 624.description: Introduction to fundamental understanding of fluid mechanics and transport phenomena at micro-nanoscale; electrokinetics; chemical separation; colloids and emulsions; biophysics; micro-nanofabrication.

ME 625.title: Numerical Methods in Fluid Mechanics and Heat Transfer
ME 625.subject: ME
ME 625.description: Integration of ordinary differential equations. Finite difference solutions of partial differential equations with applications to conduction and convection. Introduction to finite element methods.

ME 626.title: Viscous Flows
ME 626.subject: ME
ME 626.description: Formulation and properties of the Navier-Stokes equations; exact solutions; creeping flows; lubrication theory; laminar boundary layers; laminar stability, and transition to turbulence; turbulent boundary layers.

ME 630.title: Rheology
ME 630.subject: ME
ME 630.description: Vector and tensor operations. Constutive equations. Generalized Newtonian fluids and linear viscoelastic fluids. Rheometry and experiments. Flow of suspensions. Advanced topics and rheology of polymers, food products, biomaterials and asphalt, laboratories.

ME 635.title: Corrosion Theory
ME 635.subject: ME
ME 635.description: Application of electrochemical theory and materials science to corrosion and oxidation reactions. Effect of environment, especially marine. Cathodic protection, coatings, inhibitors, treatment of water systems.

ME 636.title: Fundamentals of Electrochemistry
ME 636.subject: ME
ME 636.description: Thermodynamics of cells, electrode kinetics, mass transfer by migration and diffusion, microelectrode techniques, forced convection, impedance, doublelayer structure, and absorbed intermediates in electrode processes.

ME 645.title: Clinically Driven Design and Development
ME 645.subject: ME
ME 645.description: Exploration of simple, cost-effective alternatives in medicine through different stages of concept generation, design analysis, and prototype validation and investigation of their commercialization potential. Graduate students only.

ME 646.title: Mechanics and Design Composites
ME 646.subject: ME
ME 646.description: Introduction to composites; anisotropic elasticity and laminate theory; hygrothermal effects; composite beams, columns, rods, plates, and shells; energy method; failure theories; joining of composites, computer-aided design in composites.

ME 647.title: Nanoscience and Nanotechnology
ME 647.subject: ME
ME 647.description: Science and applications of nanotechnology. Synthesis of nanostructures; nanoscale structure characterization by electron microscopy and Raman spectroscopy; electrical, thermal, and mechanical properties of nanostructures; fabrication of nanodevices; energy, environmental, and biological applications of nanomaterials.

ME 648.title: Nanosystems
ME 648.subject: ME
ME 648.description: Fabrication, design, and analysis of physical systems, sensors, and actuators at the nanoscale and microscale, including electrostatic and electromagnetic interactions, signal transduction, and measurements. Course work will focus on literature review and integration of current research. Graduate students only. (Spring only

ME 650.title: Surface Phenomena
ME 650.subject: ME
ME 650.description: Fundamental and modern concepts of colloid and surface science. Main topics include surface thermodynamics, capillarity and wetting phenomena, surface forces, surfactants, and particles.

ME 651.title: Automatic Control
ME 651.subject: ME
ME 651.description: Linear optimal feedback control, discrete time optimal control, fundamentals of adaptive control, application to motion and force control of robot arms and manipulators.

ME 660.title: Introduction to Fuel Cell Technology
ME 660.subject: ME
ME 660.description: Working principles of all major fuel cell types; fundamentals of proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells; state-of-the-art theoretical models and diagnostic technologies for PEM fuel cells.

ME 671.title: Continuum Mechanics
ME 671.subject: ME
ME 671.description: Cartesian tensors in mechanics, coordinate transformations, analysis of stress and strain, principal values, invariants, equilibrium and compatibility equations, constitutive relations, field equations. Problems in elasticity.

ME 672.title: Finite Element Analysis
ME 672.subject: ME
ME 672.description: Introduction to finite element analysis and design in mechanical engineering. Applications to machine design, vibrations, elasticity, heat transfer.

ME 678.title: Advanced Dynamics
ME 678.subject: ME
ME 678.description: Lecture on rigidbody dynamics. Topics include: dynamical systems; motion representation and constraints; Newtonian mechanics; Lagrangian mechanics; Hamilton’s principle; stability analysis; introduction to multibody dynamics.

ME 680.title: High Growth Entrepreneurship
ME 680.subject: ME
ME 680.description: An interdisciplinary (JD-MBA) course examining legal, business, and technology issues related to building high growth companies. Student teams develop company feasibility reports and skills necessary to advise or build high growth businesses.

ME 691.title: Seminar
ME 691.subject: ME
ME 691.description: Current problems in all branches of mechanical engineering. All graduate students are required to attend; registrants are expected to present talks.

ME 696.title: Advanced Topics in Mechanical Engineering
ME 696.subject: ME
ME 696.description: Highly specialized topics in thermosciences, mechanics, materials, system, or design.

ME 699.title: Directed Reading or Research
ME 699.subject: ME
ME 699.description: Directed study on subject of mutual interest to student and a staff member. Student must find faculty sponsor before registering.

ME 700.title: Thesis Research
ME 700.subject: ME
ME 700.description: Thesis for degree of MS in mechanical engineering.
ME 700.prereq_raw: admission to candidacy and consent of thesis advisor

ME 799.title: Directed Instruction
ME 799.subject: ME
ME 799.description: Student assists in undergraduate classroom and/or project instruction under the direction and close supervision of faculty member.
ME 799.prereq_raw: admission to PhD candidacy or consent

ME 800.title: Dissertation Research
ME 800.subject: ME
ME 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in mechanical engineering

prereq_tree.text: candidacy for PhD in mechanical engineering

HWST 107.title: Hawai‘i: Center of the Pacific
HWST 107.subject: HWST
HWST 107.description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawai‘i and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

HWST 107A.title: Hawai‘i: Center of the Pacific
HWST 107A.subject: HWST
HWST 107A.description: An introduction to the unique aspects of the native point of view in Hawai‘i and in the larger Pacific with regards to origins, language, religion, land, art, history, and modern issues.

HWST 207.title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupua‘a
HWST 207.subject: HWST
HWST 207.description: Examination of the ahupua‘a system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the malama ‘aina track designed to build critical writing skills.

HWST 220.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Visual Culture Studio
HWST 220.subject: HWST
HWST 220.description: Introduction to a variety of material (fiber, bone, wood, and stone) and skills in the media used in the Hawaiian culture. Research and explore basic techniques within the media with emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses, and conservation.

HWST 222.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana No‘eau Ma‘awe
HWST 222.subject: HWST
HWST 222.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to a variety of fibers used in the Hawaiian culture. Emphasis on cultivation, preparation, uses and conservation of the fibers. Areas explored are kapa, plaiting, netting and twining.

HWST 224.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
HWST 224.subject: HWST
HWST 224.description: Research and express personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through Hawaiian visual culture. Introduction to painting and drawing media and exploration of various materials and techniques as applied to individual student styles.

HWST 225.title: Introduction to Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
HWST 225.subject: HWST
HWST 225.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Introduction to Native Hawaiian perspective and world view in images used in print and the basic material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery through the indigenous eyes.

HWST 234.title: Introduction to the Literature of Native Hawaiians and Other Indigenous People Written in English
HWST 234.subject: HWST
HWST 234.description: Surveys literature of Native Hawaiians and other Indigenous Peoples, especially to focus on the situational impetus from which these texts were created.

HWST 270.title: Hawaiian Mythology
HWST 270.subject: HWST
HWST 270.description: Survey of gods, ‘aumâkua, kupua, mythical heroes, heroines, and their kinolau as the basis of traditional Hawaiian metaphor.

HWST 271.title: Papahulilani Hawaiian Astronomy I
HWST 271.subject: HWST
HWST 271.description: Introduction to Hawaiian ancestral understandings of the movements of the sun, moon and stars, and their use in ordering the Hawaiian year in planting, fishing, and ceremony.
HWST 271.prereq_raw: (107 and 270) with a minimum grade of B

HWST 281.title: Ho‘okele I: Hawaiian Astronomy
HWST 281.subject: HWST
HWST 281.description: Introduction to Hawaiian views of astronomy and the stars used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators. Introduction and comparison to various Pacific island non-instrument navigation systems and star names. Restricted to majors.

HWST 282.title: Ho‘okele II: Hawaiian Navigation
HWST 282.subject: HWST
HWST 282.description: Hawaiian and other Oceanic canoe design, navigation, Pacific weather, sailing dynamics for canoes, and sail planning strategies used by Polynesian Voyaging Society navigators for long voyages.

HWST 282L.title: Ho‘okele II Laboratory
HWST 282L.subject: HWST
HWST 282L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands on experience on voyaging skills and sailing canoes to accompany 282.

HWST 285.title: La‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Herbs
HWST 285.subject: HWST
HWST 285.description: Presentation of Hawaiian medicinal herbs including basic philosophy, identification, utilization, and preparation of such herbs for human ailments.

HWST 301.title: Perspectives in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 301.subject: HWST
HWST 301.description: Interdisciplinary lectures and discussions examining traditional and contemporary experiences in Hawaiian society and setting; resources, methods, and techniques.

HWST 307.title: Malama ‘Aina Resource Management Visual Technologies
HWST 307.subject: HWST
HWST 307.description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

HWST 320.title: Advanced Art Media
HWST 320.subject: HWST
HWST 320.description: Examine and explore advance techniques within the media and the customary and contemporary uses of a variety of material and skills used in traditional Hawaiian everyday life.

HWST 322.title: Advanced Hawaiian Fiber Arts Studio-Hana No‘eau Ma‘awe
HWST 322.subject: HWST
HWST 322.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Examine the customary and contemporary use of fiber materials and the skills used in Hawaiian culture. Research and explore advanced techniques within the media used in traditional Hawai‘i.

HWST 324.title: Advanced Hawaiian Painting and Drawing Studio
HWST 324.subject: HWST
HWST 324.description: Advanced research and expression of personal relationship to specific Hawaiian paradigms through visual culture and language. Students will further their definitions, analysis skills, research, and understandings through painting and drawing media.

HWST 325.title: Advanced Hawaiian Printmaking Studio
HWST 325.subject: HWST
HWST 325.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Advanced Native Hawaiian perspective in imagery in print and the material, technical, and conceptual aspects of hand printed imagery. Lecture-lab with studio work time.

HWST 327.title: Mele Hula o Pelehonuamea
HWST 327.subject: HWST
HWST 327.description: Performance based course exploring Kanaka Maoli identity and world view through ancestral knowledge as presented in the Pele and Hi‘iaka epic and preserved in the hula tradition.

HWST 330.title: Native Hawaiian Traditions in Literature
HWST 330.subject: HWST
HWST 330.description: Discusses theoretical frameworks, main features, and cultural contexts of Hawaiian literature.

HWST 341.title: Hawaiian Genealogies
HWST 341.subject: HWST
HWST 341.description: Survey of major Hawaiian chiefly lineages from the four main islands: Hawai‘i, Maui, O‘ahu and Kaua‘i. Political history from the Kumulipo to Western contact.

HWST 342.title: Chiefs of Post-Contact Hawai‘i
HWST 342.subject: HWST
HWST 342.description: Survey of Hawaiian chiefs from 1778 to the present, including genealogy, political function, and historical impact.

HWST 343.title: Myths of Hawaiian History
HWST 343.subject: HWST
HWST 343.description: Thematic exploration of some common myths of Hawaiian history, including infanticide, slavery, feudalism, constant warfare, human sacrifice, and a limited pre-contact population, to determine the role of myth making in perceptions of Hawaiian history. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 351.title: Mahi‘ai Kalo I: Taro Cultivation
HWST 351.subject: HWST
HWST 351.description: Historical, cultural and philosophical foundations of the cultivation and uses of taro.

HWST 352.title: Mahi‘ai Kalo II: Advanced Taro
HWST 352.subject: HWST
HWST 352.description: In depth-study of taro cultivation techniques and systems.

HWST 353.title: Malama Loko I‘a
HWST 353.subject: HWST
HWST 353.description: Study of traditional Hawaiian fishpond management with hands-on experience at He‘eia fishpond near Kane‘ohe, merging traditional Native knowledge and ways of seeing with Western science.

HWST 356.title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
HWST 356.subject: HWST
HWST 356.description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 362.title: Pana O‘ahu: Famous Place Names
HWST 362.subject: HWST
HWST 362.description: A survey of the famous place names in each ahupua‘a of O‘ahu, including accounts of mythical heroes, heiau, fishponds, wind, rain names, and their metaphoric value in Hawaiian literature.

HWST 365.title: Pana Paemoku o Kanaloa: The Northwestern Hawaiian Islands
HWST 365.subject: HWST
HWST 365.description: Will look at the use of the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands during pre-contact times, the historical period of the Kingdom of Hawai‘i, after the islands were ceded to the U.S., and the contemporary politics that surround the region today.

HWST 372.title: Oli Makawalu: Makawalu Methodology in Hawaiian Protocol Chants
HWST 372.subject: HWST
HWST 372.description: Introduces the use of Makawalu Methodology to analyze kaona in Hawaiian protocol chants, which influences the oral production of such chants.
HWST 372.prereq_raw: 270 (or concurrent) and HAW 201 (or concurrent), or consent

HWST 385.title: La‘au Lapa‘au: Ho‘i Ka Mana i Loko
HWST 385.subject: HWST
HWST 385.description: Advanced study and preparation of Hawaiian medicinal herb combinations.

HWST 390.title: Issues in Modern Hawai‘i
HWST 390.subject: HWST
HWST 390.description: Cultural and political aspects of the current Hawaiian movement; historical colonization; conflicts over tourism, the military, and agriculture; forms of native self-determination. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 396.title: Native Hawaiian Rights and Practices
HWST 396.subject: HWST
HWST 396.description: Students will strengthen their cultural, political, and legal foundations by: (1) reviewing Hawai‘i’s historical traditions and customs, (2) learning legal analysis techniques, and (3) applying those techniques to issues that govern native Hawaiian “rights” today. Sophomore or higher standing.

HWST 421.title: Visiting Artist Seminar
HWST 421.subject: HWST
HWST 421.description: (2 cr. Lec, 2 cr. Lab) Explore indigenous concepts through the media of a visiting indigenous master artist by looking at traditional media in indigenous cultures, and the possibilities for contemporary expression in other media.
HWST 421.prereq_raw: 107, one course in 220 level (222, 224, 225), one course in 320 level (322, 324, 325); or consent. (Once a year)

HWST 440.title: Mâhele Land Awards
HWST 440.subject: HWST
HWST 440.description: Practical guide to the researching of land awards and change in title for a single ahupua‘a, 1848 to present. Focus on field trips.

HWST 441.title: Ceded Lands: Focus on Crown and Government Lands (1848 to Present)
HWST 441.subject: HWST
HWST 441.description: Inventorying “Ceded Lands” in Hawai‘i with emphasis on historical, legal, and cultural changes from the Kingdom through statehood.

HWST 442.title: Introduction to Indigenous Research Methods
HWST 442.subject: HWST
HWST 442.description: Survey course introduces students to a range of methods by beginning with a critical analysis of dominant research methodologies from the perspective of Indigenous scholars. Junior/senior standing only.

HWST 445.title: Hawaiian Institutions
HWST 445.subject: HWST
HWST 445.description: Comprehensive analysis of institutions like Bishop Estate/Kamehameha Schools, OHA, Lili‘uokalani Trust, Department of Hawaiian Home Lands and The Queen’s Hospital.

HWST 451.title: Wehe Ka ‘Aina: Cultivating a Sovereign Land Base
HWST 451.subject: HWST
HWST 451.description: A Malama ‘Aina and Kukulu ‘Aupuni course that identifies modern options in land access for reestablishing or resuming Hawaiian traditional and customary practices relating to food sovereignty and self-sustainability. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 455.title: Ola I Ka Wai; Water and Sovereignty in Hawai‘i
HWST 455.subject: HWST
HWST 455.description: Focus on Hawaiian relationships with Ka Wai Ola a Kane (water), traditional and contemporary water management practices, as well as contemporary resource management issues and native Hawaiian community advocacy for water.

HWST 456.title: Kia‘i Kanaloa–Guarding Our Ocean Resources
HWST 456.subject: HWST
HWST 456.description: Students will actively monitor and practice coastal and ocean stewardship in support of local communities and practitioners while also exploring how the Hawaiian worldview can plan a role in aloha ‘âina conservation movements. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 457.title: ‘Aina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
HWST 457.subject: HWST
HWST 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

HWST 458.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
HWST 458.subject: HWST
HWST 458.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.

HWST 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
HWST 459.subject: HWST
HWST 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

HWST 460.title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
HWST 460.subject: HWST
HWST 460.description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.

HWST 461.title: Hawai‘i & Indigenous Economies
HWST 461.subject: HWST
HWST 461.description: Students will map out indigenous economies by articulating cultural similarity and diversity between academic experience and professional experiences.

HWST 467.title: Malama ‘Aina Field Methods Course
HWST 467.subject: HWST
HWST 467.description: Intensive field methods program to research Mâlama ‘Âina strategies. Introduces students to a variety of field techniques in doing land research and integrating it with historical documents. Travel cost covered by student. Junior standing or higher.

HWST 470.title: ‘Ike Akua Papaku Makawalu: Ancestral Understanding of Elements
HWST 470.subject: HWST
HWST 470.description: Uses Dr. Pualani Kanahele’s Papaku Makawalu methodology to analyze akua as elements and as a paradigm for understanding ancestral knowledge. Senior standing or higher.

HWST 478.title: Mele Au Hou: Music and Native Identity
HWST 478.subject: HWST
HWST 478.description: Presents Hawaiian music as it has been an avenue for native social, cultural and political expression in traditional and contemporary society.

HWST 485.title: Mahi La‘au Lapa‘au: Hawaiian Medicinal Horticulture
HWST 485.subject: HWST
HWST 485.description: The science of planting and harvesting Hawaiian medicinal plants and exploring production and marketing strategies.

HWST 487.title: Hawaiian Aquatic Medicine
HWST 487.subject: HWST
HWST 487.description: Identification, extraction and preparation of complexes of aquatic herbs to formulate a healing combination to contribute to maintaining overall health.

HWST 490.title: Senior Seminar in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 490.subject: HWST
HWST 490.description: Critical examination of existing research; individual or team development, execution, and evaluation of selected projects.
HWST 490.prereq_raw: senior major in Hawaiian studies or consent

HWST 491.title: Senior Capstone Project in Hawaiian Studies
HWST 491.subject: HWST
HWST 491.description: Capstone seminar designed to provide a culminating academic experience through in-depth examination, analysis, articulation, and projects relevant to a HWST area of concentration. Senior standing only.
HWST 491.prereq_raw: 341, 342, 343 or 390 or 490 (or concurrent) and [207/SUST 217 or 281 or 285 or 351] and [222 or 224 or 225 or 372 or 478 (or concurrent)]

HWST 493.title: Hawaiian Political Speech: Ha‘i ‘Olelo Ku‘e
HWST 493.subject: HWST
HWST 493.description: Senior seminar in short, extemporaneous speeches in persuasive, passionate and dynamic styles of Native Hawaiian orators.
HWST 493.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341, 342, or HAW 202; or consent. (Once a year)

HWST 494.title: Modern Pacific Women’s Poetry
HWST 494.subject: HWST
HWST 494.description: Critical examination of modern indigenous women’s poetry from the Pacific Islands. Thematic concentration on land, family, sexual and national oppression.

HWST 495.title: Kumu Kanawai: Western Law and Hawai‘i
HWST 495.subject: HWST
HWST 495.description: The rise of Western law in Hawai‘i, its contribution to nation building and colonialism.

HWST 496.title: Kanawai II: Practical Application of Rights
HWST 496.subject: HWST
HWST 496.description: Historical analysis of land use, race and self-determination; introduced to legal case briefing, analysis of legal precedent, practical impacts of rules and regulations and the sociopolitical factors that influence law and law enforcement.

HWST 601.title: Indigenous Research Methodologies
HWST 601.subject: HWST
HWST 601.description: Reading seminar for developing a Native Hawaiian epistemology from sources in comparative indigenous thought.
HWST 601.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

HWST 602.title: Hawaiian Archival Research
HWST 602.subject: HWST
HWST 602.description: Research seminar aimed at familiarizing students with the rich historical primary sources existent in various archives in Honolulu.
HWST 602.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

HWST 603.title: Review of Hawaiian Literature
HWST 603.subject: HWST
HWST 603.description: Seminar in review of Hawaiian literature to understand the significance of secondary sources in Hawaiian subjects. This makes up part of the Hawaiian Studies graduate core.
HWST 603.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

HWST 604.title: Writing a Hawaiian Thesis
HWST 604.subject: HWST
HWST 604.description: Seminar to help fashion student’s research and thesis proposal. To be taken by all HWST MA students as they begin designing their capstone project. Course will be team-taught by HWST faculty.

HWST 620.title: ‘Ike Pono-Visual/Cultural Interpretations
HWST 620.subject: HWST
HWST 620.description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that examines (from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint) colonial imaging; collecting and site of contestation; resilience and resistance; and re-righting.
HWST 620.prereq_raw: 107, and one course from 220-225, and one course from 320-325; or consent

HWST 621.title: ‘Ike Maka-Visual/Cultural Knowledge
HWST 621.subject: HWST
HWST 621.description: Graduate seminar and visual studio that carefully examines and develops critical consciousness–from a Kanaka Maoli viewpoint–visual hegemony, rhetorical tropes; and representation–imag(in)ing and reimag(in)-ing.

HWST 631.title: Pono Science: Ethical Implications of Science in Hawai‘i
HWST 631.subject: HWST
HWST 631.description: Support student dialogue on the foundations of pono science. Through discussions and structured guidance, students will explore Hawaiian ethics, implications of research, and decolonizing methodology. Graduate students only.

HWST 640.title: Mo‘olelo ‘Oiwi: Historical Perspectives
HWST 640.subject: HWST
HWST 640.description: Research seminar for developing interpretations of the past from Native Hawaiian and foreign world views with particular emphasis on understanding the meaning of culturally-based knowledge systems.

HWST 650.title: Hawaiian Geography and Resource Management
HWST 650.subject: HWST
HWST 650.description: Seminar in geography of Hawai‘i from a Native Hawaiian perspective that will enable the researcher to define and develop resource management methods consistent with Native Hawaiian understandings and traditions.
HWST 650.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent). (Once a year)

HWST 651.title: ‘Aina Waiwai: Water, Food Sovereignty, and Ancestral Abundance
HWST 651.subject: HWST
HWST 651.description: Topical graduate seminar focuses on indigenous perspectives on water, food sovereignty, Hawaiian terrestrial and marine food production systems, and ancestral abundance. Seminar perspective to change each term.

HWST 652.title: Kanawai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
HWST 652.subject: HWST
HWST 652.description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall)

HWST 670.title: Kumu Kahiki: Comparative Hawaiian and Tahitian Cosmogonies
HWST 670.subject: HWST
HWST 670.description: Seminar comparing Gods/myths from Ancient Tahiti by Teiura Henry (600 pages) with the six volumes of Hawaiian historians Kamakau and Malo.

HWST 671.title: Kumu Kahiki: Pacific Life Narratives in Mixed Media and Literature
HWST 671.subject: HWST
HWST 671.description: Research seminar in relevant literary traditions, histories of interaction, colonization, and literary politics in the Pacific region through the examination of life narratives in mixed media and literature.

HWST 675.title: Huaka‘i Huli Heiau Hawai‘inuiakea: Study Abroad on Polynesian Temples
HWST 675.subject: HWST
HWST 675.description: Comparative study of Hawaiian/Polynesian temple design taught over a 3-week period in Hawai‘i and Polynesia. Travel costs to be paid by student.
HWST 675.prereq_raw: 670 (with a minimum grade of B) and HAW 302 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

HWST 690.title: Kukulu Aupuni: Envisioning the Nation
HWST 690.subject: HWST
HWST 690.description: A research seminar designed to provide an overview of community activism and Native Hawaiian empowerment in Hawai‘i in contexts that range from local to international, and to provide a foundation for further study and professional growth.
HWST 690.prereq_raw: 107, 270, 341 (or concurrent), 342 (or concurrent), and one of the following: 343 (or concurrent) or 390 (or concurrent) or 490 (or concurrent); or consent

HWST 691.title: Kukulu Aupuni: Sovereign Hawaiian State, Domestic Kingdom Law, Governance and Politics
HWST 691.subject: HWST
HWST 691.description: Research seminar on the subject of domestic law, governance, and politics of the Hawaiian Kingdom and the historical relevance of this to the contemporary case for independent, sovereign state continuity under public international law. (Alt. years)

HWST 700.title: Thesis Research
HWST 700.subject: HWST
HWST 700.description: Research for master’s thesis. (F) Full-time. S/U for (F) only.

HAW 100.title: Language in Hawai‘i: A Microcosm of Global Language Issues
HAW 100.subject: HAW
HAW 100.description: Survival kit for life in Hawai‘i: Introduction to Hawaiian and language related issues enhancing communicative experience in Hawai‘i. Examination of social, cultural, political, and linguistic cross-cultural interaction locally and globally. Taught in English/Hawai‘i Creole English.

HAW 101.title: Elementary Hawaiian
HAW 101.subject: HAW
HAW 101.description: Listening, speaking, reading, writing. Meets five hours weekly; daily lab work.

HAW 105.title: Intensive Elementary Hawaiian
HAW 105.subject: HAW
HAW 105.description: Content of 101 and 102 covered in one semester. Meets two hours daily, Monday–Friday, plus lab work.

HAW 200.title: I Ka ‘Olelo No Ke Ola
HAW 200.subject: HAW
HAW 200.description: Accelerated lecture/lab to bridge fluent speakers mainly from Kula Kaiapuni into Kawaihuelani’s system of Hawaiian that reflects a Hawaiian worldview, including HAW 101-201 content, grammar, writing, and spelling conventions. Students matriculate into HAW 202.

HAW 201.title: Intermediate Hawaiian
HAW 201.subject: HAW
HAW 201.description: Continuation of 102. Meets five hours weekly; reading of traditional texts; daily lab work.

HAW 206.title: Intensive Intermediate Hawaiian
HAW 206.subject: HAW
HAW 206.description: Content of 201 and 202 covered in one semester. Meets two hours daily, plus lab work.

HAW 261.title: Hawaiian Literature in Translation
HAW 261.subject: HAW
HAW 261.description: Survey of Hawaiian literature, including prose narration and poetry with reference to Polynesian and Western themes and forms.

HAW 284.title: Papa Mele I (Mele in the Hawaiian Language Classroom)
HAW 284.subject: HAW
HAW 284.description: The incorporation of mele and the performance thereof for the enhancement of second language acquisition in Hawaiian.

HAW 301.title: Third-Level Hawaiian
HAW 301.subject: HAW
HAW 301.description: Continuation of 202. Conducted in Hawaiian. Advanced conversation and reading.

HAW 321.title: Hawaiian Conversation
HAW 321.subject: HAW
HAW 321.description: Systematic practice on various topics for control of spoken Hawaiian.

HAW 331.title: Hawaiian Composition
HAW 331.subject: HAW
HAW 331.description: Intensive work in the grammatical, semantic, and pragmatic dimensions of composition writing in Hawaiian.

HAW 332.title: Listening Comprehension and Transcription
HAW 332.subject: HAW
HAW 332.description: Development of listening comprehension through transcription and discussion of tape recordings.

HAW 345.title: Ulu ka Hoi
HAW 345.subject: HAW
HAW 345.description: Lecture offering focused study and creation of Hawaiian language newspapers with a concentration on the characteristics of writing in this genre. Students will produce a monthly newsletter in Hawaiian.

HAW 373.title: Ka Mo‘omeheu Hawai‘i
HAW 373.subject: HAW
HAW 373.description: A survey course on the study of traditional Hawaiian culture including origins, the socioeconomic system, land tenure, religion, values, and the arts. The course will be taught in Hawaiian.

HAW 383.title: Hana ‘Oe a Kani Pono-Hawaiian Radio Broadcasting
HAW 383.subject: HAW
HAW 383.description: Combined lecture/lab involving students in the planning and production of a weekly Hawaiian language radio broadcast. Includes research, writing, and voicing of mele and their stories on live radio.
HAW 383.prereq_raw: 302 or 384 (or concurrent with consent), or consent

children.text: ( or concurrent with consent ) , or consent

HAW 384.title: Ka Haku Mele
HAW 384.subject: HAW
HAW 384.description: Composers and Their Compositions. Provides a venue which will allow students to analyze, dissect and discuss mele (song, poetry and chant), paying close attention to the style of composition by identifying reoccurring nuances found in mele composed by the same as well as various authors.
HAW 384.prereq_raw: completion of 202 or consent. (Once a year)

HAW 401.title: Fourth-Level Hawaiian
HAW 401.subject: HAW
HAW 401.description: Advanced reading, writing, and discussion in Hawaiian. Transcribing and translating Hawaiian language tapes. Translating English into Hawaiian, and Hawaiian into English.

HAW 425.title: Mo‘olelo Hawai‘i
HAW 425.subject: HAW
HAW 425.description: Survey of the major works by Hawaiian scholars writing about the history and culture of Hawai‘i including David Malo, Kamakau, Kepelino, and John Papa Î‘i.

HAW 426.title: Ka‘ao Hawai‘i
HAW 426.subject: HAW
HAW 426.description: Survey of the core literature written by Hawaiian scholars, including both historical and mythological epics and folk tales.

HAW 427.title: I Le‘a Ka Hula I Ka Ho‘opa‘a (Mo‘olelo, Ka‘ao, Mele and Hula)
HAW 427.subject: HAW
HAW 427.description: The incorporation of mele and hula performance with mo‘olelo and ka‘ao.

HAW 428.title: Ka Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i–Political Thought in Hawaiian
HAW 428.subject: HAW
HAW 428.description: Intensive study of Hawaiian political thought in writing and speech.

HAW 429.title: Ka Ho‘ike Honua
HAW 429.subject: HAW
HAW 429.description: Study of Hawaiian land tenure practices through readings and discussions of audiotapes, written primary sources, maps, wind names, rain names, ‘olelo no‘eau (wise sayings), and mele (poetry). Readings are drawn from 19th and 20th century Hawaiian newspapers and other primary sources.

HAW 430.title: Ma Ka Hana Ka ‘Ike
HAW 430.subject: HAW
HAW 430.description: Study of traditional Hawaiian language and cultural practices through hands-on applications and lectures.

HAW 431.title: Haku Mo‘olelo–Creative Writing in Hawaiian
HAW 431.subject: HAW
HAW 431.description: Study and composition of written works in various creative genres of Hawaiian storytelling, with a focus on the adaptation and maintenance of a Hawaiian voice and worldview in writing.

HAW 433.title: I Pa‘a Ke Kahua
HAW 433.subject: HAW
HAW 433.description: An experiential approach to the acquisition of vocabulary, which will allow students to broaden and deepen their knowledge of language and the range of domains to perpetuate Hawaiian as a living language.

HAW 434.title: E Pu Pa‘akai Kakou: A Study of Traditional Hawaiian and Contemporary Food Culture
HAW 434.subject: HAW
HAW 434.description: A study of traditional Hawaiian and contemporary food culture through hands-on applications and lectures.

HAW 445.title: Na Politika ma ka Nuhou Hawai‘i– Politics in Hawaiian Language Media
HAW 445.subject: HAW
HAW 445.description: Study of Hawaiian news media with emphasis on political content. Includes field trips to various archives.

HAW 452.title: Structure of Hawaiian
HAW 452.subject: HAW
HAW 452.description: Descriptive linguistic analysis. Intensive exercises in advanced grammar.

HAW 453.title: ‘Olelo Ni‘ihau I
HAW 453.subject: HAW
HAW 453.description: Basic study of ‘Olelo Ni‘ihau. Speaking and listening comprehension will be developed through listening to audio recordings, watching video recordings, and participating in faceto-face conversations with Ni‘ihau native speakers.

HAW 454.title: History of the Hawaiian Language
HAW 454.subject: HAW
HAW 454.description: Development from proto-Polynesian. Phonology, morphology, and grammar; history of research.

HAW 463.title: Language for the Classroom
HAW 463.subject: HAW
HAW 463.description: Examination of language needs in various classroom settings and introduction to new vocabulary in school content areas.

HAW 466.title: Kuleana Kula Kaiapuni
HAW 466.subject: HAW
HAW 466.description: Examination of the political struggles of the Kula Kaiapuni (Hawaiian Immersion Program)–past and present. Special attention given to federal and state governments, Department of Education, and internal political struggles.

HAW 470.title: Ho‘omohala Ha‘awina Kaiapuni Curriculum Development
HAW 470.subject: HAW
HAW 470.description: Examination of curricular issues of indigenous language programs; weekly participation in an immersion classroom; development of materials.

HAW 483.title: Papa Mele Wahi Pana
HAW 483.subject: HAW
HAW 483.description: Will provide students with the opportunity to learn mele, mainly poetry and song, composed specifically for a certain area of Hawai‘i.

HAW 484.title: Hawaiian Poetry
HAW 484.subject: HAW
HAW 484.description: Historical survey and analysis of poetry found in traditional chants, folk songs, modern poetry written in Hawaiian. Interpreting and composing Hawaiian poetry.

HAW 485.title: Haku Hanakeaka–Hawaiian Language Playwriting
HAW 485.subject: HAW
HAW 485.description: The creation and authoring of Hawaiian language play scripts based on traditional motifs.

HAW 486.title: Kahua Hanakeaka (Hawaiian Medium Stage Production)
HAW 486.subject: HAW
HAW 486.description: From design to performance, students mount an original production based on traditional motifs.

HAW 488.title: ‘Olelo No‘eau
HAW 488.subject: HAW
HAW 488.description: Survey and analysis of traditional proverbs and their kaona or symbolic meanings.

HAW 490.title: Ka Makau‘olelo A‘o Kula Kaiapuni Hawai‘i
HAW 490.subject: HAW
HAW 490.description: Assess the linguistic competence of prospective Hawaiian language immersion teachers to assure that all teachers entering the state DOE Hawaiian Immersion Program meet the requirements of the program with respect to Hawaiian language proficiency.

HAW 499.title: Directed Studies
HAW 499.subject: HAW
HAW 499.description: Study of Hawaiian language through vernacular readings in various academic fields.

HAW 601.title: Kakau Mo‘olelo
HAW 601.subject: HAW
HAW 601.description: Analyzes various genres of written Hawaiian literature.

HAW 602.title: Kaka‘olelo Oratory
HAW 602.subject: HAW
HAW 602.description: A survey of oral performance styles to build increased oral skills.

HAW 604.title: Haku Palapala Noi Laeo‘o/Writing a Hawaiian Master’s Proposal
HAW 604.subject: HAW
HAW 604.description: Seminar to select and develop students’ research topic, proposal, and organizational plan for Plan A or B completion. Majors are encouraged not to take this course in their first semester of the program. (Once a year)

HAW 605.title: Ka Hana Noi‘i (Research Methods)
HAW 605.subject: HAW
HAW 605.description: Research methodology course utilizing active research in the major repositories of Hawaiian language materials and Hawaiian-related knowledge.

HAW 612.title: Na Mana‘o Politika Hawai‘i (Hawaiian Political Thought)
HAW 612.subject: HAW
HAW 612.description: Study of Hawaiian political thought in writing from ca. 1825 to the present, with emphasis on theory and research methods.

HAW 615.title: Kuana‘ike
HAW 615.subject: HAW
HAW 615.description: The examination of Hawaiian ways of speaking, as contrasted with English focusing on those features that are uniquely Hawaiian and can be said to constitute a Hawaiian worldview. Section 1 taught in Hawaiian; Section 2 taught in English.

HAW 625.title: Mo‘olelo Hawai‘i
HAW 625.subject: HAW
HAW 625.description: Intensive study, research, and analysis of Hawaiian history.

HAW 643.title: Ke A‘o ‘Olelo Hou ‘Ana (Teaching Hawaiian As a Second Language)
HAW 643.subject: HAW
HAW 643.description: Survey of existing texts and teaching resources; analysis of student clientele and needs; review of pedagogical approaches for heritage and non-heritage learners; syllabus and materials development; practicum.

HAW 652.title: Pilina ‘Olelo
HAW 652.subject: HAW
HAW 652.description: In-depth examination and research into the grammar of Hawaiian including discussion of theories of language and incorporation of meta-language.

HAW 653.title: ‘Olelo Ni‘ihau
HAW 653.subject: HAW
HAW 653.description: Intensive, advanced study and analysis of traditional Hawaiian Ni‘ihau dialect through face-to-face conversations with Ni‘ihau native speakers, listening to audio recordings and watching video recordings of Ni‘ihau native speakers.
HAW 653.prereq_raw: (402 and 453) with a minimum grade of B- or consent

HAW 684.title: Noi‘i Mele
HAW 684.subject: HAW
HAW 684.description: Intensive study focusing on original compositions of Hawaiian poetry and song.

HAW 695.title: Papahana Laeo‘o
HAW 695.subject: HAW
HAW 695.description: Research for Plan B project/non-thesis. May include but not limited to internship with cultural practitioner.

HAW 699.title: Directed Research
HAW 699.subject: HAW
HAW 699.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and graduate chair

HAW 700.title: Noi‘i Pepa Laeo‘o (Thesis)
HAW 700.subject: HAW
HAW 700.description: Research for master’s thesis. Satisfactory/Unsatisfactory only.

HSSW 477.title: Southeast Asian Cultures in Health/ Social Welfare
HSSW 477.subject: HSSW
HSSW 477.description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in Southeast and South Asian region.

HSSW 478.title: Pacific Cultures in Health/Social Welfare
HSSW 478.subject: HSSW
HSSW 478.description: The study of cultures and their implications in the health and social welfare context for a number of countries in the Pacific region.

CIS 701.title: Communication/Information Theories of Society
CIS 701.subject: CIS
CIS 701.description: A critical review of major theoretical and empirical traditions in communication and information sciences. Focus on European, American, Third World, and applied research.

CIS 702.title: Communication/Information Technologies
CIS 702.subject: CIS
CIS 702.description: Technological concepts underlying data communications; information processing and computers; communication channels and networks, information storage and retrieval, and computer hardware and software.

CIS 703.title: Communication/Information Research Methods
CIS 703.subject: CIS
CIS 703.description: Current research methodologies in decision sciences, computer science, library science, and communication. Emphasis on methodologies suitable for interdisciplinary analysis.

CIS 704.title: Special Topics in Communication and Information Sciences
CIS 704.subject: CIS
CIS 704.description: Seminar reflecting research interests of faculty and current interdisciplinary topics in communication and information sciences. Graduate students only.

CIS 705.title: Data Science Foundations
CIS 705.subject: CIS
CIS 705.description: All aspects of data science: the methodology and processes; ethics and regulatory issues; programming tools; data acquisition, cleaning, analysis and mining; visualization, publication, curation, and preservation; applications in various fields. Graduate students only.

CIS 720.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar in Communication and Information Sciences
CIS 720.subject: CIS
CIS 720.description: Exploration of relationships between disciplines in social sciences, science and technology, and humanities. Faculty and student presentations.

CIS 799.title: Directed Reading and/or Research
CIS 799.subject: CIS
CIS 799.description: Individualized program of directed reading and/or research outside the scope of regularly titled courses.
CIS 799.prereq_raw: consent. Plan must include goals and rationale

children.text: Plan must include goals and rationale

GHPS 680.title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
GHPS 680.subject: GHPS
GHPS 680.description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners.

GHPS 690.title: Global Health Challenges
GHPS 690.subject: GHPS
GHPS 690.description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change. (Once a year)

GHPS 719.title: Comparative Family and Gender
GHPS 719.subject: GHPS
GHPS 719.description: Discusses the major perspectives on family and gender relations and examines related empirical research. Emphasis is on the cross-cultural comparisons across the U.S. and Asia in the context of globalizing economies and cultures. (Alt. years)

ANAT 599.title: Independent Study in Anatomy
ANAT 599.subject: ANAT
ANAT 599.description: Elective course for advanced medical students. (B) human gross anatomy; (C) histology; (D) research in anatomy and developmental biology.

ANAT 603.title: Lower Extremity, Thorax, and Abdomen
ANAT 603.subject: ANAT
ANAT 603.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the lower extremity, thorax, and abdomen. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

ANAT 604.title: Upper Extremity, Head, Neck, and Spine
ANAT 604.subject: ANAT
ANAT 604.description: Human gross anatomy dissection of the upper extremity, head, neck, and spine. Emphasis is placed on muscles, function, innervation, and vascular supply. Enrolled in DRB or KRS graduate programs (including Biomed Sci-Anat/ RepoBiol & Phys majors) only or consent.

ANAT 607.title: Human Embryology
ANAT 607.subject: ANAT
ANAT 607.description: Systematic study of human development, including implantation, placentation, basics of development of each organ system with reference to pertinent congenital anomalies and their surgical repair.

ANAT 612.title: Seminar in Anatomy Teaching
ANAT 612.subject: ANAT
ANAT 612.description: Effective teaching methods, organization of courses in anatomical sciences, development and evaluation of exams, experience in teaching with audiovisual/ computer aids. Open to graduate students in physiology or KRS.

BIOC 241.title: Fundamentals of Biochemistry
BIOC 241.subject: BIOC
BIOC 241.description: Biological chemistry stressing integration of concepts of general, inorganic, and biochemistry and application to life chemistry.
BIOC 241.prereq_raw: beginning algebra and high school science

BIOC 341.title: Elements of Biochemistry
BIOC 341.subject: BIOC
BIOC 341.description: Biochemical principles and concepts as applied to living systems, including sufficient organic chemistry to understand these principles.

BIOC 441.title: Basic Biochemistry
BIOC 441.subject: BIOC
BIOC 441.description: Principles of biochemistry, applicable to medicine and real-life situations, involving metabolism of carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, nucleic acids, and vitamins. Taught by biomedical researchers. Evaluated based on exams, quizzes, homework, and group presentation.

BIOC 499.title: Directed Research and Reading
BIOC 499.subject: BIOC
BIOC 499.description: Independent research or selected reading of current literature in the area of biochemistry and biophysics.

BIOC 545.title: Topics in Biochemistry
BIOC 545.subject: BIOC
BIOC 545.description: Fourth-year elective in which medical students take an in-depth study of selected topics in biochemistry.

BIOC 595.title: Highlights of Organ-System Biochemistry
BIOC 595.subject: BIOC
BIOC 595.description: Provides highly interactive, small group discussions on concepts of biochemistry important to the various organ systems; such as cardiac, respiratory, hematology, gastrointestinal, endocrine, musculoskeletal and neurological systems, and relevant to clinical medicine.

BIOM 499.title: Directed Research and Reading
BIOM 499.subject: BIOM
BIOM 499.description: To provide elective courses for undergraduates in the biomedical sciences specialties. Repeatable unlimited times

BIOM 601.title: Global Health and Medicine: Emerging Problems and Impact
BIOM 601.subject: BIOM
BIOM 601.description: Analysis of emerging problems and impact in countries on a multidimensional perspective.
BIOM 601.restrictions_raw: BIOM, NURS, PH, SPA majors only.

BIOM 640.title: Introduction to Clinical Research
BIOM 640.subject: BIOM
BIOM 640.description: Instruction in developing clinical research questions and creating a concise protocol that includes a literature review, study design, subject recruitment and sampling, instruments, other measures and bioinformatics, sample size, consent form, budget and timetable.

BIOM 641.title: Legal and Regulatory Issues and Bioethics
BIOM 641.subject: BIOM
BIOM 641.description: Ethical dilemmas in clinical research are identified and resolved in cases, research on human subjects regulation are discussed. Research misconduct is defined. Ethical considerations in protocol developed in the Designing Clinical Research course are resolved.

BIOM 644.title: Translational Research Methods
BIOM 644.subject: BIOM
BIOM 644.description: Lectures focus on translational research methods through selected genetic and acquired diseases including cancer, neurodevelopmental, inflammatoryimmune, and metabolic conditions with insight into analyses of DNA, RNA, genomics-proteomics, cell and animal models, and advanced imaging.

BIOM 645.title: Clinical Protocol Development
BIOM 645.subject: BIOM
BIOM 645.description: Provides training in proposal development. Governance structures of funding agencies; funding opportunities and decisions; review processes; NIH application and processes; reading RFAs; compliance issues; cultural sensitivity; and types of questions using databases are addressed.

BIOM 646.title: Clinical Research Seminar
BIOM 646.subject: BIOM
BIOM 646.description: Provides overview of research related to health and health disparities in Hawai‘i. Seminar topics include ethnic disparities in health research, Native Hawaiian health, childhood research initiatives, fitness and obesity, social and cultural factors and ethics.

BIOM 647.title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research I
BIOM 647.subject: BIOM
BIOM 647.description: Introductory lecture-seminar on the conduct of multidisciplinary research from a culturally competent perspective. Enrolled in MS or PhD in Biomedical Sciences program only. (Alt. years)

BIOM 648.title: Foundations of Biomedical Ethics
BIOM 648.subject: BIOM
BIOM 648.description: Explores the foundations of biomedical ethics via small group seminars and discussion, presentations. Enrolled in MS or PhD in Biomedical Sciences program only. (Alt. years)

BIOM 649.title: Advanced Ethics in Biomedical Research II
BIOM 649.subject: BIOM
BIOM 649.description: Develop biomedical ethics through case studies to incite discussions on topics such as gene therapy, gene enhancement, genetic counseling, informed consent, health care professional/patient and investigator/student participant communication, advanced directives and living wills, clinical research in developing countries, clinical research in ethnic minority and socio-economically disadvantaged populations, and non-discrimination in health care and research settings.

BIOM 650.title: Cultural Competence in Biomedical Research II
BIOM 650.subject: BIOM
BIOM 650.description: Explore topics in cultural competence in greater depth, encouraging trainees to address issues from a unified yet flexible conceptual framework. Involves building knowledge, skills and action plans to address a range of learning styles and to appreciate and benefit from diversity.

BIOM 651.title: PhD Team Building Seminar
BIOM 651.subject: BIOM
BIOM 651.description: Seminar focuses on teaching participants to work independently and collaborate in order to accomplish specific results. Students will be exposed to group dynamics, communication, healthy competition, conflict resolution, and innovative means of crossing boundaries between departments, organizations, industries and disciplines.

BIOM 654.title: Medical Genetics
BIOM 654.subject: BIOM
BIOM 654.description: Focus on heritable disorders, genetic mechanisms, patterns of inheritance, phenotype-genotype correlations, genetic/ environmental factors, clinical diagnoses, genomic and precision medicine.

BIOM 660.title: Mentored Research Practicum
BIOM 660.subject: BIOM
BIOM 660.description: Conduct research under the direction of a mentor. Participants will be responsible for submission of a proposal, acquisition of IRB approval, and conduct of the project. BIOM students only.

BIOM 667.title: Advanced Biostatistics for Clinical Research
BIOM 667.subject: BIOM
BIOM 667.description: Current methods for analyzing longitudinal and clustered, clinical data through lectures, discussions, and a group analysis. Topic areas include multi-level, multi-state, multi-process, and structural equation models.

BIOM 699.title: Directed Research
BIOM 699.subject: BIOM
BIOM 699.description: Students may register on approval of department.

BIOM 701.title: Disasters and Pandemics: Medical and PH Management and Risk Communication
BIOM 701.subject: BIOM
BIOM 701.description: Assess impact on health in disasters and diseases. Enhances research skills related to management and communication.
BIOM 701.restrictions_raw: BIOM, PH, NURS, and SPA majors only.

BIOM 800.title: Dissertation Research
BIOM 800.subject: BIOM
BIOM 800.description: Research for doctoral dissertation. CR/ NC only.

PHYL 103.title: Human Physiology and Anatomy
PHYL 103.subject: PHYL
PHYL 103.description: Introduction to human physiology and anatomy designed to serve the needs of dental hygiene students and others interested in pursuing health-related careers.

PHYL 141.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
PHYL 141.subject: PHYL
PHYL 141.description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

PHYL 141L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
PHYL 141L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 141L.description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

PHYL 142.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology
PHYL 142.subject: PHYL
PHYL 142.prereq_raw: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in 141 or equivalent

children.text: should have an understanding of basic physiology concepts as presented in 141

PHYL 142L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
PHYL 142L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 142L.description: Anatomy, histology, physiology, biochemistry, genetics of human organ systems presented in integrated anatomy-physiology format. Priority to students in nursing.

PHYL 301.title: Advanced Anatomy and Physiology
PHYL 301.subject: PHYL
PHYL 301.description: Integrated presentation of human anatomy and physiology. An optional laboratory (PHYL 301L) is available separately.
PHYL 301.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and BIOL 172, or any PHYL course; and CHEM 161 (or higher) or any BIOC course; or consent

PHYL 301L.title: Human Anatomy and Physiology Lab
PHYL 301L.subject: PHYL
PHYL 301L.description: Laboratory study of human anatomy and physiology by means of models, histology slides, experiments, and demonstrations.

PHYL 401.title: Human Physiology: Organ Systems
PHYL 401.subject: PHYL
PHYL 401.description: Basic function of the major organ systems in man. Covers cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, acid-base, and gastrointestinal physiology.

PHYL 402.title: Human Physiology: Integrative Systems
PHYL 402.subject: PHYL
PHYL 402.description: Senior-level course in integrative systems (central nervous system and endocrinology). Complements 401.
PHYL 402.prereq_raw: 401 and either BIOC 341 or CHEM 152, or consent

PHYL 405.title: Applied Muscle Physiology
PHYL 405.subject: PHYL
PHYL 405.description: Science and technology of strength training. Anatomy, kinesiology, physics, and physiology applied to development of muscular strength and mass.

PHYL 499.title: Directed Reading or Research
PHYL 499.subject: PHYL
PHYL 499.description: Students will learn fundamental concepts and multiple techniques in molecular biology, physiology, and histology for cardiovascular research through the projects in the lab. Junior or senior standing only.

REPR 611.title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
REPR 611.subject: REPR
REPR 611.description: Presentation and discussion of current research topics in biomedical sciences.

REPR 705.title: Special Topics in Reproductive Biology
REPR 705.subject: REPR
REPR 705.description: In-depth discussion of selected areas of reproductive biology, with special emphasis on recent research results and methodologies. May be retaken for credit.

CAAM 401.title: Mindfulness Meditation and Stress Reduction
CAAM 401.subject: CAAM
CAAM 401.description: Practice mindfulness meditation to reduce burnout and live life in the present moment. Learn life skills to handle life better and be more resilient. Respond rather than react to life. No experience necessary.

CAAM 415.title: Clinical Nutrition
CAAM 415.subject: CAAM
