CAAM 415.description: Overview of applied clinical nutrition that includes nutrients, dietary recommendations for healthy populations, and medical nutrition therapies for patients with diet related diseases or conditions. Junior standing and higher.
CAAM 415.prereq_raw: CHEM 151 (or higher) or BIOC 241 (or higher); PHYL 141 or ZOOL 141; highly encouraged: FSHN 185 or any other basic nutrition course

CAAM 445.title: Introduction to Integrative Medicine
CAAM 445.subject: CAAM
CAAM 445.description: Overview of integrative (complementary) medicine covering Traditional Chinese Medicine, Ayurvedic medicine, naturapathy, traditional healing practices, homeopathy, nutrition and diet, herbs and dietary supplements, environmental health, mind-body, energy, spiritual, and positive psychology.

CAAM 595.title: Nutrition for Clinicians
CAAM 595.subject: CAAM
CAAM 595.description: Provides in-depth lectures and case studies reviewing the role of nutritional therapy in health and illness.

CAAM 599.title: Research Topics in Complementary and Alternative Medicine
CAAM 599.subject: CAAM
CAAM 599.description: Research elective for medical students. MD students only.

QHS 601.title: Biomedical Statistics
QHS 601.subject: QHS
QHS 601.description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

QHS 602.title: Biomedical Statistics II
QHS 602.subject: QHS
QHS 602.description: Advanced biomedical statistics principles and tools as well as their applications will be introduced. Topics include: model selection, hierarchical model, repeated measurements, proportional hazard model, classification methods, structural equation modeling and multivariate analysis.
QHS 602.prereq_raw: 601 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

QHS 610.title: Bioinformatics I
QHS 610.subject: QHS
QHS 610.description: Fundamental concepts in bioinformatics with a strong emphasis on hands-on training. Covers topics such as molecular biology, sequence alignment, biological databases, phylogeny, and genomics, including microarray and RNA-seq data analysis.

QHS 611.title: Bioinformatics II
QHS 611.subject: QHS
QHS 611.description: Focus on bioinformatics approaches for functional genomics related to DNA, RNA, and protein. It will provide of virus, bacteria, and human genome and bioinformatics approaches to human disease.
QHS 611.prereq_raw: 610 (or equivalent) (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) ( with a minimum grade of B ) or consent

QHS 620.title: Introduction to Clinical Trials
QHS 620.subject: QHS
QHS 620.description: Introduction to clinical trials. Topics include history, definitions/terminology, adverse events, FDA and government regulatory agencies, ethics; monitoring committees, recruitment, introduction to protocol development, basis designs.

QHS 621.title: Design and Analysis of Clinical Trials
QHS 621.subject: QHS
QHS 621.description: Covers basic and advanced statistical methods utilized in clinical trials design, conduct, and data analysis. Topics cover statistician’s role in drug development and DSMB, statistical theory in phases I-IV clinical trial designs and analysis.

QHS 650.title: Secondary Data Analysis
QHS 650.subject: QHS
QHS 650.description: Will allow students who are new to using secondary data to become comfortable with accessing the data, forming hypotheses, and designing study proposals. Will introduce examples with basic and advanced techniques.

QHS 651.title: Secondary Data Analysis Practicum
QHS 651.subject: QHS
QHS 651.description: Introduces students to issues in working with complex data sets and adds the hands-on experience needed to conduct individual research using secondary databases.
QHS 651.prereq_raw: (601 (or equivalent) and 650) with a minimum grade of B, which can be taken concurrently

children.text: ( or equivalent) and 650 ) with a minimum grade of B , which can be taken concurrently

QHS 670.title: Special Topics in Quantitative Health Sciences
QHS 670.subject: QHS
QHS 670.description: Special topics in quantitative health sciences. Reflects special research interest of QHS faculty or guest lecturers.

QHS 675.title: Biostatistical Consulting
QHS 675.subject: QHS
QHS 675.description: Investigate the roles and responsibilities of the biostatistician as both consultant and collaborator with biomedical researchers, guide students in enhancing problem-solving and communication skills, and provide opportunity to observe real-life biostatistical consultations.

QHS 676.title: Biostatistical Consulting Practicum
QHS 676.subject: QHS
QHS 676.description: Under the supervision of biostatistics faculty members, students will have the opportunity to provide statistical consultations to biomedical researchers and gain hands-on experience conducting biostatistical analysis in solving real-life analytic problems.

QHS 699.title: Directed Research
QHS 699.subject: QHS
QHS 699.description: Directed research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through the process of conducting a research study.

CMB 351.title: Genetics, Evolution and Society
CMB 351.subject: CMB
CMB 351.description: The role of genetics in evolution, medicine, behavior, plant and animal breeding and technology; its impact on today’s society.
CMB 351.prereq_raw: one semester of biological science at college level or consent. Not a BIOL major elective

children.text: one semester of biological science at college level

CMB 411.title: Human Genetics
CMB 411.subject: CMB
CMB 411.description: Principles of human genetics. Designed for pre-medical or pre-dental students or others who require a course with emphasis on human genetics.

CMB 499.title: Genetical Problems
CMB 499.subject: CMB
CMB 499.description: Directed reading and research in genetics.

CMB 515.title: Unit V Topics in Genetics
CMB 515.subject: CMB
CMB 515.description: First-year elective course in which medical students may take an in-depth study of genetics.

CMB 526.title: Bioethics
CMB 526.subject: CMB
CMB 526.description: Prepare medical students to identify and resolve ethical dilemmas in medical career and biomedical research, and to maintain integrity and professionalism in accordance with relevant ethical principles, policies, and laws.

CMB 599.title: Research Topics in Cell Molecular Biology
CMB 599.subject: CMB

CMB 604.title: Evolutionary Genetics
CMB 604.subject: CMB
CMB 604.description: Genetic changes involved in the processes of adaptation and in species formation.

children.text: Recommended: population and / or quantitative genetics

CMB 606.title: Introduction to Neurosciences
CMB 606.subject: CMB
CMB 606.description: An interdisciplinary overview of the central nervous system, drawn from current knowledge and research on vertebrate and invertebrate neurobiology.

CMB 610.title: Public Health Biology
CMB 610.subject: CMB
CMB 610.description: Writing intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year)

CMB 611.title: Seminar in Biomedical Sciences
CMB 611.subject: CMB
CMB 611.description: Presentation and discussion of research topics in biomedical science.

CMB 621.title: Cell Molecular Biology I
CMB 621.subject: CMB
CMB 621.description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
CMB 621.prereq_raw: BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; and BIOC 441, BIOL 408, and graduate standing; or consent. Recommended: CHEM 351

CMB 622.title: Cell Molecular Biology II
CMB 622.subject: CMB
CMB 622.description: Molecular approaches to cell structure and function emphasizing cells in multi-cellular plants and animals.
CMB 622.prereq_raw: 621, BIOC 441, and BIOL 408; and either BIOL 402 or MBBE 402; or consent

CMB 625.title: Advanced Topics in Genetics
CMB 625.subject: CMB
CMB 625.description: Advanced treatment of frontiers in genetics.
CMB 625.prereq_raw: graduate standing in genetics or consent

CMB 626.title: Ethics in Biomedical Research
CMB 626.subject: CMB
CMB 626.description: Topics include responsible data management, recording, reporting, misconduct and scientific fraud, conflicts of interest, critical use of animals and human issues and subjects in research, genetic screening, stem cell and gene therapy and patenting.

CMB 631.title: Research Rotations
CMB 631.subject: CMB
CMB 631.description: Individualized research project in three laboratories of CMB faculty with a written report on each project. Faculty laboratories will be selected by consultation with student’s graduate committee and individual faculty.

CMB 640.title: Neuropharmacology
CMB 640.subject: CMB
CMB 640.description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
CMB 640.prereq_raw: 606, or consent from the course director

CMB 641.title: Introductory Biostatistics for the Bench Biologist
CMB 641.subject: CMB
CMB 641.description: Lecture and example-based introduction to the critical biostatistics skills commonly required of the bench life scientist. Technical literacy and basic practical application are the goals. Problem sets will be scored.

CMB 642.title: Introductory Bioinformatics for the Bench Biologist
CMB 642.subject: CMB
CMB 642.description: Modern biomolecular and genomic concepts are explored through brief guided hands-on web-based bioinformatic projects using public domain resources. Understanding key concepts and algorithms, technical literacy, and operational confidence are goals. Programming skill development is student-optional.

CMB 650.title: Population Genetics
CMB 650.subject: CMB
CMB 650.description: Mathematical, observational, experimental results on effects of mutation, selection, and systems of mating on distribution of genes. Analysis of non-experimental populations.

CMB 652.title: Literature Analysis and Scientific Writing
CMB 652.subject: CMB
CMB 652.description: Aims to improve the skills of graduate students in Biomedical Sciences in literature search, analysis, and management, as well as in scientific writing and other forms of scientific communication. Graduate students only or consent.

CMB 669.title: Essentials in Grant Writing
CMB 669.subject: CMB
CMB 669.description: (1 2-hr Lec) Presentation and discussion of hypothesis-driven research and grant writing. Topics include the process of proposal, submission, and review. Course work includes writing, critiquing, and revising a proposal. Graduate students only. CR/ NC only.

CMB 671.title: Techniques in Genetics
CMB 671.subject: CMB
CMB 671.description: Laboratory training in procedures used in diagnosis of genetic diseases, cytogenetics, immunogenetics, and dermatoglyphics.
CMB 671.prereq_raw: graduate standing in genetics or consent

CMB 705.title: Special Topics in Neurosciences
CMB 705.subject: CMB
CMB 705.description: Advanced topics in neuroscience, from basic neurobiology to clinical neurology and psychiatry. Emphasis on current investigations at the cellular or molecular level.

CSD 431.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
CSD 431.subject: CSD
CSD 431.description: Will overview anatomy and physiology of speech and hearing. Students gain exposure to structures and functions of respiration, phonation, resonance, articulation, deglutition, and hearing systems required for normal communication and swallowing.

CSD 432.title: Phonetics
CSD 432.subject: CSD
CSD 432.description: Introduction to the fundamentals of phonetic and phonological development. International Phonetic Alphabet Transcription of English speech sounds; phonological developments and models; cultural variations; analysis interpretation and other considerations related to speech sound development and production.

CSD 433.title: Speech and Language Development
CSD 433.subject: CSD
CSD 433.description: Will develop an understanding of children’s acquisition of speech, language, and normal communication development from birth through adolescence.

CSD 434.title: Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Speech and Hearing
CSD 434.subject: CSD
CSD 434.description: Provides an understanding of the fundamental processes underlying the production and perception of speech. Students gain an understanding of the physical and psychological aspects of sound and their measurement.

CSD 435.title: Introduction to Clinical Methods in Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 435.subject: CSD
CSD 435.description: Provides observation and discussion of the clinical management of individuals with communication disorders, and practical experience related to clinical procedures and requirements.

CSD 436.title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 436.subject: CSD
CSD 436.description: Information and theoretical foundations serve as an introduction to the field of communication disorders. Will provide an overview of the normal processes and disorders of speech, language, hearing, and swallowing.

CSD 437.title: Introduction to Audiometry and Auditory Disorders
CSD 437.subject: CSD
CSD 437.description: Covers anatomy and physiology of the auditory system, acoustic, basic knowledge of auditory disorders and testing procedures, and introduction to rehabilitative audiology.

CSD 438.title: Basic Statistics for Health-Related Professionals
CSD 438.subject: CSD
CSD 438.description: Provides students from behavioral sciences and health-related professions with an overview of normal distribution, central tendency, variability, sampling, hypothesis testing, frequency distribution, correlation, regression, and t-test.

CSD 600.title: Research Methods
CSD 600.subject: CSD
CSD 600.description: Research methods applicable to the field of speech-language pathology and audiology; analysis and reporting of data. Required of all CSD graduate students.
CSD 600.prereq_raw: previous coursework in inferential statistics and consent

CSD 601.title: Neuroscience in Communication Sciences and Disorders
CSD 601.subject: CSD
CSD 601.description: Explores the neuroanatomy and neurophysiology of the human nervous system as it relates to communication and swallowing and how neurological pathologies lead to behavioral deficits in those areas.

CSD 604.title: Seminar in Motor Speech Disorders
CSD 604.subject: CSD
CSD 604.description: Provides in-depth examination of various motor speech disorders, including apraxia of speech and dysarthria. Emphasis is on assessment/treatment of these diagnoses. Review of current treatment literature, anatomy/physiology, practical exercises in treatment planning.

CSD 610.title: Disorders of Phonology and Articulation
CSD 610.subject: CSD
CSD 610.description: Study of the etiology, assessment, and remediation of disorders and articulation.

CSD 612.title: Child Language Disorders
CSD 612.subject: CSD
CSD 612.description: Study of the etiology, behavioral characteristics and treatment methods for child language disorders. Examination of methods, test, and instruments employed in diagnosis of child language disorders. Includes identification of language deficits and writing intervention goals.

CSD 613.title: Language Development for Children with Hearing Deficiencies
CSD 613.subject: CSD
CSD 613.description: Language acquisition by hard-of-hearing and deaf children; methods of stimulating growth.

CSD 616.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology I
CSD 616.subject: CSD
CSD 616.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

CSD 617.title: Audiology Practicum for SpeechLanguage Pathology
CSD 617.subject: CSD
CSD 617.description: Clinical practice in administering tests, interpreting results; counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

CSD 620.title: Voice Disorders
CSD 620.subject: CSD
CSD 620.description: Contemporary development and theoretical issues in the diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of vocal system disorders in children and adults; current literature and clinical practice issues are addressed.

CSD 622.title: Adult Neurogenic Language and Cognitive-Communication Disorders
CSD 622.subject: CSD
CSD 622.description: Study of acquired adult language and cognitive communication disorders associated with stroke, traumatic brain injury, and dementia. Application of evidence-based procedures and strategies for assessment and intervention, review of current literature, and discussion of professional issues.

CSD 695.title: Research–Speech Pathology
CSD 695.subject: CSD
CSD 695.description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing speech-language pathology.

CSD 696.title: Research–Audiology
CSD 696.subject: CSD
CSD 696.description: Required of all CSD graduate students following the non-thesis (Plan B) program and emphasizing audiology.

CSD 701.title: Amplification: Assessment and Applications
CSD 701.subject: CSD
CSD 701.description: Comprehensive study of amplification. Assessment, fitting, evaluation, electroacoustic evaluation, dispensing. Personal instruments and instructional-educational systems.

CSD 702.title: Disorders of Fluency
CSD 702.subject: CSD
CSD 702.description: Contemporary developments and theoretical issues in diagnosis, evaluation, and treatment of disorders of fluency such as stuttering in both children and adults.

CSD 703.title: Electrophysiologic Audiometry
CSD 703.subject: CSD
CSD 703.description: Study of early, middle, and late auditory evoked potentials with emphasis on the auditory brainstem response.

CSD 709.title: Dysphagia: Disorders of Swallowing
CSD 709.subject: CSD
CSD 709.description: Explores the dynamics of normal and disordered swallowing across the life span with emphasis on the adult population.

CSD 716.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology II
CSD 716.subject: CSD
CSD 716.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedures with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings. Repeatable unlimited times, credit earned for 12 credits only

CSD 717.title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology II
CSD 717.subject: CSD
CSD 717.description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results; counseling individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

CSD 721.title: Seminar in Audiology–Diagnostic Procedures
CSD 721.subject: CSD
CSD 721.description: Study of diagnostic procedures as reflected in current literature.

CSD 723.title: Seminar in Audiology–Rehabilitative Procedures
CSD 723.subject: CSD
CSD 723.description: Procedures and philosophies presented in recent literature dealing with rehabilitative phases of audiology.

CSD 724.title: Advanced Practicum in Speech Pathology III
CSD 724.subject: CSD
CSD 724.description: Clinical practice in diagnostic and therapeutic procedure with various types of speech and language problems in different clinical settings.

CSD 725.title: Advanced Practicum in Audiology III
CSD 725.subject: CSD
CSD 725.description: Clinical practice in administering tests and interpreting results, counseling of individuals with impaired hearing; use of various rehabilitation techniques.

FMCH 531.title: 7-Week Family Medicine Clerkship
FMCH 531.subject: FMCH
FMCH 531.description: Ambulatory-based clerkship in Hawai‘i. Students learn history taking, physical exam skills, and management of family medicine patients. Emphasis on behavioral care, caring for the underserved, sports medicine, preventive care, common acute/chronic ambulatory problems.

FMCH 532.title: Family Medicine and Community Health Longitudinal Clerkship
FMCH 532.subject: FMCH
FMCH 532.description: 5.5-month ambulatory clerkship. Students learn history taking, physical exam skills, and management of family medicine patients. Emphasis on behavioral care, caring for the underserved, sports medicine, preventive care, and common acute/chronic ambulatory problems.
FMCH 532.coreq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses

GERI 541.title: Geriatric and Palliative Care
GERI 541.subject: GERI
GERI 541.description: This four-week rotation provides medical students with an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in outpatient, inpatient, home care and nursing home settings. Students will receive one half-day per week of geriatric medicine didactic seminars and one half-day per week of palliative medicine didactic sessions. The clinical placements will be provided at several teaching sites including Kuakini Medical Center, Queen’s Medical Center, the VA, several nursing homes on O‘ahu, Kaiser Permanente, Hospice Hawai‘i, St. Francis Hospice, Kapiolani Hospital, Straub Hospital, and the Pain & Symptom Management Program at Queen’s Medical Center.

GERI 542.title: Geriatric Medicine Research
GERI 542.subject: GERI
GERI 542.description: Medical students will have the opportunity to complete a research project in the field of epidemiology of aging, and present an abstract at a local meeting. Basic principles of epidemiology and statistics will be taught.

GERI 545.title: Geriatric and Palliative Medicine Elective
GERI 545.subject: GERI
GERI 545.description: Four-week elective provides medical students with an overview of geriatric and palliative medicine in outpatient, inpatient, home care and nursing home settings. Students receive one half-day per week of geriatric medicine didactic seminars and one half-day per week of palliative medicine didactic sessions.

GERI 595.title: Medical Student Training in Aging Program
GERI 595.subject: GERI
GERI 595.description: Introduces medical students to clinical, research, and academic experiences in geriatrics, under the mentorship of faculty members.

MDED 527.title: Evidence-Based Medicine
MDED 527.subject: MDED
MDED 527.description: Critical appraisal track designed to improve the student’s ability to seek and evaluate new medical knowledge.

MDED 528.title: Unit 8 Block Electives
MDED 528.subject: MDED
MDED 528.description: Through lectures, self-assessments and independent study, second-year medical students will consolidate their knowledge of the application of the biological sciences to patient care.

MDED 541.title: Clinical Skills Assessment
MDED 541.subject: MDED
MDED 541.description: Required comprehensive interdepartment multidisciplinary assessment program for fourth-year medical students.
MDED 541.prereq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531 or 532

children.text: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, SURG 531

MDED 551.title: MD 1 Health and Illness
MDED 551.subject: MDED
MDED 551.description: Introduction to concepts of health and disease through lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 1 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 551L.title: MD 1 Health and Illness Tutorials
MDED 551L.subject: MDED
MDED 551L.description: Introductory series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on concepts of health and disease through MD 1 health care problems.

MDED 552.title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary
MDED 552.subject: MDED
MDED 552.description: Concepts focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 2 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 552L.title: MD 2 CV/Pulmonary Tutorials
MDED 552L.subject: MDED
MDED 552L.description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on cardiovascular and pulmonary health care problems.

MDED 553.title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology
MDED 553.subject: MDED
MDED 553.description: Concepts focusing on renal and hematologic systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 3 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 553L.title: MD 3 Renal/Hematology Tutorials
MDED 553L.subject: MDED
MDED 553L.description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on renal and hematology health care problems.

MDED 554.title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine
MDED 554.subject: MDED
MDED 554.description: Concepts focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine systems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 4 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 554L.title: MD 4 GI/Endocrine Tutorials
MDED 554L.subject: MDED
MDED 554L.description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for first-year medical students focusing on gastrointestinal and endocrine health care problems.

MDED 556.title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System and Behavioral Problems
MDED 556.subject: MDED
MDED 556.description: Concepts focusing on the locomotor/neurological systems and behavioral problems through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 6 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 556L.title: MD 6 Locomotor System, Nervous System, and Behavioral Problems
MDED 556L.subject: MDED
MDED 556L.description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on neurological/ locomotor systems and behavioral health care problems.

MDED 557.title: MD 7 The Life Cycle
MDED 557.subject: MDED
MDED 557.description: Concepts focusing on the life cycle through integrated basic science lectures, laboratories, and colloquia intended to broaden the learning from MD 7 health care problems in tutorials.

MDED 557L.title: MD 7 The Life Cycle Tutorials
MDED 557L.subject: MDED
MDED 557L.description: Advanced series of problem-based learning tutorials for second-year medical students focusing on the life cycle health care problems.

MDED 563.title: Third Year Colloquia
MDED 563.subject: MDED
MDED 563.description: A series of lecture-discussions intended to broaden the perspectives of the Unit VI experiences and healthcare problems.

MDED 571.title: Introduction to Clinical Skills
MDED 571.subject: MDED
MDED 571.description: Introductory lectures and laboratories on history taking and physical exam skills.

MDED 572.title: Unit 2 Clinical Skills
MDED 572.subject: MDED
MDED 572.description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 2.

MDED 573.title: Unit 3 Clinical Skills
MDED 573.subject: MDED
MDED 573.description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 3.

MDED 574.title: Unit 4 Clinical Skills
MDED 574.subject: MDED
MDED 574.description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 4.

MDED 576.title: Unit 6 Clinical Skills
MDED 576.subject: MDED
MDED 576.description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 6.

MDED 577.title: Unit 7 Clinical Skills
MDED 577.subject: MDED
MDED 577.description: History and physical exam skills pertinent to the health care problems in Unit 7.

MDED 581.title: Unit 1 Community Health
MDED 581.subject: MDED
MDED 581.description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

MDED 582.title: Unit 2 Community Health
MDED 582.subject: MDED
MDED 582.description: Field experience placing students in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

MDED 583.title: Unit 3 Community Health
MDED 583.subject: MDED
MDED 583.description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

MDED 584.title: Unit 4 Community Health
MDED 584.subject: MDED
MDED 584.description: Field experience placing student in community settings to work with health care professionals as they provide services to patients.

MDED 599.title: Research in Medical Education
MDED 599.subject: MDED
MDED 599.description: An elective for medical students to work on research projects related to improving medical education, student wellness, and community health under the direction of a faculty member in the Office of Medical Education.

MED 531.title: Internal Medicine Clerkship
MED 531.subject: MED
MED 531.description: Required for third-year medical students, 11-week duration. Ambulatory care and hospital-based experience.

MED 532.title: Internal Medicine Longitudinal Clerkship
MED 532.subject: MED
MED 532.description: Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting, and six-week hospital-based experience.
MED 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses. Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting, and six-week hospital-based experience. Repeatable one time. Pre: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses

children.text: concurrent registration in 532 courses. Six-month long clerkship in ambulatory setting,
six-week hospital-based experience. Repeatable one time. Pre: third-year standing

MED 541.title: Advanced Medicine Clerkship
MED 541.subject: MED
MED 541.description: Required 4 weeks duration for fourth-year medical students. Advanced experiences in ambulatory and hospital-based medical care. Proficiency in this course may be established by examination.
MED 541.prereq_raw: fourth-year standing and completion of 531, or consent

MEDT 151.title: Introduction to Medical Technology
MEDT 151.subject: MEDT
MEDT 151.description: Designed to acquaint students to the field of medical technology (clinical laboratory science).

MEDT 251.title: Introduction to Medical Technology II
MEDT 251.subject: MEDT
MEDT 251.description: Basic principles and lab skills in medical technology (medical lab science). Required for second bachelor’s degree students (not MLT credentialed) wishing to major in medical technology. Second bachelor’s degree students only.

MEDT 301.title: The Clinical Laboratory
MEDT 301.subject: MEDT
MEDT 301.description: Theory and clinical application of medical laboratory methods and healthcare professional relationships.

MEDT 302.title: The Clinical Laboratory II
MEDT 302.subject: MEDT
MEDT 302.description: Theory and clinical application of medical technology methods and healthcare professional relationships. Companion course to MEDT 301; and required, for second bachelor’s degree students who were admitted to MEDT major. Second Bachelor’s degree standing or higher.

MEDT 331.title: Clinical Lab Management
MEDT 331.subject: MEDT
MEDT 331.description: Student will become familiar with fundamental administration of a clinical laboratory to include technical, personnel, and financial management areas.

MEDT 451.title: Hematology
MEDT 451.subject: MEDT
MEDT 451.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Fundamental study of blood in normal and pathological states: formation, development, and classification of blood cells.

MEDT 464.title: Immunohematology
MEDT 464.subject: MEDT
MEDT 464.description: Antigen-antibody relationships in human blood, study of blood groups, clinical problems in transfusion.

MEDT 471.title: Clinical Biochemistry I
MEDT 471.subject: MEDT
MEDT 471.description: Biochemical processes in human health and disease states.

MEDT 477.title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses I
MEDT 477.subject: MEDT
MEDT 477.description: Lab experiments illustrating fundamental principles and methods of clinical laboratory analyses.

MEDT 478.title: Clinical Lab Methods and Analyses II
MEDT 478.subject: MEDT

MEDT 481.title: Professional Issues in Medical Lab Science
MEDT 481.subject: MEDT
MEDT 481.description: Discussions about various professional issues through oral presentations and critiquing of peer presentations.

MEDT 495.title: Special Topics in Medical Technology
MEDT 495.subject: MEDT
MEDT 495.description: Acquaints student with role of the medical technologist and overlap of major sciences in clinical situations to help student develop qualities unique to med technology.

MEDT 531.title: Advanced Lab Management Concepts and Contemporary Issues
MEDT 531.subject: MEDT
MEDT 531.description: Concepts in clinical laboratory management and discussion of contemporary issues for graduates and practicing clinical laboratory scientists.

MEDT 551.title: Advanced Clinical Laboratory Hematology and Hemostasis
MEDT 551.subject: MEDT
MEDT 551.description: Advanced-level study of hematology and hemostasis through clinical laboratory cases.

MEDT 581.title: Clinical Microbiology Preceptorship
MEDT 581.subject: MEDT
MEDT 581.description: Clinical training for students with bachelor’s degree in microbiology to be able to qualify as clinical microbiologists in a healthcare setting. Includes specimen procurement, processing, detection and identification, susceptibility testing, and other diagnostic technology.

MEDT 591.title: Clinical Training in Medical Technology
MEDT 591.subject: MEDT
MEDT 591.description: Application of theory and simulated laboratory experiences in immuno-hematology, clinical chemistry, microbiology, parasitology, hematology, coagulation, urinalysis, immunology, to meet stated career entry-level competencies.

MEDT 690.title: Seminar in Medical Technology
MEDT 690.subject: MEDT
MEDT 690.description: Analysis of research and recent literature pertaining to various aspects of medical technology.

NHH 450.title: Applied Health Disparities Research
NHH 450.subject: NHH
NHH 450.description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

NHH 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
NHH 499.subject: NHH
NHH 499.description: Individual reading and/or research. Junior standing or higher.

NHH 501.title: Humanities in Medicine I
NHH 501.subject: NHH
NHH 501.description: Introduction to medical science stressing key historical figures and significant events to exemplify the development of scientific methods. Special emphasis on writing skills, health team concept, and culture and contributions of the Pacific.
NHH 501.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

prereq_tree.text: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

NHH 503.title: Medical Biology I
NHH 503.subject: NHH
NHH 503.description: Foundation in medical sciences, including anatomy, physiology, microbiology, pathology, and pharmacology (focus on respiratory, cardiovascular, and urinary systems); develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Includes lectures, problembased tutorials, and histology and gross anatomy labs.
NHH 503.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

prereq_tree.text: admission to Imi Ho‘ola PostBaccalaureate Program

NHH 505.title: Medical Biochemistry I
NHH 505.subject: NHH
NHH 505.description: Provide background knowledge of chemistry, biochemistry, and molecular biology with emphasis in principles of biochemical processes as well as clinical correlations to medical conditions; develop critical thinking, standardized test taking skills, and problem-solving skills.
NHH 505.prereq_raw: admission to Imi Ho‘ola Post-Baccalaureate Program

prereq_tree.text: admission to Imi Ho‘ola Post-Baccalaureate Program

NHH 513.title: Native Hawaiian Health and Traditional Healing
NHH 513.subject: NHH
NHH 513.description: Introduction to Native Hawaiian health issues and traditional healing practices.

NHH 545.title: Native Hawaiian Health Care
NHH 545.subject: NHH
NHH 545.description: Clinical experience in the Native Hawaiian Health Care System and community health care centers, incorporating both western and traditional Hawaiian medicine. Open to fourth year medical students interested in Native Hawaiian Health Care.

NHH 575.title: Seminar in Issues of Social Justice in Health
NHH 575.subject: NHH
NHH 575.description: Social justice provides an analytical and prescriptive framework to understand health inequities; understand connections between social forces and health outcomes, and the role of the individual student in improving social justice in the health system. Graduate standing only.

NHH 595.title: Clinical Skills Preceptorship in the Lau Ola Clinic of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health
NHH 595.subject: NHH
NHH 595.description: Provides a focused experience in clinical medicine with opportunities to practice the history and physical examination in Lau Ola, the clinical setting of the Department of Native Hawaiian Health.

NHH 650.title: Advanced Applied Health Disparities Research
NHH 650.subject: NHH
NHH 650.description: Instruction on social determinants of health, issues of health equity, and how these issues can be addressed through research. Discussions and activities promote a greater understanding of health disparities research.

NHH 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
NHH 699.subject: NHH
NHH 699.description: Individual reading and/or research. Graduate standing only.

OBGN 532.title: Obstetrics and Gynecology Longitudinal Clerkship
OBGN 532.subject: OBGN
OBGN 532.description: Year-long clerkship in outpatient setting, covering assessment, diagnosis, treatment, and/or management of common gynecologic problems and normal and complicated pregnancies. Emphasis on prevention and health maintenance.
OBGN 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing, and concurrent registration in 532 courses
OBGN 532.coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, PED, PSTY, and SURG 632

PATH 499.title: Directed Research
PATH 499.subject: PATH
PATH 499.description: Pathology of aging, nutrition, alcoholism, and immunology. Open to selected undergraduate students.

PATH 512.title: Unit II Concurrent Elective
PATH 512.subject: PATH
PATH 512.description: Elective course for first-year medical students.

PATH 515.title: Unit V Concurrent Elective
PATH 515.subject: PATH
PATH 515.description: Elective course for second-year medical students.

PATH 525.title: Unit V Block Elective
PATH 525.subject: PATH
PATH 525.description: Required elective for second-year medical students, objectives to be determined by contract. One option is a review of USMLE Part I.

PATH 541.title: Pathology Practicum
PATH 541.subject: PATH
PATH 541.description: Required autopsy experience involving dissection and microscopic examination of tissues and detailed evaluation of disease process.

PATH 595.title: Introduction to Pathology and Laboratory Medicine
PATH 595.subject: PATH
PATH 595.description: Provides an introduction to the practice of pathology and laboratory medicine and the role pathologists and the laboratory play in the diagnosis and management of disease. MD students only.

PATH 599.title: Electives in Pathology
PATH 599.subject: PATH
PATH 599.description: Individualized instruction in clinical and/or anatomic pathology. Third-year elective.

PED 501.title: Pediatric Seminars
PED 501.subject: PED
PED 501.description: Interactive weekly lecture/seminar designed to teach topics in pediatrics and supplemented by small group 2-hour encounters with faculty clinicians in pediatric emergency medicine, inpatient pediatric, and enonatology to gain exposure in pediatric hospital care. Medical students only.

PED 506.title: Introduction to Research Methodology, Biostatistics, and Epidemiology
PED 506.subject: PED
PED 506.description: Interactive seminar series to cover the following topics: data types, descriptive statistics, inferential statistics, selecting a statistical test, data distributions, measures of data spread, statistical test assumptions, standard deviation vs. standard error, etc. Medical students only.

PED 532.title: Pediatrics Longitudinal Clerkship
PED 532.subject: PED
PED 532.description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, covering evaluation, diagnosis, and treatment of childhood diseases. Emphasis on primary prevention, normal growth and development of the neonate to adolescent, and arrangement of pediatric care, including outpatient, inpatient, and emergency room experiences.
PED 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses
PED 532.coreq_raw: MED, OBGN, PED, PSTY, and SURG 532

PSTY 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
PSTY 499.subject: PSTY
PSTY 499.description: Individualized directed readings and/or research in mental health and psychiatry under the supervision of an instructor. Open to non-majors.

PSTY 532.title: Psychiatry Longitudinal Clerkship
PSTY 532.subject: PSTY
PSTY 532.description: Year-long clerkship in ambulatory setting, including knowledge, skills, attitudes for assessment, diagnosis, and management of psychiatric problems in medical practice, inpatient, and emergency room settings. Emphasis on development and application of psychosocial cultural formulations in all areas of psychiatric and medical practice.
PSTY 532.prereq_raw: third-year standing and concurrent registration in 532 courses
PSTY 532.coreq_raw: FMCH, MED, OBGN, PEDS, SURG 532 and SURG 535

PSTY 595.title: Philosophy & Human Suffering
PSTY 595.subject: PSTY
PSTY 595.description: To see how various philosophies and religions have tackled the question, “why is there suffering in the world?” Read short excerpts from “classic” texts and discuss in a welcoming atmosphere and draw own conclusions. Medical students only.

QHS 499.title: Directed Reading/Research
QHS 499.subject: QHS
QHS 499.description: Directed reading/research in quantitative health sciences. Students will work closely with a QHS faculty member or mentor who will guide them through quantitative methodologies and/or the process of conducting a research study.

SURG 531.title: Surgery Clerkship
SURG 531.subject: SURG
SURG 531.description: A clinically based, introductory course in general surgery and elected subspecialties.

SURG 532.title: Surgery Longitudinal Clerkship
SURG 532.subject: SURG
SURG 532.description: A clinically based, year-long, introductory in general surgery and selected subspecialties. Outpatient-conducted one day per week for six months in a community-based, ambulatory care facility. Inpatient-conducted for four weeks in an acute-care hospital facility.

SURG 541.title: Emergency Medical Care
SURG 541.subject: SURG
SURG 541.description: Clinical experiences in management of medical, surgical, and psychiatric problems requiring urgent care.

DRB 601.title: Fertilization and Early Development
DRB 601.subject: DRB
DRB 601.description: Lecture on the basics of vertebrate and invertebrate fertilization and early embryonic development. Open to all graduate students.

DRB 613.title: Seminar in Developmental and Reproductive Biology I
DRB 613.subject: DRB
DRB 613.description: Presentations of current research carried out by developmental and reproductive biology graduate program faculty.

DRB 614.title: Developmental and Reproductive Biology Scientific Investigations
DRB 614.subject: DRB
DRB 614.description: Discussion of current research in developmental and reproductive biology.

DRB 650.title: Stem Cell Biology
DRB 650.subject: DRB
DRB 650.description: Seminar designed to teach graduate students and advanced undergraduate students about current topics relating to stem cell biology, as well as the application of stem cells to modern medicine.

DRB 666.title: Applied Developmental and Reproductive Biology
DRB 666.subject: DRB
DRB 666.description: Combined lecture-lab on current technologies and methods for mammalian reproduction and developmental biology.

DRB 695.title: DRB Research Rotation
DRB 695.subject: DRB
DRB 695.description: Introductory laboratory research experience under the supervision of faculty.

DRB 699.title: Directed Research
DRB 699.subject: DRB
DRB 699.description: Research experience in developmental and reproductive biology.

PHRM 201.title: Introduction to General Pharmacology
PHRM 201.subject: PHRM
PHRM 201.description: Drugs discussed with emphasis on sites and mechanism of action, toxicity, fate, and uses of major therapeutic agents.
PHRM 201.prereq_raw: mammalian physiology and dental hygiene major

PHRM 203.title: General Pharmacology
PHRM 203.subject: PHRM
PHRM 203.description: Similar to 201 but wider in scope of drugs discussed. Intended for undergraduates in the health sciences and related fields.

PHRM 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
PHRM 499.subject: PHRM
PHRM 499.description: Directed reading and research in experimental pharmacology.

PHRM 590.title: Selected Topics in Pharmacology
PHRM 590.subject: PHRM
PHRM 590.description: Elective for medical students in Pharmacology.

PHRM 595.title: Principles of Pharmacology
PHRM 595.subject: PHRM
PHRM 595.description: Pharmacology elective course for medical students. MD students only.

PHRM 599.title: Research in Pharmacology
PHRM 599.subject: PHRM
PHRM 599.description: Pharmacology research elective for medical students.

PHRM 601.title: General Pharmacology
PHRM 601.subject: PHRM
PHRM 601.description: Pharmacodynamics, receptor theory, modeling, clinical trials and the FDA will be covered. Concepts in ADME/T and clinical research are also considered.

PHRM 602.title: Systemic Pharmacology
PHRM 602.subject: PHRM
PHRM 602.description: Provides instruction at an organ systems/functional level covering major organ and functional systems of the human body. Concepts in pharmacological research at the animal, organ system and whole human level will also be considered.

PHRM 640.title: Neuropharmacology
PHRM 640.subject: PHRM
PHRM 640.description: Physiology and pharmacology of central and peripheral nervous systems, focusing on synaptic chemistry and signaling.
PHRM 640.prereq_raw: CMB 606, or consent from the course director

TRMD 441.title: International Health Disparities
TRMD 441.subject: TRMD
TRMD 441.description: Overview of biosciences research related to health and health disparities in a global setting as well as in Hawai‘i. Workshop topics include health research, Native Hawaiian health, global health, and cultural competency. MHIRT cohort only.

TRMD 545.title: Topics in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 545.subject: TRMD
TRMD 545.description: Elective for fourth-year medical students for advanced study of selected topics within the field of tropical medicine and medical microbiology.

TRMD 590.title: Selected Topics in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases
TRMD 590.subject: TRMD
TRMD 590.description: Elective for medical students in Tropical Medicine and Infectious Diseases. Medical students only.

TRMD 601.title: Tropical Medicine Journal Club
TRMD 601.subject: TRMD
TRMD 601.description: Students gain experience in the presentation and discussion of topics of current interest in the fields of tropical medicine and infectious diseases. Graduate students only.

TRMD 602.title: Laboratory Methods in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 602.subject: TRMD
TRMD 602.description: Microbiologic methods and techniques for identification of pathogenic viruses, bacterial, and parasitic organisms including specimen handling, culturing, and laboratory safety. Graduate standing only.

TRMD 603.title: Infectious Disease Microbiology I: Medical Parasitology
TRMD 603.subject: TRMD
TRMD 603.description: Epidemiology, pathogenesis, immunobiology and diagnostic aspects of human parasitic infections; principles of host-pathogen interactions; public health aspects of parasitic infections.

TRMD 604.title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
TRMD 604.subject: TRMD
TRMD 604.description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

TRMD 605.title: Infectious Disease Micro II
TRMD 605.subject: TRMD
TRMD 605.description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

TRMD 606.title: Tropical Medicine Laboratory Rotations
TRMD 606.subject: TRMD
TRMD 606.description: Practical experience in use of equipment and procedures in infectious disease and immunology research; introduction to research in tropical medicine.

TRMD 607.title: Neurovirology
TRMD 607.subject: TRMD
TRMD 607.description: Seminar on neuroinvasive viruses giving basics of viruses causing nervous system diseases and discussing recent advances in the research field of neurovirology.

TRMD 608.title: Infectious Disease Microbiology III
TRMD 608.subject: TRMD
TRMD 608.description: Basic structure, physiology, epidemiology, and genetics of pathogenic bacteria as well as the host response to these organisms. Correlation of these characteristics to disease pathogenesis in humans and animal models.

TRMD 609.title: Advances In Medical Immunology
TRMD 609.subject: TRMD
TRMD 609.description: Presentations/discussions of current literature concerning recent advances in immunology relevant to disease and to disease processes.

TRMD 610.title: Infection and Immunity
TRMD 610.subject: TRMD
TRMD 610.description: Combined lecture/discussion of interactions of pathogens with the innate and acquired immune systems. Topics will include the role of novel receptors in pathogen detection, inflammation in disease pathogenesis, pathogen immune evasion, and neuroimmunology.

TRMD 650.title: Ecological Epidemiology
TRMD 650.subject: TRMD
TRMD 650.description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

TRMD 651.title: Vaccinology
TRMD 651.subject: TRMD
TRMD 651.description: History/evolution of vaccines, current and next generation vaccines, vaccine immunology, adjuvants, vaccine strategies, vaccines for viral, bacterial, and parasitic diseases, vaccine-proof-of-concept and downstream developmental studies; vaccine safety production processes. Graduate students only.
TRMD 651.prereq_raw: (604 and 605) with a minimum grade of B. (Spring only

TRMD 652.title: Advanced Genetics and Evolution of Infectious Diseases
TRMD 652.subject: TRMD
TRMD 652.description: An evolutionary perspective to examine the interactive responses between infectious agents and the immune system. Topics will include natural selection, life history evolution, population genetics of pathogens and hosts, and anti-microbial resistance.

TRMD 653.title: Bioinformatics and Molecular Evolution
TRMD 653.subject: TRMD
TRMD 653.description: Combined lecture/computer lab on bioinformatic tools used in genomics, including sequence assembly, search algorithms, alignment, phylogenetics, and molecular evolution/epidemiology. Focus will be on infectious disease examples. Open to nonmajors.

TRMD 654.title: Advances in HIV/AIDS
TRMD 654.subject: TRMD
TRMD 654.description: History of HIV, basic biology and virology, epidemiology, HIV pathogenesis and immunology, clinical features, and co-morbidities. Treatment and prevention of HIV/ AIDS, including research methods, statistics, cultural competence, genetics, pathophysiology, drug and vaccine development.

TRMD 655.title: Biomedical Statistics
TRMD 655.subject: TRMD
TRMD 655.description: Fundamental biomedical statistics concepts and tools will be introduced, as well as their applications to biomedical data. Students will perform hands-on analysis using statistical software and learn to interpret and present the results.

TRMD 671.title: Advanced Medical Parasitology
TRMD 671.subject: TRMD
TRMD 671.description: Consideration of ultrastructure, physiology, biochemistry, in-vitro cultivation and host-parasite relationship of parasites of medical importance.

TRMD 672.title: Advanced Medical Virology
TRMD 672.subject: TRMD
TRMD 672.description: In-depth study of the major groups of viruses pathogenic for human; virus replication, host range, pathogenesis, immunology, and epidemiology.

TRMD 673.title: Advanced Medical Bacteriology
TRMD 673.subject: TRMD
TRMD 673.description: Role of bacteria in infectious diseases, with emphasis on clinical aspects and identification of etiological agents.

TRMD 675.title: Epidemiology of Tropical Infectious Diseases
TRMD 675.subject: TRMD
TRMD 675.description: Epidemiology of infectious diseases as it relates to tropical medicine. Lecture/seminar format.

TRMD 690.title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
TRMD 690.subject: TRMD
TRMD 690.description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

TRMD 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
TRMD 695.subject: TRMD
TRMD 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

TRMD 699.title: Directed Research
TRMD 699.subject: TRMD
TRMD 699.description: Directed research in medical microbiology (bacteriology, parasitology, virology).

TRMD 700.title: Thesis Research
TRMD 700.subject: TRMD
TRMD 700.description: Research for master’s thesis. Approval of department faculty required.

TRMD 705.title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
TRMD 705.subject: TRMD
TRMD 705.description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health.

TRMD 800.title: Dissertation Research
TRMD 800.subject: TRMD
TRMD 800.description: Research for doctoral thesis. Approval of department faculty is required.

DH 231.title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology
DH 231.subject: DH
DH 231.description: The study of the structure and functions of the head and neck with emphasis on structures in or related to the oral cavity; of tooth morphology.

DH 231L.title: Oral Anatomy and Tooth Morphology Lab
DH 231L.subject: DH
DH 231L.description: (2 3-hr Lab) Application of DH 231 didactic concepts to laboratory activities and practices.
DH 231L.prereq_raw: BIOC 241 and PHYL 103, PHYL 103L; or equivalent

DH 238.title: Basic Dental Hygiene I
DH 238.subject: DH
DH 238.description: Relationship to dentistry, problems, trends, issues; role and functions of dental hygienists in prevention and control of chronic oral diseases; preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including vital signs; team concepts in dentistry.

DH 238L.title: Basic Dental Hygiene I Lab
DH 238L.subject: DH
DH 238L.description: Application of preliminary dental hygiene clinical and support procedures including instrumentation, vital signs, and team concepts in dentistry.

DH 240.title: Basic Dental Hygiene II
DH 240.subject: DH
DH 240.description: Basic dental hygiene theory and skills including competencies in health history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, plaque control and support procedures.

DH 240L.title: Basic Dental Hygiene II Lab/Clinic
DH 240L.subject: DH
DH 240L.description: Laboratory and clinical experiences in basic dental hygiene skills and competencies including history taking, examination, patient care plan, oral prophylaxis, application of caries preventive agents, and clinic procedures.

DH 250.title: General Histology
DH 250.subject: DH
DH 250.description: Cells, tissues, the organs they make up, and their embryologic origin.

DH 251.title: Oral Histology and Embryology
DH 251.subject: DH
DH 251.description: Cells and tissues as they relate to the oral cavity and the embryological development of the head, neck, and related oral structures.

DH 281.title: Dental Radiography
DH 281.subject: DH
DH 281.description: Basic principles of radiation and fundamental information to understand and safely use radiation in dental radiography.

DH 281L.title: Dental Radiography Lab/Clinic
DH 281L.subject: DH
DH 281L.description: (1 3-hr Lab/Clinic) Preparation and evaluation of radiographic survey of patients with varying dentition; methods, and indications of safety considerations in clinical application of roentgen rays.

DH 361.title: Health Education and Promotion
DH 361.subject: DH
DH 361.description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups and the larger public.
DH 361.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

DH 366.title: General Pathology
DH 366.subject: DH
DH 366.description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases an tissue alterations associated with the human body organ systems.

DH 367.title: Oral Pathology
DH 367.subject: DH
DH 367.description: The study of the nature and causes of diseases, the progress and termination or associated alterations of tissue with emphasis on diseases affecting the teeth and the structures of the oral cavity.

DH 369.title: Dental Materials
DH 369.subject: DH
DH 369.description: Science of dental materials and its application to dentistry and dental hygiene.

DH 369L.title: Dental Materials Lab/Clinic
DH 369L.subject: DH
DH 369L.description: Laboratory and clinical application of concepts in the science of dental materials.

DH 370.title: Expanded Functions in Dental Hygiene
DH 370.subject: DH
DH 370.description: Basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

DH 370L.title: Expanded Functions Lab/Clinic
DH 370L.subject: DH
DH 370L.description: (2 1.5-hr Lab/Clinic) Application of basic concepts of expanded functions in dental hygiene.

DH 375.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I
DH 375.subject: DH
DH 375.description: Development of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.

DH 375L.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene I Clinic
DH 375L.subject: DH
DH 375L.description: Clinical instruction and application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing, and evaluating total oral hygiene care of patients; review and critical analysis of current dental periodicals and research.

DH 380.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II
DH 380.subject: DH
DH 380.description: Continued development of dental hygiene concepts, skills, emergency procedures, team approach to dentistry, planning, implementing and evaluating oral hygiene care of patients. Review and analyze dental periodicals and conduct a case study. Emphasis on writing.

DH 380L.title: Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
DH 380L.subject: DH
DH 380L.description: Continuation of 375. Clinical application of dental hygiene concepts and skills; emergency procedures; team approach to dentistry; planning, implementing and evaluating total oral hygiene care to patients.

DH 389.title: Pain Control and Local Anesthesia in Dentistry
DH 389.subject: DH
DH 389.description: Basic concepts of pain control and local anesthesia in dentistry with appropriate emphasis on psychological preparation, pharmacological preparation, and safe and effective administration of anesthesia in the practice of dental hygiene.

DH 390.title: Periodontology I
DH 390.subject: DH
DH 390.description: Normal periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy.

DH 391.title: Periodontology II
DH 391.subject: DH
DH 391.description: Continuation of DH 390. Normal Periodontium, etiology, pathogenesis, clinical manifestations and epidemiology of periodontal diseases, and mode of periodontal therapy.

DH 473.title: Community Health
DH 473.subject: DH
DH 473.description: Introduction and application of the principles of health education and dental public health into practice in schools, community agencies, and private dental offices (inclusive of problem assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation processes); epidemiology and biostatistics.

DH 475.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene I
DH 475.subject: DH
DH 475.description: An in-depth knowledge and clinical application of expanded function in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 475L.title: Advanced Dental Hygiene I Clinic
DH 475L.subject: DH
DH 475L.description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 480.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II
DH 480.subject: DH
DH 480.description: In-depth knowledge development of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modifications in behavior.

DH 480L.title: Advanced Clinical Dental Hygiene II Clinic
DH 480L.subject: DH
DH 480L.description: Application of knowledge of expanded functions in periodontics with emphasis on principles, techniques, procedures in pain-anxiety control, soft tissue curettage, host factors, and modification of behavior.

DH 484.title: Pediatric Growth and Development
DH 484.subject: DH
DH 484.description: Focus on the normal growth and development of children based on current clinical practice guidelines and evidence in pediatric research.

DH 485.title: Advanced Health and Diagnostic Assessment for Pediatric Patients
DH 485.subject: DH
DH 485.description: Focus on advanced health and diagnostic assessment for pediatric patients. Includes behavior management techniques as well as oral habits and subsequent malocclusions and speech difficulties.

DH 486.title: Pharmacological Principles and Clinical Therapeutics in Pediatric Dental Care
DH 486.subject: DH
DH 486.description: Focus on pharmacological principles and clinical therapeutics in pediatric dental care.

DH 487.title: Interprofessional Collaborative Practice Simulation Lab
DH 487.subject: DH
DH 487.description: Focus on interprofessional practice principles and competencies while providing students an opportunity to participate in interprofessional team simulations to address health care issues of children.

DH 488.title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical I
DH 488.subject: DH
DH 488.description: Field experience. Clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

DH 489.title: Management of Pediatric Dental Emergencies
DH 489.subject: DH
DH 489.description: Focus on the management of dental emergencies in children.

DH 490.title: Community-Based Dental Hygiene Care of Vulnerable and Special Needs Children
DH 490.subject: DH
DH 490.description: Emphasizes community-based oral health promotion, dental disease risk reduction and management in children 0-5 years of age with a focus on vulnerable and special needs populations.

DH 491.title: Community-Based Practice Capstone
DH 491.subject: DH
DH 491.description: Provides an opportunity to synthesize, analyze, and develop solutions to an oral health care problem affecting children ages 0-5 years. Requires one credit to be spent in fieldwork to meet course requirements.

DH 492.title: Dental Hygiene Pediatric Training Clinical II
DH 492.subject: DH
DH 492.description: Advanced clinical application and knowledge in the care of pediatric patients 0-5 years of age.

DH 499.title: Directed Reading, Field Work, or Research
DH 499.subject: DH
DH 499.description: Individualized program of directed reading, field work, or research for major under supervision in related areas of dentistry and dental hygiene.

NURS 200.title: Introduction to Professional Nursing I
NURS 200.subject: NURS
NURS 200.description: This first level course focuses on nursing practice and education. Professional responsibilities in the practice of nursing are emphasized.

NURS 201.title: Introduction to Professional Nursing II
NURS 201.subject: NURS
NURS 201.description: This second level course builds on the knowledge and skills gained in the first level and focuses on professional responsibilities in nursing practice and education.

NURS 210.title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan
NURS 210.subject: NURS
NURS 210.description: Focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. It introduces the nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.
NURS 210.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 210L.title: Health Promotion Across the Lifespan Lab
NURS 210L.subject: NURS
NURS 210L.description: Clinical course focuses on a health promotion model of care, assessment, and communication skills. Introduces nurse’s roles, code of ethics, and evidence-based practice.

NURS 211.title: Professionalism in Nursing
NURS 211.subject: NURS
NURS 211.description: Professional responsibilities of nursing practice are examined through the history of nursing, practice and education, legal and ethical issues, contemporary issues, and nursing roles.
NURS 211.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 212.title: Pathophysiology
NURS 212.subject: NURS
NURS 212.description: Focus on pathophysiological concepts that are basic to understanding illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human responses, which serve as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning.
NURS 212.prereq_raw: admission to the School of Nursing and Dental Hygiene, or consent

children.text: admission to the School of Nursing

NURS 213.title: Pharmacology for Nursing
NURS 213.subject: NURS
NURS 213.description: This course will help students to gain knowledge of the mechanism of action, toxicity, adverse reactions, side effects, therapeutic uses, and nursing implications of the major categories of drugs.

NURS 220.title: Health and Illness I
NURS 220.subject: NURS
NURS 220.description: Focuses on nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness.

NURS 220L.title: Health and Illness I Lab
NURS 220L.subject: NURS
NURS 220L.description: Clinical course focuses on using nursing assessment to support identification of risk factors and detection/prevention of complications from illness. Nursing skills are integrated into clinical experiences.

NURS 301.title: Introduction to Evidence Based Practice and Health Promotion
NURS 301.subject: NURS
NURS 301.description: Provides an introduction to the HSNC Competencies and spiraling of concepts and is based on the assumption of student responsibility for learning. Emphasis on writing instruction, and research evidence to support nursing care.

NURS 306.title: Statistics in Nursing Research
NURS 306.subject: NURS
NURS 306.description: Focuses on the basic concepts and applications of statistics as applied to nursing research.

NURS 320.title: Health and Illness II: Family Health
NURS 320.subject: NURS
NURS 320.description: Nursing care and health promotion for maternal-newborn and pediatric clients and families in the acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care.

NURS 320L.title: Health and Illness II: Family Health Lab
NURS 320L.subject: NURS
NURS 320L.description: Nursing care and health promotion for maternal-newborn and pediatric clients and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care.

NURS 321.title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health
NURS 321.subject: NURS
NURS 321.description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute care and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools for providing culturally sensitive, client-centered care. Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 321L.title: Women, Newborn, and Family Health Lab
NURS 321L.subject: NURS
NURS 321L.description: Nursing care and health promotion for women, newborn, and families in acute and community settings. Utilization of family theories and assessment tools when providing culturally sensitive, family-centered care. Emphasis on teaching writing for the profession. Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 322.title: Child and Family Health
NURS 322.subject: NURS
NURS 322.description: Nursing care and health promotion for children and families. Emphasis on concepts related to the delivery of familycentered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 322L.title: Child and Family Health Lab
NURS 322L.subject: NURS
NURS 322L.description: Nursing care and health promotion lab for children and families. Application of concepts related to the delivery of family-centered holistic, culturally sensitive, therapeutic nursing care to children and families in acute care and community settings. Sophomore standing or higher.

NURS 340.title: Contemporary Ethical Issues in Health Care
NURS 340.subject: NURS
NURS 340.description: Explore contemporary ethical issues and their legal implications in health care. Focus on decision-making in professional practice and social policy formation.
NURS 340.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 343.title: Gerontology: Its Nursing Implications
NURS 343.subject: NURS
NURS 343.description: Explores attitudes toward the aged, biological and psychological aspects, ethnicity, sexuality, nutritional problems, community resources, other related topics.
NURS 343.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 344.title: Nursing in the Multicultural Milieu
NURS 344.subject: NURS
NURS 344.description: Relates values, beliefs, attitudes, family organization, lifestyles, and health practices in different ethnic groups to health-care and nursing practice.
NURS 344.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 360.title: Health and Illness III
NURS 360.subject: NURS
NURS 360.description: Focuses on complex situations requiring strong recognition skills, and rapid decision making. The evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.

NURS 360L.title: Health and Illness III Lab
NURS 360L.subject: NURS
NURS 360L.description: Clinical course focuses on complex situations requiring application of strong recognition skills and rapid decision making. Evidence base supporting assessment and nursing intervention is explored.

NURS 361.title: Health Education and Promotion
NURS 361.subject: NURS
NURS 361.description: Provides an overview of the concepts and application of health education and health promotion theories and principles as applies to individuals, groups, and the larger public.
NURS 361.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 362.title: Professionalism in Nursing II
NURS 362.subject: NURS
NURS 362.description: Continuation of 211. Focus is on current issues in nursing and health care and nursing roles. Principles of organizational structure, leadership, decision-making, priority setting, and change will be discussed.

NURS 363.title: Introduction to Nursing Research
NURS 363.subject: NURS
NURS 363.description: Introduction to the research process and an understanding of the applicability of the scientific approach to nursing. Analysis and resolution of contemporary medical ethics issues in research and general nursing practice are primary focuses.

NURS 399.title: Directed Reading/Research I, II
NURS 399.subject: NURS
NURS 399.description: Limited to juniors and seniors in nursing.

NURS 402.title: Student Ambassador Program
NURS 402.subject: NURS
NURS 402.description: Focuses on professional leadership development, mentorship, and professional skills for nurses. Students learn to be representatives between the Department of Nursing and alumni, prospective students, and the general public.
NURS 402.prereq_raw: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

prereq_tree.text: one semester as a Nursing Student Ambassador

NURS 411.title: NCLEX Review
NURS 411.subject: NURS
NURS 411.description: Overview of the NCLEX-RN licensure examination and regular, systematic practice in taking multiple choice examinations.
NURS 411.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 420.title: Cooperative Education in Nursing
NURS 420.subject: NURS
NURS 420.description: A two-semester course with seminar in professional role development in addition to paid work experience in nursing at a local agency. Upper division NURS majors only.

NURS 421.title: Summer Internship
NURS 421.subject: NURS
NURS 421.description: Summer practicum experience for students to learn the role of the professional nurse by building on previously learned knowledge and skills in the nursing program.

NURS 431.title: Complementary and Alternative Therapies
NURS 431.subject: NURS
NURS 431.description: Survey of complementary and alternative therapies used for health promotion of individuals and groups.
NURS 431.prereq_raw: open to non-nursing majors with consent

prereq_tree.text: open to non-nursing majors with consent

NURS 432.title: Veteran Healthcare, Education, and Cultural Needs
NURS 432.subject: NURS
NURS 432.description: Provides a broad overview of the Veteran-Military population and their unique culture, educational, and health care needs. Open to non-nursing majors.

NURS 449.title: Gerontology, Health Care, and the Law (Elder Law)
NURS 449.subject: NURS
NURS 449.description: Provides a basic foundation for studies at the intersection of gerontology, health care, and the law and places an emphasis on proactive and preventive law for older adults in society.

NURS 450.title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing
NURS 450.subject: NURS
NURS 450.description: Theory course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 450L.title: Community, Public, and Global Health Nursing Lab
NURS 450L.subject: NURS
NURS 450L.description: Clinical course focuses on community, public, and global health nursing with an emphasis on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 452.title: Cultural Aspects of Health Management in Populations Indigenous to Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia
NURS 452.subject: NURS
NURS 452.description: Focuses on cultural aspects that influence health management in indigenous populations of Hawai‘i, the Pacific, and Asia, with an emphasis on development of culturally sensitive strategies to promote and improve health management.
NURS 452.restrictions_raw: NURS majors only. Undergraduate majors only.

NURS 453.title: Introduction to Genetics in Nursing Practice
NURS 453.subject: NURS
NURS 453.description: Fundamentals of genetics and genomics, including principles of inheritance in humans; cells and development, chromosome structure and function, and implications on health. Includes overview of topics relevant to genetics/genomics in the clinical setting.

NURS 460.title: Complex Nursing and Leadership
NURS 460.subject: NURS
NURS 460.description: Theory course emphasizes the judgments, knowledge, and skills necessary for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. The experience focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership.

NURS 460L.title: Complex Nursing and Leadership Lab
NURS 460L.subject: NURS
NURS 460L.description: Clinical course emphasizes application of knowledge and skills for nursing practice, including case management and quality management experiences. Focuses on complex clinical judgments, interdisciplinary team functioning, and leadership. Emphasis on writing instruction.

NURS 461.title: Advanced Pathophysiology
NURS 461.subject: NURS
NURS 461.description: Provides an advanced understanding of pathophysiologic mechanisms underlying human illness across the lifespan. Provides a foundation for formulating clinical decisions and therapeutic plans of care to promote disease prevention and health promotion.

NURS 462.title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN
NURS 462.subject: NURS
NURS 462.description: Theory focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 462L.title: Community Health Nursing for Executive RN Field Work
NURS 462L.subject: NURS
NURS 462L.description: Field work focuses on community health nursing with an emphasis for the Executive RN on strategies applied to improve health and decrease health inequities at the local as well as national and international levels.

NURS 465.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing
NURS 465.subject: NURS
NURS 465.description: Examination of human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.

NURS 465L.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Nursing Lab
NURS 465L.subject: NURS
NURS 465L.description: Application of the nursing process involving human responses to psychiatric and mental illness in relation to physiologic, psychological, social, cultural, and environmental concepts. Emphasis on self-awareness, therapeutic communication, and holistic, individualized health-related outcomes.

NURS 481.title: Nursing Honors Research Project
NURS 481.subject: NURS
NURS 481.description: Involves directed, mentored research study for SONDH Honors students with their honors advisor. The course grade depends on meeting objectives negotiated each course semester.

NURS 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
NURS 499.subject: NURS
NURS 499.description: Planned individualized study or research in specialized area related to interprofessional collaborative practice. Senior undergraduate NURS students only.

NURS 501.title: Professionalism in Nursing
NURS 501.subject: NURS
NURS 501.description: Introduction to history of nursing and leaders in the field. Will explore contemporary nursing issues and research. Strategies to foster adherence to a professional code of ethics in practice will be examined. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only. (Once a year)

NURS 502.title: Pathophysiology
NURS 502.subject: NURS
NURS 502.description: Web-enhanced on pathophysiologic concepts as a basis of illness and injury and the corresponding spectrum of human response, which serves as a foundation for the formulation of clinical decisions and care planning. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only. (Once a year)

NURS 503.title: Pharmacology for Nursing Practice
NURS 503.subject: NURS
NURS 503.description: Essential principles of pharmacology using a pathophysiologic approach with emphasis on administering medications and evaluating their effects. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.
