NURS 504.title: Health Assessment
NURS 504.subject: NURS
NURS 504.description: Concepts/theories of health assessment, data collection, and analysis to distinguish between health/wellness, risk factors or health deviations across the lifespan. Attention to principles of communication and interviewing. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 504L.title: Health Assessment Lab
NURS 504L.subject: NURS
NURS 504L.description: Application of assessment skills in dry lab and clinical settings, with attention to principles of communication, interviewing and physical examination skills. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 505.title: Foundations of Nursing Science
NURS 505.subject: NURS
NURS 505.description: Nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 505L.title: Foundations of Nursing Science and Practice Lab
NURS 505L.subject: NURS
NURS 505L.description: Application of the nursing process and scientific based nursing interventions to meet basic human needs using basic psycho-motor skills to support assessment, intervention, and evaluation activities. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 507.title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing
NURS 507.subject: NURS
NURS 507.description: Biopsychosocial theories of human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; reviews current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 507L.title: Bio-Behavioral Health Nursing Clinic/Lab
NURS 507L.subject: NURS
NURS 507L.description: Application of current knowledge regarding human behavior related to function, alteration, and/or disruption of mental processes; applies current knowledge related to nursing care, psychiatric treatment/psychosocial rehabilitation of identified mentally ill adults/children and their families. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 508.title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families
NURS 508.subject: NURS
NURS 508.description: Introduction to the theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care of the perinatal family. Women’s and men’s health issues are discussed. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 508L.title: Nursing Care of Childbearing Families Clinical/Lab
NURS 508L.subject: NURS
NURS 508L.description: Application of the nursing care of the mother and family. The student will apply clinical and theoretical concepts of holistic nursing care for women experiencing customary and complicated perinatal processes. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 509.title: Nursing Care of Children and Families
NURS 509.subject: NURS
NURS 509.description: Examines the bio/psycho/social response of the child and family to health and illness, as well as nursing care for acute and chronic conditions. Lab course taken concurrently. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 509L.title: Nursing Care of Children and Families Clinical/Lab
NURS 509L.subject: NURS
NURS 509L.description: Accompanies and supports Pediatric Nursing to provide educational experiences in the hospital and outpatient or community settings. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 513.title: Acute Care Nursing
NURS 513.subject: NURS
NURS 513.description: Addresses the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatment in the acute setting will be covered. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 513L.title: Acute Care Nursing Lab
NURS 513L.subject: NURS
NURS 513L.description: Application of the bio/psycho/social human health response to a wide range of conditions. Application of health promotion, risk reduction and disease detection and nursing care treatments in the acute care setting. NURS majors only or consent. Admission into GEPN only.

NURS 517.title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice
NURS 517.subject: NURS
NURS 517.description: Examination of continuity of care for clients with complex needs. Emphasis on application of leadership, management, and quality improvement in the clinical setting. NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 517L.title: Clinical Immersion to Nursing Practice Lab
NURS 517L.subject: NURS
NURS 517L.description: Deliver comprehensive nursing care to clients with complex needs in community and/or acute care settings. Leadership, management, and quality improvement competencies are stressed. NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 518.title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing
NURS 518.subject: NURS
NURS 518.description: Introduces community and public health nursing with an emphasis on application to nursing practice in the community and public health settings. NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 518L.title: Introduction to Community and Public Health Nursing Lab
NURS 518L.subject: NURS
NURS 518L.description: Application of health promotion, risk reduction, and disease prevention and detection and nursing care treatments in the community setting. NURS majors only or consent. Admission to GEPN only.

NURS 600.title: Epidemiology for Advanced Nursing
NURS 600.subject: NURS
NURS 600.description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods, with an emphasis on its application to nursing practice. (Once a year)

NURS 605.title: Health Promotion and Disease Prevention
NURS 605.subject: NURS
NURS 605.description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and prevention of common health and illness conditions with culturally diverse individuals, families, groups, and communities. Includes didactic (30 hrs) and fieldwork (45 hrs).
NURS 605.prereq_raw: classified graduate student status in the SONDH

prereq_tree.text: classified graduate student status in the SONDH

NURS 608.title: Genetics and Health Care
NURS 608.subject: NURS
NURS 608.description: Addresses the scientific, psycho-social, ethical, cultural, and spiritual issues surrounding genetic disease, genetic testing, and living with an inherited condition.

NURS 609.title: Health Politics & Policy
NURS 609.subject: NURS
NURS 609.description: Review of contemporary national health policies, issues and concerns; and international comparison of health policy evolution; includes didactic and 45 hours of fieldwork experience learning.

NURS 611.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Assessment and Diagnosis
NURS 611.subject: NURS
NURS 611.description: Identification and synthesis of pertinent biopsychosocial and cultural data to complete advanced psychiatric-mental health assessments and diagnoses.

NURS 612.title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning
NURS 612.subject: NURS
NURS 612.description: Provides a framework for the development of advanced skills for systematic and comprehensive data collection, organization, precise recording, accurate assessment and communication of data reflecting the biopsychophysical status of individuals across the life span. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 612L.title: Advanced Assessment and Clinical Reasoning Lab
NURS 612L.subject: NURS
NURS 612L.description: Clinical lab and practicum for advanced practice nursing. Emphasis on integration of knowledge, skills and outcome evaluation. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 613.title: Pathophysiology for Advanced Practice
NURS 613.subject: NURS
NURS 613.description: Provides an understanding of normal physiological mechanisms and pathological processes to serve as a foundation for clinical assessment, decision making, and clinical management across the lifespan. NURS majors only or consent.
NURS 613.prereq_raw: enrollment as a classified student in a graduate program in the SONDH

prereq_tree.text: enrollment as a classified student in a graduate program in the SONDH

NURS 615.title: Clinical Skills and Procedures for Advanced Practice Nursing
NURS 615.subject: NURS
NURS 615.description: Clinical laboratory that focuses on clinical skills and procedures performed by advanced practice nurses (nurse practitioners and/or clinical nurse specialists). Topics will vary by section and semester.

NURS 616.title: Psychobiology of Human Behavior and Psychopharmacology
NURS 616.subject: NURS
NURS 616.description: Survey of the psychobiological basis of selected human behaviors and mental disorders across the lifespan and psychopharmacologic treatments prescribed by health care providers. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 617.title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-A
NURS 617.subject: NURS
NURS 617.description: The first of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis, and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.

NURS 618.title: Human Responses to Acute and Chronic Illness-B
NURS 618.subject: NURS
NURS 618.description: Second of two courses that focuses on the delivery of advanced practice nursing in the assessment, diagnosis and management of common acute and chronic adult health problems in the acute care setting.

NURS 619.title: Emerging Diseases & Implications for Advanced Nursing Practice
NURS 619.subject: NURS
NURS 619.description: Selected emerging diseases are examined within historical context, known science (past and present) and societal factors that influence prevention, detection, treatment and containment strategies. Considerations for advanced public health nursing practice are identified and examined.

NURS 620.title: Nursing Research, Theory, and Evidence-Based Practice
NURS 620.subject: NURS
NURS 620.description: Examination of theory, research, and evidence-based inquiry to support evidence-based practice among MS prepared nurses.
NURS 620.prereq_raw: enrollment as a classified student in the graduate degree program in SONDH

prereq_tree.text: enrollment as a classified student in the graduate degree program in SONDH

NURS 621.title: Acute and Episodic Care Management
NURS 621.subject: NURS
NURS 621.description: Diagnosis and management of health and illness with emphasis on clients with common acute/episodic conditions seen in context of family and community. Advanced practice nurse-client relationship, practice roles, and culturally relevant care are included. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 622.title: Psychiatric-Mental Health Issues and Roles
NURS 622.subject: NURS
NURS 622.description: Exploration of major issues and roles in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 623.title: Psychopharmacology
NURS 623.subject: NURS
NURS 623.description: Survey of biopsychological bases of and biotherapies for major mental disorders, including the schizophrenias, affective and personality disorders, pediatric and geriatric problems, and neurological dysfunctions with appropriate applications to health care.

NURS 624.title: Adolescent and Family PsychiatricMental Health Care
NURS 624.subject: NURS
NURS 624.description: Seminar on theory/ research in advanced psychiatric-mental health nursing of adolescents and families representing diverse populations. Emphasis on developmental and nursing theories, evidence-based practice, therapeutic modalities and disease management of psychiatric illness.

NURS 625.title: Advanced Nursing Roles
NURS 625.subject: NURS
NURS 625.description: Provides students with an understanding of different roles of the advanced professional nurse; an ability to proactively manage the environment of their specialty practice; includes 45 hours of field work experience.

NURS 626.title: Advanced Population Health Nursing
NURS 626.subject: NURS
NURS 626.description: Introduction to the core competencies, key theoretical models and concepts that guide advanced population health nursing. The student will initiate their professional portfolio, which must be completed during the last semester of the MS program.

NURS 627.title: Child/Family Health Assessment
NURS 627.subject: NURS
NURS 627.description: (2 Sem, 8-hr Lab) Opportunity to develop specialized clinical competence in assessment of children as a basis for the development of clinical specialization. Development of the individual’s potential toward health maintenance functioning. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 628.title: Child Health: Special Health Needs
NURS 628.subject: NURS
NURS 628.description: Provides a theoretical basis required for specialized clinical competence in adapting recent findings on child/parent assessments, social and health risk indicators, the role of environment, and multidisciplinary settings in the care of pediatrics.

NURS 629.title: Pharmacology for Nurses in Advanced Practice
NURS 629.subject: NURS
NURS 629.description: Prepares APNs to evaluate, monitor, and prescribe pharmaceuticals to treat acute and chronic illness across lifespan. Emphasis on drug indications, mechanisms of action, clinical efficacy, adverse effects, interactions, monitoring, education, and cost effectiveness. Enrollment as a classified student in a SONDH graduate degree program. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 630.title: Introduction to Information Technology in Healthcare
NURS 630.subject: NURS
NURS 630.description: Introduction to the use of information systems in healthcare. Selected information systems and data sets are explored with application of results to various patient populations and clinical practice settings.

NURS 632.title: Therapeutic Modalities
NURS 632.subject: NURS
NURS 632.description: Therapeutic modalities used in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations.

NURS 633.title: Child Health: Promotion and Maintenance
NURS 633.subject: NURS
NURS 633.description: Presents normal developmental, physiological and social needs of children within the context of family; then focuses on the management of common acute and chronic illnesses of children. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 634.title: Child Health: Advanced Pediatric Acute/Chronic Care
NURS 634.subject: NURS
NURS 634.description: Focuses on the evaluation of pediatric clients with higher acuity and more complex management issues. Emphasizes critical analysis of evidence based research in pediatric health care. NURS majors only or consent.
NURS 634.prereq_raw: Admission into the PNP and FNP program; 612/612L, and 633

NURS 635.title: Women’s Health: Promotion and Maintenance
NURS 635.subject: NURS
NURS 635.description: Provides a foundation of concepts necessary to maintain and promote women’s health, including developmental, physiological and social needs of women of all ages and the management of common health problems and concerns specific to women. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 636.title: Women’s Health: Special Problem
NURS 636.subject: NURS
NURS 636.description: (2 Sem, 12-hr Lab) Focuses upon assessment and intervention of at-risk and high-risk women during pregnancy, interconception, and the menopausal years. Emphasizes critical analysis of research in pregnancy, family planning, and common gynecological problems.
NURS 636.prereq_raw: 635 or consent. NURS majors only or consent

NURS 638.title: Child and Adolescent PsychiatricMental Health
NURS 638.subject: NURS
NURS 638.description: Theory and research in advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing of children and adolescents representing culturally diverse populations. Emphasis on growth and development, assessment and diagnosis, and therapeutic modalities.

NURS 639.title: Disciplinary Knowledge I
NURS 639.subject: NURS
NURS 639.description: Exploration of a variety of philosophies of science and examination of factors influencing the development of nursing theory and the emergence of nursing as a discipline.

NURS 640.title: Chronic Illness Management
NURS 640.subject: NURS
NURS 640.description: Management of chronic illness using selected health care systems in culturally diverse communities. Management includes practice, consultation, education, research, and evaluation. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 641.title: Advanced Nursing in the Global Health Environment
NURS 641.subject: NURS
NURS 641.description: Exploration and analysis of key global health topics of concern for APNs.

NURS 642.title: Health Care Technology and Informatics
NURS 642.subject: NURS
NURS 642.description: Introduction to the field of health care technology and informatics for clinicians through the application of health care information systems. Open to students in other healthcare fields by permission.

NURS 646.title: Advanced Psychiatric-Mental Health Practicum
NURS 646.subject: NURS
NURS 646.description: Supervised application of theories, research, and skills for advanced practice psychiatric-mental health nursing with individuals, families, and groups representing culturally diverse populations. Includes the program’s capstone experience.

NURS 647.title: Family Systems in Health and Illness
NURS 647.subject: NURS
NURS 647.description: Family systems approach to include selected family theories, family research and family centered culturally sensitive clinical assessment and intervention in health and illness situations.

NURS 650.title: Complementary and Traditional Care
NURS 650.subject: NURS
NURS 650.description: A review of theoretical systems and approaches to complementary and traditional care in culturally diverse populations with a focus on wellness. Appropriate for all health-care professionals.

NURS 655.title: Tests and Measurement in Nursing Education
NURS 655.subject: NURS
NURS 655.description: Testing and evaluation applied to nursing education.

NURS 661.title: Human Resource Management in Healthcare Agencies
NURS 661.subject: NURS
NURS 661.description: Analyze and critically evaluate basic issues, policies and trends in human resource management as it applies to health care agencies.

NURS 662.title: Leadership, Role, Identity and Organizational/System Change
NURS 662.subject: NURS
NURS 662.description: Study of theoretical and conceptual models of leadership and management as applied to relevant advanced nurses’ roles, their respective populations, and changing healthcare environments. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 663.title: Analysis of Healthcare Delivery Models
NURS 663.subject: NURS
NURS 663.description: Analysis of various clinical management concepts and health-care delivery systems influencing outcomes, process, and costs in the delivery of care.

NURS 664.title: Seminar and Practicum in Nursing Executive Leadership
NURS 664.subject: NURS
NURS 664.description: Supervised practicum to build mid to senior level nursing leadership competencies and facilitate change in complex healthcare organizations.

NURS 665.title: Clinical Economics and Finance
NURS 665.subject: NURS
NURS 665.description: Economic and financial concepts and tools for use in developing and managing patient care processes.

NURS 668.title: Community Based Participatory Research (CBPR) for Advanced Practice Nurses
NURS 668.subject: NURS
NURS 668.description: Online course focuses on use of CBPR methods by Advanced Practice Nurses to address population level issues amendable to nursing interventions; 15 hours of didactic and 90 hours of field experience are included. (Once a year)

NURS 669.title: Evaluating Research for Evidencebased Practice
NURS 669.subject: NURS
NURS 669.description: Introduces evidence-based practice methods for improving the quality of nursing practice. Develops skills in differentiating quantitative and qualitative research, statistical methods, and searching, critiquing, and synthesizing literature, pertinent to health care issues.

NURS 670.title: Advanced Practice Nursing During Public Health Disasters
NURS 670.subject: NURS
NURS 670.description: The role of the advanced professional nurse in public health preparedness, planning and response. Includes 45 hours of field work where the student will practice emergency response functional roles.

NURS 671.title: Biostatistics: Application in the Advanced Nursing Practice Setting
NURS 671.subject: NURS
NURS 671.description: Includes basic bio-statistical techniques and the application of statistical findings to practice programmatic decisions.
NURS 671.prereq_raw: graduate standing in the Department of Nursing or consent. (Once a year)

children.text: in the Department of Nursing or consent . ( Once a year)

NURS 672.title: Advanced Practice Population Health Nursing Practicum
NURS 672.subject: NURS
NURS 672.description: Student will conduct a complex service project for a public or community based agency. May be taken for 1-6 credits. (45 hours of practicum experience awarded for each one credit of the course) NURS majors only.
NURS 672.prereq_raw: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing or consent

children.text: 24 credits of MS in Advanced Population Health Nursing

NURS 673.title: Implementation and Evaluation Strategies for Evidence-Based Practice
NURS 673.subject: NURS
NURS 673.description: Using knowledge of translational science, designs an implementation plan for a practice guideline. Determines evaluation methods and selects outcome variables that best measure success. Discusses institutionalization of, and identifies facilitators and barriers to, practice change. Graduate standing only.

NURS 675.title: Advanced Practice Clinical
NURS 675.subject: NURS
NURS 675.description: Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 676.title: Primary Care I Seminar: Health Assessment
NURS 676.subject: NURS
NURS 676.description: Seminar to discuss the evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management. Utilization of clinical cases and current literature on health care assessment.

NURS 676L.title: Primary Care I Lab (beginning level): Health Assessment
NURS 676L.subject: NURS
NURS 676L.description: Beginning level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients for advanced practice nursing students in primary care settings.

NURS 677.title: Primary Care II Seminar: Management of the Adult
NURS 677.subject: NURS
NURS 677.description: Intermediate level seminar where students discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of adult clients.

NURS 677L.title: Primary Care II Lab (intermediate level): Acute & Chronic Conditions (Adult)
NURS 677L.subject: NURS
NURS 677L.description: Intermediate level practicum. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, management, and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for advanced practice nursing focusing on adults with acute or chronic diagnoses in primary care.

NURS 678.title: Primary Care III Seminar: Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
NURS 678.subject: NURS
NURS 678.description: Intermediate level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).

NURS 678L.title: Primary Care III Lab (intermediate level): Special Populations (Peds, Gero, Women)
NURS 678L.subject: NURS
NURS 678L.description: Intermediate level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients in a primary care setting for advanced practice nursing students focusing on vulnerable populations (pediatric, geriatric, women).

NURS 679.title: Primary Care IV Seminar: Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
NURS 679.subject: NURS
NURS 679.description: Advanced level seminar. Students will discuss current evidence, concepts, and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management focusing on primary care of clients across the lifespan.

NURS 679L.title: Primary Care IV Lab (advanced level): Primary Care Integration Across the Lifespan
NURS 679L.subject: NURS
NURS 679L.description: Advanced level clinical experience. Application of concepts and principles of assessment, diagnosis, evaluation, and management of clients across the lifespan in primary care settings for advanced practice nursing students.

NURS 680.title: Cultural Competency in Nursing Education
NURS 680.subject: NURS
NURS 680.description: Evaluates the impact of history on the culture of nursing and nursing education. Explore strategies to provide education in a culturally sensitive manner to culturally diverse students.

NURS 682.title: Health and Healing Practices of Populations with Health Disparities in Hawai‘i and Other Places
NURS 682.subject: NURS
NURS 682.description: Teaching and learning concepts applied to health promotion and the prevention of common conditions of disease among populations with health disparities in Hawai‘i and other places; includes didactic and 45 hours of field experience.

NURS 683.title: Occupational Health I
NURS 683.subject: NURS
NURS 683.description: Historical development of occupational health; occupational diseases and accidents; control of hazards in occupational environment; study of selected occupations and specific problems. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 690.title: Curriculum Evaluation in Nursing Education
NURS 690.subject: NURS
NURS 690.description: Current trends of planning for evaluation and critical analysis and application of curriculum evaluation frameworks in nursing education.

NURS 692.title: Introduction to Research Methods
NURS 692.subject: NURS
NURS 692.description: Nursing research methods for qualitative and quantitative studies, institutional review board procedures, and how to develop a research proposal.

NURS 693.title: Advanced Practice Clinical for Clinical Nurse Specialists
NURS 693.subject: NURS
NURS 693.description: Application of concepts and principles of education, consultation, research, and management and evaluation of clients in supervised clinical practicum for adult health clinical nurse specialist students.
NURS 693.prereq_raw: 612 (or concurrent), 612L (or concurrent), 613 (or concurrent), and 629 (or concurrent); or consent

NURS 695.title: Successful Aging: Physiologic
NURS 695.subject: NURS
NURS 695.description: Advanced study of the functional, cultural, psychological, and socioeconomic phenomena that impact the physiology of normal and abnormal aging. Emphasis is on promoting successful aging among elder residents of the Pacific Basin and applications to primary health care. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 696.title: Nursing Education Capstone
NURS 696.subject: NURS
NURS 696.description: A culminating experience in nursing education program designed for students to integrate, critique, extend, and apply knowledge gained in the program.

NURS 699.title: Directed Study or Research
NURS 699.subject: NURS
NURS 699.description: Directed study of problems related to nursing theory and practice.

NURS 702.title: Philosophical Thoughts
NURS 702.subject: NURS
NURS 702.description: Introduces the major fields of philosophy for use in research. Frameworks for the evaluation and critique of philosophical approaches to research will be explored, debated, analyzed, and applied as relevant to the PhD student’s dissertation.

NURS 710.title: Designing and Conducting Clinical Trials
NURS 710.subject: NURS
NURS 710.description: Small group sections will guide students as they produce their own clinical trial protocol. Topics like ethics and statistical power will be addressed briefly.

NURS 721.title: Instrument Development and Evaluation in Research
NURS 721.subject: NURS
NURS 721.description: Theory of testing and evaluation applied to nursing research in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 730.title: Principles of Evidence-based Practice for Advanced Nursing
NURS 730.subject: NURS
NURS 730.description: Evaluates conceptual models for use in evidence-based practice. Refines skills in searching and critiquing the literature for application to practice change. Synthesizes a body of literature to design interventions pertinent to a practice problem.

NURS 739.title: Advanced Nursing Science
NURS 739.subject: NURS
NURS 739.description: Provides opportunities to know and practice the process of theory development in nursing and to test concepts, relationships, and models about health behavior in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 741.title: Quantitative Methods and Measures
NURS 741.subject: NURS
NURS 741.description: Critical analysis of quantitative research methods used to analyze problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 741.prereq_raw: 620 or equivalent course and an advanced statistics course; or consent

NURS 742.title: Qualitative Methods I
NURS 742.subject: NURS
NURS 742.description: Introduction to qualitative research methods in the development of nursing disciplinary knowledge related to culturally diverse populations.

NURS 743.title: Qualitative Methods II
NURS 743.subject: NURS
NURS 743.description: Advanced in-depth exploration of the data collection, data analysis and methodological issues in the qualitative research traditions (ethnography, grounded theory, phenomenology and critical theory) used in nursing research.

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . ( Once a year)

NURS 744.title: Seminar on Women and Health
NURS 744.subject: NURS
NURS 744.description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.

NURS 745.title: Creative Learning Strategies for Adults
NURS 745.subject: NURS
NURS 745.description: Analysis of forces that affect adult learners. Concept of lifelong learning vis-à-vis development of creative strategies that assist maturing, self-directed persons to develop their potentialities.

NURS 746.title: Methods of Program Evaluation & Quality Improvement
NURS 746.subject: NURS
NURS 746.description: Principles of and frameworks for program evaluation. Students develop logic models and evaluation plans for a community program and collect and analyze evaluation data.

NURS 747.title: Curriculum Development
NURS 747.subject: NURS
NURS 747.description: Current theories, issues, and trends of curriculum development in nursing. Application and critiques of related research. NURS majors only or consent.

NURS 748.title: Supervised Practicum in Teaching
NURS 748.subject: NURS
NURS 748.description: Supervised experience in instructional planning and teaching.

NURS 750.title: Foundation of Health Systems and Translation Science
NURS 750.subject: NURS
NURS 750.description: Integrate scientific findings from various fields of study to the leadership and management of healthcare systems to ensure the delivery of quality and safe care.

NURS 751.title: Concept Development and Analysis
NURS 751.subject: NURS
NURS 751.description: First course offering in-depth analysis of specific concepts and theoretical formulations of nursing and other disciplines pertinent to the student’s area of research interest. Addresses human responses to health in culturally diverse populations.

NURS 752.title: Advanced Statistics I
NURS 752.subject: NURS
NURS 752.description: Advanced application of general linear model theory to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 752.prereq_raw: 741 (or equivalent) or consent. Once a year

children.text: ( or equivalent) or consent . Once a year

NURS 753.title: Advanced Statistics II
NURS 753.subject: NURS
NURS 753.description: Advanced application of multivariate statistics to analyze complex problems of interest to nursing in culturally diverse populations.
NURS 753.prereq_raw: 741 and 752 or equivalent courses, or consent. Once a year

NURS 760.title: Trends in Healthcare
NURS 760.subject: NURS
NURS 760.description: Evaluates the historical foundations of healthcare systems and their relationship to current issues and trends in healthcare services. Analyzes the variations in healthcare delivery systems across nations and the impact on health outcomes.

NURS 761.title: Translation Science
NURS 761.subject: NURS
NURS 761.description: Synthesis and analysis of interventions and variables that influence the rate of adoption of innovations. Application of concepts to patient populations and systems of healthcare.

NURS 767.title: Culturally Competent Research Methods
NURS 767.subject: NURS
NURS 767.description: Analysis of concepts, issues, and methods in conducting culturally competent research in the health field.

NURS 768.title: Advanced Clinical Economics and Finance
NURS 768.subject: NURS
NURS 768.description: Theory and practice of financial management to achieve high quality and cost effectiveness in healthcare. Hybrid course which combines face-to-face with online learning.

NURS 769.title: Dissertation Proposal Writing Seminar
NURS 769.subject: NURS
NURS 769.description: Provides students with advanced study and critique from faculty leading to the development of a draft dissertation proposal. Peer exchange facilities individual scholarship, research topic mastery, and ability to conduct rigorous critique.

NURS 774.title: Best Practices in Leading Healthcare Patient Safety and Quality
NURS 774.subject: NURS
NURS 774.description: Examination of quality of health care, the process of managing healthcare outcomes and costs in the delivery of care through the interdisciplinary process.

NURS 775.title: Capstone Field Study
NURS 775.subject: NURS
NURS 775.description: Supervised experience in executive nursing leadership to address important health issues for high-risk or under-served populations utilizing an interdisciplinary systems-based approach.

NURS 776.title: Doctor of Nursing Practice Project
NURS 776.subject: NURS
NURS 776.description: Under the guidance of their DNP Project Team members, students will synthesize, integrate, and translate newly acquired knowledge and skills in the implementation and evaluation of their DNP Project.

NURS 777.title: Nursing Research Practicum
NURS 777.subject: NURS
NURS 777.description: Faculty guided research opportunity to gain mastery of research skills and techniques through participation in mentored research. PhD students only.
NURS 777.prereq_raw: 741 (with a minimum grade of B-), 742 (with a minimum grade of B-), 751 (with a minimum grade of B-) and a quantitative methods course

NURS 796.title: Grant Writing and Grant Management
NURS 796.subject: NURS
NURS 796.description: Designed to introduce students to grants, grant writing, and grant management. Combined lecture discussion, seminar, and exercises on grants, grant writing, and grant management for health sciences. Open to NURS students only, others with approval.

ASAN 312A.title: Contemporary Asian Civilization
ASAN 312A.subject: ASAN
ASAN 312A.description: Multidisciplinary examination of problems and issues affecting peoples and institutions of contemporary Asia: ethnic, language, religious, and cultural differences; population growth; public health; economic development; political and social change; environmental problems; etc.

ERTH 101A.title: Dynamic Earth
ERTH 101A.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101A.description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

HON 101.title: Introduction to Research and Creative Work at Mânoa
HON 101.subject: HON
HON 101.description: Combines lectures by instructors and faculty guests with workshops and hands-on experience in small group projects, including bibliographic searches, laboratory science, social surveys and interviews. A significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Honors Program students only.

HON 120.title: Mathematical Modes of Thinking
HON 120.subject: HON
HON 120.description: Mathematics as both a language and a thought process expressed in that language. Historical and contemporary relations to culture.

HON 190.title: Honors Tutorial
HON 190.subject: HON
HON 190.description: Supplements a 100 or 200 lecture course or standard lab time with discussion section, instructor-intensive lab time or directed research. Limited enrollment.

HON 301.title: Public Policy-Making
HON 301.subject: HON
HON 301.description: Students develop understanding of theory, practice, and ethical issues of public policy-making. Combines lecture/ discussion and fieldtrips. Students develop policy analysis and strategic plans that identify issues, interests, and methods of influence.

HON 303.title: Civic Engagement, Volunteerism & Community Service
HON 303.subject: HON
HON 303.description: Seminar on history and theory and practice of volunteerism in the U.S. Involves comparative study of volunteerism, individual research projects on volunteerism, and conduct of field service activities together with written reports.

HON 330.title: Honors Study Abroad Project
HON 330.subject: HON
HON 330.description: Honors students participating in study abroad enhance their experience through an individually proposed project to be carried out in the host country. Project must be approved by the Honors and Study Abroad directors. Honors students only.
HON 330.prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and Study Abroad director

children.text: of Honors director and Study Abroad director

HON 333.title: Experiential Learning and Scholarly Engagement
HON 333.subject: HON
HON 333.description: Students develop an understanding of theory and practice of experiential learning through direct engagement and focused scholarly reflection while assimilating and synthesizing new knowledge and developing critical thinking skills. Honors Program approval only.

HON 340.title: The Publication Process
HON 340.subject: HON
HON 340.description: Publication process focuses on experiential learning and ethics. Learn how to solicit contributions, review and edit articles, and learn about publishing from multiple perspectives. Honors students only.
HON 340.prereq_raw: consent of Honors director and instructor

HON 380.title: Peer Mentoring
HON 380.subject: HON
HON 380.description: Students develop understanding of dynamics of leadership skills within the contexts of paired to large groups. Significant portion is dedicated to writing and oral communication instruction. Honors Program students only. Pre-semester training sessions, on-going training and supervision.

HON 491.title: Junior Seminar
HON 491.subject: HON
HON 491.description: Project-based experiential learning involving community-based research or creative work. Focus on project design, practical skills, and teamwork. Significant portion is dedicated to writing instruction. Multi-disciplinary topics vary each semester. Honors Program students only.

HON 492.title: Honors Colloquium
HON 492.subject: HON
HON 492.description: Weekly meetings for discussion of enduring issues and problems of an interdisciplinary nature. Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

HON 494.title: Honors Workshop
HON 494.subject: HON
HON 494.description: Supplemental workshop for students beginning independent work on their senior honors thesis. HON students only. Junior or senior standing only.

HON 495.title: Honors Thesis Proposal
HON 495.subject: HON
HON 495.description: Library research skills; scholarship of research and creative work; methodological and ethical issues; development of individual proposal or prospectus for Senior Honors Project. Limited to candidates for the Honors degree.

HON 496.title: Senior Honors Project
HON 496.subject: HON
HON 496.description: Original research, creative work, performance or other form of scholarly project appropriate to a major and supervised by a faculty member. Limited to candidates for Honors degree.

IS 300A.title: Field Study
IS 300A.subject: IS
IS 300A.description: Pre-arranged systematic field investigation of selected topics.
IS 300A.prereq_raw: written proposal approved by Honors director and appropriate faculty member. Repeatable up to 16 credits

children.text: written proposal approved by Honors director
appropriate faculty member. Repeatable up to 16 credits

MICR 140A.title: Microbiology Laboratory
MICR 140A.subject: MICR
MICR 140A.description: (2 2-hr Lab) Primarily for students in nursing and dental hygiene.

TIM 102A.title: Food and World Cultures
TIM 102A.subject: TIM
TIM 102A.description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

IS 099.title: Mânoa International Exchange
IS 099.subject: IS
IS 099.description: Designed for students accepted for participation in an international exchange program while enrolled at UH Mânoa.
IS 099.prereq_raw: admittance to an international exchange program

prereq_tree.text: admittance to an international exchange program

IS 100.title: Marine Option Program Seminar
IS 100.subject: IS
IS 100.description: Overview of ocean issues and organizations involved with marine activities, management, education, research, and business. Exploration of internships, research, and career opportunities. Preparation of resumes, proposals, and professional presentations. Not a BIOL major elective.

IS 206.title: Introduction to Applied Gerontology: Helping Yourself and Others to Thrive in Later Life
IS 206.subject: IS
IS 206.description: Introduction to essential information on aging and the field of gerontology. Counters ageist stereotypes, develops skills for translating research into practice, and provides an introductory survey course for the undergraduate certificate in aging. A-F only

IS 250.title: Personal Development for Effective Teams
IS 250.subject: IS
IS 250.description: Exploration and application of basic leadership theories and processes which foster personal and interpersonal development via cognitive experiential classroom methods and mentoring relationships with experienced peer leaders.

IS 291.title: Community Service Practicum
IS 291.subject: IS
IS 291.description: Supervised fieldwork in community agency, arranged by student.
IS 291.prereq_raw: written proposal approved by Honors director and appropriate faculty advisor

children.text: written proposal approved by Honors director

IS 300.title: Field Study
IS 300.subject: IS
IS 300.description: Pre-arranged systematic field investigation of selected topics.
IS 300.prereq_raw: written proposal approved by Honors director and appropriate faculty member. Repeatable up to 16 credits

children.text: written proposal approved by Honors director
appropriate faculty member. Repeatable up to 16 credits

IS 305.title: Ethics, Aging & Society
IS 305.subject: IS
IS 305.description: Addresses ethical issues in gerontology and long-term care for older adults as raised by public policy, health care problems, and social attitudes toward elders. Explores established practices and new directions for ethics in aging.

IS 321.title: Native Americans and Native Hawaiians
IS 321.subject: IS
IS 321.description: Comparative-contrastive examination of similarities and differences between Native Americans and Native Hawaiians as the only indigenous peoples of the U.S. with special attention to sociohistorical parallels and mutual contacts since contact with Europeans. Perspective is explicitly interdisciplinary by drawing not only on sociology and history, but also on archaeology, ethnology, linguistics and still other disciplines.
IS 321.prereq_raw: HIST 152 and an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science or sociology; or consent

children.text: an introductory course in cultural anthropology, political science

IS 322.title: Ethnohistory
IS 322.subject: IS
IS 322.description: Review of ethnohistory, i.e. the interdisciplinary, holistic and inclusive investigation of the histories of native peoples drawing not only on documented sources, but also on ethnography, linguistics, archaeology, ecology and other disciplines as an alternative to conventional Eurocolonial history.

IS 330.title: Information Technology and Culture
IS 330.subject: IS
IS 330.description: Investigation of the impact of information technologies on contemporary culture from a variety of perspectives.

IS 331.title: Science and Culture
IS 331.subject: IS
IS 331.description: Cultural studies of science from historical, philosophical, sociological and literary perspectives. Examination of intersections of science, race, gender and environment.

IS 340.title: Human Values and the Environment
IS 340.subject: IS
IS 340.description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts–literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics–in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
IS 340.prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent. (Once a year)

IS 347.title: Pidgin and Creole Languages
IS 347.subject: IS
IS 347.description: Nature, history, structure, and geographic distribution of pidgins and creoles.

IS 361.title: People, the Ocean and the Environment
IS 361.subject: IS
IS 361.description: People’s impact on quality of coastal and ocean environments, especially Hawaiian; scientific, legal, socioeconomic aspects. Ocean pollution, ocean technology.
IS 361.prereq_raw: OCN 201, ORE 202, or ZOOL 200; or consent

IS 369.title: British Life and Culture
IS 369.subject: IS
IS 369.description: For Study Abroad Program students participating in the UH Mânoa Semester in London. Emphasis is placed on understanding within historical contexts important issues for contemporary British society—particularly those of class, power, gender, and race.

IS 400.title: Ocean Internships and Research
IS 400.subject: IS
IS 400.description: Students carry out marine-related internships, practica, research projects or field experience on-or off-campus with faculty guidance.
IS 400.prereq_raw: minimum cum GPA of 2.5, junior or senior standing in any field of study and IS 100/BIOL 104 or consent, project proposal

children.text: in any field of study and IS 100 / BIOL 104 or consent , project proposal

IS 410.title: The Humboldt Brothers’ Legacy
IS 410.subject: IS
IS 410.description: Life and thought of the two Humboldt brothers. Alexander (1769-1859) helped to lay the foundations of modern science, including geology, geography, botany, zoology, physiology and anthropology. Older, less well-known Wilhelm (1767–1835) was an influential statesman, classical scholar, man of letters, humanist, political philosopher, anthropologist and linguist, and founded the University of Berlin. Review of the two polymaths’ impact on modern science in the Americas, the Pacific and Asia.

IS 414.title: Introduction to Linguistic Anthropology
IS 414.subject: IS
IS 414.description: Introduction to the ethnographic study of speech and language.

IS 489.title: Environmental Practicum
IS 489.subject: IS
IS 489.description: Field experience in study and abatement of environmental problems under faculty direction. Project proposal, narrative activity log, and documentary report are required.
IS 489.prereq_raw: upper division standing, courses in appropriate discipline, and consent

children.text: upper division standing, courses in appropriate discipline,

IS 610.title: Field Study in Gerontology
IS 610.subject: IS
IS 610.description: Individually designed field experience for advanced certificate in gerontology students. Placements arranged at community programs, research sites, and special projects at the Center on Aging.

IS 650.title: Principles of Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
IS 650.subject: IS
IS 650.description: Combined lecture-discussion on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss.

IS 651L.title: Laboratory A in Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
IS 651L.subject: IS
IS 651L.description: Combined lecture-laboratory on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss.

IS 652L.title: Laboratory B in Applied Evolutionary Ecology: Biodiversity Loss, Biological Invasions and Emerging Disease
IS 652L.subject: IS
IS 652L.description: Practical laboratory/ field rotation on the ecological and evolutionary underpinnings of the coupled process of biological invasion, disease emergence and biodiversity loss. Continuation of 650 and 651L.

IS 750.title: Topics in Biocultural Diversity and Conservation
IS 750.subject: IS
IS 750.description: Biological, cultural, and linguistic conservation are intimately linked, but rarely studied simultaneously. Adopts a trans-disciplinary view of diversity and conservation of nature, cultures, and languages, along with issues in anthropology, law, and ethics.

UNIV 102.title: Using Data to Guide the Career Search
UNIV 102.subject: UNIV
UNIV 102.description: Introduction to probability and statistics; including standard deviation, calculations, and inferences about means, normal distributions, and linear correlation. Integrates occupational outlook data from O*NET to understand how to link majors with careers.

UNIV 131.title: Academic and Personal Exploration
UNIV 131.subject: UNIV
UNIV 131.description: Seminar introduces students to goal setting, time management, major exploration, academic planning, service-learning opportunities, student/faculty meetings, financial literacy, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Instructor approval required.

UNIV 132.title: Academic and Career Exploration
UNIV 132.subject: UNIV
UNIV 132.description: Seminar introduces exploratory students to major and career exploration resources, guides students in developing personal, academic, and career goals and plans, and encourages frequent self-reflection. Instructor approval required.

UNIV 240.title: Fresh-More Experience
UNIV 240.subject: UNIV
UNIV 240.description: Seminar provides freshmen and sophomores with the knowledge and skills to thrive in college and beyond. Topics include major, career, and graduate school exploration. May not be taken concurrently or after UNIV 340. Freshmen and sophomores only. Exploratory designations only.

UNIV 327.title: Metacognitive Strategies for College Success
UNIV 327.subject: UNIV
UNIV 327.description: Theories of the memory processes and the application of the Information Processing Systems in developing metacognitive strategies for college classroom success.

UNIV 340.title: Academic Exploration Through Advising
UNIV 340.subject: UNIV
UNIV 340.description: Major exploration designed to assist exploratory students in the process of researching personal, career, and educational goals and the impact of these goals on the decision-making process. Emphasis on self-reflection and identity.

UNIV 350.title: Mânoa Peer Advisor Training Course
UNIV 350.subject: UNIV
UNIV 350.description: Intensive course designed for peer advisor trainees to learn General Education requirements, university policies and procedures, and campus resources. Trainees also develop skills and strategies necessary to provide quality advising to their fellow students. A-F only

UNIV 370.title: Financial Literacy Peer Educator Training Course
UNIV 370.subject: UNIV
UNIV 370.description: Intensive course designed for peer educator trainees to learn principles of personal finance, including budgeting, credit, insurance, buying a home or automobile, savings, and financing education. Trainees will develop communication, facilitation, and practical leadership skills.

UNIV 387.title: Collaborative Learning: Foundations of Tutoring
UNIV 387.subject: UNIV
UNIV 387.description: Theory and practice of collaborative learning in academic contexts. Sophomore standing or higher.

UNIV 421.title: Passages
UNIV 421.subject: UNIV
UNIV 421.description: Interactive course develops mentoring skills and relationships with peers, mentors, and “elders.” Sophomore standing or higher.

UNIV 450.title: Mânoa Peer Advisor Leader Training and Leadership Practicum
UNIV 450.subject: UNIV
UNIV 450.description: A reflective apprenticeship in which Peer Advisor Leaders solidify their understanding of advising and learn more about leadership and deepen their facilitation, communication, collaboration, and leadership skills by mentoring a cohort of peer advisor trainees.
UNIV 450.prereq_raw: 350 (or equivalent course) (with a minimum grade of B). (Summer only

children.text: ( or equivalent course) ( with a minimum grade of B ) . ( Summer only

UNIV 499.title: Directed Reading or Research
UNIV 499.subject: UNIV
UNIV 499.description: Individual reading or research. Junior standing.

UROP 399.title: Faculty Mentored Research and Creative Work Project
UROP 399.subject: UROP
UROP 399.description: Directed research for undergraduate students conducting faculty-mentored research or creative work projects.
UROP 399.prereq_raw: consent of UROP director and student faculty mentor

children.text: of UROP director and student faculty mentor

SUST 111L.title: Biology & Society Laboratory
SUST 111L.subject: SUST
SUST 111L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Explores connections between biological principles and everyday life with a focus on the environment. Topics include environmental health and sustainability with examples from Hawai‘i. Not a BIOL major elective.

SUST 112.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability
SUST 112.subject: SUST
SUST 112.description: Introduction to principles of environmental science and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning with an emphasis on sustaining resources and mitigating pollution to ecosystems.

SUST 112L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
SUST 112L.subject: SUST
SUST 112L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
SUST 112L.prereq_raw: (112 or GES 102 or OCN 102) or concurrent

SUST 113.title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
SUST 113.subject: SUST
SUST 113.description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

SUST 114.title: Sustainable Cities
SUST 114.subject: SUST
SUST 114.description: How do we plan and design cities to meet our long-term economic and environmental needs? Students will learn how sustainability applies to key urban issues like energy, transportation, land, and food.

SUST 115.title: Sustainability in a Changing World
SUST 115.subject: SUST
SUST 115.description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment.

SUST 116.title: Humans and the Environment
SUST 116.subject: SUST
SUST 116.description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

SUST 120.title: Chemistry in a Sustainable World
SUST 120.subject: SUST
SUST 120.description: Introduction to chemistry for non-science majors. Discussion of role of natural and man-made chemicals in everyday life, with an emphasis on sustainable and environmentally-sensitive use of chemicals to improve our world.

SUST 156.title: Sustainable Food and Energy Field Course
SUST 156.subject: SUST
SUST 156.description: Examines the nexus of food, energy, and water in Hawai‘i for sustainable development.

SUST 157.title: Global Environmental History
SUST 157.subject: SUST
SUST 157.description: Explores the influence of nature–climate, topography, plants, animals, and microorganisms–on human history and the way people, in turn, have influenced the natural world around them.

SUST 204.title: Historical Ecology of Hawai‘i
SUST 204.subject: SUST
SUST 204.description: The Hawaiian socio-ecosystem is the product of centuries of human land use and resource exploitation. Explores the events and processes that have shaped the islands’ ecology and future sustainability.

SUST 210.title: Introduction to Environmental Science
SUST 210.subject: SUST
SUST 210.description: Analysis of our environment with emphasis on understanding relationships and interactions of physical, biological, technological, and political components using scientific methods of inquiry. Food supply and safety, water quality, pollution control, biodiversity, environmental policy. Open to nonmajors.

SUST 211.title: Agriculture, Environment, and Society
SUST 211.subject: SUST
SUST 211.description: Relationship of plants, soils, and the environment, and how they relate to cultural practices and society in agroecosystems with an emphasis on Hawai‘i as a model system.

SUST 217.title: Hawaiian Perspectives in Ahupua‘a
SUST 217.subject: SUST
SUST 217.description: Examination of the ahupua‘a system as it was conceptualized by the ancient Hawaiians, and exploration of its relevance in modern society; an introductory class to the malama ‘aina track designed to build critical writing skills.

SUST 220.title: Agricultural and Resource Economics
SUST 220.subject: SUST
SUST 220.description: Introduction to basic economics concepts, including demand, supply, exchange, market price and market failure. Economic evaluation and policy for the uses of various natural resource endowments, especially in production agriculture, is included.

SUST 221.title: Organic Food Crop Production
SUST 221.subject: SUST
SUST 221.description: Combined lecture/lab on the theory and practice of certified organic food production. Field visits to organic farms/markets included. Open to nonmajors.

SUST 222.title: Hawaiians
SUST 222.subject: SUST
SUST 222.description: The sustainable social system, culture, spirituality, language, land stewardship, and governance of Native Hawaiians. Transformation of the sustainable Hawaiian social system by a capitalist economy. Resiliency, land issues, and Native Hawaiian quest for sovereign governance.

SUST 250.title: Introduction to Sustainability from Social Science Perspectives
SUST 250.subject: SUST
SUST 250.description: Introduction to key concepts and theories in social sciences in relation to sustainability issues.

SUST 251.title: Scientific Principles of Sustainability
SUST 251.subject: SUST
SUST 251.description: Introduction to the scientific principles of sustainability, including the ecology of managed and natural ecosystems, global change biology, ecological principles of natural resource management, renewable energy technologies, and the environmental impacts of humans.

SUST 310.title: Conservation Ethics
SUST 310.subject: SUST
SUST 310.description: Introduction to and discussion of ethical issues associated with biodiversity, ecology, and conservation biology.
SUST 310.prereq_raw: any DB course or consent. (Once a year)

SUST 311.title: Natural Resources Management
SUST 311.subject: SUST
SUST 311.description: Biological and physical science aspects of natural resource management at local, national, and global scales. Topics covered include resource management of soil, water, forests, wetlands, coasts and wildlife.
SUST 311.prereq_raw: NREM/TPSS 251 or 210; CHEM 151 or higher; and BIOL 172; or consent

SUST 312.title: Natural Resource and Environmental Policy
SUST 312.subject: SUST
SUST 312.description: Introduction to American government policy in natural resources and environmental protection at federal, Hawai‘i state and county levels. Policy principles, legal structure, governmental agencies, major statutes and programs, analytical techniques, program assessments.
SUST 312.prereq_raw: SUST/NREM/PEPS 210 or (BIOL 101 or higher) or GEO 101 or (ERTH 101 or higher); and 220/NREM 220 or one ECON course or two DS courses

SUST 313.title: Plant Conservation Biology
SUST 313.subject: SUST
SUST 313.description: Introduction to the concepts and principles of plant conservation biology and to plant conservation-in-practice in Hawai‘i and elsewhere.

SUST 313L.title: Plant Conservation Biology Lab
SUST 313L.subject: SUST
SUST 313L.description: Introduction to approaches, methods, and analyses used in the study and practice of plant conservation, with an emphasis on experimental design and problem-solving. Includes both laboratory and field components.

SUST 314.title: Global Environmental Issues
SUST 314.subject: SUST
SUST 314.description: Use and abuse of natural resources and humanity’s progress toward developing a sustainable relationship with its supporting environment. (Once a year)

SUST 315.title: Water and Society
SUST 315.subject: SUST
SUST 315.description: Interaction of people with water at household, community, regional, national, and international scales, from cultural, political, economic, and biophysical perspectives.
SUST 315.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

SUST 316.title: Environmental Ethics
SUST 316.subject: SUST
SUST 316.description: Application of traditional moral theories to environmental issues. Development and evaluation of specific environmental ethical theories. Application of ethical theories to environmental decision-making.
SUST 316.prereq_raw: 210 or GEO 101 or PHIL 101 or PHIL 103

SUST 317.title: Malama ‘Aina Resource Management Visual Technologies
SUST 317.subject: SUST
SUST 317.description: Requires a broad set of knowledge systems. Will introduce students to a variety of visual technologies for use in resource management and the ethical application of these technologies.

SUST 318.title: Race, Indigeneity, and Environmental Justice
SUST 318.subject: SUST
SUST 318.description: Introduction to environmental justice, explores the premise that all people have a right to a life-affirming environment. Will examine environmental racism, and the geographical dimensions of race and indigeneity.
SUST 318.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent

SUST 320.title: Environment and Agriculture
SUST 320.subject: SUST
SUST 320.description: Overview of environmental issues and impacts associated with agriculture, specifically pest management issues, and options for environmentally responsible management and amelioration of these impacts.

SUST 321.title: Hawai‘i and the Pacific
SUST 321.subject: SUST
SUST 321.description: Hawai‘i as part of the Pacific community: selected historical and contemporary problems of Pacific areas; cultural and economic imperialism, land alienation, and the impact of development on Pacific peoples.

SUST 322.title: Globalization and Environment
SUST 322.subject: SUST
SUST 322.description: Debates on globalization and development, population and resources; root causes of environmental degradation; impacts of globalization on environmentalism and environmental change; social approaches to managing environmental change.

SUST 323.title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
SUST 323.subject: SUST
SUST 323.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
SUST 323.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

SUST 324.title: Global Environmental Politics
SUST 324.subject: SUST
SUST 324.description: Evolution of international politics, law and decision-making on a variety of environmental concerns; from endangered species to pollution to climate change. Interaction of population, development, and environment in global governance.

SUST 325.title: Communicating Sustainability
SUST 325.subject: SUST
SUST 325.description: Application of scientific communication theory, strategic communication, and multimedia techniques to select issues of environmental sustainability.
SUST 325.prereq_raw: COM 201 (with a minimum grade of B) or consent

SUST 326.title: Geography, Environment, and Society
SUST 326.subject: SUST
SUST 326.description: Examines the geography of resources and environmental change with a holistic and multi-scale perspective. Social approaches to resolving environmental problems.

SUST 330.title: Culture and Environment
SUST 330.subject: SUST
SUST 330.description: Introduction to cultural geography, the cultural landscape, and perceptions of the environment across different cultures. Sophomore standing or higher.

SUST 332.title: Economics of Global Climate Change
SUST 332.subject: SUST
SUST 332.description: Nature and causes of global climate change and economic solutions. Topics include valuing climate change impacts, energy solutions, environmental implications, societal adaptation, and international cooperation.
SUST 332.prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

SUST 333.title: Climate Change and Cultural Response: Past, Present, and Future
SUST 333.subject: SUST
SUST 333.description: Climate change is a reality, yet there is much uncertainty about how it will affect our lives. Investigates cultural response to climate change, using studies of the past to plan for the future. (Alt. years: spring)

SUST 336.title: Energy Economics and Policy
SUST 336.subject: SUST
SUST 336.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of energy use, and interactions of markets for various nonrenewable and renewable energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop alternative energy sources.

SUST 340.title: Human Values and the Environment
SUST 340.subject: SUST
SUST 340.description: Examination of nature-culture dynamic over a range of contexts–literary ecology, systems ecology, political ecology, eco-feminism, environmental ethics–in order to articulate new possibilities for interdisciplinary understanding of the human place in nature.
SUST 340.prereq_raw: any ENG DL or PHIL or GEO course, or consent. (Once a year)

SUST 341.title: Land Tenure and Use in Hawai‘i
SUST 341.subject: SUST
SUST 341.description: Dynamics of change: indigenous Hawaiian land tenure; Great Mahele and Kuleana Act; ethnic succession of land ownership; concentration of ownership today; effects of land development on ethnic communities.

SUST 350.title: Sustainable Development
SUST 350.subject: SUST
SUST 350.description: Transdisciplinary introduction to sustainable development. Interactions between environment, economy, and public policy, especially in Hawai‘i. Topics include: curse of paradise, global warming, energy use, health, poverty, population, water resources, traffic congestion, biodiversity, pollution controls.
SUST 350.prereq_raw: 120 or 130 or 131, or consent. (Once a year)

SUST 351.title: Economic Change and Hawai‘i’s People
SUST 351.subject: SUST
SUST 351.description: Hawai‘i’s economic transformation from sustainable communal subsistence through mercantile capitalism, plantation capitalism, and global finance capital and impact on its people. Alternative sustainable enterprises for a self-sufficient island economy.

SUST 356.title: Aloha Kanaloa-Marine Resources and Abundance
SUST 356.subject: SUST
SUST 356.description: Undergraduate course exposing students to the resources and processes of the ocean, research, and management approaches, as well as a Hawaiian worldview of oceanic elements. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 358.title: Basic Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
SUST 358.subject: SUST
SUST 358.description: Fundamentals of benefit-cost analysis with extensions to environmental impacts and projects; case studies.

SUST 367.title: Sustainability, Technoscience, and Social Justice
SUST 367.subject: SUST
SUST 367.description: Examines politics of sustainability and technoscience with an explicit attention to social justice and power relations in society.
SUST 367.prereq_raw: 151 or any 200- or 300-level WS course, or 100 or any 200-level SOC course, or consent

children.text: -level WS course, or 100 or any 200 -level SOC course, or consent

SUST 371.title: Genetics: Theory to Application
SUST 371.subject: SUST
SUST 371.description: Fundamentals of genetic theory using traditional breeding and biotechnological procedures in insect and plant pathogen management for sustainable agricultural production.

SUST 380.title: Environmental Law and Politics
SUST 380.subject: SUST
SUST 380.description: Focuses on theories, laws, policies, ethics, and sustainable futures of Hawai‘i and the U.S. Sophomore standing or higher.
SUST 380.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level POLS course, or consent

SUST 387.title: Politics of the Ocean
SUST 387.subject: SUST
SUST 387.description: Study of the ocean as a political place. Engagement with theories, policies, and lived-experiences of the ocean through a political lens, including literature and experiential learning. Sophomore standing or higher.
SUST 387.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200-level POLS course, or consent

SUST 410.title: Sustainable Soil and Plant Health Management
SUST 410.subject: SUST
SUST 410.description: Provides knowledge and understanding of soils, agroecology, and sustainable approaches for plant health management, and prepares students for applied research in various tropical cropping systems. (Alt. years: spring)

SUST 411.title: Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
SUST 411.subject: SUST
SUST 411.description: Introduces fundamental techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

SUST 412.title: The Ocean Economy
SUST 412.subject: SUST
SUST 412.description: Examination of society’s interaction with the ocean. Topics include: ocean recreation, shipping, boat building, ports, offshore energy production, aquaculture, fishing, coastal construction, and coral reef protection.

SUST 413.title: Past Global Change and the Human Era
SUST 413.subject: SUST
SUST 413.description: Study of past environments to understand present and future global change. Focus on terrestrial Quaternary environments and global processes.
SUST 413.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

SUST 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
SUST 415.subject: SUST
SUST 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

SUST 416.title: Ecological Anthropology
SUST 416.subject: SUST
SUST 416.description: Relationship of humans with natural environment; role of culture in ecological systems.

SUST 420.title: Community and Natural Resource Management
SUST 420.subject: SUST
SUST 420.description: Theory and tools for working with groups and communities in the management of natural resources is presented using a participatory format. Topics include sustainable development, extension programming, participatory learning and communication, evaluation, and conflict management.
SUST 420.prereq_raw: two social science courses or consent

SUST 421.title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
SUST 421.subject: SUST
SUST 421.description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

SUST 422.title: Biocontrol of Invasive Species
SUST 422.subject: SUST
SUST 422.description: Biological control of invasive insects and weeds using natural enemies; biological control as a cornerstone of sustainable pest management; contributions of biocontrol to economic, environmental, and societal sustainability; reduced dependence on pesticides; increased sustainability of pest management.

SUST 423.title: Agriculture, Food and Society
SUST 423.subject: SUST
SUST 423.description: Examines historical and contemporary development of the global agro-food systems. The impacts of technological, political and economic changes to food security, environment and development. Open to nonmajors.
SUST 423.prereq_raw: junior standing or higher, or consent

SUST 425.title: Environmental Geochemistry
SUST 425.subject: SUST
SUST 425.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

SUST 426.title: Environment, Resources and Society
SUST 426.subject: SUST
SUST 426.description: Human interaction with the environment. How market, property institution, and technological change affect the environment. Epistemological basis of environmental policies. Debates on controversial environmental issues.

SUST 427.title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
SUST 427.subject: SUST
SUST 427.description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Junior standing or higher, or consent.

SUST 433.title: Interdisciplinary Science Curriculum
SUST 433.subject: SUST
SUST 433.description: Conceptual schemes and processes for integrating science curricula within the sciences and with subject areas. Methods and models of curricular integration such as interdisciplinary, culturally relevant, place and community-based learning.

SUST 436.title: Use, Re-use, and Radical Re-use
SUST 436.subject: SUST
SUST 436.description: Explores the related concepts of use, re-use, and radical re-use through an exploration of new applications of traditional fiber techniques and contexts of making.
SUST 436.prereq_raw: ART 113 and 116 and one 200-level or above fiber course, and consent

SUST 440.title: Vulnerability & Adaptation on Coastal Infrastructure
SUST 440.subject: SUST
SUST 440.description: Assessing vulnerability of coastal communities to climate change stressors and providing technical engineering solutions for adaptation.

SUST 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
SUST 441.subject: SUST
SUST 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

SUST 442.title: Environmental Management Systems
SUST 442.subject: SUST
SUST 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

SUST 444.title: Infrastructure: Project Impacts, Policy and Sustainability
SUST 444.subject: SUST
SUST 444.description: Evaluation of infrastructure impacts. Impacts regulation and mitigation. Effects of environmental and other policies on infrastructure. Infrastructure relations to sustainability. Energy consumption, transportation efficiency and infrastructure recycling. Lectures and presentations by experts and enrolled students. Senior standing or higher.
SUST 444.prereq_raw: senior standing, open to engineering, science, urban planning, and economics majors

children.text: open to engineering, science, urban planning,

SUST 445.title: Ethnoecology and Conservation
SUST 445.subject: SUST
SUST 445.description: Ecological implications of cultural uses of plants. Examines the biological basis for, and ecological effects of traditional and local resource management systems.

SUST 446.title: Hawaiian Ethnobotany
SUST 446.subject: SUST
SUST 446.description: Methods and techniques of handling and identifying plant materials used by early Hawaiians and modern Hawaiians for house and canoe construction, clothing, household and fishing items, medicine, and food preparation. Reading, laboratory, and fieldwork.

SUST 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis and Applications
SUST 449.subject: SUST
SUST 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.
SUST 449.restrictions_raw: ATMO, CEE, ERTH, GES, OCN, NREM majors only.

SUST 450.title: Natural History of Hawaiian Islands
SUST 450.subject: SUST
SUST 450.description: Geography, geology, climatology, biotic environment of Pacific Basin and Hawaiian Islands; endemism and evolution in terrestrial and marine biota.
SUST 450.prereq_raw: one semester of biological sciences at college level

prereq_tree.text: one semester of biological sciences at college level

SUST 451.title: Wildlife Ecology and Management
SUST 451.subject: SUST
SUST 451.description: Lecture-based overview of the history, ecology, and management of wildlife species from around the world and Hawai‘i.

SUST 455.title: Hawaiian Sovereignty in Pacific Context
SUST 455.subject: SUST
SUST 455.description: Causes and dynamics of ethnic conflicts with attention to problem resolution; (B) Middle East; (C) Hawaiian sovereignty in Pacific context.
SUST 455.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course, or consent for (C)

SUST 456.title: Natural Resource Issues and Ethics
SUST 456.subject: SUST
SUST 456.description: Overview of the history of land, resources and power in Hawai‘i; players and processes influencing land and natural resources policies today explored from Native Hawaiian and other viewpoints. Extensive use of case studies.

SUST 457.title: ‘Aina Mauliola: Hawaiian Ecosystems
SUST 457.subject: SUST
SUST 457.description: Comprehensive analysis of traditional Hawaiian and modern resource management practices. Rigorous overview of the dominant physical and biological processes from the uplands to the oceans in Hawai‘i.

SUST 458.title: Project Evaluation and Resource Management
SUST 458.subject: SUST
SUST 458.description: Principles of project evaluation and policy analysis. Shadow pricing, economic cost of taxes and tariffs; public policy for exhaustible, renewable, and environmental resources.

SUST 459.title: Strategies in Hawaiian Resource Use
SUST 459.subject: SUST
SUST 459.description: Analyzing diverse land and water use strategies of O‘ahu, from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives, through classroom and on-site lectures. Topics include traditional Hawaiian methods, modern development, threatened ecosystems, ecotourism and scientific research.

SUST 460.title: Hui Konohiki Practicum
SUST 460.subject: SUST
