SUST 460.description: A “hands-on” internship in an environmental or resource-management organization in Hawai‘i. The experience will be broadened and supplemented by classroom lectures, discussion and analysis from traditional Hawaiian, scientific and economic perspectives.

SUST 461.title: Global Ethnic Conflict
SUST 461.subject: SUST
SUST 461.description: Ethnic conflicts cause most wars on our globe today. Examines causes of ethnic conflict, including climate change. Will evaluate approaches to building peaceful relations between groups and developing sustainable relationships with the environment. Junior standing or higher.
SUST 461.prereq_raw: one DS or DH course or consent

SUST 480.title: Applied Forest Ecology
SUST 480.subject: SUST
SUST 480.description: Application of ecological theory to sustainable management of forest resources in Hawaii and beyond, including silviculture (production of timber and nontimber forest products), restoration (restoring damaged or degraded forests), and conservation (conserving existing forest resources).

SUST 481.title: American Environmental History
SUST 481.subject: SUST
SUST 481.description: Survey history of the complex relations between American societies and diverse U.S. ecosystems, from European contact and colonization to the present.

SUST 482.title: Anthropology and the Environment: Culture, Power, and Politics
SUST 482.subject: SUST
SUST 482.description: Investigates environmental problems from an anthropological perspective, and examines the cultural politics of contestations over resources, rights, and the meanings of nature.

SUST 494.title: Environmental Problem Solving
SUST 494.subject: SUST
SUST 494.description: Senior-level capstone for NREM and related majors. Ecosystem management within problemsolving context. Applications of research and analytical methods, management tools to case studies. Focus on student teamwork and oral communications.

SUST 495.title: Sustainability Capstone
SUST 495.subject: SUST
SUST 495.description: Capstone for undergraduate students in interdisciplinary studies focusing on sustainability. The capstone experience provides an opportunity for students to gain knowledge and research experience in an applied setting.

SUST 496.title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
SUST 496.subject: SUST
SUST 496.description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

SUST 608.title: Literacy Across the Disciplines
SUST 608.subject: SUST
SUST 608.description: Explores theoretical and practical principles of literacy and sustainability across academic disciplines, investigating the role of language and literate practices of reading, writing, speaking, visualizing, and representing in social, cultural, and educational contexts. Graduate students only.

SUST 610.title: Seminar on Water in History
SUST 610.subject: SUST
SUST 610.description: Explores how various forms of salt, fresh, and brackish water have played transformative roles in the evolution of human communities throughout history.

SUST 611.title: Resource and Environmental Policy Analysis
SUST 611.subject: SUST
SUST 611.description: Exploration of institutional and policy dimensions of natural resource development, management, allocation, markets and pricing, focusing on their environmental impacts. Emphasis on policy analysis using case studies and empirical findings. Original paper required.
SUST 611.prereq_raw: grade of Cor above in ECON 130 or NREM/SUST 220, or consent

children.text: grade of Cor above in ECON 130

SUST 612.title: Predicting and Controlling Degradation in Human-Dominated Terrestrial Ecosystems
SUST 612.subject: SUST
SUST 612.description: Historic, present, and projected trends in understanding and managing human-dominated ecosystems; predicting, measuring and mitigating degradation especially in terrestrial ecosystems with a focus on small volcanic islands in tropical settings.
SUST 612.prereq_raw: NREM 301/SUST 311 and NREM 304 (or equivalent) and NREM 600. Recommended NREM 461, or consent

children.text: ( or equivalent) and NREM 600 . Recommended NREM 461 , or consent

SUST 613.title: Advanced Methods in Wildlife Management & Conservation
SUST 613.subject: SUST
SUST 613.description: Introduces advanced techniques for wildlife management and conservation. In addition to hands-on training, students will learn underlying biological and ecological principles, as well as quantitative skills, with an emphasis on sustainable management.

SUST 620.title: Environmental Planning and Policy
SUST 620.subject: SUST
SUST 620.description: Overview of urbanization and environmental change. An examination of environmental laws, policies, planning and urban design strategies designed to minimize and mitigate urban impacts.

SUST 623.title: Science and Science Curriculum, PK-12
SUST 623.subject: SUST
SUST 623.description: Application of recent developments in science, sustainability, curriculum development, and learning theory to pre-kindergarten through secondary school. Science philosophy, content and methodology stressed, including inquiry, nature of science, sustainability, and science literacy.

SUST 625.title: Climate Change, Energy and Food Security in the Asia/Pacific Region
SUST 625.subject: SUST
SUST 625.description: Analysis of planning responses to human-induced climate change and related environmental problems. Part of the Asia/Pacific Initiative taught in collaboration with universities throughout the region via videoconferencing.

SUST 628.title: Urban Environmental Problems
SUST 628.subject: SUST
SUST 628.description: Seminar that examines environmental problems associated with urbanization. Reviews strategic approaches and collaboration among key actors to address such problems.

SUST 632.title: Planning in Hawai‘i and Pacific Islands
SUST 632.subject: SUST
SUST 632.description: Urban and regional planning in island settings. Experiences in Hawai‘i, Polynesia, Melanesia, and Micronesia.

SUST 636.title: Renewable Energy Economics and Policy
SUST 636.subject: SUST
SUST 636.description: Analysis of economic and policy aspects of renewable energy use, and interactions of markets for renewable energy and other energy options. Evaluations of policies to develop renewable energy options.
SUST 636.prereq_raw: college calculus and principles of microeconomics; or consent

SUST 637.title: Resource Economics
SUST 637.subject: SUST
SUST 637.description: Analysis of problems of development and management of natural resources with emphasis on resources in agriculture and role in economic development.

SUST 638.title: Environmental Resource Economics
SUST 638.subject: SUST
SUST 638.description: Principles of policy design and evaluation for environmental resources management, forestry and watershed conservation, and sustainable economic development.

SUST 640.title: Land Systems Science
SUST 640.subject: SUST
SUST 640.description: Through discussion of primary land systems science literature and use of environmental modeling software, this interdisciplinary course explores how drivers, states, and trends in human appropriation of land affect socio-ecological system function.
SUST 640.prereq_raw: NREM 477 or NREM 677 or GEO 470 or GEO 476 or ERTH 460 or ERTH 461

SUST 647.title: Urban and Regional Planning for Sustainability
SUST 647.subject: SUST
SUST 647.description: Focus on ideology, conceptual models, accounting frameworks, appropriate technologies, and indicators of planning for sustainability. Central and local policies, plans, and best practices in various countries and settings will be covered. Graduate students only.

SUST 652.title: Kanawai Lawai‘a: Hawa‘i’s Ocean and Fisheries Laws
SUST 652.subject: SUST
SUST 652.description: Seminar on pre-contact, customary laws on fishing and ocean stewardship, their codification in written laws during the Hawaiian Kingdom period, and changes and impacts through U.S. annexation and statehood, including current models of ocean governance. (Alt. years: Fall)

SUST 658.title: Advanced Environmental Benefit Cost Analysis
SUST 658.subject: SUST
SUST 658.description: Advanced environmental benefit-cost analysis will require that proficiency be demonstrated on fundamentals and address topics related to sustainability, including income equality, non-market goods, risk, cost of public funds, and the social discount rate.

SUST 661.title: Hawaiian Vascular Plants
SUST 661.subject: SUST
SUST 661.description: Identification, systematics, evolution, and biogeography of native plants. Field trips.

SUST 670.title: Sociology of Sustainability
SUST 670.subject: SUST
SUST 670.description: Analyses of sustainability, environmental, and technoscience issues from sociological perspectives. Graduate students only.

SUST 677.title: Marine Renewable Energy
SUST 677.subject: SUST
SUST 677.description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.
SUST 677.prereq_raw: ORE 607; basic knowledge of thermodynamics desirable

SUST 696.title: Sustainability & Resilience Seminar
SUST 696.subject: SUST
SUST 696.description: Weekly seminar covering research, processes, and initiatives related to sustainability and resilience in practice. The intent is to foster intellectual engagement and to help and encourage students to spawn their own original research ideas.

ASAN 101.title: Introduction to Asian Studies
ASAN 101.subject: ASAN
ASAN 101.description: Introductory course focuses on change and continuity in the history, culture, values, and political institutions of South, East, and Southeast Asia, and the region’s interrelationships with the rest of the world.

ASAN 201.title: Introduction to Asian Studies: East Asia
ASAN 201.subject: ASAN
ASAN 201.description: Understanding East Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

ASAN 202.title: Introduction to Asian Studies: South/ Southeast Asia
ASAN 202.subject: ASAN
ASAN 202.description: Understanding South and Southeast Asia through multidisciplinary approaches. Examines the interrelationship of policies, economy, literature, religion, the arts, and history as the basis for such an understanding.

ASAN 308.title: Chinese Political Economy
ASAN 308.subject: ASAN
ASAN 308.description: Interdisciplinary review and analysis of the social and political issues in contemporary China, the interchange between state and society in national policies, the relationship between cultural tradition and technological modernization in the social transformation process.
ASAN 308.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

ASAN 310.title: Asian Humanities
ASAN 310.subject: ASAN
ASAN 310.description: Multidisciplinary. Classics of literature, philosophy, and religion shaping Asian beliefs and values.

ASAN 312.title: Contemporary Asian Civilization
ASAN 312.subject: ASAN
ASAN 312.description: Multidisciplinary examination of problems and issues affecting peoples and institutions of contemporary Asia: ethnic, language, religious, and cultural differences; population growth; public health; economic development; political and social change; environmental problems; etc.

ASAN 323.title: The Way of Tea in Japanese History and Culture
ASAN 323.subject: ASAN
ASAN 323.description: History and culture of Japan as revealed in study and practice of tea ceremony: Zen, aesthetics, calligraphy, architecture, ceramics, gardens, politics.

ASAN 324.title: Chado-the Way of Tea Practicum
ASAN 324.subject: ASAN
ASAN 324.description: Actual practice of the tea ceremony as history and culture of Japan.

ASAN 330.title: Chinese Film: Art and History
ASAN 330.subject: ASAN
ASAN 330.description: Study and analysis of Chinese film; its history and relationship to cultural, social, philosophical, and aesthetic contexts.

ASAN 356.title: Geography of Southeast Asia
ASAN 356.subject: ASAN
ASAN 356.description: An investigation of the development context of Southeast Asia including socioeconomic, cultural, and environmental resources. Problems and prospects for change.

ASAN 360.title: Buddhist Philosophy
ASAN 360.subject: ASAN
ASAN 360.description: Survey of central thinkers and schools.

ASAN 361.title: Southeast Asian Literature in Translation
ASAN 361.subject: ASAN
ASAN 361.description: Survey in English traditional and modern literatures of Southeast Asia.

ASAN 364.title: 20th-Century Chinese Women Writers
ASAN 364.subject: ASAN
ASAN 364.description: A survey and critical examination of contemporary Chinese women writers from China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong. Traces a genealogy of women’s writing from the early 1920s up until now through novels, poetry, drama, and film.
ASAN 364.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course, or consent

ASAN 406.title: Modern Philippines
ASAN 406.subject: ASAN
ASAN 406.description: Survey of major developments from pre-colonial through Spanish and American colonial periods, the revolution, Japanese occupation, and post-war republic.

ASAN 407.title: Peace Processes in Philippines and Hawai‘i
ASAN 407.subject: ASAN
ASAN 407.description: History of Philippine Islam and the Moro struggle, the peace process in Mindanao and sovereignty movement for Hawaiian nation. 75 min. Lec, 75-min. joint online discussion with Philippine students. Junior standing only.

ASAN 410.title: Gender and Politics in U.S.-Okinawa Relations
ASAN 410.subject: ASAN
ASAN 410.description: Examines gender in Okinawa in relation to historical dynamics in the Asia-Pacific region with attention to issues such as militarism and violence, colonialism and memory, and tourism and commodification of indigenous culture.

ASAN 411.title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
ASAN 411.subject: ASAN
ASAN 411.description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies. (Alt. years)

ASAN 420.title: Korean Cinema
ASAN 420.subject: ASAN
ASAN 420.description: Develop an understanding of Korean culture and society through visual, narrative, and contextual analysis of Korean films. Topics include post-Korean War experience, compressed modernity, authoritarianism, and postauthoritarian transformation. Special attention to independent films.

ASAN 422.title: Contested Issues Korea and Japan
ASAN 422.subject: ASAN
ASAN 422.description: In-depth understanding of Korean-Japanese relations in the past and present by examining conflicting views and interpretations by Japanese, Korean, and Western scholars on important issues that divide the people of East Asia.

ASAN 438.title: Sustainable Asian Development: Impact of Globalization
ASAN 438.subject: ASAN
ASAN 438.description: Investigates the impact of globalization on sustainable development in Asia. Globalization and sustainability often contradict, raising serious planning issues. Examines how these issues affect Asian development policies and urban planning.

ASAN 442.title: Globalization and Identity in the Himalayas
ASAN 442.subject: ASAN
ASAN 442.description: Examines the influence of local culture and global flows on identity formation in the Himalayan region. Topics include: Hindu caste and gender, constructions of ethnicity, Tibetans and tourists, Sherpas and mountaineers, development ideologies, and consumerism.
ASAN 442.prereq_raw: 202 or ANTH 152 or ANTH 301 or consent

ASAN 449.title: Asian Cities: Evolution of Urban Space
ASAN 449.subject: ASAN
ASAN 449.description: Reviews the evolution of Asian urban space. Political history, migration, culture, and production are the determinants of urban changes. Uses visual material to illustrate the change in Asian cityscape.
ASAN 449.prereq_raw: 310 or PLAN 310 or ASAN 312, or consent

ASAN 462.title: Contested Issues in Contemporary Japan
ASAN 462.subject: ASAN
ASAN 462.description: Familiarizes students with public discourse in Japan by analyzing key current issues widely debated in the Japanese media and in public forums in light of their political, historical, cultural, social and economic contexts. Previous course work related to Japan or Asia will be helpful.

ASAN 463.title: Gender Issues in Asian Society
ASAN 463.subject: ASAN
ASAN 463.description: Construction of gender identities in contemporary Asia. How these interface with other aspects of social difference and inequality (e.g., with class, religion, ethnicity).

ASAN 464.title: K-pop and J-pop: Korean and Japanese Popular Music and Society
ASAN 464.subject: ASAN
ASAN 464.description: Examines modern Japan and South Korea through popular music. Examines genres from early popular music, today’s K-pop and J-pop music.

ASAN 465.title: Japan Cool: Anime, Manga, and Film
ASAN 465.subject: ASAN
ASAN 465.description: Focus on the world of Japanese anime, manga, and films. What can one learn about Japan from these products? Focus on issues of gender, national identity, and race.

ASAN 469.title: Ethnic Diversity in China
ASAN 469.subject: ASAN
ASAN 469.description: Surveying Tibetans, Mongols, Manchus, Muslims, and other minorities, as well as analyzing the nature of minority/ majority identity in China from an anthropological perspective.

ASAN 470.title: Sustainable Development in East Asia
ASAN 470.subject: ASAN
ASAN 470.description: Interdisciplinary investigation of development in East Asia is an urgent issue. Status and role of Asian business; current technological, economic, and financial developments; impact on world economy.

ASAN 471.title: Introduction to Contemporary Asian Cinema
ASAN 471.subject: ASAN
ASAN 471.description: Acquaint students with significant films from the major countries in Asia and how these films reflect and comment on profound social, political, and historical changes that have occurred in recent decades.

ASAN 473.title: Topics in Chinese Cultural Studies: Visual Culture–Chinese Diaspora
ASAN 473.subject: ASAN
ASAN 473.description: Multidisciplinary and historically located study of Chinese culture through the examination of literary/visual texts and critical essays from cultural studies. Specific topics will depend upon term.
ASAN 473.prereq_raw: one DH or DL course or consent

ASAN 474.title: Transnational Chinese Popular Culture
ASAN 474.subject: ASAN
ASAN 474.description: Survey of contemporary Chinese popular entertainment forms that are produced and appreciated transnationally. Examples include martial arts genres, kung fu films, commercial novels, ballroom dancing, karaoke culture, music videos and rock music. Material will be selected based upon availability and readings will include critical essays from the fields of popular culture, media studies, and literary criticism.
ASAN 474.prereq_raw: any 300- or 400-level DL or DH course

ASAN 478.title: Music Cultures: India
ASAN 478.subject: ASAN
ASAN 478.description: Approaches the cultural study of music and performance through a specific focus on South Asia.

ASAN 480.title: Culture and Economy of Southeast Asia
ASAN 480.subject: ASAN
ASAN 480.description: An exploration of the cultural and economic development of the countries of Southeast Asia from early times to the present day, with an emphasis on the effects of outside influences.

ASAN 481.title: Film, Culture, and Modernity in Southeast Asia
ASAN 481.subject: ASAN
ASAN 481.description: Examines interplay between tradition and modernity; religion and secularism; individual and collective; youth, wisdom, and the world; and role of gender identification/community response as they find articulation in medium of film across Southeast Asia.

ASAN 482.title: Asia Through Fiction
ASAN 482.subject: ASAN
ASAN 482.description: Explores core values and cultural principles of the four major Asian region as represented in major works of fiction from those regions.

ASAN 483.title: Imperialism, Colonialism, and Nationalism in Southeast Asia
ASAN 483.subject: ASAN
ASAN 483.description: Theoretical and historical analysis of a global, nineteenth, and twentieth century phenomenon using an interdisciplinary approach organized around lectures, readings, and discussions.

ASAN 485.title: Contemporary Chinese Development
ASAN 485.subject: ASAN
ASAN 485.description: Development and planning in contemporary China: economic policy and institutional structure in the development and urbanization process; urban and rural transformation in a socialist economy.

ASAN 492.title: Women and Revolution
ASAN 492.subject: ASAN
ASAN 492.description: Conditions under which women’s activism and participation in protest and revolutionary movements developed in the 19th- and 20th-centuries. Cross-cultural comparisons

ASAN 493.title: Globalization in Asia
ASAN 493.subject: ASAN
ASAN 493.description: Globalization affects the economic, political, and cultural lives of people in Asia. Transformations by capitalism in agricultural and industrial sectors of contemporary societies. Perspective is historical and global; approach is interdisciplinary.

ASAN 494.title: Food, Culture, and Politics in Asia
ASAN 494.subject: ASAN
ASAN 494.description: Examines Asia’s role in the development of global foodways. Topics include the relationship between spices and imperialism, global popularity of Asian cuisines, Asian-influenced “hapa” cuisine in Hawai‘i, McDonaldization in Asia, and food security and sustainability.

ASAN 495.title: Encountering Tourism in Asian-Pacific Societies
ASAN 495.subject: ASAN
ASAN 495.description: A critical examination and current impact of tourism on contemporary Asian and Pacific Island societies. Topics include colonial antecedents, social impacts, cultural and environmental concerns, case studies (including Hawai‘i).

ASAN 496.title: Religions of Island Southeast Asia
ASAN 496.subject: ASAN
ASAN 496.description: A comparative, interdisciplinary examination of indigenous beliefs, Islam, Christianity, and Hinduism in island Southeast Asia, and how they have been adjusted because of economic and social change.

ASAN 600.title: Approaches to Asian Studies
ASAN 600.subject: ASAN
ASAN 600.description: Major issues in and approaches to the interdisciplinary study of Asia and Asian regions; resources for the advanced study of Asia at UH; developing a research focus; preparing and presenting research proposals. (C) China; (I) South Asia; (J) Japan; (K) Korea; (P) Philippines; (S) Southeast Asia; (Z) Inter-Asia.

ASAN 608.title: Politics and Development: China
ASAN 608.subject: ASAN
ASAN 608.description: Consists of three parts: key theories for socialist transition as basis for seminar discussion, policy evolution to illustrate the radical changes, and emerging and prominent current development and practice.

ASAN 611.title: Comparative Muslim Societies in Asia
ASAN 611.subject: ASAN
ASAN 611.description: Will compare Muslim societies and cultures in Asia with each other and with the so-called “core” Middle Eastern Muslim societies.

ASAN 612.title: Topics in 20th Century Chinese Literary and Cultural Studies
ASAN 612.subject: ASAN
ASAN 612.description: Critical scholarship in Chinese literature and cultural studies, broadly defined to include the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, and others. Reading knowledge of Chinese desirable but not required.

ASAN 618.title: Contemporary China: Development and Culture
ASAN 618.subject: ASAN
ASAN 618.description: Selected topics on contemporary China. Center for Chinese Studies has details of current offering.

ASAN 620.title: Problems/Issues of Contemporary Asia
ASAN 620.subject: ASAN
ASAN 620.description: Analysis from multidisciplinary perspective: rural development, urbanization, international relations, ethnicity, religion, language, etc.

ASAN 623.title: Gender in Asian Performing Arts
ASAN 623.subject: ASAN
ASAN 623.description: Performance is a rich site for gender construction, critique, and articulation in Asia. This seminar examines gender reflected in traditional music, dance, and theatre, including character role and performer persona; approaches of performance and culture studies, and an “Asian way.” (Once a year

ASAN 624.title: Culture and Colonialism
ASAN 624.subject: ASAN
ASAN 624.description: Analysis of theories and debates (cultural studies, feminist writings, post-colonial issues). Case studies of the transformation and creation of “traditional” cultures under colonialism.

ASAN 625.title: Comparative Development in East and Southeast Asia
ASAN 625.subject: ASAN
ASAN 625.description: Comparative developmental analysis of Asia’s leading economic powers. Considers Japanese political and economic developmental model; discusses problems for continued Asian growth; examines Korea, Taiwan, China, Indonesia, Thailand, Philippines and other Asian nations.

ASAN 626.title: Capitalism in Contemporary Asia
ASAN 626.subject: ASAN
ASAN 626.description: Historically grounded theoretical examination of capitalism in 20th-century Asia; multidisciplinary approach to fundamental change in political and economic structures and institutions, prospects for the future.

ASAN 627.title: Ethnic Nationalism in Asia
ASAN 627.subject: ASAN
ASAN 627.description: Contemporary theories of ethnic and cultural nationalism from perspective of Asia. Issues of nationstate, power hierarchies, modernity, and identity in contemporary societies.

ASAN 628.title: Southeast Asian Development: Costs and Benefits
ASAN 628.subject: ASAN
ASAN 628.description: Interdisciplinary approach to broad economic, social, and political issues. Focus on benefits and costs of economic development and effects on local cultures. Exploration of dilemmas of modernization and comparison of societal responses to development.

ASAN 629.title: Asian Security Cultures
ASAN 629.subject: ASAN
ASAN 629.description: Comparative study of conceptualizations, practices and institutions of national security in Asia in light of their geographic and historic contexts.

ASAN 630.title: Southeast Asia Now
ASAN 630.subject: ASAN
ASAN 630.description: Examines the ways global influences are shaping the cultural developments in the diverse societies of contemporary Southeast Asia.

ASAN 633.title: Seafood in Southeast Asia
ASAN 633.subject: ASAN
ASAN 633.description: Seafood production in Southeast Asia, including both regional fisheries and aquaculture. Case studies used to illustrate challenges to the implementation of sustainable seafood production and emerging approaches, such as community supported seafood.

ASAN 636.title: Culture & Urban Form in Asia
ASAN 636.subject: ASAN
ASAN 636.description: Cultural and historical impact on urban form, contention of tradition and modernity in urban space, spatial expression of state and society, perception and utilization of urban design, evolution of urban form in selected Asian capitals.

ASAN 638.title: Asian Development and Urbanization
ASAN 638.subject: ASAN
ASAN 638.description: Theories of globalization and sustainability in development, impacts of globalization and sustainability on development planning and policy formation, selected case studies of Asia-Pacific development.
ASAN 638.prereq_raw: (600 or PLAN 630) with a grade of B or above

ASAN 640.title: Topics in Japanese Literature
ASAN 640.subject: ASAN
ASAN 640.description: Intensive study of selected topics in Japanese literature, primarily of the modern period. English translations of original texts will be provided whenever available.

ASAN 649.title: Asian Cities: Historical Evolution of Urban Form
ASAN 649.subject: ASAN
ASAN 649.description: Examination of the impact of economy, society, and history on urban form; case studies of the evolution of Asian urban form.

ASAN 650.title: Marriage and Family in East Asia
ASAN 650.subject: ASAN
ASAN 650.description: Examines gendered/generational practices, expectations, and ideologies of marriage, childrearing, and caregiving; state’s role in legitimizing certain kinds of families; how transnational marriage migration is changing notions of belonging, relatedness, and national identity in East Asia. Graduate standing or consent.

ASAN 651.title: East Asia Now
ASAN 651.subject: ASAN
ASAN 651.description: Views East Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic and political themes including various experiences with the West. Focus upon present state of the region.

ASAN 652.title: Contemporary Japanese Studies Seminar
ASAN 652.subject: ASAN
ASAN 652.description: Selected human and physical features that represent economic, social, and political life.

ASAN 653.title: Major Authors in Modern Korean Literature
ASAN 653.subject: ASAN
ASAN 653.description: Advanced study of major Korean fiction writers from the 1910s to the present with emphasis on critical reading of their lives and writings to arrive at informed appraisal of their contribution to modern Korean literature.

ASAN 654.title: South Asia Now
ASAN 654.subject: ASAN
ASAN 654.description: Views South Asia as an interactive region. Examines common historical and cultural, economic, and political themes, including global interactions. Focus upon present state of the region. Graduate students only.

ASAN 658.title: Telecom and the Internet in East Asia
ASAN 658.subject: ASAN
ASAN 658.description: Offers interdisciplinary approach to study of internet and telecommunications in East Asia. Examines growth and development of telecommunications networks in China, Japan, South and North Korea. Focuses on contemporary social media and government policy. (Alt. years: spring)

ASAN 664.title: Topics and Issues in Modern Korean Literature
ASAN 664.subject: ASAN
ASAN 664.description: Intensive study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary Korean fiction, focusing on texts that problematize critical sociocultural issues in the evolving contexts of modern Korean intellectual history.

ASAN 665.title: Special Topics in East Asian Literary Culture & Society
ASAN 665.subject: ASAN
ASAN 665.description: In-depth study of selected topics and issues in modern/contemporary East Asian literary and cultural studies using an interdisciplinary, inter-regional, and transnational approach, from an intercultural perspective.

ASAN 671.title: The Splendor that was Southeast Asia
ASAN 671.subject: ASAN
ASAN 671.description: Interdisciplinary examination of the classical civilizations of Southeast Asia, the 9th to 14th centuries. Includes Pagan, Sukhothai, Angkor, Dai Viet, Srivijaya, and Majapahit. Considers historical themes and patterns, issues in Southeast Asian studies.

ASAN 686.title: Law and Society in China
ASAN 686.subject: ASAN
ASAN 686.description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

ASAN 687.title: Conflict and Cooperation in Asia
ASAN 687.subject: ASAN
ASAN 687.description: Explores conflict and cooperation among Asian nations. Topics may include economic integration, business networks, space and cyberspace, military alliances, territorial disputes, transnational crime, environmental cooperation, soft power, and regional institutional architecture. Graduate students only.

ASAN 688.title: China’s International Relations
ASAN 688.subject: ASAN
ASAN 688.description: Examination of China’s rise and world view, review of China’s regional relations, China and U.S. relations, formation of a new world order.

ASAN 689.title: International Relations in Asia
ASAN 689.subject: ASAN
ASAN 689.description: How well do international relations theories explain interstate relations in Asia? How do international issues interact with domestic politics? Covers Japan, China, Korea, ASEAN nations, India, and touches on Russia, Australia, and New Zealand. Graduate students only.

ASAN 693.title: Field Study in Asia
ASAN 693.subject: ASAN
ASAN 693.description: With prior consent and supervision of an Asian Studies faculty, students design, conduct, and write the results of a field research project. Graduate students only.

ASAN 694.title: Topics in Buddhist Studies
ASAN 694.subject: ASAN
ASAN 694.description: Seminar on selected topics in Buddhist studies.
ASAN 694.prereq_raw: PHIL 360, PHIL 406, REL 475, or REL 490; or consent

ASAN 695.title: Asian Studies Master’s Plan B Culminating Experience
ASAN 695.subject: ASAN
ASAN 695.description: Students work with their advisor to select, revise, and defend a portfolio of work produced in seminars before a three-person faculty committee. Graduate students only.

ASAN 705.title: Asian Research Materials and Methods
ASAN 705.subject: ASAN
ASAN 705.description: Bibliography, reference tools, and research methods in sources on Asia in Western and Asian languages. Discussion of published and archival repositories.

ASAN 710.title: MAIA Capstone
ASAN 710.subject: ASAN
ASAN 710.description: Capstone experience for MAIA students that emphasizes practical applications of Asia knowledge. Develop an Asiarelated project necessary for career goals, or work with a professional partner to address well-defined, realworld problem. Graduate students only.

ASAN 792.title: Orientalism and Visual Culture
ASAN 792.subject: ASAN
ASAN 792.description: Investigates artistic representations, appropriations, and exchanges constructed on the basis of East/Orient vs. West/Occident differences. Includes analysis of: Orientalizing artistic traditions throughout history, history and concept of Orient, post-colonial critique of Orientalism.

PACS 108.title: Pacific Worlds: An Introduction to Pacific Islands Studies
PACS 108.subject: PACS
PACS 108.description: Introduces students to the geography, societies, histories, cultures, contemporary issues, and arts of Oceania, including Hawai‘i. Combines lectures and discussion that emphasize Pacific Islander perspectives and experiences.

PACS 201.title: Islands of Globalization
PACS 201.subject: PACS
PACS 201.description: Combined lectures, service-learning. Examines the nature and impact of globalization on Pacific Island societies, viewed from the perspective of islanders who engage with global forces and processes, and create strategies to survive. Limit 20 students.

PACS 202.title: Pacific Islands Movement and Migration
PACS 202.subject: PACS
PACS 202.description: Combined lecture and service-learning activities. Examines the diaspora of Pacific Islanders. Includes a service-learning activity examining cultural, political, and economic status of groups of Pacific Islanders living in other Pacific places. Limit of 20 students.

PACS 203.title: Arts in Oceania–An Introduction
PACS 203.subject: PACS
PACS 203.description: Practical and theoretical study of arts in Oceania in relevant cultural contexts.

PACS 301.title: Pacific Communities in Hawai‘i
PACS 301.subject: PACS
PACS 301.description: Examines Pacific Islander communities’ experiences in Hawai‘i through service learning, reading, writing, lecture, and discussion. Concerns about housing, employment, education, health, language, and culture are central.

PACS 302.title: Contemporary Issues in Oceania
PACS 302.subject: PACS
PACS 302.description: Combined lecture/discussion. Examination of critical political, social, and economic issues in the Pacific Islands region today.

PACS 303.title: Thinking Through Pacific Arts, Ritual, and Performance
PACS 303.subject: PACS
PACS 303.description: Lecture, discussion, and workshop series surveys arts, ritual, and performance practices throughout the Pacific. Engaging with Pacific traditions of thought, and creative approaches to research, students also return findings to Pacific communities.

PACS 371.title: Literature of the Pacific
PACS 371.subject: PACS
PACS 371.description: Basic concepts and representative texts for the study of the literature of the Pacific, including Pacific voyagers and contemporary writings in English by Pacific Islanders.
PACS 371.prereq_raw: one ENG DL course or consent

PACS 401.title: Senior Capstone
PACS 401.subject: PACS
PACS 401.description: Capstone for Pacific Islands Studies students to engage in intensive collaborative research with a Pacific Islander community in Hawai‘i, culminating in a research paper and public presentation.

PACS 462.title: Drama and Theatre of Oceania
PACS 462.subject: PACS
PACS 462.description: Survey of the contemporary drama and theatre of Oceania that combines island and Western traditions. Includes Papua New Guinea, Hawai‘i, Fiji, Samoa, Australia, New Zealand.

PACS 474.title: Studies in Hawaiian and/or Pacific Literature
PACS 474.subject: PACS
PACS 474.description: Intensive study of selected questions, issues, traditions, writers, movements, or genres in the field of Pacific literature.
PACS 474.prereq_raw: ENG 320 and one other 300-level ENG course

PACS 493.title: Moving Images in the Pacific Islands
PACS 493.subject: PACS
PACS 493.description: Critically examines indigenous and foreign representations of the Pacific Islands and is designed to make film a central focus of inquiry for students interested in the contemporary Pacific.

PACS 494.title: Culture and Consumption in Oceania
PACS 494.subject: PACS
PACS 494.description: Lecture on changing patterns of consumption in Oceania, and the historical, political, cultural, artistic, and economic forces shaping such practices.

PACS 495.title: Encountering Tourism in AsianPacific Societies
PACS 495.subject: PACS
PACS 495.description: A critical examination of a wide spectrum of issues relating to the evolution and current impact of tourism on contemporary Asian and Pacific Islands societies. Topics include colonial antecedents, social impacts, cultural and environmental concerns, case studies (including Hawai‘i).

PACS 601.title: Learning Oceania
PACS 601.subject: PACS
PACS 601.description: Graduate seminar. Introduction to the nature and origins of Pacific Studies as an organized field of study. Epistemological, conceptual, political and ethical issues facing students of the region today.

PACS 602.title: Re/Presenting Oceania: Pacific and American Perspectives
PACS 602.subject: PACS
PACS 602.description: Graduate seminar. Critical analysis of the way physical, social and cultural aspects of Oceania have been represented in scholarly and popular media.

PACS 603.title: Researching Oceania: Creative and Conventional Methods of Inquiry
PACS 603.subject: PACS
PACS 603.description: Graduate seminar. Literacy, theory and method in the creation of a Master’s research project.

PACS 640.title: Women in Oceania
PACS 640.subject: PACS
PACS 640.description: Will look at feminist theory, ethnography, culture, activism and globalization in the context of writing, research and film on or by Women in Oceania.

PACS 690.title: Graduate Seminar: Change in the Pacific
PACS 690.subject: PACS
PACS 690.description: Interrelationship of change in selected Pacific Islands regions, institutions, and processes.

PACS 695.title: Master’s Portfolio Project
PACS 695.subject: PACS
PACS 695.description: Independent study for students working on MA portfolio projects. A grade of satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

AS 101.title: Foundations of the United States Air Force
AS 101.subject: AS
AS 101.description: Study of the total force structure, strategic offensive and defensive, general purpose, and aerospace support forces of the Air Force in the contemporary world.

AS 101L.title: Initial Military Training I
AS 101L.subject: AS
AS 101L.description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps. Course is open to all majors.

AS 102.title: Foundations of the United States Air Force
AS 102.subject: AS

AS 102L.title: Initial Military Training II
AS 102L.subject: AS
AS 102L.description: Laboratory consists of activities that focus and promote the Air Force way of life. Instruction will include leadership and followership development, teamwork, physical fitness training, and activities designed to build camaraderie and esprit de corps. Course is open to all majors.

AS 201.title: Evolution of USAF Air and Space Power
AS 201.subject: AS
AS 201.description: Study of Air Force heritage, Quality Air Force principles, ethics, and an introduction to leadership and group leadership problems. Application of written and verbal communication skills is included.

AS 201L.title: Field Training Preparation I
AS 201L.subject: AS
AS 201L.description: Laboratory consists of preparing second-year AFROTC cadets with the skills needed to successfully complete AFROTC Field Training. Students will learn basic military skills, Field Training skills, and participate in physical fitness training.

AS 202.title: Evolution of USAF Air and Space Power
AS 202.subject: AS

AS 251L.title: Leadership Laboratory
AS 251L.subject: AS
AS 251L.description: Laboratory on the basic skills of leadership and followership. Lab includes application of leadership/followership skills, various field trips to military installations, group projects, and physical training.

AS 252L.title: Leadership Laboratory II
AS 252L.subject: AS
AS 252L.description: Continuation of 251L. Open to all majors.

AS 301.title: Air Force Leadership Studies
AS 301.subject: AS
AS 301.description: Focuses on an examination of ethical Air Force leadership and management concepts. Continued emphasis is given to the refinement of ethical thought through writing and debate.

AS 301L.title: Intermediate Cadet Leader I
AS 301L.subject: AS
AS 301L.description: Laboratory consists of demonstration of leadership and management skills needed to successfully function as an Air Force officer. Instruction will include lessons covering planning, organizational and communication skills, and the ability to use available resources to complete an assigned task.
AS 301L.prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

AS 302.title: Air Force Leadership Studies II
AS 302.subject: AS
AS 302.description: Continuation of 301. Focuses on an examination of Air Force leadership and management concepts. Continued emphasis is given to the refinement of both written and oral communicative skills.

AS 302L.title: Intermediate Cadet Leader II
AS 302L.subject: AS
AS 302L.prereq_raw: must have completed AFROTC Field Training; or consent

children.text: must have completed AFROTC Field Training;

AS 401.title: National Security Affairs
AS 401.subject: AS
AS 401.description: Study of the national security process, regional studies, advanced leadership, ethics, and Air Force doctrine. Special focus placed on preparation for active duty and current issues affecting professionalism.

AS 401L.title: Senior Cadet Leader I
AS 401L.subject: AS
AS 401L.description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty.
AS 401L.prereq_raw: must have completed 351 and 352L; or consent

AS 402L.title: Senior Cadet Leader II
AS 402L.subject: AS
AS 402L.description: Laboratory consists of providing prospective Air Force officers opportunities to continue to develop leadership, managerial, and supervisory skills. Instruction will include preparation for active duty.
AS 402L.prereq_raw: must have completed 351 and 352L; or consent

MSL 100.title: Introduction to Physical Fitness
MSL 100.subject: MSL
MSL 100.description: Hands-on participatory course following the Army’s physical fitness program. Classes conducted three days per week with Army ROTC cadets. Focus is on aerobic conditioning, muscular strength and endurance.

MSL 101.title: Introduction to Military Science I
MSL 101.subject: MSL
MSL 101.description: Introduces cadets to personal challenges and competencies critical for effective leadership; personal development of life skills such as goal setting, time management, physical fitness, and stress management related to leadership, officership, and the Army profession. Focus on developing basic knowledge and comprehension of Army Leadership Dimensions while understanding the ROTC program, its purpose in the Army, and its advantages for the student.

MSL 101L.title: Introduction to Military Science I Lab
MSL 101L.subject: MSL
MSL 101L.description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

MSL 102.title: Introduction to Military Science II
MSL 102.subject: MSL
MSL 102.description: Overviews leadership fundamentals such as setting direction, problem-solving, listening, presenting briefs, providing feedback and using effective writing skills. Explores leadership values, attributes, skills, and actions in the context of practical, hands-on, and interactive exercises. Cadre role models and building stronger relationships among cadets through common experience and practical interaction are critical.

MSL 102L.title: Introduction to Military Science II Lab
MSL 102L.subject: MSL
MSL 102L.description: Practical application in adventure training, Army field craft, rifle marksmanship, land navigation, drill and ceremonies, physical training.

MSL 201.title: Intermediate Military Science I
MSL 201.subject: MSL
MSL 201.description: Explores creative and innovative tactical leadership strategies and styles through historical case studies and engaging in interactive student exercises. Cadets practice aspects of personal motivation and team building by planning, executing, and assessing team exercises. Focus is on continued development of leadership values and attributes through understanding of rank, uniform, customs and courtesies.

MSL 202.title: Intermediate Military Science II
MSL 202.subject: MSL
MSL 202.description: Challenges of leading complex, contemporary operational environments. Dimensions of cross-cultural challenges of leadership in a constantly changing world are highlighted and applied to practical Army leadership tasks and situations. Cadets develop greater self awareness as they practice communication and team building skills, and tactics in real world scenarios. Provides a smooth transition to MSL 301.

MSL 203.title: ROTC Basic Camp
MSL 203.subject: MSL
MSL 203.description: Four-week summer course conducted at Ft. Knox, Kentucky. Substitutes for ROTC basic course (101, 102, 201, and 202) and fulfills course requirement for admission to ROTC advanced courses. Credit will be given for 203 or basic courses, but not both.

MSL 301.title: Leading Small Organizations I
MSL 301.subject: MSL
MSL 301.description: Challenges cadets to study, practice, and evaluate adaptive leadership skills with demands of the ROTC Advanced Camp. Challenging scenarios related to small unit tactical operations will develop self-awareness and critical thinking skills. Cadets will receive systematic, specific feedback on their leadership abilities, and analyze/evaluate their leadership values, attributes, skills and actions.

MSL 302.title: Leading Small Organizations II
MSL 302.subject: MSL
MSL 302.description: Intense situational leadership challenges to build awareness and skills in leading small units. Decision-making, persuading, and motivating team members under fire are explored, evaluated, and developed. Military operations are reviewed to prepare for the ROTC Advance Camp. Cadets apply principles of Law of Land Warfare, Army training, and motivation to troop leading procedures; and are evaluated on what they know and do as leaders.

MSL 303.title: ROTC Advanced Camp
MSL 303.subject: MSL
MSL 303.description: Five-week summer field training exercise conducted at Fort Knox, Kentucky. Arduous and intensified leadership training is conducted throughout the five-week period. Required for U.S. Army commissioning.

MSL 391.title: History of Military Warfare
MSL 391.subject: MSL
MSL 391.description: Lecture/discussion on the art and science of warfare concentrating on U.S. military history from the Colonial Period to present. Generally restricted to Army ROTC students, requiring twenty pages of graded writing assignments.

MSL 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
MSL 399.subject: MSL
MSL 399.description: Limited to military science students who have had at least one previous military science course for which a grade of B or higher was earned and a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better.

MSL 400.title: Fundamentals of Leadership
MSL 400.subject: MSL
MSL 400.description: Introduces students to the fundamentals of leadership. Activities challenge students to connect theory to practice, develop positive relationships through application of effective leadership concepts for leader development, and team-building.

MSL 401.title: Leadership Challenges and Goal Setting
MSL 401.subject: MSL
MSL 401.description: Develops proficiency to plan, execute, and assess complex operations; function as a staff member, provide leadership performance feedback to subordinates. Situational opportunities to assess risk, make ethical decisions, and provide coaching to fellow ROTC cadets; challenged to analyze, evaluate, and instruct younger cadets.

MSL 402.title: Transition to Lieutenant
MSL 402.subject: MSL
MSL 402.description: Explores dynamics of leading in complex situations of current military operations. Examines differences in customs and courtesies, military law, principles of war, and rules of engagement in the face of international terrorism. Interaction with nongovernment organizations, civilians on the battlefield, and host nation support are examined and evaluated. Case studies, scenarios, and What Now, Lieutenant? exercises prepare cadets to lead as commissioned officers in the U.S. Army.

MSL 499.title: Advanced Military Research
MSL 499.subject: MSL
MSL 499.description: Directs the student to conduct detailed research on a military topic and present to the department leadership plus assist MSL 400 series students on a battle analysis. Must be in Military Science and Leadership Program or Military Service member in junior or greater standing.

ATMO 101.title: Introduction to Weather and Climate
ATMO 101.subject: ATMO
ATMO 101.description: Introductory physical science course for all undergraduates in any major. A non-mathematical introduction to basic atmospheric variables, Earth’s past climates, global warming, air pollution, El Nino, hurricanes, tornadoes, and forecasting weather in Hawai‘i.

ATMO 101L.title: Introduction to Weather and Climate Lab
ATMO 101L.subject: ATMO
ATMO 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Exercises with meteorological data and measurement systems. Characteristics of Hawaiian winds, temperatures, and rainfall

ATMO 102.title: Pacific Climates and Cultures
ATMO 102.subject: ATMO
ATMO 102.description: Highlights the interface between the observed weather and climate of the Pacific and the past and future culture of the people of the Hawaiian and Pacific islands. (Alt. years)

ATMO 150.title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
ATMO 150.subject: ATMO
ATMO 150.description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
ATMO 150.prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140

ATMO 199.title: Introduction to MET Undergraduate Directed Research
ATMO 199.subject: ATMO
ATMO 199.description: Students gain familiarity with ATMO research. Students can select 1-3 credits per semester for maximum 6 credits over 4 semesters. Students must pre-arrange research and reading content with instructor. Freshman and sophomore standing only.

ATMO 200.title: Atmospheric Processes and Phenomena
ATMO 200.subject: ATMO
ATMO 200.description: Atmospheric variables, gas laws, radiation processes, thermodynamics, conservation laws, dynamic approximations, clouds and precipitation, convection, atmospheric circulations, mid-latitude and tropical weather systems, forecasting, climate.

ATMO 302.title: Atmospheric Physics
ATMO 302.subject: ATMO
ATMO 302.description: Energy and thermodynamics, statics and stability, physical processes of cloud formation, radiation and Earthatmosphere heat balance, kinetic theory, optical effects.

ATMO 303.title: Introduction to Atmospheric Dynamics
ATMO 303.subject: ATMO
ATMO 303.description: Scalar and vector development of basic laws of hydrodynamics, equations of motion, kinematics, divergence and vorticity, viscosity and turbulence, introduction to numerical weather prediction, general circulation.

ATMO 305.title: Meteorological Instruments and Observations
ATMO 305.subject: ATMO
ATMO 305.description: Each week targets a different meteorological instrument and culminates in a lab exercise and report. The focus is on accurate measurement and scientific-style writing.

ATMO 310.title: Global Environmental Change
ATMO 310.subject: ATMO
ATMO 310.description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc.
ATMO 310.prereq_raw: 200, OCN 201, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent

ATMO 320.title: Programming for Meteorologists
ATMO 320.subject: ATMO
ATMO 320.description: Scientific programming in Fortran 77, graphics software and meteorological applications. A-F or Audit.

ATMO 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
ATMO 395.subject: ATMO
ATMO 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.

ATMO 399.title: Undergraduate Directed Reading
ATMO 399.subject: ATMO
ATMO 399.description: Individual reading in Atmospheric Sciences. ATMO students only. Junior and senior standing only.

ATMO 402.title: Applied Atmospheric Dynamics
ATMO 402.subject: ATMO
ATMO 402.description: Advanced concepts in dynamics: vorticity, cyclogenesis, jet streams, fronts, mesoscale circulations.

ATMO 405.title: Synoptic Satellite Meteorology
ATMO 405.subject: ATMO
ATMO 405.description: Satellite applications to synoptic meteorology and forecasting, including orbital elements, ephemerides, viewing geometry, radiation, satellite sensors, and interpreting satellite data.

ATMO 406.title: Tropical Meteorology
ATMO 406.subject: ATMO
ATMO 406.description: History; tropical clouds and hydrometeors; typhoons; monsoons; local and diurnal effects.

ATMO 412.title: Meteorological Analysis Lab
ATMO 412.subject: ATMO
ATMO 412.description: (2 4-hr Lab) Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in middle and high latitudes; modern methods of forecasting extratropical systems.

ATMO 416.title: Tropical Analysis Lab
ATMO 416.subject: ATMO
ATMO 416.description: Techniques of portraying and analyzing atmospheric structure and weather systems in tropical and equatorial regions; forecasting tropical systems.

ATMO 449.title: Climate Modeling, Data Analysis, and Applications
ATMO 449.subject: ATMO
ATMO 449.description: Introduction to regional and global climate modeling for environmental scientists and engineers. Learn principles of climate modeling, how to access and use climate data for sustainable engineering and environmental management solutions, and effectively communicate results. Senior standing or higher, or consent.
ATMO 449.restrictions_raw: ATMO, CEE, ERTH, GES, OCN, NREM majors only.

ATMO 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
ATMO 499.subject: ATMO
ATMO 499.description: Capstone for senior Meteorology majors. Undergraduate thesis project includes literature review, experiment or research design, data collection and analysis, technical writing of a final thesis paper and oral presentation of the paper. Junior and senior standing only.

ATMO 600.title: Atmospheric Dynamics I
ATMO 600.subject: ATMO
ATMO 600.description: Governing equations for moist atmospheric motions, approximations, basic theoretical models, boundary layer dynamics, atmospheric waves, quasi-geostrophic theory for mid-latitudes.
ATMO 600.prereq_raw: 402, and either MATH 402 or MATH 405; or consent

ATMO 601.title: Atmospheric Dynamics II
ATMO 601.subject: ATMO
ATMO 601.description: Overview of dynamic meteorology, numerical weather prediction, geophysical fluid instabilities, approximate dynamical systems, atmospheric general circulation, stratospheric dynamics.

ATMO 606.title: Cumulus Dynamics
ATMO 606.subject: ATMO
ATMO 606.description: Dynamics of convective systems: tornadoes, waterspouts, squall lines. Interactions with synoptic scale.

ATMO 607.title: Mesoscale Meteorology
ATMO 607.subject: ATMO
ATMO 607.description: Scale analysis. Observational and theoretical aspects of mesoscale circulation systems.

ATMO 610.title: Tropical Climate and Weather
ATMO 610.subject: ATMO
ATMO 610.description: Climate and general circulation of the tropics; El Niño and Southern Oscillation; intraseasonal oscillation; trade winds; tropical weather systems; energy balance; typhoons.

ATMO 611.title: Satellite Data Applications
ATMO 611.subject: ATMO
ATMO 611.description: Principles and practices of satellite remote sensing as used in the atmospheric sciences, specifically clouds, aerosols, precipitation, ocean and land cover datasets from various satellites. Develop skills including data manipulation, analysis, and visualization using Matlab.

ATMO 614.title: Tropical Cyclones
ATMO 614.subject: ATMO
ATMO 614.description: Lecture covering fundamentals of tropical cyclone structure, motion, and impacts on society. Observations from satellites, aircraft, ships and buoys, and numerical simulations focusing on storm structure and track. Some forecasting exercises.

ATMO 616.title: Monsoon Meteorology
ATMO 616.subject: ATMO
ATMO 616.description: Synoptic components of monsoons, regional and temporal variability, numerical models, research exercises.

ATMO 620.title: Physical Meteorology
ATMO 620.subject: ATMO
ATMO 620.description: Molecular kinetics, atmospheric thermodynamics, cloud physics, precipitation processes, atmospheric electricity, scattering and absorption of solar radiation, absorption and emission of infrared radiation, radiative transfer.

ATMO 628.title: Radar Meteorology
ATMO 628.subject: ATMO
ATMO 628.description: Radar hardware, electromagnetic propagation and scattering, radar equation, signal processing, precipitation estimation and polarimetric applications, Multi-Doppler wind synthesis, mobile and spaceborne radars, forecasting, and data assimilation applications.
ATMO 628.prereq_raw: 620 (with a minimum grade of B- or higher) or consent

ATMO 631.title: Statistical Meteorology
ATMO 631.subject: ATMO
ATMO 631.description: Probability; frequency distributions of atmospheric variables; linear models; time series analysis (frequency and time domain); principal component analysis; statistical weather forecasting and verification.

ATMO 632.title: Advanced Statistical Methods in the Geosciences
ATMO 632.subject: ATMO
ATMO 632.description: ) Methods for numerous multivariate analyses will include singular spectrum, extended empirical orthogonal function, singular-value decomposition, canonical correlation, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other advanced topics include wavelet analysis, statistical downscaling and Bayesian analysis. A-F only and audit.

ATMO 640.title: Paleoclimate Model-Proxy Synthesis
ATMO 640.subject: ATMO
ATMO 640.description: Basics of Earth System Model development, parameterizations, intermodel variability and design of paleoclimate simulations. Types of proxies, tools and techniques for paleoclimate record development and reconstructions. Hypothesis testing and methods for proxy-model comparison studies. Graduate students only. (Alt. years: spring)
ATMO 640.restrictions_raw: ATMO, GEO, EPET, NREM, OCN, and ORE majors only.

ATMO 665.title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
ATMO 665.subject: ATMO
ATMO 665.description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
ATMO 665.prereq_raw: MATH 402 and 403 (or their equivalents) and either 600 or OCN 620; or consent

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either 600 or OCN 620 ; or consent

ATMO 666.title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
ATMO 666.subject: ATMO
ATMO 666.description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the stateof-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Niño/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

ATMO 702.title: Numerical Weather Prediction
ATMO 702.subject: ATMO
ATMO 702.description: Fundamental methods and techniques in numerical weather prediction: time differencing, spatial finite differencing, spectral methods, numerical stability, explicit and implicit methods. Modern operational and research forecast models. Hands-on laboratory includes simple to complex dynamic models, with a term project.
ATMO 702.prereq_raw: 600 or OCN 620; MATH 407 or 408; or consent

ATMO 704.title: Climate and Climate Variability
ATMO 704.subject: ATMO
ATMO 704.description: Physical basis of climate, numerical climate models, paleoclimatic indicators, modern instrumental climate records, assessment of human impact on climate, predictions of future climate.

ATMO 706.title: Tropical Climate Dynamics and Modeling
ATMO 706.subject: ATMO
ATMO 706.description: Overview of current progress in tropical climate dynamics with a particular focus on large-scale atmosphere-ocean interactions; introduction of basic numerical techniques for students to construct and run immediate tropical atmosphere and ocean models.

ATMO 708.title: General Circulation of the Atmosphere
ATMO 708.subject: ATMO
ATMO 708.description: Theory, observations, large-scale analyses, and global model simulations that describe characteristic large-scale circulation of the Earth’s atmosphere. Includes zonally averaged climatology, asymmetric features of the general circulation, and El NinoSouthern Oscillation phenomenon.

ATMO 752.title: Special Topics in Meteorology
ATMO 752.subject: ATMO
ATMO 752.description: Concentrated studies on selected atmospheric problems.

ATMO 765.title: Seminar in Meteorology
ATMO 765.subject: ATMO
ATMO 765.description: Participation in departmental seminars and presentation of a seminar on research results. Includes written critiques of departmental seminars.

EPET 201.title: Exploration of the Solar System
EPET 201.subject: EPET
EPET 201.description: Introduction to the science or engineering of Solar System exploration. Covers science instruments, mission trajectories (fly-by, orbit, or lander), and science and engineering constraints imposed on spacecraft design. Lectures, discussions, class projects.

EPET 301.title: Space Science and Instrumentation
EPET 301.subject: EPET
EPET 301.description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces and their measurement. Design of space flight instrumentation.
EPET 301.prereq_raw: 201, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 101L and ERTH 105, or ERTH 101 and ERTH 107; and CHEM 161 and PHYS 272

EPET 302.title: Space Mission Design
EPET 302.subject: EPET
EPET 302.description: Will cover all aspects of spacecraft design, subsystems, science payload, systems engineering, project management, and budgets that are important to producing a fully successful mission.

EPET 401.title: Capstone Project: Producing a Science Satellite
EPET 401.subject: EPET
EPET 401.description: Develops a space mission with a multidisciplinary team of engineers and scientists using concurrent science and engineering methodologies. Will build a small spacecraft and payload. The project will seek to answer important science questions.

ERTH 101.title: Dynamic Earth
ERTH 101.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101.description: The natural physical environment; the landscape; rocks and minerals, rivers and oceans; volcanism, earthquakes, and other processes inside the Earth; effects of human use of the Earth and its resources. Field trip.

ERTH 101L.title: Dynamic Earth Laboratory
ERTH 101L.subject: ERTH
ERTH 101L.description: (1 3-hr Lab) Hands-on study of minerals, rocks, and topographic maps. Examine volcanism, hydrology, coastal processes and hazards, geologic time and earthquakes. Field trips to investigate landslides, beaches and O‘ahu geology.

ERTH 102.title: Quantifying Global and Environmental Change
ERTH 102.subject: ERTH
ERTH 102.description: Introductory mathematical approaches to quantifying key aspects of global and environmental change. Includes data analysis, graphical representation and modeling of population growth, greenhouse gas emissions and fate, sustainable resource utilization, and sea level change.

ERTH 103.title: Geology of the Hawaiian Islands
ERTH 103.subject: ERTH
ERTH 103.description: Hawaiian geology and geologic processes: origin of Hawaiian islands, volcanism, rocks and minerals, landforms, stream and coastal processes, landslides, earthquakes and tsunamis, groundwater, geologic and environmental hazards. Field trip.

ERTH 104.title: Volcanoes in the Sea
ERTH 104.subject: ERTH
ERTH 104.description: Lecture with field trips covering the manner in which geological conditions, resources, and events have affected past and present circum-Pacific societies.

ERTH 105.title: Voyage through the Solar System
ERTH 105.subject: ERTH
ERTH 105.description: An illustrated voyage through the Solar System based on recent scientific results. The class highlights the origin, evolution, and current knowledge of the eight planets, their moons, asteroids, comets, and one star, the Sun. Field trip.

ERTH 106.title: Humans and the Environment
ERTH 106.subject: ERTH
ERTH 106.description: Prepares students to make decisions such as where to build/buy a house, sustainable use of natural resources, and what environmental actions relevant to society and Earth’s ecosystem are appropriate on a local and global scale.

ERTH 107.title: Solar System Studio
ERTH 107.subject: ERTH
ERTH 107.description: Explore the wonders of the Solar System through hands-on experience of science. Will study satellite images, evaluate planetary surface observations, analyze data of objects in our Solar System, conduct experiments, and communicate their findings.

ERTH 111.title: Introduction to Volcanoes
ERTH 111.subject: ERTH
ERTH 111.description: Examines the origin and classification of volcanoes, volcanic eruptions, and volcanic deposits. Includes the history of volcanic studies, myths, and legends. Emphasis on volcanic eruptions, eruptive products, volcanic hazards, and risk management.

ERTH 130.title: Geological Hazards
ERTH 130.subject: ERTH
ERTH 130.description: Introductory course covering the causes of, and effects from, earthquakes, tsunami, volcanic eruptions, landslides, rockfalls, and other natural geologic phenomena. Open to non-majors. Field trips. (Alt. years)

ERTH 135.title: Natural Disasters and Human History
ERTH 135.subject: ERTH
ERTH 135.description: Examines how natural hazards have affected the course of human culture and societies from pre-history to the present in Hawai‘i/Oceania, Asia, Africa, Europe, and the Americas.

ERTH 150.title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
ERTH 150.subject: ERTH
ERTH 150.description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
ERTH 150.prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140

ERTH 170.title: Physical Geology
ERTH 170.subject: ERTH
ERTH 170.description: Structure, composition and evolution of Earth; processes responsible for formation, deformation and transformation of rocks; plate tectonics. Emphasis on quantitative methods, problem solving and critical thinking to geology. Laboratory and field trips required.

ERTH 199.title: Introduction to Directed Research
ERTH 199.subject: ERTH
ERTH 199.description: Lower division reading and research in any area of ERTH under the direction of a faculty member.

ERTH 200.title: Geological Inquiry
ERTH 200.subject: ERTH
ERTH 200.description: Origin and age of the solar system and earth: interior of the earth; plate tectonics and records of biological evolution and past environments.
ERTH 200.prereq_raw: 170, or 101 and 101L, or 103 and 101L; or consent. 101L may be taken concurrently. ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors

children.text: 101L may be taken concurrently. ERTH and GEOL majors only. Consent required for all non-majors

ERTH 250.title: Scientific Programming
ERTH 250.subject: ERTH
ERTH 250.description: Introduction to solving scientific problems by computer programming. Overview of the MatLab programming language and environment. Emphasis placed on good style, logical reasoning, and applied mathematics.

ERTH 300.title: Volcanology
ERTH 300.subject: ERTH
ERTH 300.description: Volcanic eruptions and their consequences. Includes models for volcanic eruptions including explosive eruptions and lava flows, monitoring of active volcanoes, evaluation and impacts of volcanic hazards, and mitigation of volcanic risk. Field trips. Normally fall. ERTH and GEOL majors or consent.

ERTH 301.title: Mineralogy
ERTH 301.subject: ERTH
ERTH 301.description: Crystallography, crystal chemistry, phase equilibria, and crystal structures. Also covers mineral optics and identification and includes an introduction to modern methods of mineralogy and crystallography.

ERTH 302.title: Igneous and Metamorphic Petrology
ERTH 302.subject: ERTH
ERTH 302.description: Survey of composition, classification, and occurrence of igneous and metamorphic rocks. Hand-specimen identification and optical petrography of igneous and metamorphic rocks. Development of critical thinking and writing skills.

ERTH 303.title: Structural Geology
ERTH 303.subject: ERTH
ERTH 303.description: Introduction to (a) the geometry, kinematics, and mechanics of crustal deformation, and (b) continuum mechanics in geology. Develops skills in three-dimensional thinking through geologic maps, cross sections, various projections, experiments, and vector analyses.
ERTH 303.prereq_raw: 200, 250, MATH 241 or MATH 251A, and PHYS 151 or PHYS 170; or consent

ERTH 304.title: Physics of Earth and Planets
ERTH 304.subject: ERTH
ERTH 304.description: Essentials of geophysics: formation of Solar System and Earth, gravity, seismology, heat flow, geomagnetism, isostasy, plate tectonics. Course work involves application of basic physics to understanding Earth structure. Labs include field surveys and computer analyses.
ERTH 304.prereq_raw: 250, 303, MATH 241, MATH 242, and PHYS 272; or consent

ERTH 305.title: Geological Field Methods
ERTH 305.subject: ERTH
ERTH 305.description: Methods used in geological investigations in the field. Eight hours on Saturday in the field.

ERTH 306.title: Work of Water
ERTH 306.subject: ERTH
ERTH 306.description: Physical properties of water, geological aspects of surface water and ground water occurrence, surface water and groundwater resources, use, and problems.

ERTH 309.title: Sedimentology and Stratigraphy
ERTH 309.subject: ERTH
ERTH 309.description: Principles of sedimentology, sedimentary petrology, geochemistry and stratigraphy. Description and discussion of modern and past processes and environments that form sedimentary rocks, properties of sedimentary rocks and interpretation of these properties and stratigraphic relationships in terms of Earth history.

ERTH 312.title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
ERTH 312.subject: ERTH
ERTH 312.description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

ERTH 325.title: Geochemistry
ERTH 325.subject: ERTH
ERTH 325.description: Theory and applications of chemical principles and chemical analysis to Earth, ocean and environmental sciences; chemistry of hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere system, origin/differentiation of Earth/Solar system, volcanic processes, natural radioactivity, organic/inorganic chemistry.
ERTH 325.prereq_raw: 200, 250, MATH 241 or MATH 251A, CHEM 162 (or concurrent); or consent

ERTH 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
ERTH 395.subject: ERTH
ERTH 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Open to undergraduate SOEST majors.

ERTH 399.title: Directed Reading
ERTH 399.subject: ERTH
ERTH 399.description: Individual reading in geology and geophysics.

ERTH 401.title: Introduction to mineral Physics
ERTH 401.subject: ERTH
ERTH 401.description: Scientific study of the materials that make up the Earth. Properties of minerals on micro- and macro-scales; their properties and behavior.

ERTH 402.title: Hawaiian Geology
ERTH 402.subject: ERTH
ERTH 402.description: Consists of lectures, discussions, and field trips about the geology of the Hawaiian islands. Focus on geological processes and the geologic history of all islands will be covered.

ERTH 404.title: Remote Compositional Analysis: Spectroscopy, Mineralogy, and Geochemistry of Planetary Surfaces
ERTH 404.subject: ERTH
ERTH 404.description: Essential techniques for remote compositional analysis of planets; understanding spectroscopy, mineralogy, and geochemistry of planetary surfaces. Comparative studies of fundamental planetary science phenomena. Planetary surface science discoveries. Sustainability of planetary environments.
ERTH 404.prereq_raw: (101 or 105 or 107 or ASTR 150; and CHEM 161; and MATH 241 and 242 and PHYS 272) with a minimum grade of C+; or consent

ERTH 406.title: Natural Disasters: Geoethics and the Layman
ERTH 406.subject: ERTH
ERTH 406.description: Evaluates ethical practice of geoscience as it relates to studies of natural disasters that result from geological and meteorological phenomena and the means that earth scientists interact with the laymen.

ERTH 407.title: Energy and Mineral Resources
ERTH 407.subject: ERTH
ERTH 407.description: Lecture and discussion on the origin, distribution and exploitation of fossil fuels, renewable energy resources and ore deposits. Coverage and detail will depend partly on student interest and background.

ERTH 410.title: Undergraduate Seminar
ERTH 410.subject: ERTH
ERTH 410.description: Gain professional training, practical experience, and evaluate peers on giving scientific presentations emphasizing topics in geology, geophysics, and planetary science. 60% of the grade is based on the equivalent of three oral communication assignments.

ERTH 413.title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
ERTH 413.subject: ERTH
ERTH 413.description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data.

ERTH 420.title: Beaches, Reefs, and Climate Change
ERTH 420.subject: ERTH
ERTH 420.description: Global and local aspects of climate change and paleoclimate; beach and reef processes and response to climate change; management of coastal environments; field study local sites. Junior standing or higher, or consent.

ERTH 423.title: Marine Geology
ERTH 423.subject: ERTH
ERTH 423.description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

ERTH 425.title: Environmental Geochemistry
ERTH 425.subject: ERTH
ERTH 425.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system, remediation methods, prevention, industrial/agricultural best practices. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase, and ecosystem impacts of environmental contaminants.

ERTH 444.title: Plate Tectonics
ERTH 444.subject: ERTH
ERTH 444.description: Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

ERTH 450.title: Geophysical Methods
ERTH 450.subject: ERTH
ERTH 450.description: Combined lecture/lab covering basic geophysical theories, exploration, and interpretation. Seismic reflection and refraction, gravity, and electromagnetics. Constraints on models of Earth’s internal structure and composition.
ERTH 450.prereq_raw: 250, 303, MATH 241, MATH 242, and PHYS 272; or consent

ERTH 451.title: Earthquakes and Crustal Deformation
ERTH 451.subject: ERTH
ERTH 451.description: Earthquakes and crustal deformation through modern seismological and geodetic observations; elastic properties of rocks, seismic waves, causes, detection, and location of earthquakes; crustal motions of the earthquake cycle; tsunami generation, liquefaction, and planetary observations.

ERTH 454.title: Engineering Geology
ERTH 454.subject: ERTH
ERTH 454.description: Solutions of geotechnical problems by geologists and engineers through recognition, characterization, evaluation, and assessment of geologic processes that impact people, engineering structures, and engineering operations. Group format. Junior standing and higher.
ERTH 454.restrictions_raw: ERTH, GEOL, and CEE majors only.

ERTH 455.title: Hydrogeology
ERTH 455.subject: ERTH
ERTH 455.description: Occurrence, characteristics, movement, quality, development, and contamination of water in the Earth’s crust.

ERTH 460.title: Geological Remote Sensing
ERTH 460.subject: ERTH
ERTH 460.description: Combined lecture-lab on the concepts behind, geologic uses for, and techniques of satellite and airborne remote sensing. Lab work will consist of computer image processing. Field trips. Open to non-majors.

ERTH 461.title: Geospatial Information
ERTH 461.subject: ERTH
ERTH 461.description: Combined lecture/lab covering the collection, analysis and use of geospatially registered field data.

ERTH 466.title: Planetary Geology
ERTH 466.subject: ERTH
ERTH 466.description: Comparative geology of the terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, tectonism, geomorphology, weathering; manned and unmanned space exploration.

ERTH 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
ERTH 499.subject: ERTH
ERTH 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

ERTH 593.title: Earth and Planetary Sciences Workshops
ERTH 593.subject: ERTH
