ERTH 593.description: Designed for in-service school professionals to learn new approaches and concepts in the fields of earth and planetary sciences. Credits earned in these courses cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

ERTH 600.title: Equations of Geophysics
ERTH 600.subject: ERTH
ERTH 600.description: Least-square approximation of functions by orthogonal series; potential, wave heat flow equations; boundary value problems; Bessel Hankel functions, spherical harmonics, potential theory, plane waves, spherical waves; emphasis on geophysics application.
ERTH 600.prereq_raw: MATH 244 or MATH 253A, PHYS 400, or consent

ERTH 601.title: Explosive Volcanism
ERTH 601.subject: ERTH
ERTH 601.description: Explosive volcanic eruptions: from causes to consequences. Review of current physical volcanology including ascent and fragmentation of magma, transport and deposition processes in pyroclastic eruptions, volcanic crisis management and volcanic eruption scenarios. Seven-day field trip.

ERTH 602.title: Theoretical Petrology
ERTH 602.subject: ERTH
ERTH 602.description: Derivation of phase diagrams from basic thermodynamics principles. Equilibria of natural silicate systems. Crystal chemistry, kinetics, diffusion, etc., Applied to igneous and metamorphic petrology.

ERTH 603.title: Petrology of Ocean Lithosphere
ERTH 603.subject: ERTH
ERTH 603.description: Petrogenesis of the oceanic lithosphere, including mantle processes and rocks from mid-ocean ridges, seamounts, oceanic hotspots, back-arc basins, and intra-oceanic arcs.

ERTH 604.title: Disaster Management: Understanding the Nature of Hazards
ERTH 604.subject: ERTH
ERTH 604.description: Combined lecture/discussion in disaster management focusing on the scientific understanding of the forces and processes underlying natural hazards; and human attempts to respond to these through mitigation and planning activities.

ERTH 605.title: Lava Flow Rheology and Morphology
ERTH 605.subject: ERTH
ERTH 605.description: Effusion eruptions: from eruption to final flow form. Includes: rheology, effusion rate, heat loss, and field measurements, followed by inflation, flow forms, lava lakes, domes, flow hazard and modeling. Field trips to Kilauea and Makapuu.

ERTH 606.title: Current Events in Volcanology
ERTH 606.subject: ERTH
ERTH 606.description: Discussion of active areas of volcanism and new publications on volcanology.

ERTH 607.title: Submarine Volcanoes
ERTH 607.subject: ERTH
ERTH 607.description: Seminar exploring different aspects of submarine effusive and explosive volcanism, hydrothermal activity, and volcano-hosted ecosystems.

ERTH 608.title: Isotopes and Trace Elements
ERTH 608.subject: ERTH
ERTH 608.description: Principles of radiogenic and stable isotope, and trace element geochemistry as applied to igneous petrology, mantle dynamics, plate tectonics, and terrestrial evolution.

ERTH 609.title: Graduate Teaching Geology
ERTH 609.subject: ERTH
ERTH 609.description: For ERTH graduate students who lead, under faculty supervision, a scheduled class in Geology and Geophysics. The instructor will define the student’s responsibilities when offering ERTH 609, and these responsibilities must be met for a passing grade. As the consent to take the class must also be granted by the department chair, the chair will also review the responsibilities required by the instructor. ERTH graduate students only.
ERTH 609.prereq_raw: consent of instructor and department chair

ERTH 610.title: Graduate Seminar
ERTH 610.subject: ERTH
ERTH 610.description: Seminar in which students present a 15- to 20-minute talk on their research or a related topic. Meets once a week with two to three talks per meeting. Graduate students are required to register for this course once per year.

ERTH 611.title: Accelerated Introduction to Earth Sciences I
ERTH 611.subject: ERTH
ERTH 611.description: Lecture presenting a rapid-paced survey of earth sciences for graduate students. Includes origin of the Solar System, tectonics, volcanology, whole-earth composition, phase transformations, petrology (igneous, metamorphic, and sedimentary), historical geology, and hydrology. Saturday field trips.

ERTH 613.title: Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
ERTH 613.subject: ERTH
ERTH 613.description: Exploratory data analysis, error propagation, probability theory and statistics, curve fitting, regression, sequence and spectral analysis, multivariate analysis, and analysis of directional data. Credit earned only one time for either 413 or 613.

ERTH 615.title: Literate Programming With R and RStudio
ERTH 615.subject: ERTH
ERTH 615.description: Literate programming with R, RStudio, and R Markdown for data analysis and research. Introduction to Matlab for rapid modeling. Emphasis on the preparation of research papers for scholarly publication in the Earth and environmental sciences.
ERTH 615.prereq_raw: competence in basic differential and integral calculus

ERTH 616.title: How to Write a Scientific Paper
ERTH 616.subject: ERTH
ERTH 616.description: Designed for students who have collected data and want to know how to publish their work in a scientific journal. Covers the essential parts of paper preparation and submission. ERTH students only.

ERTH 617.title: Summer Fieldschool Program: Hydrogeophysics in Volcanic Environments
ERTH 617.subject: ERTH
ERTH 617.description: Will cover the full hydrogeophysical workflow including theory, acquisition design, field data acquisition, data processing, data inversion, and hydrogeological interpretation. Methods include ambient seismic, 3D electrical resistivity tomography and induced polarization, and self-potential.

ERTH 620.title: Coastal Geology
ERTH 620.subject: ERTH
ERTH 620.description: Geological history and geologic framework of the Hawaiian shoreline. Modern climate change, paleoclimate, focus on sea level change. Modern coastal management and problems in the coastal environment. Coastal planning.

ERTH 621.title: Electron Microprobe Analysis
ERTH 621.subject: ERTH
ERTH 621.description: Combined lecture-lab on the principles of geochemical analysis by electron microprobe and X-ray fluorescence. Hands-on experience with the electron microprobe. Required to operate the UH electron microprobe.

ERTH 625.title: Advanced Environmental Geochemistry
ERTH 625.subject: ERTH
ERTH 625.description: Theory and applications of contaminant/pollutant distribution in the hydrosphere-geosphere-biosphere-atmosphere system and remediation methods. Topics include aqueous geochemistry, organic, inorganic, gas phase and isotope chemistry of environmental contaminants.

ERTH 630.title: Numerical Modeling of Physical Systems
ERTH 630.subject: ERTH
ERTH 630.description: Finite difference, finite element, and other modeling techniques applied to geological and geophysical problems. Physical modeling of heat flow, molecular diffusion, solidification and melting, deformation, fluid flow, wave propagation, and other phenomena. (Once a year)

ERTH 631.title: Geophysics–Solid, Fluid, and Wave Mechanics
ERTH 631.subject: ERTH
ERTH 631.description: Continuum mechanics in geophysics, as applied to the deformation of Earth materials (elastic, viscous, viscoelastic, and plastic deformations) and seismic wave propagation (body waves, surface waves, anisotropy, and attenuation).
ERTH 631.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent)

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

ERTH 632.title: Geophysics–Gravity, Magnetics, and Heat Transfer
ERTH 632.subject: ERTH
ERTH 632.description: Fundamental theory and practical applications of the use of gravity, magnetics, and heat conduction to probing the structure of the Earth; heat transfer via mantle convection is a major control on Earth’s internal structure.
ERTH 632.prereq_raw: (with a minimum grade of B-) for PHYS 170, PHYS 272, and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 (or equivalent)

children.text: for PHYS 170 , PHYS 272 , and MATH 307 or ERTH 312 ( or equivalent)

ERTH 635.title: Seismology
ERTH 635.subject: ERTH
ERTH 635.description: Elasticity, wave equations, body waves, surface waves, free oscillations, seismometry, seismogram interpretation, tectonics, inversion, source theory, and waveform modeling.

ERTH 638.title: Earth System Science and Global Change
ERTH 638.subject: ERTH
ERTH 638.description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmospheric-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
ERTH 638.prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus; or consent

ERTH 639.title: Stable Isotope Biogeochemistry
ERTH 639.subject: ERTH
ERTH 639.description: Stable isotope geochemistry applied to questions of biogeochemical cycling in the oceans, sediment diagenesis, paleoceanography, environmental geochemistry and ecology.

ERTH 640.title: Coastal Geochemistry
ERTH 640.subject: ERTH
ERTH 640.description: Geochemistry at the land-ocean interface: coastal hydrology, subterranean estuaries and coastal mixing and their importance in governing the distribution of selected radiotracers, trace metals and nutrients. Combined lecture-lab with field trips and group projects.
ERTH 640.prereq_raw: CHEM 162, and MATH 241 or MATH 251A; or consent

ERTH 641.title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
ERTH 641.subject: ERTH
ERTH 641.description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

ERTH 642.title: Elemental Composition Changes
ERTH 642.subject: ERTH
ERTH 642.description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

ERTH 644.title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
ERTH 644.subject: ERTH
ERTH 644.description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.
ERTH 644.prereq_raw: CHEM 171, or CHEM 161 and CHEM 162; PHYS 152; and MATH 242 or MATH 252A; and consent

ERTH 651.title: Geomagnetism and Cosmic Magnetism
ERTH 651.subject: ERTH
ERTH 651.description: Magnetic fields of Earth, planets, stars, and galaxies; dynamo theories; paleomagnetism; terrestrial and lunar rock magnetism; planetary, regional, and local geomagnetic sounding.

ERTH 654.title: Groundwater Contamination
ERTH 654.subject: ERTH
ERTH 654.description: Principles of groundwater chemistry; chemical evolution in natural groundwater flow systems; sources of contamination; mass transport processes; hydrochemical behavior of contaminants.

ERTH 656.title: Groundwater Modeling
ERTH 656.subject: ERTH
ERTH 656.description: Introduction to the finite-difference method; steady-state and transient groundwater flow in saturated and unsaturated media; applications to groundwater recharge and aquifer evaluation.

ERTH 657.title: Astrochemistry–A Molecular Approach
ERTH 657.subject: ERTH
ERTH 657.description: Formation of astrobiologically important molecules and their precursors in the interstellar medium and in our solar system: first principles and latest trends.

ERTH 666.title: Planetary Surfaces
ERTH 666.subject: ERTH
ERTH 666.description: Comparative geology of terrestrial planets (moon, Mars, Mercury, Venus, and Earth); impact cratering, volcanism, geomorphology; remote sensing; manned and unmanned space exploration.

ERTH 669.title: Cosmochemistry
ERTH 669.subject: ERTH
ERTH 669.description: Formation and evolution of planets as astrophysical objects, geologic bodies, and abodes of life; current understanding from studies of the Solar System, star formation, meteorites, exoplanets; theory of formation and dynamics; atmospheres, oceans, habitability, biosignatures.

ERTH 672.title: Seminar in Tectonics
ERTH 672.subject: ERTH
ERTH 672.description: Evolution of ocean basins, margins, foldbelts, and platforms, from plate tectonics and regional syntheses of structure, petrology, geophysics, and stratigraphy. (Alt. years)

ERTH 674.title: Paleoceanography
ERTH 674.subject: ERTH
ERTH 674.description: Study of the paleoceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere and biosphere.

ERTH 675.title: The Generic Mapping Tools
ERTH 675.subject: ERTH
ERTH 675.description: Introduction to the Generic Mapping Tools (GMT). Processing of scientific data and the automated preparation of maps and illustrations using GMT on UNIX workstations, with introduction to UNIX and the C shell environment.

ERTH 691.title: Data Exploration and Processing
ERTH 691.subject: ERTH
ERTH 691.description: Time- and frequency analysis, filtering, factor and cluster analysis, interpolation, quantitative map analysis, and introduction to wavelets and fractals.

ERTH 695.title: Bayesian Data Analysis
ERTH 695.subject: ERTH
ERTH 695.description: Linear and nonlinear techniques for model selection, parameter estimation, simulation and forecasting, from Bayesian principles with particular attention to large data sets and sparse noisy data.

ERTH 701.title: Physics of the Earth’s Interior
ERTH 701.subject: ERTH
ERTH 701.description: Interpretation of geophysical and laboratory data to understand elastic and anelastic properties, composition, phase relationships, temperature distribution in the Earth.

ERTH 703.title: Fractures and Faults
ERTH 703.subject: ERTH
ERTH 703.description: Lecture on elasticity theory, fracture mechanics and boundary element modeling, with application to faults and fractures in the Earth.

ERTH 710.title: Selected Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
ERTH 710.subject: ERTH

ERTH 711.title: Special Topics in Earth and Planetary Sciences
ERTH 711.subject: ERTH

ERTH 740.title: MGeo Seminar
ERTH 740.subject: ERTH
ERTH 740.description: Seminar to improve student awareness of trends and practices in geoscience professions, and develop ability to prepare, deliver, and evaluate a professional scientific presentation. Targets abstract writing, oral presentation, and technical criticism.

ERTH 750.title: MGeo Professional Project
ERTH 750.subject: ERTH
ERTH 750.description: Practical hands-on professional experience, typically with a local company or agency, and involving a final written report and an oral presentation. A grade of credit is assigned when the internship presentations are satisfactorily completed.

GES 100.title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
GES 100.subject: GES
GES 100.description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors.

GES 102.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability
GES 102.subject: GES
GES 102.description: Introduction to principles of environmental science and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning with an emphasis on sustaining resources and mitigating pollution to ecosystems.

GES 102L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
GES 102L.subject: GES
GES 102L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
GES 102L.prereq_raw: (102 or OCN 102 or SUST 112) or concurrent

GES 310.title: Global Environmental Change
GES 310.subject: GES
GES 310.description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc.
GES 310.prereq_raw: OCN 201, ATMO 200, ERTH 101, ERTH 103, or ERTH 170; or consent

GES 310L.title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
GES 310L.subject: GES
GES 310L.description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement OCN 310. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
GES 310L.prereq_raw: MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, CHEM 161/161L, and OCN 310; or consent

GES 320.title: Aquatic Pollution
GES 320.subject: GES
GES 320.description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives.

GES 399.title: Directed Reading
GES 399.subject: GES
GES 399.description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

GES 401.title: Biogeochemical Systems
GES 401.subject: GES
GES 401.description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course.
GES 401.prereq_raw: OCN 201, OCN 310/310L or ATMO310/310L or OEST 310/310L, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, MATH 241, MATH 243 & 252A, MATH 373 (or ECON 321), ATMO200, PHYS 170/170L, and PHYS 272/272L; or consent

children.text: & 252A , MATH 373 ( or ECON 321 ) , ATMO200 , PHYS 170 / 170L , and PHYS 272 / 272L ; or consent

GES 454.title: Earth’s Microbiome
GES 454.subject: GES
GES 454.description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
GES 454.prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

GES 454L.title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
GES 454L.subject: GES
GES 454L.description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
GES 454L.prereq_raw: OCN 102 or OCN 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

GES 463.title: Earth System Science Databases
GES 463.subject: GES
GES 463.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.
GES 463.prereq_raw: MATH 242; and either 310 and 310L, or OCN 310 and OCN 310L; or consent

GES 490.title: Communication of Research Results
GES 490.subject: GES
GES 490.description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester.

GES 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
GES 499.subject: GES
GES 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

OCN 100.title: Global Environmental Science Seminar
OCN 100.subject: OCN
OCN 100.description: Seminar to introduce new GES majors to the research interests of GES faculty and the research facilities available within SOEST. Restricted to GES majors.

OCN 102.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability
OCN 102.subject: OCN
OCN 102.description: Introduction to principles of environmental science and sustainability as they apply to ecosystems. Sustainability will be introduced through active learning with an emphasis on sustaining resources and mitigating pollution to ecosystems.

OCN 102L.title: Introduction to the Environment and Sustainability Lab
OCN 102L.subject: OCN
OCN 102L.description: Introduction to a variety of quantitative and qualitative approaches and methodologies to describe and assess key components to the environment.
OCN 102L.prereq_raw: (102 or GES 102 or SUST 112) or concurrent

OCN 105.title: Sustainability in a Changing World
OCN 105.subject: OCN
OCN 105.description: Environmentally sustainable and non-sustainable practices, and the impacts of climate change, on the development and spread of human societies from pre-history to the 1500s in Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Hawai‘i/Oceania. Active learning environment.

OCN 120.title: Global Environmental Challenges
OCN 120.subject: OCN
OCN 120.description: Scientific approach to evaluating human-caused environmental challenges and their potential solutions. Open to non-majors.

OCN 150.title: Introduction to Quantitative Earth and Environmental Science
OCN 150.subject: OCN
OCN 150.description: Introduction to pre-calculus math and physics applied to Earth and environmental science. Students work on real-world problems and engage in participatory learning. Preparatory for classes in calculus and physics.
OCN 150.prereq_raw: MATH 134, 161, or MATH assessment exam (with score required for MATH 140)

children.text: MATH assessment exam ( with score required for MATH 140

OCN 196.title: Research Experiences in Marine Science
OCN 196.subject: OCN
OCN 196.description: Inquiry-driven and experimental marine biology summer program based on the expertise of HIMB researchers whose specialties demonstrate how human impacts and global change affect coral reef ecosystems. Emphases on student team research projects. High school or UG freshman only.

OCN 199.title: Introduction to Directed Research
OCN 199.subject: OCN
OCN 199.description: Reading and research in any area of Oceanography under the direction of a faculty member.

OCN 201.title: Science of the Sea
OCN 201.subject: OCN
OCN 201.description: Structure, formation, and features of ocean basins; seawater properties and distributions; currents; waves; tides; characteristics of marine organisms; marine ecological principles; man and the sea. Field trip required.

OCN 201L.title: Science of the Sea Laboratory
OCN 201L.subject: OCN
OCN 201L.description: Experiments, computer exercises, and field trips demonstrating the geological, physical, chemical, and biological principles of earth and ocean sciences.

OCN 310.title: Global Environmental Change
OCN 310.subject: OCN
OCN 310.description: Global environmental change problems such as carbon dioxide and the greenhouse effect, acid rain, chlorofluorocarbons and the ozone layer, global deforestation and the effect on climate, etc.
OCN 310.prereq_raw: 201, ATMO 200, GG/ERTH 101, GG/ERTH 103, or GG/ERTH 170; or consent

OCN 310L.title: Global Environmental Change Laboratory
OCN 310L.subject: OCN
OCN 310L.description: (2-hr Lab) Laboratory to supplement OCN 310. Quantitative aspects of global environmental change will be addressed through problem-solving and computer modeling.
OCN 310L.prereq_raw: MATH 242, PHYS 170/170L, CHEM 161/161L, and OCN 310; or consent

OCN 312.title: Advanced Mathematics for Scientists and Engineers I
OCN 312.subject: OCN
OCN 312.description: Advanced mathematical methods with emphasis on application to the earth and ocean sciences and engineering. Topics include linear algebra, vector calculus, ordinary differential equations, and numerical methods.

OCN 315.title: The Role of Models in Global Environmental Science
OCN 315.subject: OCN
OCN 315.description: Introduction to philosophy of science for those with some background in the natural sciences. Special emphasis on issues arising from the construction and use of models.
OCN 315.prereq_raw: any course 200 or above in PHIL or any course 200 or above with either DB or DP designation, or consent

OCN 318.title: Introduction to Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
OCN 318.subject: OCN
OCN 318.description: Introduction to environmental monitoring systems for earth science students. Students will learn how to construct, program, and deploy simple environmental monitoring systems to collect in-situ environmental data.
OCN 318.prereq_raw: 201/201L or ERTH 101/101L, CHEM 161/161L, and MATH 241; or consent

OCN 320.title: Aquatic Pollution
OCN 320.subject: OCN
OCN 320.description: Pollution of freshwater and marine systems by human activities. Causes, consequences, and correctives.

OCN 321.title: Applied Principles of Environmental & Energy Policy
OCN 321.subject: OCN
OCN 321.description: Introduction to the methods and techniques of environmental and energy policy in relation to energy systems. Analysis of enacted policies from case studies to understanding the effectiveness, challenges, contradictions, and limitations of each. Junior standing or higher.
OCN 321.prereq_raw: any 100 or 200 level OCN course, or consent

OCN 330.title: Mineral and Energy Resources of the Sea
OCN 330.subject: OCN
OCN 330.description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration, and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

OCN 331.title: Living Resources of the Sea-Mai ke Kai Mai ke Ola
OCN 331.subject: OCN
OCN 331.description: Marine fisheries, aquaculture, and law of the sea. Principles of management of renewable resources. Political and scientific constraints and limitations.

OCN 340.title: Ecology of Infectious Diseases and Symbioses
OCN 340.subject: OCN
OCN 340.description: Introduction to the ecology of infectious diseases of animals, plants, and humans. Factors affecting disease transmission and virulence. Effects of human activities and environmental change on disease transmission. Emphasis on issues pertinent to Hawai‘i.

OCN 395.title: Undergraduate Internship
OCN 395.subject: OCN
OCN 395.description: Experiential approach to earth science; students serve as interns to field professionals; responsibilities include supervised field work. Undergraduate SOEST majors only. Open to GES majors. CR/ NC only.

OCN 399.title: Directed Reading
OCN 399.subject: OCN
OCN 399.description: Directed reading in earth system science, oceanography, or environmental science.

OCN 401.title: Biogeochemical Systems
OCN 401.subject: OCN
OCN 401.description: Relationship of biogeochemical cycles in the atmosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere to global chemical cycles and planetary climatic conditions. GES degree foundation and capstone course.
OCN 401.prereq_raw: 201, 310/310L or ATMO 310/310L or OEST 310/310L, BIOL 172/172L, CHEM 162/162L, ERTH 101/101L, MATH 241, MATH 243 & 252A, MATH 373 (or ECON 321), ATMO 200, PHYS 170/170L, and PHYS 272/272L; or consent

children.text: & 252A , MATH 373 ( or ECON 321 ) , ATMO 200 , PHYS 170 / 170L , and PHYS 272 / 272L ; or consent

OCN 403.title: Marine Functional Ecology and Biotechnology
OCN 403.subject: OCN
OCN 403.description: Marine functional genomics, biodiversity of marine natural habitats, marine microbial communities and their ecological functions, interactions of marine microbes and their host, climate change and marine biodiversity, marine biotechnology.

OCN 411.title: The Ethics of Climate Change and Geoengineering
OCN 411.subject: OCN
OCN 411.description: Provide a scientific basis to examine the consequences of climate change and the proposed geoengineering solutions, and examine the fundamental ethical basis that underlies environmental policies.

OCN 418.title: Advanced Environmental Monitoring Systems and Measurements
OCN 418.subject: OCN
OCN 418.description: Builds upon 318 using more advanced microprocessors and environmental sensors, 3D printing, programming, etc. to construct, program, and deploy environmental monitoring systems to collect and stream in-situ time-series environmental measurements.
OCN 418.prereq_raw: 318, MATH 242, PHYS 272/272L, and CHEM 162/162L; or consent

OCN 423.title: Marine Geology
OCN 423.subject: OCN
OCN 423.description: Sediments, structure, geophysics, geochemistry, history of ocean basins and margins.

OCN 430.title: Introduction to Deep-Sea Biology
OCN 430.subject: OCN
OCN 430.description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deepsea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction and global climate change.

OCN 435.title: Climate Change and Urbanization
OCN 435.subject: OCN
OCN 435.description: The following topics will be addressed: How are cities impacted by, and impacting climate change? How do urbanization, alteration of atmospheric processes, and extreme weather events affect urban systems and populations?

OCN 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
OCN 441.subject: OCN
OCN 441.description: Key principles of sustainability and its analysis. Quantification of environmental impact/assessment using target plots, mass/energy balances, and life cycle analyses (cradle to gate/grave) applied to products, processes, or systems. Use of SimaPro.

OCN 442.title: Environmental Management Systems
OCN 442.subject: OCN
OCN 442.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

OCN 444.title: Plate Tectonics
OCN 444.subject: OCN
OCN 444.description: Quantitative geometrical analysis techniques of plate tectonics theory; instantaneous and finite rotation poles; triple-junction analysis; plate boundary stresses.

OCN 450.title: Aquaculture Production
OCN 450.subject: OCN
OCN 450.description: Theory and practice of aquaculture: reproduction, yield trials, management, economics, and business case studies of fish, crustaceans, and molluscs. Field classes held at commercial farm and hatchery.
OCN 450.prereq_raw: ANSC 321 and ANSC 445: or BIOL 172/172L and CHEM 162/162L or higher

OCN 454.title: Earth’s Microbiome
OCN 454.subject: OCN
OCN 454.description: Lecture on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
OCN 454.prereq_raw: 102 or 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

OCN 454L.title: Earth’s Microbiome Lab
OCN 454L.subject: OCN
OCN 454L.description: Lab on the diversity and function of the Earth’s microbiomes, inclusive of terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems, symbiotic and free living microorganisms with a focus on the microbial underpinnings of the Earth’s biogeochemistry.
OCN 454L.prereq_raw: 102 or 201 or BOT 305 or BIOL 305, or BIOL 171 and BIOL 172

OCN 457.title: Ridge to Reef: Coastal Ecosystem Ecology and Connectivity
OCN 457.subject: OCN
OCN 457.description: Watershed and coastal biogechemistry/ecosystem science. Emphasis on field surveying and sampling of stream and reef habitats; laboratory chemical/biological analyses. Analysis of land use impacts on ecosystem health and ahupua‘a resource management.

OCN 463.title: Earth System Science Databases
OCN 463.subject: OCN
OCN 463.description: Combined lecture, discussion, and laboratory on global Earth system databases and satellite instrumentation, including computer laboratory.
OCN 463.prereq_raw: MATH 242; and either 310 and 310L, or GES 310 and GES 310L; or consent

OCN 480.title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
OCN 480.subject: OCN
OCN 480.description: Combined lecture and discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
OCN 480.prereq_raw: 201/201L, 310/310L or GES 310/310L, and PHYS 272/272L; or consent

OCN 481.title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
OCN 481.subject: OCN
OCN 481.description: Introduction to modeling biogeochemical and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on plankton blooms. Students learn ecosystem dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.
OCN 481.prereq_raw: 310, GES 310 or PHYS 272, and OCN/ERTH 312 (with a minimum grade of B-)

children.text: OCN/ERTH 312 ( with a minimum grade of B-

OCN 490.title: Communication of Research Results
OCN 490.subject: OCN
OCN 490.description: Lecture/discussion to provide instruction and experience in oral and written presentation of scientific results and material. GES majors only in their final semester.

OCN 496.title: Topics in Global Environmental Science
OCN 496.subject: OCN
OCN 496.description: Lecture and discussion or seminar. Current topics in environmental science explored in detail. Typically offered by faculty in their specialties, or developed in response to student interest.

OCN 499.title: Undergraduate Thesis
OCN 499.subject: OCN
OCN 499.description: Directed research in which the student carries out a scientific project of small to moderate scope with one or more chosen advisors. The student must complete a document in the style of a scientific journal article.

OCN 601.title: Marine Biology-Environments and Organisms
OCN 601.subject: OCN
OCN 601.description: (3 hr Lec, 3 hr Lab) Introduction to the diversity of marine organisms and the many specialized coastal, reef, and oceanic habitats in which they live. Lab and field research exercises will complement lecture subjects. Graduate standing in Marine Biology graduate degree program only. MB ad OCN majors only.

OCN 602.title: Marine Biology-Processes and Impacts
OCN 602.subject: OCN
OCN 602.description: (3 hr Lec, 3 hr Lab) Investigation of biological phenomena and processes related to productivity and food webs, community structure and ecology, adaptations, and physiology, and impacts of human activities and fisheries. Graduate standing in Marine Biology graduate degree program only.

OCN 620.title: Physical Oceanography
OCN 620.subject: OCN
OCN 620.description: Introduction to properties of seawater, oceanographic instruments and methods, heat budget, general ocean circulation, regional oceanography, waves, tides, sea level. Formation of water masses, dynamics of circulation.

OCN 621.title: Biological Oceanography
OCN 621.subject: OCN
OCN 621.description: Factors governing productivity, population dynamics, distribution of organisms in major ecosystems of the ocean, emphasis on ecology of pelagic zone.

OCN 622.title: Geological Oceanography
OCN 622.subject: OCN
OCN 622.description: Marine geological processes, ocean basin structure and tectonics, sedimentation.

OCN 623.title: Chemical Oceanography
OCN 623.subject: OCN
OCN 623.description: Chemical processes occurring in marine waters; why they occur and how they affect oceanic environment.

OCN 625.title: Aquatic Photosynthesis
OCN 625.subject: OCN
OCN 625.description: Biochemical and biophysical concepts of photosynthesis. Application and interpretation of ecological processes of photosynthesis in aquatic systems. Open to nonmajors.

OCN 626.title: Marine Microplankton Ecology
OCN 626.subject: OCN
OCN 626.description: Distribution, abundance, and ecology of marine microplankton, including bacteria, algae, and protozoans, with an emphasis on metabolic rates and processes.

OCN 627.title: Ecology of Pelagic Marine Animals
OCN 627.subject: OCN
OCN 627.description: Ecology of pelagic animals including feeding, energetics, predation, and anti-predation tactics. Life-history strategies, vertical flux of materials, population dynamics, fisheries.

OCN 628.title: Benthic Biological Oceanography
OCN 628.subject: OCN
OCN 628.description: Processes controlling the structure and function of benthic communities, including organism-sediment-flow interactions, sediment geochemistry, feeding strategies, recruitment, succession, and population interactions.

OCN 629.title: Molecular Methods in Marine Ecology
OCN 629.subject: OCN
OCN 629.description: Molecular methods for studying marine functional ecology; emphasis on hand-on tools for ecological and biogeochemical processes of microbes; developing practical skills for research project in marine microbial ecology and biological oceanography.

OCN 630.title: Deep-Sea Biology
OCN 630.subject: OCN
OCN 630.description: (1.5 Lec, 1.5 Discussion) Biology and ecology of deep-sea organisms and communities. Topics including bentho-pelagic coupling, depth zonation, energetics, diversity, adaptations, hydrothermal vents, seamounts, abyssal plains, deep-sea resource extraction, and global climate change.

OCN 631.title: Ocean Minerals
OCN 631.subject: OCN
OCN 631.description: Distribution, origin, processes of formation. Sulfides, oxides, and placer minerals. Comparative studies of continental ore bodies. Submarine rift, subduction, and abduction.

OCN 633.title: Biogeochemical Methods in Oceanography
OCN 633.subject: OCN
OCN 633.description: Current methods of analysis used in the ocean sciences, both in the field and in the laboratory. An ocean-going field trip provides students with hands-on training in sample collection and processing. The latter is followed by laboratory analyses of the collected samples throughout the remainder of the semester.
OCN 633.prereq_raw: BIOL 171 and CHEM 161 and ERTH 101; or consent

OCN 637.title: Aquatic Microbial Geochemistry
OCN 637.subject: OCN
OCN 637.description: The synergy between the biogeochemistry of element cycling and the microbial organisms involved, interfacing across disciplines from the perspective of a practical blend of aquatic chemistry, microbiology, biogeochemistry, and molecular biology.

OCN 638.title: Earth System Science and Global Change
OCN 638.subject: OCN
OCN 638.description: Global view of the planet and how it functions as an integrated unit. Biogeochemical processes, dynamics, and cycles, and analysis of natural and human-induced environmental change. Chemical history of ocean-atmosphere-sediment system and co-evolution of the biota.
OCN 638.prereq_raw: BS in environmentally related science or one year of chemistry, physics, and calculus

OCN 640.title: Observational Physical Oceanography
OCN 640.subject: OCN
OCN 640.description: Application of the scientific method; physical regimes in the ocean; ocean processes and observational strategies; resolution, sampling, array design and observing systems; models and data assimilation; major field programs; operational oceanography and climate prediction.

OCN 641.title: Origin of Sedimentary Rocks
OCN 641.subject: OCN
OCN 641.description: Environment of deposition and subsequent diagenesis of modern and ancient sediments. Petrogenesis of siliciclastic, carbonate and orthochemical rocks. Sedimentology, sedimentary petrography and geochemistry.

OCN 642.title: Elemental Composition Changes
OCN 642.subject: OCN
OCN 642.description: Changes in the chemical composition of meteorites, bulk Earth, Earth’s mantle and crust, sedimentary rocks, hydrosphere and biosphere, and underlying principles.

OCN 643.title: Topics in Marine Geochemistry
OCN 643.subject: OCN
OCN 643.description: Seminar on a broad topic; discussion and critique of research papers.

OCN 644.title: Sedimentary Geochemistry
OCN 644.subject: OCN
OCN 644.description: Geochemical thermodynamics and kinetics and their use in interpreting the origin of sediments, sedimentary rocks, and natural waters over a range of pressure-temperature conditions.

OCN 650.title: Math Techniques for Oceanographers
OCN 650.subject: OCN
OCN 650.description: Introduction to numerical methods, data analysis, error propagation, box models, linear and nonlinear least squares, perturbation theory, numerical integration.

OCN 653.title: Methods in Microbiology Oceanography
OCN 653.subject: OCN
OCN 653.description: (1 8-hr Lab) Modern methods for sampling microbial populations from the sea and for quantifying biomass and in siturates of metabolism. Integrated field projects, theme varies.

OCN 660.title: Ocean Waves I
OCN 660.subject: OCN
OCN 660.description: Survey of wave types-acoustic, capillary, gravity, inertial, vorticity. Basic wave concepts emphasized: phase and group velocities, standing waves, energy conservation, dispersion, refraction, diffraction. Rotation and boundary effects are covered: reflection, basin modes, trapping, tides.

OCN 661.title: Ocean Waves II
OCN 661.subject: OCN
OCN 661.description: Baroclinic gravity waves, inertial waves, mid-latitude Rossby waves, topographic waves, equatorial waves.

OCN 662.title: Marine Hydrodynamics
OCN 662.subject: OCN
OCN 662.description: Introduction to classical hydrodynamics and continuum mechanics. Techniques for solution of Navier Stokes equations on various scales of oceanic motion; potential theory, dynamic modeling, and viscous and rotational processes.

OCN 663.title: Satellite Oceanography
OCN 663.subject: OCN
OCN 663.description: Techniques of satellite observations of the ocean, including temperature, pigment concentration, currents, and winds; analysis of a satellite data set as term project.

OCN 664.title: Oceanographic Instrumentation and Technology
OCN 664.subject: OCN
OCN 664.description: Measurement techniques in physical oceanography, including pressure, temperature, salinity, oxygen, optical sensors, current meters, navigation systems, ocean acoustics, and mooring structures. Includes a laboratory research project.

OCN 665.title: Small-Scale Air-Sea Interaction
OCN 665.subject: OCN
OCN 665.description: Observations and theory of small-scale processes which couple the atmosphere and ocean boundary layers, including introduction to turbulence theory and parameterization of turbulent fluxes.
OCN 665.prereq_raw: MATH 402 and MATH 403 (or their equivalents) and either 620 or ATMO 600, or consent

children.text: ( or their equivalents) and either 620 or ATMO 600 , or consent

OCN 666.title: Large-Scale Ocean-Atmosphere Interactions
OCN 666.subject: OCN
OCN 666.description: Lecture/seminar introduces physical oceanography and meteorology students to the state-of-the-art theories and observations of large-scale ocean-atmosphere interaction, as well as conveying the fundamental understanding that has been developed during the past 30 years. Emphasis will be on phenomena such as El Nino/Southern Oscillation, the North Atlantic Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, and global climate change.

OCN 667.title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics I
OCN 667.subject: OCN
OCN 667.description: Basic concepts and equations to describe large-scale ocean circulation; numerical models; boundary layers; models of wind-driven circulation of a homogeneous ocean.

OCN 668.title: Advanced Geophysical Fluid Dynamics II
OCN 668.subject: OCN
OCN 668.description: Thermodynamics of stratified fluids; convection; mixing; models of the thermohaline circulation; the role of eddies in the large-scale ocean circulation.

OCN 674.title: Paleoceanography
OCN 674.subject: OCN
OCN 674.description: Study of the paloeceanographic and paleoclimate evolution of the Earth’s oceans, atmosphere, and biosphere.

OCN 680.title: Dynamics of Marine Ecosystems: Biological-Physical Interactions in the Oceans
OCN 680.subject: OCN
OCN 680.description: Combined lecture/discussion examining biological and physical interactions in the oceans and their impacts on the functioning of marine ecosystems.
OCN 680.prereq_raw: previous course in marine science, or consent

OCN 681.title: Introduction to Ocean Ecosystem Modeling
OCN 681.subject: OCN
OCN 681.description: Introduction to modeling biological and physical oceanic processes by building a coupled model of the Pacific to investigate physical effects on biological production. Students will learn biological-physical dynamics, basic numerical methods, and programming.

OCN 682.title: Introduction to Programming and Statistics in R
OCN 682.subject: OCN
OCN 682.description: (3 hr Lec/Lab) Introduces project management, data analysis, and mathematical and statistical modeling using R as a platform. Students will learn principles and benefits of programming languages to apply skills to their own research.

OCN 683.title: Advanced Statistics in R
OCN 683.subject: OCN
OCN 683.description: (2 hr Lec, 1 hr Lab) In-depth introduction to the modern statistical methods necessary for analyzing biological/ ecological data, including GLMs, GAMs, mixed models, ordination, etc. Students will learn how to perform these methods in R. (Fall only

OCN 750.title: Topics in Biological Oceanography
OCN 750.subject: OCN
OCN 750.description: Seminar. Literature and concepts in one of several active fields considered in detail.

OCN 760.title: Topics in Physical Oceanography
OCN 760.subject: OCN
OCN 760.description: Near-shore processes, advanced mathematical techniques, recent developments, etc. Typically given by visiting professors in their specialties, or in response to student interest.

OCN 791.title: Proposal Development
OCN 791.subject: OCN
OCN 791.description: Introduction to the organization and functioning of oceanography funding agencies, the peer-review process, and the design and development of a research proposal.
OCN 791.prereq_raw: two of the following: 621, 626, 627 (or concurrent), or 628 (or concurrent); or consent

OEST 099.title: International Exchange Study/Research
OEST 099.subject: OEST
OEST 099.description: Study overseas in an approved international exchange or similar program.
OEST 099.restrictions_raw: GES, ERTH, and MET majors only.

OEST 100.title: The College Experience
OEST 100.subject: OEST
OEST 100.description: Required for entering SOEST majors to develop skills and applications for a successful college experience. Students will examine academic goals and implement strategies to achieve goals including time management and career exploration.

OEST 101.title: Natural Hazards
OEST 101.subject: OEST
OEST 101.description: Science of natural hazards: impact on human civilization of events in the lithosphere, atmosphere, biosphere, and hydrosphere (e.g., earthquakes, hurricanes, red tides, and floods), and impact of humans on their exposure to and mitigation of the hazards.

OEST 103.title: An Introduction to Integrative Systems Biology: Hawaiian Biomes as a Framework
OEST 103.subject: OEST
OEST 103.description: Lecture/discussion introduces students to the field of biology through the integration of microbiology and macrobiology into a single, comprehensive systems biology with a focus on Hawaiian biomes and ecosystem sustainability.

OEST 109.title: Contemporary Issues in Energy Systems
OEST 109.subject: OEST
OEST 109.description: Introductory experience in energy systems including current status of fossil fuel, renewable energy technologies, energy utilization and conservation; environmental and policy aspects.

OEST 350.title: Ethics in Scientific Research
OEST 350.subject: OEST
OEST 350.description: Introduction to issues of ethics in scientific research and scientific misconduct. ERTH, GES, or ATMO majors only.

OEST 441.title: Principles of Sustainability Analysis
OEST 441.subject: OEST
OEST 441.description: Introduction to the principles of sustainability analysis through execution of Life Cycle Analysis applied to products, processes, or systems. LCA and the evaluation of environmental impact will be presented. Personal computer or laptop (Word 97 or higher) OS, and minimum of 4GB RAM. Junior standing or higher.
OEST 441.prereq_raw: (CHEM 161 and PHYS 170) with a minimum grade of C-; or consent

OEST 510.title: Earth Sciences Professional Development Education
OEST 510.subject: OEST
OEST 510.description: Specialized Earth Science topics workshops designed for in-service teachers who wish to learn new approaches and content areas in geology and geophysics, meteorology and oceanography. Credits earned cannot be applied for graduate degrees.

OEST 696.title: Communicating Ocean Sciences
OEST 696.subject: OEST
OEST 696.description: Application of current learning theory and pedagogical practices in formal and informal learning environments to improve communication and instructional skills. Graduate students from multiple science disciplines welcome. Requires knowledge of biology, earth sciences, and/or chemistry.
OEST 696.prereq_raw: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry or marine science, an interest in ocean science, and enthusiasm for teaching science; or consent

children.text: at least one course in introductory biology, geology, earth science, chemistry
marine science, an interest in ocean science,

OEST 699.title: Directed Reading/Research
OEST 699.subject: OEST
OEST 699.description: Selected interdisciplinary ocean/earth-related topics involving science, technology, engineering, and/or policy.

OEST 735.title: Ocean Policy and Management
OEST 735.subject: OEST
OEST 735.description: Interdisciplinary approach to problems relating to humans and their interactions with the world’s oceans and coasts. Focus includes institutions for governing the world’s oceans and coasts at all scales and on the role of scientific knowledge in managing marine and coastal resources.

ORE 202.title: Ocean Technology—Man in the Sea
ORE 202.subject: ORE
ORE 202.description: Survey of human activities in the ocean, from the most traditional to the most innovative technical and engineering accomplishments.

ORE 203.title: Surf Science and Culture
ORE 203.subject: ORE
ORE 203.description: Focuses on the science of surf and the importance of ocean waves to research pursuits, cultural perspectives in Hawai‘i and the Pacific, navigation, and engineering.

ORE 203L.title: Surf Science and Culture Lab
ORE 203L.subject: ORE
ORE 203L.description: Focuses on the science of surf and the importance of ocean waves to research pursuits, cultural perspectives in Hawai‘i and the Pacific, navigation, and engineering.

ORE 330.title: Mineral and Energy Resources
ORE 330.subject: ORE
ORE 330.description: Hard mineral and petroleum origins, exploration and exploitation. Renewable and non-renewable resources distribution. Political and scientific constraints.

ORE 411.title: Buoyancy and Stability
ORE 411.subject: ORE
ORE 411.description: Ship nomenclature and geometry, hydrostatic principles of surface ships and underwater vehicles in free-floating, partially waterborne, and damaged conditions. Subdivision of ships. Launching.

ORE 601.title: Ocean and Resources Engineering Laboratory
ORE 601.subject: ORE
ORE 601.description: Design, construction, and evaluation of an engineering system. Laboratory and field experience and data analysis supplemented with appropriate theory.

ORE 603.title: Oceanography for Ocean Engineers
ORE 603.subject: ORE
ORE 603.description: Physical, chemical, biological, and geological ocean environments for ocean engineers. Introduction to ocean dynamical processes and general circulation. Ocean measurement techniques, theory of underwater acoustics. Sonar, swath bathymetry, and tomography applications.

ORE 607.title: Water Wave Mechanics
ORE 607.subject: ORE
ORE 607.description: Governing equations in free surface flow, deterministic and probabilistic wave theories, wave transformation, wave-induced coastal currents, tides, ocean engineering operational sea state, and design wave criteria.

ORE 608.title: Probability and Statistics for Ocean Engineers
ORE 608.subject: ORE
ORE 608.description: Probability and statistical analysis including distributions, multiple regression and correlation, autocovariance, cross-spectra, and practical applications in ocean engineering.

ORE 609.title: Hydrodynamics of Fluid-Body Interaction
ORE 609.subject: ORE
ORE 609.description: Hydrodynamics of ships, coastal and offshore structures. Wave forces by potential theory and by Morison’s equation. Method of source distribution for potential flow problems. Flows with prescribed body motion, fixed and freely floating bodies.

ORE 612.title: Dynamics of Ocean Structures
ORE 612.subject: ORE
ORE 612.description: Response of floating platforms and vessels to wave action, spectral analysis in sea keeping. Frequency and time domain analyses of rigid body motions in six degrees of freedom.

ORE 630.title: Structural Analysis in Ocean Engineering
ORE 630.subject: ORE
ORE 630.description: Structural and finite element analyses and design of ocean structures to withstand hydrostatic and hydrodynamic loading of the sea. Considerations include material type, safety factor, stress concentration, and fatigue.

ORE 641.title: Environmental Fluid Dynamics
ORE 641.subject: ORE
ORE 641.description: Fluid dynamics for coastal and estuarine environments. Turbulent mixing processes in homogeneous and stratified fluids. Buoyancy driven flows, internal hydraulics, topographic effects and estuarine circulation. Spill and pollutant dispersal.

ORE 654.title: Applications in Ocean Acoustics
ORE 654.subject: ORE
ORE 654.description: Using sound to observe the ocean. Fundamentals of propagation. Topics include marine mammals, navigation and communication, seismics, ships, wind and rain, ocean dynamics, flow and biological imaging and measurement, seafloor mapping, and the forward/ inverse problem.

ORE 661.title: Coastal and Harbor Engineering
ORE 661.subject: ORE
ORE 661.description: Planning and design of seawalls, groins, jetties, breakwaters, and layout of ports. Design requirements for harbor entrances and channels. Littoral drift and sedimentation problems. Navigation and mooring requirements.

ORE 664.title: Nearshore Processes and Sediment Transport
ORE 664.subject: ORE
ORE 664.description: coastal areas and its effect on morphological processes. Effect of man-made structures on littoral drift and shoreline.

ORE 677.title: Marine Renewable Energy
ORE 677.subject: ORE
ORE 677.description: Ocean thermal energy conversion (OTEC) systems: applicability, thermodynamics, design challenges; wave energy converters: floating devices, oscillating water column, optimal hydrodynamic performance; current, tidal, and offshore wind power.

ORE 678.title: Marine Mineral Resources Engineering
ORE 678.subject: ORE
ORE 678.description: Activities in marine minerals development are examined in a multidisciplinary systems approach involving engineering, Earth and environmental sciences and economics.

ORE 680.title: Ocean Engineering and Resilience in a Changing Climate
ORE 680.subject: ORE
ORE 680.description: Focus on understanding the changing ocean conditions (e.g. waves and sea levels) relevant to the resilience of practical ocean engineering applications. Graduate students only.

ORE 695.title: Plan B Master’s Project
ORE 695.subject: ORE
ORE 695.description: Independent study for students working on a Plan B master’s project. A grade of Satisfactory (S) is assigned when the project is satisfactorily completed.

ORE 700.title: Thesis Research
ORE 700.subject: ORE
ORE 700.prereq_raw: candidacy for MS in ocean and resources engineering

ORE 707.title: Nonlinear Water Wave Theories
ORE 707.subject: ORE
ORE 707.description: Higher-order theories. Forced oscillations. Stoke’s theory. Nonlinear shallow-water wave equations and hydraulic jumps; effects of rotation. Internal waves. Analytical techniques necessary will be developed as course progresses.

ORE 766.title: Numerical Methods in Ocean Engineering
ORE 766.subject: ORE
ORE 766.description: Formulation and application of numerical methods for simulating and solving ocean engineering problems. Mathematical and computational fundamentals; accuracy and stability; numerical interpolation, differentiation, and integration; boundary element, finite difference, and finite element methods.

ORE 791.title: Special Topics in Ocean and Resources Engineering
ORE 791.subject: ORE
ORE 791.description: Content will reflect special interests of visiting and permanent faculty.

ORE 792.title: Seminar in Ocean and Resources Engineering
ORE 792.subject: ORE
ORE 792.description: Attendance at 15 approved seminars is required along with submission of notes.

ORE 800.title: Dissertation Research
ORE 800.subject: ORE
ORE 800.prereq_raw: candidacy for PhD in ocean and resources engineering

PH 201.title: Introduction to Public Health
PH 201.subject: PH
PH 201.description: Introduces public health concepts with an emphasis on principles and tools for population health, disease prevention, health professions and healthcare systems, and public health professions and systems.

PH 202.title: Public Health Issues in Hawai‘i
PH 202.subject: PH
PH 202.description: Application of general public health concepts and tools with broader public health issues as they relate to the State of Hawai‘i.

PH 203.title: Introduction to Global Health
PH 203.subject: PH
PH 203.description: Introduction to the basic principles of global PH. Topics include the application of these principles to global PH issues, exploration of links between health, economic, and social status, health disparities and global interventions.

PH 210.title: Quantitative Reasoning for Public Health
PH 210.subject: PH
PH 210.description: Inductive and deductive reasoning; tabular, symbolic, verbal, and graphical forms of functions and relations; graphs and pictorial representations of data; interpretations of probabilistic data; surveys and statistical studies as related to public health.

PH 301.title: Seminar in Public Health Issues
PH 301.subject: PH
PH 301.description: Seminar will explore current issues and case studies in epidemiology, issues and causes of chronic and infectious diseases, how the environment interacts with health, and how social and behavioral factors affect personal health.

PH 305.title: Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
PH 305.subject: PH
PH 305.description: Seminar to work with faculty in applying evidence-based knowledge on social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians. Junior standing or higher.

PH 310.title: Introduction to Epidemiology
PH 310.subject: PH
PH 310.description: Lecture/discussion on the fundamental principles of epidemiology, exploring patterns of disease, threats to health and EPI methods for prevention, control, and treatment.
PH 310.prereq_raw: 201, and 210 or MATH 140 or MATH 161 or higher

PH 325.title: Youth Risk and Protection–Public Health Research, Practice, and Policy
PH 325.subject: PH
PH 325.description: Application of public health, related to youth health risks and protective factors using an eco-developmental framework.

PH 330.title: The United States Health Care System
PH 330.subject: PH
PH 330.description: Overview of the U.S. health care system. Topics will include health economics, health service expenditures, comparative health systems, health policy, and issues of cost containment, access, and quality of care.

PH 340.title: Public Health and the Environment
PH 340.subject: PH
PH 340.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with environmental effects on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Sophomore standing and above.

PH 341.title: Public Health Biology and Pathophysiology
PH 341.subject: PH
PH 341.description: Explores the biological basis of human disease and the role public health measures play in reducing both the extent and impact of chronic and acute diseases on individuals and society.
PH 341.prereq_raw: 201, and one of the following: BIOL 101 or BIOL 171 or BIOL 172 or PHYL 103 or PHYL 141 or FSHN 185

PH 350.title: Introduction to Biostatistics
PH 350.subject: PH
PH 350.description: Basic biostatistics methods in public health and biomedical research. Topics covered include data collection, data analyses, and interpretation of statistical results.

PH 410.title: Advanced Epidemiology
PH 410.subject: PH
PH 410.description: Students will gain a deeper understanding of the core concepts used in epidemiologic research and practice. Upon completion, students will have the knowledge and skills necessary to conduct an epidemiologic study. Junior standing or higher.

PH 411.title: Nutrition and Disease Prevention
PH 411.subject: PH
PH 411.description: Lecture/discussion. Examines a variety of issues associated with the effects of diet on disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies. Junior standing or higher.

PH 420.title: Social Behavioral Health I: Health Promotion for Individuals and Groups
PH 420.subject: PH
PH 420.description: Focus on the application of social and behavioral theory in health education, and how health promotion programs are constructed for various populations with an emphasis on cultural diversity and social determinants of health. Sophomore standing or higher.

PH 422.title: Social Behavioral Health II: Health Promotion in Communities
PH 422.subject: PH
PH 422.description: Introduction to health education and health promotion programming in public health, and to social/behavioral theories used to develop health interventions that affect communities, institutions, and policies. Introduction to common program planning models.

PH 425.title: Tobacco & Community Disparities
PH 425.subject: PH
PH 425.description: Assessing the facilitators and barriers of smoking initiation, cessation, and exposure to second-hand smoke within communities. Use of photovoice and its application to policy and addressing disparities.

PH 430.title: Health Policy and Management
PH 430.subject: PH
PH 430.description: Examines the role that health policy and management plays in population-based public health practice, including the delivery, quality, and costs of health care and the structure, process, and outcomes of health services delivery. Sophomore standing or higher.

PH 435.title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
PH 435.subject: PH
PH 435.description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
PH 435.prereq_raw: 201 or SW 360 or WS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent

PH 445.title: Introduction to Environmental Microbiology
PH 445.subject: PH
PH 445.description: Lecture/discussion. Will define the nature and biological activities of microorganisms in different environments and evaluate the effects of these microbes on human activities and health. Junior standing or higher.

PH 460.title: Social Determinants of Indigenous Peoples’ Health
PH 460.subject: PH
PH 460.description: Examines indigenous peoples’ health inequities using social determinants of health framework: considers this approach within the historical, political, cultural, and social context of Indigenous population’s health status to generate solutions.

PH 480.title: Application of Public Health Principles in Research and Practice
PH 480.subject: PH
PH 480.description: Introduction to a diverse range of public health projects and associated methods while working to develop an applied learning project proposal. Junior standing or higher.

PH 485.title: Public Health Applied Learning Experience
PH 485.subject: PH
PH 485.description: Allows students to execute an independent, mentor-supervised, applied learning project as implementation of skills learned in previous public health coursework. Applied project is a required component of the public health undergraduate degree program.

PH 489.title: Public Health Undergraduate Capstone Seminar
PH 489.subject: PH
PH 489.description: Integration of public health knowledge, skills, and practice acquired during the public health undergraduate degree. Students will also reflect on, finalize, and present their applied learning experience projects. Senior standing and higher.
PH 489.prereq_raw: completed public health applied learning experience and consent

children.text: completed public health applied learning experience

PH 600.title: Public Health Foundations
PH 600.subject: PH
PH 600.description: Focus will provide a broad introduction to the field of public health and orientation to overarching issues in the field.

PH 602.title: U.S. Health Care Services and Policy
PH 602.subject: PH
PH 602.description: Overview of the historical, conceptual, ethical and political context for health care delivery in the U.S. Explores current trends, practices and issues in the delivery of health care services in both private and public sector.

PH 610.title: Public Health Biology
PH 610.subject: PH
PH 610.description: Writing-intensive asynchronous computer-based course examines biological processes and challenges relevant to the public health professional. Topics include anatomical, pathophysiological, and molecular bases of public health; genetics, immunology, ethics; disease prevention, control, and management. (Once a year)

PH 623.title: Introduction to Health Promotion Theory and Methods
PH 623.subject: PH
PH 623.description: Individual and community health; implications for public health practice, individual and social change processes.

PH 626.title: Health Economics
PH 626.subject: PH
PH 626.description: Integrated concepts in health economics and its application towards health policy issues; market failures in health care; factors affecting U.S. health care spending potential impact on equity/efficiency stemming from changes in health care delivery. (Once a year)

PH 630.title: Cultural Competency in Health Care
PH 630.subject: PH
PH 630.description: Presents both analytical and practical approaches to cultural competency domains, concepts, models, frameworks, patterns and communication that occur in cross-cultural healthcare situations.

PH 633.title: Indigenous Health Activism
PH 633.subject: PH
PH 633.description: Examines how Indigenous Peoples and their allies (individually and collectively) accomplish social change in society. Graduate students only.

PH 635.title: Indigenous Health Seminar
PH 635.subject: PH
PH 635.description: Examines public health through an Indigenous lens, integrates competencies across all public health disciplines, and will apply them in context of working for and with Indigenous communities to improve health and wellness. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

PH 641.title: Advanced Topics in Health Policy
PH 641.subject: PH
PH 641.description: Examines major federal and local policies that impact health and health care delivery in the U.S. and other nations; considers effectiveness of these policy-making institutions for improving population health; covers methods in policy analysis.

PH 646.title: Grant Writing in Public Health
PH 646.subject: PH
PH 646.description: Lecture/discussion on grant writing with public health focus. Includes basic components of grant proposals, assessing appropriate funding opportunities, data sources/resources for justifying grants, and the funder’s perspective. Student will prepare a brief foundation grant proposal. (Once a year)

PH 648.title: Program Planning, Management, Evaluation, and Leadership
PH 648.subject: PH
PH 648.description: Foundation to inform, educate, and improve health for individuals, communities, and populations. Knowledge/acquisition of skills through program planning, management, evaluation and leadership that span the social-ecological range from individual-level to population-level programs.

PH 649.title: Needs Assessment
PH 649.subject: PH
PH 649.description: Knowledge and skills acquisition in conducting needs assessment in public health practice.

PH 650.title: Ecological Epidemiology
PH 650.subject: PH
PH 650.description: Applications of population biology, pathogen/host life history, and population genetics to infectious disease epidemiology, including micro- and macroparasites, and implications to disease control and prevention of strategies.

PH 652.title: Interdisciplinary Seminar
PH 652.subject: PH
PH 652.description: Topics such as contemporary issues in global health and population studies, international health programs, demographic methods, global economy and health, human right and humanitarian assistance, social justice, global environmental changes and health.

PH 653.title: Global Health and Human Security
PH 653.subject: PH
PH 653.description: Provides the knowledge, skills, and attitudes required to successfully manage health security crises and protect human vulnerability in the global context with a special focus on problems with high likelihood and risk in the Pacific.

PH 655.title: Biostatistics I
PH 655.subject: PH
PH 655.description: Introduction to statistical methods for public health sciences. Probability, experimental design, t tests and analysis of variance, 2X2 contingency tables, linear regression, introduction to life tables.

PH 656.title: Biostatistics II
PH 656.subject: PH
PH 656.description: Poisson distribution, Fisher’s exact test, contrasts in ANOVA, two way ANOVA, multiple linear regression and analysis of covariance, path analysis, logistic regression, method of maximum likelihood, likelihood ratio tests.
PH 656.prereq_raw: 655, completion of one semester of calculus; or consent

children.text: completion of one semester of calculus;

PH 658.title: Computer Applications in Public Health
PH 658.subject: PH
PH 658.description: Applications of computers to problems common to public health. Emphasis on data analysis and processing using existing computer programs.

PH 659.title: Methods of Demographic Analysis
PH 659.subject: PH
PH 659.description: Statistical evaluation and analysis of population data; data sources; population growth; composition; standardization of rates; mortality and the life table; nuptiality and fertility; distribution, migration, and urbanization; projections and stable population theory.

PH 660.title: Application of Public Health Skills
PH 660.subject: PH
PH 660.description: Application of public health skills and competencies acquired during the public health degree.

PH 663.title: Principles of Epidemiology I
PH 663.subject: PH
PH 663.description: Introduction to epidemiologic principles and methods. Topics covered include: outbreak investigation, measures of morbidity and mortality, measurements of risk, biological variability, screening, measurements of error, sampling, statistical significance, study design, and association and causation.

PH 664.title: Principles of Epidemiology II
PH 664.subject: PH
PH 664.description: Lecture/discussion on: design and interpretation of experimental and observational studies; causation and casual inference; biases in study design; random error and statistics role in epidemiology; and epidemiological data analysis.

PH 665.title: Concepts in Immunology and Immunopathogenesis
PH 665.subject: PH
PH 665.description: Immunological concepts relating to infectious diseases and host pathogen interactions.

PH 666.title: Seminar in Infectious Disease Control
PH 666.subject: PH
PH 666.description: Strategies for controlling important infectious diseases in the Pacific area. Emphasis on epidemiology, ecology, and public health principles.
PH 666.prereq_raw: 663 (or concurrent) and one semester in microbiology, or consent

PH 667.title: Infectious Disease Micro II
PH 667.subject: PH
PH 667.description: Will cover different families of animal viruses of importance to human diseases. The genome, structure, replication, as well as host immune responses, epidemiology, clinical features, and animal models will be presented.

PH 669.title: Epidemiological Study Design Critique
PH 669.subject: PH
PH 669.description: Critique of study design using published public health literature. Emphasis on exchange of ideas, alternative approaches; stresses epidemiology as science of public health.

PH 671.title: Community and Public Health Practice
PH 671.subject: PH
PH 671.description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

PH 672.title: Leading and Managing Health Programs
PH 672.subject: PH
PH 672.description: Assess how to organize community partnerships to create and communicate a shared vision for a changing future; discuss solutions to organizational and community challenges; maximize motivation to reach public health goals.

PH 673.title: Health Ethics, Law and Politics
PH 673.subject: PH
PH 673.description: Review theories and case studies concerning health care ethics, law and politics. Topics include health care quality, key health care policymakers, and the intersecting issues of policy and law with medicine, public health and ethics. (Once a year)

PH 674.title: Advanced Native Hawaiian Health Determinants
PH 674.subject: PH
PH 674.description: Applications of evidence-based knowledge about the social determinants of health in the formation of research, policy, and program development for improving population health and reducing health disparities for Native Hawaiians.

PH 675.title: Community Engaged Research and Practice
PH 675.subject: PH
PH 675.description: Explores collaborative and engaged approaches with communities in public health research and practice. With a focus on Indigenous Peoples’ health, we delve into Indigenous knowledge and empowerment in evaluation, needs assessment, intervention, and health promotion. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

PH 676.title: Hawai‘i Public Health Policies on Infectious Diseases
PH 676.subject: PH
PH 676.description: Examines quarantine/ isolation of patients infected with Hanson’s disease. Focus on PH policies before 1823 and after; analysis of other infections in Hawai‘i and the world to examine differences in policies and their effect on the public. Graduate students only.

PH 677.title: Managing Global Health Service Delivery
PH 677.subject: PH
PH 677.description: Provides knowledge, skills, attitudes and resources that health managers require to manage and maintain the quality of partnerships, facilities, programs, community services, people, drugs, and information in limited resources settings.

PH 680.title: Health Emergencies in Large Populations
PH 680.subject: PH
PH 680.description: Health Emergencies in Large Populations is run by the Center for Excellence in Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance and the Red Cross. It provides knowledge, practical skills, and networking for global health practitioners.

PH 681.title: Environmental Determinants of Health
PH 681.subject: PH
PH 681.description: Environmental factors in personal and community health; implications for public health practice. Consideration of major issues from local, U.S., and international perspectives.

PH 682.title: Building Well-Being: Health and the Built Environment
PH 682.subject: PH
PH 682.description: History, concepts, and theories behind the relationship between health and the built environment stressing transdisciplinary understanding and collaboration through readings, discussion, and real world-based exercises. PH or LAND and ARCH majors only. Graduate students only.

PH 683.title: Global Nutrition
PH 683.subject: PH
PH 683.description: Examination of global food and nutrition problems, programs, issues, policies, and strategies for improvement.

PH 684.title: Supplemental and Nutritional Approaches in Disease Prevention and Treatment
PH 684.subject: PH
PH 684.description: Examines a variety of issues associated with nutritional and supplemental approaches to reduce disease incidence, morbidity, and mortality in relation to public health prevention strategies.

PH 686.title: Advanced Child and Adolescent Nutrition
PH 686.subject: PH
PH 686.description: Addresses nutrition, growth, and development in children and adolescents and nutrition-related issues, such as childhood obesity and chronic disease risk factors, with a focus on current research in the Pacific region.

PH 688.title: Indigenous Peoples’ Food Systems, Environment and Health
PH 688.subject: PH
PH 688.description: Explores Indigenous Peoples’ food systems as local food resources Indigenous People acquire through specific cultural knowledge of traditional territories. Global forces transforming these food systems and their impact on population health and nutrition are explored. PH majors or consent. Graduate students only.

PH 689.title: Nutritional Epidemiology
PH 689.subject: PH
PH 689.description: Dietary, biochemical, anthropometric and clinical methods used for evaluating nutrition and diet in the etiology and epidemiology of disease.

PH 690.title: Global Health Challenges
PH 690.subject: PH
PH 690.description: Addresses critical, contemporary, and transnational issues best addressed by cooperative international action. Health issues are examined in the context of intersecting effects of limited resources, socioeconomics, politics, and environmental change. (Once a year)

PH 691.title: Fundamentals of Environmental Epidemiology
PH 691.subject: PH
PH 691.description: Examines the complex relationship between environmental contaminants and human health. Emphasis on environmental epidemiology study design, environmental exposure monitoring and risk assessment, disease and environmental exposure mapping, and spatial data analysis and modeling with GIS. (Once a year)

PH 695.title: Promoting Physical Activity
PH 695.subject: PH
PH 695.description: Overview of the theoretical and applied study of physical activity epidemiology. Physical activity content includes benefits, factors that influence, levels, valid instruments to assess, and programs to promote physical activity.

PH 701.title: Health Communication
PH 701.subject: PH
PH 701.description: Skills-oriented course introduces the basic structure of health communication strategies in different settings, selected elements of communication theory, the development of health communication material, and a practical training in motivational counseling skills.

PH 702.title: Health Promotion Research
PH 702.subject: PH
PH 702.description: Focus on research methods commonly used in health promotion. Topics will include randomized trials, quasi-experimental design, sampling, measurement, and correlational studies. Labwork will focus on the use of SPSS to analyze data for applied research problems.

PH 704.title: Community-Based Participatory Research
PH 704.subject: PH
PH 704.description: Explores ways academic and lay communities collaborate on research, key theoretical perspectives in the development of CBPR, and the challenges in implementing CBPR approaches. Format includes lectures, discussions, readings, writing assignments, and a fieldwork project.

PH 728.title: Indigenous Applied Research Methods
PH 728.subject: PH
PH 728.description: (2 hr Lec, 1 hr Computer Lab) Health disparities research methodologies and current topics in Indigenous health research. Special focus on statistical techniques for small data sets using quantitative and qualitative methods.

PH 729.title: Scientific Explorations in Social Justice for Indigenous People
PH 729.subject: PH
PH 729.description: Provides students with an advanced application of health disparities research methodologies to address health and social injustices faced by Indigenous people. Builds on previous courses to advance and produce scientific scholarship. PH majors only or consent. Graduate students only.

PH 742.title: Qualitative Research for Public Health Sciences
PH 742.subject: PH
PH 742.description: Provides a basic understanding of qualitative research approaches, methodologies, and techniques and for public health research and practice (needs assessment, program development, and evaluation strategies). Graduate students only.

PH 747.title: Statistical Methods in Epidemiological Research
PH 747.subject: PH
PH 747.description: Multiple variable statistical methods currently used in chronic disease epidemiology. Logistic regression, conditional logistic regression, proportional hazards regression modelling, generalized estimating equation-based methods, delta method approximations, exact tests.

PH 748.title: Chronic Disease Epidemiology
PH 748.subject: PH
