PH 748.description: Will cover selected topics in chronic diseases with critical analysis of the current epidemiologic literature. Methodologic issues, contemporary findings and recommendations for future research will be discussed.

PH 749.title: Epidemiology of Diabetes and Obesity
PH 749.subject: PH
PH 749.description: Provides an overview of the epidemiology and prevention of metabolic syndrome, diabetes, and associated complications. Discusses methodological issues associated with evaluating these in epidemiologic studies.

PH 750.title: Health Behavior Change
PH 750.subject: PH
PH 750.description: Provide an understanding of the relationship between health behaviors and outcomes including psychological, physiological, and quality of life aspects. It will also focus on the major theories of behavior and behavior change. Emphasis will be placed on understanding concepts, principles, explanations, and how these are translated into practical interventions for adoption and maintaining behavior change.

PH 751.title: Social Epidemiology
PH 751.subject: PH
PH 751.description: Examine the epidemiologic study of the social distribution and social determinants of states of health, including the identification of social-environmental exposures and their relation to physical and mental health outcomes.

PH 752.title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis
PH 752.subject: PH
PH 752.description: Covers modern methods for longitudinal data analysis. Topics include random effects and growth curve models, generalized linear models for longitudinal data including generalized estimating equations, and generalized linear mixed models.

PH 753.title: Survival Analysis
PH 753.subject: PH
PH 753.description: Construction and interpretation of various types of life tables, treatment of censored data, proportional hazards, relative risk regression models, and parametric survival analysis.

PH 754.title: Neuroepidemiology
PH 754.subject: PH
PH 754.description: Lecture/discussion providing an overview of the epidemiology of neurological and neurodegenerative diseases and their risk factors, and methodological considerations for the study of these diseases.

PH 755.title: Seminar in Tropical Medicine and Public Health
PH 755.subject: PH
PH 755.description: Weekly discussion and reports on current advances in tropical medicine and public health.

PH 756.title: Special Topics in Tropical Medicine
PH 756.subject: PH
PH 756.description: Advanced instruction in frontiers of tropical medicine and public health. Repeatable unlimited times.

PH 757.title: Evolution, Epidemiology, and Public Health
PH 757.subject: PH
PH 757.description: Will explore several aspects of human health through the perspective of how natural selection and evolution influence disease risk, with the aim of improving treatment and prevention. Graduate students only.

PH 765.title: Health Program Evaluation
PH 765.subject: PH
PH 765.description: Examines advanced principles of and frameworks for evaluation. Students integrate utilization-focused evaluation methods to improve service delivery and quality, outcomes and impact to improve community and population health.

PH 771.title: Teaching Practicum
PH 771.subject: PH
PH 771.description: Provide doctoral students with theoretical and practical teaching and course development experiences under the guidance of a faculty mentor. Students will have a portfolio documenting their accomplishments. Graduate standing in PH only.
PH 771.prereq_raw: 602 and 623 and 655 and 663 and 681 and 770(Alpha), or departmental approval

PH 772.title: Research Practicum
PH 772.subject: PH
PH 772.description: Hands-on research experience with a faculty mentor. Meet in small groups to discuss issues related to research in public health. Final project will be submission of a publishable quality paper. Graduate standing in PH only.
PH 772.prereq_raw: 602 and 623 and 655 and 663 and 681 and 770(Alpha), or departmental approval

PH 775.title: Public Health Proposal and Dissertation Writing
PH 775.subject: PH
PH 775.description: Intended for doctoral students to complete and defend their proposals and dissertations. Research and presentation methods will be reviewed, and students will be provided critiques by instructor and classmates on their written and presented work.
PH 775.prereq_raw: consent or PhD in PH or EPID only

PH 781.title: Environmental Health Lab Methods
PH 781.subject: PH
PH 781.description: Hands-on training for laboratory methods used in monitoring and detecting environmental health risk factors; learning and application of immunological-, animal cell culture- and molecular biology-based techniques for studying environmental pathogens and toxic pollutants. (Once a year)

PH 788.title: Seminar in Public Health Sciences
PH 788.subject: PH
PH 788.description: Topics related to recent developments in major areas; student and faculty research activities. Sections: (1) biostatistics; (2) environmental health; (3) epidemiology; (4) public health nutrition.

PH 789.title: Integrative Seminar
PH 789.subject: PH
PH 789.description: Integrative seminar in public health required as part of the student capstone experience to bring together key aspects of their courses, competencies, and practicum.
PH 789.prereq_raw: completed PH field practicum and consent

PH 791.title: Advanced Public Health Practice
PH 791.subject: PH
PH 791.description: Observation, study, and supervised practical work in student’s area of specialization.
PH 791.prereq_raw: public health degree candidate and completion of 15 PH credit hours and consent

PH 793.title: Special Practicum/Project
PH 793.subject: PH
PH 793.description: Supervised practical training beyond the required practicum in an area of particular interest. Provides additional opportunity to synthesize, integrate, and apply practical skills and knowledge in a public health work environment.

SW 200.title: The Field of Social Work
SW 200.subject: SW
SW 200.description: Orientation to the profession of social work; historical development, values and philosophy, scope and aims.

SW 302.title: General Social Work Practice I
SW 302.subject: SW
SW 302.description: Orientation to practice principles, concepts, values, knowledge base, and their application.
SW 302.prereq_raw: 200 (complete with C or better) and majors only

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

SW 303.title: General Social Work Practice II
SW 303.subject: SW
SW 303.description: Introduction to practice skills with individuals, families, groups, and communities. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.
SW 303.prereq_raw: 302 (complete with C or better) and majors only

children.text: ( complete with C or better ) and majors only

SW 325.title: History of Social Welfare
SW 325.subject: SW
SW 325.description: Historical developments and implications of social welfare activities, institutions, and policies and European backgrounds; introduce social welfare developments in selected non-European countries.

SW 326.title: Social Welfare as a Social Institution
SW 326.subject: SW
SW 326.description: Study of U.S. social welfare institutions and policies as an expression of societal response to human needs; interrelationship of American value system to goals, objectives, and policies of social security programs; focus on examination of Hawai‘i’s social service programs.

SW 360.title: Human Development and Behavior for Social Work Practice
SW 360.subject: SW
SW 360.description: Examination of social and cultural variables such as human development and behavior; use of knowledge in these areas by social work practitioners.

SW 361.title: Sociocultural Content for Social Work Practice
SW 361.subject: SW
SW 361.description: Examination of ethnicity, class, and sex statuses as these affect human development and behavior for social work practice.
SW 361.prereq_raw: 360 with a grade of C or better. Recommended: 200

SW 380.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 380.subject: SW
SW 380.description: An examination of current trends in the field of social welfare.

SW 391.title: Junior Practicum
SW 391.subject: SW
SW 391.description: Introduction to field instruction; application of social work knowledge, skills, and values to field experience.
SW 391.prereq_raw: 302, 325, 326 (or concurrent), 360, and 361 (or concurrent) complete with C or better; and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

SW 402.title: General Social Work Practice III
SW 402.subject: SW
SW 402.description: Use of problem-solving processes and ethical models of decision-making in practice with individuals, families, groups, and communities.
SW 402.prereq_raw: 303, 326, and 361 complete with C or better; and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better ; and majors only

SW 403.title: General Social Work Practice IV
SW 403.subject: SW
SW 403.description: Examination of practice methods and intervention models; identification and analysis of issues related to practice. A significant portion of class time is dedicated to writing instruction congruent with professional expectations.

SW 435.title: Back to the Future: Aging in Today’s Society
SW 435.subject: SW
SW 435.description: By 2050, more than a quarter of the world’s population will be 60 years of age or older. Explores what we know about aging today to encourage a lifetime of aging well.
SW 435.prereq_raw: 201 or SW 360 or WS 305 or PSY 100 or HDFS 230 or NURS 200; or consent

SW 440.title: Research Development in Social Welfare
SW 440.subject: SW
SW 440.description: Introduction to and application of language of research, theoretical concepts underlying advancement of knowledge, practical steps in research.
SW 440.prereq_raw: completion of required junior-level SW courses (i.e., 302, 303, 325, 326, 360, 361, and 391) with C or better

children.text: completion of required junior-level SW courses ( i.e., 302

SW 475.title: Social Services with Children
SW 475.subject: SW
SW 475.description: Study of current social services for children in the U.S. with focus on familiarization of child welfare programs and services in Hawai‘i.

SW 477.title: Social Welfare Concepts and Issues in Gerontology
SW 477.subject: SW
SW 477.description: Aging and its effect on the individual, family groups, associations, and communities. Impact of aging on social service delivery systems, public policy and role of social work.

SW 480.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 480.subject: SW
SW 480.description: An examination of current trends and issues in social work.

SW 490.title: Senior Practicum
SW 490.subject: SW
SW 490.description: Field instruction, application, and integration of classroom knowledge with field experiences.
SW 490.prereq_raw: 391 complete with C or better, and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

SW 491.title: Senior Practicum
SW 491.subject: SW
SW 491.description: Field instruction, application, and integration of classroom knowledge with field experiences.
SW 491.prereq_raw: 490 complete with C or better, and majors only

children.text: complete with C or better , and majors only

SW 499.title: Directed Reading and Research
SW 499.subject: SW
SW 499.description: Planned individualized study or research in special area related to social work practice interest. Up to 3 credit hours.
SW 499.prereq_raw: majors only, senior standing, and consent of program chair and faculty advisor

SW 606.title: Social Work Practice with Individuals
SW 606.subject: SW
SW 606.description: Beginning practice course introduces students to the basic processes of social work and the roles and skills needed for generalist practice. Relevant theories of social work practice with individuals are explored for the efficacy with various problems and for their applicability to practice with various ethnocultures, social classes, and oppressed populations. Interviewing and interpersonal skill development are incorporated.

SW 607.title: Social Work Practice with Families and Groups
SW 607.subject: SW
SW 607.description: Practice course builds upon the generalist framework and foundation content presented in 606. Special emphasis is given on models for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of practice with families and groups. Relevant theories of groups and the principles of group dynamics and group work methods are examined in regard to task, therapeutic, psychoeducational, and social development groups. Family content includes structural, behavioral, communication/experiential, and culturally-specific theories of intervention.

SW 630.title: Social Welfare Policy and Services
SW 630.subject: SW
SW 630.description: Examines in a historical and comparative framework the economic, social, political, organizational, and administrative factors influencing the development, formulation, and implementation of social welfare policies in the U.S. Provides opportunity for the application of various models of social policy analysis in major areas of social welfare programming and service delivery.

SW 631.title: Social Work Practice in Communities and Organizations
SW 631.subject: SW
SW 631.description: Community conceptualization; organized roles of developer, enabler, broker, mediator, and advocate; diagnostic and problem-solving technology; the special characteristics of the social worker as community organizer; matrix of structural objectives; sources and use of power; how to build an organization; and interorganizational negotiation.

SW 633.title: Organization and Administration in Social Work
SW 633.subject: SW
SW 633.description: Introduction to formal organization theory. Social service administration examined and implications for service delivery systems developed.

SW 636.title: Policies, Programs and Services on Aging
SW 636.subject: SW
SW 636.description: Explores policies, programs, and services for older adults. Students learn about the aging network, assess older adults’ needs, link older adults to appropriate services in the community, and track legislative bills that address older adults’ quality of life.

SW 637.title: Death and Dying
SW 637.subject: SW
SW 637.description: Physical, social, cultural, psychological, and spiritual dimensions of dying, death, and bereavement.

SW 639.title: Social and Cultural Aspects of Aging
SW 639.subject: SW
SW 639.description: Overview of aging from the biopsycho, socioeconomic and cultural perspectives. Explores common theories of aging. Emphasis on bridging the gap between the realm of concepts and theories, and the world of practice in gerontology.

SW 640.title: Introduction to Scientific Methods and Principles in Social Work
SW 640.subject: SW
SW 640.description: Understanding and interpreting results of nomothetic and idiographic research; design principles and statistical analyses and their relationship to practices; use of published research.

SW 650.title: Research Designs and Data Analyses for the Evaluation of Practice Effectiveness
SW 650.subject: SW
SW 650.description: Extending the study of scientific methods introduced in 640. Covers the range of empirical research methods and data analytic procedures suitable for knowledge building and practice evaluation at all levels of intervention from case to program.

SW 651.title: Quantitative Methods I
SW 651.subject: SW
SW 651.description: Introduction to quantitative methods in behavioral sciences. Introduction to general linear model as principle of data analysis. Course requires basic statistics. (Meets PhD common inquiry methods requirement or elective.)

SW 654.title: Applied Regression and Analysis of Variance
SW 654.subject: SW
SW 654.description: Introduction to linear statistical models as principle of data analysis. Topics include multiple regression models with continuous and categorical predictors. ANOVA with multiple factors, ANOVA with repeated measures, and ANCOVA.

SW 656.title: Multivariate Methods
SW 656.subject: SW
SW 656.description: Multivariate forms of multiple linear regression, analysis of variance, and analysis of co-variance. Multiple discriminant analysis, canonical correlation, and principal components analysis are discussed.

SW 659.title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment I
SW 659.subject: SW
SW 659.description: An overview of social work’s person-in-environment focus as it applies to human behavior in the context of families, groups, communities, and organizations. Using an ecological perspective, theories and evidence about human behavior are introduced and examined.

SW 660.title: Human Behavior in the Social Environment II
SW 660.subject: SW
SW 660.description: Uses social work’s person-in-environment focus to organize knowledge development about biological, psychological, social, and cultural systems as they are affected by human behavior. It is designed to provide students with an overview of human behavior and healthy and unhealthy development over the life span.

SW 663.title: Treatment of Chemical Dependency
SW 663.subject: SW
SW 663.description: Introduction to treatment of alcoholism and other chemical dependencies. Application of social work strategies in work with individuals and families in the disease and recovery process.

SW 672.title: Child Welfare as a Field of Social Work
SW 672.subject: SW
SW 672.description: Emphasis on the developments in child welfare; issues, concerns with regard to needs and rights, and the application of social work services to problems associated with needs for protection. Review of historical, theoretical, empirical, and legal findings for skill development in intervening in dysfunctional parent/child interaction.

SW 674.title: Community and Public Health Practice
SW 674.subject: SW
SW 674.description: Community organization and development applicable to the delivery of health services. Understanding community dynamics, mobilizing community groups for effective health care practice and delivery.

SW 680.title: Topics in Social Welfare
SW 680.subject: SW
SW 680.description: Current trends in field of social welfare. Recent courses have focused on forensic social work, immigrants and refugees, and leadership in human services. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 682.title: Marriage and Family Therapy
SW 682.subject: SW
SW 682.description: Introduction to couple and family therapy offers an overview of family systems perspective, theory and technique relevant to informing effective social work case planning, case management, advocacy, and interaction with clients. Graduate students only.

SW 690.title: Practicum
SW 690.subject: SW
SW 690.description: Field units are maintained by the school in public and voluntary welfare agencies, as well as in governmental programs. Students receive instruction related to their school experience with social problem situations and an opportunity to see the applicability and to experience the use of concepts and principles in actual practice.

SW 691.title: Practicum
SW 691.subject: SW
SW 691.description: Field units are maintained by the school in public and voluntary welfare agencies, as well as in governmental programs. Students receive instruction related to their school experience with social problem situations and an opportunity to see the applicability and to experience the use of concepts and principles in actual practice.

SW 696.title: Health and Aging
SW 696.subject: SW
SW 696.description: Biological and physiological changes associated with aging. Social and psychological factors associated with health maintenance. Major threats to health, changing patterns of morbidity and mortality of the aged.

SW 699.title: Directed Reading and Research
SW 699.subject: SW
SW 699.description: Students, on the basis of special interest, select a faculty member to work with on a problem for which planned individualized study or research is deemed advisable.

SW 700.title: Thesis Research
SW 700.subject: SW
SW 700.description: Independent research under supervision of a thesis committee. Includes formal proposal and defense of finished research.

SW 707.title: Methods of Group Psychotherapy
SW 707.subject: SW
SW 707.description: Designed specifically to train students in the theory and practice of leading psychotherapy groups; it includes historical developments, research, theories, and application of group psychotherapy, group techniques and exercises.

SW 715.title: Therapeutic Strategies with the Older Adult
SW 715.subject: SW
SW 715.description: Focuses on interdisciplinary strategies with older adults: individual, family, and group therapy; eclectic mental health approaches; case management; and environmental intervention. Emphasis placed on the use of these strategies as preventive, as well as supportive, measures for the well, transition, and frail elderly. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 717.title: Social Work Practice with Children and Families
SW 717.subject: SW
SW 717.description: Advanced practice course for students specializing in social work with children and families. Designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of both theoretical formulations and therapeutic techniques for practice in the field of family and child welfare. Emphasis placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of common child and family practice situations.

SW 718.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice with Children and Families
SW 718.subject: SW
SW 718.description: Designed for students in the child and family concentration and builds upon past knowledge and skill development in practice classes and in the practicum. Students integrate, demonstrate, and extend earlier learning, acquire new knowledge, and learn and practice new skills. Organized around student case presentations in a consultation format. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 722.title: Social Work Practice in Health Care
SW 722.subject: SW
SW 722.description: Didactic and experiential learning activity focuses on the major role functions of the social worker in the health field including assessment, contracting, counseling, advocacy, case management, discharge planning, family group work, community and team building. Covers health care policy, research directions in practice and social work management issues.

SW 723.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Health Care
SW 723.subject: SW
SW 723.description: Through the use of case studies developed by the students, social work practice is examined in three areas of health care: primary care provided in health departments and medical groups, hospital-based services, and long-term care. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 724.title: Seminar in Social Work Practice in Mental Health
SW 724.subject: SW
SW 724.description: Prepares students for social work practice in mental health settings. As the first course in the concentration, it focuses primarily on minor or short-term mental dysfunctioning (e.g., reactive depression, anxiety). Built on conceptual foundations including cultural implications of mental health, human ecology, life cycle/events, strengths assessments, and research. Includes a seminar component which involves student case presentations and consultations.

SW 725.title: Social Work Practice in Mental Health
SW 725.subject: SW
SW 725.description: Prepares students to work with persons who are experiencing major mental disorders and to improve the systems of care that have been developed to serve this population. It reviews the history of the community mental health movement, discusses relevant policies and laws, and describes the current mental health system in the U.S. and Hawai‘i.

SW 726.title: Social Work Practice with the Aged
SW 726.subject: SW
SW 726.description: Designed for social work students specializing in social work practice with the aged and their families. Examines normative and pathological aging and its impact on physical processes, intellectual functions, and personality. Emphasis is placed on the development of specialized knowledge and skills for assessment, intervention, and evaluation of a variety of issues and needs common in later life. Discussions on the applicability of certain interventions with the older adult and the family, along with ethnocultural and gender considerations.

SW 727.title: Seminar in Social Work with the Aged
SW 727.subject: SW
SW 727.description: Designed for social work students in the aged concentration, builds upon past knowledge and skill development from courses and practicum. Students examine micro and macro interventions used for a wide range of issues and problems encountered by older adults and their families through the use of both case presentation and case consultations assignments. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 731.title: Social Policy Analysis
SW 731.subject: SW
SW 731.description: Students pursue in-depth a specific topic in the areas of social planning, social policy analysis, evaluation of social programs, administration, supervision, and consultation. Selectively a comparative perspective is introduced and case studies used to illustrate concepts, principles, and techniques, with implications for practice. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 737.title: Social Work and the Law
SW 737.subject: SW
SW 737.description: Knowledge of judicial systems and law relevant to social work practice in corrections, child-family welfare, health, and mental health. Skills for effective participation in the legal process are acquired in moot court and in practice for testifying.

SW 741.title: Review of Research in Social Work
SW 741.subject: SW
SW 741.description: In-depth study of research in a substantive area. Each seminar will be devoted to a particular topic: e.g., foster care of children, effectiveness of social work intervention, etc.

SW 743.title: Individual or Group Research Project— Plan B
SW 743.subject: SW
SW 743.description: Independent research (group of two to seven students or by an individual student) undertaken under the sponsorship of a faculty advisor. Elements are selection of a topic related to the practice of social work or knowledge relevant to that practice, utilization of empirical research methodology in collecting and analyzing original data, and preparation of a scholarly paper.

SW 744.title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
SW 744.subject: SW

SW 746.title: Individual or Group Research Project– Plan B
SW 746.subject: SW

SW 750.title: Analysis and Development of Knowledge for Social Work
SW 750.subject: SW
SW 750.description: Focuses on developing an understanding of philosophy of science, theory development, social work epistemology, and the analysis and development of knowledge for social work practice.
SW 750.prereq_raw: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent

SW 751.title: Quantitative Methods II
SW 751.subject: SW
SW 751.description: Empirical research methodology with emphasis on design principles and measurement theory; design and measurement issues and problems in cross-cultural research.
SW 751.prereq_raw: PhD candidate in social welfare or consent

SW 752.title: Qualitative Research: Philosophical, Methodological and Analytic Approaches
SW 752.subject: SW
SW 752.description: Theories and methods of qualitative research; problem formulation, informant selection, study design, data collection and analysis utilizing qualitative approaches.

SW 755.title: Dissertation Seminar
SW 755.subject: SW
SW 755.description: Culminating experience in social welfare doctoral specialization; integration of PhD core and specialization course work.
SW 755.prereq_raw: classified student in PhD in social welfare program or consent

children.text: classified student in PhD in social welfare program

SW 772.title: Seminar in International Social Work
SW 772.subject: SW
SW 772.description: Approaches to social problems and trends in the profession in international, cross-cultural perspectives. Emphasis on developmental aspects of social work. Political, economic, social, and cultural forces shaping social welfare in national development. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 774.title: Cultural Factors in Work with Hawaiians
SW 774.subject: SW
SW 774.description: Hawaiian culture, past and present. Explores and examines possible approaches to working with Hawaiians and part-Hawaiians. Special emphasis on supports in the Hawaiian system that may promote maximal functioning for those Hawaiians experiencing problems in today’s society. Meets seminar requirement.

SW 776.title: Seminar on Women and Health
SW 776.subject: SW
SW 776.description: Women’s health and the role of women health professionals. Current literature and research regarding attitudes, roles, rights, and health care.

SW 790.title: Second-Year Practicum
SW 790.subject: SW
SW 790.description: Instruction in the field is continued. The practicum of the second year provides an opportunity for the student to test out concepts, principles, theories, and alternate approaches in actual practice settings.

SW 797.title: Advanced Social Welfare Policy Analysis and Change
SW 797.subject: SW
SW 797.description: Builds on 630 and emphasizes a more thorough and comprehensive examination of major policies, programs, and populations central to a concentration (Health, Mental Health, Gerontology, Child and Family). Students learn a more focused and applied analysis of the relationship between social policy, research, and social work practice.

TIM 099.title: International Exchange Programs
TIM 099.subject: TIM
TIM 099.description: UH Mânoa School of Travel Industry Management majors participating in approved international exchange programs.

TIM 100.title: Internship I
TIM 100.subject: TIM
TIM 100.description: Introduction to travel industry. Discussion of job search strategies, TIM internship requirements, career and academic planning.

TIM 101.title: Introduction to Travel Industry Management
TIM 101.subject: TIM
TIM 101.description: Overview of travel industry and related major business components. Analysis of links between hotel, food, transportation, recreation, and other industries comprising tourism.

TIM 102.title: Food and World Cultures
TIM 102.subject: TIM
TIM 102.description: An integrated cross-cultural approach to the study of foods and cultures. Examine history, concepts, principles of cultures and cuisines, the background of food tradition including habitat, social status, religious beliefs, gender, and other environmental considerations.

TIM 200.title: Internship II
TIM 200.subject: TIM
TIM 200.description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

TIM 300.title: Internship III
TIM 300.subject: TIM
TIM 300.description: A minimum of four hundred hours of travel industry experience. Position must be different from TIM 200 position and of a more responsible nature or in a different organization. Comprehensive report by student and performance evaluation from employer required.

TIM 301.title: Legal Environment of the Travel Industry
TIM 301.subject: TIM
TIM 301.description: Origin, development, and principles of common, statutory, constitutional, international, and maritime law relating to hospitality industry.

TIM 302.title: Information Systems Technology
TIM 302.subject: TIM
TIM 302.description: Computer applications in the travel industry; operation and evaluation of specific travel industry systems and applied business systems.

TIM 303.title: Management of Service Enterprises
TIM 303.subject: TIM
TIM 303.description: Principles and philosophies of management with special emphasis on those principles and theories that are most relevant to management in service-based industries. Students may not earn credit for 303 and BUS 315.

TIM 304.title: Principles of Travel Industry Marketing
TIM 304.subject: TIM
TIM 304.description: Concepts, problems, processes of marketing within the travel industry; development of marketing strategies including product, place, promotion, and price for travel institutions. Students may not earn credit for 304 and BUS 312.

TIM 305.title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
TIM 305.subject: TIM
TIM 305.description: Cash flow determination and management strategies for financing hospitality ventures and expansion. Determining the financial viability of proposed and existing operations through traditional and state-of-the-art techniques.
TIM 305.prereq_raw: 101, ACC 202, and NREM 203, MATH 203, MATH 215, MATH 241, or BUS 250

TIM 306.title: Human Resource Management: Travel Industry
TIM 306.subject: TIM
TIM 306.description: Human resources as a strategic asset in the travel industry; contemporary theories, issues, and developments in the field; practical training in oral communication to enhance employee recruitment, retention, and productivity.

TIM 310.title: Institutional Purchasing
TIM 310.subject: TIM
TIM 310.description: Procurement responsibilities in hospitality management. Emphasis on institutions supplying hospitality operations and legislation which controls standards of industrial supplies and goods.

TIM 311.title: Club Management
TIM 311.subject: TIM
TIM 311.description: Introduction to club and institutional management, including operations, services, and facilities.

TIM 313.title: Foodservice Management
TIM 313.subject: TIM
TIM 313.description: Critical and essential aspects of managing foodservice operations including principles of food safety and sanitation, procedural knowledge in front and back of the house and guest relations.

TIM 314.title: Hotel Management
TIM 314.subject: TIM
TIM 314.description: Comprehensive understanding of hotel management and functional departments including front office, accounting, housekeeping, food and beverage, marketing, security and safety. Simulation of management trainee programs by hotel chains. Synthesis of concepts, tools and theories of decision-making relevant to hotel operations.
TIM 314.prereq_raw: 101, 302, and 303 (with a minimum grade of C- in 302 and 303)

children.text: ( with a minimum grade of C- in 302 and 303 )

TIM 315.title: Quality Food Management
TIM 315.subject: TIM
TIM 315.description: Explore various aspects of the quality in foodservice operations and develop strategies to measure and improve the quality.

TIM 316.title: Events Planning and Marketing
TIM 316.subject: TIM
TIM 316.description: Introduction to special event planning processes and techniques. Emphasis on designing, planning, marketing, management, staging events, legal compliances, risk management, financial control, and successful event evaluation.

TIM 319.title: Quantity Foods and Institutional Purchasing
TIM 319.subject: TIM
TIM 319.description: Quantity food and beverage operations, menu development and costing, dietary menu claims, purchasing procedures, inventory control, procurement, transportation, legislation. Institutional foodservice sanitation, Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and National Restaurant Association Certification.

TIM 320.title: Introduction to Tourism Economics
TIM 320.subject: TIM
TIM 320.description: Examines tourism from an economic perspective. Topics include: the determinants of consumer demand for leisure travel, structure of competition among suppliers of tourism services, benefits and costs of tourism development to the host community, government’s role in the taxation, subsidy, regulation and protection of the tourism industry, tourism’s impact on the environment, and sustainable tourism development.

TIM 321.title: Sociocultural Issues in Tourism
TIM 321.subject: TIM
TIM 321.description: Issues arising from the impacts of tourism on societies and cultures. Class discussions of the ethical dimensions of such impacts. Includes an emphasis on writing instruction.

TIM 324.title: Geography of Global Tourism
TIM 324.subject: TIM
TIM 324.description: Tourist landscape in relation to resources, spatial patterns of supply and demand, impacts of tourism development, and models of tourist space. Flows between major world regions.
TIM 324.prereq_raw: sophomore standing or higher, or consent

TIM 327.title: Travel Distribution Management
TIM 327.subject: TIM
TIM 327.description: History, development, operations, and management of travel distribution organizations including: travel agents, tour operators and wholesalers, specialty channelers, meeting planners, incentive houses, travel associations, and other destination management organizations. Evolution and economics of the distribution of travel products through destination databases and electronic commerce.

TIM 333.title: Hotel/Resort Facilities and Design
TIM 333.subject: TIM
TIM 333.description: Comprehensive understanding of facilities management and design including maintenance systems, sustainable development options and design and environmental management.

TIM 334.title: Hotel and Convention Sales
TIM 334.subject: TIM
TIM 334.description: Functions, methods, and problems of hotel, convention, and restaurant sales. Needs of different classifications of properties; market segmentation and the sale of services vs. products.

TIM 350.title: Introduction to Tourism Transportation
TIM 350.subject: TIM
TIM 350.description: Introduction to managerial and operational issues related to all modes of transportation used by tourists into or within a tourist destination. Passenger behavior; transport infrastructure; transport networks; regulation; sustainable transport.

TIM 351.title: Principles of Logistics
TIM 351.subject: TIM
TIM 351.description: Management of logistics systems: inventory control, warehousing, materials management, physical distribution, transportation. Emphasis on Hawai‘i’s location and unique problems.

TIM 353.title: Air Transportation Management
TIM 353.subject: TIM
TIM 353.description: Marketing, management and strategies used by airlines, airports, catering, and aircraft manufacturers.

TIM 354.title: Surface Transportation Management
TIM 354.subject: TIM
TIM 354.description: Management of surface transportation such as cars, buses, and intercity rail, etc. Includes marketing, ownership and financing, supply chain, operations, regulation and promotion, human resources.

TIM 365.title: Economics in Travel Industry
TIM 365.subject: TIM
TIM 365.description: Microeconomic theory of consumer behavior and demand production cost analysis, market structure and pricing in travel companies. Economic impact of tourism. Students may not earn credit for 365 and BUS 313.

TIM 368.title: TIM Study Abroad
TIM 368.subject: TIM
TIM 368.description: Study abroad instructional experience emphasizing international travel, tourism and hospitality-related topics at equivalent, accredited programs. Content varies depending on locus of instruction and instructor. Course qualifies as either a TIM or general elective with pre-approval or department.

TIM 399.title: Directed Reading and Research
TIM 399.subject: TIM
TIM 399.description: Reading and research into problems in hotel, restaurant, transportation or tourism sectors of the travel industry.
TIM 399.prereq_raw: junior standing or above, a minimum cumulative GPA of 2.5 and consent of dean’s office and instructor based upon student’s written proposal of content and objectives of course program. TIM majors only

TIM 401.title: Resort, Spa and Wellness Management
TIM 401.subject: TIM
TIM 401.description: Principles of resort and spa development. Essential aspects of understanding the leadership and interrelationships of managing/operating and marketing resorts, spas, and wellness.

TIM 402.title: Resort Mixed Use Development
TIM 402.subject: TIM
TIM 402.description: Critical and essential aspects of developing and managing resort mixed use facilities. Includes multidimensional and dynamic interrelationships of site development and facilities, business mix, management structures and systems, and industry practices.

TIM 415.title: Nature-Based Tourism Management
TIM 415.subject: TIM
TIM 415.description: Principles of nature-based tourism, including a survey of impacts, objectives, planning, and management systems. Junior standing or higher.

TIM 420.title: Sustainable Tourism Policies and Practices
TIM 420.subject: TIM
TIM 420.description: Seminar examining the social, environmental, economic factors of sustainable tourism development. Emphasis on methods and processes and the role of stakeholders (government, industry, host community, tourists). Group projects.

TIM 425.title: Destination Development and Marketing
TIM 425.subject: TIM
TIM 425.description: Analysis of key factors in the marketing and management of tourism destinations, including destination branding, product development, integrated marketing, stakeholder relations, and the role of destination marketing/marketing organizations. Emphasis on written communication.

TIM 431.title: Strategic Management for the Travel/ Hospitality Industry
TIM 431.subject: TIM
TIM 431.description: Strategic management in the travel/hospitality industry. Case study analysis, discussion and written reports, covering strategies, management problems and industry issues. Emphasis on writing instruction.

TIM 442.title: Advanced Topics in Transportation
TIM 442.subject: TIM
TIM 442.description: Advanced level of discussion in terms of transportation, including management, economics, strategy, regulation, operating performance, fleet management, and network management.

TIM 462.title: Environmental Management Systems
TIM 462.subject: TIM
TIM 462.description: Introduction to the process of developing Environmental Management Systems that address the principles outlined in ISO14001:2015.

TIM 601.title: Research Applications in Travel Industry Management
TIM 601.subject: TIM
TIM 601.description: Analysis of methodologies appropriate for research in travel industry management. Survey of the literature of applied techniques and approaches including exploratory approaches. Familiarization with research design and implementation of development of research proposals.

TIM 602.title: Strategic Travel Marketing
TIM 602.subject: TIM
TIM 602.description: In-depth study of marketing principles and problems related to travel industry organizations. Emphasis on strategic marketing. Research applications, international and domestic marketing of travel industry services.

TIM 603.title: Information Technology, E-Commerce, and Travel Industry
TIM 603.subject: TIM
TIM 603.description: Planning, implementation, management, evaluation, and impact of information and electronic communication technologies, including e-commerce applications in the travel industry. Analysis of new information technology use as an area of research and strategic application.

TIM 604.title: Managerial Accounting for Travel Industry
TIM 604.subject: TIM
TIM 604.description: Advanced study of management accounting within travel industry: responsibility accounting, pricing decisions, concepts and application of central systems, financial planning, price level impacts, performance evaluation.

TIM 605.title: Hospitality Management
TIM 605.subject: TIM
TIM 605.description: Advanced human relations and operating issues; use of accounting, behavioral, financial, marketing, and informational systems in managing hospitality organizations.

TIM 606.title: Transportation Economics and Management
TIM 606.subject: TIM
TIM 606.description: Advanced study analysis of economics and management of passenger transportation systems serving the travel industry. Emphasis on topics such as government policy, transport economics, marketing and management, and the relationships between transportation systems and tourism development.

TIM 607.title: Global Tourism Analysis
TIM 607.subject: TIM
TIM 607.description: International trade theory and regional analysis methodologies applied to tourism and the service industry, including travel balance account, inter-regional transactions flow, economic impacts, environmental economics, demand theory and forecasting.

TIM 640.title: Financial Management for the Travel Industry
TIM 640.subject: TIM
TIM 640.description: Applications of financial analysis to both the domestic and international travel industry.

TIM 645.title: Tourism Field Studies
TIM 645.subject: TIM
TIM 645.description: Integration of concepts and application of knowledge and skills from other courses to a selected field study project.
TIM 645.prereq_raw: any two 600-level TIM courses completed and a third concurrent; or consent

TIM 694.title: Professional Paper
TIM 694.subject: TIM
TIM 694.description: Independent project or paper under faculty supervision in lieu of Plan A, TIM 700 thesis. Requires proposal approved by supervisor and graduate chair prior to registration.
TIM 694.prereq_raw: three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent

TIM 695.title: Seminar: Travel Industry Management Policy
TIM 695.subject: TIM
TIM 695.description: Integration of learning through analysis of policy issues, trends, and problems in the travel industry.
TIM 695.prereq_raw: three 600-level TIM courses completed or consent

TIM 699.title: Directed Reading
TIM 699.subject: TIM
TIM 699.description: Independent study of approved, advanced reading with faculty supervision. Requires proposal prepared by student and approved by supervisor and graduate chair before registration.

TIM 700.title: Thesis Research
TIM 700.subject: TIM
TIM 700.description: Independent supervised research. Formal and oral written presentation of research findings.

LWLM 570.title: Introduction to American Law
LWLM 570.subject: LWLM
LWLM 570.description: General introduction to the fundamental principles and distinctive aspects of the American legal system and its institutions.

LWLM 580.title: U.S. Legal Research and Writing
LWLM 580.subject: LWLM
LWLM 580.description: Introduction to the basic principles of American legal research and writing. Students review techniques of case and statutory analysis and learn to write a professional legal memoranda and client opinion letters. LL.M. students only.

LWEV 503.title: Wildlife and Natural Resources Law
LWEV 503.subject: LWEV
LWEV 503.description: Seminar covering federal and Hawai‘i laws that govern the management of wildlife resources, with a particular focus on wildlife conflicts arising in Hawai‘i.

LWEV 504.title: Conservation Transactions
LWEV 504.subject: LWEV
LWEV 504.description: Real estate transactions are an important and growing conservation strategy; examines land transactions within the environment of conservation. (Once a year)

LWEV 512.title: Environmental Compliance and Regulated Industries
LWEV 512.subject: LWEV
LWEV 512.description: In depth study of the federal and state environmental laws that impact modern businesses and industries, and exploration of the compliance issues that arise under the statutes, regulations, and case law.

LWEV 528.title: International Environmental Law
LWEV 528.subject: LWEV
LWEV 528.description: Study of the international regulation of activities and processes used to prevent environmental degradation and to preserve resources of environmental value.

LWEV 529.title: Environmental Litigation Seminar
LWEV 529.subject: LWEV
LWEV 529.description: Seminar on the techniques, law, and strategy involved in federal and state court environmental litigation.

LWEV 530.title: Climate Change Law and Policy
LWEV 530.subject: LWEV
LWEV 530.description: Climate change is a core challenge that will influence law and policy well into the future. Students will study climate change science, litigation, law and policy at state, national, and international levels. (Once a year)

LWEV 540.title: Hazardous Waste Law
LWEV 540.subject: LWEV
LWEV 540.description: Examination of major federal statutes, regulatory and case law, and Hawai‘i counterparts. Policies behind hazardous waste laws and their impact on individuals, community, and businesses.

LWEV 582.title: Environmental Law
LWEV 582.subject: LWEV
LWEV 582.description: Basic statutory law and policy questions and problems concerning the environment. Focus on federal Hawai‘i issues.

LWEV 588.title: Legal Aspects of Water Resources and Control
LWEV 588.subject: LWEV
LWEV 588.description: Legal aspects of water and water rights with focus on Hawai‘i.

LWEV 592.title: Domestic Ocean and Coastal Law
LWEV 592.subject: LWEV
LWEV 592.description: Examination of U.S. and Hawai‘i ocean and coastal law covers modern issues concerning the protection and use of the native environment including challenges in Hawai‘i.

LWEV 593.title: International Ocean Law
LWEV 593.subject: LWEV
LWEV 593.description: Examination of the history of international ocean law, including comprehensive coverage of modern problems and issues concerning the laws of the sea.

LWJT 545.title: Law Review
LWJT 545.subject: LWJT
LWJT 545.description: Students selected for the Law Review editorial board have responsibility for editorial research, writing, and production of the Law Review published by the School of Law.

LWJT 546.title: Asian-Pacific Law Journal
LWJT 546.subject: LWJT
LWJT 546.description: Students selected for the Asian-Pacific Law and Policy Journal editorial board have writing, researching, editorial and production responsibility for publication of the journal.

LWLR 501.title: Legal Research
LWLR 501.subject: LWLR
LWLR 501.description: Provides a theoretical understanding of the process of law making and of developing and implementing a research plan.

LWLR 505.title: Scholarly Research Methods
LWLR 505.subject: LWLR
LWLR 505.description: Learn to plan the prewriting process for such scholarly assignments as Second Year Seminar (SYS), writing for law review, moot court competitions, and in any course involving a scholarly approach to research and writing.

LWLW 530.title: Law Thesis
LWLW 530.subject: LWLW
LWLW 530.description: Intensive writing that satisfies the law school’s upper division writing requirement and results in advanced law paper of publishable quality, extending over two consecutive semesters of study.

LWLW 537.title: Law Teaching Seminar I
LWLW 537.subject: LWLW
LWLW 537.description: Interdisciplinary seminar used LP 1 assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of substantive law assignments and the methodology used to teach them. Instructor approval required.

LWLW 538.title: Law Teaching Seminar II
LWLW 538.subject: LWLW
LWLW 538.description: Interdisciplinary seminar uses LP II assignments and additional readings to discover and deliver the theoretical and practical underpinnings of appellate advocacy and negotiation the methodologies used to teach them. Instructor approval required.

LWLW 539.title: Legal Composition Seminar I
LWLW 539.subject: LWLW
LWLW 539.description: Study of principles and practices of teaching legal discourse one-to-one, transferring materials from composition theory and linguistics into practical papers and methods to assist students to research and write legal documents. Instructor approval required.

LWLW 540.title: Legal Composition Seminar II
LWLW 540.subject: LWLW
LWLW 540.description: Study of principles and practices of teaching scholarly legal discourse and appellate advocacy one-to-one, transferring composition theory and linguistics into individualized methods make the legal writing process efficient and the product effective. Instructor approval required.

LWPA 514.title: Law and Society in Japan
LWPA 514.subject: LWPA
LWPA 514.description: An extended historical review of the foundations of Japanese law in society: Japan’s adoption and adaptation of Chinese legal doctrines, continental European legal structures and ideas, and American influences. Consideration of the structure of contemporary law in Japan: a look at the various players in the legal system, some important legal doctrines, and the real-world operation of Japan’s laws today.

LWPA 553.title: Asian Pacific Insolvency Law
LWPA 553.subject: LWPA
LWPA 553.description: Comparison of corporate insolvency law of selected Asian and Pacific island countries, with a focus on recently enacted laws and pending proposals that have followed the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis. Law students only.

LWPA 556.title: Asian Comparative Labor Law
LWPA 556.subject: LWPA
LWPA 556.description: Area studies of Asian legal systems and issues, focusing on administration of Asian labor laws in a comparative context. Possible effects on foreign direct investment and foreign migrant contract workers. Comparison of Chinese, Japanese and other legal approaches in dealing with common issues.

LWPA 564.title: International Criminal Law
LWPA 564.subject: LWPA
LWPA 564.description: Designed to give an understanding of international criminal law. Will review all aspects of international criminal law from substantive international crimes to criminal liability and sentencing by domestic and international tribunals.

LWPA 565.title: Law and Society in Korea
LWPA 565.subject: LWPA
LWPA 565.description: Provides students with an understanding of the law, society, and legal systems in Korea. Areas of law including constitutional, civil, criminal, and business are discussed. Emphasis on South Korea.

LWPA 569.title: Human Rights in Asia
LWPA 569.subject: LWPA
LWPA 569.description: Offered to provide advanced human rights courses at the Law School. The purpose is to convey an understanding of the current situation concerning human rights in Asia, and to facilitate a chance to think about what the future may bring.

LWPA 577.title: Japanese Business Law
LWPA 577.subject: LWPA
LWPA 577.description: Focus on the legal environment facing foreign businesses operating in Japan. Includes consideration of the business environment and culture, issues relating to governmental oversight, contract consciousness, corporate law, and dispute resolution. Uses the example of an actual joint venture between an American and a Japanese company as a tool for studying the relevant issues from a practical perspective.

LWPA 578.title: Chinese Business Law
LWPA 578.subject: LWPA
LWPA 578.description: Introduction to business and commercial law in the People’s Republic of China. After a brief overview of China’s political and legal systems, the course will examine basic areas of domestic business legislation, including torts, property, and contract law, the regulation of private business, the reform of state enterprises, the development of company and securities laws, and the regulation of land-use and other property rights. More specialized topics, such as arbitration and dispute resolution, the Chinese approach to intellectual property issues, or the use of joint ventures and other foreign investment vehicles, may also be included.

LWPA 579.title: International Business Transactions
LWPA 579.subject: LWPA
LWPA 579.description: An examination of the law, rules, and practices relating to transborder commercial transactions. Roughly half of the semester focuses on international sales transactions, the remaining portion focuses on domestic and multinational governance of the international business arena.

LWPA 581.title: Native Hawaiian Rights
LWPA 581.subject: LWPA
LWPA 581.description: Status and evolution of rights of Native Hawaiians to the land and its usufructs. Potential of utilizing native rights based on statute, custom, and use to develop new and expanded rights.

LWPA 583.title: Legal History of Hawai‘i
LWPA 583.subject: LWPA
LWPA 583.description: Designed to acquaint the student with the unique legal history of Hawai‘i, emphasizing particular legal controversies that have shaped the law of our island society.

LWPA 584.title: Emerging Hawai‘i Water Issues
LWPA 584.subject: LWPA
LWPA 584.description: Introduction to the legal framework for water resource management in Hawai‘i; case studies illuminate the litigation process and evolution of the public trust, precautionary principle, and other legal, scientific, and policy areas.

LWPA 585.title: International Law
LWPA 585.subject: LWPA
LWPA 585.description: Evolving process of formulating rules to govern nations and peoples of the world in their attempts to solve problems recognized as requiring global solutions.

LWPA 586.title: Law and Society in China
LWPA 586.subject: LWPA
LWPA 586.description: Overview of the historical foundations of Chinese law and introduction to the present legal system in the People’s Republic of China.

LWPA 587.title: Comparative Law
LWPA 587.subject: LWPA
LWPA 587.description: Introduction to the civil law tradition, particularly as exemplified by the legal systems of East and Southeast Asia. After a brief review of comparative law study and the historical development of the civil law, the course will examine the structure and role of the courts, judicial process, the legal profession and constitutional law and administrative law in Western Europe and in the Asian civil law countries.

LWPA 588.title: International Human Rights Advocacy
LWPA 588.subject: LWPA
LWPA 588.description: Applying international human rights law and legal skills to promote and protect human rights by way of United Nations Charter-based human rights mechanism, treaty-based mechanism, or other international human rights institutions.

LWPA 589.title: International Law, Transitional Justice, and War Crimes Tribunals
LWPA 589.subject: LWPA
LWPA 589.description: Discusses central problems of responsibility for mass atrocity crimes such as genocide, and with the role of providing accountability through criminal accountability or other means such as truth commissions in post-conflict societies.

LWPA 590.title: International Economic Law
LWPA 590.subject: LWPA
LWPA 590.description: Problem-based course teaches theory and practice of interrelated global private regulation and public development consequences, as situated in cross-border transactions and dispute resolution in world law, international investment law, and international financial law.

LWPA 594.title: Pacific Islands Legal Systems
LWPA 594.subject: LWPA
LWPA 594.description: Study of substantive rules of one or more Pacific Islands jurisdictions, development of legal systems, relationship of legal systems to culture and tradition.

LWPA 596.title: International Intellectual Property
LWPA 596.subject: LWPA
LWPA 596.description: Primer on the World Intellectual Property Organization and the treaties it administers. Will explore the various international legislative and judicial developments in intellectual property as well as analyze international methods to harmonize several regional and national laws to protect rights in trademarks, patents, and copyrights. Students will be exposed to issues of territoriality and jurisdiction, international antitrust issues, and international dispute resolution, and human rights implications of international intellectual property rights protections.

LWUL 501.title: American Legal Systems
LWUL 501.subject: LWUL
LWUL 501.description: Introduces foundational concepts in American legal systems. Engages students in legal analysis and techniques of legal advocacy.

LWUL 502.title: American Legal Systems II
LWUL 502.subject: LWUL
LWUL 502.description: Introduces conceptual and historical foundations of systems of public and private ordering in the U.S. and its territories. Subjects include federalism, constitutional democracy, separation of powers, and the common law.

LSJD 501.title: SJD Directed Reading
LSJD 501.subject: LSJD
LSJD 501.description: Individual reading and research for SJD dissertation under supervision of faculty instructors. LAW students only.

LSJD 590.title: SJD Legal Scholarship
LSJD 590.subject: LSJD
LSJD 590.description: Provides SJD students with an overview of legal scholarship in a series of related fields. Students will be introduced to different research approaches and areas of legal analysis through presentations by instructor and other faculty. LAW students only.

LSJD 591.title: SJD Legal Writing Seminar
LSJD 591.subject: LSJD
LSJD 591.description: Provides SJD students with an overview of fundamentals for academic writing skills and opportunity to improve their writing of dissertations. LAW students only.
